entries.zh: 上天報應，鼎為周出，故名曰周鼎。
entries.en: Heaven answered that merit and sent forth the cauldron—hence men called it the tripod of Zhou.
entries.literal: High Heaven responded; the tripod came forth for Zhou—therefore its name was called Zhou tripod.

entries.zh: 今漢自高祖繼周，亦昭德顯行，布恩施惠，六合和同。
entries.en: Han, inheriting Zhou from Gaozu onward, has shown the same virtue, spread the same kindness, and brought the six quarters into harmony.
entries.literal: Now Han from High Ancestor inheriting Zhou, also displayed virtue and manifest conduct, spread favor and extended grace—the six directions harmonized as one.

entries.zh: 至於陛下，恢廓祖業，功德愈盛，天瑞並至，珍祥畢見。
entries.en: Under your hand the ancestral work has broadened, merit towers higher, and omens and prodigies crowd upon the age.
entries.literal: Reaching Your Majesty, expanding the ancestors' enterprise, merit and virtue ever more abundant, heavenly omens together arrived, auspicious signs all appeared.

entries.zh: 昔秦始皇親出鼎於彭城而不能得，天祚有德而寶鼎自出，此天之所以與漢，乃漢寶，非周寶也。」
entries.en: The First Emperor hunted that cauldron at Pengcheng in vain; Heaven gives the bronze only to the throne that owns true virtue. This vessel belongs to Han, not to the long-dead house of Zhou."
entries.literal: Formerly Qin Shi Huang personally sought the tripod at Pengcheng but could not obtain it; Heaven blesses those with virtue and the precious tripod came forth itself—this is Heaven's reason for giving Han; it is Han's treasure, not Zhou's treasure.'

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: Well said,' answered the emperor.
entries.literal: The Superior said: 'Good.'

entries.zh: 群臣皆稱萬歲。
entries.en: The court shouted ten thousand years.
entries.literal: The assembled ministers all called ten thousand years.

entries.zh: 是日，賜壽王黃金十斤。
entries.en: That day Shouwang received ten catties of gold.
entries.literal: That day he granted Shouwang ten jin of gold.

entries.zh: 後坐事誅。
entries.en: Later he died on a criminal charge.
entries.literal: Later he sat on an affair and was executed.

entries.zh: 助還，又諭淮南曰：「皇帝問淮南王：使中大夫玉上書言事，聞之。
entries.en: On his way home Yan Zhu called on Huainan with the emperor's words: "The throne has read the memorial your palace grandee lately presented.
entries.literal: When Zhu returned, again he announced to Huainan, saying: 'The Emperor asks the King of Huainan: you sent Palace Grandee Yu to submit a memorial on affairs; I have heard it.

entries.zh: 朕奉先帝之休德，夙興夜寐，明不能燭，重以不德，是以比年凶災害眾。
entries.en: I rise before dawn and retire late, yet my light does not reach every shadow; lacking virtue, I have brought plague and famine on the land.
entries.literal: We receive the former Emperor's beautiful virtue; rise early and sleep late; brightness cannot illumine; heavily because of lack of virtue, therefore in recent years baleful disasters have been many.

entries.zh: 夫以眇眇之身，托於王侯之上，內有饑寒之民，南夷相攘，使邊騷然不安，朕甚懼焉。
entries.en: This frail body sits above the kings while folk freeze and starve and southern tribes claw at our borders—I am afraid.
entries.literal: Relying on this tiny body, entrusted above the kings and marquises, within there are people of hunger and cold, southern barbarians mutually encroach, causing the border to be restless and unquiet—we are very fearful thereof.

entries.zh: 今王深惟重慮，明太平以弼朕失，稱三代至盛，際天接地，人跡所及，鹹盡賓服，藐然甚慚。
entries.en: You have weighed the age and held up the mirror of the sage-kings, where every land that felt a human foot paid homage—I stand humbled before your praise.
entries.literal: Now the King has deeply pondered and heavily considered, clarifying great peace to assist Our failures, praising the Three Dynasties' utmost flourishing, joining Heaven and touching Earth, wherever human tracks reach, all alike guest-submit—We are very ashamed, standing alone.

entries.zh: 嘉王之意，靡有所終，使中大夫助諭朕意，告王越事。」
entries.en: I honor your counsel without reserve and charge Yan Zhu to lay before you the whole business of Yue."
entries.literal: We praise the King's intent, without limit to the end; We order Palace Grandee Zhu to announce Our intent, reporting to the King the Yue affair.'

entries.zh: 主父偃，齊國臨菑人也。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan came from Linzi in Qi.
entries.literal: Zhufu Yan was a man of Linzi in the Qi state.

entries.zh: 學長短從橫術。
entries.en: He trained in the persuasive arts of coalition politics—the "short and long" and "vertical and horizontal" schools.
entries.literal: He studied the arts of short-and-long and vertical-and-horizontal persuasion.

entries.zh: 晚迺學易、春秋、百家之言。
entries.en: Only later did he turn to the Book of Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the hundred schools.
entries.literal: Only later did he study the Changes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the teachings of the hundred schools.

entries.zh: 游齊諸子閒，諸儒生相與排儐，不容於齊。
entries.en: He moved among Qi's princely households, but the Ru scholars banded against him and Qi would not keep him.
entries.literal: He wandered among the princes of Qi; the Confucian scholars together ostracized him, and he found no place in Qi.

entries.zh: 家貧，假貸無所得，北游燕、趙、中山，皆莫能厚，客甚困。
entries.en: Poor at home and unable to borrow his way forward, he went north through Yan, Zhao, and Zhongshan, but no court would shelter him generously and he lived in bitter want.
entries.literal: His family was poor; he borrowed but obtained nothing. Traveling north through Yan, Zhao, and Zhongshan, none could treat him generously, and as a guest he was greatly distressed.

entries.zh: 以諸侯莫足游者，元光元年，迺入關見衛將軍。
entries.en: Finding no prince worth his service, in the first year of Yuanguang he entered the capital to seek out General Wei Qing.
entries.literal: Because no feudal lord seemed worth serving, in the first year of Yuanguang he entered the passes to see General Wei.

entries.zh: 衛將軍數言上，上不省。
entries.en: Wei Qing spoke for him again and again, but the emperor paid no heed.
entries.literal: General Wei repeatedly spoke of him to the Emperor, but the Emperor did not take notice.

entries.zh: 資用乏，留久，諸侯賓客多厭之，迺上書闕下。
entries.en: Money ran out, his stay dragged on, and fellow clients grew tired of him; at last he sent up a memorial at the palace gate.
entries.literal: His funds were exhausted; he stayed long, and many feudal lords' guests grew weary of him; then he submitted a memorial beneath the palace gate.

entries.zh: 朝奏，暮召入見。
entries.en: He presented it in the morning and was summoned that evening.
entries.literal: Memorial in the morning, summoned to audience by evening.

entries.zh: 所言九事，其八事為律令，一事諫伐匈奴，曰：
entries.en: Nine proposals followed: eight became statutes, and one warned against war on the Xiongnu. It read:
entries.literal: Of the nine matters he spoke, eight became statutes and orders; one remonstrated against campaigning against the Xiongnu, saying:

entries.zh: 助諭意曰：「今者大王以發屯臨越事上書，陛下故遣臣助告王其事。
entries.en: Yan Zhu continued: "You wrote because troops were massing on your border against Yue; the emperor therefore sent me to explain what followed.
entries.literal: Zhu announced the intent, saying: 'Now the Great King because of raising garrison facing the Yue affair submitted a memorial; therefore Your Majesty sent your servant Zhu to report to the King the affair.

entries.zh: 王居遠，事薄遽，不與王同其計。
entries.en: You live far from the capital; news reaches you late; the throne did not wait to take your counsel.
entries.literal: The King dwells far; affairs are thin and hurried; We did not consult with the King on the plan.

entries.zh: 朝有闕政，遺王之憂，陛下甚恨之。
entries.en: When policy at court leaves you anxious, the emperor grieves.
entries.literal: When the court has flawed government, leaving worry to the King, Your Majesty deeply regrets it.

entries.zh: 夫兵固凶器，明主之所重出也，然自五帝、三王禁暴止亂，非兵，未之聞也。
entries.en: Weapons are an evil thing that a wise ruler looses only in need—yet since the age of the Five Thearchs no king has stopped violence without steel.
entries.literal: Arms are indeed a baleful tool; a clear ruler esteems issuing them rarely; yet from the Five Thearchs and Three Kings suppressing violence and stopping chaos, without arms, We have not heard of it.

entries.zh: 漢為天下宗，操殺生之柄，以制海內之命，危者望安，亂者卬治。
entries.en: Han is the head of the family of states; it holds life and death in one hand. The desperate look to us for peace, the rebellious for judgment.
entries.literal: Han is all under Heaven's lineage, holds the handle of killing and living, thereby to control the seas' command; those in peril look to peace, those in chaos look up to order.

entries.zh: 今閩越王狠戾不仁，殺其骨肉，離其親戚，所為甚多不義，又數舉兵侵陵百越，並兼鄰國，以為暴強，陰計奇策，入燔尋陽樓船，欲招會稽之地，以踐句踐之跡。
entries.en: The king of Minyue is savage and faithless—he murdered his kin, betrayed his allies, and raided his neighbors until he grew bold enough to burn the Han fleet at Yangxun and dream of seizing Kuaiji like Goujian of old.
entries.literal: Now the King of Minyue is cruel and harsh without benevolence, killing his flesh and bone, separating his kin and relatives; what he has done has many unrighteous acts; again he repeatedly raised troops to invade and bully the hundred Yue, annexing neighboring states, thereby to act violent and strong; with secret plans and strange stratagems, he entered and burned Yangxun tower-ships, wishing to summon Kuaiji lands, thereby to tread in Goujian's tracks.

entries.zh: 今者，邊又言閩王率兩國擊南越。
entries.en: The frontier now reports that the king of Minyue is driving two kingdoms against Nanyue.
entries.literal: Now moreover the border again reports the King of Min leading two states to strike Nanyue.

entries.zh: 陛下為萬民安危久遠之計，使人諭告之曰：『天下安寧，各繼世撫民，禁毋敢相並。』
entries.en: You acted for the people's long-term good, sending heralds to warn them: "The realm is at peace; every prince must govern his own people and never dare swallow his neighbor."
entries.literal: Your Majesty for the myriad people's safety and peril, long-term plan, sent men to announce to them, saying: 'All under Heaven is quiet; each in succession soothes his people; order that none dare mutually annex.

entries.zh: 有司疑其以虎狼之心，貪據百越之利，或於逆順，不奉明詔，則會稽、豫章必有長患。
entries.en: The ministers feared they nursed wolfish ambition toward the Yue tribes and might defy your edict—which would leave Kuaiji and Yuzhang in endless peril.
entries.literal: The offices suspected them of harboring tiger-and-wolf hearts, coveting to seize the hundred Yue's profit, or crossing the line between loyal and rebel, not obeying the clear edict—then Kuaiji and Yuzhang would face chronic trouble.

entries.zh: 且天子誅而不伐，焉有勞百姓苦士卒乎？
entries.en: The Son of Heaven chastises rebels; he does not grind his people under needless campaigns—why wring sweat from farmer and soldier alike?
entries.literal: Moreover the Son of Heaven punishes but does not campaign—how could there be laboring the hundred surnames and bitter troops?

entries.zh: 故遣兩將屯於境上，震威武，揚聲鄉，屯曾未會，天誘其衷，閩王隕命，輒遣使者罷屯，毋後農時。
entries.en: Two generals camped on the border to overawe them before a blow was struck—and Heaven struck first: the king of Minyue fell dead. Messengers then stood the troops down so the spring plowing would not be lost.
entries.literal: Therefore he dispatched two generals to garrison on the border, shake martial awe, raise voice toward them; the garrisons had not yet joined battle—Heaven guided their inner hearts; the King of Min lost his life; immediately he sent an envoy to dismiss the garrisons, not to miss the farming season afterward.

entries.zh: 南越王甚嘉被惠澤，蒙休德，願革心易行，身從使者入謝。
entries.en: The king of Nanyue was overwhelmed by your kindness and vowed to mend his ways; he wished to follow my escort to the capital and apologize in person.
entries.literal: The King of Nanyue greatly praised receiving blessing-moisture, received beautiful virtue, wished to change heart and alter conduct, personally to follow the envoy and enter apology.

entries.zh: 有狗馬之病，不能勝服，故遣太子嬰齊入侍；
entries.en: Illness keeps him from the journey, so he sends his heir Yingqi to wait on the throne in his stead;
entries.literal: He had dog-and-horse illness, could not bear the burden, therefore sent the crown prince Yingqi to enter attendance;

entries.zh: 病有瘳，願伏北闕，望大廷，以報盛德。
entries.en: should his strength return, he will kneel at the north gate and look upon the great hall to thank you in person.
entries.literal: if illness has recovery, he wishes to prostrate at the north gate tower, gaze on the great court, to repay supreme virtue.

entries.zh: 閩王以八月舉兵於冶南，士卒罷倦，三王之眾相與攻之，因其弱弟餘善以成其誅，至今國空虛，遣使者上符節，請所立，不敢自立，以待天子之明詔。
entries.en: In the eighth month the king of Minyue rose south of Ye, but his troops were spent; the allied kings fell on him and his younger brother Yu Shan finished the deed. The kingdom stands leaderless: envoys have brought the seals and ask you to name a successor—they dare not enthrone themselves without your word.
entries.literal: The King of Min in the eighth month raised troops south of Ye; soldiers and foot were weary; the three kings' multitudes together attacked him, relying on his weak younger brother Yu Shan to complete his execution; until now the state is empty and void; he sent an envoy to submit tallies and ribbons, requesting whom to establish, not daring to establish himself, awaiting the Son of Heaven's clear edict.

entries.zh: 此一舉，不挫一兵之鋒，不用一卒之死，而閩王伏辜，南越被澤，威震暴王，義存危國，此則陛下深計遠慮之所出也。
entries.en: Not a blade was dulled, not a man lost, yet the tyrant of Minyue paid for his crimes, Nanyue bathed in your grace, villains trembled, and a doomed state was spared—this is the fruit of your long foresight.
entries.literal: This one movement did not blunt one weapon's point, did not use one foot soldier's death, yet the King of Min submitted to guilt, Nanyue received moisture, awe shook the violent king, righteousness preserved the endangered state—this is where Your Majesty's deep plans and far thoughts issued forth.

entries.zh: 事效見前，故使臣助來諭王意。」
entries.en: You have seen the outcome with your own eyes; the emperor therefore sent me to lay his answer before you."
entries.literal: The affair's effects appeared before your eyes; therefore he sent your servant Zhu to come announce the King's intent.'

entries.zh: 於是王謝曰：「雖湯伐桀，文王伐崇，誠不過此。
entries.en: Liu An bowed and said: "Tang's war on Jie and King Wen's strike at Chong were no finer than this.
entries.literal: Thereupon the King apologized, saying: 'Although Tang campaigned against Jie, King Wen campaigned against Chong, truly they did not surpass this.

entries.zh: 臣安妄以愚意狂言，陛下不忍加誅，使使者臨詔臣安以所不聞，誠不勝厚幸！」
entries.en: I spoke rashly from a fool's heart, yet you spared my life and sent a herald to teach me what I had failed to see—such mercy leaves me speechless with gratitude!'
entries.literal: Your servant An rashly with foolish mind wildly spoke; Your Majesty could not bear to add execution; sending an envoy to descend edict on your servant An with what I had not heard—truly I cannot overcome thick good fortune!'

entries.zh: 助由是與淮南王相結而還。
entries.en: Yan Zhu left on terms of friendship with the king of Huainan.
entries.literal: Zhu on this account connected with the King of Huainan and returned.

entries.zh: 上大說。
entries.en: The emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 助侍燕從容，上問助居鄉里時，助對曰：「家貧，為友婿富人所辱。」
entries.en: At a leisurely banquet the emperor asked Yan Zhu about his youth. He answered: "I was poor and lived as a dependent son-in-law; a wealthy host treated me with contempt."
entries.literal: When Zhu attended a banquet at ease, the Emperor asked Zhu about dwelling in village and hamlet; Zhu answered, saying: 'My family was poor; as friend-son-in-law I was insulted by a rich man.'

entries.zh: 上問所欲，對願為會稽太守。
entries.en: When asked what reward he wanted, he begged for the governorship of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: The Emperor asked what he desired; he answered that he wished to be Kuaiji grand governor.

entries.zh: 於是拜為會稽太守。
entries.en: The appointment was granted at once.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was appointed Kuaiji grand governor.

entries.zh: 數年，不聞問。
entries.en: Years passed without word from the capital.
entries.literal: For several years, no inquiry was heard.

entries.zh: 賜書曰：「制詔會稽太守：君厭承明之廬，勞侍從之事，懷故土，出為郡吏。
entries.en: A rescript reached him: "You grew weary of the Chenming waiting lodge and the round of court attendance, and longed for home—so we sent you out to govern your commandery.
entries.literal: A granted letter said: 'Imperial rescript to the Kuaiji grand governor: You have grown weary of Chenming Lodge, toil of attendant-follower affairs, cherish native soil, gone out to be commandery governor.

entries.zh: 會稽東接於海，南近諸越，北枕大江。
entries.en: Kuaiji touches the sea on the east, the Yue tribes on the south, and the great river on the north.
entries.literal: Kuaiji east joins the sea, south nears the various Yue, north pillows the great river.

entries.zh: 間者，闊焉久不聞問，具有《春秋》對，毋以蘇秦從橫。」
entries.en: We have heard nothing from you for an age—send a memorial worthy of the Spring and Autumn Annals, not the empty zigzag of Su Qin.'
entries.literal: Of late, broad and distant, long without hearing inquiry—fully have a Chunqiu-type answer; do not use Su Qin's alliance-rivalry.'

entries.zh: 助恐，上書謝稱：「《春秋》天王出居於鄭，不能事母，故絕之。
entries.en: Yan Zhu answered in terror: "The Annals record how the Zhou king withdrew to Zheng because he failed his mother—and was cast off for it.
entries.literal: Zhu in fear submitted a memorial apologizing, saying: 'In Chunqiu the Heaven King went out to dwell at Zheng—because he could not serve his mother, therefore he was cut off.

entries.zh: 臣事君，猶子事父母也，臣助當伏誅。
entries.en: A minister owes his prince what a son owes his parents; I deserve death for my silence.
entries.literal: A subject serving his lord is like a son serving parents; your servant Zhu ought to submit to execution.

entries.zh: 陛下不忍加誅，願奉三年計最。」
entries.en: If you will not take my life, let me at least forward the triennial accounts in person."
entries.literal: Your Majesty cannot bear to add execution; I wish to present the three-year reckoning ultimate.'

entries.zh: 詔許，因留侍中。
entries.en: The emperor relented and kept him at court as palace attendant.
entries.literal: Edict permitted; therefore he stayed as palace attendant.

entries.zh: 有奇異，輒使為文，及作賦頌數十篇。
entries.en: Whenever omens appeared he was set to draft edicts; he also wrote dozens of rhapsodies and hymns.
entries.literal: When there were strange anomalies, then they made him compose texts, and he wrote fu and eulogies several tens of pieces.

entries.zh: 後淮南王來朝，厚賂遺助，交私論議。
entries.en: Later, when the king of Huainan visited the capital, he loaded Yan Zhu with gifts and drew him into secret talk.
entries.literal: Afterward when the King of Huainan came to court, he heavily bribed and presented to Zhu, privately exchanging discussion.

entries.zh: 及淮南王反，事與助相連，上薄其罪，欲勿誅。
entries.en: When Huainan rose in revolt, Zhu was implicated; the emperor would have let him off lightly.
entries.literal: When the King of Huainan rebelled, the affair connected with Zhu; the Emperor slighted his crime, wishing not to execute.

entries.zh: 廷尉張湯爭，以為助出入禁門，腹心之臣，而外與諸侯交私如此，不誅，後不可治。
entries.en: Zhang Tang, commandant of justice, protested: Yan Zhu passed freely through the inner palace as your confidant, yet trafficked with feudal princes—spare him and no law will ever hold.
entries.literal: Commandant of Justice Zhang Tang disputed, thinking that Zhu going in and out of forbidden gates, a heart-and-belly minister, yet outwardly so privately associating with feudal lords—if not executed, later could not be governed.

entries.zh: 助竟棄市。
entries.en: Yan Zhu was executed in the public market after all.
entries.literal: Zhu in the end was cast aside in the market.

entries.zh: 後數歲，買臣隨上計吏為卒，將重車至長安，詣闕上書，書久不報。
entries.en: Some years later he rode to Chang'an as a conscript teamster on the annual accounting caravan, presented a memorial at the palace gate, and heard nothing for months.
entries.literal: After several years, Maichen followed the commandery accounting clerk as a soldier, leading heavy carts to Chang'an, went to palace gates and submitted memorial; long time no answer.

entries.zh: 待詔公車，糧用乏，上計吏卒更乞丐之。
entries.en: While waiting at the public carriage office his food ran out; the rotating clerks had to beg scraps for him.
entries.literal: Awaiting edict at the public carriage office, provisions exhausted; the accounting clerk-foot soldiers in rotation begged from him.

entries.zh: 會邑子嚴助貴幸，薦買臣，召見，說《春秋》，言《楚詞》，帝甚說之，拜買臣為中大夫，與嚴助俱侍中。
entries.en: His townsman Yan Zhu, then in favor at court, recommended him. He discoursed on the Spring and Autumn Annals and the Songs of Chu; the emperor was charmed, named him palace grandee, and paired him with Yan Zhu as palace attendant.
entries.literal: It happened that townsmen Yan Zhu was noble and favored, recommended Maichen; summoned audience, expounded Chunqiu, spoke Chuci; the Emperor was very pleased, appointed Maichen palace grandee, together with Yan Zhu both palace attendants.

entries.zh: 是時，方築朔方，公孫弘諫，以為罷敝中國。
entries.en: While Shuofang fort was rising, Gongsun Hong argued that the work would beggar the interior.
entries.literal: At that time they were just building Shuofang; Gongsun Hong remonstrated, thinking it exhausted the central states.

entries.zh: 上使買臣難詘弘，語在《弘傳》。
entries.en: The emperor set Zhu Maichen to demolish Hong's argument—the exchange is recorded in Hong's biography.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Maichen to refute and shame Hong—the words are in Hong's treatise.

entries.zh: 後買臣坐事免，久之，召待詔。
entries.en: Later he lost office over a charge, then after a long interval was recalled to await edict.
entries.literal: Afterward Maichen sat an affair and was dismissed; after a long time summoned to await edict.

entries.zh: 是時，東越數反覆，買臣因言：「故東越王居保泉山，一人守險，千人不得上。
entries.en: Eastern Yue had rebelled again. Zhu Maichen told the throne: "Their old king held Quan Mountain, where one defender could block a thousand climbers.
entries.literal: At that time Eastern Yue repeatedly turned back; Maichen therefore said: 'Formerly the Eastern Yue king dwelt guarding Quan Mountain—one man guarding the peril, a thousand could not ascend.

entries.zh: 今聞東越王更徙處南行，去泉山五百里，居大澤中。
entries.en: They have now shifted five hundred li south into open marsh—far from that fortress.
entries.literal: Now I hear the Eastern Yue king has again moved dwelling southward, leaving Quan Mountain five hundred li, dwelling in great marshes in between.

entries.zh: 今發兵浮海，直指泉山，陳舟列兵，席捲南行，可破滅也。」
entries.en: Send a fleet straight to Quan Mountain, land in force, and sweep south—you can crush them at a blow.'
entries.literal: Now issue troops floating the sea, straight pointing at Quan Mountain, array boats and line soldiers, rolling mat southward—can destroy and exterminate them.'

entries.zh: 上拜買臣會稽太守。
entries.en: The emperor named him governor of Kuaiji.
entries.literal: The Emperor appointed Maichen Kuaiji grand governor.

entries.zh: 上謂買臣曰：「富貴不歸故鄉，如衣繡夜行，今子何如？」
entries.en: He teased him: "They say brocade is wasted on a night walk unless you show it at home—what of you now?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said to Maichen: 'Rich and noble but not returning to native village is like wearing embroidery walking at night—now you, how is it?'

entries.zh: 買臣頓首辭謝。
entries.en: Zhu Maichen kowtowed in thanks.
entries.literal: Maichen knocked head and apologized.

entries.zh: 詔買臣到郡，治樓船，備糧食、水戰具，須詔書到，軍與俱進。
entries.en: He was ordered, on reaching Kuaiji, to fit out war junks and stores and hold his fleet ready until the imperial command to sail.
entries.literal: Edict: when Maichen reached the commandery, repair tower-ships, prepare grain food and water-war equipment; wait till edict arrives, army with him together advance.

entries.zh: 數年，坐法免官，復為丞相長史。
entries.en: Some years later he lost office for a legal fault, then served as chief clerk to the chancellor.
entries.literal: After several years, sat on law dismissed office, again was chancellor chief clerk.

entries.zh: 張湯為御史大夫。
entries.en: Zhang Tang held the seal of imperial counselor.
entries.literal: Zhang Tang was imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 始，買臣與嚴助俱侍中，貴用事，湯尚為小吏，趨走買臣等前。
entries.en: Once Zhu and Yan Zhu had stood high at court while Zhang Tang was a runner who scurried at their heels.
entries.literal: At first, Maichen and Yan Zhu together were palace attendants, noble and handling affairs; Tang was still a petty clerk, hastening before Maichen and others.

entries.zh: 後湯以延尉治淮南獄，排陷嚴助，買臣怨湯。
entries.en: When Zhang Tang as commandant of justice tried the Huainan case he destroyed Yan Zhu; Zhu Maichen never forgave him.
entries.literal: Afterward Tang as commandant of justice tried Huainan case, framed and trapped Yan Zhu; Maichen resented Tang.

entries.zh: 及買臣為長史，湯數行丞相事，知買臣素貴，故陵折之。
entries.en: After Zhu became chief clerk, Zhang—often acting for the chancellor—knew how high Zhu had once stood and snubbed him at every turn.
entries.literal: When Maichen became chief clerk, Tang repeatedly carried out chancellor business, knowing Maichen had always been noble, therefore treated him harshly and humiliated him.

entries.zh: 買臣見湯，坐床上弗為禮。
entries.en: When Zhu called, Zhang lounged on his couch and refused courtesy.
entries.literal: When Maichen saw Tang, Tang sat on the couch and did not perform rites.

entries.zh: 買臣深怨，常欲死之。
entries.en: Zhu nursed a murderous grudge.
entries.literal: Maichen deeply resented, constantly wished him dead.

entries.zh: 後遂告湯陰事，湯自殺，上亦誅買臣。
entries.en: He struck back with a secret denunciation; Zhang Tang fell on his sword, and the emperor had Zhu executed as well.
entries.literal: Afterward then accused Tang of secret affairs; Tang killed himself; the Emperor also executed Maichen.

entries.zh: 買臣子山拊官至郡守，右扶風。
entries.en: His son Shanfu rose to governor of Youfufeng commandery.
entries.literal: Maichen's son Shanfu reached office as grand governor—of Youfufeng.

entries.zh: 吾丘壽王字子贛，趙人也。
entries.en: Wuqiu Shouwang, courtesy name Zigong, was a native of Zhao.
entries.literal: Wuqiu Shouwang, style Zigong, was a man of Zhao.

entries.zh: 年少，以善格五召待詔。
entries.en: In youth he won fame at the board game Wuge and was summoned to await imperial orders.
entries.literal: In youth, because good at Wuge game summoned to await edict.

entries.zh: 詔使從中大夫董仲舒受《春秋》，高才通明。
entries.en: An edict set him to study the Spring and Autumn Annals under Dong Zhongshu; he proved brilliant and quick.
entries.literal: By edict ordered to follow Palace Grandee Dong Zhongshu to receive Chunqiu—high talent and thorough clarity.

entries.zh: 遷侍中中郎，坐法免。
entries.en: He rose to gentleman-of-the-household in attendance, then lost his post for a legal offense.
entries.literal: Promoted to palace attendant gentleman-of-the-household; sat on law dismissed.

entries.zh: 上書謝罪，願養馬黃門，上不許。
entries.en: He begged to work off his guilt as a stable hand in the Yellow Gate office; the emperor refused.
entries.literal: Submitted memorial apologizing for crime, wished to groom horses at Yellow Gate; the Emperor did not permit.

entries.zh: 後願守塞扞寇難，復不許。
entries.en: He next volunteered for frontier garrison duty and was refused again.
entries.literal: Later wished to guard border and ward off bandit hardship—again not permitted.

entries.zh: 久之，上疏願擊匈奴，詔問狀，壽王對良善，復召為郎。
entries.en: Long afterward he offered a plan to strike the Xiongnu; the court questioned him, liked his answers, and restored him as gentleman.
entries.literal: After a long time, submitted memorial wishing to strike Xiongnu; edict asked his situation; Shouwang answered well and good; again summoned as gentleman.

entries.zh: 稍遷，會東郡盜賊起，拜為東郡都尉。
entries.en: He rose step by step until banditry flared in Dong commandery and he was named its chief commandant.
entries.literal: Gradually promoted; it happened Dong commandery arose robbers and bandits; appointed Dong commandery chief commandant.

entries.zh: 上以壽王為都尉，不復置太守。
entries.en: Because he held that military post, no civil governor was appointed over him.
entries.literal: The Emperor because Shouwang was chief commandant, did not again appoint grand governor.

entries.zh: 是時，軍旅數發，年歲不熟，多盜賊。
entries.en: Years of bad harvests and constant levies had filled the roads with outlaws.
entries.literal: At that time, armies repeatedly issued, years and harvests not ripe, many robbers and bandits.

entries.zh: 詔賜壽王璽書曰：「子在朕前之時，知略輻湊，以為天下少雙，海內寡二。
entries.en: A sealed rescript rebuked him: "At our side your counsel seemed unique under heaven—scarcely a second man in the seas.
entries.literal: Edict granted Shouwang sealed letter, saying: 'When you were before Us, plans and strategies gathered like wheel spokes—we thought under heaven you had no pair, within the seas scarcely two.

entries.zh: 及至連十餘城之守，任四千石之重，職事並廢，盜賊從橫，甚不稱在前時，何也？」
entries.en: Yet you hold a dozen cities and a four-thousand-bushel salary while bandits run wild—nothing like the man we knew. Why?'
entries.literal: Yet reaching connecting over ten cities' defense, bearing four-thousand-shi's weight, duties and tasks together abandoned, robbers and bandits raging criss-cross—very not matching what was before—why?'

entries.zh: 壽王謝罪，因言其狀。
entries.en: Shouwang kowtowed and explained his difficulties.
entries.literal: Shouwang apologized for crime, thereby stated his situation.

entries.zh: 書奏，上以難丞相弘。
entries.en: When the memorial reached him, the emperor threw it in Gongsun Hong's teeth.
entries.literal: When the writing was submitted, the Superior used it to challenge Chancellor Hong.

entries.zh: 弘詘服焉。
entries.en: Hong conceded defeat.
entries.literal: Hong was refuted and submitted.

entries.zh: 臣聞長老言，秦之時嘗使尉屠睢擊越，又使監祿鑿渠通道。
entries.en: The old men remember how Qin sent Commandant Tu Sui against Yue and Overseer Lu to cut a supply canal.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard the elders say that in Qin times they once sent Commandant Tu Sui to strike Yue, and again sent Overseer Lu to chisel a canal and open a road.

entries.zh: 越人逃入深山林叢，不可得攻。
entries.en: The Yue melted into the jungle where no army could root them out.
entries.literal: The Yue people fled into deep mountain forest thickets; they could not be attacked.

entries.zh: 留軍屯守空地，曠日引久，士卒勞倦，越出擊之。
entries.en: Qin camps sat on barren ground until the troops were spent; then Yue struck from the green dark.
entries.literal: The army stayed to garrison and guard empty land; days stretched long; soldiers and foot were weary; Yue came out and struck them.

entries.zh: 秦兵大破，乃發適戍以備之。
entries.en: The Qin host was shattered; only transported convicts could hold the line.
entries.literal: Qin soldiers were greatly broken; then they issued transported garrisons to guard them.

entries.zh: 當此之時，外內騷動，百姓靡敝，行者不還，往者莫反，皆不聊生，亡逃相從，群為盜賊，於是山東之難始興。
entries.en: Empire and frontier convulsed together; farmers were bled white; men marched and never came home. Despair bred banditry, and the great rebellions east of the passes began with that southern war.
entries.literal: At this time outer and inner were in turmoil, the hundred surnames worn out; those who marched did not return, those who went did not come back—all could not sustain life; fleeing and escaping followed one another, in groups becoming robbers and bandits; then the troubles east of the mountains first arose.

entries.zh: 此老子所謂「師之所處，荊棘生之」者也。
entries.en: This is what Laozi called 'where the army stays, brambles grow.'
entries.literal: This is what Laozi called 'where the army stays, brambles grow.'

entries.zh: 兵者凶事，一方有急，四面皆從。
entries.en: War is ill luck; trouble in one corner pulls the four quarters into flame.
entries.literal: Arms are a baleful affair; when one quarter has urgency, on four sides all follow.

entries.zh: 臣恐變故之生，奸邪之作，由此始也。
entries.en: Your servant fears that coups and treason will take their start from this very campaign.
entries.literal: Your servant fears changes' arising, treachery's arising, begin from this.

entries.zh: 《周易》曰：「高宗伐鬼方，三年而克之。」
entries.en: The Changes says: 'Gaozong campaigned against Guifang, in three years then overcame them.'
entries.literal: The Changes says: 'Gaozong campaigned against Guifang, in three years then overcame them.'

entries.zh: 鬼方，小蠻夷；
entries.en: Guifang was a petty border tribe;
entries.literal: Guifang was a small Man-Yi;

entries.zh: 高宗，殷之盛天子也。
entries.en: Gaozong was a Son of Heaven at the zenith of Yin power.
entries.literal: Gaozong was Yin at its flourishing Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 以盛天子伐小蠻夷，三年而後克，言用兵之不可不重也。
entries.en: Yet even a peak Son of Heaven needed three years to crush a fly-speck tribe—so heavy is the burden of arms.
entries.literal: To use a flourishing Son of Heaven to attack a small Man-Yi, yet after three years then overcome—this speaks of raising troops as not to be treated lightly.

entries.zh: 陛下臨天下，布德施惠，緩刑罰，薄賦斂，哀鰥寡，恤孤獨，養耆老，振匱乏，盛德上隆，和澤下洽，近者親附，遠者懷德，天下攝然，人安其生，自以沒身不見兵革。
entries.en: You have faced the realm with mercy—lighter taxes, gentler punishments, grain for the widow and the orphan, care for the old, relief for the hungry. Your virtue has climbed to Heaven and your kindness soaked the earth. Neighbors cling to you; distant peoples cherish your name. The empire has stood at peace; folk expected never to see war in their days.
entries.literal: Your Majesty faces all under Heaven, spreads virtue and extends favor, relaxes punishments and fines, lightens levies, pities widowers and widows, cares for orphans and the alone, nurtures the aged, relieves the destitute—supreme virtue ascends in splendor, harmonizing grace spreads below and soaks all; the near attach in kinship, the distant cherish your virtue; all under Heaven is orderly; men rest secure in their lives, themselves thinking they would never in life see arms and armour.

entries.zh: 今聞有司舉兵將以誅越，臣安竊為陛下重之。
entries.en: Now I hear that the ministries are marching an army against Yue. Your servant considers the matter grave in the extreme.
entries.literal: Now I hear the offices raise troops about to punish Yue; your servant An privately for Your Majesty esteems this weighty.

entries.zh: 越，方外之地，劗髮文身之民也。
entries.en: Yue lies outside the civilized pale; its people crop their hair, ink their skin, and obey other laws than ours.
entries.literal: Yue is a land beyond the square, a people of cut-hair and tattooed bodies.

entries.zh: 不可以冠帶之國法度理也。
entries.en: The statutes of a cap-and-girdle kingdom will not rule them.
entries.literal: One cannot use cap-and-girdle state's laws and measures to govern it.

entries.zh: 自三代之盛，胡越不與受正朔，非強弗能服，威弗能制也，以為不居之地，不牧之民，不足以煩中國也。
entries.en: Even at the height of the Three Dynasties the Hu and Yue did not take the imperial calendar—not because armies could not cow them, but because the sages judged their marshes and jungles unworthy of the central plain's trouble.
entries.literal: From the Three Dynasties' flourishing, Hu and Yue did not join in receiving the corrected first month—not because force could not subdue them or awe could not control them, but because they were thought unoccupied lands and ungoverned peoples, not worth troubling the central states.

entries.zh: 故古者封內甸服，封外侯服，侯衛賓服，蠻夷要服，戎狄荒服，遠近勢異也。
entries.en: Hence the old concentric scheme: the royal domain within the feudal ring, then the lords' belt, then the guest states, then the cord-wrapped barbarians, then the wild outer tribes—each tier farther from the center and looser in its tie.
entries.literal: Therefore in olden times within the enfeoffment was the royal domain; outside the enfeoffment was the lords' service; the lords' guard was guest service; the Man and Yi were the cord service; the Rong and Di were the wild service—far and near, their power differed.

entries.zh: 自漢初定已來七十二年，吳越人相攻擊者不可勝數，然天子未嘗舉兵而入其地也。
entries.en: In the seventy-two years since Gaozu founded the dynasty, Wu and Yue have torn at each other times without number, yet no emperor has marched the imperial host into their hills.
entries.literal: From Han's first settling until now seventy-two years, the people of Wu and Yue have attacked one another beyond counting, yet the Son of Heaven has never raised troops and entered their lands.

entries.zh: 及至高皇帝定天下，略地於邊，聞匈奴聚代谷之外而欲擊之。
entries.en: When Gaozu had pacified the realm he surveyed the north, heard the Xiongnu massing beyond Dai, and meant to strike.
entries.literal: When it reached the August Ancestor settling all under Heaven, surveying lands on the border, he heard the Xiongnu gathered beyond Dai Valley and wished to strike them.

entries.zh: 御史成諫曰：「不可。
entries.en: Censor Cheng warned: "Do not march.
entries.literal: Censor Cheng remonstrated, saying: 'Not permissible.

entries.zh: 夫匈奴，獸聚而鳥散，從之如搏景，今以陛下盛德攻匈奴，臣竊危之。」
entries.en: They herd like beasts and scatter like birds; chasing them is like wrestling a shadow. Even your majesty's might cannot safely bite that bait.'
entries.literal: The Xiongnu—beasts herd and birds scatter; following them is like grappling a shadow. Now to attack the Xiongnu with Your Majesty's flourishing virtue—your servant privately fears it.'

entries.zh: 高帝不聽，遂至代谷，果有平城之圍。
entries.en: Gaozu would not listen; he reached Dai and walked into the siege at Pingcheng.
entries.literal: High Ancestor did not listen; then reached Dai Valley, indeed had the Pingcheng siege.

entries.zh: 高帝悔之，乃使劉敬往結和親，然後天下亡干戈之事。
entries.en: He rued the day, sent Liu Jing to seal a marriage alliance, and the realm knew peace again.
entries.literal: High Ancestor repented it; then sent Liu Jing to tie cordial kinship—afterward all under Heaven had no spear-and-halberd affairs.

entries.zh: 是時，徐樂、嚴安亦俱上書言世務。
entries.en: About the same time Xu Le and Yan An also filed memorials on state affairs.
entries.literal: At that time Xu Le and Yan An also together submitted memorials speaking of worldly tasks.

entries.zh: 書奏，上召見三人，謂曰：「公皆安在？
entries.en: When the three memorials arrived, the emperor received them together and cried: "Where have you men been hiding?
entries.literal: When the writings were submitted, the Superior summoned audience with the three men, saying: 'Where have you gentlemen been?

entries.zh: 何相見之晚也！」
entries.en: Why am I meeting you only now!"
entries.literal: Why meet so late!'

entries.zh: 乃拜偃、樂、安皆為郎中。
entries.en: He named Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, and Yan An gentlemen-of-the-household on the spot.
entries.literal: Then he appointed Yan, Le, and An all gentlemen-of-the-household.

entries.zh: 偃數上疏言事，遷謁事、中郎、中大夫。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan poured in further memorials and rose through ye-shi and gentleman-of-the-household to palace grandee.
entries.literal: Yan repeatedly submitted memorials speaking of affairs, was promoted to ye-shi, gentleman-of-the-household, palace grandee.

entries.zh: 歲中四遷。
entries.en: He jumped four grades in a single year.
entries.literal: Within a year four promotions.

entries.zh: 偃說上曰：「古者諸侯地不過百里，強弱之形易制。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan urged the throne: "In antiquity no fief passed a hundred li across—strong and weak were easy to balance.
entries.literal: Yan persuaded the Superior, saying: 'In old days feudal lords' land did not exceed a hundred li—strong and weak forms easy to control.

entries.zh: 今諸侯或連城數十，地方千里。
entries.en: Today some kings hold dozens of cities and a thousand li of ground.
entries.literal: Now feudal lords sometimes connect cities by tens, territory a thousand li square.

entries.zh: 緩則驕奢易為淫亂；
entries.en: Leave them idle and they turn proud and dissolute;
entries.literal: If relaxed then arrogant and extravagant, easy to become debauched and chaotic;

entries.zh: 急則阻其強而合從以逆京師。
entries.en: squeeze them and they league their strength and turn against the imperial capital.
entries.literal: if pressed then they block their strength and join in horizontal alliance to rebel against the capital.

entries.zh: 今以法割削，則逆節萌起，前日朝錯是也。
entries.en: Cut them by naked law and they revolt—Chao Cuo proved that only yesterday.
entries.literal: Now if you use law to slice them, then contrary conduct sprouts—Chao Cuo of the other day is the example.

entries.zh: 今諸侯子弟或十數，而適嗣代立，余雖骨肉，無尺地之封，則仁孝之道不宣。
entries.en: A king may have ten sons, yet only the heir inherits; the rest, though bone of his bone, get not an inch of soil—so kindness and filial duty wither.
entries.literal: Now feudal lords' sons and younger brothers sometimes number ten or more, yet the heir alone inherits; the rest though flesh and bone receive no fief of a foot of land—thus benevolence and filial piety's way is not proclaimed.

entries.zh: 願陛下令諸侯得推恩分子弟，以地侯之。
entries.en: Command every prince to divide his domain among sons and brothers and enfeoff them as marquises.
entries.literal: May Your Majesty order the feudal lords able to extend grace dividing sons and younger brothers, enfeoffing them with land as marquises.

entries.zh: 彼人人喜得所願，上以德施，實分其國。
entries.en: Each child wins a title while you seem only generous—in truth you slice their kingdoms thin.
entries.literal: Each person rejoices at obtaining his wish; above you spread virtue, in fact you divide their states.

entries.zh: 必稍自銷弱矣。」
entries.en: In a generation they will dwindle of themselves.'
entries.literal: They will gradually self-weaken.'

entries.zh: 於是上從其計。
entries.en: The emperor adopted the policy that history calls the extended grace edict.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Superior followed his plan.

entries.zh: 又說上曰：「茂陵初立，天下豪桀兼並之家，亂眾民，皆可徙茂陵，內實京師，外銷奸猾，此所謂不誅而害除。」
entries.en: He next urged removal of the rich and overmighty to the new tomb town at Maoling—strengthening the capital while draining the provinces of troublemakers without a headsman's axe.'
entries.literal: Again he persuaded the Superior, saying: 'Maoling first established—all under Heaven's bold and predatory families who upset the masses may be moved to Maoling—inner to solidify the capital, outer to melt away knaves—this is called removing harm without executions.'

entries.zh: 上又從之。
entries.en: The throne agreed again.
entries.literal: The Superior again followed it.

entries.zh: 偃盛言朔方地肥饒，外阻河，蒙恬城以逐匈奴，內省轉輸戍漕，廣中國，滅胡之本也。
entries.en: He pressed the case for Shuofang: "fat soil shielded by the Yellow River, Meng Tian's old rampart against the Xiongnu, shorter supply lines, and a broader heartland—the true lever for breaking the steppe."
entries.literal: Yan strongly spoke of Shuofang's land being fertile and rich, outwardly blocked by the river, Meng Tian's wall to chase the Xiongnu, inwardly saving transport, garrison, and canal costs, expanding the central states—the root of destroying the Hu.

entries.zh: 上覽其說，下公卿議，皆言不便。
entries.en: The emperor circulated his plan; the high ministers voted it down.
entries.literal: The Superior read his theory, sent it down to duke ministers for discussion; all said it was not convenient.

entries.zh: 公孫弘曰：「秦時嘗發三十萬眾築北河，終不可就，已而棄之。」
entries.en: Gongsun Hong objected: "Qin once threw three hundred thousand lives at the northern river works and gave up when the ditch would not hold."
entries.literal: Gongsun Hong said: 'In Qin times they once issued three hundred thousand multitudes to build the northern river; in the end it could not be completed; afterward they abandoned it.'

entries.zh: 朱買臣難詘弘，遂置朔方，本偃計也。
entries.en: Zhu Maichen demolished Hong in debate, and Shuofang was founded on Yan's design after all.
entries.literal: Zhu Maichen refuted and shamed Hong; thereupon they established Shuofang—the root was Yan's plan.

entries.zh: 元朔中，偃言齊王內有淫失之行，上拜偃為齊相。
entries.en: During Yuanshuo he denounced the king of Qi for incest and depravity; the emperor named him chancellor of Qi to deal with it.
entries.literal: In Yuanshuo, Yan spoke of the Prince of Qi having debauched misconduct within; the Superior appointed Yan as chancellor of Qi.

entries.zh: 至齊，遍召昆弟賓客，散五百金予之，數曰：「始吾貧時，昆弟不我衣食，賓客不我內門。
entries.en: In Qi he called in kinsmen and hangers-on, flung five hundred pounds of gold on the table, and snarled: "When I starved, you gave me neither bread nor roof; you would not even let me past your gates.
entries.literal: Arriving at Qi, he everywhere summoned brothers and guests, scattered five hundred jin of gold to them, scolded, saying: 'At first when I was poor, brothers did not clothe and feed me, guests did not admit me inside the gate.

entries.zh: 今吾相齊，諸君迎我或千里。
entries.en: Now that I wear the seal of Qi, you ride a thousand li to smile in my face.
entries.literal: Now I am chancellor of Qi—you gentlemen welcomed me perhaps a thousand li.

entries.zh: 吾與諸君絕矣，毋復入偃之門！」
entries.en: The bond is cut. Never darken my threshold again!'
entries.literal: I break with you gentlemen; do not again enter Yan's gate!'

entries.zh: 乃使人以王與姊奸事動王。
entries.en: He then leaked word of the king's incest with his own half-sister to break his nerve.
entries.literal: Then he sent men to move the king with the affair of the king's illicit relations with his elder sister.

entries.zh: 王以為終不得脫，恐效燕王論死，乃自殺。
entries.en: The king saw no way out, dreaded the block like the late king of Yan, and opened his own veins.
entries.literal: The king thought in the end he could not escape, feared sharing the King of Yan's fate of ordered execution, then killed himself.

entries.zh: 偃始為布衣時，嘗游燕、趙，及其貴，發燕事。
entries.en: Zhufu Yan had once begged his bread in Yan and Zhao; once risen, he repaid Yan by exposing its secrets.
entries.literal: When Yan at first was common cloth, he once wandered Yan and Zhao; when he became noble, he exposed Yan's affairs.

entries.zh: 趙王恐其為國患，欲上書言其陰事，為居中，不敢發。
entries.en: The king of Zhao meant to memorialize his crimes but dared not move while Yan held the emperor's ear.
entries.literal: The King of Zhao feared that Yan would become a calamity to his state and wished to submit a memorial exposing Yan's secret affairs, but because Yan remained at the center of power, he did not dare send it.

entries.zh: 及其為齊相，出關，即使人上書，告偃受諸侯金，以故諸侯子多以得封者。
entries.en: The moment Yan left for Qi, Zhao's agents accused him of taking bribes from princes to push their sons' titles.
entries.literal: When he became chancellor of Qi and passed out of the passes, he immediately sent men to submit a memorial accusing Yan of receiving feudal lords' gold, whereby many feudal lords' sons obtained enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 及齊王以自殺聞，上大怒，以為偃劫其王令自殺，乃征下吏治。
entries.en: News of the suicide enraged the emperor; he believed Yan had hounded the king to death and threw him to the jailers.
entries.literal: When Qi's king's suicide was heard, the Superior was greatly angry, thought Yan had coerced his king ordering suicide, then summoned and handed him down to clerks for trial.

entries.zh: 偃服受諸侯之金，實不劫齊王令自殺。
entries.en: Yan admitted the bribes but swore he never drove the king to suicide.
entries.literal: Yan confessed receiving feudal lords' gold; in truth he did not coerce the Qi king ordering suicide.

entries.zh: 上欲勿誅，公孫弘爭曰：「齊王自殺無後，國除為郡，入漢，偃本首惡，非誅偃無以謝天下。」
entries.en: The emperor would have spared him, but Hong insisted: "Qi is now a commandery without an heir because of Yan. He is the author of the crime; spare him and you cannot face the realm."
entries.literal: The Superior wished not to execute; Gongsun Hong disputed, saying: 'The Qi king's suicide left no heir; the state was removed and became a commandery, incorporated into Han—Yan was originally the chief evil; if not executing Yan, there is no means to apologize to all under Heaven.'

entries.zh: 乃遂族偃。
entries.en: The whole Zhufu clan went to the sword.
entries.literal: Thereupon they exterminated Yan by kin-clan.

entries.zh: 偃方貴幸時，客以千數，及族死，無一人視，獨孔車收葬焉。
entries.en: Thousands feasted at his gate while he flourished; when he fell, only Kong Che dared bury the bones.
entries.literal: When Yan was noble and favored, guests numbered in the thousands; when the kin-clan died, not one person looked in—only Kong Che collected and buried him.

entries.zh: 上聞之，以車為長者。
entries.en: Learning of it, the emperor praised Kong Che as a gentleman of the old school.
entries.literal: The Superior heard it and deemed Che a man of mature decency.

entries.zh: 臣聞明主不惡切諫以博觀，忠臣不避重誅以直諫，是故事無遺策而功流萬世。
entries.en: A wise ruler welcomes blunt counsel to widen his sight; a loyal minister risks the axe to speak truth—then no policy is half-formed and fame lasts ten thousand years.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that a clear ruler does not dislike cutting remonstrance to broaden his view; a loyal subject does not avoid heavy execution to remonstrate straight—therefore affairs leave no neglected plans and merit flows to ten thousand generations.

entries.zh: 今臣不敢隱忠避死，以效愚計，願陛下幸赦而少察之。
entries.en: I dare not choose safety over loyalty; I lay a rough plan before you and beg you to weigh it with care.
entries.literal: Now your servant dares not hide loyalty nor avoid death to present a foolish plan—may Your Majesty deign to pardon and slightly examine it.

entries.zh: 故兵法曰：「興師十萬，日費千金。」
entries.en: The canon says: "A hundred thousand men in the field devour a thousand in gold each day."
entries.literal: Therefore the military writings say: 'Raising a host of a hundred thousand costs a thousand gold a day.'

entries.zh: 秦常積眾數十萬人，雖有覆軍殺將，系虜單于，適足以結怨深仇，不足以償天下之費。
entries.en: Qin hurled hundreds of thousands north; even when it shattered hosts, slew generals, and dragged the chanyu in chains, the gain was a deeper grudge, never worth the price in blood and treasure.
entries.literal: Qin constantly piled multitudes of several hundred thousand; though they overturned armies, killed generals, tied the chanyu captive—it was sufficient only to knot deep hatred, not sufficient to repay all under Heaven's expense.

entries.zh: 夫匈奴行盜侵驅，所以為業，天性固然。
entries.en: Raiding is how the Xiongnu live—it is their nature.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu raid, drive, invade—that by which they make their livelihood; by nature it is thus.

entries.zh: 上自虞、夏、殷、周，固不程督，禽獸畜之，不比為人。
entries.en: From Shun through Zhou no sage tried to govern them like Chinese farmers—they were herded as the wild creatures beyond the pale.
entries.literal: From above Shun, Xia, Yin, Zhou—they certainly did not regulate and supervise them like people; they pastured them like birds and beasts, not comparing them to people.

entries.zh: 夫不上觀虞、夏、殷、周之統，而下循近世之失，此臣之所以大恐，百姓所疾苦也。
entries.en: Ignore the mirror of antiquity and repeat Qin's blunder—that is what I dread, and what the people cannot endure.
entries.literal: Not to look up at Shun, Xia, Yin, Zhou's order, yet to follow down on recent ages' failures—this is why your servant greatly fears it, what the hundred surnames bitterly suffer.

entries.zh: 且夫兵久則變生，事苦則慮易。
entries.en: Prolonged war breeds mutiny; exhausted people change masters.
entries.literal: Moreover when arms drag on, change arises; when affairs are bitter, thoughts shift.

entries.zh: 使邊境之民靡敝愁苦，將吏相疑而外市，故尉佗、章邯得成其私，而秦政不行，權分二子，此得失之效也。
entries.en: When border folk are broken and generals sell secrets across the line, men like Zhao Tuo of the south and Zhang Han of Qin seize their chance—central command frays while power splits between traitors. That is the lesson of gain and loss.
entries.literal: If you make border people worn out and grieving, generals and clerks suspect each other and traffic with the enemy outside, therefore Zhao Tuo and Zhang Han could accomplish their private aims, and Qin government did not proceed, power split between two men—this is the proof of gain and loss.

entries.zh: 故《周書》曰：「安危在出令，存亡在所用。」
entries.en: The Zhou Documents says: "Order makes safety or peril; men make survival or ruin."
entries.literal: Therefore the Zhou Documents says: 'Safety and peril lie in what orders issue; survival and destruction lie in whom you employ.'

entries.zh: 願陛下孰計之而加察焉。
entries.en: Weigh these words, sire, with the utmost care.
entries.literal: May Your Majesty carefully calculate and add your scrutiny.

entries.zh: 間者，關東五穀數不登，年歲未復，民多窮困，重之以邊境之事，推數循理而觀之，民宜有不安其處者矣。
entries.en: Lately the east has seen repeated crop failure; the people are still on their knees, and the frontier levies press them harder. By every reckoning, many no longer feel at home in their own fields.
entries.literal: Of late east of the passes the five grains repeatedly did not rise; years are not yet recovered; the people are much poor and trapped; heavily added to this are border affairs—pushing numbers and following pattern to view it, the people ought to have those not at peace in their place.

entries.zh: 不安故易動，易動者，土崩之勢也。
entries.en: Restless men are quick to rise—that is the landslide from below.
entries.literal: Not being at peace, therefore they are easy to stir; what is easy to stir is the earthen-collapse situation.

entries.zh: 故賢主獨觀萬化之原，明於安危之機，修之廟堂之上，而銷未形之患也。
entries.en: The wise king reads the root of change, senses where safety turns to peril, and heals the wound in council before blood flows in the lanes.
entries.literal: Therefore the worthy ruler alone views the source of the myriad transformations, is clear on the triggers of safety and peril, repairs them above the temple hall, and melts away calamity before it takes shape.

entries.zh: 其要，期使天下無土崩之勢而已矣。
entries.en: His whole aim is to keep that soil from shifting—nothing more.
entries.literal: Its essential: hope only to cause all under Heaven to have no earthen-collapse situation—that is all.

entries.zh: 故雖有強國勁兵，陛下逐走獸，射飛鳥，弘游燕之囿，淫從恣之觀，極馳騁之樂，自若。
entries.en: Then, though rival kingdoms arm to the teeth, you may hunt, feast, and race your chariots across the imperial parks and still sleep sound.
entries.literal: Therefore though there be strong states and tough troops, Your Majesty may chase running beasts, shoot flying birds, enlarge the roaming hunting park, indulge the following and reckless spectacles, exhaust the pleasure of galloping and hunting—and remain at ease.

entries.zh: 金石絲竹之聲不絕於耳，帷幄之私、俳優侏儒之笑不乏於前，而天下無宿憂。
entries.en: Music may ring without end, jesters caper in your curtains—yet the realm will carry no smoldering overnight grudge.
entries.literal: Metal, stone, silk, and bamboo sounds do not cease in the ear; curtain privacy, jesters' and dwarfs' laughter is not lacking before you—and all under Heaven has no overnight stored worry.

entries.zh: 名何必夏、子，俗何必成、康！
entries.en: You need not yet rival Yu and Tang in fame, nor Cheng and Kang in the purity of your age.
entries.literal: Why must one's name necessarily equal those of Yu and Tang? Why must customs necessarily equal those of Cheng and Kang!

entries.zh: 雖然，臣竊以陛下天然之質，寬仁之資，而誠以天下為務，則不難侔，而成、康之俗未必不復興也。
entries.en: Yet given your natural breadth of mind, if you make the people's peace your daily work, you may yet rival the sage founders, and the age of Cheng and Kang may rise again.
entries.literal: Although it is so, your servant privately thinks that with Your Majesty's heaven-endowed substance and generous benevolent endowment, if you sincerely take all under Heaven as your task, then it is not hard to equal them, and Cheng and Kang's customs may not fail to revive.

entries.zh: 此二體者立，然後處尊安之實，揚廣譽於當世，親天下而服四夷，余恩遺德為數世隆，南面背依攝袂而揖王公，此陛下之所服也。
entries.en: Set those two safeguards in place and you sit in true majesty, win the age's praise, fold the four quarters beneath you, and leave your sons a fortune of kindness—facing south with your back to the embroidered screen, you may gather your sleeves and nod to kings and dukes as your vassals. That is the robe that fits you.
entries.literal: When these two forms are established, then you dwell in the substance of honored safety, raise broad fame in the present age, treat all under Heaven as kin and subdue the four barbarians; remaining grace and left virtue become several generations' flourishing; facing south with back to the patterned screen, gathering your sleeve and bowing to kings and dukes—this is what Your Majesty should take as your garment.

entries.zh: 臣聞圖王不成，其敝足以安。
entries.en: They say: Aim at kingcraft and fall short—you still win stability.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard: diagramming kingship, if not successful, its exhaustion is still enough for peace.

entries.zh: 安則陛下何求而不得，何威而不成，奚征而不服哉？
entries.en: With stability, whatever you seek is yours, whatever awe you raise is obeyed—what foe would refuse to bend?
entries.literal: If there is peace, then what Your Majesty seeks cannot fail to be obtained, what awe cannot fail to be accomplished—what campaign would not submit?

entries.zh: 臣聞天下之患，在於土崩，不在瓦解，古今一也。
entries.en: I have heard that the true peril of the realm is a landslide from below, not a crack in the roof tiles—the law holds for every age.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that all under Heaven's calamity lies in earthen collapse, not in tile collapse—ancient and modern are one.

entries.zh: 何謂土崩？
entries.en: What do I mean by a landslide from below?
entries.literal: What is called earthen collapse?

entries.zh: 秦之末世是也。
entries.en: The fall of Qin is the model.
entries.literal: Qin's last generation is the case.

entries.zh: 陳涉無千乘之尊、疆土之地，身非王公大人名族之後，無鄉曲之譽，非有孔、曾、墨子之賢，陶朱、猗頓之富也。
entries.en: Chen She owned no kingdom, no famous name, no village cheering him on—he was no sage and no millionaire.
entries.literal: Chen She had no thousand-chariot honor, no strong state's territory; his person was not heir of high king or great man's famous clan; he had no village praise; he had not Confucius', Zengzi's, or Mozi's worth, nor Tao Zhu's or Yi Dun's wealth.

entries.zh: 然起窮巷，奮棘矜，偏袒大呼，天下從風，此其故何也？
entries.en: Yet he rose from a ditch with a hoe handle in his fist, bared a shoulder, gave one cry, and the empire answered like wind—why?
entries.literal: Yet he rose from a poor alley, brandished a thorn-wood staff, bared one shoulder and shouted; all under Heaven followed like wind—what was the cause of this?

entries.zh: 由民困而主不恤，下怨而上不知，俗已亂而政不修，此三者陳涉之所以為資也。
entries.en: Because the people were desperate and the ruler felt nothing, because anger seethed below while the court slept, because order had rotted before the laws were mended—those three truths were Chen She's opening.
entries.literal: Because the people were trapped while the lord showed no pity, below resented while above did not know, customs were already chaotic while government was not cultivated—these three were what Chen She used as his capital.

entries.zh: 此之謂土崩。
entries.en: That is what I call a landslide from below.
entries.literal: This is called earthen collapse.

entries.zh: 故曰天下之患在乎土崩。
entries.en: So the deadliest danger is always that landslide from below.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said all under Heaven's calamity lies in earthen collapse.

entries.zh: 何謂瓦解？
entries.en: What do I mean by a crack in the tiles?
entries.literal: What is called tile collapse?

entries.zh: 吳、楚、齊、趙之兵是也。
entries.en: The revolt of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao is the model.
entries.literal: The troops of Wu, Chu, Qi, and Zhao are the case.

entries.zh: 七國謀為大逆，號皆稱萬乘之君，帶甲數十萬，威足以嚴其境內，財足以勸其士民，然不能西攘尺寸之地，而身為禽於中原者，此其故何也？
entries.en: Seven kings called themselves equals of the Son of Heaven, mustered hundreds of thousands in mail, had treasure to buy loyalty—yet they never won an inch west of their borders and died in chains in the heartland. Why?
entries.literal: The seven states plotted great treason; each styled himself lord of ten thousand chariots; armoured troops numbered several hundred thousand; awe was enough to awe within their borders, wealth enough to encourage their knights and people—yet they could not west seize an inch of land, and their persons were captured in the central plains—what was the cause of this?

entries.zh: 非權輕於匹夫而兵弱於陳涉也。
entries.en: Not because they were weaker than Chen She.
entries.literal: It was not that their authority was lighter than a commoner's or their arms weaker than Chen She's.

entries.zh: 當是之時，先帝之德未衰，而安土樂俗之民眾，故諸侯無竟外之助。
entries.en: Gaozu's grace still lived in memory, and the common folk clung to home and hearth, so the rebels found no echo in the villages.
entries.literal: At that time the former emperor's virtue had not declined, and people who loved their soil and delighted in custom were many; therefore the feudal lords had no unexpected outside aid.

entries.zh: 此之謂瓦解。
entries.en: That is what I call a crack in the roof tiles—a revolt of the mighty that the throne can mend.
entries.literal: This is called tile collapse.

entries.zh: 故曰天下之患不在瓦解。
entries.en: The lesser danger is that sort of tile-crack rebellion.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said all under Heaven's calamity does not lie in tile collapse.

entries.zh: 卷六十四上 嚴朱吾丘主父徐嚴終王賈傳 第三十三上
entries.en: Chapter 64a: Biographies of Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, Yan An, Zhong Jun, Wang Bao, and Jia Yi (part one).
entries.literal: Scroll sixty-four part A, Treatise thirty-three part A, on Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen, Wuqiu, Zhufu, Xu, Yan, Zhong, Wang, and Jia.

entries.zh: 人臣亦然。
entries.en: The same holds for those who serve him.
entries.literal: Ministers to others are also thus.

entries.zh: 昔賢者之未遭遇也，圖事揆策則君不用其謀，陳見悃誠則上不然其信，進仕不得施效，斥逐又非其愆。
entries.en: Before a worthy man meets his moment, the ruler ignores every plan he lays, doubts every pledge of loyalty he offers, denies him office where he might prove himself, and casts him aside for faults that are not his own.
entries.literal: Formerly when worthies had not yet met encounter, in plotting affairs and measuring strategies the lord did not use their plans; in displaying and seeing sincere devotion the superior did not deem their trust true; advancing to office they could not display effect; expulsion and banishment again was not their fault.

entries.zh: 是故伊尹勤於鼎俎，太公困於鼓刀，百里自鬻，甯子飯牛，離此患也。
entries.en: Yi Yin labored over pots and chopping boards; the Grand Duke was reduced to working as a butcher; Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen. In this way they suffered these hardships.
entries.literal: Thus Yi Yin labored at cauldrons and chopping boards, the Grand Duke was reduced to wielding a butcher's knife, Baili Xi sold himself, and Ning Qi fed oxen; thereby they suffered these hardships.

entries.zh: 及其遇明君遭聖主也，運籌合上意，諫諍即見聽，進退得關其忠，任職得行其術，去卑辱奧渫而升本朝，離疏釋蹻而享膏粱，剖符錫壤而光祖考，傳之子孫，以資說士。
entries.en: But let them find an enlightened sovereign, and every stratagem strikes home, every remonstrance wins a hearing, every move displays loyalty, every post lets their policy work. They rise from humble toil to stand in the central court, shed hemp shoes for robes of grain-fed silk, take investiture and fief to bring honor to the ancestors, and hand the credit down to their sons as a lesson to every persuader who waits in the cold.
entries.literal: When they meet a bright lord and encounter a sage master, planning matches the superior's intent, remonstrance is then heard, advance and retreat can connect their loyalty, holding office can enact their methods; they leave base shame and hidden filth and ascend to this court, depart coarse cloth and release straw sandals and enjoy fat and fine millet, split tallies and grant soil and brighten forefathers, transmit to sons and grandsons, thereby supplying persuading knights.

entries.zh: 故世必有聖知之君，而後有賢明之臣。
entries.en: So the age must first produce a sage-king; only then can it produce ministers of true clarity.
entries.literal: Therefore the age must have a sage-and-knowing lord, and afterward there are worthy-and-bright ministers.

entries.zh: 故虎嘯而冽風，龍興而致雲，蟋蟀俟秋吟，蜉蝤出以陰。
entries.en: The tiger's roar summons the biting gale; the dragon's ascent draws the rain clouds; the cricket waits for autumn to sing; the mayfly hatches when the yin ether gathers.
entries.literal: Therefore the tiger roars and biting wind comes; the dragon rises and brings clouds; the cricket waits for autumn to chirp; the mayfly emerges with yin.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：「飛龍在天，利見大人。」
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, 'The dragon flies in the heavens: it furthers one to see the great man.'
entries.literal: The Changes say: 'Flying dragon in the sky—it is favorable to see the great man.'

entries.zh: 《詩》曰：「思皇多士，生此王國。」
entries.en: The Odes sing, 'Splendid host of knights, born for this royal house.'
entries.literal: The Odes say: 'Oh, august many gentlemen, born in this king's state.'

entries.zh: 故世平主聖，俊艾將自至，若堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之君，獲稷、契、皋陶、伊尹、呂望，明明在朝，穆穆列布，聚精會神，相得益章。
entries.en: Thus, in an age of peace under a sage ruler, outstanding elders come of their own accord. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu obtained the service of Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang. Brilliant at court and solemn in their ranks, they joined their finest insights and magnified the glory of ruler and minister alike.
entries.literal: Therefore, when the age is peaceful and the ruler is a sage, outstanding elders arrive of themselves. Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Kings Wen and Wu obtained Hou Ji, Xie, Gao Yao, Yi Yin, and Lü Wang. Brilliant at court and solemnly arrayed, they united their finest insight and spirit, bringing greater splendor to ruler and minister alike.

entries.zh: 雖伯牙操遞鍾，逢門子彎烏號，猶未足以喻其意也。
entries.en: Not even Boya on the Di Zhong harp or Fengmenzi drawing the Wuhao bow could capture the harmony of that meeting.
entries.literal: Even if Boya grasped the Di Zhong zither, Fengmenzi bent the Wuhao bow, still they would not be sufficient to analogize its meaning.

entries.zh: 臣聞堯舜，聖之盛也，禹入聖域而不優，故孔子稱堯曰「大哉」，韶曰「盡善」，禹曰「無間」。
entries.en: Yao and Shun stood at the summit of sagehood; Yu entered that company yet did not surpass them—which is why Confucius called Yao 'magnificent,' the Shao music 'perfect in goodness,' and Yu 'without blemish.'
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that Yao and Shun were the height of sagehood; Yu entered the sage domain yet was not superior; therefore Confucius called Yao 'great indeed,' the Shao 'utterly good,' Yu 'without flaw.'

entries.zh: 以三聖之德，地方不過數千里，被流沙，東漸于海，朔南暨聲教，迄于四海，欲與聲教則治之，不欲與者不彊治也。
entries.en: Even those three sages held only a few thousand li of ground—west to the drifting sands, east to the sea—yet their moral voice reached north and south to the rim of the world. They ruled only those who welcomed their teaching and never forced it on those who did not.
entries.literal: By the virtue of the three sages, their territory was not more than several thousand li square; it covered the shifting sands, east reached to the sea, north and south arrived at sound and instruction, reaching to the four seas; those who wished to share sound and instruction they governed; those who did not wish to share, they did not force to govern.

entries.zh: 故君臣歌德，含氣之物各德其宜。
entries.en: Ruler and ministers could hymn one another's virtue, and every living creature found its proper place.
entries.literal: Therefore lord and ministers sang virtue; things bearing qi each obtained their proper virtue.

entries.zh: 武丁、成王，殷、周之大仁也，然地東不過江、黃，西不過氐、羌，南不過蠻荊，北不過朔方。
entries.en: Wu Ding of Shang and King Cheng of Zhou were paragons of humanity, yet Shang territory reached east only to the Jiang and Huang domains, west only to the Di and Qiang, south only to the Man tribes of Jing, and north only to Shuofang.
entries.literal: Wu Ding and King Cheng were the great benevolence of Yin and Zhou; yet their lands east did not pass Jiang and Huang, west did not pass Di and Qiang, south did not pass Man Jing, north did not pass Shuofang.

entries.zh: 是以頌聲並作，視聽之類咸樂其生，越裳氏重九譯而獻，此非兵革之所能致。
entries.en: Praise filled the air, every creature rejoiced in its life, and the Yueshang people sent tribute through nine relays of interpreters—gifts won by virtue, not by the sword.
entries.literal: Therefore eulogy voices arose together; kinds of seeing and hearing all rejoiced in their lives; the Yueshang clan passed nine interpreters and offered tribute—this is not what arms and leather could bring about.

entries.zh: 及其衰也，南征不還，齊桓捄其難，孔子定其文。
entries.en: In decline, kings marched south and never came home; Duke Huan of Qi had to rescue the house of Zhou, and Confucius fixed its text.
entries.literal: When it came to their decline, the southern expedition did not return; Duke Huan of Qi rescued its difficulty; Confucius fixed its text.

entries.zh: 以至乎秦，興兵遠攻，貪外虛內，務欲廣地，不慮其害。
entries.en: Then came Qin, which launched distant wars, starved the interior to feed ambition, and grabbed land without counting the cost.
entries.literal: Reaching to Qin, it raised troops and attacked far, greedy outside and empty inside, striving to widen territory, not considering its harm.

entries.zh: 然地南不過閩越，北不過太原，而天下潰畔，禍卒在於二世之末，長城之歌至今未絕。
entries.en: Even so Qin never pushed south beyond Min-Yue or north beyond Taiyuan, yet the empire shattered. Calamity struck under the Second Emperor, and the ballad of the Great Wall still haunts us.
entries.literal: Yet Qin's territory extended no farther south than Minyue and no farther north than Taiyuan, and still the realm disintegrated in revolt. Disaster finally came at the end of the Second Emperor's reign, and songs of the Great Wall have not ceased to this day.

entries.zh: 捐之即與興共為薦顯奏，曰：「竊見石顯本山東名族，有禮義之家也。
entries.en: Jia Juanzhi then drafted with Yang Xing a joint memorial praising Shi Xian: 'We observe that Shi Xian springs from a great Shandong lineage, a house schooled in ritual and duty.
entries.literal: Juanzhi thereupon with Xing together composed a memorial recommending Xian, saying: 'We have seen that Shi Xian originally is a famous clan of east of the mountains, a household with ritual and rightness.

entries.zh: 持正六年，未嘗有過，明習於事，敏而疾見，出公門，入私門。
entries.en: For six years he has upheld integrity without a stain, knows every detail of government, is quick and perceptive, and moves straight from the yamen to his private quarters without detour.
entries.literal: Upholding rectitude six years, never having fault, clearly practiced in affairs, keen and quick to appear, out the public gate, in the private gate.

entries.zh: 宜賜爵關內侯，引其兄弟以為諸曹。」
entries.en: He should be ennobled as a marquis within the passes, and his brothers appointed to the chief bureaus.'
entries.literal: It is fitting to grant him rank as marquis within the passes, draw his brothers to be various bureaus.'

entries.zh: 又共為薦興奏，曰：「竊見長安令興，幸得以知名數召見。
entries.en: They also filed a joint memorial for Yang Xing: 'We note that the magistrate of Chang'an has won fame and repeated audiences with Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Again together they composed a memorial recommending Xing, saying: 'We have seen the magistrate of Chang'an, Xing, fortunate enough to become known and repeatedly summoned and seen.

entries.zh: 興事父母有曾氏之孝，事師有顏閔之材，榮名聞於四方。
entries.en: He honors his parents with the devotion of Zeng Shen, serves his teachers with the gifts of Yan Hui and Min Sun, and his good name rings through the realm.
entries.literal: Xing serves father and mother with the Zeng clan's filiality, serves teachers with Yan and Min's talent; glorious name is heard in the four directions.

entries.zh: 明詔舉茂材，列侯以為首。
entries.en: When Your Majesty called for men of outstanding talent, the ranked nobles put him at the head of the list.
entries.literal: On the bright edict summoning outstanding talent, ranked marquises placed him first.

entries.zh: 為長安令，吏民敬鄉，道路皆稱能。
entries.en: As magistrate of Chang'an he commands the reverence of officials and commoners alike, and travelers on every road praise his competence.
entries.literal: As magistrate of Chang'an, clerks and people respectfully turn toward him; on the roads all praise his ability.

entries.zh: 觀其下筆屬文，則董仲舒；
entries.en: Judge him by his prose and you find another Dong Zhongshu;
entries.literal: Observe his setting brush and composing text—then Dong Zhongshu;

entries.zh: 進談動辭，則東方生；
entries.en: listen to his wit in conversation and you hear Dongfang Shuo;
entries.literal: advance talk and moving phrases—then Master Dongfang;

entries.zh: 置之爭臣，則汲直；
entries.en: set him among blunt remonstrators and he matches Ji An;
entries.literal: place him among contending ministers—then Ji Zhi;

entries.zh: 用之介冑，則冠軍侯；
entries.en: put him in armor and he rivals the Champion Marquis;
entries.literal: employ him in armor and helmet—then the Champion Marquis;

entries.zh: 施之治民，則趙廣漢；
entries.en: give him a district and he governs like Zhao Guanghan;
entries.literal: apply him to governing the people—then Zhao Guanghan;

entries.zh: 抱公絕私，則尹翁歸。
entries.en: charge him to serve the public and spurn private interest and he is another Yin Wenggui.
entries.literal: embracing public and cutting off private—then Yin Wenggui.

entries.zh: 興兼此六人而有之，守道堅固，執義不回，臨大節而不可奪，國之良臣也，可試守京兆尹。」
entries.en: Yang Xing unites the virtues of all six: he holds fast to principle, bends duty for no man, and cannot be swayed at the moment of truth. He is a pillar of the state and should be appointed acting metropolitan governor.'
entries.literal: Xing combines these six men and possesses them; keeping the Way firm and solid, grasping rightness without turning; facing great norms and not being wrested away—he is the state's good minister; may he be tried as acting Metropolitan Governor.'

entries.zh: 終軍字子雲，濟南人也。
entries.en: Zhong Jun, whose courtesy name was Ziyun, came from Jinan.
entries.literal: Zhong Jun, courtesy name Ziyun, was a man of Jinan.

entries.zh: 少好學，以辯博能屬文聞於郡中。
entries.en: From boyhood he loved study and won countywide renown for wide reading, sharp debate, and a ready pen.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning; by eloquence, breadth, and ability to compose texts he was heard of in the commandery.

entries.zh: 年十八，選為博士弟子。
entries.en: At eighteen he was chosen as a student of the imperial academy.
entries.literal: At age eighteen, he was selected as a disciple of the erudites.

entries.zh: 至府受遣，太守聞其有異材，召見軍，甚奇之，與交結。
entries.en: When he went to the yamen for his travel orders, the grand administrator heard reports of his gifts, called him in, was deeply impressed, and struck up a friendship.
entries.literal: When he arrived at the office to receive dispatch, the grand administrator heard that he had unusual talent, summoned and met Jun, greatly marveled at him, and formed ties with him.

entries.zh: 軍揖太守而去，至長安上書言事。
entries.en: Zhong Jun bowed once to the governor and left for the capital, where he filed a memorial on state policy.
entries.literal: Jun bowed to the grand administrator and departed; he reached Chang'an and submitted a memorial discussing affairs.

entries.zh: 武帝異其文，拜軍為謁者給事中。
entries.en: Emperor Wu was struck by the quality of his prose and named him court herald with standing access to the inner palace.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu marveled at his writing and appointed Jun Herald and Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 嚴安者，臨菑人也。
entries.en: Yan An came from Linzi.
entries.literal: Yan An was a man of Linzi.

entries.zh: 以故丞相史上書，曰：
entries.en: Serving as a clerk who had once worked under the chancellor, he presented a memorial that began:
entries.literal: In the capacity of a former clerk of the chancellor, he submitted a memorial, saying:

entries.zh: 從上幸雍祠五畤，獲白麟，一角而五蹄。
entries.en: He accompanied the sovereign to Yong for the sacrifices at the five shrines, where hunters brought in a white unicorn bearing a single horn and five hooves.
entries.literal: He followed the emperor in visiting Yong to sacrifice at the five altars; they obtained a white unicorn, one horn and five hoofs.

entries.zh: 時又得奇木，其枝旁出，輒復合於木上。
entries.en: About the same time someone presented a freakish tree whose limbs jutted sideways only to fuse back into the trunk.
entries.literal: At the same time they also obtained a strange tree; its branches came out sideways and then again joined together on the tree.

entries.zh: 上異此二物，博謀群臣。
entries.en: The emperor regarded both prodigies as extraordinary and asked his officials for wide-ranging counsel.
entries.literal: The emperor marveled at these two things and broadly consulted the ministers.

entries.zh: 軍上對曰：
entries.en: Zhong Jun responded with a memorial that read:
entries.literal: Jun submitted a reply, saying:

entries.zh: 夫人命初定，萬事草創，及臻六合同風，九州共貫，必待明聖潤色，祖業傳於無窮。
entries.en: At the founding of a house all institutions are rough; only when the six quarters breathe a single culture and the nine regions run on one thread does a truly enlightened sovereign put the finishing polish on them, so the patrimony may pass down without end.
entries.literal: When the mandate of man is first fixed, the myriad things are begun; when it reaches the six directions sharing one wind and the nine provinces sharing one strand, one must await a bright sage to polish, and the ancestral enterprise is transmitted to infinity.

entries.zh: 故周至成王，然後制定，而休徵之應見。
entries.en: The house of Zhou did not complete its statutes until the reign of King Cheng; only then did propitious omens begin to answer its virtue.
entries.literal: Therefore Zhou reached King Cheng, and afterward regulations were fixed, and the response of auspicious signs appeared.

entries.zh: 陛下盛日月之光，垂聖思於勒成，專神明之敬，奉燔瘞於郊宮，獻享之精交神，積和之氣塞明，而異獸來獲，宜矣。
entries.en: Your Majesty outshines sun and moon, bends sage reflection toward perfecting the record, concentrates reverence on the gods, and presents burnt and buried offerings at the suburban shrines until the subtle ether of sacrifice mingles with the spirits and a tide of harmony fills the bright sky. Small wonder strange beasts should present themselves.
entries.literal: Your Majesty flourishes the light of sun and moon, hangs sagely thought on carved completion, devotes reverence to spirits, offers burning and burying at the suburban palace; the essence of offerings and feasting intersects spirits, accumulated harmony qi fills brightness, and strange beasts come to be captured—it is fitting.

entries.zh: 昔武王中流未濟，白魚入於王舟，俯取以燎，群公咸曰「休哉！」
entries.en: Once, when King Wu had not yet finished fording the river, a white fish leaped into his barge; he lifted it out for a burnt offering, and the nobles cried, 'Excellent omen!'
entries.literal: Formerly King Wu, midstream not yet crossed, a white fish entered the king's boat; he bent and took it to burn as offering; the dukes all said, 'Auspicious!'

entries.zh: 今郊祀未見於神祇，而獲獸以饋，此天之所以示饗，而上通之符合也。
entries.en: You have not yet announced the suburban rites to the high gods, yet Heaven sends a beast fit for the altar—clear proof that the spirits accept your worship and that your virtue resonates above.
entries.literal: Now suburban sacrifice has not yet been seen by the spirits, yet a beast was obtained to present as offering—this is what Heaven uses to show feasting, and the tally of communication on high.

entries.zh: 宜因昭時令日，改定告元，苴以白茅於江淮，發嘉號于營丘，以應緝熙，使著事者有紀焉。
entries.en: Seize an auspicious season and day to proclaim a new era name, invest the princes along the Yangzi and Huai with bundles of white rushes, and broadcast a glorious title from Yingqiu, echoing the bright mandate so historians may set it down in good order.
entries.literal: It is fitting to follow the bright season and auspicious day, change and fix the proclamation of the first year, wrap with white rushes at the Yangzi and Huai, issue a fine title at Yingqiu, in order to respond to bright progress, so that those who record affairs have a record.

entries.zh: 對奏，上甚異之，由是改元為元狩。
entries.en: The emperor was so struck by the memorial that he renamed the reign Yuanshou.
entries.literal: When the reply was presented, the emperor greatly marveled at it; thereby the era name was changed to Yuanshou.

entries.zh: 後數月，越地及匈奴名王有率眾來降者，時皆以軍言為中。
entries.en: Within a few months Yue chiefs and noted Xiongnu princes began leading their followers in to surrender—just as Zhong Jun had predicted.
entries.literal: Several months later, in Yue territory and among the Xiongnu famous kings there were those who led crowds to come surrender; at the time all took Jun's words as hitting the mark.

entries.zh: 元鼎中，博士徐偃使行風俗。
entries.en: During the Yuanding era the court scholar Xu Yan was dispatched to inspect local customs.
entries.literal: In the Yuanding period, Erudite Xu Yan was sent to tour customs.

entries.zh: 偃矯制，使膠東、魯國鼓鑄鹽鐵。
entries.en: Xu Yan forged imperial orders and had Jiaodong and Lu cast iron and boil salt on their own.
entries.literal: Yan forged an edict, causing Jiaodong and the state of Lu to smelt and cast salt and iron.

entries.zh: 還，奏事，徙為太常丞。
entries.en: On his return he filed his report and was promoted to assistant director under the Chamberlain for Ceremonials.
