entries.literal: Thereupon Lord Dong was noble and favored; none in the realm did not hear of it.

entries.zh: 郡國狗馬蹴鞠劍客輻湊董氏。
entries.en: Adventurers, athletes, and swordsmen from every commandery flocked to his gate.
entries.literal: From commanderies and kingdoms dog handlers, horse trainers, kickball players, and sword guests converged on the Dong house.

entries.zh: 常從遊戲北宮，馳逐平樂，觀雞鞠之會，角狗馬之足，上大歡樂之。
entries.en: He often joined the emperor at the Northern Palace and Pingle Park for cockfights, dog races, and polo until the sovereign was wild with delight.
entries.literal: He constantly followed in sport at the Northern Palace, raced at Pingle, watched cock-kickball meets, matched dogs and horses—the emperor greatly delighted in it.

entries.zh: 於是上為竇太主置酒宣室，使謁者引內董君。
entries.en: Then the emperor prepared a banquet in the Xuanshi Hall for Grand Princess Dou and ordered Dong Yan brought in.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor set out wine for Grand Princess Dou in the Xuanshi chamber and ordered a herald to lead Lord Dong inside.

entries.zh: 是時，朔陛戟殿下，辟戟而前曰：「董偃有斬罪三，安得入乎？」
entries.en: At that time Shuo with hall halberds below the steps, parted the halberds and stepped forward, saying: "Dong Yan has three beheading crimes—how may he enter?"
entries.literal: At that time Shuo with hall halberds below the steps, parted the halberds and stepped forward, saying: Dong Yan has three beheading crimes—how may he enter?

entries.zh: 上曰：「何謂也？」
entries.en: The emperor said: "What does that mean?"
entries.literal: The emperor said: What does that mean?

entries.zh: 朔曰：「偃以人臣私侍公主，其罪一也。
entries.en: Dongfang Shuo said, "First, as a subject he has privately bedded a princess.
entries.literal: Shuo said, "Yan as a minister privately serves a princess—this is crime one.

entries.zh: 敗男女之化，而亂婚姻之禮，傷王制，其罪二也。」
entries.en: Second, he corrupts moral teaching, violates marriage rites, and wounds the kingly institutions."
entries.literal: He corrupts the transformation of male and female and disorders the rites of marriage, injuring royal regulation—this is crime two."

entries.zh: 陛下富於春秋，方積思於《六經》，留神於王事，馳騖於唐、虞，折節於三代，偃不遵經勸學，反以靡麗為右，奢侈為務，盡狗馬之樂，極耳目之欲，行邪枉之道，逕淫辟之路，是乃國家之大賊，人主之大蜮。
entries.en: Your Majesty is young and should steep yourself in the Six Classics and the models of Yao, Shun, and the Three Dynasties; instead Dong Yan spurns learning, exalts luxury, fills your days with dogs, horses, and sensual delight, and leads you down depraved paths—he is a public scourge and a parasite on the throne.
entries.literal: Your Majesty is rich in spring and autumn, just now gathering thought on the Six Classics, fixing attention on kingly affairs, racing in Yao and Shun, bending the self to the Three Dynasties—yet Yan does not follow the classics to urge study; instead he takes dissipation as right and extravagance as business, exhausts the pleasure of dogs and horses, stretches to the limit the desires of ear and eye, walks crooked and devious paths, treads wanton and perverse roads—this is the great thief of the state, the great slug of the ruler.

entries.zh: 偃為淫首，其罪三也。
entries.en: Third, he is the ringleader of this vice.
entries.literal: Yan is the head of debauchery—this is crime three.

entries.zh: 昔伯姬燔而諸侯憚，奈何乎陛下？
entries.en: Formerly when Lady Bo Ji burned, the feudal lords were awed—what of Your Majesty?
entries.literal: Formerly when Lady Bo Ji burned, the feudal lords were awed—what of Your Majesty?

entries.zh: 上默然不應良久，曰：「吾業以設飲，後而自改。」
entries.en: The emperor was silent and did not answer for a long time, then said: "I have already set the feast; afterward I will myself reform."
entries.literal: The emperor was silent and did not answer for a long time, then said: I have already set the feast; afterward I will myself reform.

entries.zh: 朔曰：「不可。
entries.en: Shuo said: "It cannot.
entries.literal: Shuo said: It cannot.

entries.zh: 夫宣室者，先帝之正處也，非法度之政不得入焉。
entries.en: Xuanshi was the late emperor's formal hall—only lawful business may enter it.
entries.literal: As for Xuanshi, it is the former emperor's correct hall; governance not of law and measure may not enter there.

entries.zh: 故淫亂之漸，其變為篡，是以豎貂為淫而易牙作患，慶父死而魯國全，管、蔡誅而周室安。」
entries.en: When debauchery and disorder are allowed to spread, they end in usurpation. Shu Diao's corruption enabled Yi Ya's treachery; Lu was preserved only after Qingfu died, and the Zhou house was secure only after Guan Shu and Cai Shu were executed."
entries.literal: Thus, the gradual advance of debauchery and disorder ends in usurpation: Shu Diao was debauched and Yi Ya brought disaster; when Qingfu died, Lu was preserved; when Guan Shu and Cai Shu were executed, the Zhou house was secure."

entries.zh: 上曰：「善。」
entries.en: The emperor said: "Good."
entries.literal: The emperor said: Good.

entries.zh: 有詔止，更置酒北宮，引董君從東司馬門。
entries.en: He canceled the Xuanshi feast, moved the party to the Northern Palace, and had Dong Yan enter by the east stable gate.
entries.literal: An edict ordered it stopped; wine was reset at the Northern Palace; Lord Dong was led in by the east stable gate.

entries.zh: 東司馬門更名東交門。
entries.en: That gate was renamed the East Crossing Gate.
entries.literal: The east stable gate was renamed the East Crossing Gate.

entries.zh: 賜朔黃金三十斤。
entries.en: Dongfang Shuo received thirty jin of gold.
entries.literal: Shuo was granted thirty jin of gold.

entries.zh: 董君之寵由是日衰，至年三十而終。
entries.en: Dong Yan's star fell from that day; he died at thirty.
entries.literal: Lord Dong's favor from this daily declined; he reached age thirty and died.

entries.zh: 後數歲，竇太主卒，與董君會葬於霸陵。
entries.en: Years later Grand Princess Dou died and was buried with Dong Yan at Baling.
entries.literal: Several years later Grand Princess Dou died; she was buried together with Lord Dong at Baling.

entries.zh: 是後，公主貴人多逾禮制，自董偃始。
entries.en: Afterward princesses and great ladies routinely overstepped ritual bounds—Dong Yan had shown the way.
entries.literal: After this, princesses and noble persons mostly exceeded ritual regulation—beginning from Dong Yan.

entries.zh: 時，天下侈靡趨末，百姓多離農畝。
entries.en: In those days the realm had turned to luxury and to chasing profit over farming, and many common folk had drifted away from the plow.
entries.literal: At that time, under Heaven there was extravagant wastefulness and a rush toward secondary pursuits, and the common people for the most part left the fields of agriculture.

entries.zh: 上從容問朔：「吾欲化民，豈有道乎？」
entries.en: The emperor asked Shuo in a relaxed tone, "I want to improve the people's ways. Is there a right path to that?"
entries.literal: The emperor, at his ease, asked Shuo: "I wish to transform the people — is there perhaps a Way?"

entries.zh: 朔對曰：「堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武、成、康上古之事，經歷數千載，尚難言也，臣不敢陳。
entries.en: Shuo answered, "The deeds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang lie so far back in time that even after millennia they are hard to discuss clearly; I would not presume to rehearse them here.
entries.literal: Shuo replied, saying: "As for the affairs of high antiquity — Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang — having passed through several thousand years, they are still difficult to speak of; your servant dares not set them forth.

entries.zh: 願近述孝文皇帝之時，當世耆老皆聞見之。
entries.en: Instead I would speak of the reign of Emperor Xiaowen, which the old men still living today actually heard and saw for themselves.
entries.literal: I wish, drawing near, to relate the time of Emperor Xiaowen, whom the venerable elders of the present age all heard of and saw.

entries.zh: 貴為天子，富有四海，身衣弋綈，足履革舄，以韋帶劍，莞蒲為席，兵木無刃，衣縕無文，集上書囊以為殿帷；
entries.en: Though he was exalted as Son of Heaven and possessed wealth as vast as the four seas, he dressed in plain black silk, wore simple leather shoes, girded his sword with a leather strap, sat on mats of rushes, kept wooden practice weapons without edges, wore undyed clothes without ornament, and strung together official document bags to hang as curtains in his hall;
entries.literal: Though honored as Son of Heaven and rich as to possess the four seas, on his body he wore robes of coarse black silk, on his feet he trod leather slippers; with a leather belt he suspended his sword; cattail and rushes served as his mat; weapons were of wood without sharp edges; garments of plain cloth bore no pattern; he gathered memorial document pouches to serve as hall drapes;

entries.zh: 以道德為麗，以仁義為準。
entries.en: He made moral power his finery and benevolence and righteousness his measure.
entries.literal: He took the Way and Virtue as splendor, and benevolence and righteousness as his plumb-line.

entries.zh: 於是天下望風成俗，昭然化之。
entries.en: The whole realm took its cue from him, customs took shape, and the transformation was plain for all to see.
entries.literal: Thereupon under Heaven, gazing upon the wind, customs formed, and they were openly and clearly transformed by it.

entries.zh: 今陛下以城中為小，圖起建章，左鳳闕，右神明，號稱千門萬戶；
entries.en: Today Your Majesty finds the capital too cramped and plans to build Jianzhang Palace: Phoenix Tower to the east, the Hall of Divine Brightness to the west, advertised as a labyrinth of a thousand gates and ten thousand doors;
entries.literal: Now Your Majesty considers the area within the walls small, and plans to raise Jianzhang — Phoenix Tower on the left, Divine Brightness on the right, proclaimed as thousand gates and myriad doors;

entries.zh: 木土衣綺繡，狗馬被繢罽；
entries.en: Timber and plaster are swathed in brocade; hounds and horses wear patterned rugs and tapestries;
entries.literal: Timber and earth are clothed in figured silks; dogs and horses are draped in embroidered felts;

entries.zh: 宮人簪玳瑁，垂珠璣；
entries.en: Palace ladies wear tortoiseshell hairpins and strings of lustrous pearls;
entries.literal: Palace women pin tortoiseshell in their hair and hang pearl pendants;

entries.zh: 設戲車，教馳逐，飾文采，叢珍怪；
entries.en: Trick chariots are staged, people are trained for reckless races, everything glitters with ornament, and wonders are piled everywhere;
entries.literal: They set up trick chariots, teach racing pursuits, adorn with patterns and colors, and heap up rare curiosities;

entries.zh: 撞萬石之鐘，擊雷霆之鼓，作俳優，舞鄭女。
entries.en: Ten-thousand-stone bells are struck, drums roll like thunder, jesters caper, and dancers from Zheng whirl on the stage.
entries.literal: They strike a bell of ten thousand stone capacity, beat drums like thunderclaps, put on jesters and buffoons, and have women of Zheng dance.

entries.zh: 上為淫侈如此，而欲使民獨不奢侈失農，事之難者也。
entries.en: When the ruler indulges in such excess, expecting the common people alone to stay frugal and keep to the fields is asking for the impossible.
entries.literal: For the sovereign to be thus licentious and extravagant, yet wish to make the people alone not extravagant and wasteful and not neglect farming — this is the difficulty of the matter.

entries.zh: 陛下誠能用臣朔之計，推甲乙之帳燔之於四通之衢，卻走馬示不復用，則堯、舜之隆宜可與比治矣。
entries.en: If Your Majesty would truly adopt my plan — haul those ranked curtains into the open crossroads and burn them, retire the racehorses and show the realm they will not be raced again — then Your government might stand comparison with the golden ages of Yao and Shun.
entries.literal: If Your Majesty truly could employ your servant Shuo's plan — roll out the curtains of the first and second ranks and burn them at the crossroads of the four thoroughfares, send the racing horses back and show that they will not be used again — then the loftiness of Yao and Shun could fittingly be matched in good order.

entries.zh: 《易》曰：『正其本，萬事理；
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, "Straighten the root and the myriad affairs fall into line;
entries.literal: The Changes says: "Set straight the root, and the myriad affairs are ordered;

entries.zh: 失之毫釐，差以千里。』
entries.en: miss by a hair's breadth, and you are a thousand miles astray."
entries.literal: Miss it by a hair's breadth, and you err by a thousand li."

entries.zh: 願陛下留意察之。」
entries.en: I ask Your Majesty to weigh these words carefully."
entries.literal: I beg Your Majesty to fix your mind upon this and examine it."

entries.zh: 朔雖詼笑，然時觀察顏色，直言切諫，上常用之。
entries.en: Shuo might banter and joke, but he read the emperor's mood and spoke bluntly when remonstrance was needed; the ruler often took his advice.
entries.literal: Though Shuo jested and laughed, yet he constantly observed facial expressions and with straight words offered cutting remonstrance, and the emperor often employed him.

entries.zh: 自公卿在位，朔皆敖弄，無所為屈。
entries.en: From the highest ministers on down, he teased and needled everyone in power and never humbled himself before them.
entries.literal: From the dukes and ministers in office on down, Shuo in every case treated them with playful irreverence and in nothing bent himself low.

entries.zh: 上以朔口諧辭給，好作問之。
entries.en: The emperor enjoyed quizzing him, for Shuo had a nimble tongue and a ready wit.
entries.literal: Because Shuo's mouth was harmonious and his words quick, the emperor delighted in posing questions to him.

entries.zh: 嘗問朔曰：「先生視朕何如主也？」
entries.en: On one occasion he asked, "Sir, what kind of sovereign do you take me to be?"
entries.literal: He once asked Shuo, saying: "Sir, in your view, what sort of ruler am I?"

entries.zh: 朔對曰：「自唐、虞之隆，成、康之際，未足以諭當世。
entries.en: Shuo answered, "Not even the heights of Yao and Shun's age, nor the peace of King Cheng and King Kang, gives us a fair yardstick for today.
entries.literal: Shuo replied, saying: "From the loftiness of Tang and Yu down to the era of Cheng and Kang — they are not sufficient to illustrate the present age.

entries.zh: 臣伏觀陛下功德，陳五帝之上，在三王之右。
entries.en: From what I have seen, Your Majesty's merit and virtue rise above the Five Thearchs and outshine the Three Kings.
entries.literal: Your servant, prostrate, has observed Your Majesty's merit and virtue: they are arrayed above the Five Thearchs and stand to the right hand of the Three Kings.

entries.zh: 非若此而已，誠得天下賢士，公卿在位咸得其人矣。
entries.en: And it is not mere rhetoric: the realm's finest minds truly serve you, and every high office is filled by the right person.
entries.literal: It is not only thus; truly you have obtained the worthy men of the realm, and those who occupy the offices of duke and minister are all the right men for their posts.

entries.zh: 譬若以周、邵為丞相，孔丘為御史大夫，太公為將軍，畢公高拾遺於後，弁嚴子為衛尉，皋陶為大理，後稷為司農，伊尹為少府，子贛使外國，顏、閔為博士，子夏為太常，益為右扶風，季路為執金吾，契為鴻臚，龍逢為宗正，伯夷為京兆，管仲為馮翊，魯般為將作，仲山甫為光祿，申伯為太僕，延陵季子為水衡，百里奚為典屬國，柳下惠為大長秋，史魚為司直，蘧伯玉為太傅，孔父為詹事，孫叔敖為諸侯相，子產為郡守，王慶忌為期門，夏育為鼎官，羿為旄頭，宋萬為式道候。」
entries.en: Imagine the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao as your chancellors; Confucius as chief censor; the Grand Duke as commander; Duke Bi Gao as court remonstrant; Bian Zhuangzi as captain of the guard; Gao Yao as chief judge; Hou Ji as minister of agriculture; Yi Yin as palace treasurer; Zigong as foreign envoy; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian as court scholars; Zixia as master of rites; Yi as western capital intendant; Zilu as capital commandant; Xie as master of guest ceremonies; Guan Longpeng as keeper of the imperial genealogy; the minister Boyi as metropolitan governor; Guan Zhong as northern capital intendant; Lu Ban as chief engineer; Zhong Shanfu as palace chamberlain; the Earl of Shen as master of the horse; Prince Jizi of Yanling as keeper of parks and waters; Baili Xi as commissioner for dependent peoples; Liuxia Hui as chamberlain to the empress; Shi Yu as censor of conduct; Qu Boyu as grand tutor; Kong Fu as supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao as chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan as commandery governor; Prince Qingji as a palace gate guard; Xia Yu as cauldron officer; Yi the Archer as vanguard officer; and Song Wan as road-clearing scout."
entries.literal: It is as if you had made the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao your chancellors; Confucius your Censor-in-Chief; the Grand Duke your general; Duke Bi Gao your remonstrant at the rear; Bian Zhuangzi your Commandant of the Guards; Gao Yao your Chief Justice; Hou Ji your Minister of Agriculture; Yi Yin your Privy Treasurer; Zigong your envoy abroad; Yan Hui and Min Ziqian your Erudites; Zixia your Minister of Ceremonies; Yi your western capital intendant; Zilu your Capital Commandant; Xie your Grand Herald; Guan Longpeng your Director of the Imperial Clan; the minister Boyi your Metropolitan Governor; Guan Zhong your northern capital intendant; Lu Ban your Superintendent of Works; Zhong Shanfu your Chamberlain for Attendants; the Earl of Shen your Grand Coachman; Prince Jizi of Yanling your Superintendent of Waters and Parks; Baili Xi your Director of Dependent States; Liuxia Hui your Chamberlain for the Empress; Shi Yu your Rectifier; Qu Boyu your Grand Tutor; Kong Fu your supervisor of the heir apparent's household; Sunshu Ao your chancellor to the feudal lords; Zichan your commandery governor; Prince Qingji your Palace Gate Guard; Xia Yu your Cauldron Officer; Yi the Archer your Vanguard Officer; and Song Wan your road-clearing scout."

entries.zh: 上乃大笑。
entries.en: The emperor burst out laughing.
entries.literal: Thereupon the emperor greatly laughed.

entries.zh: 是時，朝廷多賢材，上復問朔：「方今公孫丞相，兒大夫、董仲舒、夏侯始昌、司馬相如、吾丘壽王、主父偃、硃買臣、嚴助、汲黯、膠倉、終軍、嚴安、徐樂、司馬遷之倫，皆辯知閎達，溢於文辭，先生自視，何與比哉？」
entries.en: The court at that time teemed with talent, and the emperor pressed Shuo again: "Consider Chancellor Gongsun Hong, Censor-in-Chief Er Kuan, Dong Zhongshu, Xiahou Shichang, Sima Xiangru, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Zhu Maichen, Yan Zhu, Ji An, Jiao Cang, Zhong Jun, Yan An, Xu Le, Sima Qian, and men of that stamp. They are learned, articulate, and prolific writers. How do you measure yourself against such company?"
entries.literal: At this time the court had many worthy talents, and the emperor again asked Shuo: "At present Chancellor Gongsun Hong, Censor-in-Chief Er Kuan, Dong Zhongshu, Xiahou Shichang, Sima Xiangru, Wuqiu Shouwang, Zhufu Yan, Zhu Maichen, Yan Zhu, Ji An, Jiao Cang, Zhong Jun, Yan An, Xu Le, Sima Qian, and their like are all eloquent, learned, broad-minded, accomplished, and overflowing in literary expression. In your own view, sir, how do you compare with them?"

entries.zh: 朔對曰：「臣觀其□齒牙，樹頰胲，吐脣吻，擢項頤，結股腳，連脽尻，遺蛇其跡，行步偊旅，臣朔雖不肖，尚兼此數子者。」
entries.en: Shuo answered, "What I see in them is (lacuna) bared teeth and gums, cheeks swollen like bellows, lips forever flapping, necks craning and chins wagging, legs tangled like knotted cord, rumps welded to haunches, footprints that zigzag like a snake's trail, and a shambling, knock-kneed walk. Unworthy as I am, I flatter myself that I already embody every one of those fine qualities."
entries.literal: Shuo replied, saying: "Your servant has observed their (lacuna) teeth and gums, their jutting cheekbones, their thrusting lips and mouths, their stretched necks and chins, their knotted thighs and shanks, their buttocks joined to tailbones, their tracks winding like a snake's, their gait shambling and unsteady — though your servant Shuo is unworthy, I still combine in myself these several sons' traits."

entries.zh: 朔之進對澹辭，皆此類也。
entries.en: As for Shuo's advancing replies, his placid phrases — all were of this kind.
entries.literal: As for Shuo's advancing replies, his placid phrases — all were of this kind.

entries.zh: 客難東方朔曰：「蘇秦、張儀一當萬乘之主，而都卿相之位，澤及後世。
entries.en: The guest reproached Dongfang Shuo: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi each won an audience with a great king and walked away as chief minister; their good fortune lasted for generations.
entries.literal: A guest rebuked Dongfang Shuo, saying: "Su Qin and Zhang Yi, each in one encounter with a ruler of ten thousand chariots, then occupied minister and chancellor positions, and their bounty reached later generations.

entries.zh: 今子大夫修先王之術，慕聖人之義，諷誦《詩》、《書》、百家之言，不可勝數，著於竹帛，脣腐齒落，服膺而不釋，好學樂道之效，明白甚矣；
entries.en: You, sir, have steeped yourself in the ways of the ancient kings and the teachings of the sages; you have memorized the Odes, the Documents, and more of the masters than anyone can count, and committed it all to writing; you have worn your lips thin and your teeth out clutching those texts to your heart. Your devotion to learning is obvious to everyone;
entries.literal: Now you, sir, cultivate the arts of the former kings, admire the righteousness of the sages, intone and chant the Odes, Documents, and the words of the hundred schools — beyond counting — inscribe them on bamboo and silk; your lips are worn, your teeth have fallen; you clasp them to your breast and do not release them; the effect of loving learning and delighting in the Way is exceedingly clear;

entries.zh: 自以智能海內無雙，則可謂博聞辯智矣。
entries.en: you believe your wit unmatched under heaven — no one would deny you are learned and clever.
entries.literal: You consider your intelligence and wisdom within the seas without peer — then one may call you broadly learned and eloquently wise.

entries.zh: 然悉力盡忠以事聖帝，曠日持久，官不過侍郎，位不過執戟，意者尚有遺行邪？
entries.en: Yet though you have given the sage emperor your utmost loyalty year after year, your title has never risen above attendant-in-waiting and your duties never beyond holding the halberd at court. Are you hiding some moral flaw?
entries.literal: Yet, exhausting strength and exhausting loyalty to serve the sage emperor, days stretching long and time enduring, your office has not passed attendant-in-waiting, your rank has not passed halberd-bearer — is it perhaps that there are still conduct faults remaining?

entries.zh: 同胞之徒無所容居，其故何也？」
entries.en: Even your own kindred can barely house themselves. How do you explain that?"
entries.literal: Your fellows of the same womb have nowhere to lodge — what is the reason for this?"

entries.zh: 東方先生喟然長息，仰而應之曰：「是固非子之所能備也。
entries.en: Master Dongfang drew a long breath, lifted his eyes, and said, "That is something you simply are not in a position to understand.
entries.literal: Master Dongfang heaved a long sigh, looked up, and replied to him, saying: "This is indeed not what you, sir, are able to comprehend fully.

entries.zh: 彼一時也，此一時也，豈可同哉？
entries.en: Their age was one world; ours is another. How can you equate them?
entries.literal: That was one season; this is one season — how could they be the same?

entries.zh: 夫蘇秦、張儀之時，周室大壞，諸侯不朝，力政爭權，相禽以兵，並為十二國，未有雌雄，得士者強，失士者亡，故談說行焉。
entries.en: In Su Qin and Zhang Yi's day the house of Zhou was crumbling, the lords ignored the king, might made right, and rival armies carved the realm into a dozen warring states with no clear winner. Strength went to whoever won the talent; ruin to whoever lost it. Of course wandering persuaders flourished.
entries.literal: In the time of Su Qin and Zhang Yi, the Zhou house was greatly broken; the feudal lords did not attend court; they used forceful government and struggled for power, seized one another with arms, and stood together as twelve states; there was not yet victor or vanquished; he who obtained knights was strong, he who lost knights perished — therefore persuasion and doctrine went into practice.

entries.zh: 身處尊位，珍寶充內，外有廩倉，澤及後世，子孫長享。
entries.en: A successful strategist sat in high office, vaults groaning with treasure, granaries overflowing, and left a legacy his descendants lived on for generations.
entries.literal: The body occupied honored position; treasures filled the interior; outside there were granaries and storehouses; the bounty reached later generations, and sons and grandsons enjoyed it long.

entries.zh: 今則不然。
entries.en: Today nothing of the sort applies.
entries.literal: Now it is not so.

entries.zh: 聖帝流德，天下震懾，諸侯賓服，連四海之外以為帶，安於覆盂，動猶運之掌，賢不肖何以異哉？
entries.en: Our sage emperor's virtue overawes the realm; the lords come as guests; the four seas beyond the borders hang from his belt like a sash; the empire sits as steady as an upturned bowl; he moves it as easily as spinning something in his palm. In such a world, what separates the worthy from the worthless?
entries.literal: The sage emperor spreads virtue; under Heaven trembles in awe; the feudal lords guest-submit; he links what lies beyond the four seas to serve as his belt; he is secure as an inverted bowl; movement is like turning it in the palm — how should worthy and unworthy differ?

entries.zh: 遵天之道，順地之理，物無不得其所；
entries.en: Heaven has its constant course, earth its proper order, and every creature finds its allotted place;
entries.literal: Following Heaven's Way, complying with Earth's pattern — among things none fails to obtain its proper place;

entries.zh: 故綏之則安，動之則苦；
entries.en: soothe the people and they rest; harry them and they groan;
entries.literal: therefore, soothe them and they are at peace; stir them and they suffer;

entries.zh: 尊之則為將，卑之則為虜；
entries.en: honor a man and he becomes a general; break him and he is a prisoner;
entries.literal: honor them and they become generals; humble them and they become captives;

entries.zh: 抗之則在青雲之上，抑之則在深泉之下；
entries.en: lift him and he rides the clouds; cast him down and he sinks into the abyss;
entries.literal: raise them and they are above the blue clouds; suppress them and they are below the deep springs;

entries.zh: 用之則為虎，不用則為鼠；
entries.en: use him and he is a tiger; ignore him and he is a mouse;
entries.literal: employ them and they are tigers; do not employ them and they are rats;

entries.zh: 雖欲盡節效情，安知前後？
entries.en: even if you mean to give your whole heart to the throne, who can tell whether you will rise or fall?
entries.literal: Though one wishes to exhaust integrity and offer one's utmost feeling, how does one know what comes before and after?

entries.zh: 夫天地之大，士民之眾，竭精談說，並進輻湊者不可勝數，悉力募之，困於衣食，或失門戶。
entries.en: The world is vast, the educated class huge; countless men crowd the capital peddling advice like spokes to a hub. The ruler can summon them all, yet many still starve for want of a meal or never find a patron.
entries.literal: As for the greatness of Heaven and Earth and the multitude of knights and commoners — those who exhaust their essence in talk and doctrine, who advance together like spokes to the hub, cannot be counted; exhaust strength to recruit them, yet they are trapped in clothing and food, or lose their gate and door.

entries.zh: 使蘇秦、張儀與僕並生於今之世，曾不得掌故，安敢望常侍郎乎？
entries.en: If Su Qin and Zhang Yi were reborn today, they would be lucky to land a clerk's job, let alone a regular attendant-in-waiting like me.
entries.literal: Suppose Su Qin and Zhang Yi were born together with your servant in the present age — they would not even obtain the post of archivist; how would they dare to hope for regular attendant-in-waiting?

entries.zh: 故曰時異事異。
entries.en: So the saying goes: different times, different rules.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: the times differ, the affairs differ.

entries.zh: 「雖然，安可以不務修身乎哉！
entries.en: "Even so," he went on, "can anyone afford to neglect self-cultivation?
entries.literal: "Even so, how can one fail to devote oneself to cultivating the person!

entries.zh: 《詩》云：『鼓鐘於宮，聲聞於外。』
entries.en: The Odes says, "Beat the drum and ring the bell inside the hall, and the sound carries beyond the walls."
entries.literal: The Odes says: "The drums and bells in the palace, the sound is heard outside."

entries.zh: 『鶴鳴於九皋，聲聞於天。』
entries.en: The crane cries from the distant marsh, yet Heaven hears it."
entries.literal: The crane cries in the nine marshes, the sound is heard in Heaven."

entries.zh: 苟能修身，何患不榮！
entries.en: Cultivate yourself earnestly, and honor will follow — why doubt it?
entries.literal: If indeed one can cultivate the person, what worry is there of not being honored!

entries.zh: 太公體行仁義，七十有二乃設用於文、武，得信厥說，封於齊，七百歲而不絕。
entries.en: The Grand Duke lived out benevolence and righteousness; not until he was seventy-two did Kings Wen and Wu put his counsel to use. They believed him, enfeoffed him in Qi, and his line lasted seven hundred years.
entries.literal: The Grand Duke embodied and practiced benevolence and righteousness; only at seventy-two did he establish employment with Wen and Wu; he obtained trust for his doctrines, was enfeoffed in Qi, and for seven hundred years did not perish.

entries.zh: 此士所以日夜孳孳，敏行而不敢怠也。
entries.en: That is why a gentleman toils day and night and never dares slacken his step.
entries.literal: This is why knights day and night are diligent, act keenly, and dare not slacken.

entries.zh: 辟若鶺鴒，飛且鳴矣。
entries.en: Think of the wagtail on the wing, calling as it flies.
entries.literal: It is like the wagtail — flying and also crying.

entries.zh: 傳曰：『天不為人之惡寒而輟其冬，地不為人之惡險而輟其廣，君子不為小人之匈匈而易其行。』
entries.en: The tradition runs, "Heaven does not cancel winter because men hate the cold; earth does not shrink its breadth because men fear the heights; the gentleman does not change his course because petty people shout him down."
entries.literal: The tradition says: "Heaven does not, because humans detest cold, cease its winter; Earth does not, because humans detest precipitousness, cease its breadth; the gentleman does not, because petty men clamor, change his conduct."

entries.zh: 『天有常度，地有常形，君子有常行；
entries.en: Heaven keeps its seasons, earth its contours, the gentleman his steady practice;
entries.literal: Heaven has constant measure, Earth has constant form, the gentleman has constant conduct;

entries.zh: 君子道其常，小人計其功。』
entries.en: the gentleman cleaves to what endures; the small man chases every advantage."
entries.literal: the gentleman follows his constant; the petty man reckons his merit."

entries.zh: 《詩》云：『禮義之不愆，何恤人之言？』
entries.en: The Odes adds, "If you never stray from ritual and right, why fear gossip?"
entries.literal: The Odes says: "If in ritual and righteousness one does not transgress, what anxiety about others' words?"

entries.zh: 故曰：『水至清則無魚，人至察則無徒。
entries.en: Hence the proverb: fish cannot live in water that is too clear; a man who picks at every fault will have no friends.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: "When water is too clear there are no fish; when a man is too scrutinizing there are no companions.

entries.zh: 冕而前旒，所以蔽明；
entries.en: The king's crown hangs beaded curtains before his eyes to dim the glare;
entries.literal: The cap with pendants before the eyes — by this means to screen brightness;

entries.zh: 黈纊充耳，所以塞聰。』
entries.en: Yellow silk plugs his ears to muffle sharp sounds."
entries.literal: Yellow cotton fills the ears — by this means to block keen hearing."

entries.zh: 明有所不見，聰有所不聞，舉大德，赦小過，無求備於一人之義也。
entries.en: Even clear sight misses something; even sharp hearing fails somewhere. Reward great virtue, overlook petty slips — that is what it means not to demand perfection of any one man.
entries.literal: Brightness has what it does not see; keen hearing has what it does not hear; raising great virtue, pardoning small faults — this is the meaning of not seeking completeness in a single person.

entries.zh: 枉而直之，使自得之；
entries.en: Set crooked timber straight, but let the tree find its own grain;
entries.literal: Bend them and straighten them, causing them to obtain it themselves;

entries.zh: 優而柔之，使自求之；
entries.en: Coax and soften it, but let it seek its own shape;
entries.literal: Indulge them and soften them, causing them to seek it themselves;

entries.zh: 揆而度之，使自索之。
entries.en: measure and weigh it, but let the truth declare itself.
entries.literal: Measure and estimate them, causing them to search it out themselves.

entries.zh: 蓋聖人教化如此，欲自得之；
entries.en: The sage teaches in just this way because he wants people to discover the lesson for themselves;
entries.literal: Generally the sage's transforming instruction is thus — he desires that they obtain it themselves;

entries.zh: 自得之，則敏且廣矣。
entries.en: and what they learn for themselves is quick to take root and broad in reach.
entries.literal: when they obtain it themselves, then they are keen and broad.

entries.zh: 於是吳王懼然易容，捐薦去幾，危坐而聽。
entries.en: The king of Wu blanched, pushed away his cushion and side table, straightened his back, and listened.
entries.literal: Thereupon the king of Wu was fearful and changed countenance; he cast aside cushion and removed the low table; sat upright and listened.

entries.zh: 先生曰：「接輿避世，箕子被髮陽狂，此二人者，皆避濁世以全其身者也。
entries.en: The gentleman said: "Jieyu avoided the age; Jizi let his hair down and feigned madness—these two men both avoided a turbid age to preserve their persons.
entries.literal: The gentleman said: Jieyu avoided the age; Jizi let his hair down and feigned madness—these two men both avoided a turbid age to preserve their persons.

entries.zh: 使遇明王聖主，得清燕之閒，寬和之色，發憤畢誠，圖畫安危，揆度得失，上以安主體，下以便萬民，則五帝、三王之道可幾而見也。
entries.en: Had they found an enlightened sovereign, leisure, and an open face, they could have poured out loyal counsel, weighed every peril and profit, steadied the throne above and eased the people below—the way of the Five Emperors and Three Kings would almost have stood within reach.
entries.literal: Had they met a bright king and sage master, obtained clear repose's leisure and mild harmonious mien, vented indignation and exhausted sincerity, plotted safety and danger, measured gain and loss, above to settle the ruler's person, below to benefit the myriad people—then the way of the Five Emperors and Three Kings could nearly be seen.

entries.zh: 故伊尹蒙恥辱、負鼎俎、和五味以干湯，太公釣於渭之陽以見文王。
entries.en: That is why Yi Yin swallowed humiliation, shouldered the kitchen cauldron, and seasoned five flavors to win Tang's ear, and the Grand Duke angled on the north bank of the Wei until King Wen found him.
entries.literal: Therefore Yi Yin bore shame and dishonor, carried cauldron and stand, blended five flavors to seek Tang; the Grand Duke fished on the Wei's north bank (the sunny bank) to see King Wen.

entries.zh: 心合意同，謀無不成，計無不從，誠得其君也。
entries.en: When heart matches heart, every plan succeeds and every counsel is heeded—they had found the right lord.
entries.literal: Heart matched intent the same; no plan did not succeed, no scheme was not followed—truly they obtained their lords.

entries.zh: 深念遠慮，引義以正其身，推恩以廣其下，本仁祖義，褒有德，祿賢能，誅惡亂，總遠方，一統類，美風俗，此帝王所由昌也。
entries.en: Deep counsel, moral self-rule, spreading kindness below, honoring humanity and duty, rewarding the good, paying the worthy, crushing the wicked, binding far lands in one fabric, and polishing custom—this is how true kings grow great.
entries.literal: Deep thought and far planning, drawing rightness to rectify the self, extending grace to broaden those below, rooting in benevolence and taking rightness as ancestor, praising the virtuous, employing the worthy and able, punishing evil and disorder, gathering the distant regions, unifying kinds, beautifying customs—these are whereby emperors and kings flourish.

entries.zh: 上不變天性，下不奪人倫，則天地和洽，遠方懷之，故號聖王。
entries.en: They did not twist Heaven's pattern nor break human ties; Heaven and Earth chimed in tune and distant peoples came willingly—hence they are called sage-kings.
entries.literal: Above not altering heavenly nature, below not seizing human relations—then Heaven and Earth are harmonious and concordant, distant regions cherish them; therefore they are titled sage kings.

entries.zh: 臣子之職既加矣，於是裂地定封，爵為公侯，傳國子孫，名顯後世，民到於今稱之，以遇湯與文王也。
entries.en: Once their service was complete, they received fiefs, noble rank, and lines that still shine in history—the people praise them yet because they met Tang and King Wen.
entries.literal: When the duties of minister and son were already fulfilled, then they split land and fixed fiefs, were ennobled duke or marquis, transmitted the state to sons and grandsons, names shone in later ages; the people down to today praise them, because they encountered Tang and King Wen.

entries.zh: 太公、伊尹以如此，龍逢、比干獨如彼，豈不哀哉！
entries.en: The Grand Duke and Yi Yin met with such success, while Guan Longpeng and Bigan met with the opposite fate. Is that not tragic?
entries.literal: The Grand Duke and Yi Yin fared thus; Guan Longpeng and Bigan alone fared otherwise. Is it not pitiable?

entries.zh: 故曰談何容易！」
entries.en: So again: easier said than done."
entries.literal: Therefore it is said, how easy to speak!"

entries.zh: 卷六十五 東方朔傳第三十五
entries.en: Volume 65: the thirty-fifth biography—Dongfang Shuo.
entries.literal: Volume 65: Biography of Dongfang Shuo, Number 35.

entries.zh: 武帝末，郡國盜賊群起，暴勝之為直指使者，衣繡衣，持斧，逐捕盜賊，督課郡國，東至海，以軍興誅不從命者，威振州郡。
entries.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign bandits sprang up everywhere; Bao Shengzhi was named commissioner with plenipotentiary powers, robed in silk and carrying the imperial axe, hunted down outlaws eastward to the sea, enforced the law with military rigor, and cowed every circuit he touched.
entries.literal: Near the end of Emperor Wu, bandits rose in crowds in the commanderies and states; Bao Shengzhi became commissioner with direct mandate, wore embroidered robes, held an axe, pursued and captured bandits, supervised and assessed commanderies and states, east to the sea; by military exigency he executed those who did not obey orders; his awe shook province and commanderies.

entries.zh: 勝之素聞不疑賢，至勃海，遣吏請與相見。
entries.en: Shengzhi had long heard of Buyi's worth; on reaching Bohai he sent an officer to ask for an interview.
entries.literal: Shengzhi had long heard Buyi was worthy; when he reached Bohai he sent an official to request a meeting.

entries.zh: 不疑冠進賢冠，帶櫑具劍，佩環玦，褒衣博帶，盛服至門上謁。
entries.en: Buyi appeared in the cap of the worthy candidate, the long sword at his belt, jade ring and pendant, wide sleeves and flowing sash, and presented himself at the gate in full court dress.
entries.literal: Buyi capped himself with the cap for advancing the worthy, girded the stacked-rack sword, wore ring and jade pendant, loose robe and broad sash, in full dress arrived at the gate and submitted his visiting card.

entries.zh: 門下欲使解劍，不疑曰：「劍者，君子武備，所以衛身，不可解。
entries.en: The porters asked him to leave his sword outside. Buyi replied, "The sword is a gentleman's arms; it guards his person and must stay at his side.
entries.literal: The gate staff wished to make him ungird his sword; Buyi said: "The sword is the gentleman's martial equipment, whereby to guard the person; it cannot be ungirded.

entries.zh: 請退。」
entries.en: Then I shall withdraw."
entries.literal: I request to withdraw."

entries.zh: 吏白勝之。
entries.en: The officer reported this to Shengzhi.
entries.literal: The official reported to Shengzhi.

entries.zh: 勝之開閣延請，望見不疑容貌尊嚴，衣冠甚偉，勝之□履起迎。
entries.en: Shengzhi threw open the door to receive him; one look at Buyi's stern bearing and magnificent dress sent him scrambling from his seat in his slippers to greet him.
entries.literal: Shengzhi opened the pavilion gate and extended invitation; gazing he saw Buyi's countenance solemn and dignified, cap and robes very grand; Shengzhi treading in his slippers rose to welcome.

entries.zh: 登堂坐定，不疑據地曰：「竊伏海瀕，聞暴公子威名舊矣，今乃承顏接辭。
entries.en: When they were seated in the hall, Buyi knelt and said, "I have lived obscurely by the coast and long admired your lordship's name; today I am honored to look upon you and speak with you.
entries.literal: They ascended the hall and sat settled; Buyi knelt on the ground and said: "I have humbly lain by the sea's edge; I have heard Lord Bao's awesome name long; now I receive face and connect words.

entries.zh: 凡為吏，太剛則折，太柔則廢，威行施之以恩，然後樹功揚名，永終天祿。」
entries.en: For any magistrate, too much rigidity snaps him, too much softness undoes him; temper stern rule with kindness, and only then can he win lasting merit, a good name, and the blessings of office."
entries.literal: In general as an official, too rigid then snaps, too soft then is useless; awe in conduct apply it with kindness; then afterward establish merit and raise name, forever finish heaven's stipend."

entries.zh: 勝之知不疑非庸人，敬納其戒，深接以禮意，問當世所施行。
entries.en: Shengzhi saw he was no common man, took his counsel to heart, treated him with full courtesy, and asked his views on current policy.
entries.literal: Shengzhi knew Buyi was no ordinary man; respectfully he accepted his warning, deeply received him with ritual intent, asked what was practiced in the present age.

entries.zh: 門下諸從事皆州郡選吏，側聽不疑，莫不驚駭。
entries.en: The staff—all picked men from the provinces—listened in stunned silence.
entries.literal: The various attendants under the gate were all province-and-commandery-selected clerks; listening sideways to Buyi, none were not startled and awestruck.

entries.zh: 至昏夜，罷去。
entries.en: They talked on until nightfall before breaking up.
entries.literal: Until dusk and night, they stopped and departed.

entries.zh: 勝之遂表薦不疑，征詣公車，拜為青州刺史。
entries.en: Shengzhi memorialized his name; the court summoned him through the public carriage office and named him Governor of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Shengzhi then memorialized recommending Buyi; he was summoned to the public carriage gate and appointed Governor of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 久之，武帝崩，昭帝即位，而齊孝王孫劉澤交結郡國豪桀謀反，欲先殺青州刺史。
entries.en: In time Emperor Wu died and Emperor Zhao succeeded him. Liu Ze, grandson of Prince Xiao of Qi, conspired with bold men across the commanderies and states to rebel and planned to strike first at the governor of Qing province.
entries.literal: After a long time Emperor Wu died and Emperor Zhao came to the throne. Liu Ze, grandson of Prince Xiao of Qi, joined with powerful men of the commanderies and states in plotting rebellion and intended first to kill the Governor of Qing province.

entries.zh: 不疑發覺，收捕，皆伏其辜。
entries.en: Buyi uncovered the plot, made arrests, and all the conspirators paid with their lives.
entries.literal: Buyi discovered it, arrested and seized them, and all paid for their crimes.

entries.zh: 擢為京兆尹，賜錢百萬。
entries.en: He was promoted to Governor of the Capital and rewarded with a million cash.
entries.literal: He was promoted to Governor of the Capital and given a million cash.

entries.zh: 京師吏民敬其威信。
entries.en: Officials and commoners in the capital respected his authority.
entries.literal: The officials and commoners of the capital respected his authority and prestige.

entries.zh: 每行縣錄囚徒還，其母輒問不疑：「有所平反，活幾何人？」
entries.en: Whenever he returned from touring the counties to review prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi, "How many wrongful cases did you reverse and how many lives did you save?"
entries.literal: Whenever he returned from touring the counties to review prisoners, his mother would ask Buyi, "Were there any reversals of wrongful verdicts? How many people did you keep alive?"

entries.zh: 即不疑多有所平反，母喜笑，為飲食言語異於他時；
entries.en: If Buyi had exonerated many, his mother beamed and treated him to food and talk unlike at other times;
entries.literal: When Buyi had reversed many cases, his mother would smile with joy and treat him to food and conversation unlike at other times;

entries.zh: 或亡所出，母怒，為之不食。
entries.en: if there were none, his mother grew angry and refused to eat.
entries.literal: when there were none, his mother grew angry and would not eat on his account.

entries.zh: 故不疑為吏，嚴而不殘。
entries.en: Thus Buyi governed with severity but without cruelty.
entries.literal: Thus Buyi as an official was stern but not cruel.

entries.zh: 始元五年，有一男子乘黃犢車，建黃旐，衣黃襜褕，著黃冒，詣北闕，自謂衛太子。
entries.en: In Shiyuan 5 a man arrived at the north gate in a yellow cart under a yellow banner, dressed in yellow from cap to coat, and announced that he was the crown prince of Wei.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Shiyuan, there was a man who rode a yellow calf cart, raised a yellow banner, wore a yellow short coat, put on a yellow cap, went to the northern gate tower, calling himself the Heir Apparent of Wei.

entries.zh: 公車以聞，詔使公卿、將軍、中二千石雜識視。
entries.en: The public carriage office reported the matter, and the emperor ordered high ministers, generals, and officials at the two-thousand-shi rank to go and identify him.
entries.literal: The public carriage office reported it; an edict ordered excellencies, generals, and full-two-thousand-shi officials jointly to identify and inspect.

entries.zh: 長安中吏民聚觀者數萬人。
entries.en: Tens of thousands of officials and commoners mobbed the streets of Chang'an to watch.
entries.literal: In Chang'an officials and commoners who gathered to watch were several tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 右將軍勒兵闕下，以備非常。
entries.en: The General of the Right drew up troops beneath the gate in case of trouble.
entries.literal: The General of the Right marshaled troops below the gate tower, to guard against the extraordinary.

entries.zh: 丞相、御史、中二千石至者並莫敢發言。
entries.en: The chancellor, the imperial counselor, and every two-thousand-shi official on the scene kept silent.
entries.literal: The chancellor, imperial counselor, and those full-two-thousand-shi who arrived together none dared speak.

entries.zh: 京兆尹不疑後到，叱從吏收縛。
entries.en: Jun Buyi, Governor of the Capital, arrived last and ordered his men to arrest the man at once.
entries.literal: Governor of the Capital Buyi arrived afterward; he shouted to following clerks to seize and bind.

entries.zh: 或曰：「是非未可知，且安之。」
entries.en: Someone urged him to wait: "We cannot yet be sure—go slowly."
entries.literal: Someone said: "Right and wrong are not yet knowable; for the moment settle him."

entries.zh: 不疑曰：「諸君何患於衛太子！
entries.en: Buyi replied, "Why should you fear the crown prince of Wei?
entries.literal: Buyi said: "Why do you gentlemen worry about the Heir Apparent of Wei!

entries.zh: 昔蒯聵違命出奔，輒距而不納，《春秋》是之。
entries.en: When Prince Kuai Kui fled Wei, his son refused him entry, and the Spring and Autumn praises that refusal.
entries.literal: Formerly Kuai Kui disobeyed orders and fled out; Zhe kept him off and would not admit him; the Spring and Autumn Annals approved this.

entries.zh: 衛太子得罪先帝，亡不即死，今來自詣，此罪人也。」
entries.en: The crown prince of Wei wronged the late emperor and ran away instead of dying for it; whoever walks in now is a criminal impostor."
entries.literal: The Heir Apparent of Wei offended the former emperor, fled and did not immediately die; now he has come of himself to present himself—this is a criminal."

entries.zh: 遂送詔獄。
entries.en: He was marched off to the imperial prison.
entries.literal: Thereupon he was sent to the edict prison.

entries.zh: 廣兄子受字公子，亦以賢良舉為太子家令。
entries.en: His nephew Shu Shou, courtesy name Gongzi, was likewise recommended on the worthy-and-good list and made superintendent of the heir's household.
entries.literal: Guang's elder brother's son Shou, courtesy name Gongzi, also by worthy and good was recommended as heir-apparent household superintendent.

entries.zh: 受好禮恭謹，敏而有辭。
entries.en: Shu Shou loved ritual, was deferential and careful, quick-witted and eloquent.
entries.literal: Shou loved ritual, was respectful and careful, keen and had words.

entries.zh: 宣帝幸太子宮，受迎謁應對，及置酒宴，奉觴上壽，辭禮閑雅，上甚歡說。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan visited the heir's palace, Shou received him with flawless courtesy; at the banquet he raised the toast with such grace that the emperor was delighted.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan visited the heir's palace; Shou greeted, visited, answered; when they set wine and feast, he raised the cup and offered longevity; his phrasing and ritual were leisurely and elegant; the sovereign was very pleased.

entries.zh: 頃之，拜受為少傅。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was named junior tutor.
entries.literal: Before long, Shou was appointed junior tutor.

entries.zh: 定國少學法於父，父死，後定國亦為獄中、郡決曹，補廷尉史，以選與御史中丞從事治反者獄，以材高舉侍御史，遷御史中丞。
entries.en: Dingguo studied law under his father as a youth. After his father died, Dingguo too served in the prison office and the commandery sentencing bureau, became a clerk of the commandant of justice, and by selection assisted the imperial counselor in treason cases. For his outstanding ability he was recommended as attendant imperial counselor and then promoted to imperial counselor.
entries.literal: Dingguo in youth studied law under his father. After his father died, Dingguo too served in the prison office and the commandery sentencing bureau, filled a post as clerk of the commandant of justice, and by selection joined the imperial counselor in handling treason cases; for his high talent he was recommended and became attendant imperial counselor, then was promoted imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 會昭帝崩，昌邑王征即位，行淫亂，定國上書諫。
entries.en: When Emperor Zhao died, the king of Changyi was summoned to the throne and behaved with dissolute disorder; Dingguo memorialized in remonstrance.
entries.literal: It happened that Emperor Zhao died; the King of Changyi was summoned and enthroned, behaving with dissolute disorder, and Dingguo submitted a memorial remonstrating.

entries.zh: 後王廢，宣帝立，大將軍光領尚書事，條奏群臣諫昌邑王者皆超遷。
entries.en: After the king was deposed and Emperor Xuan took the throne, Grand General Guang directed the Masters of Writing and memorialized that every minister who had remonstrated the king of Changyi should be promoted out of turn.
entries.literal: After the king was deposed and Emperor Xuan was enthroned, Grand General Guang held charge of the Masters of Writing and memorialized item by item that all the ministers who had remonstrated the King of Changyi should receive exceptional promotion.

entries.zh: 定國由是為光祿大夫，平尚書事，甚見任用。
entries.en: Dingguo thereupon became Imperial Household Grandee, assisted with the Masters of Writing, and was greatly trusted.
entries.literal: From this Dingguo became Imperial Household Grandee, assisted with Masters of Writing affairs, and was greatly employed.

entries.zh: 數年，遷水衡都尉，超過廷尉。
entries.en: Several years later, he was promoted to Superintendent of Waterways and Parks, then advanced exceptionally to Commandant of Justice.
entries.literal: Several years later, he was promoted to Superintendent of Waterways and Parks, then advanced exceptionally to Commandant of Justice.

entries.zh: 甘露中，代黃霸為丞相，封西平侯。
entries.en: During the Ganlu era he replaced Huang Ba as chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.
entries.literal: In the Ganlu era he replaced Huang Ba as chancellor and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.

entries.zh: 三年，宣帝崩，元帝立，以定國任職舊臣，敬重之。
entries.en: Three years later Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan succeeded him; as an old minister still in office, Dingguo was held in high regard.
entries.literal: Three years later Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan was enthroned; because Dingguo was an old minister in office, he was respected and honored.

entries.zh: 時陳萬年為御史大夫，與定國並位八年，論議無所拂。
entries.en: Chen Wannian then served as commandant of the imperial counselors; he and Dingguo held equal rank for eight years without clashing in council.
entries.literal: At that time Chen Wannian was commandant of the imperial counselors; with Dingguo he shared rank eight years, and in discussion there was no friction.

entries.zh: 後貢禹代為御史大夫，數處駁議，定國明習政事，率常丞相議可。
entries.en: Later Gong Yu replaced him as commandant of the imperial counselors and often disagreed in debate, but Dingguo knew administration thoroughly and the chancellor's views usually carried the day.
entries.literal: Later Gong Yu replaced him as commandant of the imperial counselors and repeatedly offered rebuttals in discussion; Dingguo was clear and practiced in government affairs, and as a rule the chancellor's proposals were approved.

entries.zh: 然上始即位，關東連年被災害，民流入關，言事者歸咎於大臣。
entries.en: But the new emperor's reign opened with disaster after disaster in Guandong; refugees poured through the passes, and memorialists blamed the high ministers.
entries.literal: Yet when the sovereign first took the throne, Guandong suffered disasters year after year, the people flowed into the passes, and those who spoke on affairs blamed the great ministers.

entries.zh: 上於是數以朝日引見丞相、御史，入受詔，條責以職事，曰：「惡吏負賊，妄意良民，至亡辜死。
entries.en: The emperor therefore repeatedly summoned chancellor and imperial counselor on court days, received them with edicts, and rebuked them point by point for their duties, saying, "Wicked clerks shelter bandits and falsely accuse honest people, even to the death of the innocent.
entries.literal: The sovereign therefore repeatedly on court days summoned the chancellor and imperial counselor, had them enter to receive edicts, and item by item reproached them for their duties, saying: "Wicked clerks harbor bandits, falsely suspect good commoners, even to innocent death.

entries.zh: 或盜賊發，吏不亟追而反系亡家，後不敢復告，以故浸廣。
entries.en: When bandits struck, officers failed to pursue them but instead detained ruined households; afterward people dared not report crimes, and the evil spread.
entries.literal: Sometimes when bandits rose, clerks did not pursue them urgently but instead detained bereft households; afterward people did not dare report again, and for this reason the evil spread.

entries.zh: 民多冤結，州郡不理，連上書者交於闕廷。
entries.en: Grievances multiplied while provinces and commanderies neglected them, and memorials piled up at the palace gates.
entries.literal: The people had many grievances of injustice; the provinces and commanderies did not handle them, and successive memorials piled up at the court gate.

entries.zh: 二千石選舉不實，是以在位多不任職。
entries.en: Recommendations for two-thousand-shi posts were false, and many officeholders failed their duties.
entries.literal: The two-thousand-shi selections were not truthful, and therefore many in office did not perform their duties.

entries.zh: 民田有災害，吏不肯除，收趣其租，以故重困。
entries.en: When farmers' fields were ruined, clerks refused remission and still pressed for rent, deepening their hardship.
entries.literal: When commoners' fields suffered disaster, clerks would not grant remission but collected and pressed their rents, and for this reason distress was severe.

entries.zh: 關東流民饑寒疾疫，已詔吏轉漕，虛倉廩開府臧相振救，賜寒者衣，至春猶恐不贍。
entries.en: Refugees from Guandong faced hunger, cold, and plague; the court had ordered grain shipments, emptied granaries, opened treasuries, and given clothes to the freezing, yet even by spring he feared the relief would not suffice.
entries.literal: The drifting people of Guandong suffered hunger, cold, and pestilence; edicts had already ordered clerks to transfer grain by transport, empty the granaries, open the treasuries, and aid one another in relief, and bestow clothing on the cold; even until spring he still feared it would not suffice.

entries.zh: 今丞相、御史將欲何施以塞此咎？
entries.en: What do chancellor and imperial counselor propose to do to answer for this blame?
entries.literal: Now what do the chancellor and imperial counselor intend to apply to stop this blame?

entries.zh: 悉意條狀，陳朕過失。」
entries.en: Set out everything in full and lay Our faults before Us."
entries.literal: Lay out everything fully in items and set forth Our faults."

entries.zh: 定國上書謝罪。
entries.en: Dingguo memorialized to apologize.
entries.literal: Dingguo submitted a memorial apologizing for his guilt.

entries.zh: 永光元年，春霜夏寒，日青亡光，上復以詔條責曰：「郎有從東方來者，言民父子相棄。
entries.en: In the first year of Yongguang, frost came in spring and cold in summer, and the sun turned pale and dim. The emperor again rebuked them by edict, saying, "A court gentleman arrived from the east reporting that fathers and sons were abandoning one another.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongguang, spring brought frost and summer brought cold; the sun turned blue and lost its light. The sovereign again with an edict item by item reproached them, saying: "A gentleman-attendant came from the east saying that fathers and sons were abandoning one another.

entries.zh: 丞相、御史案事之吏匿不言邪？
entries.en: Have the chancellor's and imperial counselor's investigating clerks concealed this and said nothing?
entries.literal: Did the chancellor and imperial counselor's clerks who handled the cases conceal it and not speak?

entries.zh: 將從東方來者加增之也？
entries.en: Or has the man from the east exaggerated it?
entries.literal: Or did the one who came from the east exaggerate it?

entries.zh: 何以錯繆至是？
entries.en: How could things have gone so wrong?
entries.literal: How could error reach this point?

entries.zh: 欲知其實。
entries.en: We wish to know the truth.
entries.literal: We wish to know the truth of it.

entries.zh: 方今年歲未可預知也，即有水旱，其憂不細。
entries.en: This year's harvest cannot yet be foretold; if flood or drought comes, the worry will be grave.
entries.literal: Just now this year's harvest cannot yet be foreknown; if there are flood or drought, the worry is not slight.

entries.zh: 公卿有可以防其未然，救其已然者不？
entries.en: Can any of you prevent what has not yet happened and remedy what has already happened?
entries.literal: Among the excellencies and ministers, is there anyone who can guard against what has not yet happened and rescue what has already happened?

entries.zh: 各以誠對，毋有所諱。」
entries.en: Answer with full sincerity and hide nothing."
entries.literal: Each answer with sincerity and do not conceal anything."

entries.zh: 定國惶恐，上書自劾，歸侯印，乞骸骨。
entries.en: Dingguo, in fear and trembling, memorialized against himself, returned his marquis seal, and asked to retire.
entries.literal: Dingguo was fearful and trembling; he submitted a memorial impeaching himself, returned his marquis seal, and begged for his bones.

entries.zh: 上報曰：「君相朕躬，不敢怠息，萬方之事，大錄於君。
entries.en: The emperor answered, "You assist Our person; We dare not slacken. The affairs of the realm rest largely upon you.
entries.literal: The sovereign replied saying: "You assist Our person; We dare not slacken or rest. The affairs of the myriad regions are largely recorded through you.

entries.zh: 能毋過者，其唯聖人。
entries.en: Only a sage can be wholly without fault.
entries.literal: Those who can be without fault—perhaps only the sage.

entries.zh: 方今承周、秦之敝，俗化陵夷，民寡禮誼，陰陽不調，災咎之發，不為一端而作，自聖人推類以記，不敢專也，況於非聖者乎！
entries.en: We inherit the exhaustion left by Zhou and Qin; custom has decayed, the people lack ritual and duty, yin and yang are awry, and disasters do not spring from one cause alone. Even a sage, when extending categories to record blame, does not take it all upon himself—how much less anyone who is no sage!
entries.literal: Just now We inherit the exhaustion of Zhou and Qin; custom and transformation decline, the people lack ritual and righteousness, yin and yang are not tuned, and the arising of disasters and blame does not come from a single cause. Even the sage, in extending categories to record them, does not dare to monopolize the blame—how much less one who is not a sage!

entries.zh: 日夜惟思所以，未能盡明。
entries.en: Day and night We ponder the remedy, yet cannot see it fully.
entries.literal: Day and night We only think of the means, yet have not been able to make everything fully clear.

entries.zh: 經曰：『萬方有罪，罪在朕躬。』
entries.en: The Classic says, "When the myriad regions are guilty, the guilt lies in Our person."
entries.literal: The Classic says, "When the myriad regions are guilty, the guilt lies in Our person."

entries.zh: 君雖任職，何必顓焉？
entries.en: Though you hold office, why must you shoulder all the blame?
entries.literal: Though you hold office, why must you monopolize the blame?

entries.zh: 其勉察郡國守相群牧，非其人者毋令久賊民。
entries.en: Examine the governors and regional shepherds of the commanderies and states, and do not let unfit men long prey upon the people.
entries.literal: Strive to examine the governors, administrators, and regional shepherds of commanderies and states; where they are not the right men, do not let them long harm the people.

entries.zh: 永執綱紀，務悉聰明，強食慎疾。」
entries.en: Hold fast to discipline, strive to be wholly clear-minded, eat well, and guard your health."
entries.literal: Forever hold the guiding cords, strive to be wholly clear and bright, eat heartily and guard against illness."

entries.zh: 定國遂稱篤，固辭。
entries.en: Dingguo then pleaded grave illness and firmly declined.
entries.literal: Dingguo thereupon claimed grave illness and firmly declined.

entries.zh: 上乃賜安車駟馬、黃金六十斤，罷就第。
entries.en: The emperor then gave him a comfortable carriage, four horses, and sixty jin of gold, dismissed him, and sent him home.
entries.literal: The sovereign then bestowed a comfortable carriage with four horses and sixty jin of gold, dismissed him, and let him return to his residence.

entries.zh: 數歲，七十餘薨。
entries.en: Some years later he died, aged more than seventy.
entries.literal: Some years later, at more than seventy, he died.

entries.zh: 謚曰安侯。
entries.en: He was given the posthumous title Marquis An.
entries.literal: His posthumous title was Marquis An.

entries.zh: 子永嗣。
entries.en: His son Yu Yong inherited his title.
entries.literal: His son Yong succeeded.

entries.zh: 少時，耆酒多過失，年且三十，乃折節修行，以父任為侍中中郎將、長水校尉。
entries.en: In youth he drank hard and often stumbled; near thirty he mended his ways, and through his father's rank became a palace attendant, General of the Household, and Colonel of the Changshui Archers.
entries.literal: In youth he loved wine and had many faults; when his years approached thirty, then he broke his bent and cultivated conduct; by father's privilege he became palace attendant, General of the Household, and Colonel of the Changshui Archers.

entries.zh: 定國死，居喪如禮，孝行聞。
entries.en: When Dingguo died, he observed the full mourning rites and his filial piety became known.
entries.literal: When Dingguo died, he dwelt mourning according to ritual; filial conduct was heard.

entries.zh: 由是以列侯為散騎、光祿勳，至御史大夫。
entries.en: He rose from full marquis to attendant at leisure and superintendent of the imperial household, then to commandant of the imperial counselors.
entries.literal: From this as full marquis he became attendant at leisure and superintendent of the imperial household, reaching commandant of the imperial counselors.

entries.zh: 尚館陶公主施。
entries.en: He was given in marriage to Princess Guantao, whose personal name was Shi.
entries.literal: He married Princess Guantao Shi.

entries.zh: 施者，宣帝長女，成帝姑也，賢有行，永以選尚焉。
entries.en: Shi was Emperor Xuan's eldest daughter and Emperor Cheng's aunt, a woman of virtue and good repute; Yong was chosen as her consort.
entries.literal: Shi was Emperor Xuan's eldest daughter, Emperor Cheng's aunt; worthy, had conduct; Yong by selection married her.

entries.zh: 上方欲相之，會永薨。
entries.en: The emperor was on the point of making him chancellor when Yu Yong died.
entries.literal: The sovereign was about to make him chancellor when it happened Yong died.

entries.zh: 子恬嗣。
entries.en: His son Yu Tian inherited the line.
entries.literal: His son Tian succeeded.

entries.zh: 恬不肖，薄於行。
entries.en: Yu Tian proved unworthy and mean in his conduct.
entries.literal: Tian was not like his forebears, thin in conduct.

entries.zh: 疏廣字仲翁，東海蘭陵人也。
entries.en: Shu Guang, courtesy name Zhongweng, came from Lanling in Donghai commandery.
entries.literal: Shu Guang, courtesy name Zhongweng, was a man of Lanling in Donghai.

entries.zh: 少好學，明《春秋》，家居教授，學者自遠方至。
entries.en: He loved learning from boyhood, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, and taught at home until students came from afar.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning, understood the Spring and Autumn Annals; at home he dwelt teaching, scholars from distant places came.

entries.zh: 徵為博士、太中大夫。
entries.en: The court summoned him as an erudite and then as Grand Counselor of the Palace.
entries.literal: He was summoned as erudite and Grand Counselor of the Palace.

entries.zh: 地節三年，立皇太子，選丙吉為太傅，廣為少傅，數月，吉遷御史大夫，廣徙為太傅。
entries.en: In Dijie 3, when the heir apparent was installed, Bing Ji became grand tutor and Shu Guang junior tutor; a few months later Ji rose to commandant of the imperial counselors and Guang succeeded him as grand tutor.
entries.literal: In the third year of Dijie, the imperial heir was established; Bing Ji was selected as grand tutor, Guang as junior tutor; after several months Ji was promoted commandant of the imperial counselors, Guang was transferred to be grand tutor.

entries.zh: 太子外祖父特進平恩侯許伯以為太子少，白使其弟中郎將舜監護太子家。
entries.en: The heir's maternal grandfather, Marquis of Ping'en Xu Bo, thought the boy needed more minders and asked that his brother, General of the Household Xu Shun, oversee the heir's establishment.
entries.literal: The heir's maternal grandfather, specially advanced Marquis of Ping'en Xu Bo, thought the heir young, reported and made his younger brother General of the Household Shun supervise and guard the heir's household.

entries.zh: 上以問廣，廣對曰：「太子國儲副君，師友必於天下英俊，不宜獨親外家許氏。
entries.en: The emperor consulted Shu Guang, who answered, "The heir is the nation's reserve; his teachers and companions should be the finest men in the empire, not drawn chiefly from the Xu in-laws.
entries.literal: The sovereign thereon asked Guang; Guang replied: "The heir is the state's stored successor-lord; teachers and friends must be from the realm's outstanding talents; it is not fitting to be intimate only with the maternal kin Xu clan.

entries.zh: 且太子自有太傅、少傅。
entries.en: Besides, he already has a grand tutor and a junior tutor.
entries.literal: Moreover the heir already has grand tutor and junior tutor.

entries.zh: 官屬已備，今復使舜護太子家，視陋，非所以廣太子德於天下也。」
entries.en: His staff is complete; to add Xu Shun as overseer looks petty and does nothing to spread the heir's virtue through the realm."
entries.literal: Official subordinates are already complete; now again to make Shun guard the heir's household shows meanness; it is not the means whereby to broaden the heir's virtue in the realm."

entries.zh: 上善其言，以語丞相魏相，相免冠謝曰：「此非臣等所能及。」
entries.en: The emperor approved and repeated the remark to Chancellor Wei Xiang, who removed his cap and said, "We could never have risen to that."
entries.literal: The sovereign approved his words, told Chancellor Wei Xiang; Xiang doffed cap and apologized saying: "This is not what your servants could reach."

entries.zh: 廣由是見器重，數受賞賜。
entries.en: From then on Guang stood high in favor and often received imperial gifts.
entries.literal: Guang from this was seen as weighty and trusted, repeatedly received rewards and gifts.

entries.zh: 太子每朝，因進見，太傅在前，少傅在後。
entries.en: Whenever the heir attended court, the grand tutor walked before him and the junior tutor behind.
entries.literal: Whenever the heir attended court, thereby advancing to audience, grand tutor in front, junior tutor behind.

entries.zh: 父子並為師傅，朝廷以為榮。
entries.en: Uncle and nephew serving together as the heir's tutors was counted an honor throughout the court.
entries.literal: Uncle and nephew together were tutors; the court thought it glorious.

entries.zh: 自元帝時，韋玄成為丞相，奏罷太上皇寢廟園，當上書言：「臣聞孔子曰：『如有王者，必世而後仁。』
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan, Chancellor Wei Xuancheng had persuaded the throne to close the shrine park of the Exalted Supreme Emperor. Ping Dang memorialized: "Confucius said, 'Give a true king one generation and benevolence will appear.'
entries.literal: From Emperor Yuan's time, Wei Xuancheng was chancellor, memorialized to abolish the Exalted Supreme Emperor's resting temple park; Dang submitted memorial saying: "Your servant has heard Confucius say: 'If there were a true king, after a generation then benevolence.'

entries.zh: 三十年之間，道德和洽，制禮興樂，災害不生，禍亂不作。
entries.en: Within thirty years virtue and custom would blend, rites and music would flourish, and neither disaster nor rebellion would arise.
entries.literal: Within thirty years, virtue and the Way harmonized and joined; regulated ritual and raised music; disasters did not arise, calamities and disorders did not occur.

entries.zh: 今聖漢受命而王，繼體承業二百餘年，孜孜不怠，政令清矣。
entries.en: Sacred Han has held the mandate for more than two hundred tireless years, and the statutes run clear.
entries.literal: Now sagely Han received the mandate and ruled, inheriting the body receiving the enterprise over two hundred years, diligent without slackening; government orders are clear.

entries.zh: 然風俗未和，陰陽未調，災害數見，意者大本有不立與？
entries.en: Yet custom is still discordant, yin and yang are out of tune, and omens come thick and fast—can the great foundations still be unsettled?
entries.literal: Yet customs are not harmonious, yin and yang are not tuned, disasters and prodigies repeatedly appear—I suspect perhaps the great root has something not established?

entries.zh: 何德化休征不應之久也！
entries.en: How long has virtuous rule waited in vain for its auspicious answer!
entries.literal: How long virtuous transformation and auspicious signs have not responded!

entries.zh: 禍福不虛，必有因而至者焉。
entries.en: Blessing and calamity do not strike at random; each has its cause.
entries.literal: Fortune and misfortune are not empty; there must be that by which they arrive.

entries.zh: 宜深跡其道而務修其本。
entries.en: We should trace the way to its source and mend the root.
entries.literal: It is fitting deeply to trace its way and strive to cultivate its root.

entries.zh: 昔者帝堯南面而治，先『克膽俊德，以親九族』，而化及萬國《孝經》曰『天地之性人為貴，人之行莫大於孝，孝莫大於嚴父，嚴父莫大於配天，則周公其人也。』
entries.en: Emperor Yao faced his court and began by illumining matchless virtue and bringing harmony to his nine clans, until his influence spread to every state. The Classic of Filial Piety says that among heaven and earth's gifts none ranks above man, that among human deeds none ranks above filial piety, that honoring the father is filial piety's height, and that joining the father to heaven is its summit—and the Duke of Zhou is the model.
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Yao faced south and governed; first 'he was able to illumine matchless virtue and draw near the nine kindreds,' and transformation reached the myriad states. The Classic of Filial Piety says: 'Of heaven and earth's nature man is noblest; of man's conduct none is greater than filial piety; of filial piety none is greater than honoring the father; of honoring the father none is greater than matching heaven—then the Duke of Zhou was such a man.

entries.zh: 夫孝子善述人之志，周公既成文、武之業而製作禮樂，修嚴父配天之事，知文王不欲以子臨父，故推而序之，上極於後稷而以配天。
entries.en: A true son carries on his forebears' purpose. The Duke of Zhou, having finished the work of Kings Wen and Wu, composed the rites and music and set his father King Wen beside heaven; knowing that a living son must not overshadow his father, he pushed the line back through the ancestors to Hou Ji so that Hou Ji might share heaven's honor.
entries.literal: As for the filial son who well transmits others' aims, the Duke of Zhou when he had completed Wen and Wu's enterprise then made ritual and music, cultivated the affair of honoring the father matching heaven; knowing King Wen did not wish the son to stand over the father, therefore he pushed and ordered it, upward reaching to Hou Ji and thereby matching heaven.

entries.zh: 此聖人之德，亡以加於孝也。
entries.en: That is sage virtue, and filial piety cannot rise higher.
entries.literal: This is the sage's virtue; there is nothing whereby to add to filial piety.

entries.zh: 高皇帝聖德受命，有天下，尊太上皇，猶周文、武之追王太王、王季也。
entries.en: The High Emperor received heaven's mandate and ruled the world; he honored his father as Exalted Supreme Emperor just as Kings Wen and Wu of Zhou posthumously ennobled King Tai and Wang Ji.
entries.literal: The High Emperor by sagely virtue received the mandate, possessed the realm, honored the Exalted Supreme Emperor, just as Zhou Wen and Wu posthumously titled King Tai and Wang Ji.

entries.zh: 此漢之始祖，後嗣所宜尊奉以廣盛德，孝之至也。
entries.en: He is Han's founding forebear; later generations owe him reverent service to magnify the dynasty's virtue—that is filial piety in full measure.
entries.literal: This is Han's first ancestor; posterity ought to honor and serve him so as to broaden splendid virtue—it is the utmost of filial piety.

entries.zh: 《書》云：『正稽古建功立事，可以永年，傳於亡窮。』」
entries.en: The Documents says, 'He who founds lasting deeds on the lessons of antiquity may enjoy long life and hand his work down forever.'"
entries.literal: The Documents says: 'Correctly examine antiquity, establish merit and accomplish affairs—then you may prolong the years, transmit to without end.'"

entries.zh: 上納其言，下詔復太上皇寢廟園。
entries.en: The emperor accepted the argument and ordered the shrine park of the Exalted Supreme Emperor restored.
entries.literal: The sovereign accepted his words, issued edict restoring the Exalted Supreme Emperor's resting temple park.

entries.zh: 薛廣德字長卿，沛郡相人也。
entries.en: Xue Guangde, courtesy name Changqing, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.
entries.literal: Xue Guangde, courtesy name Changqing, was a man of Xiang in Pei commandery.

entries.zh: 以《魯詩》教授楚國，龔勝、捨師事焉。
entries.en: He taught the Lu recension of the Classic of Songs in the state of Chu; Gong Sheng and Gong She became his disciples.
entries.literal: By the Lu version of the Classic of Songs he instructed the state of Chu; Gong Sheng and She took him as teacher to serve.

entries.zh: 蕭望之為御史大夫，除廣德為屬，數與論議，器之，薦廣德經行宜充本朝。
entries.en: When Xiao Wangzhi was commandant of the imperial counselors he took Guangde onto his staff, debated policy with him often, admired him, and recommended his learning and character as fit for high office at court.
entries.literal: When Xiao Wangzhi was commandant of the imperial counselors, he appointed Guangde as subordinate, repeatedly debated with him, valued him, recommended Guangde's classical learning and conduct as fitting to fill this court.

entries.zh: 為博士，論石渠，遷諫大夫，代貢禹為長信少府、御史大夫。
entries.en: He served as an erudite, took part in the Stone Canal conference, became remonstrance grandee, then succeeded Gong Yu as superintendent of the Changle Palace and as commandant of the imperial counselors.
entries.literal: He became erudite, debated at Stone Canal, was promoted remonstrance grandee, replaced Gong Yu as superintendent of the Changle Palace and commandant of the imperial counselors.

entries.zh: 雋不疑
entries.en: Jun Buyi
entries.literal: Jun Buyi.

entries.zh: 數年，宣帝即位，徵相入為大司農，遷御史大夫。
entries.en: Some years later, when Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Wei Xiang was summoned as grand minister of agriculture and then promoted to imperial censor.
entries.literal: Some years later, when Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Xiang was summoned to enter as grand minister of agriculture and was promoted imperial censor.

entries.zh: 四歲，大將軍霍光薨，上思其功德，以其子禹為右將軍，兄子樂平侯山復領尚書事。
entries.en: Four years later Grand General Huo Guang died. The emperor recalled his service, made his son Huo Yu general of the right, and had his nephew Huo Shan, Marquis of Leping, again direct the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: Four years later Grand General Huo Guang passed away. The sovereign thought on his merit and virtue, made his son Yu general of the right, and had his elder brother’s son Shan, Marquis of Leping, again direct the affairs of the Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 相因平恩侯許伯奏封事，言：「春秋譏世卿，惡宋三世為大夫，及魯季孫之專權，皆危亂國家。
entries.en: Wei Xiang submitted a sealed memorial through Marquis of Ping’en Xu Bo, saying, "The Spring and Autumn Annals condemn hereditary ministers, detest the Song line’s three generations as grand ministers, and the Ji clan of Lu’s monopoly of power—all of which endanger the state.
entries.literal: Xiang, through Marquis of Ping’en Xu Bo, submitted a sealed memorial, saying, "The Spring and Autumn Annals condemn hereditary ministers, detest the Song line’s three generations as grand ministers, and the Ji clan of Lu’s monopolizing power—all endanger and disorder the state.

entries.zh: 自後元以來，祿去王室，政繇冢宰。
entries.en: Since the Houyuan era, emoluments have left the royal house and government has passed through the chief steward.
entries.literal: Since the Houyuan period, salaries have departed from the royal house and government has passed through the chief steward.

entries.zh: 今光死，子復為大將軍，兄子秉樞機，昆弟諸婿據權勢，在兵官。
entries.en: Now that Huo Guang is dead, his son again serves as grand general, his nephew holds the pivot of power, and brothers and sons-in-law hold authority in military offices.
entries.literal: Now that Guang is dead, his son again serves as grand general, his elder brother’s son holds the pivot of power, and brothers, sons-in-law, and others hold authority and power in military offices.

entries.zh: 光夫人顯及諸女皆通籍長信宮，或夜詔門出入，驕奢放縱，恐寖不制。
entries.en: Huo Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changxin Palace; some came and went through the edict gate by night, arrogant and unrestrained, and I fear they may gradually escape control.
entries.literal: Guang’s wife Xian and his daughters all had registry access to Changxin Palace; some passed through the edict gate by night, arrogant, extravagant, and unrestrained—I fear they may gradually become ungovernable.

entries.zh: 宜有以損奪其權，破散陰謀，以固萬世之基，全功臣之世。」
entries.en: Measures should be taken to diminish their power, break up secret plots, secure the foundation for ages to come, and preserve the house of meritorious ministers."
entries.literal: There should be means to diminish and seize their power, break up secret plots, thereby to secure the foundation for ten thousand generations and preserve the house of meritorious ministers."

entries.zh: 又故事諸上書者皆為二封，署其一曰副，領尚書者先發副封，所言不善，屏去不奏。
entries.en: By precedent, memorialists submitted two sealed copies, one marked as the duplicate. The director of the Masters of Writing opened the duplicate first; if the contents were unsuitable, the memorial was set aside and never presented.
entries.literal: Again, by precedent all who submitted memorials made two seals, marking one as the copy. Whoever directed the Masters of Writing first opened the copy seal; if what was said was not good, it was set aside and not memorialized.

entries.zh: 相復因許伯白，去副封以防雍蔽。
entries.en: Wei Xiang again reported through Xu Bo to abolish the duplicate seal so that memorials could not be blocked or concealed.
entries.literal: Xiang again reported through Xu Bo to remove the copy seal in order to guard against obstruction and concealment.

entries.zh: 宣帝善之，詔相給事中，皆從其議。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan approved and made Wei Xiang supernumerary household grandee with palace access; all his proposals were adopted.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan approved it and issued an edict making Xiang supernumerary household grandee with palace access; all followed his proposals.

entries.zh: 霍氏殺許后之謀始得上聞。
entries.en: Only then did the Huo clan’s plot to murder Empress Xu reach the emperor.
entries.literal: Only then did the Huo clan’s plot to kill Empress Xu first reach the sovereign’s hearing.

entries.zh: 乃罷其三侯，令就第，親屬皆出補吏。
entries.en: The three marquisates were then abolished, the men were ordered home, and their kinsmen were all sent out to fill official posts.
entries.literal: Thereupon their three marquisates were abolished, they were ordered to return to their residences, and kinsmen were all sent out to fill official posts.

entries.zh: 於是韋賢以老病免，相遂代為丞相，封高平侯，食邑八百戶。
entries.en: Wei Xian was then dismissed on account of old age and illness, and Wei Xiang succeeded him as chancellor, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoping with eight hundred households.
entries.literal: Thereupon Wei Xian was dismissed on account of old age and illness, and Xiang then replaced him as chancellor, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gaoping, with a fief of eight hundred households.

entries.zh: 及霍氏怨相，又憚之，謀矯太后詔，先召斬丞相，然後廢天子。
entries.en: When the Huo clan both resented and feared Wei Xiang, they plotted to forge an empress dowager edict, summon and execute the chancellor first, and then depose the emperor.
entries.literal: When the Huo clan resented Xiang and also feared him, they plotted to forge an empress dowager edict, first summon and execute the chancellor, and then depose the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 事發覺，伏誅。
entries.en: When the plot was discovered, they were executed.
entries.literal: When the affair was discovered, they were executed.

entries.zh: 宣帝始親萬機，厲精為治，練群臣，核名實，而相總領眾職，甚稱上意。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan then personally took charge of government, strove to govern well, trained his ministers, and examined names against realities, while Wei Xiang oversaw the offices and greatly pleased him.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan then personally took charge of the myriad affairs, strove in spirit to govern, trained the ministers, examined names and realities, and Xiang oversaw the mass of offices—greatly matching the sovereign’s intent.

entries.zh: 後吉為車騎將軍軍市令，遷大將軍長史，霍光甚重之，入為光祿大夫給事中。
entries.en: He rose to army market director under the chariot-and-cavalry general, then chief clerk to the grand general; Huo Guang valued him highly and brought him into court as supernumerary household grandee.
