entries.literal: Peng came out and proclaimed, saying: "In my audience I spoke of five small faults and one great crime of the former general.

entries.zh: 中書令在旁，知我言狀。」
entries.en: The secretariat director stood at his side and heard every word I spoke."
entries.literal: The palace secretariat director was at his side and knows what I said."

entries.zh: 望之聞之，以問弘恭、石顯。
entries.en: When Wangzhi heard this, he questioned Hong Gong and Shi Xian.
entries.literal: When Wangzhi heard this, he questioned Hong Gong and Shi Xian about it.

entries.zh: 顯、恭恐望之自訟，下於它吏，即挾朋及待詔華龍。
entries.en: Shi Xian and Hong Gong feared that Wangzhi would defend himself and the case would be handed to other officials. They therefore pressured Peng and Hua Long, another man awaiting imperial summons, into acting against him.
entries.literal: Shi Xian and Hong Gong feared that Wangzhi would defend himself and that the matter would then be referred to other officials, so they immediately brought pressure to bear on Peng and Hua Long, who was awaiting imperial summons.

entries.zh: 龍者，宣帝時與張子蟜等待詔，以行汙濊不進，欲入堪等，堪等不納，故與朋相結。
entries.en: Hua Long had once awaited summons with Zhang Zijiao and others under Emperor Xuan; his foul conduct blocked advancement, and when Zhou Kan's circle refused him he allied with Peng.
entries.literal: Long had in Emperor Xuan's time awaited summons with Zhang Zijiao and others; because his conduct was filthy he did not advance, wished to join Kan and the rest, and when they would not take him in he allied with Peng.

entries.zh: 恭、顯令二人告望之等謀欲罷車騎將軍疏退許、史狀，候望之出休日，令朋、龍上之。
entries.en: Hong Gong and Shi Xian had the two accuse Wangzhi and his allies of plotting to remove General Shi Gao and of memorializing to oust the Xu and Shi clans; they waited for Wangzhi's day off and had Peng and Long submit the charge.
entries.literal: Gong and Xian had the two men accuse Wangzhi and company of plotting to remove the chariot-and-cavalry general and of memorializing to push aside Xu and Shi; they waited for Wangzhi's day off and had Peng and Long submit it.

entries.zh: 事下弘恭問狀，望之對曰：「外戚在位多奢淫，欲以匡正國家，非為邪也。」
entries.en: The case went to Hong Gong for investigation. Wangzhi replied, "The consort clans in power are mostly extravagant; our aim was to correct the state, not to do wrong."
entries.literal: The matter went down to Hong Gong for inquiry. Wangzhi answered, saying: "The outer kin in office are mostly extravagant and licentious; the aim is to correct the state, not to do evil."

entries.zh: 恭、顯奏「望之、堪、更生朋黨相稱舉，數譖訴大臣，毀離親戚，欲以專擅權勢，為臣不忠，誣上不道，請謁者召致廷尉。」
entries.en: Hong Gong and Shi Xian memorialized that "Wangzhi, Zhou Kan, and Liu Gengsheng had formed a faction, repeatedly slandered great ministers, divided kinsmen, and sought to monopolize power; as disloyal ministers guilty of impiety toward the throne, they asked that an usher deliver them to the commandant of justice."
entries.literal: Gong and Xian memorialized: "Wangzhi, Kan, and Gengsheng formed a faction praising one another, repeatedly slandering great ministers, tearing apart relatives, wishing to monopolize power; as ministers they are disloyal and have deceived the sovereign with impiety—we request that an usher summon them before the commandant of justice."

entries.zh: 時上初即位，不省「謁者召致廷尉」為下獄也，可其奏。
entries.en: The newly enthroned emperor did not realize that "summon before the commandant of justice" meant prison; he approved their memorial.
entries.literal: At that time the sovereign had just ascended the throne and did not understand that "usher summons before the commandant of justice" meant imprisonment; he approved the memorial.

entries.zh: 後上召堪、更生，曰繫獄。
entries.en: When the emperor later summoned Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng, he was told they were already in prison.
entries.literal: Later the sovereign summoned Kan and Gengsheng and was told they were in prison.

entries.zh: 上大驚曰：「非但廷尉問邪？」
entries.en: The emperor was shocked and said, "Surely this is not mere questioning by the commandant of justice?"
entries.literal: The sovereign was greatly startled and said: "Is it not merely questioning by the commandant of justice?"

entries.zh: 以責恭、顯，皆叩頭謝。
entries.en: He rebuked Hong Gong and Shi Xian, and both kowtowed in apology.
entries.literal: He rebuked Gong and Xian, and both knocked their heads and apologized.

entries.zh: 上曰：「令出視事。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "Let them go out and resume their duties."
entries.literal: The sovereign said: "Let them go out and resume their duties."

entries.zh: 恭、顯因使高言：「上新即位，未以德化聞於天下，而先驗師傅，既下九卿大夫獄，宜因決免。」
entries.en: Hong Gong and Shi Xian then had Shi Gao speak, saying, "Your Majesty has just taken the throne and your transforming virtue is not yet known throughout the realm, yet you have first put your tutors on trial. Now that nine ministers and grandees sit in prison, you ought to dismiss them at once."
entries.literal: Gong and Xian then had Gao speak, saying: "The sovereign has newly ascended the throne and his transforming virtue is not yet known throughout the realm, yet he has first put his tutors to the test; now that nine ministers and grandees are in prison, he ought to take this occasion to dismiss them."

entries.zh: 於是制詔丞相御史：「前將軍望之傅朕八年，亡它罪過，今事久遠，識忘難明。
entries.en: An edict then went to the chancellor and imperial counselor: "Former general Wangzhi instructed Us for eight years without other fault; the affair is long past and hard to clarify.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to the chancellor and imperial counselor: "Former general Wangzhi tutored Us eight years without other fault; the matter is long past and memory hard to clarify.

entries.zh: 其赦望之罪，收前將軍光祿勳印綬，及堪、更生皆免為庶人。」
entries.en: Pardon Wangzhi, take back his seals as former general and superintendent of the household, and dismiss Zhou Kan and Liu Gengsheng to commoner status."
entries.literal: Pardon Wangzhi's crime, take back the seals of former general and superintendent of the household, and let Kan and Gengsheng all be dismissed as commoners."

entries.zh: 而朋為黃門郎。
entries.en: Peng was made a gentleman of the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: And Peng was made a gentleman of the yellow gates.

entries.zh: 望之既左遷，而黃霸代為御史大夫。
entries.en: Wangzhi's demotion opened the path for Huang Ba as imperial counselor.
entries.literal: After Wangzhi was demoted, Huang Ba replaced him as imperial counselor.

entries.zh: 數月間，丙吉薨，霸為丞相。
entries.en: Bing Ji died within months, and Ba stepped up to the chancellorship.
entries.literal: Within a few months Bing Ji died; Ba became chancellor.

entries.zh: 霸薨，於定國復代焉。
entries.en: When Ba in turn died, Yu Dingguo inherited the post.
entries.literal: When Ba died, Yu Dingguo succeeded him in turn.

entries.zh: 望之遂見廢，不得相。
entries.en: Wangzhi had been passed over; the chancellorship never came to him.
entries.literal: Wangzhi was thus set aside and never became chancellor.

entries.zh: 為太傅，以《論語》、《禮服》授皇太子。
entries.en: As grand tutor he lectured the crown prince on the Analects and the Mourning Dress classic.
entries.literal: As grand tutor he instructed the heir apparent in the Analects and Mourning Dress.

entries.zh: 顯等封以付謁者，敕令召望之手付，因令太常急發執金吾車騎馳圍其第。
entries.en: They sealed the order, told the usher to hand it to Wangzhi in person, and had the Grand Master of Ceremonies rouse the metropolitan commandant to surround his house with horse and chariot.
entries.literal: Xian and others sealed the document and handed it to the yeoman, ordering him to summon Wangzhi and deliver it by hand, and also ordered the Grand Master of Ceremonies to hurry dispatch the metropolitan commandant's chariot and cavalry troops to gallop and surround his residence.

entries.zh: 使者至，召望之。
entries.en: The messenger came and summoned him.
entries.literal: When the envoy arrived, he summoned Wangzhi.

entries.zh: 望之欲自殺，其夫人止之，以為非天子意。
entries.en: Wangzhi wanted to kill himself, but his wife stopped him, convinced that this could not be the emperor's intention.
entries.literal: Wangzhi wished to kill himself; his wife stopped him, thinking it was not the Son of Heaven's intent.

entries.zh: 望之以問門下生朱雲。
entries.en: He turned to his disciple Zhu Yun for counsel.
entries.literal: Wangzhi asked his student Zhu Yun about it.

entries.zh: 雲者好節士，勸望之自裁。
entries.en: Yun, a man who honored uncompromising heroes, urged suicide.
entries.literal: Yun was one who admired men of integrity; he urged Wangzhi to take his own life.

entries.zh: 於是望之仰天歎曰：「吾嘗備位將相，年逾六十矣，老入牢獄，苟求生活，不亦鄙乎！」
entries.en: Wangzhi looked skyward and cried, "I have worn general's and minister's ribbons; I am past sixty—would I crawl through a jail for a few more breaths?"
entries.literal: Thereupon Wangzhi, sighing toward heaven, said, "I have filled the posts of general and minister; my years exceed sixty; to enter old age in prison and cravenly cling to life—would it not be base!"

entries.zh: 字謂雲曰：「游，趣和藥來，無久留我死！」
entries.en: Addressing Zhu Yun by his courtesy name, Wangzhi said, "You, hurry and bring the poison. Do not keep me waiting to die!"
entries.literal: Addressing Zhu Yun by his courtesy name, he said, "You, hurry and bring the prepared poison. Do not delay my death!"

entries.zh: 竟飲鴆自殺。
entries.en: He drank the poison and died.
entries.literal: In the end he drank poison and killed himself.

entries.zh: 天子聞之驚，拊手曰：「曩固疑其不就牢獄，果然殺吾賢傅！」
entries.en: The emperor struck his hands together in shock. "I feared from the first that he would never submit to prison. They have killed my worthy tutor!"
entries.literal: When the emperor heard, he was startled and struck his hands together: "I suspected from the first that he would not submit to imprisonment. They have indeed killed my worthy tutor!"

entries.zh: 是時，太官方上晝食，上乃卻食，為之涕泣，哀慟左右。
entries.en: The noon meal had just arrived; he pushed it away and wept until his attendants wept with him.
entries.literal: At that time the palace kitchen had just served the noon meal; the emperor then pushed aside his food, wept for him, and grieved until those at his left and right were stricken.

entries.zh: 於是召顯等責問以議不詳。
entries.en: He called in Shi Xian and his party and scolded them for the careless memorial.
entries.literal: Thereupon he summoned Xian and others and rebuked them for the memorial not having been thorough.

entries.zh: 皆免冠謝，良久然後已。
entries.en: They doffed their caps and begged forgiveness until the storm slowly passed.
entries.literal: All took off their caps and apologized; only after a long time did it stop.

entries.zh: 望之有罪死，有司請絕其爵邑。
entries.en: Because he had died a condemned man, the ministries asked to revoke his title and fief.
entries.literal: Wangzhi having died under accusation, the offices requested to strip his noble rank and fief.

entries.zh: 有詔加恩，長子伋嗣為關內侯。
entries.en: By special edict, his eldest son Ji was allowed to inherit the rank of Marquis within the Passes.
entries.literal: An edict extended special favor, allowing his eldest son Ji to succeed as Marquis within the Passes.

entries.zh: 天子追念望之，不忘每歲時遣使者祠祭望之塚，終元帝世。
entries.en: For the rest of Emperor Yuan's reign the court sent offerings to his tomb every season.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven thought back on Wangzhi; each year he did not fail to send envoys to sacrifice at Wangzhi's tomb—for the whole of Emperor Yuan's reign.

entries.zh: 望之八子，至大官者育、咸、由。
entries.en: Of his eight sons, Yu, Xian, and You rose highest.
entries.literal: Wangzhi had eight sons; those who reached high office were Yu, Xian, and You.

entries.zh: 育字次君，少以父任為太子庶子。
entries.en: Yu, courtesy name Cijun, entered service young as palace attendant to the crown prince through his father's influence.
entries.literal: Yu, courtesy name Cijun, in youth by his father's appointment became palace attendant to the heir.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，為郎，病免，後為御史。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan took the throne he became a court gentleman, retired on grounds of illness, and later served as an imperial clerk.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he became a gentleman; illness led to dismissal, and later he became an imperial clerk.

entries.zh: 大將軍王鳳以育名父子，著材能，除為功曹，遷謁者，使匈奴副校尉。
entries.en: Grand General Wang Feng, noting the fame of father and son and Yu's proven ability, made him merit officer, then usher, then deputy colonel on a Xiongnu mission.
entries.literal: Grand general Wang Feng, because Yu was a famous father and son with manifest talent, appointed him merit officer, transferred him to usher, and made him deputy colonel on mission to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 後為茂陵令，會課，育第六。
entries.en: He later became magistrate of Maoling; at the annual review he ranked sixth.
entries.literal: Later he became magistrate of Maoling; at the annual review Yu ranked sixth.

entries.zh: 而漆令郭舜殿，見責問，育為之請，扶風怒曰：「君課第六，裁自脫，何暇欲為左右言？」
entries.en: Magistrate Guo Shun of Qi ranked last and was rebuked; Yu pleaded for him. The governor of Fufeng snapped, "You ranked sixth yourself and barely escaped censure—what business have you speaking for others?"
entries.literal: But the magistrate of Qi, Guo Shun, was last; he was rebuked and questioned, and Yu pleaded for him. The governor of Fufeng grew angry and said: "Your review rank is sixth—you barely escape yourself; what leisure have you to speak for others?"

entries.zh: 及罷出，傳召茂陵令詣後曹，當以職事對。
entries.en: After court he was summoned to the rear bureau to answer on official business.
entries.literal: When the session ended and they went out, a summons was sent for the magistrate of Maoling to go to the rear bureau and answer on official business.

entries.zh: 育徑出曹，書佐隨牽育，育案佩刀曰：「蕭育杜陵男子，何詣曹也！」
entries.en: Yu walked straight out; a clerk grabbed him, and Yu gripped his sword and cried, "I am Xiao Yu of Duling—why should I go to the bureau!"
entries.literal: Yu went straight out of the bureau; a clerical assistant followed and pulled at Yu; Yu set hand to the sword at his belt and said: "Xiao Yu, a man of Duling—why should I go to the bureau!"

entries.zh: 遂趨出，欲去官。
entries.en: He strode out, ready to resign.
entries.literal: He then hurried out, wishing to resign office.

entries.zh: 明旦，詔召入，拜為司隸校尉。
entries.en: The next morning an edict summoned him and appointed him colonel director of the retainers.
entries.literal: The next morning an edict summoned him in and he was appointed colonel director of the retainers.

entries.zh: 育過扶風府門，官屬掾史數百人拜謁車下。
entries.en: As he passed the Fufeng government gate, hundreds of officials bowed beneath his carriage.
entries.literal: When Yu passed the gate of the Fufeng government, several hundred clerks and assistants of the officials bowed in homage beneath his carriage.

entries.zh: 後坐失大將軍指免官。
entries.en: He was later dismissed for failing to follow Grand General Wang Feng's instructions.
entries.literal: Later he was dismissed from office for failing to follow the grand general's instructions.

entries.zh: 復為中郎將使匈奴。
entries.en: He was again made leader of the palace gentlemen on a Xiongnu mission.
entries.literal: He was again made leader of the palace gentlemen on mission to the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 歷冀州、青州兩郡刺史，長水校尉，泰山太守，入守大鴻臚。
entries.en: He served as inspector of Ji and Qing provinces, colonel of the Chang River guard, governor of Taishan, and finally grand messenger.
entries.literal: He served successively as inspector of the two commanderies Jizhou and Qingzhou, colonel of the Chang River guard, governor of Taishan, and entered to hold the post of grand messenger.

entries.zh: 以鄠名賊梁子政阻山為害，久不伏辜，育為右扶風數月，盡誅子政等。
entries.en: When the notorious bandit Liang Zizheng of Hu had long defied the law from the hills, Yu as governor of Right Fufeng exterminated him and his band within months.
entries.literal: Because the notorious bandit Liang Zizheng of Hu blocked the mountains and did harm and long would not submit to punishment, Yu as governor of Right Fufeng within several months executed Zizheng and the rest entirely.

entries.zh: 坐與定陵侯淳于長厚善免官。
entries.en: He was dismissed for his close friendship with Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang.
entries.literal: He was dismissed from office for being on intimate terms with Dingling Marquis Chunyu Chang.

entries.zh: 後數月，制詔御史：「國之將興，尊師而重傅。
entries.en: Months later the emperor told the counselor: "A rising state exalts its teachers.
entries.literal: Several months later an edict to the imperial counselor: "When a state is about to flourish, it honors its teacher and esteems its tutor.

entries.zh: 故前將軍望之傅朕八年，道以經術，厥功茂焉。
entries.en: The former general Wangzhi instructed Us in the classics for eight years with conspicuous merit.
entries.literal: Therefore the former general Wangzhi tutored Us eight years, guiding Us with the classics; his merit was abundant.

entries.zh: 其賜望之爵關內侯，食邑六百戶，給事中，朝朔望，坐次將軍」天子方倚欲以為丞相，會望之子散騎中郎伋上書訟望之前事，事下有司，復奏：「望之前所坐明白，無譖訴者，而教子上書，稱引亡辜之《詩》，失大臣體，不敬，請逮捕。」
entries.en: Let Wangzhi be granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, an estate of six hundred households, the status of Palace Attendant, audiences at the new and full moons, and a seat immediately below the generals." The emperor was then relying on Wangzhi and intended to make him chancellor. Just then Wangzhi's son Ji, a Gentleman of the Cavalry, petitioned to reopen his father's former case. The responsible offices replied that the earlier charges were clear and no one had slandered him; by instructing his son to submit a memorial and quote an Ode proclaiming innocence, Wangzhi had violated the bearing of a great minister and shown disrespect. They requested his arrest.
entries.literal: Let Wangzhi be granted the rank of Marquis within the Passes, an estate of six hundred households, the status of Palace Attendant, audience at the new and full moons, and a seat immediately below the generals." The emperor was then relying on Wangzhi and intended to make him chancellor. Just then Wangzhi's son Ji, a Gentleman of the Cavalry, submitted a memorial disputing his father's former case. The matter was referred to the responsible offices, which again reported: "The charges on which Wangzhi was previously convicted are clear, and no one falsely accused him. Yet he instructed his son to memorialize and cite an Ode proclaiming innocence. This violates the bearing of a great minister and is disrespectful. We request his arrest."

entries.zh: 弘恭、石顯等知望之素高節，不詘辱，建白：「望之前為將軍輔政，欲排退許、史，專權擅朝。
entries.en: Hong Gong, Shi Xian, and the others knew that Wangzhi had always maintained lofty integrity and would not bend under humiliation, so they reported, "When Wangzhi formerly assisted the government as general, he wanted to push aside the Xu and Shi families and monopolize power at court.
entries.literal: Hong Gong, Shi Xian, and others knew Wangzhi had always borne lofty integrity and would not bend to humiliation; they memorialized: "Wangzhi formerly as general aided the government, wishing to push aside Xu and Shi and monopolize the court.

entries.zh: 幸得不坐，復賜爵邑，與聞政事，不悔過服罪，深懷怨望，教子上書，歸非於上，自以托師傅，懷終不坐。
entries.en: Spared once, enriched again, and still in council, he showed no remorse, nursed a grudge, coached his son to blame the throne, and assumed the tutor's mantle would shield him forever.
entries.literal: Fortunate enough to escape conviction, again granted rank and fief, participating in government—yet he has not repented or accepted guilt, harbors deep resentment, taught his son to memorialize, attributing fault to the sovereign, trusting on his status as tutor, expecting never to be convicted.

entries.zh: 非頗詘望之於牢獄，塞其怏怏心，則聖朝亡以施恩厚。」
entries.en: Only by humbling him behind bars could the court stifle his sulk and still show mercy."
entries.literal: Unless Wangzhi is somewhat broken into prison to stop his sullen heart, the sagely court will have no way to show generous favor."

entries.zh: 上曰：「蕭太傅素剛，安肯就吏？」
entries.en: The emperor protested, "The grand tutor is proud—he will never submit to petty clerks."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Grand Tutor Xiao has always been rigid; how would he consent to go to the clerks?"

entries.zh: 顯等曰：「人命至重，望之所坐，語言薄罪，必亡所憂。」
entries.en: Shi Xian and the others said, "Human life is weightiest; the charge against Wangzhi is a light offense of words—he is sure to have nothing to fear."
entries.literal: Xian and others said, "Human life is weightiest; what Wangzhi is charged with is a light offense of words—he is sure to have nothing to fear."

entries.zh: 上乃可其奏。
entries.en: The emperor relented and approved the arrest.
entries.literal: The emperor then approved their memorial.

entries.zh: 卷七十八 蕭望之傳第四十八
entries.en: Volume 78: Biography of Xiao Wangzhi, the forty-eighth.
entries.literal: Volume 78, Biography of Xiao Wangzhi, Number 48.

entries.zh: 漢興，文帝時馮唐顯名，即代相子也。
entries.en: Under Han, Feng Tang won renown under Emperor Wen—he was that chancellor of Dai's son.
entries.literal: When Han arose, in Emperor Wen's time Feng Tang became famous; he was the son of the chancellor of Dai.

entries.zh: 至武帝末，奉世以良家子選為郎。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Wu's reign he was chosen from a respectable household and entered service as a court gentleman.
entries.literal: By the end of Emperor Wu's reign, Fengshi was selected from a good family to serve as a court gentleman.

entries.zh: 昭帝時，以功次補武安長。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhao he earned appointment as magistrate of Wu'an by seniority of service.
entries.literal: In Emperor Zhao's time, by order of merit he was appointed magistrate of Wu'an.

entries.zh: 失官，年三十餘矣，乃學《春秋》涉大義，讀兵法明習，前將軍韓增奏以為軍司空令。
entries.en: Stripped of rank past thirty, he mastered the Spring and Autumn, absorbed its large themes, and pored over strategy until the former general Han Zeng nominated him as director of the army works command.
entries.literal: He lost office; already past thirty, he then studied the Spring and Autumn Annals and grasped its great principles, read military texts until expert, and the former general Han Zeng memorialized to appoint him director of the army works command.

entries.zh: 本始中，從軍擊匈奴。
entries.en: During Benshi he campaigned with the host against the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: In the Benshi period he followed the army to strike the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 軍罷，復為郎。
entries.en: After demobilization he returned to the gentleman corps.
entries.literal: When the army was disbanded, he again became a gentleman.

entries.zh: 馮奉世字子明，上黨潞人也，徙杜陵。
entries.en: Feng Fengshi, style Ziming, came from Lu in Shangdang and later settled at Duling.
entries.literal: Feng Fengshi, courtesy name Ziming, was a man of Lu in Shangdang; his family moved to Duling.

entries.zh: 其先馮亭，為韓上黨守。
entries.en: His forebear Feng Ting had held Shangdang for the state of Han.
entries.literal: His ancestor was Feng Ting, who was governor of Shangdang for Han.

entries.zh: 秦攻上黨，絕太行道，韓不能守，馮亭乃入上黨城守於趙。
entries.en: When Qin severed the Taihang passes and Han could not defend the commandery, Feng Ting turned the territory over to Zhao and defended it in Zhao's name.
entries.literal: Qin attacked Shangdang, cut the Taihang road, and Han could not hold it; Feng Ting thereupon entered the city of Shangdang and held it for Zhao.

entries.zh: 趙封馮亭為華陽君，與趙將括距秦，戰死於長平。
entries.en: Zhao enfeoffed him as lord of Huayang; he fought beside the general Zhao Kuo against Qin and fell at Changping.
entries.literal: Zhao ennobled Feng Ting as lord of Huayang; with the Zhao general Kuo he resisted Qin and died in battle at Changping.

entries.zh: 宗族由是分散，或留潞，或在趙。
entries.en: The clan scattered; one branch stayed in Lu, another in Zhao.
entries.literal: The lineage was thereby scattered; some remained in Lu, some were in Zhao.

entries.zh: 在趙者為官帥將，官帥將子為代相。
entries.en: The Zhao branch produced garrison commanders, and a commander's son rose to chancellor of Dai.
entries.literal: Those in Zhao became commanders of garrison officers; a son of a garrison commander became chancellor of Dai.

entries.zh: 及秦滅六國，而馮亭之後馮毋擇、馮去疾、馮劫皆為秦將相焉。
entries.en: After Qin swallowed the rival kingdoms, Feng Ting's descendants Wuzhe, Quji, and Jie all served Qin as generals and ministers.
entries.literal: When Qin extinguished the six states, descendants of Feng Ting—Feng Wuzhe, Feng Quji, and Feng Jie—all became generals and ministers of Qin.

entries.zh: 先是時，漢數出使西域，多辱命不稱，或貪污，為外國所苦。
entries.en: Han envoys to the Western Regions had often failed or grown rich at local expense, to the outer states' misery.
entries.literal: Earlier, Han had repeatedly sent envoys to the Western Regions; many disgraced their commissions or proved unworthy, some were corrupt, and the outer states suffered for it.

entries.zh: 是時，烏孫大有擊匈奴之功，而西域諸國新輯，漢方善遇，欲以安之，選可使外國者。
entries.en: Wusun had lately bloodied the Xiongnu, the Tarim states were settling under Han favor, and the court wanted a trustworthy envoy.
entries.literal: At that time Wusun had achieved great merit in striking the Xiongnu, while the states of the Western Regions had newly been brought to order; Han was treating them generously and wished to pacify them, and therefore selected one who could be sent abroad.

entries.zh: 前將軍增舉奉世以衛候使持節送大宛諸國客。
entries.en: Han Zeng nominated him as guard commandant bearing the staff to convoy Ferghana's party and the rest.
entries.literal: The former general Han Zeng recommended Fengshi as guard commandant with staff of authority to escort the guests of Ferghana and the other states.

entries.zh: 至伊脩城，都尉宋將言莎車與旁國共攻殺漢所置莎車王萬年，並殺漢使者奚充國。
entries.en: At Yixiu the local commandant Song Jiang warned that Shache and allies had murdered Wannian, Han's puppet king of Shache, and slaughtered envoy Xi Chongguo.
entries.literal: When he reached Yixiu city, commandant Song Jiang reported that Shache together with neighboring states had jointly attacked and killed Wannian, the king of Shache whom Han had installed, and had also killed Han's envoy Xi Chongguo.

entries.zh: 時，匈奴又發兵攻車師城，不能下而去。
entries.en: The Xiongnu had just besieged Jushi without success and marched away.
entries.literal: At that time the Xiongnu had again sent troops to attack the city of Jushi but could not take it and withdrew.

entries.zh: 莎車遣使揚言北道諸國已屬匈奴矣，於是攻劫南道，與歃盟畔漢，從鄯善以西皆絕不通。
entries.en: Shache's envoys proclaimed that the states of the northern route already belonged to the Xiongnu; they then raided the southern route, swore a blood-oath alliance, rebelled against Han, and cut off communication west of Shanshan.
entries.literal: Shache sent envoys to boast that the states of the northern route already belonged to the Xiongnu; thereupon it raided the southern route, smeared blood in alliance, rebelled against Han, and from Shanshan westward all communication was cut.

entries.zh: 都護鄭吉、校尉司馬意皆在北道諸國間。
entries.en: Protector-general Zheng Ji and colonel Sima Yi were tied up on the northern line.
entries.literal: The protector-general Zheng Ji and colonel Sima Yi were both among the states of the northern route.

entries.zh: 奉世與其副嚴昌計，以為不亟擊之則莎車日強，其勢難制，必危西域。
entries.en: Fengshi and deputy Yan Chang judged that delay would let Shache swell until the whole region slipped from Han control.
entries.literal: Fengshi and his deputy Yan Chang planned, holding that unless they struck quickly Shache would grow stronger day by day, its power hard to control, and the Western Regions would surely be endangered.

entries.zh: 遂以節諭告諸國王，因發其兵，南北道合萬五千人進擊莎車，攻拔其城。
entries.en: He invoked the staff, rallied the kings, and raised fifteen thousand men from both routes to storm Shache and take its walls.
entries.literal: Thereupon with the staff he issued proclamations to the kings of the states and mobilized their troops; the northern and southern routes combined fifteen thousand men and advanced to attack Shache, storming and taking its city.

entries.zh: 莎車王自殺，傳其首詣長安。
entries.en: The Shache king committed suicide; his head went to Chang'an.
entries.literal: The king of Shache killed himself; his head was sent to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 諸國悉平，威振西域。
entries.en: The oases submitted; his name thundered across the Tarim.
entries.literal: All the states were pacified; his might shook the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 奉世乃罷兵以聞。
entries.en: Fengshi stood the army down and memorialized what he had done.
entries.literal: Fengshi thereupon disbanded the troops and reported the matter.

entries.zh: 宣帝召見韓增，曰：「賀將軍所舉得其人。」
entries.en: Emperor Xuan called in Han Zeng and said, "Your nomination was sound."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan summoned Han Zeng and said, "We congratulate the general on recommending the right man."

entries.zh: 奉世遂西至大苑。
entries.en: He then pushed on west to Ferghana.
entries.literal: Fengshi thereupon proceeded west to Ferghana.

entries.zh: 大苑聞其斬莎車王，敬之異於它使。
entries.en: Ferghana, learning he had decapitated the Shache king, treated him with a respect no other envoy had known.
entries.literal: Ferghana, hearing that he had beheaded the king of Shache, honored him differently from other envoys.

entries.zh: 得其名馬象龍而還。
entries.en: He brought back the celebrated "Elephant Dragon" steed.
entries.literal: He obtained their famous horse "Elephant Dragon" and returned.

entries.zh: 上甚說，下議封奉世。
entries.en: The throne was delighted and ordered discussion of a fief for Fengshi.
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and sent the matter down for deliberation on enfeoffing Fengshi.

entries.zh: 丞相、將軍皆曰：「《春秋》之義，大夫出疆，有可以安國家，則顓之可也。
entries.en: The chancellor and the generals all said, "According to the principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a grandee goes beyond the borders, he may act on his own authority if doing so can secure the state.
entries.literal: The chancellor and the generals all said, "By the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a grandee goes beyond the frontier, if there is something by which the state can be secured, specialized authority is permissible.

entries.zh: 奉世功傚尤著，宜加爵士之賞。」
entries.en: Fengshi's achievement stood out; he deserved noble rank and a fief."
entries.literal: Fengshi's merit and effect were especially conspicuous; he should receive reward of rank and fief."

entries.zh: 少府蕭望之獨以奉世奉使有指，而擅矯制違命，發諸國兵，雖有功效，不可以為後法。
entries.en: Xiao Wangzhi alone argued that Fengshi had carried fixed orders yet counterfeited an imperial rescript and mobilized foreign troops without warrant—precedent-making even if successful.
entries.literal: Junior privy treasurer Xiao Wangzhi alone held that Fengshi had gone on mission with definite orders, yet on his own forged an edict and disobeyed command in raising the troops of the states; though there was merit and effect, it cannot be taken as a precedent for later.

entries.zh: 即封奉世，開後奉使者利，以奉世為比，爭逐發兵，要功萬里之外，為國家生事於夷狄。
entries.en: Ennobling him would tempt every future envoy to raise armies for glory ten thousand li away and embroil the court in barbarian quarrels.
entries.literal: If Fengshi is enfeoffed, it opens the way for later envoys to profit, taking Fengshi as their model, competing to raise troops and seek merit beyond ten thousand li, thereby creating trouble for the state among the Yi and Di.

entries.zh: 漸不可長，奉世不宜受封。
entries.en: Such habits must not be fed; Fengshi should not take a fief.
entries.literal: What gradually grows must not be encouraged; Fengshi should not receive a fief.

entries.zh: 上善望之議，以奉世為光祿大夫、水衡都尉。
entries.en: The emperor took Wangzhi's side, naming Fengshi grand counselor of the palace and superintendent of the palace parks instead.
entries.literal: The emperor approved Wangzhi's proposal and appointed Fengshi grand counselor of the palace and superintendent of the palace parks.

entries.zh: 上於是以璽書勞奉世，且讓之，曰：「皇帝問將兵右將軍，甚苦暴露。
entries.en: The throne answered with a sealed rescript both praising and scolding: "The emperor asks his right general: you have borne hard weather long.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon with a rescript on the imperial seal consoled Fengshi and also reproached him, saying, "The emperor asks the right general who leads troops: you have greatly suffered exposure in the open.

entries.zh: 羌虜侵邊境，殺吏民，甚逆天道，故遣將軍帥士大夫行天誅。
entries.en: The Qiang murder our people and offend Heaven; We send you to execute that sentence with gentry and troops.
entries.literal: The Qiang raiders encroach on the border, kill officials and common people, greatly oppose Heaven's way; therefore We dispatch the general to lead gentlemen and officials to carry out Heaven's punishment.

entries.zh: 以將軍材質之美，奮精兵，誅不軌，百下百全之道也。
entries.en: Given your gifts and picked soldiers, lawless men should fall at the first blow.
entries.literal: With the general's fine quality of stuff and wielding crack troops to execute the lawless, it is the way of a hundred descents and a hundred completenesses.

entries.zh: 今乃有畔敵之名，大為中國羞。
entries.en: Yet the army is matched against the foe—a deep shame to China.
entries.literal: Now instead there is the reputation of matching the enemy, greatly shaming the Middle Kingdom.

entries.zh: 以昔不閑習之故邪？
entries.en: Is it want of training?
entries.literal: Is it because of former lack of practice and drill?

entries.zh: 以恩厚未洽，信約不明也？
entries.en: Or because our kindness and clear pledges have not reached them?
entries.literal: Or because favor and kindness have not fully penetrated, trust and covenant are not clear?

entries.zh: 朕甚怪之。
entries.en: We are much perplexed.
entries.literal: We are greatly puzzled by it.

entries.zh: 上書言羌虜依深山，多徑道，不得不多分部遮要害，須得後發營士，足以決事，部署已定，勢不可復置大將，聞之。
entries.en: Your letter says the Qiang hold the heights and many trails, so you must split the army to seal choke points and wait for reinforcements to decide the fight; dispositions are set and a new high commander would only tangle them—We have read you.
entries.literal: Your memorial states that the Qiang raiders rely on deep mountains and many bypaths, so you cannot but divide the army in many parts to block the critical points, and that you must await later-arriving camp troops to be sufficient to settle the affair; deployment is already fixed and the situation cannot again accommodate a great general—We have heard it.

entries.zh: 前為將軍兵少，不足自守，故發近所騎，日夜詣，非為擊也。
entries.en: We rushed local cavalry to you earlier because your numbers could not hold the line, not to take command of the attack from you.
entries.literal: Earlier, because the general's troops were few and insufficient to guard yourselves, therefore We raised nearby cavalry, day and night hurrying to you—it was not for attack.

entries.zh: 今發三輔、河東、弘農越騎、跡射、佽飛、彀者、羽林孤兒及呼速累、嗕種，方急遣。
entries.en: We now press toward you the swift riders, trace archers, flying spears, crossbow specialists, palace orphans, and tribal auxiliaries from the capital districts, Hedong, and Hongnang.
entries.literal: Now We are dispatching in urgent haste the swift riders, trace-and-shoot archers, flying spearmen, crossbowmen, Forest of Feathers orphans, and the Husuli and Ru tribes from the three adjuncts, Hedong, and Hongnang.

entries.zh: 且兵，凶器也，必有成敗者，患策不豫定，料敵不審也，故復遣奮武將軍。
entries.en: Arms are ill omens; victory turns on forethought and intelligence of the foe—hence the second general Who Rouses Might.
entries.literal: Moreover troops are inauspicious instruments; there must be those who succeed or fail—the worry is that plans are not settled in advance and the enemy is not carefully gauged; therefore We again dispatch the general Who Rouses Might.

entries.zh: 兵法曰大將軍出必有偏裨，所以揚威武，參計策，將軍又何疑焉？
entries.en: The canon says every commander needs lieutenants to lend weight and counsel—do not take offense.
entries.literal: Military texts say that when a great general goes out there must be wing commanders, whereby martial awesomeness is displayed and plans are consulted—why should the general doubt?

entries.zh: 夫愛吏士，得眾心，舉而無悔，禽敵必全，將軍之職也。
entries.en: Cherish the men, win their loyalty, strike without regret, and annihilate the foe—that is your charge.
entries.literal: To cherish officers and soldiers, win the host's hearts, move without regret, and capture the enemy completely—this is a general's duty.

entries.zh: 若乃轉輸之費，則有司存，將軍勿憂。
entries.en: Supply is the ministries' problem, not yours.
entries.literal: As for the costs of transport, the offices exist for that; let the general not worry.

entries.zh: 須奮武將軍兵到，合擊羌虜。」
entries.en: Stand until Who Rouses Might arrives, then crush the Qiang together."
entries.literal: Await the arrival of the troops of the general Who Rouses Might and jointly strike the Qiang raiders."

entries.zh: 奮武將軍任千秋者，其父宮，昭帝時以丞相征事捕斬反者左將軍上官桀，封侯，宣帝時為太常，薨。
entries.en: Ren Qianqiu's father Ren Gong had served Emperor Zhao's chancellor as investigator, cut down mutineer Shangguan Jie, taken a marquisate, and ended as Grand Master of ceremonies under Xuan.
entries.literal: General Who Rouses Might Ren Qianqiu—his father was Ren Gong, who in Emperor Zhao's time, as investigating clerk to the chancellor, captured and beheaded the rebel left general Shangguan Jie, was ennobled marquis, became Grand Master of ceremonies under Emperor Xuan, and died.

entries.zh: 千秋嗣後，復為太常。
entries.en: Qianqiu inherited the fief and likewise rose to Grand Master of ceremonies.
entries.literal: Qianqiu inherited afterward and again became Grand Master of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 成帝時，樂昌侯王商代奉世為左將軍，而千秋為右將軍，後亦為左將軍。
entries.en: Under Cheng, Wang Shang of Lechang succeeded Fengshi as left general while Qianqiu held the right, then moved left in turn.
entries.literal: In Emperor Cheng's time Marquis of Lechang Wang Shang replaced Fengshi as left general, while Qianqiu was right general; later he too became left general.

entries.zh: 子孫傳國，至王莽乃絕云。
entries.en: The line held the marquisate until Wang Mang ended it.
entries.literal: Sons and grandsons transmitted the state until Wang Mang, when it was cut off.

entries.zh: 野王字君卿，受業博士，通《詩》。
entries.en: Yewang, style Junqing, studied under an erudite and mastered the Odes.
entries.literal: Yewang, courtesy name Junqing, received instruction from an erudite and was conversant with the Odes.

entries.zh: 少以父任為太子中庶子。
entries.en: As a youth he entered the heir apparent's household by yin privilege.
entries.literal: In youth by his father's privilege he became attendant to the heir apparent for the inner court.

entries.zh: 年十八，上書願試守長安令。
entries.en: At eighteen he volunteered to trial-run the magistracy of Chang'an.
entries.literal: At age eighteen he submitted a memorial begging to be tried as acting magistrate of Chang'an.

entries.zh: 宣帝奇其志，問丞相魏相，相以為不可許。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan admired the audacity; Chancellor Wei Xiang said no.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan marveled at his ambition and asked Chancellor Wei Xiang, who held it could not be permitted.

entries.zh: 後以功次補當陽長，遷為櫟陽令，徙夏陽令。
entries.en: He later rose through Dangyang, Liyang, and Xiayang by merit.
entries.literal: Later by order of merit he was appointed magistrate of Dangyang, was promoted magistrate of Liyang, and transferred magistrate of Xiayang.

entries.zh: 元帝時，遷隴西太守，以治行高，入為左馮翊。
entries.en: Under Yuan he governed Longxi with such distinction that the capital made him left governor of Fengyi.
entries.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time he was promoted governor of Longxi; because his administration was high in quality, he entered as left governor of Fengyi.

entries.zh: 歲餘，而池陽令並素行貪污，輕野王外戚年少，治行不改。
entries.en: A year in, Chiyang magistrate Bing, a grafter, sneered at Yewang as a young in-law and kept stealing.
entries.literal: After more than a year, the magistrate of Chiyang, Bing, by nature corrupt in conduct, despised Yewang as a young maternal relative of the consort and did not reform his administration.

entries.zh: 野王部督郵掾示殳祤趙都案驗，得其主守盜十金罪，收捕。
entries.en: Yewang directed his regional inspector clerk Zhao Du of Duiyu to investigate; he proved Bing's crime of embezzling ten jin of gold while in office, and arrested him.
entries.literal: Yewang ordered his regional inspector clerk to display the case to Zhao Du of Shuyi for investigation; obtaining proof of Bing's crime of guarding office property and stealing ten jin of gold, he arrested him.

entries.zh: 並不首吏，都格殺。
entries.en: Bing resisted arrest and Du killed him in the scuffle.
entries.literal: Bing would not submit to the clerks; Du struck and killed him.

entries.zh: 並家上書陳冤，事下廷尉。
entries.en: Bing's kin appealed; the file went to the commandant of justice.
entries.literal: Bing's family submitted a memorial stating grievance; the matter went down to the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 都詣吏自殺以明野王，京師稱其威信，遷為大鴻臚。
entries.en: Du killed himself at the yamen gate to spare Yewang; the capital praised his loyalty and promoted Yewang to grand herald.
entries.literal: Du went to the clerks and committed suicide to clear Yewang; the capital praised his trustworthiness and awe, and Yewang was promoted grand herald.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，為執金吾。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan he became metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he became metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 上郡屬國歸義降胡萬餘人反去。
entries.en: Over ten thousand surrendered Xiongnu of Shang commandery's dependent state rose and bolted.
entries.literal: More than ten thousand surrendered Hu of the dependent state of Shang commandery rebelled and fled.

entries.zh: 初，昭帝末，西河屬國胡伊酋若王亦將眾數千人畔，奉世輒持節將兵追擊。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Zhao's reign the Xihe dependent chieftain Yijiuoru had mutinied with thousands; Fengshi had seized the staff and run him down.
entries.literal: Earlier, at the end of Emperor Zhao's reign, the Xiongnu noble Yijiuoru king of the dependent state of Xihe also led several thousand followers in rebellion; Fengshi immediately took the staff and led troops in pursuit.

entries.zh: 右將軍典屬國常惠薨，奉世代為右將軍典屬國，加諸吏之號。
entries.en: When right general Chang Hui died, Fengshi succeeded him as right general and director of dependent states, with the collective title "various officials."
entries.literal: When the right general and director of dependent states Chang Hui died, Fengshi replaced him as right general and director of dependent states, with the added title of various officials.

entries.zh: 數歲，為光祿勳。
entries.en: A few years later he rose to superintendent of the household.
entries.literal: After several years he became superintendent of the household.

entries.zh: 奉世有子男九人，女四人。
entries.en: Fengshi fathered nine sons and four daughters.
entries.literal: Fengshi had nine sons and four daughters.

entries.zh: 長女媛以選充兵宮，為元帝昭儀，產中山孝王。
entries.en: His eldest daughter Yuan was selected for the palace women's quarters, became Brilliant Companion to Emperor Yuan, and bore the filial king of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: The eldest daughter Yuan was selected to enter the palace women's quarters, became a Brilliant Companion to Emperor Yuan, and bore the filial king of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 元帝崩，媛為中山太后，隨王就國。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan died she became dowager of Zhongshan and went with her son to his fief.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Yuan became grand empress dowager of Zhongshan and followed the king to his state.

entries.zh: 奉世長子譚，太常舉孝廉為郎，功次補天水司馬。
entries.en: Eldest son Tan, filial and incorrupt from the Grand Master of ceremonies' nomination, became a gentleman and then Tianshui marshal by seniority.
entries.literal: Fengshi's eldest son Tan was recommended filial and incorrupt by the Grand Master of ceremonies and became a gentleman, then by order of merit was appointed marshal of Tianshui.

entries.zh: 奉世擊西羌，譚為校尉，隨父從軍有功，未拜病死。
entries.en: Tan served as colonel in the Qiang war and earned merit beside his father, then died of sickness before promotion.
entries.literal: When Fengshi struck the Western Qiang, Tan was a colonel; following his father in the army he had merit, but before appointment he died of illness.

entries.zh: 譚弟野王、逡、立、參至大官。
entries.en: Younger brothers Yewang, Qun, Li, and Shen all rose high.
entries.literal: Tan's younger brothers Yewang, Qun, Li, and Shen reached high office.

entries.zh: 數年，御史大夫李延壽病卒，在位多舉野王。
entries.en: When Counselor Li Yanshou died, the bureaucracy backed Yewang.
entries.literal: Several years later Imperial Counselor Li Yanshou died of illness; many in office recommended Yewang.

entries.zh: 上使尚書選第中二千石，而野王行能第一。
entries.en: The emperor ordered the secretariat to rank the two-thousand-bushel corps; Yewang topped the list.
entries.literal: The emperor had the secretariat rank the full two-thousand-bushel officials; Yewang's conduct and ability were first.

entries.zh: 上曰：「吾用野王為三公，後世必謂我私後宮親屬，以野王為比。」
entries.en: The emperor said, "If I name him one of the Three Dukes, posterity will say I bought favor for the harem."
entries.literal: The emperor said, "If We employ Yewang among the three dukes, later generations will surely say We favored inner-palace kin, taking Yewang as the precedent."

entries.zh: 乃下詔曰：「剛強堅固，確然亡欲，大鴻臚野王是也。
entries.en: So he issued a litany of virtues: "Grand Herald Yewang is granite and free of appetite;
entries.literal: Thereupon he issued an edict, saying, "Rigid and firm, steadfastly without desire—Grand Herald Yewang is such.

entries.zh: 心辨善辭，可使四方，少府五鹿充宗是也。
entries.en: Wulu Chongzong has a ready tongue for embassies;
entries.literal: Mind discerning and skilled in speech, able to be sent to the four quarters—Junior Privy Treasurer Wulu Chongzong is such.

entries.zh: 廉潔節儉，太子少傅張譚是也。
entries.en: Zhang Tan is clean and spare;
entries.literal: Incorrupt and frugal—Junior tutor to the heir apparent Zhang Tan is such.

entries.zh: 其以少傅為御史大夫。」
entries.en: let the junior tutor take the counselor's seal."
entries.literal: Let the junior tutor become imperial counselor."

entries.zh: 上繇下第而用譚，越次避嫌不用野王，以昭儀兄故也。
entries.en: He picked lower-ranked Zhang Tan to dodge the charge of nepotism—Yewang was the Brilliant Companion's brother.
entries.literal: The emperor for this reason used Tan, who had ranked low, skipping order to avoid suspicion and not employing Yewang, because he was the elder brother of the Brilliant Companion.

entries.zh: 野王乃歎曰：「人皆以女寵貴，我兄弟獨以賤！」
entries.en: Yewang sighed and said, "Others all rise through a daughter's favor; we brothers alone are brought low by it!"
entries.literal: Yewang thereupon sighed, saying, "Others all become noble through a woman's favor; we brothers alone are brought low by it!"

entries.zh: 野王雖不為三公，甚見器重，有名當世。
entries.en: He never took a ducal chair yet remained indispensable and famous.
entries.literal: Although Yewang did not become one of the three dukes, he was greatly valued and esteemed and had a name in his generation.

entries.zh: 初，野王嗣父爵為關內侯，免歸。
entries.en: Yewang had earlier inherited marquis-within-the-passes rank and lost it.
entries.literal: Earlier, Yewang had inherited his father's rank as marquis within the passes and been dismissed to return home.

entries.zh: 數年，年老，終於家。
entries.en: Years later he died at home in old age.
entries.literal: Several years later, old in years, he ended at home.

entries.zh: 子座嗣爵，至孫坐中山太后事絕。
entries.en: Son Zuo inherited until a grandson lost the title in the Zhongshan dowager scandal.
entries.literal: His son Zuo inherited the rank; reaching the grandson, it was cut off on account of the affair of the grand empress dowager of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 參字叔平，學通《尚書》。
entries.en: Shen, style Shuping, mastered the Documents.
entries.literal: Shen, courtesy name Shuping, studied until he was thoroughly versed in the Documents.

entries.zh: 少為黃門郎給事中，宿衛十餘年，參為人矜嚴，好修容儀，進退恂恂，甚可觀也。
entries.en: As a youth he served as yellow-gate gentleman and attendant within the gates, on night watch for more than ten years. Stern and dignified, he cultivated his bearing; his measured advance and retreat were a sight to behold.
entries.literal: In youth he was a yellow-gate gentleman attendant within the gates; he kept night watch for more than ten years. Shen was by nature stern and dignified, fond of cultivating deportment; in advance and retreat he was measured and respectful—a sight very much worth seeing.

entries.zh: 參，昭儀少弟，行又敕備，以嚴見憚，終不得親近侍帷幄。
entries.en: Shen was the Brilliant Companion's younger brother; his conduct was meticulous. His severity inspired fear, and he never drew near to serve within the curtained chambers.
entries.literal: Shen was the younger brother of the Brilliant Companion; his conduct was moreover careful and complete. Because of his severity he was feared, and in the end he could not draw near to attend within the curtained chambers.

entries.zh: 竟寧中，以王舅出補渭陵食官令。
entries.en: In Jingning, as the prince's uncle, he was posted overseer of provisions at Weiling.
entries.literal: In the Jingning period, as the king's maternal uncle he went out to be appointed overseer of provisions at Weiling.

entries.zh: 以數病徙為寢中郎，有詔勿事。
entries.en: Repeated illness moved him to gentleman of the imperial tomb, with an edict excusing him from duties.
entries.literal: Because of repeated illness he was transferred to gentleman of the imperial tomb; an edict ordered that he perform no duties.

entries.zh: 陽朔中，中山王來朝，參擢為上河農都尉。
entries.en: During Yangshuo, when the King of Zhongshan came to court, Shen was raised to chief agricultural commandant of Shanghe.
entries.literal: In the Yangshuo period, when the King of Zhongshan came to court, Shen was promoted chief agricultural commandant of Shanghe.

entries.zh: 病免官，復為渭陵寢中郎。
entries.en: Illness ended his post; he returned as gentleman of the Weiling imperial tomb.
entries.literal: Illness freed him from office; he again became gentleman of the Weiling imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 永始中，超遷代郡太守。
entries.en: In Yongshi he was leap-promoted to governor of Dai.
entries.literal: In the Yongshi period he was promoted in exceptional leap to governor of Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 以邊郡道遠，徙為安定太守。
entries.en: The distant frontier route got him transferred to Anding governor.
entries.literal: Because the frontier commandery's route was distant, he was transferred to governor of Anding.

entries.zh: 數歲，病免，復為諫大夫，使領護左馮翊都水。
entries.en: Years later illness ended his term; he became grandee remonstrant and oversaw Left Fengyi waterways.
entries.literal: Several years later, illness freed him; he again became grandee remonstrant and was sent to oversee the waterways of Left Fengyi.

entries.zh: 綏和中，立定陶王為皇太子，以中山王見廢，故封王舅參為宜鄉侯，以慰王意。
entries.en: In Suihe the King of Dingtao became heir apparent; with Zhongshan deposed, the prince's uncle Shen was made Marquis of Yixiang to soothe him.
entries.literal: In the Suihe period the King of Dingtao was established as heir apparent. Because the King of Zhongshan had been deposed, the king's maternal uncle Shen was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yixiang to comfort the king's feelings.

entries.zh: 參之國，上書願至中山見王、太后。
entries.en: Going to his fief, Shen memorialized asking to visit Zhongshan and see the king and dowager.
entries.literal: When Shen went to his state, he submitted a memorial wishing to go to Zhongshan to see the king and the grand empress dowager.

entries.zh: 行未到而王薨。
entries.en: He had not yet arrived when the king died.
entries.literal: Before he arrived on the journey, the king died.

entries.zh: 王病時，上奏願貶參爵以關內侯食邑留長安。
entries.en: While ill, the king asked that Shen's rank be reduced to marquis within the passes with his fief kept at Chang'an.
entries.literal: When the king was ill, he submitted a memorial wishing to demote Shen's rank to marquis within the passes with a fiefdom left at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 上憐之，下詔曰：「中山孝王短命早薨，願以舅宜鄉侯參為關內侯，歸家，朕甚愍之。
entries.en: The emperor pitied him and issued an edict: "The Filial King of Zhongshan died young. He wished his uncle, Marquis of Yixiang Shen, made marquis within the passes and sent home. We are deeply moved.
entries.literal: The emperor pitied him and issued an edict, saying, "The Filial King of Zhongshan died young before his time. He wished that his maternal uncle, Marquis of Yixiang Shen, be made marquis within the passes and return home. We are deeply moved.

entries.zh: 其還參京師，以列侯奉朝請。」
entries.en: Let Shen return to the capital and attend court as a full marquis."
entries.literal: Let Shen return to the capital to attend court at morning audience as a full marquis."

entries.zh: 五侯皆敬憚之。
entries.en: The Five Marquises all respected and feared him.
entries.literal: The Five Marquises all respected and feared him.

entries.zh: 丞相翟方進亦甚重焉，數謂參：「物禁太甚。
entries.en: Chancellor Zhai Fangjin also esteemed him and often told Shen, "Things forbid excess.
entries.literal: Chancellor Zhai Fangjin also thought highly of him and repeatedly told Shen, "Things forbid excess.

entries.zh: 君侯以王舅見廢，不得在公卿位，今五侯至尊貴也，與之並列，宜少詘節卑體，視有所宗。
entries.en: You, my lord, as the deposed king's uncle, could not hold ministerial rank. The Five Marquises are supreme; standing among them, you should bend your manner and show deference to someone above you.
entries.literal: You, my lord, as the deposed king's maternal uncle, could not hold a ministerial post. Now the Five Marquises are supremely exalted; standing among them on equal footing, you ought to bend your manner somewhat and lower your body, showing that you have someone to look up to.

entries.zh: 而君侯盛修容貌以威嚴加之，此非所以下五侯而自益者也。」
entries.en: Yet you lavishly groom your appearance and add severity on top—that is not how to place yourself below the Five Marquises and help yourself."
entries.literal: Yet you, my lord, lavishly cultivate your appearance and pile severity on top—this is not the way to place yourself below the Five Marquises and benefit yourself."

entries.zh: 參性好禮儀，終不改其恆操。
entries.en: Shen loved ritual and decorum and never changed his steady ways.
entries.literal: Shen's nature loved ritual and decorum; to the end he did not alter his constant conduct.

entries.zh: 頃之，哀帝即位，帝祖母傅太后用事，追怨參姊中山太后，陷以祝詛大逆之罪，語在《外戚傳》。
entries.en: Soon Ai ruled; Grand Empress Dowager Fu hated Shen's sister, the Zhongshan dowager, and framed her for witchcraft—see the outer-kin annals.
entries.literal: Before long Emperor Ai ascended the throne; the emperor's grandmother Grand Empress Dowager Fu held power, nursed resentment against Shen's elder sister the grand empress dowager of Zhongshan, and trapped her with the great irreverence charge of curse-praying—the account is in the "Biography of the Outer Kin."

entries.zh: 參以同產當相坐，謁者承製召參詣廷尉，參自殺。
entries.en: Shen faced kin liability; the usher's summons to the commandant of justice drove him to suicide.
entries.literal: Shen, as born of the same womb, was to suffer joint liability; the yeoman, carrying the edict, summoned Shen to the commandant of justice, and Shen killed himself.

entries.zh: 且死，仰天歎曰：「參父子兄弟皆備大位，身至封侯，今被惡名而死，姊弟不敢自惜，傷無以見先人於地下！」
entries.en: About to die, he sighed toward heaven and said, "My father, brothers, and I have all filled high posts and attained marquis rank; now I die bearing a foul name. Sister and brother—I do not pity ourselves; I grieve only that we cannot face our ancestors underground!"
entries.literal: About to die, he sighed toward heaven, saying, "My father, brothers, and I have all filled high posts and attained marquis rank; now I die bearing a foul name. Sister and brother—I do not pity ourselves; I grieve only that we cannot face our ancestors underground!"

entries.zh: 死者十七人，眾莫不憐之。
entries.en: Seventeen lives ended; the realm wept for them.
entries.literal: Seventeen died; none among the multitude did not pity them.

entries.zh: 宗族徙歸故郡。
entries.en: The clan was deported to its ancestral commandery.
entries.literal: The lineage was moved back to the old commandery.

entries.zh: 成帝立，有司奏野王王舅，不宜備九卿，以秩出為上郡太守，加賜黃金百斤。
entries.en: At Cheng's accession the ministries barred maternal uncles from the nine ministers; Yewang went to Shang commandery with a hundred jin of gold as consolation.
entries.literal: When Emperor Cheng was established, the offices reported that Yewang, as the king's maternal uncle, was not fit to fill one of the nine ministers; by rank he was sent out as governor of Shang commandery, with an added gift of one hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 朔方刺史蕭育奏封事，薦言：「野王行能高妙，內足與圖身，外足以慮化。
entries.en: Xiao Yu, regional inspector of Shuofang, submitted a sealed memorial recommending him: "Yewang's conduct and ability are lofty and refined. At court he is capable of assisting in plans for the ruler; in the provinces he is capable of thinking through moral transformation.
entries.literal: The regional inspector of Shuofang, Xiao Yu, submitted a sealed memorial recommending, saying, "Yewang's conduct and ability are lofty and subtle; inwardly sufficient to plan for the self, outwardly sufficient to consider transformation.

entries.zh: 竊惜野王懷國之寶，而不得陪朝廷與朝者並。
entries.en: he mourned that such a jewel stood outside the hall;
entries.literal: Your servant privately pities Yewang for cherishing the state's treasure yet not being able to stand in court with those who attend audience.

entries.zh: 野王前以王舅出，以賢復入，明國家樂進賢也。」
entries.en: to recall him for talent would prove the court loves worth over kin."
entries.literal: Yewang earlier went out because he was the king's maternal uncle; now to re-enter on account of worth shows that the state delights in advancing the worthy."

entries.zh: 上自為太子時聞知野王。
entries.en: Cheng had admired Yewang since his own princedom.
entries.literal: The emperor had known of Yewang since he himself was heir apparent.

entries.zh: 會其病免，復以故二千石使行河堤，因拜為琅邪太守。
entries.en: When illness cashiered him, the court sent him, still at two-thousand-bushel rank, to inspect dikes, then named him governor of Langye.
entries.literal: It happened that he was dismissed on illness; again, as a former two-thousand-bushel official, he was sent to inspect the river dikes, and thereupon was appointed governor of Langye.

entries.zh: 是時，成帝長舅陽平侯王鳳為大司馬大將軍，輔政八九年矣，時數有災異，京兆尹王章譏鳳專權不可任用，薦野王代鳳。
entries.en: Wang Feng, Cheng's senior uncle, had run the state nearly a decade when capital governor Wang Zhang attacked his monopoly and nominated Yewang to replace him.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor's senior maternal uncle, Marquis of Yangping Wang Feng, was grand marshal and great general, aiding the government eight or nine years; at the time there were frequent disasters and prodigies; the governor of the capital, Wang Zhang, ridiculed Feng as wielding sole power unfit for employment, and recommended Yewang to replace Feng.

entries.zh: 上初納其言，而後誅章，語在《元后傳》。
entries.en: The throne first agreed, then executed Wang Zhang—the tale is told with the Yuan empress.
entries.literal: The emperor at first accepted his words, but afterward executed Zhang—the account is in the "Biography of the Yuan Empress Dowager."

entries.zh: 於是野王懼不自安，遂病，滿三月賜告，與妻子歸杜陵就醫藥。
entries.en: Yewang grew terrified, took three months' medical leave, and fled to Duling with his family.
entries.literal: Thereupon Yewang was afraid and not at ease in himself; he fell ill, and when three months of sick leave were granted, he went with wife and children to Duling to seek medicine.

entries.zh: 大將軍鳳風御史中丞劾奏野王賜告養病而私自便，持虎符出界歸家，奉詔不敬。
entries.en: Feng nudged the palace secretary to charge that Yewang had abused sick leave, crossed out of his command with the tiger tally, and insulted imperial grace.
entries.literal: Great general Feng hinted to the palace secretary to memorialize impeachment: Yewang had received granted sick leave to nurse illness but privately took convenience, held the tiger tally and crossed the boundary to return home—disrespect to an edict.

entries.zh: 杜欽時在大將軍莫府，欽素高野王父子行能，奏記於鳳，為野王言曰：「竊見令曰，吏二千石告，過長安謁，不分別予賜。
entries.en: Du Qin, in Feng's staff, argued the statute: two-thousand-bushel men passing through the capital on leave were not split between "ordinary" and "granted" sick leave;
entries.literal: Du Qin was then in the great general's headquarters; Qin had always esteemed the conduct and ability of Yewang and his father, and submitted a note to Feng, speaking for Yewang, saying, "Your servant has seen in the ordinance that when officials of two thousand bushels take leave and pass through Chang'an to audience, it does not distinguish granting ordinary versus granted sick leave.

entries.zh: 今有司以為予告得歸，賜告不得，是一律兩科，失省刑之意。
entries.en: treating the two differently was one law with two faces and betrayed the spirit of merciful judgment;
entries.literal: Now the offices hold that ordinary leave may return home but granted sick leave may not—this is one statute with two grades and loses the meaning of reviewing punishments.

entries.zh: 夫三最予告，令也；
entries.en: top-rated merit leave was statute;
entries.literal: The three highest ratings granting ordinary leave is ordinance;

entries.zh: 病滿三月賜告，詔恩也。
entries.en: three months' imperial sick leave was grace;
entries.literal: sick leave of three months granted is edict grace.

entries.zh: 令告則得，詔恩不得，失輕重之差。
entries.en: to honor one and forbid the other skewed weight and weightlessness;
entries.literal: Ordinance allows it but edict grace does not—this misses the balance of light and heavy.

entries.zh: 又二千石病賜告得歸有故事，不得去郡亡著令。
entries.en: precedent let sick two-thousand-bushel men go home, and no written rule barred leaving the command.
entries.literal: Moreover for two-thousand-bushel illness with granted leave to return home there is precedent; there is no written ordinance forbidding leaving the commandery.

entries.zh: 傳曰：『賞疑從予，所以廣恩勸功也；
entries.en: The tradition runs, "If reward is doubtful, give—thus widening grace;
entries.literal: Tradition says, "When reward is doubtful, incline to grant—thereby broadening grace and encouraging merit;

entries.zh: 罰疑從去，所以慎刑，闕難知也。』
entries.en: if punishment is doubtful, withhold—thus sparing the blade for gray cases."
entries.literal: when punishment is doubtful, incline to remit—thereby being careful with punishments and leaving what is hard to know."

entries.zh: 今釋令與故事而假不敬之法，甚違闕疑從去之意。
entries.en: To scrap precedent for a vague "disrespect" charge betrayed that maxim.
entries.literal: Now to discard ordinance and precedent and borrow the law of irreverence greatly violates the meaning of "when punishment is doubtful, remit.

entries.zh: 即以二千石守千里之地，任兵馬之重，不宜去郡，將以制刑為後法者，則野王之罪，在未制令前也。
entries.en: Even if a new rule should chain governors to their posts, Yewang acted before any such rule existed.
entries.literal: Even if, because a two-thousand-bushel guards a thousand li of territory and bears the weight of arms and horses, he ought not leave the commandery, intending to make punishment regulation for later law—then Yewang's offense lies before the ordinance was made.

entries.zh: 刑賞大信，不可不慎。」
entries.en: Reward and punishment are the throne's bond with the realm—handle them with care."
entries.literal: Punishment and reward are great trust—they cannot but be careful."

entries.zh: 鳳不聽，竟免野王。
entries.en: Feng ignored him and cashiered Yewang anyway.
entries.literal: Feng would not listen and in the end dismissed Yewang.

entries.zh: 郡國二千石病賜告不得歸家，自此始。
entries.en: From that day governors on sick leave could not go home.
entries.literal: That commandery and kingdom two-thousand-bushels on granted sick leave could not return home began from this.

entries.zh: 贊曰：《詩》稱「抑抑威儀，惟德之隅。」
entries.en: The historian cites the Odes: "Grave is the bearing that fences virtue."
entries.literal: The appraising comment says: The Odes praises "solemn, solemn awe-inspiring deportment—the corner of virtue."

entries.zh: 宜鄉侯參鞠躬履方，擇地而行，可謂淑人君子，然卒死於非罪，不能自免，哀哉！
entries.en: Marquis Shen walked every inch by the book—a true gentleman—yet perished on a false charge he could not escape.
entries.literal: Marquis of Yixiang Shen bowed the body and trod the square, choosing the ground in walking—he may be called a virtuous man and noble man, yet in the end he died of a crime he did not commit, unable to save himself—alas!

entries.zh: 讒邪交亂，貞良被害，自古而然。
entries.en: Slander devouring the good is as old as history.
entries.literal: Slander and evil crisscrossing, the chaste and good injured—this has been so since antiquity.

entries.zh: 故伯奇放流，孟子宮刑，申生雉經，屈原赴湘，《小弁》之詩作，《離騷》之辭興。
entries.en: So Boqi was driven out, Mengzi was castrated, Crown Prince Sheng hanged himself, Qu Yuan drowned—the "Little Boy" ode and "Li sao" rose from such pain.
entries.literal: Therefore Boqi was banished, Mengzi suffered palace castration, Sheng'er strangled with pheasant cord, Qu Yuan threw himself into the Xiang; the poem "Little Boy" was composed, the words of "Li sao" arose.

entries.zh: 經曰：「心之憂矣，涕既隕之。」
entries.en: The canon says, "The heart's grief already wets the cheek with tears."
entries.literal: The classic says, "The heart's sorrow—tears already fall."

entries.zh: 馮參姊弟，亦云悲矣！
entries.en: Shen and his sister—pitiful indeed.
entries.literal: Shen's elder sister and younger brother—one may also say it was pitiful!

entries.zh: 卷七十九 馮奉世傳第四十九
entries.en: Volume 79: Biography of Feng Fengshi, the forty-ninth.
entries.literal: Volume 79, Biography of Feng Fengshi, Number 49.

entries.zh: 孝宣皇帝五男
entries.en: Emperor Xuan had five sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.

entries.zh: 孝宣皇帝五男。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan had five sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan had five sons.

entries.zh: 許皇后生孝元帝，張婕妤生淮陽憲王欽，衛婕妤生楚孝王囂，公孫婕妤生東平思王宇，戎婕妤生中山哀王竟。
entries.en: Empress Xu gave birth to Emperor Yuan. Lady Zhang the Honored Lady bore Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin; Lady Wei the Honored Lady bore Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao; Lady Gongsun the Honored Lady bore Prince Si of Dongping, Yu; and Lady Rong the Honored Lady bore Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing.
entries.literal: Empress Xu bore Emperor Xiaoyuan; Lady Zhang Jieyu bore Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin; Lady Wei Jieyu bore Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao; Lady Gongsun Jieyu bore Prince Si of Dongping, Yu; Lady Rong Jieyu bore Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing.

entries.zh: 淮陽憲王欽，元康三年立，母張婕妤有寵於宣帝。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin, was established in the third year of Yuankang (63 BCE). His mother, Lady Zhang the Honored Lady, enjoyed Emperor Xuan’s favor.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang, Qin was enfeoffed in the third year of Yuankang; his mother Lady Zhang Jieyu was favored by Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 霍皇后廢後，上欲立張婕妤為后。
entries.en: After Empress Huo was cast aside, the emperor meant to raise Lady Zhang to empress.
entries.literal: After Empress Huo was deposed, the emperor wished to make Lady Zhang Jieyu empress.

entries.zh: 久之，懲艾霍氏欲害皇太子，乃更選後宮無子而謹慎者，乃立長陵王婕妤為后，令母養太子。
entries.en: In time, mindful of how the Huo family had tried to harm the crown prince, he looked elsewhere among his childless, cautious consorts and made Lady Wang of Changling empress, charging her with raising the heir.
entries.literal: After a long time, chastened by the Huo clan’s attempt to harm the heir apparent, he instead chose from the rear palace a woman who had borne no sons and was careful and modest, and established Lady Wang Jieyu of Changling as empress, ordering her to mother the heir.

entries.zh: 後無寵，希御見，唯張婕妤最幸。
entries.en: The new empress soon lost his attention and seldom saw him; Lady Zhang alone remained his favorite.
entries.literal: Afterward she had no favor and rarely attended him; only Lady Zhang Jieyu was most favored.

entries.zh: 而憲王壯大，好經書、法律，聰達有材，帝甚愛之。
entries.en: As the Prince of Huaiyang came of age, he took to the classics and law, proved quick and capable, and won the emperor’s deep affection.
entries.literal: The Prince Xian grew to adulthood, loved the classics and statutes, was intelligent and talented, and the emperor loved him greatly.

entries.zh: 太子寬仁，喜儒術，上數嗟歎憲王，輔曰：「真我子也！」
entries.en: The crown prince was mild and humane and loved Confucian scholarship; the emperor would sigh over Prince Xian and tell his attendants, “Now that is my son!”
entries.literal: The heir apparent was generous and humane and delighted in Confucian learning; the emperor often sighed in admiration of the Prince Xian, saying, “He is truly my son!”

entries.zh: 常有意欲立張婕妤與憲王，然用太子起於微細，上少依倚許氏，及即位而許后以殺死，太子蚤失母，故弗忍也。
entries.en: He often toyed with making Lady Zhang and the prince his succession, yet the crown prince had come up from nothing: as a young man the emperor had leaned on the Xu clan, and after his accession Empress Xu had been executed, leaving the boy motherless—so he could not bring himself to replace him.
entries.literal: He often had the intention of establishing Lady Zhang Jieyu and the Prince Xian, but because the heir had risen from low beginnings, in youth he had relied on the Xu family, and when he took the throne Empress Xu had died by execution, and the heir had early lost his mother, therefore he could not bear it.

entries.zh: 久之，上以故丞相韋賢子玄成陽狂讓侯兄，經明行高，稱於朝廷，乃召拜玄成為淮陽中尉，欲感諭憲王，輔以推讓之臣，由是太子遂安。
entries.en: Years later he recalled how Wei Xuancheng, son of the former chancellor Wei Xian, had played mad to yield his noble title to an elder brother—learned in the classics and renowned for integrity—and summoned him to serve as commandant in Huaiyang, hoping such an example of deference would steady the ambitious prince and quiet the succession.
entries.literal: After a long time, because the former Chancellor Wei Xian’s son Xuancheng feigned madness to yield the marquisate to his elder brother, was clear in the classics and high in conduct, and was praised at court, he summoned and appointed Xuancheng as Commandant of Huaiyang, wishing to instruct and admonish the Prince Xian and support him with a minister who practiced yielding; thereby the heir apparent was secured.

entries.zh: 宣帝崩，元帝即位，乃遣憲王之國。
entries.en: When Xuan died and Yuan ascended, the new emperor sent Prince Qin to his fief at Huaiyang.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan died and Emperor Yuan took the throne, he then sent the Prince Xian to his kingdom.

entries.zh: 卷八十 宣元六王傳第五十
entries.en: Volume 80: Biographies of the Six Princes of Emperors Xuan and Yuan (no. 50).
entries.literal: Volume 80: Biographies of the Six Princes of Emperors Xuan and Yuan, Number 50.

entries.zh: 立三十三年薨，子煬王雲嗣。
entries.en: He reigned thirty-three years and died; his son Yun, posthumously Yang, succeeded.
entries.literal: He was established thirty-three years and died; his son King Yang Yun succeeded.

entries.zh: 哀帝時，無鹽危山土自起覆草，如馳道狀，又瓠山石轉立。
entries.en: In Emperor Ai’s reign soil at Wuyan’s Danger Mountain heaved up over the turf in the shape of an imperial causeway, and a boulder at Gourd Mountain rolled upright.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Ai, at Danger Mountain in Wuyan earth rose of itself and covered grass in the shape of an imperial thoroughfare; also at Gourd Mountain a stone turned and stood upright.

entries.zh: 雲及後謁自之石所祭，治石像瓠山立石，束倍草，並祠之。
entries.en: Yun and Queen Ye visited the omens, set up a stone like the one at Gourd Mountain, bound paired stalks of grass, and offered joint sacrifice.
entries.literal: Yun and his queen Ye went in person to the stone place to sacrifice, worked a stone in the image of the Gourd Mountain standing stone, tied double grass, and jointly sacrificed to them.

entries.zh: 建平三年，息夫躬、孫寵等共因幸臣董賢告之。
entries.en: In Jianping 3, Xi Fu Gong, Sun Chong, and others denounced them through the favorite Dong Xian.
entries.literal: In the third year of Jianping, Xi Fu Gong, Sun Chong, and others together through the favored minister Dong Xian reported it.

entries.zh: 是時，哀帝被疾，多所惡，事下有司，逮王、後謁下獄驗治，言使巫傅恭、婢合歡等祠祭詛祝上，為雲求為天子。
entries.en: Ai was ill and ill-tempered; officers jailed king and queen and proved they had set shamans Fu Gong and the slave girl Hehuan cursing the throne so Yun might become Son of Heaven.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor Ai was afflicted with illness and had many taboos; the matter was handed to the responsible officials, who arrested the king and Queen Ye and put them in prison for examination; it was said they had shamans Fu Gong and the maid Hehuan and others sacrifice and curse-pray for the emperor, seeking the kingship for Yun.

entries.zh: 雲又與知災異者高尚等指星宿，言上疾必不愈，雲當得天下。
entries.en: Yun and omen-readers such as Gao Shang traced the stars, swearing the emperor would not recover and the mandate would fall to Yun.
entries.literal: Yun also with one who knew disasters and anomalies, Gao Shang and others, pointed to asterisms, saying the emperor’s illness would surely not improve and Yun ought to obtain the realm.

entries.zh: 石立，宣帝起之表也。
entries.en: The standing stone had been the omen of Emperor Xuan’s ascent.
entries.literal: The stone standing upright was the sign of Emperor Xuan’s rise.

entries.zh: 有司請誅王，有詔廢徙房陵。
entries.en: Some demanded the king’s death; the edict spared his life but deposed him and banished him to Fangling.
entries.literal: The responsible officials asked to execute the king; there was an edict deposing him and moving him to Fangling.

entries.zh: 雲自殺，謁棄市。
entries.en: Yun committed suicide; Ye was executed in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Yun killed himself; Ye was exposed in the market.

entries.zh: 立十七年，國除。
entries.en: Seventeen years into his reign the kingdom was abolished.
entries.literal: He had been established seventeen years; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 東平思王宇，甘露二年立。
entries.en: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu, was enfeoffed in the second year of Ganlu (52 BCE).
entries.literal: Prince Si of Dongping, Yu was established in the second year of Ganlu.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，就國。
entries.en: When Yuan became emperor, Yu proceeded to his fief.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan took the throne, he went to his kingdom.

entries.zh: 壯大，通姦犯法，上以至親貰弗罪，傅相連坐。
entries.en: Once grown, he fornicated and broke the law; the emperor spared him as kin, but his tutor and minister paid for it with their posts.
entries.literal: When he grew to maturity he committed adultery and broke the law; the emperor, because he was closest kin, pardoned him without punishment, but the tutor and chancellor suffered joint liability.

entries.zh: 孝元皇帝三男
entries.en: Emperor Yuan had three sons
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons

entries.zh: 孝元皇帝三男。
entries.en: Emperor Yuan had three sons.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoyuan had three sons.

entries.zh: 王皇后生孝成帝，傅昭儀生定陶共王康，馮昭儀生中山孝王興。
entries.en: Empress Wang gave birth to Emperor Cheng. Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang; Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing.
entries.literal: Empress Wang bore Emperor Xiaocheng; Lady Fu the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Gong of Dingtao, Kang; Lady Feng the Brilliant Companion bore Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing.

entries.zh: 成帝即位，緣先帝意，厚遇異於它王。
entries.en: When Cheng succeeded, he followed his predecessor's wishes and favored him more generously than any other prince.
entries.literal: When Emperor Cheng took the throne, following the former emperor's intent, he treated him generously, differently from other kings.

entries.zh: 十九年薨，子欣嗣。
entries.en: He died in the nineteenth year of his reign; his son Xin inherited.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he died; his son Xin succeeded.

entries.zh: 十五年，成帝無子，徵入為皇太子。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year of Xin's reign, as Emperor Cheng had no son, Xin was summoned to the capital as crown prince.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, as Emperor Cheng had no son, Xin was summoned to enter the capital as heir apparent.

entries.zh: 上以太子奉大宗後，不得顧私親，乃立楚思王子景為定陶王，奉共王後。
entries.en: Because the crown prince was to carry on the main imperial line and could not favor his own kin, the emperor made Jing, son of Prince Si of Chu, king of Dingtao to continue Prince Gong's line.
entries.literal: The emperor, because the heir apparent was to serve the main lineage and could not attend to private kin, thereupon established Jing, son of Prince Si of Chu, as King of Dingtao to continue the line of Prince Gong.

entries.zh: 成帝崩，太子即位，是為孝哀帝。
entries.en: When Emperor Cheng died, the crown prince ascended as Emperor Ai.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng died; the heir apparent took the throne—this was Emperor Ai.

entries.zh: 即位二年，追尊共王為共皇帝，置寢廟京師，序昭穆，儀如孝元帝。
entries.en: In the second year of his reign he posthumously honored Prince Gong as Emperor Gong, set up his spirit temple in the capital, arranged the zhao and mu order, and followed the ceremonial model of Emperor Xiaoyuan.
entries.literal: In the second year of his reign he posthumously honored Prince Gong as Emperor Gong, established his spirit temple in the capital, arranged the ancestral order of zhao and mu, with ceremonies like those for Emperor Xiaoyuan.

entries.zh: 徙定陶王景為信都王云。
entries.en: King Jing of Dingtao was transferred to Xindu, the record says.
entries.literal: Jing was moved from King of Dingtao to King of Xindu, it is said.

entries.zh: 宇立二十年，元帝崩。
entries.en: Twenty years after Yu took the throne, Yuan died.
entries.literal: Yu had been established twenty years when Emperor Yuan died.

entries.zh: 宇謂中謁者信等曰：「漢大臣議天子少弱，未能治天下，以為我知文法，建欲使我輔佐天子。
entries.en: Yu told the usher Xin and others, “The great ministers think the boy emperor too weak to rule and, because I know the statutes, mean to set me at his elbow.
entries.literal: Yu said to the palace usher Xin and others, “Han ministers have deliberated that the Son of Heaven is young and weak and unable to govern the realm; they consider that I understand statutes and precedents, and propose that I assist the Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 我見尚書晨夜極苦，使我為之，不能也。
entries.en: I have watched the masters of writing toil day and night—I could never bear that office.
entries.literal: I have seen how the secretariat works morning and night in extreme toil; were it made me to do it, I could not.

entries.zh: 今暑熱，縣官年少，持服恐無處所，我危得之！」
entries.en: The weather is stifling, the emperor is young, and when the court goes into mourning it may have no pillar to lean on—I could nearly win the post!”
entries.literal: Now it is hot; the Son of Heaven is young; when he dons mourning I fear the court will have nowhere to turn—I could nearly obtain it!”

entries.zh: 比至下，宇凡三哭，飲酒食肉，妻妾不離側。
entries.en: When the edict of mourning arrived, Yu wept three times for show, then feasted on wine and meat while his wives and concubines never left his side.
entries.literal: By the time the mourning edict came down, Yu had wept only three times in all, drank wine and ate meat, and wives and concubines did not leave his side.

entries.zh: 又姬朐臑故親幸，後疏遠，數歎息呼天。
entries.en: A former favorite, the concubine Qu Nai, had been cast aside; she sighed to heaven again and again.
entries.literal: Also his concubine Qu Nai had formerly been favored; afterward she was estranged and several times sighed and called to Heaven.

entries.zh: 宇聞，斥朐臑為家人子，掃除永巷，數笞擊之。
entries.en: Yu heard it, reduced her to menial rank, put her to sweeping the palace lane, and beat her repeatedly.
entries.literal: When Yu heard, he demoted Qu Nai to the rank of family servant, set her to sweeping the long lane, and several times flogged her.

entries.zh: 朐臑私疏宇過失，數令家告之。
entries.en: She drafted a secret catalogue of his misdeeds and had kin report them upstream.
entries.literal: Qu Nai privately drafted a list of Yu’s faults and several times had her family report them.

entries.zh: 宇覺知，絞殺朐臑。
entries.en: When Yu found out, he strangled her.
entries.literal: When Yu perceived it, he strangled Qu Nai to death.

entries.zh: 有司奏請逮捕，有詔削樊、亢父二縣。
entries.en: Officials asked for his arrest; the emperor instead stripped two counties—Fan and Kangfu—from his fief.
entries.literal: The responsible officials memorialized requesting arrest; there was an edict stripping Fan and Kangfu, two counties.

entries.zh: 後三歲，天子詔有司曰：「蓋聞仁以親親，古之道也。
entries.en: Three years later the emperor told his officers: “Kindness begins with kin—that was the way of the ancients.
entries.literal: After three years the Son of Heaven ordered the responsible officials, saying, “We have heard that benevolence lies in cherishing kin—this is the way of antiquity.

entries.zh: 前東平王有闕，有司請廢，朕不忍。
entries.en: When Dongping erred before, some urged me to depose him; I could not.
entries.literal: Formerly the King of Dongping had faults; the responsible officials asked to depose him; We could not bear it.

entries.zh: 又請削，朕不敢專。
entries.en: Others asked to shave his domain; I would not act unilaterally.
entries.literal: They again asked to strip territory; We did not dare decide alone.

entries.zh: 惟王之至親，未嘗忘於心。
entries.en: Yet you are bone of my bone—I have not forgotten you.
entries.literal: Only as to the king’s closest kin, We have never forgotten it in Our heart.

entries.zh: 今聞王改行自新，尊修經術，親近仁人，非法之求，不以奸吏，朕甚嘉焉。
