entries.en: Word comes that you have mended your ways, take the classics seriously, keep company with good men, and no longer let sharp clerks peddle illicit favors—I applaud that.
entries.literal: Now We hear the king has changed conduct and renewed himself, honors and cultivates the classics, draws near to benevolent men, and does not employ crafty clerks for unlawful requests—We greatly approve.

entries.zh: 傳不雲乎？
entries.en: Does not the tradition say?
entries.literal: Does not the tradition say?

entries.zh: 朝過夕改，君子與之。
entries.en: Wrong at dawn and right by dusk wins the gentleman’s praise.
entries.literal: Fault in the morning and reform by evening—the gentleman approves.

entries.zh: 其復前所削縣如故。」
entries.en: Restore the counties I once took away.”
entries.literal: Let him restore the former stripped counties as before.”

entries.zh: 中山孝王興，建昭二年立為信都王。
entries.en: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing, was made king of Xindu in Jianzhao 2.
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing, in the second year of Jianzhao was established as King of Xindu.

entries.zh: 十四年，徙中山。
entries.en: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Zhongshan.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year he was moved to Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 成帝之議立太子也，御史大夫孔光以為《尚書》有殷及王，兄終弟及，中山王元帝之子，宜為後。
entries.en: When Cheng debated the succession, Imperial Counselor Kong Guang cited the Documents on Yin brother-to-brother transmission and argued that Xing, Yuan’s son and king of Zhongshan, should follow.
entries.literal: When Emperor Cheng deliberated establishing the heir apparent, Imperial Counselor Kong Guang thought the Documents had Yin and royal houses where the elder brother ended and the younger brother succeeded; the King of Zhongshan was Emperor Yuan’s son and ought to be successor.

entries.zh: 成帝以中山王不材，又兄弟，不得相入廟。
entries.en: Cheng judged Xing unfit and held that brothers could not share one temple line.
entries.literal: Emperor Cheng considered the King of Zhongshan untalented and also that brothers could not enter one another’s temples.

entries.zh: 外家王氏與趙昭儀皆欲用哀帝為太子，故遂立焉。
entries.en: The Wangs at court and Lady Zhao the brilliant companion both wanted Ai as heir, so he was chosen.
entries.literal: The maternal Wang clan and Lady Zhao the Brilliant Companion both wished to use Emperor Ai as heir apparent; therefore he was finally established.

entries.zh: 上乃封孝王舅馮參為宜鄉侯，而益封孝王萬戶，以尉其意。
entries.en: The emperor then made Xing’s uncle Feng Can marquis of Yixiang and added ten thousand households to Xing’s fief to soothe him.
entries.literal: The emperor thereupon enfeoffed Prince Xiao’s maternal uncle Feng Can as Marquis of Yixiang and increased Prince Xiao’s fief by ten thousand households to comfort his mind.

entries.zh: 三十年，薨，子衎嗣。
entries.en: He died in the thirtieth year of his reign; his son Kan inherited.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year he died; his son Kan succeeded.

entries.zh: 七年，哀帝崩，無子，征中山王衎入即位，是為平帝。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Kan’s reign Ai died childless; Kan was summoned to the capital as Emperor Ping.
entries.literal: In the seventh year Emperor Ai died without a son; they summoned the King of Zhongshan Kan to enter and take the throne—this was Emperor Ping.

entries.zh: 太皇太后以帝為成帝後，故立東平思王孫桃鄉頃侯子成都為中山王，奉孝王後。
entries.en: The grand empress dowager, treating Ping as Cheng’s heir, enfeoffed Chengdu—son of Marquis Qing of Taoxiang and grandson of Prince Si of Dongping—as king of Zhongshan to carry on Xing’s line.
entries.literal: The Grand Empress Dowager, because the emperor was to continue Cheng’s line, therefore established Chengdu, son of Marquis Qing of Taoxiang, grandson of Prince Si of Dongping, as King of Zhongshan, to continue Prince Xiao’s line.

entries.zh: 王莽時絕。
entries.en: The line ended under Wang Mang.
entries.literal: At the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

entries.zh: 贊曰：孝元之後，遍有天下，然而世絕於孫，豈非天哉！
entries.en: The summation runs: from Emperor Yuan onward they held all under heaven, yet the line died with the grandson—can we call it anything but fate?
entries.literal: The eulogy says: After Emperor Xiaoyuan, they broadly held the realm, yet the generations were cut off at the grandson—is it not Heaven!

entries.zh: 淮陽憲王於時諸侯為聰察矣，張博誘之，幾陷無道。
entries.en: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was the sharpest of the kings of his day; Zhang Bo led him to the brink of treason.
entries.literal: Prince Xian of Huaiyang was among the feudal lords the most perceptive; Zhang Bo enticed him and he nearly fell into lack of the Way.

entries.zh: 《詩》云「貪人敗類」，古今一也。
entries.en: The Classic of Poetry says, “The greedy man destroys his kind”—the same in ancient times and today.
entries.literal: The Odes says, “The greedy man destroys his kind”—the same in ancient times and today.

entries.zh: 楚孝王囂，甘露二年立為定陶王，三年徙楚，成帝河平中入朝，時被疾，天子閔之，下詔曰：「蓋聞『天地之性人為貴，人之行莫大於孝』。
entries.en: Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao, was enfeoffed as king of Dingtao in Ganlu 2 and transferred to Chu in Ganlu 3. During the He Ping era under Emperor Cheng he came to court but fell ill. The emperor pitied him and issued an edict: "We have heard that 'among the nature of Heaven and Earth, humanity is most prized, and among human conduct nothing is greater than filial piety.'
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Chu, Ao, was established as King of Dingtao in the second year of Ganlu; in the third year he was moved to Chu. Under Emperor Cheng, during the He Ping era, he came to court to pay homage. At that time he was afflicted with illness. The Son of Heaven pitied him and issued an edict, saying: "We have heard that 'among the nature of Heaven and Earth, humanity is most prized, and among human conduct nothing is greater than filial piety.'

entries.zh: 楚王囂素行孝順仁慈，之國以來二十餘年，孅介之過未嘗聞，朕甚嘉之。
entries.en: King Ao of Chu has always been filial, kind, and humane. In more than twenty years since he took his fief, We have never heard the least fault of him, and We greatly commend him.
entries.literal: The King of Chu, Ao, has always acted with filial obedience, kindness, and benevolence. Since coming to his kingdom more than twenty years have passed, and We have never heard of the slightest fault. We greatly commend this.

entries.zh: 今乃遭命，離於惡疾，夫子所痛，曰：『蔑之，命矣夫！
entries.en: Now fate has struck, and he is stricken with grievous illness. The Master lamented, saying, 'Alas for him! Such is fate!'
entries.literal: Now he has encountered fate and is separated by a grievous illness. The Master grieved, saying, 'Alas for him! Such is fate!'

entries.zh: 斯人也而有斯疾也！』
entries.en: That such a man should have such an illness!
entries.literal: That such a man should have such an illness!

entries.zh: 朕甚閔焉。
entries.en: We are deeply grieved.
entries.literal: We are deeply grieved.

entries.zh: 夫行純茂而不顯異，則有國者將何勖哉？
entries.en: When pure and abundant conduct wins no special recognition, what are rulers to take as encouragement?
entries.literal: When conduct is pure and abundant yet no distinction is shown, what shall those who hold states take as encouragement?

entries.zh: 《書》不云乎：『用德章厥善』？
entries.en: Does not the Documents say, 'With virtue make known his goodness'?
entries.literal: Does not the Documents say, 'With virtue make known his goodness'?

entries.zh: 今王朝正月，詔與子男一人俱，其以廣戚縣戶四千三百封其子勳為廣戚侯。」
entries.en: At this New Year's court audience, let him come with one son. We enfeoff his son Xun with the four thousand three hundred households of Guangqi county as marquis of Guangqi."
entries.literal: At this New Year's court audience, let him come with one son or younger brother; We hereby enfeoff his son Xun with four thousand three hundred households of Guangqi county as Marquis of Guangqi."

entries.zh: 明年，囂薨。
entries.en: The next year Ao died.
entries.literal: The next year Ao died.

entries.zh: 子懷王文嗣，一年薨，無子，絕。
entries.en: His son Prince Huai, Wen, succeeded; he died within a year, leaving no heir, and the line ended.
entries.literal: His son King Huai Wen succeeded; in one year he died, without a son, and the line was cut off.

entries.zh: 明年，成帝復立文弟平陸侯衍，是為思王。
entries.en: The next year Emperor Cheng re-established Wen's younger brother Yan, marquis of Pinglu, as Prince Si.
entries.literal: The next year Emperor Cheng again established Wen's younger brother Yan, Marquis of Pinglu, who is known as Prince Si.

entries.zh: 二十一年薨，子紆嗣，王莽時絕。
entries.en: He died in the twenty-first year of his reign; his son Yu inherited, and the line ended under Wang Mang.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year he died; his son Yu succeeded; at the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

entries.zh: 中山哀王竟
entries.en: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing
entries.literal: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing

entries.zh: 中山哀王竟，初元二年立為清河王。
entries.en: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing, was made king of Qinghe in Chuyuan 2.
entries.literal: Prince Ai of Zhongshan, Jing, in the second year of Chuyuan was established as King of Qinghe.

entries.zh: 三年，徙中山，以幼少未之國。
entries.en: The next year he was transferred to Zhongshan but, still a child, did not take up the fief.
entries.literal: In the third year he was moved to Zhongshan; because he was young and small he did not go to the kingdom.

entries.zh: 建昭四年，薨邸，葬杜陵，無子，絕。
entries.en: He died at the princely residence in Jianzhao 4 and was buried at Du; without an heir the line ended.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianzhao he died in the lodge, was buried at Du Mausoleum, had no son, and the line was cut off.

entries.zh: 太后歸居外家戎氏。
entries.en: His mother the queen dowager went back to live with her Rong kin.
entries.literal: The empress dowager returned to dwell with her maternal Rong clan.

entries.zh: 初，成帝時又立紆弟景為定陶王。
entries.en: Earlier, under Emperor Cheng, Jing—Yu’s younger brother—had been made king of Dingtao.
entries.literal: At the beginning, under Emperor Cheng, they again established Jing, younger brother of Yu, as King of Dingtao.

entries.zh: 廣戚侯勳薨，謚曰煬侯，子顯嗣。
entries.en: The marquis of Guangqi, Xun, died with the posthumous title Yang; his son Xian succeeded.
entries.literal: Marquis of Guangqi Xun died; his posthumous title was Marquis Yang; his son Xian succeeded.

entries.zh: 平帝崩，無子，王莽立顯子嬰為孺子，奉平帝后。
entries.en: When Emperor Ping died childless, Wang Mang set Xian’s son Ying on the throne as the infant heir to carry on Ping’s line.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ping died without a son, Wang Mang established Xian’s son Ying as the Infant, to serve Empress Dowager Ping.

entries.zh: 莽篡位，以嬰為定安公。
entries.en: When Mang seized the throne he demoted Ying to duke of Ding’an.
entries.literal: When Mang usurped the throne, he made Ying Duke of Ding’an.

entries.zh: 漢既誅莽，更始時嬰在長安，平陵方望等頗知天文，以為更始必敗，嬰本統當立者也，共起兵將嬰至臨涇，立為天子。
entries.en: After Han destroyed Wang Mang, Ying was still in Chang’an under the Gengshi regime. Fang Wang of Pingling and others, versed in the stars, believed Gengshi would fall and that Ying was the rightful heir; they rose in arms, escorted him to Linjing, and proclaimed him emperor.
entries.literal: When Han had executed Mang, at the time of Gengshi Ying was in Chang’an; Fang Wang and others at Pingling, who knew astronomy somewhat, thought Gengshi would surely fail and that Ying by original succession ought to have been established; they jointly raised troops and brought Ying to Linjing and established him as Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 更始遣丞相李松擊破殺嬰云。
entries.en: Gengshi’s chancellor Li Song crushed the rising and killed Ying, or so the record runs.
entries.literal: Gengshi sent Chancellor Li Song to attack, defeat, and kill Ying, it is said.

entries.zh: 是時，博女婿京房以明《易》陰陽得幸於上，數召見言事。
entries.en: Bo’s son-in-law Jing Fang had won favor by expounding the Book of Changes and yin–yang theory and was repeatedly called to advise the throne.
entries.literal: At this time Bo’s son-in-law Jing Fang, through clarity in the Changes and yin and yang, had gained the emperor’s favor and was several times summoned to speak on affairs.

entries.zh: 自謂為石顯、五鹿充宗所排，謀不得用，數為博道之。
entries.en: He complained that Shi Xian and Wulu Chongzong had blocked him and that none of his policies were adopted, and he poured this out to Bo again and again.
entries.literal: He claimed that he was squeezed out by Shi Xian and Wulu Chongzong and his plans could not be used, and several times spoke of this to Bo.

entries.zh: 博常欲誑耀淮陽王，即具記房諸所說災異及召見密語，持予淮陽王以為信驗，詐言：「已見中書令石君求朝，許以金五百斤。
entries.en: Bo had long wanted to impress the King of Huaiyang, so he wrote down everything Jing Fang had said about disasters and anomalies, along with confidential remarks from imperial audiences, and brought the notes to the king as proof. He falsely claimed, “I have already gone to Palace Secretary Shi to ask for an audience; he agreed in exchange for five hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: Bo always wished to dazzle the King of Huaiyang, and so fully recorded all that Fang had said about disasters and anomalies and secret words at audiences, and took them to give to the King of Huaiyang as proof, falsely saying, “I have already seen Palace Secretary Shi and sought an audience; he promised it for five hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 賢聖制事，蓋慮功而不計費。
entries.en: The sages weighed outcomes, not price tags.
entries.literal: The sages in ordering affairs surely weigh merit and do not reckon expense.

entries.zh: 昔禹治鴻水，百姓罷勞，成功既立，萬世賴之。
entries.en: When Yu tamed the flood, the people wore themselves to the bone, yet once the work was done, countless ages lived by it.
entries.literal: In antiquity Yu controlled the flood waters; the common people were exhausted by toil; when the achievement was established, myriad generations relied on it.

entries.zh: 今聞陛下春秋未滿四十，發齒墮落，太子幼弱，佞人用事，陰陽不調，百姓疾疫饑饉死者且半，鴻水之害殆不過此。
entries.en: They say you are not yet forty, yet your hair and teeth fail, the heir is a child, favorites run the court, heaven and earth are out of tune, and plague and famine have carried off perhaps half the realm—no less dire than Yu’s deluge.
entries.literal: Now I hear that Your Majesty’s years are not yet forty, hair and teeth are falling, the heir is young and weak, crafty men hold power, yin and yang are not in harmony, and among the common people plague and famine have killed nearly half; the harm of the flood waters is perhaps no worse than this.

entries.zh: 大王緒欲救世，將比功德，何可以忽？
entries.en: You mean to save the age, my lord—set that deed beside a few hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: The great king in succession wishes to save the age; compared with that merit, how can this be neglected?

entries.zh: 博已與大儒知道者為大王為便宜奏，陳安危，指災異，大王朝見，先口陳其意而後奏之，上必大說。
entries.en: I have lined up learned men to draft a memorial on peril and portent; when you face the throne, speak the heart of it aloud, then hand up the text, and the Son of Heaven will be overjoyed.
entries.literal: Bo has already joined with great Confucians who know the way to draft for the great king a convenient memorial stating safety and danger, pointing to disasters and anomalies; when the great king has his audience, first declare the intent orally and then submit it, and the emperor will surely be greatly pleased.

entries.zh: 事成功立，大王即有周、邵之名，邪臣散亡，公卿變節，功德亡比，而梁、趙之寵必歸大王，外家亦將富貴，何復望大王之金錢？」
entries.en: Success would give you the stature of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao, sweep the sycophants from power, and turn every minister’s coat—while the favor now lavished on Liang and Zhao would fall to you and your wife’s clan. Why haggle over gold?”
entries.literal: When the affair succeeds and the achievement is established, the great king will then have the names of the dukes of Zhou and Shao, wicked ministers will scatter and flee, dukes and ministers will change their ways, merit without compare—and the favor shown Liang and Zhao will surely return to the great king, and the maternal kin will also become rich and noble; why look again to the great king’s gold and cash?”

entries.zh: 王喜說，報博書曰：「乃者詔下，止諸侯朝者，寡人憯然不知所出。
entries.en: The prince wrote back gladly: “When the edict lately barred princes from audience, I was at a loss.
entries.literal: The king was pleased and replied to Bo’s letter saying, “Recently an edict came down forbidding the feudal kings from attending court; I was dismayed and did not know what to do.

entries.zh: 子高素有顏、冉之資，臧武之智，子貢之辯，卞莊子之勇，兼此四者，世之所鮮。
entries.en: You have Yan Hui’s and Ran Boniu’s gifts, Zang Wuzhong’s wit, Zigong’s tongue, and Bian Zhuangzi’s nerve—four virtues seldom met in one man.
entries.literal: Zi Gao has always had the endowment of Yan and Ran, the wisdom of Zang Wuzhong, the eloquence of Zigong, and the courage of Bian Zhuangzi; to combine these four is rare in the world.

entries.zh: 既開端緒，願卒成之。
entries.en: You have opened the way; see it through with me.
entries.literal: Since the beginning has been opened, I wish to see it through to the end.

entries.zh: 求朝，義事也，奈何行金錢乎！」
entries.en: Seeking an audience is a matter of right—how can we buy it with money!”
entries.literal: To seek an audience is a righteous affair; how can one traffic in gold and cash!”

entries.zh: 博報曰：「已許石君，須以成事。」
entries.en: Bo answered, “I have given Shi my word—we need the gold to finish this.”
entries.literal: Bo replied saying, “I have already promised Secretary Shi; we must use it to complete the affair.”

entries.zh: 王以金五百斤予博。
entries.en: The prince handed over five hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: The king gave Bo five hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 三十六年薨。
entries.en: He died in the thirty-sixth year of his reign.
entries.literal: In the thirty-sixth year he died.

entries.zh: 子文王玄嗣，二十六年薨。
entries.en: His son Prince Wen, Xuan, succeeded and died in the twenty-sixth year of his reign.
entries.literal: His son King Wen Xuan succeeded; in the twenty-sixth year he died.

entries.zh: 子縯嗣，王莽時絕。
entries.en: His son Yan inherited the title; the line ended under Wang Mang.
entries.literal: His son Yan succeeded; at the time of Wang Mang the line was cut off.

entries.zh: 元始元年，王莽欲反哀帝政，白太皇太后，立雲太子開明為東平王，又立思王孫成都為中山王。
entries.en: In Yuanshi 1, Wang Mang, undoing Ai’s policies, persuaded the grand empress dowager to make Yun’s heir Kai Ming king of Dongping and to enfeoff Chengdu, grandson of the Prince of Dongping, as king of Zhongshan.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanshi, Wang Mang wished to reverse Emperor Ai’s policies, reported to the Grand Empress Dowager, established Kai Ming, heir of Yun, as King of Dongping, and also established Chengdu, grandson of Prince Si, as King of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 開明立三年，薨，無子。
entries.en: Kai Ming reigned three years and died without issue.
entries.literal: Kai Ming was established three years and died; he had no son.

entries.zh: 復立開明兄嚴鄉侯信子匡為東平王，奉開明後。
entries.en: The court then set Kuang, son of Marquis Yanxiang Xin, on the Dongping throne to continue Kai Ming’s line.
entries.literal: They again established Kuang, son of Marquis Yanxiang Xin, as King of Dongping, to continue Kai Ming’s line.

entries.zh: 王莽居攝，東郡太守翟義與嚴鄉侯信謀舉兵誅莽，立信為天子。
entries.en: Under Mang’s regency the eastern governor Zhai Yi conspired with Marquis Xin to march against Mang and proclaimed Xin emperor.
entries.literal: When Wang Mang held regency, Governor of the Eastern Region Zhai Yi plotted with Marquis Yanxiang Xin to raise troops to execute Mang and established Xin as Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 兵敗，皆為莽所滅。
entries.en: Their forces were crushed and Mang wiped them out.
entries.literal: The army was defeated; all were destroyed by Mang.

entries.zh: 中山孝王興
entries.en: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing
entries.literal: Prince Xiao of Zhongshan, Xing

entries.zh: 王商字子威，涿郡蠡吾人也，徙杜陵。
entries.en: Wang Shang, whose courtesy name was Ziwei, came from Liwu in Zhuo Commandery; the household later relocated to Duling.
entries.literal: Wang Shang, courtesy name Ziwei, was a man of Liwu in Zhuo Commandery, and his family moved to Duling.

entries.zh: 商公武、武兄無故，皆以宣帝舅封。
entries.en: Wang Shang's father was Wang Wu, and Wu's elder brother Wang Wugu; both received marquisates as maternal uncles of Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: Shang's father was Wu; Wu's elder brother was Wugu; both were enfeoffed because they were uncles on the mother's side of Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 無故為平昌侯，武為樂昌侯。
entries.en: Wugu was made Marquis of Pingchang, while Wu became Marquis of Lechang.
entries.literal: Wugu became Marquis of Pingchang, and Wu became Marquis of Lechang.

entries.zh: 語在《外戚傳》。
entries.en: The fuller story appears in the chapter on the imperial in-laws.
entries.literal: The account is in the 'Biographies of the Consort Families.'

entries.zh: 史丹字君仲，魯國人也，徙杜陵。
entries.en: Shi Dan, courtesy name Junzhong, came from Lu; his family later relocated to Duling.
entries.literal: Shi Dan, courtesy name Junzhong, was a man of Lu state; his family moved to Duling.

entries.zh: 祖父恭有女弟，武帝時爲衞太子良娣，產悼皇考。
entries.en: His grandfather Shi Gong had a younger sister who, in Emperor Wu's reign, served as a worthy lady attendant to Crown Prince Wei and bore the Lamented Imperial Father.
entries.literal: His grandfather Gong had a younger sister who in Emperor Wu's time was a worthy lady attendant to the Heir of Wei, the crown prince, and bore the Lamented Imperial Father.

entries.zh: 皇考者，孝宣帝父也。
entries.en: The Lamented Imperial Father was Emperor Xuan's father.
entries.literal: The Imperial Father was the father of Emperor Xuan of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 宣帝微時依倚史氏。
entries.en: In his lowly days Emperor Xuan relied on the Shi family.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was in humble circumstances he relied on the Shi clan.

entries.zh: 語在《史良娣傳》。
entries.en: The fuller account appears in the biography of Lady Attendant Shi.
entries.literal: The account is in the "Biography of Worthy Lady Attendant Shi."

entries.zh: 及宣帝即尊位，恭已死，三子，高、曾、玄。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Gong was already dead, leaving three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan assumed the exalted throne, Gong was already dead; he had three sons: Gao, Zeng, and Xuan.

entries.zh: 曾、玄皆以外屬舊恩封：曾爲將陵侯，玄平台侯。
entries.en: Zeng and Xuan were both enfeoffed as maternal relatives on account of old favor: Zeng as Marquis of Jiangling and Xuan as Marquis of Pingtai.
entries.literal: Zeng and Xuan were both enfeoffed for old favor as outer kin: Zeng became Marquis of Jiangling, Xuan Marquis of Pingtai.

entries.zh: 高侍中，貴幸，以發舉反者大司馬霍禹功封樂陵侯。
entries.en: Shi Gao served as palace attendant and enjoyed high favor; for exposing the rebel Grand Marshal Huo Yu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yueling.
entries.literal: Gao was palace attendant, honored and favored; for exposing and reporting the rebel Grand Marshal Huo Yu he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yueling.

entries.zh: 宣帝疾病，拜高爲大司馬、車騎將軍，領尚書事。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan fell ill, he appointed Shi Gao Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry with oversight of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan was ill, Gao was appointed Grand Marshal and General of Chariots and Cavalry, overseeing Masters of Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 帝崩，太子襲尊號，是爲孝元帝。
entries.en: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded as Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: The emperor died; the heir apparent assumed the exalted title—this was Emperor Yuan of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 高輔政五年，乞骸骨，賜安車駟馬、黃金，罷就第。
entries.en: Shi Gao served as regent for five years, then asked to retire. He was given a comfortable carriage and team of four, gold, and permission to withdraw to his estate.
entries.literal: Gao assisted government five years, begged for his old bones, was granted a secure carriage and four horses and gold, was dismissed, and went to his mansion.

entries.zh: 薨，謚曰安侯。
entries.en: When he died he was posthumously titled Marquis An.
entries.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis An.

entries.zh: 建昭之後，元帝被疾，不親政事，留好音樂。
entries.en: After the Jianzhao period Emperor Yuan fell ill, ceased to attend to government himself, and devoted himself to music.
entries.literal: After the Jianzhao era, Emperor Yuan was afflicted with illness, did not personally handle government affairs, and lingered in love of music.

entries.zh: 或置鼙鼓殿下，天子自臨軒檻上，隤銅丸以擿鼓，聲中嚴鼓之節。
entries.en: Drums were sometimes set below the hall; the emperor himself stood on the upper balustrade, dropped copper balls to beat the drums, and matched the rhythm of the ceremonial drum pattern.
entries.literal: Sometimes side drums were set below the hall; the Son of Heaven himself stood on the balustrade above, dropped copper balls to strike the drums, and the sound hit the cadence of the ceremonial drums.

entries.zh: 後宮及左右習知音者莫能爲，而定陶王亦能之，上數稱其材。
entries.en: None of the harem or the emperor's attendants who knew music could match the feat, yet the Prince of Dingtao could, and the emperor repeatedly praised his ability.
entries.literal: Those in the rear palace and at the sovereign's side practiced in knowing music yet none could do it; but the Prince of Dingtao could also do it, and the sovereign repeatedly praised his talent.

entries.zh: 丹進曰：「凡所謂材者，敏而好學，溫故知新，皇太了是也。
entries.en: Shi Dan stepped forward and said, "True talent means quickness and love of learning, reviewing the old to know the new—the crown prince is such a man.
entries.literal: Dan advanced and said: "What is called talent is quickness and love of learning, warming the old and knowing the new—the heir apparent is such.

entries.zh: 若乃器人於絲竹鼓鼙之間，則是陳惠、李微高於匡衡，可相國也。」
entries.en: If you measure men by skill with music and drums, then Chen Hui and Li Wei outrank Kuang Heng and ought to be chancellor."
entries.literal: If one gauges men amid strings, bamboo, drums, and side drums, then Chen Hui and Li Wei are higher than Kuang Heng and could be chancellor of the state."

entries.zh: 於是上嘿然而笑。
entries.en: The emperor smiled but said nothing.
entries.literal: Thereupon the sovereign gave a silent laugh.

entries.zh: 其後，中山哀王薨，太子前吊。
entries.en: Later Prince Ai of Zhongshan died, and the crown prince went to offer condolences.
entries.literal: After this the Prince Ai of Zhongshan died; the heir apparent went forward to mourn.

entries.zh: 哀王者，帝之少弟，與太子遊學相長大。
entries.en: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the crown prince had studied and grown up together.
entries.literal: Prince Ai was the emperor's younger brother; he and the heir apparent studied and traveled together and grew up together.

entries.zh: 上望見太子，感念哀王，悲不能自止。
entries.en: When the emperor saw the crown prince, memories of Prince Ai overwhelmed him and he could not stop grieving.
entries.literal: The sovereign looked and saw the heir apparent, was moved by thoughts of Prince Ai, and grieved beyond self-control.

entries.zh: 太子既至前，不哀。
entries.en: When the crown prince came forward, he showed no grief.
entries.literal: When the heir apparent had come forward, he did not mourn.

entries.zh: 上大恨曰：「安有人不慈仁而可奉宗廟爲民父母者乎！」
entries.en: The emperor was furious and said, "How can anyone lacking kindness and humaneness be fit to tend the ancestral temple and be father and mother to the people!"
entries.literal: The sovereign greatly resented it and said: "How can there be a man lacking kindness and humaneness who can be entrusted with the ancestral temple and be father and mother to the people!"

entries.zh: 上以責謂丹。
entries.en: The emperor reproached Shi Dan.
entries.literal: The sovereign blamed and addressed Dan.

entries.zh: 丹免冠謝上曰：「臣誠見陛下哀痛中山王，至以感損。
entries.en: Shi Dan removed his cap and apologized: "Your servant saw that Your Majesty was grieving for Prince Ai of Zhongshan to the point of harming your health.
entries.literal: Dan removed his cap and apologized to the sovereign, saying: "Your servant truly saw Your Majesty grieving for the Prince of Zhongshan, even to the point of being moved and harmed.

entries.zh: 向者太子當進見，臣竊戒屬毋涕泣，感傷陛下。
entries.en: When the crown prince was about to appear, I privately warned him not to weep and add to Your Majesty's sorrow.
entries.literal: When the heir apparent was about to come forward in audience, your servant privately admonished and instructed him not to weep and cry, lest he move and wound Your Majesty.

entries.zh: 罪乃在臣，當死。」
entries.en: The fault is mine alone, and I deserve death."
entries.literal: The crime lies in your servant; I deserve death."

entries.zh: 上以爲然，意乃解。
entries.en: The emperor accepted this explanation and his anger subsided.
entries.literal: The sovereign thought it so; his resentment then dissolved.

entries.zh: 丹之輔相，皆此類也。
entries.en: Shi Dan's guidance of the crown prince was always of this sort.
entries.literal: Dan's assisting and guiding the heir were all of this kind.

entries.zh: 竟寧元年，上寢疾，傅昭儀及定陶王常在左右，而皇后、太子希得進見。
entries.en: In Jingning 1 the emperor was bedridden. Consort Fu and the Prince of Dingtao were constantly at his side, while the empress and crown prince were rarely admitted.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jingning the sovereign lay ill; Consort Fu and the Prince of Dingtao were constantly at his side, while the empress and heir apparent seldom obtained audience.

entries.zh: 上疾稍侵，意忽忽不平，數問尚書以景帝時立膠東王故事。
entries.en: As his illness deepened, the emperor grew restless and repeatedly asked the Masters of Writing about the precedent from Emperor Jing's reign of enthroning the Prince of Jiaodong instead of the crown prince.
entries.literal: The sovereign's illness gradually worsened; his mind was unsettled and uneasy; he repeatedly questioned the Masters of Writing about the precedent of Emperor Jing's time in establishing the Prince of Jiaodong.

entries.zh: 是時，太子長舅陽平侯王鳳爲衛尉、侍中，與皇后、太子皆憂，不知所出。
entries.en: The crown prince's elder maternal uncle, Yangping Marquis Wang Feng, served as Commandant of the Guard and palace attendant; he, the empress, and the crown prince were all anxious and at a loss.
entries.literal: At this time the heir apparent's elder maternal uncle, Yangping Marquis Wang Feng, was Commandant of the Guard and palace attendant; he together with the empress and heir apparent were all worried and did not know what course to take.

entries.zh: 丹以親密臣得侍視疾，侯上間獨寢時，丹直入臥內，頓首伏青蒲上，涕泣言曰：「皇太子以適長立，積十餘年，名號繫於百姓，天下莫不歸心臣子。
entries.en: As an intimate adviser permitted to attend the sickbed, Shi Dan waited until the emperor was resting alone, then entered the inner chamber, prostrated himself on the green rush mat, and weeping said, "The crown prince was established as the legitimate eldest son more than ten years ago. His title is bound up with the people, and all the realm looks to him as heir.
entries.literal: Dan, as an intimate minister, was allowed to attend and view the illness; waiting until the sovereign was alone at rest, Dan went straight into the sleeping quarters, knocked his head and lay prostrate on the green rush mat, and with tears said: "The heir apparent was established as eldest son of the primary consort and has accumulated more than ten years; his title is tied to the hundred surnames; all under heaven none do not turn their hearts to him as lord and son.

entries.zh: 見定陶王雅素愛幸，今者道路流言，爲國生意，以爲太子有動搖之議。
entries.en: The Prince of Dingtao has long enjoyed your favor, and now rumor runs through the streets that the succession may be changed.
entries.literal: Seeing the Prince of Dingtao has long been loved and favored, now there are rumors on the roads; the state is stirred; people think there is talk of shaking the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 審若此，公卿以下必以死爭，不奉詔。
entries.en: If that is true, the high ministers and officials below them will resist to the death and refuse to obey any contrary edict.
entries.literal: If this is truly so, from the dukes and ministers downward they will surely contend unto death and not obey the edict.

entries.zh: 臣願先賜死以示群臣！」
entries.en: Your servant asks to die first as a warning to the court!"
entries.literal: Your servant wishes first to be granted death to show the host of ministers!"

entries.zh: 天子素仁，不忍見丹涕泣，言又切至，上意大感，喟然太息曰：「吾日困劣，而太子、兩王幼少，意中戀戀，亦何不念乎！
entries.en: The emperor was by nature humane and could not bear to see Shi Dan weeping. His words cut to the heart. Deeply moved, the emperor sighed and said, "My days are failing, and the crown prince and the two princes are still young. My heart clings to them—how could I not think of them!
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven was by nature humane; he could not bear to see Dan weeping; his words were also urgent and penetrating; the sovereign was greatly moved, sighed deeply, and said: "My days are weary and weak, yet the heir apparent and the two princes are young and small; my heart is attached and lingering—how could I not think of them!

entries.zh: 然無有此議。
entries.en: But there is no such plan.
entries.literal: Yet there is no such deliberation.

entries.zh: 且皇后謹慎，先帝又愛太子，吾豈可違指！
entries.en: Besides, the empress is prudent, and the late emperor loved the crown prince. How could I go against his intent!
entries.literal: Moreover the empress is careful and cautious; the former emperor also loved the heir apparent—how could I go against his intent!

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉安所受此語？」
entries.en: Chief Commandant of Horsemen-at-attendance, where did you hear such talk?"
entries.literal: Chief Commandant of Horsemen-at-attendance, from where did you receive these words?"

entries.zh: 丹即卻，頓首曰：「愚臣妾聞，罪當死！」
entries.en: Shi Dan drew back and kowtowed: "This foolish servant merely heard rumor. The offense deserves death!"
entries.literal: Dan at once withdrew and knocked his head, saying: "Your foolish servant and concubine-subject heard it; the crime deserves death!"

entries.zh: 上因納，謂丹曰：「吾病浸加，恐不能自還。
entries.en: The emperor accepted this and said to Shi Dan, "My illness grows worse, and I fear I may not recover.
entries.literal: The sovereign thereupon accepted it and said to Dan: "My illness is gradually increasing; I fear I cannot return on my own.

entries.zh: 善輔道太子，毋違我意！」
entries.en: Guide the crown prince well and do not betray my intent!"
entries.literal: Well assist and guide the heir apparent; do not go against my intent!"

entries.zh: 丹噓唏而起。
entries.en: Shi Dan sobbed and rose.
entries.literal: Dan sobbed and rose.

entries.zh: 太子由是遂爲嗣矣。
entries.en: The crown prince was thereby secured as successor.
entries.literal: The heir apparent thereby became the successor.

entries.zh: 元帝竟崩，成帝初即位，擢丹爲長樂衛尉，遷右將軍，賜爵關內侯，食邑三百戶，給事中，後徙左將軍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: When Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng first succeeded, Shi Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, then General of the Right, granted Marquis within the Pass with a three-hundred-household fief and palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.
entries.literal: Emperor Yuan finally died; when Emperor Cheng first ascended the throne, Dan was promoted to Commandant of the Chang'le Palace Guard, transferred to General of the Right, granted rank as Marquis within the Pass with a fief of three hundred households, given palace attendance, and later moved to General of the Left and Grand Master of the Household.

entries.zh: 鴻嘉元年，上遂下詔曰：「夫褒有德，賞元功，古今通義也。
entries.en: In Hongjia 1 the emperor issued an edict: "Honoring the virtuous and rewarding great service is a principle honored in every age.
entries.literal: In the first year of Hongjia the sovereign then issued an edict saying: "To praise those with virtue and reward primary merit is the common principle of antiquity and the present.

entries.zh: 左將軍丹往時導朕以忠正，秉義醇一，舊德茂焉。
entries.en: General of the Left Shi Dan long ago guided Us with loyal uprightness, held to pure integrity, and his old merit is abundant.
entries.literal: General of the Left Dan in former times guided Us with loyalty and uprightness, held righteousness pure and single, and old virtue flourished therein.

entries.zh: 其封丹爲武陽侯，國東海郯之武強聚，戶千一百。」
entries.en: Let Shi Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with a fief at Wuqiang in Tan county, Donghai commandery, of eleven hundred households."
entries.literal: Let Dan be enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyang, with his state at Wuqiang village in Tan of Donghai, one thousand one hundred households."

entries.zh: 贊曰：自宜、元、成、哀外戚興者，許、史、三王、丁、傅之家，皆重侯累將，窮貴極富，見其位矣，未見其人也。
entries.en: The historian's judgment: From the reigns of Xuan through Ai, the consort clans—the Xu, the Shi, the three Wang lines, the Ding, and the Fu—stacked marquisates and generalships until they towered in wealth and rank; you could see their offices, rarely the men who deserved them.
entries.literal: The appraiser says: From Emperor Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, and Ai, those by whom outer kin rose—the houses of Xu, Shi, the three Wangs, Ding, and Fu—all piled marquisates and repeated generalships, exhausted nobility and exhausted wealth; one sees their positions, one has not seen their persons.

entries.zh: 陽平之王多有材能，好事慕名，其勢尤盛，曠貴最久。
entries.en: The Yangping Wangs were unusually able, ambitious, and conspicuous; no other kin clan held such power for so long.
entries.literal: The Wangs of Yangping mostly had talent and ability, loved affairs and sought fame; their power was especially flourishing; among them they held noble rank the longest.

entries.zh: 然至於莽，亦以覆國。
entries.en: Yet it was that same house that produced Wang Mang and overturned the dynasty.
entries.literal: Yet reaching to Mang, thereby also overturned the state.

entries.zh: 王商有剛毅節，廢黜以憂死，非其罪也。
entries.en: Wang Shang was a man of iron principle; driven from office, he died of grief for a fault that was not his own.
entries.literal: Wang Shang had firm and resolute integrity; dismissed and demoted, he died of worry; it was not his crime.

entries.zh: 史丹父子相繼，高以重厚，位至三公。
entries.en: Shi Dan and his father Shi Gao followed each other into high office; the father was famed for sober reliability, and both rose to the Three Excellencies.
entries.literal: Shi Dan and his father succeeded one another in office; Gao was famed for weighty steadiness, and their rank reached the Three Excellencies.

entries.zh: 丹之輔道副主，掩惡揚美，傅會善意，雖宿儒達士無以加焉。
entries.en: In guiding the heir he glossed over faults, magnified virtues, and put the best face on the prince's intentions—skills no veteran scholar could have surpassed.
entries.literal: Dan's assisting and guiding the deputy lord, covering evil and raising beauty, attaching and joining good intentions—even old Confucians and penetrating scholars had nothing by which to add thereto.

entries.zh: 及其歷房闥，入臥內，推至誠，犯顏色，動寤萬乘，轉移大謀，卒成太子，安母后之位。
entries.en: When he crossed into the inner apartments, spoke with blunt sincerity, and risked the emperor's anger, he swayed a decision that touched the throne itself, secured the succession for the crown prince, and preserved the empress's station.
entries.literal: Reaching to when he passed through the bedchamber doors, entered the inner sleeping quarters, pushed utmost sincerity, violated facial expression, moved and awakened the ten thousand chariots, shifted great plans, in the end completed the heir apparent, secured the empress dowager's position.

entries.zh: 「無言不讎」，終獲忠貞之報。
entries.en: The ode says, 'No loyal word goes unanswered'—and he lived to see the reward of his constancy.
entries.literal: 'No word spoken without answer'—in the end he obtained the reward of loyalty and steadfastness.

entries.zh: 傅喜守節不傾，亦蒙後凋之賞。
entries.en: Fu Xi held his integrity without wavering and likewise earned the praise reserved for the last evergreen.
entries.literal: Fu Xi guarded integrity and did not lean; also received the reward of later withering.

entries.zh: 哀、平際會，禍福速哉！
entries.en: How swiftly fortune and misfortune alternated at the juncture of the Ai and Ping reigns!
entries.literal: At the juncture meeting of Ai and Ping—misfortune and fortune swift!

entries.zh: 商少爲太子中庶子，以肅敬敦厚稱。
entries.en: In youth Wang Shang served as palace attendant to the crown prince and was known for solemn respect and steadfast integrity.
entries.literal: When young, Shang served as palace attendant to the heir and was known for solemn respect and solid integrity.

entries.zh: 父薨，商嗣爲侯，推財以分異母諸弟，身無所受，居喪哀戚。
entries.en: When his father died, Wang Shang inherited the marquisate, gave away his share of the estate to his half-brothers, kept nothing for himself, and mourned with deep grief.
entries.literal: When his father died, Shang succeeded as marquis, pushed out wealth to divide among half-brothers by a different mother, himself received nothing, and in mourning was grief-stricken.

entries.zh: 於是大臣薦商行可以厲群臣，義足以厚風俗，宜備近臣。
entries.en: Senior ministers then recommended him, saying his conduct could set an example for the bureaucracy and his righteousness could strengthen public morals; he ought to serve close to the throne.
entries.literal: Thereupon great ministers recommended Shang, saying his conduct could sharpen the host of officials and his righteousness was sufficient to enrich custom; he should be prepared as a close minister.

entries.zh: 繇是擢爲諸曹、侍中、中郎將。
entries.en: He was therefore promoted to posts in the various bureaus, as palace attendant, and as leader of the palace gentlemen.
entries.literal: From this he was promoted to the various bureaus, palace attendant, and leader of the palace gentlemen.

entries.zh: 元帝時，至右將軍、光祿大夫。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan he rose to General of the Right and Grand Master of the Household.
entries.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time he reached General of the Right and Grand Master of the Household.

entries.zh: 是時，定陶共王愛幸，幾代太子。
entries.en: At that time Prince Kang of Dingtao enjoyed the emperor's favor and nearly displaced the crown prince.
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Gong of Dingtao was loved and favored and nearly replaced the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 商爲外戚重臣輔政，擁佑太子，頗有力焉。
entries.en: As a leading consort-clan minister in the government, Wang Shang supported the crown prince and did much to protect his position.
entries.literal: Shang, as a weighty minister among the consort kin assisting government, supported and protected the heir apparent and had considerable force therein.

entries.zh: 自元帝為太子時，丹以父高任為中庶子，侍從十餘年。
entries.en: While Emperor Yuan was still crown prince, Shi Dan, through his father Shi Gao's standing, was appointed palace attendant to the heir and served at his side for more than a decade.
entries.literal: From the time when Emperor Yuan was heir apparent, Dan, through his father Shi Gao's rank, was appointed palace attendant to the heir and attended him for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 元帝即位，為駙馬都尉侍中，出常驂乘，甚有寵。
entries.en: When Yuan took the throne, Shi Dan became chief commandant of horsemen-at-attendance and palace attendant, routinely rode beside the emperor in the side car, and basked in imperial favor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan ascended the throne, he became chief commandant of horsemen-at-attendance and palace attendant; when going out he often rode in the accompanying chariot; he had great favor.

entries.zh: 上以丹舊臣，皇考外屬，親信之，詔丹護太子家。
entries.en: The emperor treated Shi Dan as a veteran of his father's household and a maternal relative, kept him close, and ordered him to oversee the crown prince's establishment.
entries.literal: The sovereign because Dan was an old minister and outer kin of the imperial father trusted him closely, and issued an edict for Dan to guard the heir apparent's household.

entries.zh: 是時，傅昭儀子定陶共王有材藝，子母俱愛幸，而太子頗有酒色之失，母王皇后無寵。
entries.en: At that time Consort Fu's son, Prince Kang of Dingtao, was gifted and accomplished, and mother and son both enjoyed the emperor's affection, whereas the crown prince showed a weakness for wine and women and his mother, Empress Wang, had fallen out of favor.
entries.literal: At this time, Consort Fu's son the Prince of Dingtao, the Prince of Gong, had talent and arts; son and mother were both loved and favored, while the heir apparent had quite failings of wine and sex, and his mother Empress Wang had no favor.

entries.zh: 元帝崩，成帝即位，甚敬重商，徙為左將軍。
entries.en: After Emperor Yuan died and Emperor Cheng took the throne, the new sovereign held Wang Shang in high regard and appointed him General of the Left.
entries.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Emperor Cheng ascended the throne; he greatly respected Wang Shang and transferred him to be General of the Left.

entries.zh: 而帝元舅大司馬大將軍王鳳顓權，行多驕僭。
entries.en: Meanwhile Wang Feng, the emperor's senior maternal uncle, served as grand marshal and grand general and dominated the government, and his behavior was frequently overbearing and out of line.
entries.literal: But the emperor's eldest uncle on the mother's side, Grand Marshal and Grand General Wang Feng, monopolized power, and his conduct was often arrogant and presumptuous.

entries.zh: 商論議不能平鳳，鳳知之，亦疏商。
entries.en: Wang Shang could not curb Wang Feng in council debate; Feng noticed the friction and kept his distance from him.
entries.literal: In deliberations Shang could not restrain Feng; Feng knew it and also kept Shang at a distance.

entries.zh: 建始三年秋，京師民無故相驚，言大水至，百姓奔走相蹂躪、老弱號呼，長安中大亂。
entries.en: In the autumn of Jianshi 3, rumor swept the capital that a catastrophic flood was imminent; people panicked, stampeded, and trampled one another while the elderly and children wailed, and Chang'an descended into chaos.
entries.literal: In the autumn of the third year of the Jianshi era, the people of the capital for no reason frightened one another, saying great floodwaters were coming; the common people ran about, trampling one another, the old and weak cried out, and great chaos arose in Chang'an.

entries.zh: 天子親御前殿，召公卿議。
entries.en: The emperor went in person to the front hall and called the high ministers into council.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven personally went to the front hall and summoned the dukes and ministers to deliberate.

entries.zh: 大將軍鳳以為太后與上及後宮可御船，令吏民上長安城以避水。
entries.en: Wang Feng proposed putting the empress dowager, the emperor, and the harem aboard boats and ordering officials and townsfolk onto the ramparts of Chang'an to ride out the supposed flood.
entries.literal: Grand General Feng thought the empress dowager, the sovereign, and the rear palace could board boats, and ordered clerks and people to ascend the walls of Chang'an to escape the water.

entries.zh: 群臣皆從鳳議。
entries.en: The entire court fell in behind Wang Feng's plan.
entries.literal: The host of ministers all followed Feng's proposal.

entries.zh: 左將軍商獨曰：「自古無道之國，水猶不冒城郭。
entries.en: Only General of the Left Wang Shang objected: 'Since antiquity, even in states without the Way, floodwaters have not overrun city walls.
entries.literal: General of the Left Shang alone said, 'Since antiquity, even in states without the Way, floodwaters have not overrun city walls.

entries.zh: 今政治和平，世無兵革，上下相安，何因當有大水一日暴至？
entries.en: We live in a time of peace, without war, and ruler and ruled are secure together; what could cause a deluge to strike the capital in an instant?
entries.literal: Now government and policies are peaceful, the age has no warfare, high and low are at ease with one another—what reason could there be for great waters suddenly to arrive in a single day?

entries.zh: 此必訛言也，不宜令上城，重驚百姓。」
entries.en: This is surely a groundless scare. Ordering everyone onto the walls would only panic the populace again.'
entries.literal: This must be false rumor; it is not fitting to order people onto the walls and again frighten the hundred surnames.'

entries.zh: 上乃止。
entries.en: The emperor dropped the idea.
entries.literal: The sovereign thereupon stopped.

entries.zh: 有頃，長安中稍定，問之，果訛言。
entries.en: Before long calm returned to Chang'an, and inquiries confirmed that the alarm had been nothing but rumor.
entries.literal: After a while, within Chang'an things gradually settled; when it was investigated, it was indeed false rumor.

entries.zh: 上於是美壯商之固守，數稱其議。
entries.en: The emperor then praised Wang Shang for holding firm and repeatedly commended his counsel.
entries.literal: The sovereign thereupon praised and admired Shang's steadfast holding firm, and repeatedly commended his proposal.

entries.zh: 而鳳大慚，自恨失言。
entries.en: Wang Feng was deeply embarrassed and bitterly regretted his rash words.
entries.literal: But Feng was greatly ashamed and hated himself for having misspoken.

entries.zh: 於是左將軍丹等奏：「商位三公，爵列侯，親受詔策為天下師，不遵法度以翼國家，而回辟下媚以進其私，執左道以亂政，為臣不忠，罔上不道，《甫刑》之辟，皆為上戮，罪名明白。
entries.en: General of the Left Shi Dan and his colleagues then memorialized: 'Wang Shang ranks among the Three Excellencies and holds a marquisate; he was personally commissioned to guide the realm. Instead of upholding the law to support the state, he courts favor below and pursues private ends, peddling heterodox practices that corrupt government. Such disloyalty and deceit of the throne violate the standards of the Fu Xing and merit execution; his offenses are plain.
entries.literal: Thereupon General of the Left Dan and others submitted: 'Shang occupies the Three Excellencies, his noble rank is marquis; he personally received edicts and appointments as teacher to all under heaven; he does not follow laws and regulations in order to wing the state, but turns aside and flatters those below to advance his private interests, holds to the left path and disorders government; as a minister he is disloyal, deceives the sovereign and is not in accord with the Way; the punishments of the Fu Xing are all capital executions for superiors—his guilt is clear.

entries.zh: 臣請詔謁者召商詣若盧詔獄。」
entries.en: We ask that Your Majesty order the court usher to take Wang Shang into custody at the Rolu imperial prison.'
entries.literal: We request that an edict be issued to the usher summoning Shang to the Rolu imperial prison.'

entries.zh: 上素重商，知匡言多險，制曰「勿治」。
entries.en: The emperor had long respected Wang Shang and recognized Zhang Kuang's memorial for the vicious attack it was, so he ruled, 'Take no further action.'
entries.literal: The sovereign had always esteemed Shang; he knew Kuang's words were mostly treacherous, and issued a rescript saying, 'Do not prosecute.'

entries.zh: 鳳固爭之，於是制詔御史：「蓋丞相以德輔翼國家，典領百寮，協和萬國，為職任莫重焉。
entries.en: Wang Feng would not let the matter drop, and the emperor had to issue an edict to the censor-in-chief: 'The chancellor exists to support the dynasty with moral authority, to head the bureaucracy, and to keep the realm in harmony—no burden is weightier.
entries.literal: Feng firmly disputed it; thereupon an edict was issued to the imperial secretary: 'In general the chancellor with virtue assists and wings the state, presides over the host of officials, harmonizes the myriad states—of offices and duties none is heavier.

entries.zh: 今樂昌侯商為丞相，出入五年，未聞忠言嘉謀，而有不忠執左道之辜，陷於大辟。
entries.en: Yet in five years as chancellor, Lechang Marquis Wang Shang has offered no loyal counsel worthy of the name, while the charge of disloyalty and heterodox conduct would carry the death penalty.
entries.literal: Now Lechang Marquis Shang has been chancellor, going in and out five years; loyal words and fine plans have not been heard from him, yet there is the guilt of disloyalty and holding to the left path, falling into great execution.

entries.zh: 前商女弟內行不修，奴賊殺人，疑商教使，為商重臣，故抑而不窮。
entries.en: Earlier his younger sister's private conduct was scandalous: a household slave committed murder, and some suspected Wang Shang ordered it. Because he was a pillar of the court, I suppressed the case and did not press to the bottom.
entries.literal: Earlier Shang's younger sister's conduct within was not cultivated; a slave villainously killed a person; there was suspicion Shang instructed and sent him; because Shang was a weighty minister, therefore it was suppressed and not fully investigated.

entries.zh: 今或言商不以自悔而反怨懟，朕甚傷之。
entries.en: Now I am told he shows no remorse but nurses grievance instead. That wounds me deeply.
entries.literal: Now some say Shang does not thereby repent himself but instead harbors resentment; We are greatly wounded by it.

entries.zh: 惟商與先帝有外親，未忍致於理。
entries.en: Yet Wang Shang is tied to the late emperor by marriage, and I cannot bring myself to subject him to full criminal process.
entries.literal: Only, Shang has outer kinship with the late emperor; We have not been able to bear bringing him to the law.

entries.zh: 其赦商罪。
entries.en: I therefore pardon his offenses.
entries.literal: Let Shang's crimes be pardoned.

entries.zh: 使者收丞相印綬。」
entries.en: Envoys shall relieve him of the chancellor's seal and sash.'
entries.literal: Let envoys collect the chancellor's seal and ribbon.'

entries.zh: 會日有蝕之，太中大夫蜀郡張匡，其人佞巧，上書願對近臣陳日蝕咎。
entries.en: When a solar eclipse occurred, Palace Grandee Zhang Kuang of Shu commandery, a sly and fawning man, submitted a memorial asking to address the emperor's close advisers on the meaning of the eclipse.
entries.literal: It happened that there was a solar eclipse; Grand Master of the Palace Zhang Kuang of Shu commandery, a man crafty and sycophantic, submitted a memorial wishing to address close ministers and explain the eclipse's blame.

entries.zh: 下朝者左將軍丹等問匡，對曰：「竊見丞相商作威作福，從外制中，取必於上，性殘賊不仁，遣票輕吏微求人罪，欲以立威，天下患苦之。
entries.en: After court, General of the Left Shi Dan and others questioned Zhang Kuang. He answered, "I have observed Chancellor Wang Shang wielding arbitrary power, controlling the court from outside, and extracting whatever he wants from the throne. He is cruel and ruthless, sending out swift minor officials to hunt for crimes in order to terrify the realm, and the people suffer greatly under him.
entries.literal: When the court adjourned, General of the Left Dan and others questioned Kuang; he replied: "I have privately seen Chancellor Shang making authority and making favor, controlling the center from outside, taking what he must from above; his nature is cruel, predatory, and without humaneness; he sends swift light clerks to probe subtly for people's crimes, wishing thereby to establish awe; all under heaven suffer and are pained by it.

entries.zh: 前頻陽耿定上書言商與父傅通，及女弟淫亂，奴殺其私夫，疑商教使。
entries.en: Earlier Geng Ding of Pinyang memorialized that Wang Shang had slept with his father's concubine, that his younger sister was promiscuous, and that a slave had killed her lover—some suspected Wang Shang had ordered it.
entries.literal: Earlier Geng Ding of Pinyang submitted a memorial saying Shang had illicit relations with his father's concubine, and that his younger sister's conduct was licentious—a slave killed her paramour, and there was suspicion Shang instructed and sent him.

entries.zh: 章下有司，商私怨懟。
entries.en: The memorial was referred to the proper offices, and Wang Shang nursed private resentment.
entries.literal: The memorial was sent down to the proper offices; Shang privately harbored resentment and defiance.

entries.zh: 商子俊欲上書告商，俊妻左將軍丹女，持其書以示丹，丹惡其父子乘迕，爲女求去。
entries.en: Wang Shang's son Jun tried to memorialize against his father. Jun's wife was Shi Dan's daughter; she showed the draft to her father. Dan despised the father-and-son breach and sought a divorce for his daughter.
entries.literal: Shang's son Jun wished to submit a memorial accusing Shang; Jun's wife was General of the Left Dan's daughter; she took the memorial and showed it to Dan; Dan hated the father and son's mutual defiance and sought divorce for his daughter.

entries.zh: 商不盡忠納善以輔至德，知聖主崇孝，遠別不親，後庭之事皆受命皇太后，太后前聞商有女，欲以備後宮，商言有固疾，後有耿定事，更詭道因李貴人家內女，執左道以亂政，誣罔悖大臣節，故應是而日蝕。
entries.en: Wang Shang has not served with full loyalty or accepted good counsel to support your supreme virtue. Knowing that a sage ruler honors filial piety and that the empress dowager governs the inner palace, he refused when the empress dowager earlier asked for his daughter for the harem, pleading chronic illness. After the Geng Ding affair he tried again through the household of the newly favored Lady Li to smuggle a daughter inside. He practices heterodox ways that corrupt government and violates every standard of a chief minister—hence the eclipse.
entries.literal: Shang does not exhaust loyalty and accept goodness to assist utmost virtue; knowing the sage sovereign honors filial piety and that distant partings are not intimate, rear-palace affairs all receive command from the empress dowager—the empress dowager earlier heard Shang had a daughter and wished to prepare her for the rear palace; Shang said she had a chronic illness; later came the Geng Ding affair, and further by devious paths through the household of the newly favored Lady Li he sought to send in a daughter; he holds to the left path and disorders government, deceives and violates a great minister's integrity—therefore Heaven responded with a solar eclipse.

entries.zh: 《周書》曰：『以左道事君者誅。』
entries.en: The Documents of Zhou says, "Those who serve their ruler by heterodox means are put to death."
entries.literal: The Documents of Zhou says: "Those who serve the ruler by the left path are executed."

entries.zh: 《易》曰：『日中見昧，則折其右肱。』
entries.en: The Changes says, "When darkness appears at noon, break the right arm."
entries.literal: The Changes says: "When gloom appears at midday, break the right upper arm."

entries.zh: 往者丞相周勃再建大功，及孝文時纖介怨恨，而日爲之蝕，於是退勃使就國，卒無怵惕憂。
entries.en: Formerly Chancellor Zhou Bo had rendered great service twice, yet when minor resentments arose under Emperor Wen the sun was eclipsed on his account; the emperor then sent Bo back to his fief, and he lived out his days without further fear.
entries.literal: In the past Chancellor Zhou Bo twice established great merit; when in Emperor Wen's time there were minute resentments, the sun was eclipsed for it; then Bo was dismissed and sent to his state, and in the end had no fearful worry.

entries.zh: 今商無尺寸之功，而有三世之寵，身位三公，宗族爲列侯、吏二千石、侍中諸曹，給事禁門內，連昏諸侯王，權寵至盛。
entries.en: Today Wang Shang has achieved nothing, yet enjoys three generations of imperial favor. He holds one of the Three Excellencies; his clan fills marquisates, two-thousand-shi offices, palace attendance, and bureau posts inside the forbidden gates; his family is intermarried with kings and lords, and his power and favor are at their height.
entries.literal: Now Shang has not a sliver of merit, yet enjoys three generations of favor; his person ranks among the Three Excellencies; his clan are ranked marquises, officials of two thousand shi, palace attendants and bureau officials, serving inside the forbidden gates; he has allied by marriage with feudal lords and kings—power and favor reach the utmost.

entries.zh: 審有內亂殺人怨懟之端，宜究竟考問。
entries.en: There are clear signs of domestic scandal, murder, and defiance; the matter should be thoroughly investigated.
entries.literal: Truly there are beginnings of inner disorder, murder, resentment, and defiance; he should be fully investigated and questioned.

entries.zh: 臣聞秦丞相呂不韋見王無子，意欲有秦國，即求好女以爲妻，陰知其有身而獻之王，產始皇帝。
entries.en: I have heard that Qin's chancellor Lü Buwei, seeing that the king had no heir, plotted to seize Qin: he found a beautiful woman, knew she was pregnant, and presented her to the king, and she bore the First Emperor.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that Qin chancellor Lü Buwei, seeing the king had no son, wished to possess the state of Qin; he then sought a fine woman as wife, secretly knowing she was with child and presenting her to the king, and she bore the First Emperor.

entries.zh: 及楚相春申君亦見王無子，心利楚國，即獻有身妻而產懷王。
entries.en: Chu's chancellor Lord Chunshen did the same when he saw the king had no heir, scheming for Chu's advantage by presenting a pregnant wife who bore King Huai of Chu.
entries.literal: And Chu chancellor Lord Chunshen likewise saw the king had no son, his heart set on benefiting the state of Chu; he then presented a pregnant wife and she bore King Huai.

entries.zh: 自漢興幾遭呂、霍之患，今商有不仁之性，乃因怨以內女，其奸謀未可測度。
entries.en: Since the founding of Han the dynasty has nearly fallen to the Lü and Huo clans. Wang Shang is ruthless and, nursing grievance, now tries to place a daughter in the palace—who can gauge the depth of such treachery?
entries.literal: Since Han rose, the dynasty has nearly suffered the calamities of the Lü and Huo clans; now Shang has an unkind nature and, because of resentment, seeks to send in a daughter—his treacherous plot cannot be measured.

entries.zh: 前孝景世七國反，將軍周亞夫以爲即得雒陽劇孟，關東非漢之有。
entries.en: In Emperor Jing's reign the seven states rebelled. General Zhou Yafu said that with Ju Meng of Luoyang on their side, the rebels could take everything east of the Pass from Han.
entries.literal: Formerly in Emperor Jing's time the seven states rebelled; General Zhou Yafu thought that if one obtained Ju Meng of Luoyang, the lands east of the Pass would not belong to Han.

entries.zh: 今商宗族權勢，合貲巨萬計，私奴以千數，非特劇孟匹夫之徒也。
entries.en: Today Wang Shang's clan commands wealth beyond counting and keeps thousands of private slaves—they are far more dangerous than a lone adventurer like Ju Meng.
entries.literal: Now Shang's clan in power and influence together possess wealth reckoned in tens of thousands; private slaves number in the thousands—they are not merely the likes of Ju Meng, a common man.

entries.zh: 且失道之至，親戚畔之，閨門內亂，父子相訐，而欲使之宜明聖化，調和海內，豈不謬哉！
entries.en: When a man has lost the Way so completely that kin rebel, the household is in scandal, and father and son denounce each other, how can he be expected to embody sage rule and harmonize the empire? The very idea is absurd!
entries.literal: Moreover, when one reaches the extreme of losing the Way, kin turn against one, the women's quarters are in inner disorder, father and son accuse each other—and yet one wishes to make him clarify and spread sage transformation and harmonize the realm within the seas: is this not absurd!

entries.zh: 商視事五年，官職陵夷而大惡著於百姓，甚虧損盛德，有鼎折足之凶。
entries.en: In five years in office Wang Shang has let government decay while the people suffer openly, gravely harming your sacred virtue—the omen of a broken tripod leg.
entries.literal: Shang has held office five years; official duties have declined while great evil is manifest among the hundred surnames, greatly damaging and diminishing august virtue—there is the omen of a tripod with a broken leg.

entries.zh: 臣愚以爲聖主富於春秋，即位以來，未有懲奸之威，加以繼嗣未立，大異並見，尤宜誅討不忠，以遏未然。
entries.en: Your servant believes that although Your Majesty is still young, since your accession you have not yet shown decisive power against traitors. With the succession unsettled and great portents appearing together, this is the moment to punish disloyalty and forestall worse to come.
entries.literal: Your foolish servant thinks the sage sovereign is rich in years of spring and autumn; since ascending the throne there has not been awe in punishing the treacherous; moreover the succession is not yet established and great prodigies appear together—it is especially fitting to execute and attack the disloyal to check what is not yet happened.

entries.zh: 行之一人，則海內震動，百奸之路塞矣。」
entries.en: Strike down this one man, and the empire will tremble; the roads of every kind of treachery will be closed."
entries.literal: Act against one man, and the realm within the seas will be shaken; the paths of a hundred treacheries will be blocked."

entries.zh: 商死後，連年日蝕、地震，直臣京兆尹王章上封事召開，訟商忠直無罪，言鳳顓權蔽主。
entries.en: After Wang Shang's death, solar eclipses and earthquakes followed year on year. Wang Zhang, the principled governor of the capital, submitted a sealed memorial; when the emperor summoned him and opened it, Zhang argued that Wang Shang had been loyal and blameless and that Wang Feng had monopolized power and blinded the throne.
entries.literal: After Shang died, year after year there were solar eclipses and earthquakes; the upright official metropolitan governor Wang Zhang submitted a sealed memorial; when summoned, it was opened, and he argued that Shang was loyal and straight and without guilt, saying Feng monopolized power and blocked the ruler.

entries.zh: 鳳竟以法誅章，語在《元後傳》。
entries.en: Wang Feng eventually had Wang Zhang executed on a legal pretext; the story is told in the biography of Empress Dowager Yuan.
entries.literal: Feng in the end by law executed Zhang; the account is in the 'Biography of the Yuan Empress Dowager.'

entries.zh: 至元始中，王莽為安漢公，誅不附己者，樂昌侯安見被以罪，自殺，國除。
entries.en: In the Yuanshi years Wang Mang, as Duke of Anhan, purged everyone who would not bend to him. Lechang Marquis Wang An was framed, took his own life, and his marquisate was extinguished.
entries.literal: By the Yuanshi era, Wang Mang was Duke of Anhan; he executed those who did not attach to himself; Lechang Marquis An was seen to be charged with crime, killed himself, and the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 卷八十二 王商史丹傅喜傳第五十二
entries.en: Volume 82: Biographies of Wang Shang, Shi Dan, and Fu Xi (the fifty-second chapter).
entries.literal: Volume 82: Biographies of Wang Shang, Shi Dan, and Fu Xi, Number 52.

entries.zh: 久之，哀帝初即位，博士申咸給事中，亦東海人也，毀宣不供養行喪服，薄於骨肉，前以不忠孝免，不宜復列封侯在朝省。
entries.en: Some time after Emperor Ai came to the throne, Erudit Shen Xian of Donghai served in palace attendance. He attacked Xue Xuan for failing to wear mourning while supporting the living and for coldness toward kin. Having once been dismissed for disloyalty and unfilial conduct, he ought not again to hold marquis rank and office at court.
entries.literal: After a long time, when Emperor Ai had just succeeded, Erudit Shen Xian served in palace attendance; he too was a man of Donghai. He slandered Xuan for not observing mourning dress while supporting the living and for being cold toward kin—he had earlier been dismissed for disloyalty and unfilial conduct and ought not again to be listed among enfeoffed marquises and court officials.

entries.zh: 宣子況為右曹侍郎，數聞其語，賕客楊明，欲令創咸面目，使不居位。
entries.en: Xue Xuan's son Kuang served as gentleman of the right bureau. Hearing Shen Xian's talk again and again, he bribed retainer Yang Ming to maim Shen Xian's face and drive him from office.
entries.literal: Xuan's son Kuang served as gentleman of the right bureau; having repeatedly heard his words, he bribed retainer Yang Ming, wishing to have Xian's face wounded so he would not hold office.

entries.zh: 會司隸缺，況恐咸為之，遂令明遮斫咸宮門外，斷鼻脣，身八創。
entries.en: When the metropolitan superintendency fell vacant, Kuang feared Shen Xian would be appointed. He sent Ming to ambush and hack Shen Xian outside the palace gate, cutting his nose and lips and leaving eight wounds on his body.
entries.literal: When the metropolitan superintendency fell vacant, Kuang feared Xian would get it; he therefore ordered Ming to waylay and hack Xian outside the palace gate, cutting nose and lips—eight wounds on his body.

entries.zh: 事下有司，御史中丞眾等奏：「況朝臣，父故宰相，再封列侯，不相敕丞化，而骨肉相疑，疑咸受修言以謗毀宣。
entries.en: The case went to the regular judiciary. Vice-Imperial Secretary Zhong and colleagues memorialized: "Xue Kuang is a court official whose father was twice a chancellor and a marquis, yet instead of setting a moral example he let kin turn on kin; Shen Xian is thought to have taken Xue Xiu's stories and used them to defame Xue Xuan.
entries.literal: The matter went down to the proper offices; Vice-Imperial Secretary Zhong and others submitted: "Kuang is a court minister; his father was a former chancellor, twice enfeoffed as marquis; he did not mutually instruct and assist transformation, yet flesh and bone suspected one another; it is suspected that Xian received Xiu's words to slander and destroy Xuan.

entries.zh: 咸所言皆宣行跡，眾人所共見，公家所宜聞。
entries.en: What Shen Xian said was common knowledge about Xue Xuan's conduct—facts the court should already have heard.
entries.literal: What Xian spoke was all Xuan's conduct and traces, what the multitude together saw and what the public house ought to have heard.

entries.zh: 況知咸給事中，恐為司隸舉奏宣，而公令明等迫切宮闕，要遮創戮近臣於大道人眾中，欲以隔塞聰明，杜絕論議之端。
entries.en: Kuang knew Shen Xian served in palace attendance and feared he would impeach Xue Xuan once metropolitan superintendent; he therefore sent Ming and others to crowd the palace approaches, waylay a senior minister in broad daylight in a public street, hoping to deafen the throne to criticism.
entries.literal: Kuang knew Xian was in attendance within the palace and feared he would impeach Xuan as metropolitan superintendent; he openly ordered Ming and others to press close to the palace gates, intercept and wound a near minister in the middle of the great road among the crowd, wishing thereby to block clear hearing and cut off the beginnings of discussion.

entries.zh: 桀黠無所畏忌，萬眾言雚嘩，流聞四方，不與凡民忿怒爭鬥者同。
entries.en: It was a brazen, calculated act that set the capital roaring—not a common brawl among angry townsfolk.
entries.literal: Wicked and cunning, without anything they feared or shunned, the myriad crowd clamored and hubbubbed, flowing rumor to the four quarters—not the same as common people angry and fighting.

entries.zh: 臣聞敬近臣，為近主也。
entries.en: I have heard that to respect the ruler's near ministers is to draw near the ruler himself.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that to respect near ministers is to be near the ruler.

entries.zh: 禮，下公門，式路馬，君畜產且猶敬之。
entries.en: Ritual requires even a duke's gate horse to be treated with respect—how much more a man at the emperor's side?
entries.literal: By ritual, when descending from a duke's gate one pats the road horse; the ruler's domestic animals are yet respected.

entries.zh: 《春秋》之義，意惡功遂，不免於誅，上浸之源不可長也，況首為惡，明手傷，功意俱惡，皆大不敬。
entries.en: The Spring and Autumn Annals condemn evil intent even when the crime "succeeds"; the first trickle of contempt for authority must not be tolerated—especially when the blow is premeditated, delivered with the fist, and both motive and act are outrageous.
entries.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is: when the intent is evil though the deed succeeds, execution is not avoided; the spring of upward seeping must not be lengthened—how much more when one is first in evil, clearly wounds with the hand, and both deed and intent are evil—all is great irreverence.

entries.zh: 明當以重論，及況皆棄市。」
entries.en: Ming deserves the full penalty; Kuang and his accomplices should die in the public square."
entries.literal: Ming should be judged heavily; Kuang and the rest should be exposed in the market."

entries.zh: 廷尉直以為：「律曰『斗以刃傷人，完為城旦，其賊加罪一等，與謀者同罪。』
entries.en: Commandant of justice Zhi argued: "The code says that in a brawl a cut with a blade earns wall-dawn labor at intact status, malicious wounding adds one degree, and accomplices share the principal's guilt.
entries.literal: Commandant of justice Zhi held: "The statute says, 'In a brawl, if one wounds another with a blade, let him be intact and sentenced to wall dawn; if it is malicious wounding, add one degree to the crime, the same guilt as conspirators.

entries.zh: 詔書無以詆欺成罪。
entries.en: Imperial edicts do not treat mere defamation as a completed capital offense.
entries.literal: Edicts do not make slander alone a completed crime.

entries.zh: 傳曰：『遇人不以義而見□者，與□人之罪鈞，惡不直也。』
entries.en: The exegetical tradition says that when someone wrongs you without justice, striking back matches the wrongdoer's guilt—because the response is not upright."
entries.literal: The tradition says, 'When one meets a person not in accordance with rightness and is wronged by him, to strike the wrongdoer is equal guilt—evil is not being straight.

entries.zh: 咸厚善修，而數稱宣惡，流聞不誼，不可謂直。
entries.en: Shen Xian was Xiu's intimate and kept retailing scandal about Xue Xuan; the talk that spread was hardly honorable—so his conduct was not "straight" either.
entries.literal: Xian was thickly friendly with Xiu and repeatedly proclaimed Xuan's evil; rumor spread of impropriety—this cannot be called straight.

entries.zh: 況以故傷咸，計謀已定，後聞置司隸，因前謀而趣明，非以恐咸為司隸故造謀也。
entries.en: Kuang struck Shen Xian over an old feud; the ambush was already planned before a metropolitan superintendent was named, and Ming merely carried it out—Kuang did not hatch the scheme only because he feared Shen Xian's new appointment.
entries.literal: Kuang for an old grudge wounded Xian; the plot was already set when later he heard a metropolitan superintendent was appointed; he therefore pressed forward with the earlier plan through Ming—it was not that he newly devised the plot because he feared Xian would become metropolitan superintendent.

entries.zh: 本爭私變，雖於掖門外傷咸道中，與凡民爭鬥無異。
entries.en: At bottom it was a private quarrel; though the blow fell outside the Ye Gate, it was still a street fight among private citizens.
entries.literal: Originally they disputed private matters; although they wounded Xian outside the Ye Gate on the road, it differs nothing from common people fighting.

entries.zh: 殺人者死，傷人者刑，古今之通道，三代所不易也。
entries.en: Killers die and wounders are punished—that rule has held since high antiquity and the three dynasties never changed it.
entries.literal: Those who kill die, those who wound suffer punishment—the thoroughfare from antiquity to the present, what the three ages have not altered.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：『必也正名。』
entries.en: Confucius said, "The first task is to set names right."
entries.literal: Confucius said, "There must be correction of names."

entries.zh: 名不正，則至於刑罰不中；
entries.en: If names are wrong, penalties cannot be even;
entries.literal: If names are not correct, then punishments do not hit the mean;

entries.zh: 刑罰不中，而民無所錯手足。
entries.en: when penalties are uneven, the people lose all bearings.
entries.literal: if punishments do not hit the mean, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot.

entries.zh: 今以況為首惡，明手傷為大不敬，公私無差。
entries.en: To brand Kuang as the arch-villain and Ming's punch as "great irreverence" collapses public crime with private brawling.
entries.literal: Now to treat Kuang as chief in evil and Ming's hand-wounding as great irreverence makes no distinction between public and private.

entries.zh: 《春秋》之義，原心定罪。
entries.en: The Annals teach us to weigh intent when fixing guilt.
entries.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn is: examine the heart to fix the crime.

entries.zh: 原況以父見謗發忿怒，無它大惡。
entries.en: Kuang acted from rage at slander against his father; there was no deeper treason.
entries.literal: Examining Kuang, he was moved by anger because his father was slandered; he had no other great evil.

entries.zh: 加詆欺，輯小過成大辟，陷死刑，違明詔，恐非法意，不可施行。
entries.en: Piling on defamation, inflating a petty affray into a capital case, and ignoring an explicit amnesty would violate the spirit of the statutes.
entries.literal: To add slander charges, gather petty faults into a capital crime, trap him in death penalty, and violate a clear edict—We fear it is not the intent of the law and cannot be carried out.

entries.zh: 聖王不以怒增刑。
entries.en: A sage ruler does not sharpen sentences in a fit of temper.
entries.literal: A sage king does not increase punishment because of anger.

entries.zh: 明當以賊傷人不直，況與謀者皆爵減完為城旦。」
entries.en: Ming should answer for malicious battery; Kuang and his fellow plotters should lose one noble rank and serve wall-dawn labor at intact status."
entries.literal: Ming should be sentenced for malicious wounding without rightness; Kuang and the conspirators should all have noble rank reduced and intact wall dawn."

entries.zh: 上以問公卿議臣。
entries.en: The emperor referred the question to his ministers and policy advisers.
entries.literal: The sovereign thereupon asked the dukes and ministers and deliberating officials.

entries.zh: 丞相孔光、大司空師丹以中丞議是，自將軍以下至博士、議郎皆是廷尉。
entries.en: Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan agreed with the censor's bench; from the generals down through the academicians everyone backed the commandant of justice.
entries.literal: Chancellor Kong Guang and Grand Minister of Works Shi Dan held the vice-imperial secretary's opinion correct; from generals downward to erudits and deliberation gentlemen, all sided with the commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 況竟減罪一等，徙敦煌。
entries.en: Kuang's sentence was commuted one step and he was exiled to Dunhuang.
entries.literal: Kuang in the end had his crime reduced one degree and was banished to Dunhuang.

entries.zh: 宣坐免為庶人，歸故郡，卒於家。
entries.en: Stripped of office for his connection to the affair, Xue Xuan went home to his native commandery and died there.
entries.literal: Xuan by the case was dismissed to commoner status, returned to his home commandery, and died at home.

entries.zh: 初，漢興襲秦官，置丞相、御史大夫、太尉。
entries.en: At the founding Han copied Qin by installing chancellor, imperial secretary, and grand commandant.
entries.literal: At first, when Han rose it inherited Qin offices, setting chancellor, imperial secretary, and grand commandant.

entries.zh: 至武帝罷太尉，始置大司馬以冠將軍之號，非有印綬官屬也。
entries.en: Emperor Wu dropped the grand commandant and added the title grand marshal as a general's honorific, without its own seal or staff.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu abolished the grand commandant, he first established grand marshal as a cap title for generals; it had no seal-ribbon or subordinate staff.

entries.zh: 及成帝時，何武為九卿，建言：「古者民樸事約，國之輔佐必得賢聖，然猶則天三光，備三公官，各有分職。
entries.en: Under Emperor Cheng, Minister He Wu argued: "In high antiquity life was simple and government lean; even sage assistants modeled the three lights of heaven, so the three dukes each had a clear portfolio.
entries.literal: By Emperor Cheng's time He Wu was among the nine ministers and submitted advice: "In antiquity the people were simple and affairs few; the state's assistants had to be worthy sages, yet still they modeled heaven's three luminaries, fully providing the three duke offices, each with divided duties.

entries.zh: 今末俗之弊，政事煩多，宰相之材不能及古，而丞相獨兼三公之事，所以久廢而不治也。
entries.en: Today business is tangled and no single chancellor can match the old ideal, yet one man still does three jobs—that is why government drags.
entries.literal: Now the flaws of decadent custom are many and affairs vexatious; the chancellor's talent cannot match antiquity, yet the chancellor alone combines the three dukes' business—therefore governance has long lain waste and is not ordered.

entries.zh: 宜建三公官，定卿大夫之任，分職授政，以考功效。」
entries.en: He urged restoring the three dukes, defining ministers' roles, and splitting authority so performance could be judged."
entries.literal: It is fitting to establish the three duke offices, fix the duties of ministers and grandees, divide offices and grant administration, and thereby examine merit and effect."

entries.zh: 其後上以問師安昌侯張禹，禹以為然。
entries.en: The emperor consulted Tutor Zhang Yu of Anchang, who agreed.
entries.literal: Later the sovereign asked Tutor Marquis of Anchang Zhang Yu; Yu held it correct.

entries.zh: 時曲陽侯王根為大司馬票騎將軍，而何武為御史大夫。
entries.en: Wang Gen, Marquis of Quyang, then held grand marshal with the agile-cavalry generalship, while He Wu was imperial secretary.
entries.literal: At that time Marquis of Quyang Wang Gen was grand marshal and general-in-chief of agile cavalry, while He Wu was imperial secretary.

entries.zh: 於是上賜曲陽侯根大司馬印綬，置官屬，罷票騎將軍官，以御史大夫何武為大司空，封列侯，皆增奉如丞相，以備三公官焉。
entries.en: The throne gave Wang Gen the grand marshal seal and staff, dropped the separate agile-cavalry post, made He Wu grand minister of works with a marquisate and chancellor-level salary, rounding out the three excellencies.
entries.literal: Thereupon the sovereign bestowed on Marquis of Quyang Gen the grand marshal seal and ribbon, established subordinate staff, abolished the agile-cavalry general office, made Imperial Secretary He Wu grand minister of works, enfeoffed him as marquis, and increased their salaries like the chancellor's, thereby completing the three duke offices.

entries.zh: 議者多以為古今異制，漢自天下之號下至佐史皆不同於古，而獨改三公，職事難分明，無益於治亂。
entries.en: Critics complained that Han titles from the throne down to runners bore little resemblance to antiquity, so tinkering with the three excellencies only blurred lines of authority without helping order.
entries.literal: Discussants mostly thought ancient and present institutions differed; Han from the title of all under heaven down to assistant clerks all differed from antiquity, yet to change only the three dukes made duties hard to separate clearly and brought no benefit to order or chaos.

entries.zh: 是時，御史府吏捨百餘區井水皆竭；
entries.en: About then the censorate's hundred-odd clerk dormitories saw every well run dry;
entries.literal: At that time in the censorate yamen more than a hundred clerk lodgings had wells whose water all ran dry;

entries.zh: 又其府中列柏樹，常有野烏數千棲宿其上，晨去暮來，號日「朝夕烏」，烏去不來者數月，長老異之。
