entries.en: In the courtyard there was also a row of cypress trees where several thousand wild crows used to roost. They left at dawn and returned at dusk, and were called the "dawn-and-dusk crows." When the crows went away and did not return for several months, the elders found it uncanny.
entries.literal: moreover in its courtyard stood a row of cypress trees on which several thousand wild crows habitually roosted, leaving at dawn and returning at dusk, called the "dawn-and-dusk crows"; the crows left and did not come for several months—the elders thought it strange.

entries.zh: 後二歲餘，朱博為大司空，奏言：「帝王之道不必相襲，各由時務。
entries.en: More than two years later, after Zhu Bo became Grand Minister of Works, he memorialized: "The way of emperors and kings need not copy one another; each follows the needs of its time.
entries.literal: More than two years later Zhu Bo became grand minister of works and submitted: "The way of emperors and kings need not copy one another; each follows the tasks of the time.

entries.zh: 高皇帝以聖德受命，建立鴻業，置御史大夫，位次丞相，典正法度，以職相參，總領百官，上下相監臨，歷載二百年，天下安寧。
entries.en: Gaozu created the imperial secretary below the chancellor to guard the statutes, coordinate the bureaucracy, and keep checks on power—a system that kept peace for two hundred years.
entries.literal: The August Founder by sagely virtue received the mandate, set up the great enterprise, established the imperial secretary, rank next the chancellor, in charge of correcting law and standards, to participate in duties by office, oversee the hundred offices, and mutually supervise high and low—for two hundred years the realm has been peaceful.

entries.zh: 今更為大司空，與丞相同位，未獲嘉祐。
entries.en: Renaming that office grand minister of works and making it equal to the chancellor has brought no blessing.
entries.literal: Now it has been changed to grand minister of works, coequal with the chancellor, and auspicious blessing has not been obtained.

entries.zh: 故事，選郡國守相高第為中二千石，選中二千石為御史大夫，任職者為丞相，位次有序，所以尊聖德，重國相也。
entries.en: Custom promoted star governors to full two-thousand-dan, then to imperial secretary, then to chancellor—a ladder that honored the realm's chief minister.
entries.literal: By precedent the top-ranked commandery governors are chosen as fully two-thousand-dan; from fully two-thousand-dan the imperial secretary is chosen; the one who takes office becomes chancellor—the order of rank is sequential, thereby honoring sagely virtue and weighting the state's minister.

entries.zh: 今中二千石未更御史大夫而為丞相，權輕，非所以重國政也。
entries.en: Skipping the censorate on the way to chancellor weakens the chain of command.
entries.literal: Now fully two-thousand-dan men become chancellor without passing through imperial secretary; the power is light—not the way to weight state government.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為大司空官可罷，復置御史大夫，遵奉舊制。
entries.en: I move to abolish grand minister of works and restore the imperial secretary under the old rules.
entries.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the grand minister of works office may be abolished and the imperial secretary restored, following the old system.

entries.zh: 臣願盡力，以御史大夫為百僚率。」
entries.en: I will serve with all I have as first among the ministers."
entries.literal: Your servant wishes to exert his strength to the utmost, taking the imperial secretary as leader of the hundred offices."

entries.zh: 哀帝從之，乃更拜博為御史大夫。
entries.en: Emperor Ai agreed and named Zhu Bo imperial secretary.
entries.literal: Emperor Ai followed it; then he again appointed Bo imperial secretary.

entries.zh: 會大司馬喜免，以陽安侯丁明為大司馬衛將軍，置官屬，大司馬冠號如故事。
entries.en: When Grand Marshal Fu Xi fell, Ding Ming became grand marshal and guards general with full staff, reviving the old grand marshal style.
entries.literal: It happened that Grand Marshal Xi was dismissed; Marquis of Yang'an Ding Ming was made grand marshal and guards general with subordinate staff; the grand marshal cap title followed old precedent.

entries.zh: 後四歲，哀帝遂改丞相為大司徒，復置大司空、大司馬焉。
entries.en: Four years on, Ai renamed the chancellor grand minister of education and reinstated grand minister of works and grand marshal.
entries.literal: Four years later Emperor Ai changed the chancellor to grand minister of education, and again set grand minister of works and grand marshal.

entries.zh: 卷八十三 薛宣朱博傳第五十三
entries.en: Volume 83: Biographies of Xue Xuan and Zhu Bo (chapter fifty-three).
entries.literal: Volume 83: Biographies of Xue Xuan and Zhu Bo, Number 53.

entries.zh: 莽聞之，大懼，乃拜其黨親輕車將軍成武侯孫建為奮武將軍，光祿勳成都侯王邑為虎牙將軍，明義侯王駿為強弩將軍，春王城門校尉王況為震威將軍，宗伯忠孝侯劉宏為奮衝將軍，中少府建威侯王昌為中堅將軍，中郎將震羌侯竇兄為奮威將軍，凡七人，自擇除關西人為校尉軍吏，將關東甲卒，發奔命以擊義焉。
entries.en: Mang was terrified. He commissioned seven kinsmen and allies: Sun Jian, Marquis of Chengwu, as Raising Martial general; Wang Yi, Marquis of Chengdu, as Tiger Fang general; Wang Jun, Marquis of Mingyi, as Strong Crossbow general; Wang Kuang, commandant of the Chunwang Gate, as Shaking Awe general; Liu Hong, Marquis of Loyal Filial Piety, as Raising Assault general; Wang Chang, Marquis of Jianwei, as Center Hard general; and Dou Xiong, Marquis Who Shakes the Qiang, as Raising Might general. Mang personally picked officers from west of the passes as colonels and staff, mobilized armored troops from the east, and called out every emergency levy to crush Yi.
entries.literal: When Mang heard it, he was greatly afraid; thereupon he appointed his faction and kin—Light Chariot general Marquis of Chengwu Sun Jian as Raising Martial general, Superintendent of the Household Marquis of Chengdu Wang Yi as Tiger Fang general, Marquis of Mingyi Wang Jun as Strong Crossbow general, Spring Gate Commandant of the Gates Wang Kuang as Shaking Awe general, Minister of the Imperial Clan Marquis of Loyal Filial Piety Liu Hong as Raising Assault general, Privy Treasurer Jianwei Marquis Wang Chang as Center Hard general, Gentleman of the Palace Marquis Who Shakes the Qiang Dou Xiong as Raising Might general—in all seven men; he himself chose and appointed men from west of the passes as colonels and army clerks, led east-of-the-pass armored soldiers, and issued emergency call-ups to strike Yi.

entries.zh: 復以太僕武讓為積弩將軍屯函谷關，將作大匠蒙鄉侯逯並為橫野將軍屯武關，羲和紅休侯劉歆為揚武將軍屯宛，太保後丞丞陽侯甄邯為大將軍屯霸上，常鄉侯王惲為車騎將軍屯平樂館，騎都尉王晏為建威將軍屯城北，城門校尉趙恢為城門將軍，皆勒兵自奮。
entries.en: He also named Grand Coachman Wu Rang Piled Crossbow general at Hangu Pass; Court Architect Lu Bing, Marquis of Mengxiang, as Transverse Wild general at Wu Pass; Liu Xin, Hongxiu marquis and minister of the calendar, as general displaying martial prowess at Nanyang; Zhen Han, Marquis of Chengyang, as grand general at Bashang; Wang Yun, Marquis of Changxiang, as chariot-and-cavalry general at Pingle Lodge; Cavalry Commandant Wang Yan as Establishing Might general north of the walls; and Gate Commandant Zhao Hui as gate general. Each braced his command for battle.
entries.literal: Again he made Grand Coachman Wu Rang Piled Crossbow general to garrison Hangu Pass, Court Architect Marquis of Mengxiang Lu Bing Transverse Wild general to garrison Wu Pass, Minister of the Calendar Hongxiu Marquis Liu Xin General Who Displays Martial Prowess to garrison Wan, Grand Guardian and Rear Chancellor Marquis of Chengyang Zhen Han grand general to garrison Bashang, Marquis of Changxiang Wang Yun chariot and cavalry general to garrison Pingle Lodge, Cavalry Commandant Wang Yan Establishing Might general to garrison north of the city, Commandant of the Gates Zhao Hui Gate general—all tightened troops and roused themselves.

entries.zh: 初，三輔聞翟義起，自茂陵以西至□二十三縣盜賊並發，趙明、霍鴻等自稱將軍，攻燒官寺，殺右輔都尉及□令，劫略吏民，眾十餘萬，火見未央宮前殿。
entries.en: When Yi rebelled, from Maoling west through twenty-three counties the capital region erupted: Zhao Ming and Huo Hong declared themselves generals, torched yamen, slew metropolitan deputies and magistrates, looted towns, and gathered more than a hundred thousand men until flames lit the sky before Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: At first, when the Three Adjuncts heard Zhai Yi had risen, from Maoling west to □ twenty-three counties bandits rose together; Zhao Ming, Huo Hong, and others styled themselves generals, attacked and burned government offices, killed the capital-region deputy and □ magistrate, plundered officials and commoners—the host was more than a hundred thousand; fire was seen before Weiyang Palace's front hall.

entries.zh: 莽晝夜抱孺子禱宗廟。
entries.en: Mang day and night clutched the boy emperor and prayed in the shrines of his ancestors.
entries.literal: Mang day and night embraced the infant and prayed in the ancestral shrines.

entries.zh: 復拜衛尉王級為虎賁將軍，大鴻臚望鄉侯閻遷為折衝將軍，與甄邯、王晏西擊趙明等。
entries.en: He named Wang Ji, commandant of the guards, Tiger Fury general, and Yan Qian, Marquis of Wangxiang, as Assault general, and sent them with Zhen Han and Wang Yan west against Zhao Ming.
entries.literal: Again he appointed Commandant of the Guards Wang Ji as Tiger Fury general, Grand Herald Marquis of Wangxiang Yan Qian as Assault general, together with Zhen Han and Wang Yan to strike Zhao Ming and others from the west.

entries.zh: 正月，虎牙將軍王邑等自關東還，便引兵西。
entries.en: In the first month Wang Yi, Tiger Fang general, marched back from the east and at once turned his column west.
entries.literal: In the first month, Tiger Fang general Wang Yi and others returned from east of the passes and thereupon led troops west.

entries.zh: 強弩將軍王駿以無功免，揚武將軍劉歆歸故官。
entries.en: Wang Jun lost his post as Strong Crossbow general for failure; Liu Xin went back to his old portfolio as general displaying martial prowess.
entries.literal: Strong Crossbow general Wang Jun was dismissed for lacking merit; General Who Displays Martial Prowess Liu Xin returned to his former office.

entries.zh: 復以邑弟侍中王奇為揚武將軍，城門將軍趙恢為強弩將軍，中郎將李□為厭難將軍，復將兵西。
entries.en: Wang Yi's brother Wang Qi, a palace attendant, was named general displaying martial prowess; Zhao Hui became Strong Crossbow general; a Gentleman Li □ took the Hardship-quelling title, and the western column marched again.
entries.literal: Again he made Yi's younger brother, attendant Wang Qi, General Who Displays Martial Prowess, Gate general Zhao Hui Strong Crossbow general, Gentleman of the Palace Li □ Hardship-quelling general, and again led troops west.

entries.zh: 二月，明等殄滅，諸縣悉平，還師振旅。
entries.en: By the second month Zhao Ming's band was destroyed, every county was quiet, and the host marched home in good order.
entries.literal: In the second month Ming and the others were wiped out; all counties were pacified; the army returned and shook the ranks.

entries.zh: 莽乃置酒白虎殿，勞饗將帥，大封拜。
entries.en: Mang then held a banquet in the White Tiger Hall for his generals, heaped rewards on them, and handed out a fresh round of titles.
entries.literal: Mang thereupon set wine in the White Tiger Hall, feasted and rewarded generals and commanders, and greatly invested and appointed.

entries.zh: 先是，益州蠻夷及金城塞外羌反畔，時州郡擊破之。
entries.en: Earlier the Yi tribesmen and the Jincheng Qiang beyond the wall had risen; provincial troops had already beaten them down.
entries.literal: Earlier, the barbarians of Yi commandery and the Qiang beyond the barrier of Jincheng had rebelled; at the time commanderies and states had crushed them.

entries.zh: 莽乃並隸，以小大為差，封侯、伯、子、男凡三百九十五人，曰「皆以奮怒，東指西擊，羌寇蠻盜，反虜逆賊，不得旋踵，應時殄滅，天下咸服」之功封雲。
entries.en: Wang Mang then grouped these campaigns together and graded the awards by importance, enfeoffing 395 men as marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons. He declared that they were rewarded for the merit of having "roused themselves in anger, struck east and west, and destroyed Qiang raiders, Man bandits, rebel captives, and traitorous thieves before they could even turn on their heels, so that all under heaven submitted."
entries.literal: Mang thereupon combined and subsumed them, by great and small as gradation, enfeoffing marquises, earls, viscounts, and barons—three hundred ninety-five persons in all—saying "all by raging anger, pointing east and striking west, Qiang raiders and Man bandits, rebel captives and traitorous thieves, could not turn heel; they were wiped out in season, and the realm all submitted"—merit for enfeoffment was thus declared.

entries.zh: 莽於是自謂大得天人之助，至其年十二月，遂即真矣。
entries.en: Convinced that Heaven and humanity favored him, in the twelfth month of that year he took the throne in his own name.
entries.literal: Mang thereupon deemed himself greatly to have obtained Heaven and man's aid; reaching that year's twelfth month, he thereupon assumed the true position.

entries.zh: 卷八十四 翟方進傳第五十四
entries.en: Volume 84, the fifty-fourth biography: Zhai Fangjin.
entries.literal: Volume 84, Biography the Fifty-Fourth: Zhai Fangjin.

entries.zh: 數年，出為安定太守。
entries.en: Several years later he was sent out as governor of Anding.
entries.literal: Several years later he went out as governor of Anding.

entries.zh: 時上諸舅皆修經書，任政事。
entries.en: At that time the emperor's maternal uncles all studied the classics and held government posts.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor's maternal uncles all studied the classics and held government posts.

entries.zh: 平阿侯譚年次當繼大將軍鳳輔政，尤與永善。
entries.en: Marquis of Ping'a Tan, next in line to succeed Grand General Wang Feng, was especially close to Yong.
entries.literal: Marquis of Ping'a Tan by seniority ought to succeed Grand General Feng in assisting government, and was especially friendly with Yong.

entries.zh: 陽朔中，鳳薨。
entries.en: During Yangshuo, Wang Feng died.
entries.literal: In the Yangshuo period Feng died.

entries.zh: 鳳病困，薦從弟御史大夫音以自代。
entries.en: On his deathbed Feng recommended his younger cousin, Imperial Counselor Wang Yin, to succeed him.
entries.literal: Feng, gravely ill, recommended his younger cousin, imperial counselor Yin, to replace himself.

entries.zh: 上從之，以音為大司馬車騎將軍，領尚書事，而平阿侯譚位特進，領城門兵。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, making Yin grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry with charge of masters-of-writing affairs, while Marquis of Ping'a Tan held special advancement and commanded the gate troops.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this, making Yin grand marshal and general of chariots and cavalry with charge of masters-of-writing affairs, while Marquis of Ping'a Tan held special advancement and commanded the gate troops.

entries.zh: 永聞之，與譚書曰：「君侯躬周召之德，執管晏之操，敬賢下士，樂善不倦，宜在上將久矣，以大將軍在，故抑鬱於家，不得舒憤。
entries.en: Yong wrote to Tan: "You bear the virtue of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao and the conduct of Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, honoring worthies and delighting in good without weariness—you should long have stood among the chief generals. While the grand general lived you were kept at home and could not vent your grievance.
entries.literal: Yong heard this and wrote to Tan: "Lord, you personally bear the virtue of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao and hold the conduct of Guan Zhong and Yan Ying, honoring worthies and lowering yourself to scholars, delighting in good without weariness—you ought long ago to have stood among the chief generals. Because the grand general was alive, you were depressed at home and could not vent your grievance.

entries.zh: 今大將軍不幸蚤薨，絫親疏，序材能，宜在君侯。
entries.en: Now the grand general has died young; weighing kinship and ability, the post ought to be yours.
entries.literal: Now the grand general has unhappily died young; weighing kin near and far and ordering ability, the place ought to be yours, lord.

entries.zh: 拜吏之日，京師士大夫悵然失望。
entries.en: On appointment day the capital's scholar-officials were despondent and disappointed.
entries.literal: On the day of appointment the capital's scholar-officials were despondent and disappointed.

entries.zh: 此皆永等愚劣，不能褒揚萬一。
entries.en: This is because men like me are too foolish to praise you as you deserve.
entries.literal: All this is because Yong and others are foolish and base, unable to praise you one ten-thousandth.

entries.zh: 屬聞以特進領城門兵，是則車騎將軍秉政雍容于內，而至戚賢舅執管籥於外也。
entries.en: I hear you now hold special advancement and command the gate troops—so the general of chariots and cavalry rules at ease within while the nearest kin and worthy uncle holds the keys without.
entries.literal: I have just heard that you hold special advancement and command the gate troops—this means the general of chariots and cavalry holds government at ease within, while the nearest kin and worthy uncle holds the keys without.

entries.zh: 愚竊不為君侯喜。
entries.en: I cannot rejoice for you in this.
entries.literal: Your foolish servant privately does not rejoice for you, lord.

entries.zh: 宜深辭職，自陳淺薄不足以固城門之守，收太伯之讓，保謙謙之路，闔門高枕，為知者首。
entries.en: You ought deeply to decline, saying yourself too shallow to secure the gates, take Taibo's example of yielding, keep to humility, shut your gates and rest easy, and be foremost among the wise.
entries.literal: You ought deeply to decline the post, declaring yourself too shallow to secure the gate defense, take Taibo's yielding, keep the path of humility, shut your gates and rest easy, and be foremost among the wise.

entries.zh: 願君侯與博覽者參之，小子為君侯安此。」
entries.en: Consult the broadly learned; I write this for your peace."
entries.literal: I wish you, lord, to consult the broadly learned; your young servant writes this for your peace."

entries.zh: 譚得其書大感，遂辭讓不受領城門職。
entries.en: Tan, deeply moved, declined and refused command of the gate troops.
entries.literal: Tan, greatly moved by the letter, thereupon declined and did not accept command of the gate troops.

entries.zh: 由是譚、音相與不平。
entries.en: From this Tan and Yin grew mutually resentful.
entries.literal: From this Tan and Yin were mutually resentful.

entries.zh: 音用從舅越親輔政，威權損於鳳時，永復說音曰：「將軍覆上將之位，食豪腴之都，任周、召之職，擁天下之樞，可謂富貴之極，人臣無二，天下之責四面至矣，將何以居之？
entries.en: When Yin came to power through a maternal uncle and his authority fell short of Wang Feng's, Yong urged him: "You hold a marshal's rank, feed on the richest commanderies, bear the burden of the Zhou dukes, and turn the empire's hinge—you have reached the peak of wealth and power, yet blame now converges from every quarter. How will you bear it?
entries.literal: Yin by maternal uncle's kin overstepping nearness aided government; awe and power were less than in Feng's time; Yong again exhorted Yin, saying: "General, you cover the highest general's position, eat from rich and fat capitals, bear the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao's duties, grasp the realm's pivot—it may be called wealth and honor's utmost, among ministers none second; the realm's blame comes from all four sides—how will you dwell in it?

entries.zh: 宜夙夜孳孳，執伊尹之強德，以守職匡上，誅惡不避親愛，舉善不避仇讎，以章至公，立信四方。
entries.en: Labor day and night in the stern virtue of Yi Yin: keep your charge, aid the throne, punish evil without sparing kin, promote good without shunning enemies—only thus can you show perfect fairness and win trust across the realm.
entries.literal: You ought morning and night be diligent, grasp Yi Yin's strong virtue, thereby to guard duty and correct the ruler, punish wickedness without shrinking from kin and loved ones, raise good without shrinking from foes and enemies, thereby to display utmost fairness, establish trust in the four directions.

entries.zh: 篤行三者，乃可以長堪重任，久享盛寵。
entries.en: Faithfully do these three, and you may long bear heavy office and long keep supreme favor.
entries.literal: Earnestly practice these three, then you can long bear heavy charge, long enjoy flourishing favor.

entries.zh: 太白出西方六十日，法當參天，今已過期，尚在桑榆之間，質弱而行遲，形小而光微。
entries.en: Venus rose in the west for sixty days—by rule it should have climbed the zenith, yet it lingers low in the sky, faint and slow, small and dim: a weakened star.
entries.literal: Grand White appeared in the west sixty days; by rule it ought to join Heaven; now it has already passed the term, still is between mulberry and elm—substance weak and motion slow, form small and light faint.

entries.zh: 熒惑角怒明大，逆行守尾。
entries.en: Mars blazes angry and bright, retrograde, lodged in the Tail constellation.
entries.literal: Mars' horns angry, bright and large; retrograde, guarding the Tail.

entries.zh: 其逆，常也；
entries.en: Retrograde motion is common enough;
entries.literal: Its retrograde motion is constant;

entries.zh: 守尾，變也。
entries.en: to halt at the Tail is the omen of crisis.
entries.literal: Guarding the Tail is change.

entries.zh: 意豈將軍忘湛漸之義，委曲從順，所執不強，不廣用士，尚有好惡之忌，蕩蕩之德未純，方與將相大臣乖離之萌也？
entries.en: Does it mean you have forgotten how power seeps like water—yielding everywhere, holding your course weakly, failing to employ men broadly, still nursing likes and dislikes—so that your broad virtue is not pure and the first rift opens between you and the great ministers of state?
entries.literal: Could it be the general has forgotten steep soaking's meaning, bends and yields compliance, what is grasped is not strong, does not broadly employ gentlemen, still has love-hate's taboos, vast vast virtue not pure—just with generals and ministers great ministers the sprout of estrangement?

entries.zh: 何故始襲司馬之號，俄而金火並有此變？
entries.en: Why, the moment you took the title of marshal, should Venus and Mars together show such a change?
entries.literal: Why reason: you first inherited marshal's title, and suddenly metal and fire together had this change?

entries.zh: 上天至明，不虛見異，唯將軍畏之慎之，深思其故，改求其路，以享天意。」
entries.en: High Heaven does not warn without cause. Dread these signs, search your heart, mend your course, and answer Heaven's will."
entries.literal: High Heaven is utmost clear; it does not vainly show prodigies—only, general, fear them and be careful, deeply ponder their cause, change and seek their road, thereby to enjoy Heaven's intent."

entries.zh: 音猶不平，薦永為護菀使者。
entries.en: Yin, still resentful, had Yong appointed commissioner of the imperial hunting park.
entries.literal: Yin still was not appeased; he recommended Yong as commissioner for the imperial park.

entries.zh: 杜鄴字子夏，本魏郡繁陽人也。
entries.en: Du Ye, styled Zixia, was originally from Fanyang in Wei commandery.
entries.literal: Du Ye, courtesy name Zixia, by origin was a man of Fanyang in Wei commandery.

entries.zh: 祖父及父積功勞皆至郡守，武帝時徙茂陵。
entries.en: His grandfather and father rose on merit to grand warden and were moved to Maoling under Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: Grandfather and father by accumulated merit both reached grand warden; in Emperor Wu's time they moved to Maoling.

entries.zh: 鄴少孤，其母張敞女。
entries.en: Ye lost his father young; his mother was a daughter of Zhang Chang.
entries.literal: Ye in youth was orphaned; his mother was Zhang Chang's daughter.

entries.zh: 鄴。
entries.en: Du Ye.
entries.literal: Du Ye.

entries.zh: 鄴壯，從敞子吉學問，得其家書。
entries.en: As a grown man he studied under Zhang Ji and inherited the Zhang family library.
entries.literal: When Ye grew strong, he followed Chang's son Ji in study and inquiry, obtaining that family's books.

entries.zh: 以孝廉為郎。
entries.en: Filial-incorrupt nomination made him a gentleman-attendant.
entries.literal: By filial and incorrupt nomination he became a gentleman-attendant.

entries.zh: 卞和獻寶，刖足願之。
entries.en: Bian He offered the jade though it cost him his feet;
entries.literal: Bian He presented the jewel, cut feet yet wished it.

entries.zh: 臣幸得奉直言之詔，無二者之危，敢不極陳！
entries.en: I am summoned to speak plainly without facing their fate—how can I hold back?
entries.literal: Your servant is fortunate to receive the edict for straight speech, without the two dangers—how dare I not exhaust statement!

entries.zh: 臣聞陽尊陰卑，卑者隨尊，尊者兼卑，天之道也。
entries.en: Yang is high and yin low; the low follows the high—that is Heaven's Way.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard yang is honored, yin is low; the low follows the honored, the honored embraces the low—it is Heaven's Way.

entries.zh: 是以男雖賤，各為其家陽；
entries.en: Thus the man, though humble, is the yang of his house;
entries.literal: Therefore though the male is low, each is yang for his household;

entries.zh: 女雖貴，猶為其國陰。
entries.en: the woman, though exalted, remains the yin of the state.
entries.literal: Though the female is high, still she is yin for her state.

entries.zh: 故禮明三從之義，雖有文母之德，必繫於子。
entries.en: Rite therefore binds even a woman of Tai Si's virtue to her son's line.
entries.literal: Therefore ritual clarifies the three followings' meaning; though she have Mother Wen's virtue, she must be tied to the son.

entries.zh: 《春秋》不書紀侯之母，陰義殺也。
entries.en: The "Spring and Autumn" omits the mother of the marquis of Ji because a woman's power must not eclipse the yin role.
entries.literal: The "Spring and Autumn" does not record the mother of the Marquis of Ji—the feminine principle demands restraint.

entries.zh: 昔鄭伯隨姜氏之欲，終有叔段篡國之禍；
entries.en: Duke Zhuang of Zheng indulged his mother and reaped Shu Duan's revolt;
entries.literal: Anciently Duke Zhuang of Zheng followed Lady Jiang's desires, and in the end had the disaster of Shu Duan usurping the state;

entries.zh: 周襄王內迫惠後之難，而遭居鄭之危。
entries.en: King Xiang of Zhou, squeezed by palace strife, fell into danger as a guest of Zheng.
entries.literal: King Xiang of Zhou was inwardly pressed by Empress Hui's trouble, and met the peril of dwelling with Zheng.

entries.zh: 漢興，呂太后權私親屬，又以外孫為孝惠後，是時繼嗣不明，凡事多暗，晝昏冬雷之變，不可勝載。
entries.en: When Han first rose, Empress Dowager Lü wielded power for her private relatives and also made a maternal grandson the successor to Emperor Xiaohui. At that time the line of succession was unclear and all affairs were largely dark; changes such as daytime gloom and thunder in winter were too many to record.
entries.literal: When Han rose, Empress Dowager Lu wielded power on behalf of her own relatives and moreover made a maternal grandson Emperor Xiaohui's successor. At that time the succession was unclear and affairs were largely benighted; daytime gloom, thunder in winter, and other portents were too numerous to record.

entries.zh: 竊見陛下行不偏之政，每事約儉，非禮不動，誠欲正身與天下更始也。
entries.en: I see you govern even-handedly, live frugally, and never act without ritual—you mean to reform yourself and begin anew with the realm.
entries.literal: Your servant privately sees Your Majesty practicing impartial government, in each matter restrained and frugal, not moving without ritual—you truly wish to rectify the person and with All-under-Heaven make a fresh start.

entries.zh: 然嘉瑞未應，而日食、地震，民訛言行籌，傳相驚恐。
entries.en: Yet no blessed omens answer; instead come eclipse and earthquake while the people whisper of divining rods and panic spreads.
entries.literal: Yet fine auspice has not answered, while solar eclipse and earthquake come; the people spread rumors and counting-rods divination, passing alarm one to another.

entries.zh: 案《春秋》災異，以指象為言語，故在於得一類而達之也。
entries.en: The "Spring and Autumn" reads each portent as a pointed image—one type unlocks the whole lesson.
entries.literal: Investigating the "Spring and Autumn" on disasters and prodigies, it takes pointing images as language; therefore it lies in obtaining one category and penetrating it.

entries.zh: 日食，明陽為陰所臨，《坤卦》乘《離》，《明夷》之象也。
entries.en: An eclipse means yin has veiled yang—Kun mounting Li, the "Brightness Wounded" sign.
entries.literal: Solar eclipse means bright yang is overshadowed by yin—the hexagram Kun riding Li, the image of Mingyi.

entries.zh: 《坤》以法地，為土為母，以安靜為德。
entries.en: Kun stands for earth, the mother principle, whose virtue is stillness.
entries.literal: Kun takes law from earth, is earth and mother, takes quiet stillness as virtue.

entries.zh: 震，不陰之效也。
entries.en: The earthquake shows that yin is failing to function properly.
entries.literal: The earthquake is the effect of yin failing to act as yin.

entries.zh: 占象甚明，臣敢不直言其事！
entries.en: The reading is plain—I must speak plainly!
entries.literal: The divination image is very clear—your servant dares not fail to speak straight of the affair!

entries.zh: 臣聞野雞著怪，高宗深動；
entries.en: When wild pheasants foretold the Shang restoration, Gaozong took fright;
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when wild pheasants showed prodigy, Gaozong was deeply moved;

entries.zh: 大風暴過，成王怛然。
entries.en: when the gale tore the mulberry grove, King Cheng trembled.
entries.literal: When a great wind violently passed, King Cheng was alarmed.

entries.zh: 願陛下加致精誠，思承始初，事稽諸古，以厭下心，則黎庶群生無不說喜，上帝百神收還威怒，禎祥福祿何嫌不報！
entries.en: Add utmost sincerity, think back to your first intent, test policy against the classics, and win the people's hearts—then the spirits will lay aside wrath and blessings will return without stint.
entries.literal: I wish Your Majesty would add utmost sincerity, think to inherit the beginning, examine affairs against antiquity, thereby to satisfy those below—then the black-haired multitude will none fail to rejoice; High God and the hundred spirits will gather back awesome anger—how would auspicious blessing grudge not to answer!

entries.zh: 卷八十五 谷永杜鄴傳第五十五
entries.en: Volume 85, the fifty-fifth biography: Gu Yong and Du Ye.
entries.literal: Volume 85, Biography the Fifty-Fifth: Gu Yong and Du Ye.

entries.zh: 揚雄字子雲，蜀郡成都人也。
entries.en: Yang Xiong, courtesy name Ziyun, was a native of Chengdu in the Shu commandery.
entries.literal: Yang Xiong, styled Ziyun, was a man of Chengdu in Shu Commandery.

entries.zh: 其先出自有周伯僑者，以支庶初食采於晉之揚，因氏焉，不知伯僑周何別也。
entries.en: His line descended from Bo Qiao of the Zhou royal house; a younger branch first held its fief at Yang in Jin and took that place name as their surname—Bo Qiao's exact relation within the Zhou kin is no longer known.
entries.literal: His ancestor came from one Bo Qiao of the Zhou; as a collateral line he first received a food-fief at Yang in Jin, and from this took the surname; it is not known what branch of Zhou Bo Qiao was.

entries.zh: 揚在河、汾之間，周衰而揚氏或稱侯，號曰揚侯。
entries.en: Their fief lay between the Yellow and Fen rivers; as the Zhou waned the clan was ennobled as marquises of Yang.
entries.literal: Yang lay between the He and Fen; when Zhou declined, the Yang clan was sometimes titled marquis, called the Marquis of Yang.

entries.zh: 會晉六卿爭權、韓、魏、趙興而范中行、知伯弊。
entries.en: Then came the struggle of the six ministerial houses of Jin: Han, Wei, and Zhao rose to power while the houses of Fan, Zhonghang, and Zhi were destroyed.
entries.literal: It happened that Jin's six ministers struggled for power; Han, Wei, and Zhao rose while Fan, Zhonghang, and Zhi Bo were ruined.

entries.zh: 當是時，逼揚侯，揚侯逃於楚巫山，因家焉。
entries.en: Under that pressure the marquis of Yang fled to the Wu mountains of Chu and settled there.
entries.literal: At this time they pressed the Marquis of Yang; the Marquis of Yang fled to Chu Mount Wu and thereupon made his home there.

entries.zh: 楚漢之興也，揚氏溯江上，處巴江州。
entries.en: When Chu and Han contended for the empire, the Yangs moved up the Yangzi and settled in the Ba river country.
entries.literal: At the rise of Chu and Han, the Yang clan went upstream on the Yangzi and dwelt at Ba Jiangzhou.

entries.zh: 而揚季官至廬江太守。
entries.en: Yang Ji rose to be grand administrator of Lujiang.
entries.literal: And Yang Ji reached office as Grand Administrator of Lujiang.

entries.zh: 漢元鼎間避仇復溯江上，處岷山之陽曰郫，有田一廛，有宅一區，世世以農桑為業。
entries.en: During Yuanding they fled a blood feud, moved again upriver, and settled south of Mount Min at Pi—one homestead, one plot of land—where for generations they lived by farming and silk.
entries.literal: In Han's Yuanding period, fleeing feud they again went upstream on the Yangzi and dwelt south of Mount Min at Pi; they had one chan of fields and one plot of house; generation after generation they took farming and sericulture as their occupation.

entries.zh: 自季至雄，五世而傳一子，故雄亡它揚於蜀。
entries.en: From Ji to Xiong each generation had only a single male heir, so in Shu there were no other branches of the Yang clan.
entries.literal: From Ji to Xiong, for five generations they transmitted one son each; therefore Xiong had no other Yangs in Shu.

entries.zh: 於是事變物化，目駭耳回，蓋天子穆然珍台閒館璇題玉英□蜎蠖濩之中，惟夫所以澄心清魂，儲精垂思，感動天地，逆釐三神者。
entries.en: Things shifted and the senses reeled; the emperor sat withdrawn in jade-decked halls, purifying mind and soul, gathering spirit in meditation, to move Heaven and earth and draw down the favor of the Three Powers.
entries.literal: Then affairs shifted and things transformed; eyes started, ears spun— for the Son of Heaven, in solemn quiet, in terraces and lodges of jade boss and jade bloom, coiled in stillness— this was how he clarified heart and purified soul, stored essence and let thought descend, to move Heaven and earth and welcome blessing from the Three Powers.

entries.zh: 乃搜逑索耦皋、伊之徒，冠倫魁能，函甘棠之惠，挾東征之意，相與齊乎陽靈之宮。
entries.en: He gathered men worthy to stand beside Gao and Yi, the best of their generation, mindful of old kindness and eastern expeditions, and together they entered the Yang Spirit shrine.
entries.literal: Then he sought pairs matched like Gao and Yi, crowning the foremost and able, bearing the kindness of the sweet pear, carrying the mind of the eastern campaign; together they aligned themselves at the Palace of the Yang Spirit.

entries.zh: 靡薜荔而為席兮，折瓊技以為芳，吸清雲之流瑕兮，飲若木之露英，集虖禮神之囿，登乎頌祇之堂。
entries.en: They spread rushes for a seat and broke jade sprigs for incense; they drew pure mist and drank immortal dew; they entered the sacred park and the hall of praise to the earth.
entries.literal: They spread elseland for mat, broke jade branches for fragrance; they breathed the clear cloud's lingering haze, drank the dew-bright blooms of the ruo tree; they gathered in the park where rites honor the gods, mounted the hall that hymns the earth lord.

entries.zh: 建光耀之長旓兮，昭華覆之威威，攀璇璣而下視兮，行遊目乎三危，陳眾車於東坑兮，肆玉釱而下馳，漂龍淵而還九垠兮，窺地底而上回。
entries.en: Long streamers of light rose; jeweled canopies spread wide; from on high they gazed toward Sanwei; chariots massed in the eastern hollow then charged with loosened reins; they circled the sacred pool and scanned the nine regions, then swept back toward the sky.
entries.literal: They raised long banners of blazing light, spread glorious canopies august and wide; from the turning jade Sieve they looked down, let the roaming eye reach Mount Sanwei; they ranged the many chariots in the eastern pit, loosed jade curb-bands and galloped down; they drifted the Dragon Pool and circled the nine bounds, peeped to earth's floor and swept upward again.

entries.zh: 風傱□而扶轄兮，鸞鳳紛其御蕤，梁弱水之濎濴兮，躡不周之逶蛇，想西王母欣然而上壽兮，屏玉女而卻虙妃。
entries.en: Wind steadied the wheels; phoenix attendants flocked; they crossed the weak stream and trod the winding crest of Buzhou; they imagined the Queen Mother of the West offering the cup of long life— while jade girls and river goddesses were waved away.
entries.literal: Wind rushed to steady the axle; phoenixes thronged with fluttering plumes; they crossed the weak water's deep swirl, trod the winding snake-path of Mount Buzhou; they thought how Queen Mother of the West would joyfully toast long life— they screened the jade maid and sent back Lady Fu.

entries.zh: 玉女無所眺其清盧兮，虙妃曾不得施其蛾眉。
entries.en: The jade maid might not flash her bright eyes; the river goddess might not raise her painted brows.
entries.literal: The jade maid had nowhere to flash her clear glance; Lady Fu could not arch her moth brows.

entries.zh: 方攬道德之精剛兮，侔神明與之為資。
entries.en: He embraces the adamantine core of the Way; he makes the spirits his companions and support.
entries.literal: Now he embraces the firm essence of the Way and Power; he matches the bright spirits and takes them as his aides.

entries.zh: 甘泉本因秦離宮，既奢泰，而武帝復增通天、高光、迎風。
entries.en: Sweet Springs was first a Qin summer palace; already lavish, Emperor Wu added the Access to Heaven, Height of Light, and Wind-Meeting towers.
entries.literal: Sweet Springs began as a Qin detached palace; already extravagant, Emperor Wu added Access to Heaven, Height of Light, and Wind-Meeting.

entries.zh: 宮外近則洪崖、旁皇、儲胥、弩阹，遠則石關、封巒、枝鵲、露寒、棠梨、師得，遊觀屈奇瑰瑋，非木摩而不雕，牆塗而不畫，周宣所考，般庚所遷，夏卑宮室，唐、虞棌椽三等之制也。
entries.en: Nearby stood Hongya, Panhuang, and the rest; farther off Stone Pass, Seal Peak, and other lodges— marvels of touring architecture, yet meant to recall King Xuan's scrutiny, Pan Geng's migration, Xia's humble halls, and the three grades of unadorned rafters of Tang and Yu.
entries.literal: Near the palace lay Hongya, Panhuang, Chuxu, Nuqu; farther stood Stone Pass, Seal Peak, Branch Magpie, Cold Dew, Tang Pear, Shide— touring sights strange and grand, not carved where wood was not to be carved, not painted where plaster was not to be painted— such was the restraint King Xuan reviewed, such the move Pan Geng praised, such the low halls of Xia, such the unplaned rafters of three grades in Tang and Yu.

entries.zh: 且其為已久矣，非成帝所造，欲諫則非時，欲默則不能已，故遂推而隆之，乃上比於帝室紫宮，若曰此非人力之所為，黨鬼神可也。
entries.en: The complex was old, not Cheng's creation— ill-timed to attack, impossible to ignore— so Xiong praised it as rival to the celestial Purple Palace, hinting it was beyond mortal craft, almost the work of ghosts and spirits.
entries.literal: Moreover it had stood long; Emperor Cheng did not build it— to remonstrate would miss the moment, yet silence was impossible; so he extolled and magnified it, comparing it to the Purple Palace of Heaven, as if to say no human force fashioned this— one might almost call it the work of ghosts and gods.

entries.zh: 又是時趙昭儀方大幸，每上甘泉，常法從，在屬車間豹尾中。
entries.en: Lady Zhao then held the emperor's favor; each visit to Sweet Springs she rode in the regulated escort among the leopard-tail guard.
entries.literal: At that time the Honored Lady Zhao was in highest favor; whenever the sovereign went to Sweet Springs she rode in lawful train among the attendant cars in the leopard-tail file.

entries.zh: 故雄聊盛言車騎之眾，參麗之駕，非所以感動天地，逆釐三神。
entries.en: So Xiong for the moment heaped up description of chariots and paired outriders— not as means to move Heaven and earth or draw down the Three Powers.
entries.literal: Therefore Xiong for the moment piled up talk of the host of chariots and the triple-paired teams— not as a way to move Heaven and earth or win blessing from the Three Powers.

entries.zh: 又言「屏玉女，卻虙妃」，以微戒齋肅之事。
entries.en: He also quoted the lines, "Screen the jade maid; send back Lady Fu," as a subtle admonition to keep fasting and the sacrifice solemn.
entries.literal: He also said "screen the jade maid, send back Lady Fu"— a veiled hint to keep fasting and the rite solemn.

entries.zh: 賦成，奏之，天子異焉。
entries.en: When he submitted the piece the emperor was struck with wonder.
entries.literal: When the rhapsody was finished he presented it; the Son of Heaven marveled at it.

entries.zh: 其十二月羽獵，雄從。
entries.en: In the twelfth month the emperor held the great feather hunt; Xiong went along.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month came the feathered hunt; Xiong accompanied.

entries.zh: 以為昔在二帝、三王，宮館、台榭、沼池、苑囿、林麓、藪澤，財足以奉郊廟、御賓客、充庖廚而已，不奪百姓膏腴谷土桑柘之地。
entries.en: Under the ancient sage-kings parks served only the suburban sacrifices, guests, and kitchens— they never seized the people's best farmland.
entries.literal: He thought: of old the Two Thearchs and Three Kings kept palaces, terraces, pools, parks, groves, and marshes only large enough to supply suburban altars, entertain guests, and fill the kitchens— they did not seize the people's rich soil of grain and mulberry.

entries.zh: 女有餘布，男有餘粟，國家殷富，上下交足，故甘露零其庭，醴泉流其唐，鳳皇巢其樹，黃龍游其沼，麒麟臻其囿，神爵棲其林。
entries.en: Then women had extra cloth and men extra grain; the realm prospered— dew fell, springs flowed, phoenix and dragon, qilin and sacred birds appeared.
entries.literal: Women had surplus cloth, men surplus grain; the state was rich, high and low alike had enough— so sweet dew fell in the courtyards, sweet springs flowed in the walks, phoenix nested in the trees, yellow dragons swam in the pools, unicorn came to the park, sacred sparrow rested in the wood.

entries.zh: 昔者禹任益虞而上下和，草木茂；
entries.en: When Yu put Yi in charge of the wilds, harmony reigned and vegetation flourished.
entries.literal: Of old Yu employed Yi as warden of marshes and high and low were at peace; plants grew thick.

entries.zh: 成湯好田而天下用足；
entries.en: Tang of Shang loved hunting and still the realm wanted for nothing.
entries.literal: Cheng Tang loved the hunt yet the world had enough.

entries.zh: 文王囿百里，民以為尚小；
entries.en: King Wen's park measured a hundred li; the people still thought it small.
entries.literal: King Wen's park was a hundred li yet the people thought it still too small.

entries.zh: 齊宣王囿四十里，民以為大；
entries.en: King Xuan of Qi's forty-li park the people thought too large.
entries.literal: King Xuan of Qi's park was forty li and the people thought it too large.

entries.zh: 裕民之與奪民也。
entries.en: The difference is enriching the people or robbing them.
entries.literal: This is enriching the people versus stripping the people.

entries.zh: 武帝廣開上林，南至宜春、鼎胡、御宿、昆吾，旁南山而西，至長楊、五柞，北繞黃山，瀕渭而東，周袤數百里，穿昆明池象滇河，營建章、鳳闕、神明、馺娑，漸台、泰液象海水周流方丈、瀛洲、蓬萊。
entries.en: Emperor Wu stretched Shanglin from the southern lodges to the northern hills, dug Kunming to mirror the Dian pool, and raised Jianzhang and the tiered terraces to mimic the fairy isles in the sea.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu widened Shanglin south to Yichun, Dinghu, Yusu, Kunwu, along the Southern Marchmount west to Changyang and Wuzuo, north round Yellow Mountain, hugging the Wei eastward— hundreds of li in circuit; he dug Kunming Pool to mimic the Dian river; he built Jianzhang, Phoenix Gate, Spirit Brightness, Sasuo, the Gradual Terrace and Grand Liquid to mimic the sea flowing round Fangzhang, Yingzhou, and Penglai.

entries.zh: 遊觀侈靡，窮妙極麗。
entries.en: Excursions grew wasteful, wonder and splendor pushed to the extreme.
entries.literal: Touring sights were extravagant, subtlety and beauty pushed to the limit.

entries.zh: 雖頗割其三垂以贍齊民，然至羽獵、田車、戎馬、器械、儲偫、禁御所營，尚泰奢麗誇詡，非堯、舜、成湯、文王三驅之意也。
entries.en: Some outer parkland was cut back for the people, yet the hunt itself—chariots, horses, gear—still swaggered in luxury, far from the restrained three-sided chase of the sages.
entries.literal: Though he somewhat carved back the three outer belts to feed the commoners, yet down to feather hunt, war chariots, mounts, gear, stores, and palisades the work remained grand and boastful— not the meaning of Yao, Shun, Cheng Tang, and King Wen's three-sided hunt.

entries.zh: 又恐後世復修前好，不折中以泉台，故聊因《校獵賦》以風，其辭曰：
entries.en: Lest posterity revive old excesses without the lesson of moderation, he framed the School Hunt Rhapsody as criticism. It begins:
entries.literal: Fearing later ages would again pursue former excess and not hold the mean shown by the terrace of springs, he therefore used the Rhapsody on the School Hunt to remonstrate; its words say:

entries.zh: 卷八十七上 揚雄傳第五十七上
entries.en: Book 87a—the fifty-seventh memoir, first part: Yang Xiong.
entries.literal: Scroll 87, part one: Biography of Yang Xiong, number fifty-seven, part one.

entries.zh: 主人曰：「昔有強秦，封豕其士，□窳其民，鑿齒之徒相與摩牙而爭之，豪俊麋沸雲擾，群黎為之不康。
entries.en: The host said: "Once there was brutal Qin, devouring its land like a boar and grinding its people down; ruffians sharpened their teeth on one another while heroes boiled up like stampeding deer in a fog, and the common folk knew no rest.
entries.literal: The host said: "In olden times there was mighty Qin, a great boar over its soil, [missing] over its people; fellows like Chisel-Teeth together ground their fangs and struggled for it; heroes seethed like elk and swarmed like clouds, and the black-haired people were thereby unpeaceful.

entries.zh: 於是上帝眷顧高祖，高祖奉命，順斗極，運天關，橫巨海，票崑崙，提劍而叱之，所麾城摲邑，下將降旗，一日之戰，不可殫記。
entries.en: Then Heaven turned to Gaozu. He took the mandate, aligned himself with the pole star, burst the passes of the sky, crossed wide seas, swept past Kunlun, and swept his sword before him; cities fell at a wave of his standard, captains struck their colors, and the clashes of a single day are beyond counting.
entries.literal: Thereupon High God looked kindly on Gaozu; Gaozu received the mandate, followed the Dipper’s pivot, moved the heaven-gate, crossed the vast sea, brushed past Kunlun, raised his sword and shouted at it; wherever his banner pointed cities were torn down and towns pulled down, generals lowered flags—the battles of a single day cannot be fully recorded.

entries.zh: 當此之勤，頭蓬不暇疏，饑不及餐，□鍪生蟣虱，介冑被沾汗，以為萬姓請命乎皇天。
entries.en: In that labor there was no time to comb matted hair or finish a meal; lice crawled under the casques, mail ran with sweat—all to plead the lives of the people before High Heaven.
entries.literal: In this toil, hair on the head had no leisure to be combed, hunger did not reach to eating; [missing] helmets bred lice and fleas, armor and helmet were soaked with sweat, in order to beg life for the myriad surnames from August Heaven.

entries.zh: 乃展民之所詘，振民之所乏，規億載，恢帝業，七年之間而天下密如也。
entries.en: He eased what had squeezed the people, supplied what they lacked, laid plans for ages to come, and widened the imperial foundations until, inside seven years, the empire stood firm and still.
entries.literal: Then he unfolded what the people were cramped in, revived what the people lacked, planned for myriad ages, expanded the imperial enterprise; within seven years the realm was dense-like in order.

entries.zh: 其後熏鬻作虐，東夷橫畔，羌戎睚眥，閩越相亂，遐萌為之不安，中國蒙被其難。
entries.en: Later the Xiongnu turned savage, eastern tribes rose in arms, Qiang and Rong glared across the passes, Min and Yue tore at one another, the frontiers trembled, and the heartland reeled under the blow.
entries.literal: After that the Xiongnu acted cruelly, the eastern Yi rebelled across, the Qiang and Rong glared with hatred, Min and Yue threw each other into chaos; distant sprouts were thereby unpeaceful, and the central states bore its hardships.

entries.zh: 於是聖武勃怒，□整其旅，乃命票、衛，汾□沸渭，雲合電發，飆騰波流，機駭蜂軼，疾如奔星，擊如震霆，砰轒□，破穹廬，腦沙幕，髓余吾。
entries.en: Then Emperor Wu’s wrath flared: he dressed the ranks, sent Huo Qubing and Wei Qing ahead, and the Fen and Wei valleys seethed like a cauldron. The army massed like storm clouds, struck like lightning, surged like wind on water, swifter than meteors, louder than thunder—wagons rolled, yurts shattered, the desert ran with blood down to the Yuyu River.
entries.literal: Thereupon Sage Martial raged in wrath, [missing] arrayed his hosts, then ordered Huo Qubing and Wei Qing; Fen [missing] boiled along the Wei, clouds gathered and lightning shot forth, whirlwinds rose and waves flowed, engines startled, bees surged, swift as shooting stars, striking like thunderclaps, rumbling [missing], smashing domed tents, shattering heads on the sand curtains, marrow at Yuyu.

entries.zh: 遂獵乎王廷。
entries.en: They carried the hunt into the barbarian king’s own hall.
entries.literal: Then they hunted in the royal court.

entries.zh: 驅橐它，燒□蠡，分梨單于，磔裂屬國，夷坑谷，拔鹵莽，刊山石，蹂屍輿廝，係累老弱，兗鋋瘢耆、金鏃淫夷者數十萬人，皆稽顙樹頷，扶服蛾伏，二十餘年矣，尚不敢惕息。
entries.en: Camels were driven before the host, signal fires blazed on beacon towers, the Chanyu’s power was broken, client tribes ripped apart, gullies filled, salt pans cleared, cliffs carved with records of victory, the dead ground underfoot, old men and boys roped in lines—hundreds of thousands scarred by blades and bolts groveled brow to dust and dared not catch their breath for twenty years.
entries.literal: They drove camels, burned [missing] gourds, split the Chanyu, tore apart dependent states, leveled pits and valleys, uprooted brine thickets, cut inscriptions on mountains, trampled corpses and grooms, bound old and weak; several hundred thousand with wounds from halberds and spears, scars from elders, metal arrowheads and slaughtered foreigners, all knocked foreheads and planted chins, crawling prone like moths; for more than twenty years they still did not dare draw frightened breath.

entries.zh: 夫天兵四臨，幽都先加，回戈邪指，南越相夷，靡節西征，羌僰東馳。
entries.en: Imperial troops closed in from every quarter: the northern heartland fell first, then spears swung south to crush Yue, banners streamed west while Qiang and Bo tribes were chased eastward.
entries.literal: As for heaven’s hosts pressing on four sides, Youdu was first struck; turning spears awry they pointed, Southern Yue was leveled together; without tally they marched west, Qiang and Bo raced east.

entries.zh: 是以遐方疏俗殊鄰絕黨之域，自上仁所不化，茂德所不綏，莫不蹺足抗手，請獻厥珍，使海內淡然，永亡邊城之災，金革之患。
entries.en: Even the farthest corners—lands once beyond the reach of kindness or awe—stood on tiptoe, hands lifted, offering tribute of their own accord, so that the realm grew quiet and the border knew neither siege nor the clash of arms.
entries.literal: Therefore in regions of distant quarters, sparse customs, strange neighbors, and cut-off cliques—those which supreme benevolence had not transformed, luxuriant virtue had not soothed—none did not stand on tiptoe and raise hands, requesting to present their treasures, causing within the seas to be tranquil, forever without border-city disasters or metal-and-leather troubles.

entries.zh: 雄以為賦者，將以風之也，必推類而言，極麗靡之辭，閎侈巨衍，競於使人不能加也，既乃歸之於正，然覽者已過矣。
entries.en: Yang Xiong held that fu verse was meant to remonstrate, yet it piles analogy upon analogy, heaps the richest diction, swells to grandiose excess until nothing more can be added, and only then veers toward moral correction—by which time the reader has long since been swept past the point.
entries.literal: Xiong thought that rhapsodies, intending to admonish by them, must extend categories in speaking, exhaust gorgeous and extravagant phrasing, vast and huge and overflowing, competing to the point that others cannot add more; only afterward do they return them to rectitude—yet those who view have already passed by.

entries.zh: 往時武帝好神仙，相如上《大人賦》，欲以風，帝反縹縹有陵雲之志。
entries.en: When Emperor Wu doted on immortals, Sima Xiangru offered his "Rhapsody of the Great Man" as a cautionary mirror—only to leave the sovereign drifting, more eager than ever to ride the wind above the clouds.
entries.literal: In former times Emperor Wu loved transcendents; Xiangru presented the 《Lord Great Man Rhapsody》, intending to admonish by it, but the emperor on the contrary floated lightly with a mind to mount the clouds.

entries.zh: 由是言之，賦勸而不止，明矣。
entries.en: From this it is plain: fu may counsel, but it rarely restrains.
entries.literal: From this speaking, rhapsody admonishes yet does not restrain—it is clear.

entries.zh: 又頗似俳優淳于髡、優孟之徒，非法度所存，賢人君子詩賦之正也，於是輟不復為。
entries.en: It smacked too much of court buffoons like Chunyu Kun or You Meng—far from the norm for poetry and fu that gentlemen should keep—so he gave the genre up.
entries.literal: Moreover it rather resembles jesters like Chunyu Kun and You Meng’s sort—not what statutes preserve, not the correctness of poetry and rhapsody for worthy men and gentlemen; thereupon he ceased and did not again compose.

entries.zh: 而大潭思渾天，參摹而四分之，極於八十一。
entries.en: He turned instead to the armillary cosmos, modeled it in threes and fours, and carried the numerology to eighty-one.
entries.literal: Then broadly he pondered the armillary heaven, thrice modeled and quartered it, reaching the limit at eighty-one.

entries.zh: 旁則三摹九據，極之七百二十九贊，亦自然之道也。
entries.en: From that base—three tiers, nine divisions—it runs out to seven hundred twenty-nine "appraisals," following nature’s own arithmetic.
entries.literal: At the side then thrice model, nine bases, reaching the limit at seven hundred twenty-nine appraisals—it is also the way of what is natural.

entries.zh: 故觀《易》者，見其卦而名之；
entries.en: Readers of the 《Changes》 read a hexagram and know its name.
entries.literal: Therefore those who view the 《Changes》 see its hexagrams and name them;

entries.zh: 觀《玄》者，數其畫而定之。
entries.en: Readers of the 《Great Mystery》 count its strokes and fix its sense.
entries.literal: those who view the 《Mystery》 count its lines and fix it.

entries.zh: 《玄》首四重者，非卦也，數也。
entries.en: The fourfold heads of the 《Mystery》 are numerology, not hexagrams in the 《Changes》 sense.
entries.literal: The 《Mystery》 heads’ fourfold layering: they are not hexagrams, they are numbers.

entries.zh: 其用自天元推一晝一夜陰陽數度律歷之紀，九九大運，與天終始。
entries.en: From the celestial pivot it reckons the round of day and night, yin and yang, pitch and calendar, the great nine-times-nine cycle that begins and ends with heaven itself.
entries.literal: Its application from heaven’s origin pushes one day and one night’s yin-yang numbers, measures the threads of pitch-pipes and calendars, the nine-nines great cycle, ending and beginning with heaven.

entries.zh: 故《玄》三方、九州、二十七部、八十一家、二百四十三表、七百二十九贊，分為三卷，曰一二三，與《泰初歷》相慶，亦有顓頊之歷焉。
entries.en: So the work maps three realms, nine domains, twenty-seven parts, eighty-one lineages, two hundred forty-three charts, and seven hundred twenty-nine appraisals in three books titled One, Two, Three—harmonizing with the 《Grand Inception》 calendar and echoing Zhuanxu’s old reckoning.
entries.literal: Therefore the 《Mystery》’s three directions, nine provinces, twenty-seven departments, eighty-one houses, two hundred forty-three tables, seven hundred twenty-nine appraisals, divided into three fascicles, called one-two-three, mutually celebrate with the 《Grand Inception Calendar》, and there is also Zhuanxu’s calendar therein.

entries.zh: 手筮之以三策，關之以休咎，絣之以象類，播之以人事，文之以五行，擬之以道德仁義禮知。
entries.en: One divines with three stalks, reads good or ill, ties image to category, sifts human affairs, weaves in the five phases, and frames everything with virtue, the Way, benevolence, right, ritual, and wisdom.
entries.literal: By hand divining them with three tallies, linking them with blessing and ill, binding them with image-categories, sowing them with human affairs, patterning them with the five phases, modeling them with virtue, way, benevolence, righteousness, rites, and wisdom.

entries.zh: 無主無名，要合《五經》，苟非其事，文不虛生。
entries.en: It claims no arbitrary master: at every turn it aligns with the 《Five Classics》, and no passage appears without a real referent.
entries.literal: Without lord, without name, summarily joining the 《Five Classics》; if it is not their affair, the text is not vainly born.

entries.zh: 為其泰曼漶而不可知，故有《首》、《沖》、《錯》、《測》、《摛》、《瑩》、《數》、《文》、《□》、《圖》、《告》十一篇，皆以解剝《玄》體，離散其文，章句尚不存焉。
entries.en: Because the core text is so vast and hard to parse, he added eleven expository books—from 《Head》 through 《Announcement》—to dissect the 《Mystery》 and spread its meaning; even line glosses were still lacking.
entries.literal: Because it was too diffuse and vast and unknowable, therefore there are the eleven pieces 《Head》, 《Rush》, 《Crossing》, 《Measuring》, 《Unfolding》, 《Gleaming》, 《Number》, 《Pattern》, 《Bound》, 《Chart》, 《Announcement》, all in order to peel apart the 《Mystery》’s body, scatter its text—even chapter-and-phrase glosses are not yet preserved therein.

entries.zh: 《玄》文多，故不著，觀之者難知，學之者難成。
entries.en: The main text is too bulky to print in full here: readers struggle to grasp it, students struggle to master it.
entries.literal: The 《Mystery》’s text is much, therefore it is not set down; those who view it find it hard to know, those who study it find it hard to complete.

entries.zh: 客有難《玄》大深，眾人之不好也，雄解之，號曰《解難》。
entries.en: When a visitor attacked the 《Mystery》 for its obscurity and unpopularity, Yang Xiong answered him in a piece titled 《Dispelling Difficulty》.
entries.literal: There was a guest who faulted the 《Mystery》 as too deep, the multitude’s not liking it; Xiong explained it, calling it 《Dispelling Difficulty》.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The piece begins:
entries.literal: Its words say:

entries.zh: 今朝廷純仁，遵道顯義，並包書林，聖風雲靡；
entries.en: Today the court is steeped in kindness, the Way is honored and right principle shown abroad, the classics are gathered like a forest, and the sovereign’s transforming influence drifts everywhere on the wind.
entries.literal: Now the court is purely benevolent, follows the Way and displays righteousness, embraces together the forest of writings, and sagely wind clouds spread and vanish;

entries.zh: 英華沉浮，洋溢八區，普天所覆，莫不沾濡；
entries.en: Fine talent rises and falls like surf, spilling across the eight directions until nothing under heaven lies outside its soak.
entries.literal: Essence and flower sink and float, overflow and fill the eight regions; wherever heaven’s cover reaches, none is not moistened;

entries.zh: 士有不談王道者則樵夫笑之。
entries.en: Any scholar who refuses to talk the language of the true king’s government is mocked even by charcoal burners.
entries.literal: If among gentlemen there is one who does not discourse on the kingly way, then woodcutters laugh at him.

entries.zh: 故意者以為事罔隆而不殺，物靡盛而不虧，故平不肆險，安不忘危。
entries.en: The design is this: power may swell yet must be checked, plenty may peak yet cannot stay whole—so in calm times one does not court recklessness, and in ease one keeps danger in mind.
entries.literal: Therefore those who set the policy think that affairs do not rise high without being reduced and things do not flourish without loss; hence in peace one does not recklessly venture into danger, in security one does not forget peril.

entries.zh: 乃時以有年出兵，整輿竦戎，振師五莋，習馬長楊，簡力狡獸，校武票禽。
entries.en: So, when harvests allow, the host moves out: chariots aligned, troops stiffened, maneuvers held at Wuzuo, horses schooled at Changyang, sturdy game chosen for the chase, and archers matched against swift quarry.
entries.literal: Then at times in a good year he sends out troops, arrays chariots and rouses weapons, shakes the army at Wuzuo, exercises horses at Changyang, selects strength among crafty beasts, compares martial prowess in swift-catching birds.

entries.zh: 乃萃然登南山，瞰烏弋，西厭月，東震日域。
entries.en: They mass to climb the southern range, gaze down on Wuyi in the west, and send their renown from the moon’s verge to the sun’s eastern rim.
entries.literal: Then gathering they ascend the Southern Mountains, look down on Wuyi, in the west press the moon, in the east shake the sun’s domain.

entries.zh: 又恐後世迷於一時之事，常以此取國家之大務，淫荒田獵，陵夷而不御也，是以車不安軔，日未靡旃，從者彷彿，□屬而還；
entries.en: Yet he dreads lest posterity mistake a seasonal show of force for the true business of state, slide into endless sport, and lose the rein—so the train wheels homeward while axles still tremble, banners scarcely lowered, escorts only half visible in the dust.
entries.literal: Moreover he fears later generations will be deluded by affairs of a single moment, constantly taking this as the great task of the state, dissolute and wasteful in field hunting, declining and not controlled; therefore the chariot does not secure the crossbar, the sun has not yet set the pennants, followers seem dim, [missing] connected and return;

entries.zh: 亦所以奉太宗之烈，遵文、武之度，復三王之田，反五帝之虞；
entries.en: It is also how he honors Taizong’s martial legacy, holds to the models of Wen and Wu, revives the royal hunts of the Three Kings, and walks again in the royal parks of the Five Sovereigns.
entries.literal: It is also thereby to serve the fierce merit of Grand Ancestor, follow the measures of Wen and Wu, restore the fields of the Three Kings, return to the parks of the Five Emperors;

entries.zh: 使農不輟□，工不下機，婚姻以時，男女莫違；
entries.en: Farmers are not pulled from the plow, weavers not dragged from the loom, weddings keep their proper season, and men and women are not torn apart against custom.
entries.literal: Causing farmers not to cease [missing], artisans not to leave the loom, marriage according to season, men and women without violation;

entries.zh: 出愷弟，行簡易，矜劬勞，休力役；
entries.en: He shows kindness and easy government, pities the weary, and gives the people respite from forced labor.
entries.literal: Issuing kindness and brotherliness, practicing simplicity and ease, pitying toil and labor, resting corvée labor;

entries.zh: 見百年，存孤弱，帥與之，同苦樂。
entries.en: He seeks out the very old, shelters widows and orphans, and shares their hardship and ease as their leader.
entries.literal: Seeing the hundred-year-olds, preserving orphans and weak, leading together with them, sharing bitterness and joy.

entries.zh: 然後陳鐘鼓之樂，鳴□磬之和，建碣□之□，拮隔鳴球，掉八列之舞；
entries.en: Only then come bells and drums in concert, chimes answering one another, stone drums and jade clappers sounding, the eight rows of dancers wheeling through the courtyard.
entries.literal: Then they array the music of bells and drums, sound the harmony of [missing] chime-stones, raise stone-tablet [missing] [missing], strike and block sounding jades, brandish the dance of eight rows;

entries.zh: 酌允鑠，餚樂胥，聽廟中之雍雍，受神人之福祜；
entries.en: Cups brim with fine ale, dishes delight the guests, the ancestral hall fills with measured resonance, and sovereign and people alike receive heaven’s favor.
entries.literal: They pour the bright ale, lay out the joyous meats, listen to the harmonious harmony within the temple, receive the blessing of spirits and men;

entries.zh: 歌投頌，吹合雅。
entries.en: Hymns rise with the songs, and panpipes keep time with the canonical airs.
entries.literal: Songs cast hymns, winds match the Ya.

entries.zh: 其勤苦此，故真神之所勞也。
entries.en: Such effort is precisely what wins the gods to your side.
entries.literal: Its toil and bitterness are thus; therefore it is what the true spirits labor at.

entries.zh: 方將俟元符，以禪梁甫之基，增泰山之高，延光於將來，比榮乎往號，豈徒欲淫覽浮觀，馳聘粳稻之地，周流梨栗之林，蹂踐芻蕘，誇詡眾庶，盛□之收，多麋鹿之獲哉！
entries.en: He waits for the great portent that will let him ascend Mount Tai and add another stone to Liangfu, stretching his fame toward the future to rival ancient sovereigns—not to idle through paddies and orchards, trample the commoners’ fodder, dazzle the mob with heaps of game, or pile up empty trophies.
entries.literal: He is about to await the great tally, in order to yield-altar on Liangfu’s foundation, increase Mount Tai’s height, extend radiance into the future, compare glory with past titles—how could he merely desire dissolute viewing and floating gazing, galloping through glutinous-rice fields, circling pear and chestnut forests, trampling grass and firewood, boasting to the multitude, abundant [missing] harvests, many elk and deer captures!

entries.zh: 且盲不見咫尺，而離婁燭千里之隅；
entries.en: The blind stumble an inch from their faces, yet Lilou could light up a cranny a thousand leagues off.
entries.literal: Moreover the blind do not see within a foot, while Lilou illuminates a corner a thousand li away;

entries.zh: 客徒愛胡人之獲我禽獸，曾不知我亦已獲其王侯。」
entries.en: You fret that the nomads took a few of our beasts, and never notice that we have already taken their kings and chiefs captive."
entries.literal: The guest merely loves that the Hu men capture our birds and beasts, and never knows that we have also captured their kings and marquises."

entries.zh: 今大漢左東海，右渠搜，前番禺，後陶塗。
entries.en: Great Han today: the Eastern Sea on the left, the desert of Qusou on the right, Panyu to the south, the northern marches to the rear.
entries.literal: Now great Han: on the left the Eastern Sea, on the right Qusou, in front Panyu, behind Taotu.

entries.zh: 東南一尉，西北一候。
entries.en: A single commandant holds the southeast, a lone scout watches the northwest.
entries.literal: In the southeast one commandant, in the northwest one scout.

entries.zh: 徽以糾墨，制以質鐵，散以禮樂，風以《詩》、《書》，曠以歲月，結以倚廬。
entries.en: The law’s black cord runs everywhere, iron discipline binds the realm, yet rites and music soften the grip, the Odes and Documents shape manners, time itself is the tether, and mourning huts remind all of human debt.
entries.literal: Bound with twisted ink, regulated with iron bonds, loosened with rites and music, winded with the "Odes" and "Documents," extended with months and years, tied with leaning huts.

entries.zh: 天下之士，雷動雲合，魚鱗雜襲，鹹營於八區，家家自以為稷、契，人人自以為咎繇，戴縰垂纓而談者皆擬於阿衡，五尺童子羞比晏嬰與夷吾，當塗者入青雲，失路者委溝渠，旦握權則為卿相，夕失勢則為匹夫；
entries.en: Scholars swarm like thunderheads—layer on layer they crowd the eight circuits, every house fancying itself the line of Ji and Xie, every man a second Gao Yao; anyone in cap and ribbons plays at being Yi Yin, and boys barely five feet tall scorn to mention Yan Ying or Guan Zhong. Catch favor and you ride the clouds; miss your footing and you lie in the gutter—minister at dawn, nobody at dusk.
entries.literal: The gentlemen of the realm, thunder-moved and cloud-gathered, fish-scale layered in assault, all encamp in the eight regions; every household thinks itself Ji and Xie, every person thinks himself Gao Yao; those who wear head-wrap and trailing tassel in discourse all compare themselves to Yi Yin; five-foot boys are ashamed to compare with Yan Ying and Yiwu; those on the road enter blue clouds, those who lose the way are cast in ditches; at dawn grasping power they become ministers and chancellors, at dusk losing power they become common men;

entries.zh: 譬若江湖之雀，勃解之鳥，乘雁集不為之多，雙鳧飛不為之少。
entries.en: They are like marsh sparrows: a thousand wild geese settling does not make the flock seem large, two ducks rising does not make it seem small.
entries.literal: It is like sparrows on rivers and lakes, birds of Bojie; a flock of wild geese alighting does not make them many, a pair of ducks flying does not make them few.

entries.zh: 昔三仁去而殷虛，二老歸而周熾，子胥死而吳亡，種、蠡存而粵伯，五□入而秦喜，樂毅出而燕懼，范睢以折□而危穰侯，蔡澤雖噤吟而笑唐舉。
entries.en: The Three Worthies left and Shang collapsed; the Two Elders came home and Zhou flourished; Wu died with Wu Zixu; Yue rose while Zhong and Fan Li lived; five captives entered Xianyang to Qin’s delight; Yue Yi’s exile struck terror into Yan; Fan Ju’s stratagem toppled the Marquis of Rang; Cai Ze, stammering all the while, still got the laugh on the physiognomist Tang Ju.
entries.literal: Formerly when the Three Worthies left, Yin was hollow; when the Two Elders returned, Zhou blazed; when Zixu died, Wu perished; when Zhong and Li survived, Yue became hegemon; when five [missing] entered, Qin rejoiced; when Yue Yi departed, Yan feared; Fan Ju by breaking [missing] endangered the Marquis of Rang; though Cai Ze stammered and groaned, he laughed at Tang Ju.

entries.zh: 故當其有事也，非蕭、曹、子房、平、勃、樊、霍則不能安；
entries.en: When trouble came, only Xiao He, Cao Shen, Zhang Liang, Chen Ping, Zhou Bo, Fan Kuai, and Huo Guang could set it right.
entries.literal: Therefore when there was affair in it, without Xiao, Cao, Zifang, Ping, Bo, Fan, and Huo it could not be settled;

entries.zh: 當其亡事也，章句之徒相與坐而守之，亦亡所患。
entries.en: In quiet times pedants could sit in a circle reciting glosses and the empire never noticed their absence.
entries.literal: When there was no affair in it, chapter-and-phrase fellows together sat and guarded it, and also there was nothing to worry about.

entries.zh: 故世亂，則聖哲馳騖而不足；
entries.en: In chaos even sages race until they drop and still cannot save the day.
entries.literal: Therefore when the age is chaotic, then sages and wise men gallop in haste and it is not enough;

entries.zh: 世治，則庸夫高枕而有余。
entries.en: When the age is ordered, the dullest soul can pillow high and feel he has done enough.
entries.literal: When the age is ordered, then ordinary men high-pillow and have surplus.

entries.zh: 揚子曰：「范雎，魏之亡命也，折脅拉髂，免於微索，翕肩蹈背，扶服入橐，激卬萬乘之主，界涇陽抵穰侯而代之，當也。
entries.en: Yang Xiong replied: "Fan Ju fled Wei with a broken body, dodged the searchers, crept into a sack to reach Qin, roused the king of ten thousand chariots, blocked Lord Jingyang, and unseated the Marquis of Rang—that was exactly the right moment for such a man.
entries.literal: Master Yang said: "Fan Ju was Wei’s fugitive; ribs broken and hip wrenched, he escaped fine cords; shrugging shoulder and treading back, crawling prone he entered the sack; he stirred and raised the lord of ten thousand chariots, stopped Jingyang and pressed the Marquis of Rang and replaced him—it was fitting.

entries.zh: 蔡澤，山東之匹夫也，顉頤折頞，涕唾流沫，西揖強秦之相，扼其咽，炕其氣，附其背而奪其位，時也。
entries.en: Cai Ze was a rough man from the eastern hills—stooped, scarred, slobbering—yet he crossed to Qin, bowed to the chief minister, seized him by the throat, leaned on his back, and took his chair because the hour called for it.
entries.literal: Cai Ze was a common fellow from east of the mountains; chin drawn and nose broken, tears and spittle flowing in foam, westward he bowed to the strong Qin minister, choked his throat, checked his breath, clung to his back and seized his position—it was the moment.

entries.zh: 天下已定，金革已平，都於雒陽，婁敬委輅脫挽，掉三寸之舌，建不拔之策，舉中國徙之長安，適也。
entries.en: When the wars were over and the court sat at Luoyang, Lou Jing dropped his harness, used nothing but eloquence, and persuaded the throne to move the seat of empire to Chang’an—that was the fitting move for that age.
entries.literal: When the realm was already settled, metal and leather already pacified, with capital at Luoyang, Lou Jing cast aside axle-bar and slipped traces, brandished a three-inch tongue, set up an unshakeable plan, lifted the central states and moved them to Chang’an—it was appropriate.

entries.zh: 五帝垂典，三王傳禮，百世不易，叔孫通起於枹鼓之間，解甲投戈，遂作君臣之儀，得也。
entries.en: The Five Sovereigns left models, the Three Kings handed down ritual—unchanged for ages—yet Shusun Tong stepped from the drum corps, laid down arms, and drafted the court ceremony for the new dynasty; that was what the times required.
entries.literal: The Five Emperors hung down canons, the Three Kings handed on rites, a hundred generations unchanged; Shusun Tong rose from between drum and drumstick, doffed armor and cast aside spear, then made the rites of lord and minister—it was obtaining.

entries.zh: 《甫刑》靡敝，秦法酷烈，聖漢權制，而蕭何造律，宜也。
entries.en: The old "Fu punishments" had decayed, Qin’s code was savage; sagely Han needed a measured code, and Xiao He framed the statutes—that was appropriate.
entries.literal: The 'Punishments of Fu’ was worn out, Qin law was cruel and fierce; sagely Han weighed measures, and Xiao He made statutes—it was fitting.

entries.zh: 故有造蕭何律於唐、虞之世，則悖矣；
entries.en: Had someone drafted Xiao He’s Han code in the age of Yao and Shun, it would have been absurd.
entries.literal: Therefore if one made Xiao He’s statutes in the age of Tang and Yu, then it would be perverse;

entries.zh: 有作叔孫通儀於夏、殷之時，則惑矣；
entries.en: To stage Shusun Tong’s court rituals in the days of Xia or Shang would be sheer folly.
entries.literal: If there were one who performed Shusun Tong’s rites in the age of Xia and Yin, then he would be deluded;

entries.zh: 有建婁敬之策於成周之世，則繆矣；
entries.en: To press Lou Jing’s resettlement scheme on the mature Zhou would be wide of the mark.
entries.literal: if there were one who set up Lou Jing’s plan in the age of completed Zhou, then it would be erroneous;

entries.zh: 有談范、蔡之說於金、張、許、史之間，則狂矣。
entries.en: To peddle the stratagems of Fan Ju and Cai Ze in the antechambers of the Jin, Zhang, Xu, and Shi clans would be madness.
entries.literal: if there were one who discoursed on Fan and Cai’s doctrines among Jin, Zhang, Xu, and Shi, then he would be mad.

entries.zh: 夫蕭規曹隨，留侯畫策，陳平出奇，功若泰山，向若□隤，唯其人之贍知哉，亦會其時之可為也。
entries.en: Xiao He drew the blueprint, Cao Shen kept to it; Zhang Liang plotted, Chen Ping surprised—merit steady as Taishan, effect like an avalanche. Credit their genius, yes, but credit the age that let them act.
entries.literal: As for Xiao He setting the measure and Cao Shen following it, the Marquis of Liu drawing plans, Chen Ping producing the unexpected—their merit was like Mount Tai, their impact like a landslide: was it only those men’s ample wisdom? It was also that they encountered times when action was possible.

entries.zh: 故為可為於可為之時，則從；
entries.en: Do the doable when the time allows, and you ride the tide.
entries.literal: Therefore doing what can be done in a time when it can be done, then one follows;

entries.zh: 為不可為於不可為之時，則凶。
entries.en: Attempt the impossible when the moment forbids it, and ruin follows.
entries.literal: doing what cannot be done in a time when it cannot be done, then there is ill fortune.

entries.zh: 夫藺先生收功於章台，四皓采榮於南山，公孫創業於金馬，票騎發跡於祁連，司馬長卿竊訾於卓氏，東方朔割炙於細君。
entries.en: Lord Lin won his fame on the Zhangtai terrace; the Four Whiteheads took honor on Mount Shang; Gongsun Hong built a career from the Golden Horse gate; Huo Qubing made his name beyond Qilian; Sima Xiangru wangled a fortune from the Zhuos; Dongfang Shuo carved a roast for his bride.
entries.literal: As for Master Lin gathering merit at Zhangtai, the Four Hoaryheads gathering glory on the Southern Mountains, Gongsun founding enterprise at the Golden Horse, the Flying-General rising from origins at Qilian, Sima Changqing stealing bride-price from the Zhuo clan, Dongfang Shuo cutting roast meat for his wife.

entries.zh: 僕誠不能與此數公者並，故默然獨守吾《太玄》。」
entries.en: I am no match for such men; I keep silence and cling to my 《Great Mystery》."
entries.literal: I truly cannot stand together with these several gentlemen; therefore silently alone I guard my 《Great Mystery》."

entries.zh: 仲尼之後，訖於漢道，德行顏、閔、股肱蕭、曹，□及名將尊卑之條，稱述品藻。
entries.en: From Confucius down to Han times—Yan Hui and Min Ziqian for virtue, Xiao He and Cao Shen as arms of state, and the ranking of celebrated generals—each is weighed and characterized.
entries.literal: After Zhongni, down to Han’s way, conduct and virtue of Yan and Min, thigh-and-arm Xiao and Cao, down to famous generals’ high-low threads, praised and described, graded and polished.

entries.zh: 撰《淵騫》第十一。
entries.en: Book XI, 《Yuan and Qian》.
entries.literal: Composed 《Yuan and Qian》 as the eleventh.

entries.zh: 時，大司空王邑、納言嚴尤聞雄死，謂桓譚曰：「子常稱揚雄書，豈能傳於後世乎？」
entries.en: When Grand Minister of Works Wang Yi and Yan You heard of his death, they asked Huan Tan, "You always praised Yang Xiong. Will his books survive?"
entries.literal: At that time Grand Minister of Works Wang Yi and Accepting-the-Words Yan You heard of Xiong’s death and said to Huan Tan: "You always praised Yang Xiong’s writings—can they be transmitted to later generations?"

entries.zh: 譚曰：「必傳。
entries.en: Huan Tan replied, "They will endure.
entries.literal: Tan said: "They will certainly be transmitted.

entries.zh: 顧君與譚不及見也。
entries.en: Only you and I will not live to see the day.
entries.literal: Only you and Tan will not reach to see it.

entries.zh: 凡人賤近而貴遠，親見揚子雲祿位容貌不能動人，故輕其書。
entries.en: Men scorn the near and revere the distant. They saw Yang Ziyun’s modest rank and plain looks and felt no awe, so they underrate his writing.
entries.literal: As a rule men despise what is near and honor what is far; having personally seen Yang Ziyun’s stipend-rank and appearance, they could not be moved, therefore they slight his books.

entries.zh: 昔老聃著虛無之言兩篇，薄仁義，非禮學，然後世好之者尚以為過於《五經》，自漢文、景之君及司馬遷皆有是言。
entries.en: Laozi wrote two brief texts that spurned benevolence, right, and ritual learning—yet later admirers ranked them above the Five Classics. Emperors Wen and Jing of Han, and Sima Qian, said as much.
entries.literal: Formerly Laozi composed two pieces of empty-nothing talk, belittling benevolence and righteousness, rejecting rites and learning—yet later generations who loved them still thought them to surpass the 《Five Classics》; from Han’s Wendi and Jingdi rulers down to Sima Qian all had this saying.

entries.zh: 今診子之書文義至深，而論不詭於聖人，若使遭遇時君，更閱賢知，為所稱善，則必度越諸子矣。」
entries.en: Yangzi’s writing runs deeper than most, and his doctrine never strays from the sages. Given a receptive ruler and a circle of discerning scholars to praise it, it would tower above the philosophers of his age."
entries.literal: Now the Yangzi’s book’s pattern and meaning reach extreme depth, yet its discourse does not deviate from the sages—if it were to meet a timely lord, further reviewed by worthy and wise, praised as good, then it would certainly surpass the various masters."

entries.zh: 諸儒或譏以為雄非聖人而作經，猶春秋吳楚之君僭號稱王，蓋誅絕之罪也。
entries.en: Some scholars jeered that for a non-sage to compose a classic was like Wu or Chu usurping the royal title in the Spring and Autumn period—a capital offense.
entries.literal: Some of the Ru ridiculed, holding that Xiong, not being a sage, yet made classics, was like the lords of Wu and Chu in the Spring and Autumn usurping titles and calling themselves kings—probably a crime deserving execution and extinction.

entries.zh: 自雄之沒至今四十餘年，其《法言》大行，而《玄》終不顯，然篇籍具存。
entries.en: More than forty years have passed since his death: the "Exemplary Sayings" circulates widely, the "Great Mystery" never quite caught on, yet every scroll is still extant.
entries.literal: From Xiong’s death until now more than forty years; his 《Exemplary Sayings》 greatly flourishes, while the 《Mystery》 in the end does not shine forth—yet the fascicles and tablets all remain.

entries.zh: 卷八十七下 揚雄傳第五十七下
entries.en: Volume 87b: Biography of Yang Xiong, Part Two.
entries.literal: Volume 87b, Biography of Yang Xiong, Part 57b.

entries.zh: 漢興之初，反秦之敝，與民休息，凡事簡易，禁罔疏闊，而相國蕭、曹以寬厚清靜為天下帥，民作「畫一」之歌。
entries.en: In the early Han, the court reversed the abuses of Qin and let the people recover. Government was simple, prohibitions were few, and the law's net was loosely cast. Chancellors Xiao He and Cao Shen made lenience, generosity, and quiet administration the model for the realm, and the people composed the song "Uniformity."
entries.literal: At the beginning of the rise of Han, they reversed the defects of Qin, rested the people with them, in all affairs were simple and easy, prohibitions and nets were loose and broad, and Chancellors Xiao and Cao took generous kindness and clarity-quietness as models for the realm; the people composed the song "uniformity."

entries.zh: 孝惠垂拱，高后女主，不出房闥，而天下晏然，民務稼穡，衣食滋殖。
entries.en: Under Emperor Hui the court scarcely stirred; the Grand Empress Dowager Gao ruled from behind the curtain without stepping beyond the inner palace, yet the realm stayed calm. Folk bent their backs to farming, and food and clothing grew more plentiful.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaohui hung his sleeves (did nothing), Empress Gao was chief female ruler, did not go out from inner chambers, yet the realm was peaceful; the people devoted themselves to sowing and reaping, clothing and food multiplied.

entries.zh: 至於文、景，遂移風易俗。
entries.en: By the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing, customs had begun to change for the better.
entries.literal: As for Wen and Jing, thereupon they shifted customs and changed habits.

entries.zh: 是時，循吏如河南守吳公、蜀守文翁之屬，皆謹身帥先，居以廉平，不至於嚴，而民從化。
entries.en: Among them were model officials like the governor of Henan, Lord Wu, and the governor of Shu, Wen Weng: each kept his own conduct strict, led by example, governed with integrity and even-handed justice without leaning on harshness, and the people willingly came round.
entries.literal: At this time, upright officials such as Administrator of Henan Lord Wu and Administrator of Shu Wen Weng and their kind all were careful with themselves and led first, dwelt with incorruptibility and fairness, did not reach severity, and the people followed transformation.

entries.zh: 文翁，廬江舒人也。
entries.en: Wen Weng came from Shu District in Lujiang Commandery.
entries.literal: Wen Weng was a man of Shu in Lujiang.

entries.zh: 少好學，通《春秋》，以郡縣吏察舉。
entries.en: As a young man he loved books, mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals, and won recommendation from a county post.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning, penetrated the Spring and Autumn, by commandery and county clerk was investigated and raised.

entries.zh: 景帝末，為蜀郡守，仁愛好教化。
entries.en: Near the end of Emperor Jing's reign he was appointed governor of Shu, ruling with kindness and a passion for civilizing the people through education.
entries.literal: At the end of Emperor Jing's reign, he became Administrator of Shu Commandery; humane and loving, he liked transforming instruction.

entries.zh: 見蜀地辟陋有蠻夷風，文翁欲誘進之，乃選郡縣小吏開敏有材者張叔等十餘人親自飭厲，遣詣京師，受業博士，或學律令。
entries.en: Shu struck him as backward, almost frontier in manners. To lift it up he picked a dozen sharp young clerks like Zhang Shu, drilled them himself, and sent them to the capital to study under the court academicians or to train in the law codes.
entries.literal: Seeing Shu territory crude and narrow had barbarian Yi customs, Wen Weng wished to entice and advance them; then he selected commandery and county petty clerks who were open, keen, and talented—more than ten men such as Zhang Shu—personally disciplined and urged them, sent them to the capital, received instruction under erudites, or studied statutes and ordinances.

entries.zh: 減省少府用度，買刀布蜀物，繼計吏以遺博士。
entries.en: He trimmed his own privy purse, purchased Shu knives and cloth, and sent them along with the annual accounting mission as gifts for the academicians.
entries.literal: He reduced and saved Privy Treasurer expenditures, bought knives and cloth Shu goods, attached them to the accounting clerks to present to erudites.
