entries.zh: 數歲，蜀生皆成就還歸，文翁以為右職，用次察舉，官有至郡守刺史者。
entries.en: Within a few years his protégés finished their studies and came home. He placed them in senior posts, recommended them in turn for higher office, and some rose to governorships or regional inspectorates.
entries.literal: After several years, Shu students all achieved completion and returned; Wen Weng made them right-hand posts, in sequence investigated and raised them; offices went as far as grand administrators and regional inspectors.

entries.zh: 及至孝宣，由仄陋而登至尊，興於閭閻，知民事之艱難。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan had climbed from humble obscurity to the throne; he came up through ordinary neighborhoods and knew firsthand how hard life could be for common folk.
entries.literal: When it reached Emperor Xiaoxuan, from narrow lowliness he ascended to supreme honor, rose from lanes and alleys, knew the people's affairs' hardship.

entries.zh: 自霍光薨後始躬萬機，厲精為治，五日一聽事，自丞相已下各奉職而進。
entries.en: Only after Huo Guang died did he take personal charge of government. He threw himself into administration, holding court every five days, while everyone from the chancellor down brought forward their business in orderly turn.
entries.literal: From after Huo Guang's death he began personally to handle the myriad threads, sharpened essence for governance, every fifth day once heard affairs; from the Chancellor downward each attended duty and advanced.

entries.zh: 及拜刺史守相，輒親見問，觀其所由，退而考察所行以質其言，有名實不相應，必知其所以然。
entries.en: Whenever he named a regional inspector or a governor, he met the man face to face and sounded him out, then checked deeds against words once the appointee was in post. If reputation and performance failed to match, he dug until he understood why.
entries.literal: When appointing regional inspectors and guard administrators, he always personally saw and questioned them, observed whence they came, withdrew and investigated what they practiced to verify their words; if name and reality did not correspond, he necessarily knew the reason why.

entries.zh: 常稱曰：「庶民所以安其田裡而亡歎息愁恨之心者，政平訟理也。
entries.en: He often remarked: "Common people settle quietly on their land only when governance is fair and justice runs straight; then they have no cause for bitter complaint.
entries.literal: He often said: "The reason the multitude can rest secure in their fields and villages and lack sighing, sorrow, and resentful hearts is government being level and lawsuits being ordered.

entries.zh: 與我共此者，其唯良二千石乎！」
entries.en: The men who truly share that burden with me can only be worthy governors."
entries.literal: Those who with me share this—are they not none other than good two-thousand-bushel officials!"

entries.zh: 以為太守，吏民之本也。
entries.en: He treated the grand administrator as the foundation of both officials and people.
entries.literal: He regarded the grand administrator as the root of clerks and commoners.

entries.zh: 數變易則下不安，民知其將久，不可欺罔，乃服從其教化。
entries.en: Constant reshuffling unsettles the countryside; when folk see that a governor will stay long enough that he cannot be fooled, they accept his moral guidance.
entries.literal: Frequent changes then those below are not secure; when the people know he will long endure, cannot be deceived, then they submit and follow his transforming instruction.

entries.zh: 故二千石有治理效，輒以璽書勉厲，增秩賜金，或爵至關內侯，公卿缺則選諸所表以次用之。
entries.en: Governors who proved effective received sealed edicts of praise, promotions in salary, gifts of gold, sometimes even elevation to marquis within the passes. When high ministerial posts fell vacant, he drew his next choices from the names they had recommended, in due order.
entries.literal: Therefore when two-thousand-bushel officials had governance effects, then with imperial-seal documents he urged and encouraged them, increased rank and bestowed gold, or nobility reached marquis within the passes; when dukes and ministers were lacking, then from those they had commended he selected in order and employed them.

entries.zh: 是故漢世良吏，於是為盛，稱中興焉。
entries.en: Thus Han produced its richest crop of capable local officials in this age, and historians speak of it as the restoration.
entries.literal: Therefore Han-age good clerks, at this were flourishing; it was called middle revival.

entries.zh: 若趙廣漢、韓延壽、尹翁歸、嚴延年、張敞之屬，皆稱其位，然任刑罰，或抵罪誅。
entries.en: Men like Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Yan Yannian, and Zhang Chang filled their offices competently, yet built their reputations on harsh law; several ended condemned and put to death.
entries.literal: Such as Zhao Guanghan, Han Yanshou, Yin Wenggui, Yan Yannian, Zhang Chang and their kind, all matched their positions, yet relied on punishments; some met crime and execution.

entries.zh: 王成、黃霸、朱邑、龔遂、鄭弘、召信臣等，所居民富，所去見思，生有榮號，死見奉祀，此廩廩庶幾德讓君子之遺風矣。
entries.en: Wang Cheng, Huang Ba, Zhu Yi, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen, and their peers left districts wealthier than they found them and were mourned when they left. Honored in life and worshipped after death, they came closest to the old ideal of the gentleman who leads by deference and virtue.
entries.literal: Wang Cheng, Huang Ba, Zhu Yi, Gong Sui, Zheng Hong, Shao Xinchen and the like, where they dwelt the people were rich, where they departed they were seen and missed; alive they had glorious titles, dead they received sacrifice worship—this is trembling-trembling perhaps the leftover wind of virtuous yielding gentlemen.

entries.zh: 孝武之世，外攘四夷，內改法度，民用凋敝，奸軌不禁。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu the court drove back the border peoples abroad while overhauling statutes at home. Common folk were drained, and lawbreaking ran unchecked.
entries.literal: In the age of Emperor Xiaowu, outwardly he repelled the Four Yi, inwardly he altered laws and institutions; the people's use was withered and exhausted, wickedness and deviance were not restrained.

entries.zh: 時少能以化治稱者，惟江都相董仲舒、內史公孫弘、兒寬，居官可紀。
entries.en: Few officials then won renown for civilizing rule through moral example; only Jiangdu Chancellor Dong Zhongshu, Capital Superintendent Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan left careers worth remembering.
entries.literal: At the time few could be praised for transforming and governing; only Chancellor of Jiangdu Dong Zhongshu, Capital Superintendent Gongsun Hong, and Ni Kuan were worth recording in office.

entries.zh: 三人皆儒者，通於世務，明習文法，以經術潤飾吏事，天子器之。
entries.en: All three were Confucian scholars who understood practical administration, knew the statutes inside out, and dressed routine bureaucratic work in classical learning; the emperor regarded them highly.
entries.literal: The three men were all Ru scholars, penetrated worldly affairs, clearly practiced literary law, used classical learning to adorn and polish clerical affairs; the Son of Heaven esteemed them.

entries.zh: 仲舒數謝病去，弘、寬至三公。
entries.en: Dong Zhongshu repeatedly begged off on grounds of ill health and left office, while Gongsun Hong and Kuan rose all the way to the rank of one of the Three Dukes.
entries.literal: Zhongshu repeatedly requested leave on grounds of illness and departed; Hong and Kuan reached the Three Dukes.

entries.zh: 又修起學官於成都市中，招下縣子弟以為學官弟子，為除更徭，高者以補郡縣吏，次為孝弟力田。
entries.en: He founded a public school in the market at Chengdu and enrolled young men from the outlying counties as its students, exempting them from rotating labor service. The best graduates filled county and commandery posts; the next rank were commended as models of filial piety, brotherly duty, and diligent farming.
entries.literal: Further he built and raised study officials in Chengdu market city, recruited lower commandery's sons and younger brothers to be study-official disciples, for them removed rotation corvée; the high ones used to supplement commandery and county clerks, the next became filial, younger-brotherly, and force-in-fields.

entries.zh: 常選學官僮子，使在便坐受事。
entries.en: He regularly drafted student aides and had them take notes or attend to paperwork beside him in informal session.
entries.literal: He always selected study-official youths, made them in convenient seats receive affairs.

entries.zh: 每出行縣，益從學官諸生明經飭行者與俱，使傳教令，出入閨閣。
entries.en: On tours of the counties he brought along students who knew the classics and kept disciplined conduct, using them to relay his orders through courtyard after courtyard.
entries.literal: Whenever he went out traveling counties, increased following study-official various students who clarified classics and ordered conduct went together with him, made them transmit teach commands, enter and exit inner gates.

entries.zh: 縣邑吏民見而榮之，數年，爭欲為學官弟子，富人至出錢以求之。
entries.en: Local officials and townsfolk looked on with admiration. Within a few years families scrambled to place sons in the school, and wealthy households sometimes paid for the privilege.
entries.literal: County town clerks and people seeing honored them; after several years, vied wishing to be study-official disciples; the rich even produced cash seeking it.

entries.zh: 由是大化，蜀地學於京師者比齊魯焉。
entries.en: Education transformed the region until the stream of Shu scholars heading for the capital rivaled that from Qi and Lu.
entries.literal: Thereby great transformation; Shu territory studying at the capital compared with Qi and Lu.

entries.zh: 至武帝時，乃令天下郡國皆立學校官，自文翁為之始雲。
entries.en: By Emperor Wu's reign every commandery and kingdom was ordered to maintain official schools; the precedent is traced to Wen Weng.
entries.literal: When it reached Emperor Wu's time, then he ordered all-under-heaven commanderies and kingdoms all to establish study-school officials; from Wen Weng acting began it is said.

entries.zh: 黃霸字次公，淮陽陽夏人也，以豪傑役使徙雲陵。
entries.en: Huang Ba, courtesy name Cigong, was a native of Yangxia in Huaiyang Commandery; powerful local families had pressed him into forced labor, and he was banished with them to Yunling.
entries.literal: Huang Ba, styled Cigong, was a man of Yangxia in Huaiyang; because of powerful-clan corvée labor service he was relocated to Yunling.

entries.zh: 霸少學律令，喜為吏，武帝末以待詔入錢賞官，補侍郎謁者，坐同產有罪劾免。
entries.en: As a youth Huang Ba studied the legal codes and wanted a bureaucratic career. Late in Emperor Wu's reign he bought an expectancy appointment, became a palace usher, then lost the post when impeached because a full brother had committed a crime.
entries.literal: Ba in youth studied statutes and ordinances, liked being a clerk; at the end of Emperor Wu by awaiting edict paid cash for a reward appointment, supplemented Gentleman-attendant usher; because his full brother committed a crime he was impeached and dismissed.

entries.zh: 後復入谷沈黎郡，補左馮翊二百石卒史。
entries.en: He next offered grain for appointment to Shenli Commandery and became a junior clerk at two hundred bushels in the offices of the governor of Zuo Fengyi.
entries.literal: Later again he entered grain to Shenli Commandery, supplemented Zuo Fengyi two-hundred-bushel clerk.

entries.zh: 馮翊以霸入財為官，不署右職，使領郡錢谷計。
entries.en: The governor of Fengyi, noting that Huang Ba had bought his way in, refused him a senior title and put him in charge of the commandery budget ledgers instead.
entries.literal: Fengyi because Ba entered wealth for office, did not assign right posts, made him lead commandery cash and grain accounting.

entries.zh: 簿書正，以廉稱，察補河東均輸長，復察廉為河南太守丞。
entries.en: His books balanced perfectly and he won a reputation for honesty. Recommended for merit, he became chief of the equal-distribution office in Hedong, then was recommended again and promoted to assistant governor of Henan.
entries.literal: Ledger documents correct, by incorruptibility praised; investigated supplemented Hedong equal-transport chief; again investigated incorrupt made Henan grand administrator assistant.

entries.zh: 霸為人明察內敏，又習文法，然溫良有讓，足知，善御眾。
entries.en: Huang Ba combined sharp judgment with a quiet, nimble mind; he knew the statutes cold yet remained courteous and modest, wise enough to win respect and skilled at handling men.
entries.literal: Ba as a person was clear-seeing inward keen, also practiced literary law, yet warm good had yielding, sufficient wisdom, good at controlling multitudes.

entries.zh: 為丞，處議當於法，合人心，太守甚任之，吏民愛敬焉。
entries.en: As chief assistant he framed advice that matched both statute and popular feeling. His governor relied on him deeply, and officials and commoners alike admired him.
entries.literal: As assistant, disposing deliberation matched law, accorded people's hearts; grand administrator greatly trusted him; clerks and people loved and respected him.

entries.zh: 自武帝末，用法深。
entries.en: From the late years of Emperor Wu onward, justice grew pitiless.
entries.literal: From Emperor Wu's end, application of law was deep.

entries.zh: 昭帝立，幼，大將軍霍光秉政，大臣爭權，上官桀等與燕王謀作亂，光既誅之，遂遵武帝法度，以刑罰痛繩群下，由是俗吏上嚴酷以為能，而霸獨用寬和為名。
entries.en: Emperor Zhao came to the throne as a child while Huo Guang held power. Court factions clashed until Huo executed Shangguan Jie and his allies in the plot with the Prince of Yan. Thereafter the regime clung to Emperor Wu's harsh precedents, and petty bureaucrats climbed by proving how cruel they could be—except Huang Ba, who made his name with lenience.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhao was established, young; Grand General Huo Guang grasped government; great ministers vied power; Shangguan Jie and others with the Prince of Yan plotted to create rebellion; after Guang had executed them, then followed Emperor Wu's laws and institutions, with punishments painfully rope those below; hence vulgar clerks presented severity as ability, but Ba alone used generous harmony as name.

entries.zh: 王成，不知何郡人也。
entries.en: Wang Cheng's native commandery is not recorded.
entries.literal: Wang Cheng—unknown what commandery man.

entries.zh: 為膠東相，治甚有聲。
entries.en: As chancellor of Jiaodong he governed so effectively that his name traveled far.
entries.literal: He became Chancellor of Jiaodong; governance very had reputation.

entries.zh: 宣帝最先褒之，地節三年下詔曰：「蓋聞有功不賞，有罪不誅，雖唐、虞不能以化天下。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan singled him out for praise early on. In the third year of Dijie an edict declared: "They say that where merit goes unrewarded and guilt unpunished, not even the sage-kings Yao and Shun could civilize the realm.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan first praised him; in the third year of Dijie issued an edict saying: "I have heard if there is merit not rewarded, crime not punished, even Tang and Yu cannot thereby transform all-under-heaven.

entries.zh: 今膠東相成，勞來不怠，流民自佔八萬餘口，治有異等之效。
entries.en: Our chancellor of Jiaodong, Cheng, has worked tirelessly to settle wanderers: over eighty thousand migrants have filed for residence under his care. His administration stands out among his peers.
entries.literal: Now Jiaodong Chancellor Cheng, encouraging and summoning was not slack; drifting people self-registered more than eighty thousand mouths; governance had extraordinary-grade effects.

entries.zh: 其賜成爵關內侯，秩中二千石。」
entries.en: We therefore ennoble Cheng as marquis within the passes at the salary rank of two thousand bushels."
entries.literal: Let Cheng be granted noble rank marquis within the passes, salary grade central two thousand bushels."

entries.zh: 未及徵用，會病卒官。
entries.en: Before he could be summoned to higher duty he fell ill and died in post.
entries.literal: Before he could be summoned to higher employment, he fell ill and died in office.

entries.zh: 後詔使丞相、御史問郡國上計長吏守丞以政令得失，或對言前膠東相成偽自增加，以蒙顯賞，是後俗吏多為虛名雲。
entries.en: Later the emperor told the chancellor and chief clerk to quiz returning fiscal officers on what policies worked or failed. Some claimed the former Jiaodong chancellor Cheng had inflated his numbers to win honors. Thereafter petty officials chased hollow reputations—or so the story goes.
entries.literal: Later an edict ordered Chancellor and Imperial Clerk to question commanderies and kingdoms' accounting senior clerks and guard assistants as to policy commands' gain and loss; some replied speaking former Jiaodong Chancellor Cheng falsely self increased, thereby to obtain conspicuous reward; after this vulgar clerks mostly made empty names it is said.

entries.zh: 會宣帝即位，在民間時知百姓苦吏急也，聞霸持法平，召以為廷尉正，數決疑獄，庭中稱平。
entries.en: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he already knew from his years among commoners how the people suffered under overbearing officials. Hearing that Huang Ba applied the law evenhandedly, he summoned him as director of convicts; Ba repeatedly resolved doubtful cases until the whole court praised his fairness.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, having lived among common folk he knew how the people suffered under harsh clerks; hearing that Ba held the law evenly, he summoned him to be director of convicts, and Ba repeatedly settled doubtful cases until the court praised his fairness.

entries.zh: 守丞相長史，坐公卿大議廷中知長信少府夏侯勝非議詔書大不敬，霸阿從不舉劾，皆下廷尉，繫獄當死。
entries.en: While serving as chief clerk to the chancellor, he was implicated when, at a grand conference of court nobles, he learned that Xiahou Sheng, director of the Palace of Everlasting Faith, had criticized an imperial edict—a capital offense of great irreverence. Huang Ba connived and failed to impeach him; all were sent to the minister of justice, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.
entries.literal: Serving as chief clerk to the chancellor, at a grand court conference of dukes and ministers he learned that Director of the Palace of Everlasting Faith Xiahou Sheng had disparaged an imperial edict—a capital offense of great irreverence; Ba connived and did not impeach; all were handed to the minister of justice, imprisoned, and sentenced to death.

entries.zh: 霸因從勝受尚書獄中，再隃冬，積三歲乃出，語在勝傳。
entries.en: Huang Ba therefore studied the Documents in prison under Sheng. He endured two winters and three full years before release; the fuller account appears in Sheng's biography.
entries.literal: Ba therefore studied the Documents in prison under Sheng; across two winters and a full three years he remained inside before release—the fuller account is in Sheng's biography.

entries.zh: 勝出，復為諫大夫，令左馮翊宋畸舉霸賢良。
entries.en: After Sheng was released he became remonstrating grandee and had Song Ji, governor of Zuo Fengyi, recommend Huang Ba as worthy and good.
entries.literal: After Sheng's release he became remonstrating grandee and had Song Ji, governor of Zuo Fengyi, recommend Ba as worthy and good.

entries.zh: 勝又口薦霸於上，上擢霸為揚州刺史。
entries.en: Sheng also recommended Huang Ba orally to the emperor, who promoted him to inspector of Yang Province.
entries.literal: Sheng also orally recommended Ba to the sovereign; the sovereign promoted Ba to inspector of Yang Province.

entries.zh: 三歲，宣帝下詔曰：「制詔御史：其以賢良高第揚州刺史霸為潁川太守，秩比二千石，居官賜車蓋，特高一丈，別駕主簿車，緹油屏泥於軾前，以章有德。」
entries.en: After three years Emperor Xuan issued an edict: "By imperial command to the imperial clerk: appoint Huang Ba, inspector of Yang Province and top-ranked worthy, as governor of Yingchuan at the salary rank of two thousand bushels. Grant him a carriage canopy in office, one foot taller than usual, with chariots for his chief aide and registrar, and apply tiji oil to the screen and mudguards before the crossbar, to display his virtue."
entries.literal: After three years Emperor Xuan issued an edict saying: "By imperial command to the imperial clerk: appoint Ba, inspector of Yang Province and top-ranked worthy, as governor of Yingchuan at salary equivalent to two thousand bushels. Grant him a carriage canopy in office, one foot taller than usual, with chariots for his chief aide and registrar, and apply tiji oil to the screen and mudguards before the crossbar, to display his virtue."

entries.zh: 霸以外寬內明得吏民心，戶口歲增，治為天下第一。
entries.en: Outwardly indulgent but inwardly acute, Huang Ba won the trust of officials and commoners alike. His registers swelled year by year until his district ranked first in the empire.
entries.literal: Ba by outward generous inward clear won clerks and people's hearts; household registers yearly increased; governance was first under heaven.

entries.zh: 征守京兆尹，秩二千石。
entries.en: He was summoned to serve as governor of the capital at two thousand bushels.
entries.literal: Summoned to guard Metropolitan Governor, salary rank two thousand bushels.

entries.zh: 坐發民治馳道不先聞，又發騎士詣北軍馬不適士，劾乏軍興，連貶秩。
entries.en: He was faulted for drafting labor to repair the imperial highways without prior notice and for sending cavalry to the Northern Army with mounts unfit for the men. Accused of sabotaging a mobilization, he suffered repeated demotions.
entries.literal: Sat because mobilizing people to repair imperial roads did not first report; further mobilizing mounted knights to North Army horses did not suit knights; impeached lacking military campaign; serially demoted salary rank.

entries.zh: 有詔歸穎川太守官，以八百石居治如其前。
entries.en: An edict sent him back to Yingchuan as governor at eight hundred bushels, where he governed as before.
entries.literal: There was an edict returning Yingchuan grand administrator office, at eight hundred bushels dwell governance as his before.

entries.zh: 前後八年，郡中愈治。
entries.en: Eight years in all, and the commandery grew better governed than ever.
entries.literal: Before and after eight years, within the commandery ever more ordered.

entries.zh: 是時，鳳皇神爵數集郡國，穎川尤多。
entries.en: Phoenixes and "divine sparrows" were turning up in commanderies across the realm; Yingchuan reported more sightings than most.
entries.literal: At this time, phoenixes and divine sparrows repeatedly gathered in commanderies and kingdoms; Yingchuan especially many.

entries.zh: 天子以霸治行終長者，下詔稱揚曰：「穎川太守霸，宣佈詔令，百姓向化，孝子弟弟貞婦順孫日以眾多，田者讓畔，道不拾遣，養視鰥寡，贍助貧窮，獄或八年亡重罪囚，吏民向於教化，興於行誼，可謂賢人君子矣。
entries.en: The emperor, deeming Huang Ba's career that of a true elder statesman, issued an edict of praise: "Governor Ba of Yingchuan has broadcast my decrees until the people have turned to virtue. Filial sons, dutiful younger brothers, chaste wives, and obedient grandsons multiply by the day. Farmers yield the boundary strips to one another; no one pockets what others drop on the road. Widows and orphans are cared for, the poor relieved. Some jails have seen no serious offender in eight years. Officials and subjects alike respond to moral instruction and prize honorable conduct. He is every inch the worthy gentleman.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven because Ba's governance conduct ended as elder-kind issued an edict praising saying: "Yingchuan Grand Administrator Ba proclaimed edict commands; hundred surnames turned toward transformation; filial sons younger brothers chaste wives obedient grandsons daily grew numerous; fielders yielded field borders; on the road did not pick up lost; nourished and looked after widowers and widows, relieved and assisted poor destitute; prisons perhaps eight years without heavy-crime prisoners; clerks and people turned toward transforming instruction, rose in conduct and righteousness—can be called worthy man gentleman.

entries.zh: 《書》不雲乎？
entries.en: Does not the Book of Documents say:
entries.literal: Does not the Document say?

entries.zh: 『股肱良哉！』
entries.en: How excellent are his ministers, the arms and legs of rule!"
entries.literal: Thigh and arm—how good!"

entries.zh: 其賜爵關內侯，黃金百斤，秩中二千石。」
entries.en: Grant him the rank of marquis within the passes, a hundred catties of gold, and salary at two thousand bushels."
entries.literal: Let him be granted noble rank marquis within the passes, one hundred jin of yellow gold, salary rank central two thousand bushels."

entries.zh: 而穎川孝弟有行義民、三老、力田，皆以差賜爵及帛。
entries.en: In Yingchuan, commoners noted for filial piety and righteous conduct, village elders, and model farmers received graded titles and bolts of silk as well.
entries.literal: Moreover Yingchuan filial younger-brotherly who had conduct and righteousness commoners, village elders, force-in-fields, all by gradation were granted noble rank and silk.

entries.zh: 後數月，征霸為太子太傅，遷御史大夫。
entries.en: A few months later Huang Ba was summoned to be tutor to the heir apparent, then promoted to imperial clerk.
entries.literal: After several months, summoned Ba as heir-apparent grand tutor, promoted Imperial Clerk Grandee.

entries.zh: 神爵元年卒。
entries.en: He died in the first year of the Shenjue era.
entries.literal: In the first year of Shenjue he died.

entries.zh: 天子閔惜，下詔稱揚曰：「大司農邑，廉潔守節，退食自公，亡強外之交，束脩之饋，可謂淑人君子，遭離凶災，朕甚閔之。
entries.en: The emperor grieved and issued an edict: "Minister Zhu Yi was honest and upright, took only his public salary, cultivated no illicit ties abroad, and refused private gifts. He was the very model of a gentleman. Struck down untimely, I mourn him deeply.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven pitied and mourned; issued an edict praising saying: "Excellency of Agriculture Yi, incorrupt clean guarded integrity; lived frugally on his official salary alone; lacked forced-outside friendships; bundled-dried-meat gifts—can be called good person gentleman; meeting separation fierce calamity—I greatly pity him.

entries.zh: 其賜邑子黃金百斤，以奉其祭祀。」
entries.en: Award his son a hundred catties of gold for the ancestral offerings."
entries.literal: Let Yi's son be granted one hundred jin yellow gold, thereby to supply his sacrifices and worship.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，不久，渤海左右郡歲饑，盜賊並起，二千石不能禽制。
entries.en: Soon after Emperor Xuan took the throne, famine struck Bohai and neighboring commanderies. Bandits rose everywhere and local governors could not suppress them.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan ascended the throne; not long after, Bohai left-right commanderies year famine; robbers-thieves together arose; two-thousand-bushel officials could not capture control.

entries.zh: 上選能治者，丞相、御史舉遂可用，上以為渤海太守。
entries.en: The emperor sought a capable man; chancellor and chief clerk recommended Gong Sui, and he was named governor of Bohai.
entries.literal: The sovereign selected those able to govern; Chancellor and Imperial Clerk raised Sui as usable; the sovereign made him Bohai grand administrator.

entries.zh: 時，遂年七十餘，召見，形貌短小，宣帝望見，不副所聞，心內輕焉，謂遂曰：「渤海廢亂，朕甚憂之。
entries.en: Gong Sui was past seventy. At audience he looked undersized; Emperor Xuan, seeing him from afar, felt he did not match his reputation and secretly underestimated him. "Bohai lies in ruins," said the emperor, "and it weighs on me.
entries.literal: At the time, Sui's age was over seventy; summoned audience; form and appearance short small; Emperor Xuan looked and saw, did not match what was heard; inwardly heart slighted him; said to Sui: "Bohai ruined chaotic—I greatly worry it.

entries.zh: 君欲何以息其盜賊，以稱朕意？」
entries.en: How will you quiet the bandits there and satisfy my hopes?"
entries.literal: What method do you wish thereby to rest its robbers-thieves, thereby to match my intention?"

entries.zh: 遂對曰：「海瀕遐遠，不沾聖化，其民困於饑寒而吏不恤，故使陛下赤子盜弄陛下之兵於潢池中耳。
entries.en: Gong Sui answered: "Bohai lies far on the coast and has missed your transforming influence. The people starve while officials show no mercy, so your innocent subjects have merely borrowed your weapons to splash in a roadside puddle—no grave rebellion.
entries.literal: Sui replied saying: "The sea shore far distant, does not touch sagely transformation; its people trapped in hunger cold yet clerks do not pity; therefore made Your Majesty's crimson sons steal play Your Majesty's weapons in the irrigation pond—that is all.

entries.zh: 今欲使臣勝之邪，將安之也？」
entries.en: Do you want me to crush them by force or to bring peace?"
entries.literal: Now do you wish to make your subject conquer them, or will you settle them?"

entries.zh: 上聞遂對，甚說，答曰：「選用賢良，固欲安之也。」
entries.en: Delighted by the answer, the emperor said, "We chose a worthy man precisely because we mean to pacify them."
entries.literal: The sovereign heard Sui's reply, greatly pleased, answered saying: "In selecting and employing worthy and good, solidly wish to settle them."

entries.zh: 遂曰：「臣聞治亂民猶治亂繩，不可急也；
entries.en: Gong Sui continued: "They say unruly folk are like a snarled cord—you cannot yank it straight by force;
entries.literal: Sui said: "Your subject has heard governing unruly people is like governing a tangled rope—cannot be hurried;

entries.zh: 唯緩之，然後可治。
entries.en: only gentle patience untangles it.
entries.literal: Only slacken it, afterward then can be governed.

entries.zh: 臣願丞相、御史且無拘臣以文法，得一切便宜從事。」
entries.en: Ask the chancellor and chief clerk not to tie my hands with paperwork so I may act as circumstances require."
entries.literal: Your subject wishes Chancellor and Imperial Clerk temporarily not bind your subject with literary law—obtain all matters convenient advantage follow affairs."

entries.zh: 上許焉，加賜黃金，贈遣乘傳。
entries.en: The emperor agreed, added a gift of gold, and sent him post-haste to his post.
entries.literal: The sovereign permitted it; additionally granted yellow gold; sent off riding relay.

entries.zh: 至渤海界，郡聞新太守至，發兵以迎，遂皆遣還，移書敕屬縣悉罷逐捕盜賊吏。
entries.en: As he entered Bohai the district tried to greet him with armed escorts; he sent every soldier home and ordered all counties to dismiss officers tasked with hunting bandits.
entries.literal: When reached Bohai border, the commandery hearing new grand administrator arrived, mobilized troops thereby to welcome; Sui all sent back; moved documents ordering subordinate counties entirely abolish chase capture robber-thief clerks.

entries.zh: 諸持鋤鉤田器者皆為良民，吏毋得問，持兵者乃為盜賊。
entries.en: Anyone carrying hoes or sickles was a law-abiding farmer beyond official suspicion; only men bearing arms counted as bandits.
entries.literal: All who held hoes hooks field tools were good commoners—clerks must not question; those who held weapons then were robbers-thieves.

entries.zh: 遂單車獨行至府，郡中翕然，盜賊亦皆罷。
entries.en: He drove alone to headquarters. The commandery fell quiet, and the outlaw bands gave up.
entries.literal: Sui alone cart alone traveled arrived at residence; within commandery harmonious; robbers-thieves also all ceased.

entries.zh: 渤海又多劫略相隨，聞遂教令，即時解散，棄其兵弩而持鉤鋤。
entries.en: Bands that had roamed together looting broke up as soon as his orders circulated, dropping bows for farm tools.
entries.literal: Bohai further had many plundering following one another; hearing Sui's teach commands, immediately dispersed dissolved; abandoned their weapons crossbows and held hooks hoes.

entries.zh: 盜賊於是悉平，民安土樂業。
entries.en: Order returned; people settled back to their fields and trades.
entries.literal: Robbers-thieves thereupon all pacified; people secure soil joyful occupations.

entries.zh: 遂乃開倉廩假貧民，選用良吏，尉安牧養焉。
entries.en: He opened the granaries to feed the hungry, appointed capable officers, and nursed the district back to health.
entries.literal: Sui then opened granaries lent poor people; selected employed good clerks; comforted settled pastured nourished them.

entries.zh: 為丞相五歲，甘露三年薨，諡曰定侯。
entries.en: He served as chancellor for five years and died in the third year of Ganlu (51 BCE); his posthumous title was Marquis Ding.
entries.literal: He served as chancellor for five years and died in the third year of Ganlu; his posthumous title was Marquis Ding.

entries.zh: 霸死後，樂陵侯高竟為大司馬。
entries.en: After Huang Ba's death, Shi Gao, Marquis of Leling, eventually became grand marshal.
entries.literal: After Ba's death, Shi Gao, Marquis of Leling, ultimately became grand marshal.

entries.zh: 霸子思侯賞嗣，為關都尉。
entries.en: Huang Ba's son Shang, Marquis Si, succeeded him and served as colonel guarding the passes.
entries.literal: Ba's son Shang, Marquis Si, succeeded and served as colonel guarding the passes.

entries.zh: 薨，子忠侯輔嗣，至衛尉九卿。
entries.en: When he died, his son Fu, Marquis Zhong, succeeded and rose to one of the nine ministers as commandant of the guards.
entries.literal: When he died, his son Fu, Marquis Zhong, succeeded and rose to one of the nine ministers as commandant of the guards.

entries.zh: 薨，子忠嗣侯，訖王莽乃絕。
entries.en: When he died, his son Zhong inherited the marquisate; the line ended only under Wang Mang.
entries.literal: When he died, his son Zhong inherited the marquisate; the line ended only under Wang Mang.

entries.zh: 子孫為吏二千石者五六人。
entries.en: Five or six of his descendants held offices at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
entries.literal: Five or six descendants held offices at the two-thousand-bushel rank.

entries.zh: 是時，張敞為膠東相，與邑書曰：「明主游心太古，廣延茂士，此誠忠臣竭思之時也。
entries.en: Zhang Chang, then chancellor of Jiaodong, wrote to Zhu Yi: "Our discerning ruler looks back to high antiquity and casts a wide net for talent. This is the moment for loyal servants to give everything they have.
entries.literal: At this time, Zhang Chang was Jiaodong chancellor; he wrote to Yi saying: "The enlightened sovereign roams mind in high antiquity, broadly extends flourishing gentlemen—this truly is the time when loyal ministers exhaust thought.

entries.zh: 直敞遠守劇郡，馭於繩墨，匈臆約結，固亡奇也。
entries.en: I am stuck governing a difficult frontier commandery, hemmed in by rules until my chest feels bound—hardly the place for brilliance.
entries.literal: Only Chang far guards a severe commandery, driven by ink-line; breast-bosom tied and knotted—solidly lacks marvel.

entries.zh: 雖有，亦安所施？
entries.en: Even if I had ideas, where could I use them?
entries.literal: Even if there were, where moreover would it be applied?

entries.zh: 足下以清明之德，掌周稷之業，猶饑者甘糟糠，穰歲余梁肉。
entries.en: You hold the minister's granaries with unsullied integrity: for you the meanest grain tastes sweet, while in a fat year others leave meat on the table.
entries.literal: You, sir, by clear bright virtue grasp Zhou Houji's enterprise—like a hungry man sweetening chaff and husks, in a bumper year surplus fine grain and meat.

entries.zh: 何則？
entries.en: Why?
entries.literal: Why then?

entries.zh: 有亡之勢異也。
entries.en: Because surplus and want change how things feel.
entries.literal: Having and lacking's situation differs.

entries.zh: 昔陳平雖賢，須魏無知而後進；
entries.en: Chen Ping was a capable man, yet he advanced only after Wei Wuzhi had recommended him;
entries.literal: Formerly Chen Ping although worthy, needed Wei Wuzhi and afterward advanced;

entries.zh: 韓信雖奇，賴蕭公而後信。
entries.en: Han Xin was a prodigy, yet he won trust only after Xiao He backed him.
entries.literal: Han Xin although marvelous, relied on Lord Xiao and afterward was trusted.

entries.zh: 故事各達其時之英俊，若必伊尹、呂望而後薦之，則此人不因足下而進矣。」
entries.en: History shows every era advances its own capable men. If you insist on waiting for another Yi Yin or Lü Shang, talent will pass you by—those men will never owe their careers to you."
entries.literal: By precedent each reaches his age's heroes; if one must wait for Yi Yin and Lü Wang and afterward recommend them, then this person will not because of you, sir, advance."

entries.zh: 邑感敞言，貢薦賢士大夫，多得其助者。
entries.en: Zhu Yi took Zhang Chang's words to heart, forwarded worthy candidates to court, and many men owed their breaks to him.
entries.literal: Yi was moved by Chang's words; presented and recommended worthy scholar-officials; many obtained those he aided.

entries.zh: 身為列卿，居處儉節，祿賜以共九族鄉黨，家亡余財。
entries.en: Though he ranked among the nine ministers, he lived plainly and gave his stipends to extended family and neighbors, leaving no hoard at home.
entries.literal: His person being ranked minister, dwelling place frugal restrained; salary gifts used to supply nine kinships village community; household lacked surplus wealth.

entries.zh: 卷八十九 循吏傳第五十九
entries.en: Volume 89: Biographies of Exemplary Officials (59).
entries.literal: Volume 89: Biographies of Upright Officials, Number 59.

entries.zh: 漢興，破觚而為圜，斫雕而為樸，號為罔漏吞舟之魚。
entries.en: At Han's founding the state filed away Qin's sharp corners into smooth curves and stripped ornament back to plain wood—netting loose enough, it was said, that even a boat-swallowing fish could slip through.
entries.literal: When Han arose, they broke the square goblet and made it round, chopped carving and made plainness; it was called a net that did not leak fish that swallow boats.

entries.zh: 而吏治蒸蒸，不至於奸，黎民艾安。
entries.en: Yet governance warmed and improved, crime never ran wild, and common folk lived untroubled.
entries.literal: Yet clerk governance steamed upward, did not reach wickedness; black-haired people were pacified secure.

entries.zh: 由是觀之，在彼不在此。
entries.en: The lesson is that outcomes hinge on the spirit behind rule, not on the letter of the code alone.
entries.literal: Viewing from this, it lies in that, not in this.

entries.zh: 高後時，酷吏獨有侯封，刻轢宗室，侵辱功臣。
entries.en: Under the Grand Empress Dowager Lü the notable harsh official was Hou Feng, who rode roughshod over the imperial house and insulted the founders.
entries.literal: In Empress Gao's time, among cruel clerks there was only Hou Feng; he carved and crushed the imperial clan and encroached on and humiliated merit ministers.

entries.zh: 呂氏已敗，遂夷侯封之家。
entries.en: When the Lü faction fell, Hou Feng's entire line was wiped out.
entries.literal: After the Lü clan had been defeated, thereupon extirpated Hou Feng's household.

entries.zh: 孝景時，晁錯以刻深頗用術輔其資，而七國之亂髮怒於錯，錯卒被戮。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo won influence through pitiless legalism; the Rebellion of the Seven States vented its rage on him, and he died under the blade.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jing's time, Chao Cuo by carving depth largely employed craft to assist his endowment; the Seven Kingdoms' rebellion flared anger at Cuo; Cuo finally met execution.

entries.zh: 其後有郅都、甯成之倫。
entries.en: Men such as Zhi Du and Ning Cheng followed.
entries.literal: Afterward there were the likes of Zhi Du and Ning Cheng.

entries.zh: 郅都，河東大陽人也。
entries.en: Zhi Du came from Dayang in Hedong Commandery.
entries.literal: Zhi Du was a man of Dayang in Hedong.

entries.zh: 以郎事文帝。
entries.en: He served Emperor Wen in the corps of gentlemen.
entries.literal: As a gentleman he served Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 景帝時為中郎將，敢直諫，面折大臣於朝。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing he commanded the gentleman cadets, spoke blunt truth, and openly dressed down senior ministers in open court.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jing's time he was leader of gentleman cadets—dared straight remonstrance, face rebuked great ministers at court.

entries.zh: 嘗從入上林，賈姬在廁，野彘入廁。
entries.en: On a hunt in Shanglin Park, a favorite consort named Jia withdrew to a latrine just as a wild boar burst in.
entries.literal: Once following him into Shanglin, Concubine Jia was in the privy; a wild boar entered the privy.

entries.zh: 上目都，都不行。
entries.en: The emperor motioned Zhi Du to intervene; Zhi Du stood fast.
entries.literal: The sovereign signaled Du; Du did not move.

entries.zh: 上欲自持兵救賈姬，都伏上前曰：「亡一姬復一姬進，天下所少寧姬等邪？
entries.en: When the emperor reached for arms to rescue her, Zhi Du blocked him: "Lose one favorite and another takes her place—is the empire short of such women?
entries.literal: The sovereign wished himself to take weapons and save Concubine Jia; Du threw himself forward saying: "Lose one concubine and another concubine advances—what the realm lacks, is it surely concubines like this?

entries.zh: 陛下縱自輕，奈宗廟太后何？」
entries.en: Even if you discount your own safety, what of the altars of state and the empress dowager?"
entries.literal: Your Majesty even if slight yourself—how about the ancestral temples and the empress dowager?"

entries.zh: 上還，彘亦不傷賈姬。
entries.en: The emperor held back; the boar left without harming Lady Jia.
entries.literal: The sovereign withdrew; the boar also did not harm Concubine Jia.

entries.zh: 太后聞之，賜都金百斤，上亦賜金百斤，由此重都。
entries.en: The dowager rewarded Zhi Du with a hundred catties of gold; the emperor matched it, and both sides henceforth prized him.
entries.literal: The empress dowager heard it and granted Du a hundred jin of gold; the sovereign also granted a hundred jin of gold—thereby valued Du.

entries.zh: 濟南瞷氏宗人三百餘家，豪猾，二千石莫能制，於是景帝拜都為濟南守。
entries.en: More than three hundred households of the powerful Jian lineage dominated Jinan beyond any governor's control, so Emperor Jing named Zhi Du to the post.
entries.literal: In Jinan the Jian clan kin numbered more than three hundred households—powerful and crafty; two-thousand-bushel officials could not control them; thereupon Emperor Jing appointed Du Jinan grand administrator.

entries.zh: 至則誅瞷氏首惡，餘皆股慄。
entries.en: On arrival he executed the clan's chiefs; everyone else shook with fear.
entries.literal: When he arrived he executed the Jian ringleaders; the rest all thigh trembled.

entries.zh: 居歲餘，郡中不拾遺，旁十餘郡守畏都如大府。
entries.en: Within a year lost goods lay untouched in the streets, and a dozen neighboring governors feared him like a senior minister.
entries.literal: After residing slightly more than a year, within the commandery none picked up lost articles; neighboring more than ten commanderies' guards feared Du like a great prefecture.

entries.zh: 臨江王征詣中尉府對簿，臨江王欲得刀筆為書謝上，而都禁吏弗與。
entries.en: Prince Rong of Linjiang was hauled to headquarters for interrogation and begged for knife and stylus to draft an apology to the throne; Zhi Du barred clerks from supplying them.
entries.literal: The Prince of Linjiang was summoned to the commandant's yamen to answer charges; the Prince of Linjiang wished to obtain knife and brush to write thanking the sovereign, but Du forbade clerks and did not give.

entries.zh: 魏其侯使人間予臨江王。
entries.en: The Marquis of Weiqi smuggled writing tools to the prince.
entries.literal: Marquis Weiqi sent someone secretly to give the Prince of Linjiang.

entries.zh: 臨江王既得，為書謝上，因自殺。
entries.en: With them he penned his apology and took his own life.
entries.literal: Once the Prince of Linjiang obtained them, he wrote thanking the sovereign and thereupon killed himself.

entries.zh: 竇太后聞之，怒，以危法中都，都免歸家。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Dou, enraged, pinned a capital offense on Zhi Du and dismissed him.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Dou heard it, grew angry, struck Du with perilous law; Du was dismissed and returned home.

entries.zh: 景帝乃使使即拜都為雁門太守，便道之官，得以便宜從事。
entries.en: Emperor Jing immediately commissioned him Yanmen governor by express edict with discretionary powers en route.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing then dispatched envoys on the spot to appoint Du Yanmen grand administrator; by convenient route went to office—obtained all matters convenient advantage.

entries.zh: 匈奴素聞郅都節，舉邊為引兵去，竟都死不近雁門。
entries.en: The Xiongnu, respecting his iron integrity, pulled back from the frontier and never again pressed Yanmen while he lived.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu always heard of Zhi Du's integrity—withdrew troops along the whole border and departed; to the end of Du's death they did not approach Yanmen.

entries.zh: 匈奴至為偶人像都，令騎馳射，莫能中，其見憚如此。
entries.en: They fashioned straw effigies of him for mounted archery drills that no one could strike—such was their dread.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu even made dummy images of Du, ordered riders to gallop and shoot—none could hit; his being feared was thus.

entries.zh: 匈奴患之。
entries.en: They regarded him as a scourge.
entries.literal: The Xiongnu worried over him.

entries.zh: 乃中都以漢法。
entries.en: They maneuvered the Han court into indicting him.
entries.literal: Thereupon struck Du with Han law.

entries.zh: 景帝曰：「都忠臣。」
entries.en: Emperor Jing protested, "Zhi Du is a loyal servant."
entries.literal: Emperor Jing said: "Du is a loyal minister."

entries.zh: 欲釋之。
entries.en: He meant to spare him.
entries.literal: He wished to release him.

entries.zh: 竇太后曰：「臨江王獨非忠臣乎？」
entries.en: The dowager retorted, "Was Prince Rong not loyal?"
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Dou said: "Was the Prince of Linjiang alone not a loyal minister?"

entries.zh: 於是斬都也。
entries.en: Zhi Du went to the executioner's block.
entries.literal: Thereupon Du was beheaded.

entries.zh: 甯成，南陽穰人也。
entries.en: Ning Cheng came from Rang in Nanyang Commandery.
entries.literal: Ning Cheng was a man of Rang in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 以郎謁者事景帝。
entries.en: He served Emperor Jing as a gentleman usher.
entries.literal: As gentleman usher he served Emperor Jing.

entries.zh: 好氣，為小吏，必陵其長吏；
entries.en: Combative by nature, he browbeat superiors even as a junior clerk;
entries.literal: He loved dominance; as petty clerk he invariably lorded over his senior clerks;

entries.zh: 為人上，操下急如束濕。
entries.en: Once in charge, he squeezed subordinates as though wringing soaked rope.
entries.literal: when above others, he handled subordinates tight as binding wet hemp.

entries.zh: 猾賊任威。
entries.en: Cunning and ruthless, he ruled by terror.
entries.literal: Crafty villain employed intimidation.

entries.zh: 稍遷至濟南都尉，而郅都為守。
entries.en: He rose to commandant of Jinan while Zhi Du governed there.
entries.literal: Gradually promoted to Jinan commandant while Zhi Du was grand administrator.

entries.zh: 始前數都尉步入府，因吏謁守如縣令，其畏都如此。
entries.en: Earlier commandants had walked to headquarters and petitioned the governor through petty officers like county magistrates—such was Zhi Du's grip.
entries.literal: Formerly those several commandants always entered the yamen on foot, through clerks visited the grand administrator like county chiefs—such did they fear Du.

entries.zh: 及成往，直凌都出其上。
entries.en: Ning Cheng strode in and topped even Zhi Du.
entries.literal: When Cheng arrived, straightaway rode roughshod over Du and rose above him.

entries.zh: 都素聞其聲，善遇，與結歡。
entries.en: Zhi Du, knowing his name, treated him generously and won his goodwill.
entries.literal: Du always heard his reputation, treated him well, and bonded in friendship.

entries.zh: 久之，都死，後長安左右宗室多犯法，上召成為中尉。
entries.en: After Zhi Du died, imperial relatives around Chang'an ran riot until the emperor recalled Ning Cheng as metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: After long time Du died; afterward Chang'an left-right imperial kin many violated law; the sovereign summoned Cheng as commandant of the capital.

entries.zh: 其治效郅都，其廉弗如，然宗室豪傑人皆惴恐。
entries.en: His methods rivaled Zhi Du's ferocity without the same honesty; still every noble house quaked.
entries.literal: His governance matched Zhi Du's effects; his incorruptibility did not compare—yet imperial clan heroes all trembled in terror.

entries.zh: 周陽由，其父趙兼以淮南王舅侯周陽，故因氏焉。
entries.en: Zhouyang You inherited the surname because his father Zhao Jian, uncle to the king of Huainan, had been marquis of Zhouyang.
entries.literal: Zhouyang You—his father Zhao Jian, because he was maternal uncle to the Prince of Huainan, was enfeoffed at Zhouyang—therefore took that surname.

entries.zh: 由以宗家任為郎，事文帝。
entries.en: Through clan privilege he entered the gentleman corps under Emperor Wen.
entries.literal: You by imperial-clan appointment became gentleman and served Emperor Wen.

entries.zh: 景帝時，由為郡守。
entries.en: Under Emperor Jing he served as a governor.
entries.literal: In Emperor Jing's time You was grand administrator.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，吏治尚修謹，然由居二千石中最為暴酷驕恣。
entries.en: Emperor Wu's early bureaucracy prized sobriety, yet Zhouyang You outdid every governor in brutality and swagger.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended, clerk governance still esteemed cultivation and caution—yet among two-thousand-bushel officials You was the most violent, cruel, arrogant, and wilful.

entries.zh: 所愛者，撓法活之；
entries.en: Favorites walked free while statutes twisted around them;
entries.literal: Those he loved—he bent law to keep them alive;

entries.zh: 所憎者，曲法滅之。
entries.en: Those he hated he twisted the law to destroy.
entries.literal: those he hated—he twisted law to destroy them.

entries.zh: 所居郡，必夷其豪。
entries.en: Wherever he served he slaughtered local magnates.
entries.literal: In whatever commandery he dwelt, he invariably extirpated its powerful families.

entries.zh: 為守，視都尉如令；
entries.en: As governor he treated his commandant like a county chief;
entries.literal: As grand administrator he treated commandants like county magistrates;

entries.zh: 為都尉，陵太守，奪之治。
entries.en: as commandant he bullied governors and stole their authority.
entries.literal: as commandant he rode roughshod over grand administrators and seized their governance.

entries.zh: 汲黯為忮，司馬安之文惡，俱在二千石列，同車未嘗敢均茵馮。
entries.en: Ji An's vinegar temper and Sima An's poison pen shared two-thousand-bushel rank, yet neither would share a carriage seat evenly with Zhouyang You.
entries.literal: Ji An was harsh; Sima An's literary severity was wicked—both stood in the two-thousand-bushel ranks; riding together they never dared equal cushion mats.

entries.zh: 後由為河東都尉，與其守勝屠公爭權，相告言，勝屠公當抵罪，義不受刑，自殺，而由棄市。
entries.en: Later, as Hedong commandant, he feuded with Governor Shengtu Gong until both denounced the other; Shengtu Gong chose suicide over sentence and Zhouyang You died by public execution.
entries.literal: Later You became Hedong commandant, wrangled power with his governor Shengtu Gong, mutually informed on each other; Shengtu Gong ought to meet crime, on principle refused to suffer punishment, killed himself; while You was exposed in market.

entries.zh: 武帝即位，徙為內史。
entries.en: Emperor Wu moved him to privy treasurer of the capital precincts.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended, he was transferred privy treasurer.

entries.zh: 外戚多毀成之短，抵罪髡鉗。
entries.en: In-laws trumped up charges until he was shorn and fitted with an iron collar.
entries.literal: Outer affines largely slandered Cheng's shortcomings; he met crime—shaved and collared.

entries.zh: 是時，九卿死即死，少被刑，而成刑極，自以為不復收，及解脫，詐刻傳出關歸家。
entries.en: High ministers usually faced execution, not mutilation; Ning Cheng's sentence was cruel enough that he assumed his career over—until he forged papers, fled the frontier, and bolted home.
entries.literal: At this time among Nine Ministers death meant death—few suffered mutilation—yet Cheng's punishments reached the extreme; he thought himself never to be taken again; when freed, he forged a passport and slipped past the passes homeward.

entries.zh: 稱曰：「仕不至二千石，賈不至千萬，安可比人乎！」
entries.en: He announced, "Without a two-thousand-bushel post or a ten-million fortune you cannot measure yourself against other men!"
entries.literal: He declared: "If office does not reach two thousand bushels, if trade does not reach ten million—how can one compare with others!"

entries.zh: 乃貰貣陂田千餘頃，假貧民，役使數千家。
entries.en: He borrowed capital to bankroll over a thousand qing of diked marsh, leased plots to the destitute, and drafted thousands of households as labor.
entries.literal: Thereupon he borrowed against more than a thousand qing of marsh acreage, lent to poor people, corvée-employed several thousand households.

entries.zh: 數年，會赦，致產數千萬，為任俠，持吏長短，出從數十騎。
entries.en: Amnesty restored him; within years his fortune ran to tens of millions. Playing vigilante, he blackmailed officials and rode abroad with dozens of horsemen.
entries.literal: After several years, met amnesty; accumulated property to several tens of millions; acted knight-errant; held clerks' secrets; went out followed by several tens of mounted riders.

entries.zh: 其使民，威重於郡守。
entries.en: Commoners feared his word more than their governor's.
entries.literal: His commanding common people—awe weighed heavier than grand administrators.

entries.zh: 是時，趙禹、張湯為九卿矣，然其治尚寬，輔法而行，縱以鷹擊毛摯為治。
entries.en: Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang were harsh ministers already, but next to Yi Zong's eagle tactics they looked almost moderate.
entries.literal: At this time Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang already ranked among the Nine Ministers—yet their style stayed comparatively lenient, following statute—while Zong governed by hawk strikes and tearing feathers.

entries.zh: 後會更五銖錢白金起，民為奸，京師尤甚，乃以縱為右內史，王溫舒為中尉。
entries.en: When debased coinage drove capital fraud, the court named Yi Zong right metropolitan superintendent and Wang Wenshu commandant of the guard.
entries.literal: Later, when the new wuzhu coinage and white-metal currency spawned fraud—worst in the capital—Zong was made right privy treasurer and Wang Wenshu metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 溫舒至惡，所為弗先言縱，縱必以氣陵之，敗壞其功。
entries.en: Wang Wenshu was vicious and freelanced his raids until Yi Zong sabotaged him out of sheer rivalry.
entries.literal: Wenshu was utterly vicious; whatever he undertook he did not clear with Zong first—Zong invariably rode roughshod over him in spirit and ruined his schemes.

entries.zh: 其治，所誅殺甚多，然取為小治，奸益不勝，直指始出矣。
entries.en: The slaughter looked like small-scale policing even as crime exploded and palace inspectors fanned into the provinces.
entries.literal: Their governance slew vast numbers—yet counted only as petty policing—wickedness grew unstoppable—and imperial "direct investigators" began rolling out.

entries.zh: 吏之治以斬殺縛吏為務，閻奉以惡用矣。
entries.en: Officialdom raced to kill and bind; Yan Feng won promotion through sheer cruelty.
entries.literal: Clerk governance made beheading and binding its chief task—Yan Feng earned employment through viciousness.

entries.zh: 縱廉，其治效郅都。
entries.en: Yi Zong stayed honest and governed with Zhi Du's pitiless edge.
entries.literal: Zong was incorrupt; his administrative effects matched Zhi Du's.

entries.zh: 上幸鼎湖，病久，已而卒起幸甘泉，道不治。
entries.en: After a long illness at Dinghu Lake the emperor abruptly traveled to Sweet Springs while the highway stayed broken.
entries.literal: The sovereign favored Dinghu—ill a long while—then suddenly rose to favor Sweet Springs—the road went unrepaired.

entries.zh: 上怒曰：「縱以我為不行此道乎？」
entries.en: He snapped, "Does Yi Zong think I intend to abandon this route?"
entries.literal: The sovereign angrily said: "Does Zong imagine I will never take this road?"

entries.zh: 銜之。
entries.en: The emperor nursed a grudge.
entries.literal: He harbored resentment.

entries.zh: 至冬，楊可方受告緡，縱以為此亂民，部吏捕其為可使者。
entries.en: When Yang Ke launched the wealth-reporting inquisitions, Yi Zong called them destabilizing and seized Yang Ke's deputies.
entries.literal: Come winter Yang Ke was about to enforce the denunciation of concealed wealth—Zong deemed this would riot the people and ordered clerks to arrest Yang Ke's agents.

entries.zh: 天子聞，使杜式治，以為廢格沮事，棄縱市。
entries.en: The emperor charged Du Shi with the case, convicted Yi Zong of blocking state policy, and left him on the execution ground.
entries.literal: The Son of Heaven heard, sent Du Shi to judge him—found him guilty of obstructing imperial directives—and had Yi Zong executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 後一歲，張湯亦死。
entries.en: Zhang Tang died the following year.
entries.literal: One year later Zhang Tang also died.

entries.zh: 趙禹，斄人也。
entries.en: Zhao Yu hailed from Tai (in Fufeng).
entries.literal: Zhao Yu was a man of Tai.

entries.zh: 以佐史補中都官，用廉為令史，事太尉周亞夫。
entries.en: He rose from aide to capital posts, won recommendation as honest, became chief clerk under Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu.
entries.literal: By assistant clerk supplemented capital offices; by incorrupt became chief clerk, served Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu.

entries.zh: 亞夫為丞相，禹為丞相史，府中皆稱其廉平。
entries.en: When Zhou Yafu became chancellor, Zhao Yu served as his bureau clerk and won praise for integrity.
entries.literal: When Yafu was chancellor, Yu was chancellor clerk; within the bureau all praised his incorrupt fairness.

entries.zh: 然亞夫弗任，曰：「極知禹無害，然文深，不可以居大府。」
entries.en: Yet Yafu hesitated: "I know Zhao Yu is upright, but his legal prose is merciless—not fit for the main office."
entries.literal: Yet Yafu did not employ him, saying: "I utterly know Yu is harmless—yet his documents bite deep; cannot dwell in the great bureau."

entries.zh: 武帝時，禹以刀筆吏積勞，遷為御史。
entries.en: Under Emperor Wu he climbed from scribal clerk to imperial clerk.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu's time Yu by knife-brush clerk accumulated merit, promoted imperial clerk.

entries.zh: 上以為能，至中大夫。
entries.en: The emperor judged him capable and promoted him to palace grandee.
entries.literal: The sovereign deemed him capable—to palace grandee.

entries.zh: 與張湯論定律令，作見知，吏傳相監司以法，盡自此始。
entries.en: With Zhang Tang he framed statutes, invented mutual-liability prosecutions, and chained clerks into watchdogging one another—precedents starting here.
entries.literal: Together with Zhang Tang deliberated fixing statutes and commands, enacted "see and know"; clerks transmitting mutual surveillance by law—all began from this.

entries.zh: 尹齊，東郡茌平人也。
entries.en: Yin Qi hailed from Chiping in Dong commandery.
entries.literal: Yin Qi was a man of Chiping in Dong commandery.

entries.zh: 以刀筆吏稍遷至御史。
entries.en: He climbed from scribal clerk to imperial clerk.
entries.literal: From knife-brush clerk he gradually rose imperial clerk.

entries.zh: 事張湯，湯數稱以為廉。
entries.en: Zhang Tang repeatedly praised his honesty.
entries.literal: He served Zhang Tang—Tang repeatedly praised him incorrupt.

entries.zh: 武帝使督盜賊，斬伐不避貴勢。
entries.en: The emperor tasked him with bandit suppression regardless of rank.
entries.literal: Emperor Wu sent him to supervise robbers—executions spared no noble power.

entries.zh: 遷關都尉，聲甚於甯成。
entries.en: As pass commandant he terrified travelers worse than Ning Cheng.
entries.literal: Promoted pass commandant—reputation exceeded Ning Cheng.

entries.zh: 上以為能，拜為中尉。
entries.en: Capable in the emperor's eyes, he became metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: The sovereign deemed him capable—appointed metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 吏民益凋敝，輕齊木強少文，豪惡吏伏匿而善吏不能為治，以故事多廢，抵罪。
entries.en: His stiff manner exhausted the capital; villains hid while honest clerks stalled until scandal broke.
entries.literal: Clerks and people grew exhausted—disdained Qi's wooden stubbornness and lack of polish—powerful wicked clerks hid while honest clerks could not govern—therefore affairs largely collapsed—met conviction.

entries.zh: 後復為淮陽都尉。
entries.en: He resurfaced as Huaiyang commandant.
entries.literal: Later again Huaiyang commandant.

entries.zh: 王溫舒敗後數年，病死，家直不滿五十金。
entries.en: Years after Wang Wenshu's crash he died sick, leaving less than fifty catties of gold.
entries.literal: Several years after Wang Wenshu fell—died of illness—household worth not fifty pounds of gold.

entries.zh: 所誅滅淮陽甚多，及死，仇家欲燒其屍，妻亡去，歸葬。
entries.en: Huaiyang nursed many grudges; mourners meant to burn his body until his wife stole it away for burial.
entries.literal: Those he exterminated in Huaiyang were many—when he died enemy families wished to burn his corpse—his wife fled—returned him for burial.

entries.zh: 田廣明字子公，鄭人也。
entries.en: Tian Guangming, courtesy name Zigong, came from Zheng.
entries.literal: Tian Guangming styled Zigong—was a man of Zheng.

entries.zh: 以郎為天水司馬。
entries.en: He served as marshal of Tianshui from the gentleman corps.
entries.literal: As gentleman became Tianshui marshal.

entries.zh: 攻次遷河南都尉，以殺伐為治。
entries.en: Merit promotion brought him to commandant of Henan with a slash-and-burn style.
entries.literal: By merit he was promoted to commandant of Henan—taking slaughter as his method of rule.

entries.zh: 郡國盜賊並起，遷廣明為淮陽太守。
entries.en: When revolt spread, he became governor of Huaiyang.
entries.literal: Commanderies and kingdoms bandits arose together—promoted Guangming Huaiyang grand administrator.

entries.zh: 歲餘，故城父令公孫勇與客胡倩等謀反，倩詐稱光祿大夫，從車騎數十，言使督盜賊，止陳留傳捨，太守謁見，欲收取之。
entries.en: Former magistrate Gongsun Yong and Hu Qian forged credentials as an imperial inspector at Chenliu until the local governor moved to arrest them.
entries.literal: After slightly more than a year—former chief of Chengfu Gongsun Yong with guest Hu Qian and others plotted rebellion—Qian falsely claimed superintendent of palace gentlemen—with several tens chariot horses—declared mission supervising robbers—stopped Chenliu relay lodge—grand administrator visited wishing to seize.

entries.zh: 廣明覺知，發兵皆捕斬焉。
entries.en: Tian Guangming uncovered the plot and executed every conspirator.
entries.literal: Guangming perceived—mobilized troops—all captured executed.

entries.zh: 而公孫勇衣繡衣，乘駟馬車至圉，圉使小史侍之，亦知其非是，守尉魏不害與廄嗇夫江德、尉史蘇昌共收捕之。
entries.en: Gongsun Yong rode into Yu in counterfeit splendor until petty clerks and Commander Wei Buhai arrested him with Jiang De and Su Chang.
entries.literal: Meanwhile Gongsun Yong wore embroidered robes—rode four-horse carriage arrived Yu—Yu ordered petty clerk attend—also knew he was false—guard commandant Wei Buhai with stable bailiff Jiang De and clerk Su Chang together seized.

entries.zh: 上封不害為當塗侯，德為陽侯，昌蒲侯。
entries.en: The emperor made Wei Buhai marquis of Dangtu, Jiang De marquis of Yang, and Su Chang marquis of Pu.
entries.literal: Sovereign enfeoffed Buhai as Dangtu marquis—De as Yang marquis—Chang as Pu marquis.

entries.zh: 初，四人俱拜於前，小史竊言。
entries.en: At the mass investiture a junior clerk muttered aside.
entries.literal: Formerly four men together bowed forward—petty clerk whispered.

entries.zh: 武帝問：「言何？」
entries.en: The emperor asked: "What did he say?"
entries.literal: The emperor asked: "What did he say?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「為侯者得東歸不？」
entries.en: He replied in a whisper: "May one enfeoffed as marquis return east of the mountains?"
entries.literal: He replied: "May one enfeoffed as marquis return east?"

entries.zh: 上曰：「女欲不？
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Would you rather not take the honor?
entries.literal: The emperor said: "Do you not wish to be ennobled?

entries.zh: 貴矣。
entries.en: You are a noble now.
entries.literal: You are ennobled already.

entries.zh: 女鄉名為何？」
entries.en: What is your native village called?"
entries.literal: What is the name of your home village?"

entries.zh: 對曰：「名遺鄉。」
entries.en: He said it was called Yixiang, 'the Hamlet of the Left-Behind.'"
entries.literal: He replied: "It is called the Left-Behind Hamlet."

entries.zh: 上曰：「用遺汝矣。」
entries.en: The emperor answered, "Then the 'left-behind' fief is yours."
entries.literal: The emperor said: "I bequeath that name to you."

entries.zh: 於是賜小史爵關內侯，食遺鄉六百戶。
entries.en: He ennobled the clerk as marquis within the passes with six hundred households at Yixiang.
entries.literal: Thereupon he granted the petty clerk the rank of marquis within the passes with six hundred households at Yixiang.

entries.zh: 義縱，河東人也。
entries.en: Yi Zong came from Hedong.
entries.literal: Yi Zong was a man of Hedong.

entries.zh: 少年時嘗與張次公俱攻剽，為群盜。
entries.en: As a youth he and Zhang Cigong had robbed together as outlaws.
entries.literal: In youth he once together with Zhang Cigong both attacked and raided, acting bandit gang.

entries.zh: 縱有姊，以醫幸王太后。
entries.en: Yi Zong's sister was a physician who caught the eye of Empress Dowager Wang.
entries.literal: Zong had an elder sister who by medical skill won favor with Empress Dowager Wang.

entries.zh: 太后問：「有子、兄弟為官者乎？」
entries.en: The empress dowager asked: "Do you have sons or brothers serving as officials?"
entries.literal: The empress dowager asked: "Do you have sons or brothers serving as officials?"

entries.zh: 姊曰：「有弟無行，不可。」
entries.en: The woman answered, "I have a younger brother, but his conduct is poor—he would not do."
entries.literal: The sister said: "I have a younger brother, but he lacks good conduct—not acceptable."

entries.zh: 太后乃告上，上拜義姁弟縱為中郎，補上黨郡中令。
entries.en: The dowager then informed the emperor, who appointed Yi Xu's younger brother, Yi Zong, as a gentleman of the palace and posted him as interior chief of Shangdang.
entries.literal: The empress dowager then informed the sovereign, who appointed Yi Xu's younger brother, Yi Zong, as a gentleman of the palace and posted him as interior chief of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 治敢往，少溫籍，縣無逋事，舉第一。
entries.en: He governed boldly if bluntly, cleared every backlog, and topped the merit list.
entries.literal: In governance he dared press forward, showed little mild courtesy; the county had no backlog—raised first in rank.

entries.zh: 遷為長陵及長安令，直法行治，不避貴戚。
entries.en: Promoted to magistrate of Changling and then Chang'an, he enforced the code without fear of powerful connections.
entries.literal: Promoted chief of Changling and chief of Chang'an—straight law and enforcement, did not avoid noble affines.

entries.zh: 以捕按太后外孫脩成子中，上以為能，遷為河內都尉。
entries.en: His arrest and investigation of Zhong, a maternal grandson of the empress dowager, impressed the throne, and he became military governor of Henei.
entries.literal: By arresting and investigating Zhong, a maternal grandson of the empress dowager, the sovereign deemed him capable and promoted him to commandant of Henei.

entries.zh: 至則族滅其豪穰氏之屬，河內道不拾遺。
entries.en: He wiped out the predatory Rang lineage; afterward lost goods lay untouched throughout the commandery.
entries.literal: On arrival he exterminated the powerful Rang clan and their kind—within the commandery none picked up lost articles on the road.

entries.zh: 而張次公亦為郎，以勇悍從軍，敢深入，有功，封為岸頭侯。
entries.en: Zhang Cigong too entered the gentleman corps, fought with conspicuous daring, and was made marquis of Antou.
entries.literal: Zhang Cigong also became a gentleman; by fierce bravery he followed the army, dared deep penetration, earned merit, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Antou.

entries.zh: 上聞之，以為能，遷為中尉。
entries.en: Impressed, the emperor made him commandant of the guard.
entries.literal: The sovereign heard, deemed him capable, and promoted metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 其治復放河內，徒請召猜禍吏與從事，河內則楊皆、麻戊，關中揚贛、成信等。
entries.en: He imported Henei's poisoners—Yang Jie and Ma Wu—and paired them with Guanzhong bullies such as Yang Gan and Cheng Xin.
entries.literal: His rule again imitated Henei: he summoned clerks given to suspicion and destruction, including Yang Jie and Ma Wu from Henei and Yang Gan and Cheng Xin from Guanzhong.

entries.zh: 義縱為內史，憚之，未敢恣治。
entries.en: Privy treasurer Yi Zong kept clear of him.
entries.literal: Yi Zong as privy treasurer feared him and dared not govern wilfully.

entries.zh: 及縱死，張湯敗後，徙為廷尉。
entries.en: Once Yi Zong and Zhang Tang were gone he rose to commandant of justice.
entries.literal: After Zong died and Zhang Tang fell he shifted to commandant of justice.

entries.zh: 而尹齊為中尉坐法抵罪，溫舒復為中尉。
entries.en: Yin Qi's conviction cleared the way for Wang Wenshu's second stint as commandant.
entries.literal: When Yin Qi as metropolitan commandant met conviction under law, Wenshu returned as metropolitan commandant.

entries.zh: 為人少文，居它惛惛不辯，至於中尉則心開。
entries.en: Unpolished and tongue-tied in lesser posts, he turned sharp once made metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: As a man he had little literary polish; in other offices he seemed dull and inarticulate, but as metropolitan commandant his mind opened.

entries.zh: 素習關中俗，知豪惡吏，豪惡吏盡復為用。
entries.en: He knew Guanzhong's corrupt clerks intimately and reemployed every one.
entries.literal: Long versed in Guanzhong ways—he knew every vicious clerk—and put them all back to work.

entries.zh: 吏苛察淫惡少年，投缿購告言奸，置伯落長以收司奸。
entries.en: They shook down rowdies, offered bounties through sealed accusation boxes, and stationed street captains to spy.
entries.literal: Clerks harshly screened dissolute youths—posted denunciation urns offering rewards for informing—and set bailuo chiefs to sniff out crime.

entries.zh: 溫舒多諂，善事有勢者；
entries.en: Wang Wenshu curried favor with anyone influential;
entries.literal: Wenshu flattered constantly—clever at serving the powerful;

entries.zh: 即無勢，視之如奴。
entries.en: the powerless he handled like bondservants.
entries.literal: if powerless—he treated them like slaves.

entries.zh: 有勢家，雖有奸如山，弗犯；
entries.en: Connected houses—even guilt mountain-high—went untouched;
entries.literal: Where families had pull—even guilt piled high as mountains—he did not touch;

entries.zh: 無勢，雖貴戚，必侵辱。
entries.en: the friendless—even royal in-laws—he trampled.
entries.literal: without pull—even imperial affines—he necessarily crushed and humiliated.

entries.zh: 舞文巧，請下戶之猾，以動大豪。
entries.en: He warped indictments to hook small fry and panic grandees.
entries.literal: He twisted documents craftily—netted petty sharpers—to frighten great magnates.

entries.zh: 其治中尉如此。
entries.en: Such was his tenure as commandant.
entries.literal: Such was his metropolitan command.

entries.zh: 奸猾窮治，大氐盡靡爛獄中，行論無出者。
entries.en: Suspects rarely left prison except as corpses.
entries.literal: The crafty were hunted to ruin—most rotted in jail—sentenced without leaving alive.

entries.zh: 其爪牙吏虎而冠。
entries.en: His enforcers were tigers wearing official hats.
entries.literal: His claw clerks were tigers in caps.

entries.zh: 於是中尉部中中猾以下皆伏，有勢者為游聲譽，稱治。
entries.en: Petty crooks vanished while the connected purchased praise for "good order."
entries.literal: Then within the commandant's jurisdiction middling villains downward all submitted—those with influence bought glowing reputations—praised as well governed.

entries.zh: 數歲，其吏多以權貴富。
entries.en: Within years his staff grew wealthy peddling influence.
entries.literal: Within several years many of his clerks grew rich on connections.

entries.zh: 上以廣明連禽大奸，征入為大鴻臚，擢廣明兄雲中代為淮陽太守。
entries.en: For crushing major plots he entered the capital as grand herald while his brother governed Huaiyang.
entries.literal: Because Guangming had repeatedly captured major criminals, the sovereign summoned him to serve as grand herald and promoted Yunzhong, Guangming's elder brother, to replace him as grand administrator of Huaiyang.

entries.zh: 昭帝時，廣明將兵擊益州，還，賜爵關內侯，徙衛尉。
entries.en: Under Emperor Zhao he campaigned in Yizhou, earned a marquisette, and became guard commandant.
entries.literal: In Emperor Zhao's time Guangming led troops striking Yizhou—returned—granted noble rank marquis within passes—transferred guard commandant.

entries.zh: 後出為左馮翊，治有能名。
entries.en: Later he governed Zuo Fengyi with a reputation for competence.
entries.literal: Later went out as Zuo Fengyi—governance had capable name.

entries.zh: 宣帝初立，代蔡義為御史大夫，以前為馮翊與議定策，封昌水侯。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan named him imperial clerk for aiding the succession and created him marquis of Changshui.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan first rose—replaced Cai Yi as imperial clerk—because earlier as Fengyi participated settling succession policy—enfeoffed Changshui marquis.

entries.zh: 歲餘，以祁連將軍將兵擊匈奴，出塞至受降城。
entries.en: As Qilian general he marched to Accept Surrender City beyond the wall.
entries.literal: After slightly more than year—as Qilian general led troops striking Xiongnu—exited frontier reaching Surrender Accept city.

entries.zh: 受降都尉前死，喪柩在堂，廣明召其寡妻與奸。
entries.en: He seduced the widow of the late surrender commandant while her husband's coffin still lay in state.
entries.literal: Surrender Accept commandant died earlier—mourning coffin in hall—Guangming summoned his widow and committed adultery.

entries.zh: 既出不至質，引軍空還。
entries.en: He halted short of the hostage exchange and marched home empty-handed.
entries.literal: Already exited—not reaching hostage rendezvous—led army empty return.

entries.zh: 下太僕杜延年簿責，廣明自殺闕下，國除。
entries.en: Grand Coachman Du Yannian's audit drove him to suicide at the palace stairs and forfeiture of his fief.
entries.literal: Ordered Grand Coachman Du Yannian register reprimand—Guangming killed himself below palace gate—state abolished.

entries.zh: 兄雲中為淮陽守，亦敢誅殺，吏民守闕告之，竟坐棄市。
entries.en: His elder brother Yunzhong, another bloody governor of Huaiyang, fell to petitions at the palace gate and died in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Elder brother Yunnan as Huaiyang guard—also dared execute kill—clerks and people guarded palace gate reporting—finally sentenced exposed market.

entries.zh: 田延年字子賓，先齊諸田也，徙陽陵。
entries.en: Tian Yannian, courtesy name Zibin, came from the Qi Tian clan and moved to Yangling.
entries.literal: Tian Yannian styled Zibin was originally of the Tian clan of Qi and relocated to Yangling.

entries.zh: 延年以材略給事大將軍莫府，霍光重之，遷為長史。
entries.en: By ability he served on Huo Guang's staff, won his trust, and rose to chief clerk.
entries.literal: Yannian by talent and strategy served in the Grand General's staff office; Huo Guang valued him and promoted him to chief clerk.

entries.zh: 出為河東太守，選拔尹翁歸等以為爪牙，誅鉏豪彊，姦邪不敢發。
entries.en: As Hedong governor he recruited Yin Wenggui among his enforcers, crushed local magnates, and silenced corruption.
entries.literal: Sent out as Hedong grand administrator, he selected Yin Wenggui and others as enforcers, executed and uprooted powerful bullies, and the wicked dared not arise.

entries.zh: 以選入為大司農。
entries.en: Selected for court, he became Excellency of Agriculture.
entries.literal: By selection he entered office as Excellency of Agriculture.

entries.zh: 會昭帝崩，昌邑王嗣位，淫亂，霍將軍憂懼，與公卿議廢之，莫敢發言。
entries.en: At Emperor Zhao's death the licentious Prince of Changyi took the throne; Huo Guang consulted ministers about deposing him, but none dared speak up.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhao died, the Prince of Changyi succeeded and behaved licentiously; General Huo grew anxious and fearful and consulted with the chief ministers about deposing him, but none dared speak.

entries.zh: 延年按劍，延叱群臣，即日議決，語在光傳。
entries.en: Drawing his sword, Yannian rebuked the assembled ministers until they resolved the matter that day; details appear in Huo Guang's biography.
entries.literal: Yannian grasped his sword and shouted down the officials; that very day the deliberation was settled—as told in Huo Guang's biography.

entries.zh: 宣帝即位，延年以決疑定策封陽成侯。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan enfeoffed him as Marquis of Yangcheng for his decisive role in the succession crisis.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Yannian for resolving doubts and fixing the plan was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangcheng.

entries.zh: 嚴延年字次卿，東海下邳人也。
entries.en: Yan Yannian, courtesy name Ciqing, came from Xiapi in Donghai.
entries.literal: Yan Yannian styled Ciqing—was a man of Xiapi in Donghai.

entries.zh: 其父為丞相掾，延年少學法律丞相府，歸為郡吏。
entries.en: His father served the chancellor; he studied law there and became a county clerk.
entries.literal: His father was chancellor clerk—Yannian youth studied law in chancellor bureau—returned county clerk.

entries.zh: 以選除補御史掾，舉侍御史。
entries.en: Selection moved him to the censorate and promotion made him attendant censor.
entries.literal: By selection removed supplemented clerk to censor—raised attendant censor.

entries.zh: 是時，大將軍霍光廢昌邑王，尊立宣帝。
entries.en: At that time Grand General Huo Guang deposed Prince He of Changyi and enthroned Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: At this time Grand General Huo Guang deposed the Prince of Changyi and installed Emperor Xuan.

entries.zh: 宣帝初即位，延年劾奏光「擅廢立主，無人臣禮，不道」。
entries.en: At the beginning of Emperor Xuan's reign, Yan Yannian impeached Huo Guang, charging him with "arbitrarily deposing and enthroning rulers, lacking the propriety of a minister, and acting impiously."
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan first ascended—Yannian impeachment memorial Huo Guang "arbitrarily deposing enthroning lord—lacking minister ritual—not Way".

entries.zh: 奏雖寢，然朝廷肅焉敬憚。
entries.en: The memorial died in committee, yet the court stood in awe.
entries.literal: Memorial though shelved—yet court soberly respected feared.

entries.zh: 延年後復劾大司農田延年持兵干屬車，大司農自訟不干屬車。
entries.en: He later charged Tian Yannian with brandishing arms near the imperial escort—countered by Tian's denial.
entries.literal: Yannian later again impeached Excellency of Agriculture Tian Yannian bearing weapons interfering escort carriage—Excellency of Agriculture self-litigated not interfering escort carriage.

entries.zh: 事下御史中丞，譴責延年何以不移書宮殿門禁止大司農，而令得出入宮。
entries.en: The vice-censor rebuked Yan for failing to seal the palace gate against the minister.
entries.literal: Affair sent palace clerk—reprimanded Yannian why not transfer document palace gate forbidding Excellency of Agriculture—allowing coming going palace.

entries.zh: 於是復劾延年闌內罪人，法至死。
entries.en: Yan Yannian was then himself impeached for admitting a criminal inside the gate—a capital offense.
entries.literal: Thereupon again impeached Yannian bursting gate inner criminal—law reaching death.

entries.zh: 延年亡命。
entries.en: Yan Yannian fled.
entries.literal: Yannian fled life.

entries.zh: 會赦出，丞相、御史府征書同日到，延年以御史書先至，詣御史府，復為掾。
entries.en: Amnesty brought him back; competing summonses sent him first to the censorate as clerk.
entries.literal: Met amnesty released—chancellor and censor offices summons arrived same day—Yannian because censor document arrived first—went censor bureau—again clerk.

entries.zh: 宣帝識之，拜為平陵令，坐殺不辜，去官。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan knew him and named him magistrate of Pingling until wrongful executions cost him the post.
entries.literal: Emperor Xuan recognized him—appointed Pingling chief—sat killing innocents—removed office.

entries.zh: 後為丞相掾，復擢好畤令。
entries.en: He returned as chancellor clerk and rose to magistrate of Haozhi.
entries.literal: Later chancellor clerk—again promoted Haozhi chief.

entries.zh: 神爵中，西羌反，強弩將軍許延壽請延年為長史，從軍敗西羌，還為涿郡太守。
entries.en: During the Qiang wars he served Xu Yanshou as chief clerk, helped smash the tribes, and became governor of Zhuo.
entries.literal: In Shenjue era Western Qiang rebelled—Strong Crossbow General Xu Yanshou requested Yannian as chief clerk—followed army defeating Western Qiang—returned Zhuo grand administrator.

entries.zh: 卷九十 酷吏傳第六十
entries.en: Volume 90: Biographies of Harsh Officials (60).
entries.literal: Volume 90: Biographies of Cruel Officials, Number 60.

entries.zh: 子贛既學於仲尼，退而仕衛，發貯鬻財曹、魯之間。
entries.en: After studying with Confucius, Zigong left to serve Wei and made a fortune buying cheap and selling dear between Cao and Lu.
entries.literal: Zigong having studied with Zhongni, retired and took office in Wei, released stored goods and sold wealth between Cao and Lu.

entries.zh: 七十子之徒，賜最為饒，而顏淵簞食瓢飲，在於陋巷。
entries.en: Of the Master's seventy followers, Zigong alone grew truly rich, while Yan Hui lived on a bowl of grain and a dipper of water down a shabby alley.
entries.literal: Among the disciples of the seventy, Ci (Zigong) was the most abundant, while Yan Yuan had a basket of food and gourd of drink, dwelling in a mean lane.

entries.zh: 子贛結駟連騎，束帛之幣聘享諸侯，所至，國君無不分庭與之抗禮。
entries.en: Zigong rolled up to court in matched chariots, bearing silk gifts for every prince he called on, and each ruler stepped down to the courtyard to greet him as an equal.
entries.literal: Zigong yoked four-horse teams in linked processions; with bundles of silk as currency he visited and feasted the feudal lords; wherever he arrived, the rulers of states without exception divided the courtyard and matched him with opposing courtesy.

entries.zh: 然孔子賢顏淵而譏子贛，曰：「回也其庶乎，屢空。
entries.en: Yet the Master praised Yan Hui and chided Zigong, saying, "Hui is close to perfection, yet he is repeatedly in want.
entries.literal: Yet Confucius deemed Yan Yuan worthy and ridiculed Zigong, saying: "Hui—is he not close to it? Yet repeatedly empty.

entries.zh: 賜不受命，而貨殖焉，意則屢中。」
entries.en: Zigong will not accept his allotted lot, but instead multiplies wealth—and his market calls are uncannily right."
entries.literal: Ci does not accept what is allotted to him, but engages in multiplying wealth; his conjectures repeatedly hit the mark."

entries.zh: 白圭，周人也。
entries.en: Bai Gui came from the Zhou heartland.
entries.literal: Bai Gui was a man of Zhou.

entries.zh: 當魏文侯時，李克務盡地力，而白圭樂觀時變，故人棄我取，人取我予。
entries.en: Under Marquis Wen of Wei, Li Ke worked every field for its utmost yield, while Bai Gui thrived on contrarian timing—buying what the market dumped and selling into every rush.
entries.literal: When Marquis Wen of Wei was on the throne, Li Ke devoted himself to exhausting the productive power of the land, while Bai Gui delighted in observing how the times shifted; therefore when others cast goods aside he took them, when others seized goods he supplied them.

entries.zh: 能薄飲食，忍嗜欲，節衣服，與用事僮僕同苦樂，趨時若猛獸摯鳥之發。
entries.en: He ate plainly, smothered appetite, dressed simply, sweated beside his foremen, and when a window opened he struck as fast as a hawk stooping on prey.
entries.literal: Able to thin his drink and food, endure appetites and desires, restrain clothing, share hardship and joy with the household servants who managed affairs, rushing the moment like the release of fierce beasts and clutching birds.

entries.zh: 故曰：「吾治生猶伊尹、呂尚之謀，孫、吳用兵，商鞅行法是也。
entries.en: He liked to say, "Building a fortune takes the cunning of Yi Yin or Lü Wang, the timing of Sun and Wu in using troops, and the ruthlessness of Shang Yang's code.
entries.literal: Therefore he said: "In managing my livelihood it is like the schemes of Yi Yin and Lü Shang, Sun and Wu's use of troops, Shang Yang's carrying out of laws.

entries.zh: 故智不足與權變，勇不足以決斷，仁不能以取予，強不能以有守，雖欲學吾術，終不告也。」
