entries.en: Imperial fortune, in short, demands luminous virtue and piled-up achievements before the spirits answer and the people rally; no one seizes the dragon throne from thin air with neither merit nor mandate.
entries.literal: From this it may be said that the blessing of emperors and kings must rest on manifest sagely and brilliant virtue, on enterprises of abundant merit and thick benefit piled up layer upon layer; only then does essential sincerity penetrate the spirits, flowing favor reaches the living people, and therefore they can be blessed and feasted by ghosts and gods and be the object to which all under Heaven turns; one has never seen a ruler without root in the age's fortune, without recorded merit and virtue, who could yet vault up and occupy this position.

entries.zh: 世俗見高祖興於布衣，不達其故，以為適遭暴亂，得奮其劍，游說之士至比天下於逐鹿，幸捷而得之，不知神器有命，不可以智力求也。
entries.en: Common opinion mistakes Gaozu for a lucky swordsman who grabbed power in chaos, the "deer hunt" cliché of rhetoricians; they miss that the sacred vessel answers only to fate, not to cunning or muscle.
entries.literal: The vulgar world, seeing the Founding Ancestor rise from common cloth and not penetrating the reason, thinks he simply met violent disorder, was able to brandish his sword, and that wandering persuaders liken all under Heaven to chasing a deer, getting it by a lucky grab; they do not know that the divine regalia have a destined possessor and cannot be sought by wit or force.

entries.zh: 悲夫！
entries.en: A bitter pity.
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 此世所以多亂臣賊子者也。
entries.en: That blindness is why treason and usurpation multiply.
entries.literal: This is why the age has so many traitorous ministers and rebellious sons.

entries.zh: 若然者，豈徒闇於天道哉？
entries.en: If that were the whole story, would the fault lie only in misunderstanding Heaven?
entries.literal: If it is so, is it only darkness about the Way of Heaven?

entries.zh: 又不睹之於人事矣！
entries.en: They have not even looked at the evidence of human affairs.
entries.literal: They have also failed to observe it in human affairs!

entries.zh: 蓋在高祖，其興也有五：一曰帝堯之苗裔，二曰體貌多奇異，三曰神武有徵應，四曰寬明而仁恕，五曰知人善任使。
entries.en: Gaozu's ascent rested on five signs: Yao's bloodline, a singular physique, omens that blessed his arms, a generous humane temper, and a gift for placing the right men.
entries.literal: As for the Founding Ancestor, there were five reasons for his rise: first, he was a descendant of Emperor Yao; second, his body and appearance held many marvels; third, his divine martial prowess had confirming omens; fourth, he was lenient, enlightened, humane, and forgiving; fifth, he knew men and employed them well.

entries.zh: 加之以信誠好謀，達於聽受，見善如不及，用人如由己，從諫如順流，趣時如嚮赴；
entries.en: He was candid, loved strategy, listened well, chased every good counsel, handed offices as freely as if they were his own limbs, took advice like running water, and seized each moment as though answering a call;
entries.literal: Add to this that he was trustworthy, sincere, fond of planning, open in hearing and accepting counsel; he saw good as if he could not catch up, employed men as if using himself, followed remonstrance like going with the current, and hastened to the timely moment as if answering a summons;

entries.zh: 當食吐哺，納子房之策；
entries.en: he spat out a mouthful mid-meal to enact Zhang Liang's scheme;
entries.literal: when it was time to eat he spat out the food in his mouth, adopting Zifang's plan;

entries.zh: 拔足揮洗，揖酈生之說；
entries.en: he broke off his bath to salute Li Yiji's plea;
entries.literal: he stopped washing his feet and received Lisheng's proposal with a bow;

entries.zh: 寤戍卒之言，斷懷土之情；
entries.en: he heeded a guardsman's plea and checked his homesick march;
entries.literal: he awoke to the words of garrison soldiers and cut short his longing for native soil;

entries.zh: 高四皓之名，割肌膚之愛；
entries.en: he courted the Four Elders though it cost him a father's love;
entries.literal: he prized the fame of the Four Hoary Ones and sliced flesh-close affection;

entries.zh: 舉韓信於行陳，收陳平於亡命，英雄陳力，群策畢舉：此高祖之大略，所以成帝業也。
entries.en: He pulled Han Xin from the ranks, rescued Chen Ping from flight, and let every able man lend strength until the imperial work was done.
entries.literal: he raised Han Xin from the ranks of battle and gathered Chen Ping from life as a fugitive; heroes deployed their strength, every stratagem was offered: this was the Founding Ancestor's grand design whereby he completed the imperial enterprise.

entries.zh: 若乃靈瑞符應，又可略聞矣。
entries.en: The portents that marked him deserve a word as well.
entries.literal: As for numinous omens and confirming tokens, one may also hear them in outline.

entries.zh: 初劉媼任高祖而夢與神遇，震電晦冥，有龍蛇之怪。
entries.en: Lady Liu dreamed of a spirit when she conceived him; thunder rolled in black sky and dragon shapes writhed.
entries.literal: At first, when the elder Liu was pregnant with the Founding Ancestor, she dreamed of meeting a spirit; lightning flashed and the darkness was murky, with prodigies of dragons and serpents.

entries.zh: 及其長而多靈，有異於眾，是以王、武感物而折券，呂公睹形而進女；
entries.en: As he matured, uncanny signs set him apart, so Wang and Wu tore up old debts at a glance and Lü Gong married him a daughter for his bearing;
entries.literal: When he grew and showed many spiritual signs, different from the multitude, therefore Wang and Wu were moved by things and tore their bonds, and Duke Lü, seeing his form, advanced his daughter;

entries.zh: 秦皇東游以厭其氣，呂后望雲而知所處；
entries.en: the Qin First Emperor toured east to smother his qi, while Empress Lü read clouds to find him;
entries.literal: the First Emperor of Qin toured east to suppress his aura, and Empress Lü watched clouds to know where he dwelt;

entries.zh: 始受命則白蛇分，西入關則五星聚。
entries.en: His first mandate split the white serpent, and the five planets clustered when he entered the passes.
entries.literal: when he first received the mandate the white serpent was cleft; when he entered Guan in the west the five planets gathered.

entries.zh: 故淮陰、留侯謂之天授，非人力也。
entries.en: Han Xin and Zhang Liang called such things Heaven's investiture, not mortal striving.
entries.literal: Therefore the Marquis of Huaiyin and the Marquis of Liu called it Heaven's gift, not human power.

entries.zh: 當秦之末，豪桀共推陳嬰而王之，嬰母止之曰：「自吾為子家婦，而世貧賤，卒富貴不祥，不如以兵屬人，事成少受其利，不成禍有所歸。」
entries.en: At the end of Qin, local strongmen together urged Chen Ying to accept the title of king. His mother stopped him, saying, "Ever since I became a daughter-in-law in your family, we have been poor and lowly for generations. Sudden wealth and honor would be inauspicious. Better to place the troops under someone else: if the undertaking succeeds, you will receive a small share of the benefit; if it fails, the disaster will fall elsewhere."
entries.literal: At the end of Qin, the bold men together urged Chen Ying to take the kingly title; Ying's mother stopped him, saying, "Ever since I became your family's daughter-in-law, generation after generation we have been poor and base; to end in wealth and honor is inauspicious; better to hand the troops to another—if the affair succeeds you will receive a little benefit; if it fails disaster will have somewhere to go."

entries.zh: 嬰從其言，而陳氏以寧。
entries.en: Chen Ying obeyed, and his house survived the wars unscathed.
entries.literal: Ying followed her words, and the Chen clan thereby enjoyed peace.

entries.zh: 王陵之母亦見項氏之必亡，而劉氏之將興也。
entries.en: Wang Ling's mother likewise saw that the Xiang clan would fall and the Liu house would rise.
entries.literal: The mother of Wang Ling also saw that the Xiang clan was sure to perish and the Liu house was about to rise.

entries.zh: 是時陵為漢將，而母獲於楚，有漢使來，陵母見之，謂曰：「願告吾子，漢王長者，必得天下，子謹事之，無有二心。」
entries.en: While Wang Ling served Han, his mother was held by Chu; meeting a Han envoy, she said to him, "I beg you tell my son: the King of Han is a man of generous nature and is sure to gain all under Heaven; let him serve him carefully and harbor no second heart."
entries.literal: At that time Ling was a Han general, but his mother had been taken by Chu; when a Han envoy arrived, Ling's mother saw him and said to him, "I beg you tell my son: the King of Han is a man of generous nature and is sure to gain all under Heaven; let him serve him carefully and harbor no second heart.

entries.zh: 遂對漢使伏劍而死，以固勉陵。
entries.en: She then drew a blade before the envoy and fell dead to steel her son's resolve.
entries.literal: She thereupon fell on a sword before the Han envoy and died, thereby to firm Ling's resolve.

entries.zh: 其後果定於漢，陵為宰相封侯。
entries.en: Han triumphed, Wang Ling rose to chancellor, and ennoblement followed.
entries.literal: Afterward it was indeed settled with Han, and Ling became chancellor and was enfeoffed as marquis.

entries.zh: 夫以匹婦之明，猶能推事理之致，探禍福之機，而全宗祀於無窮，垂策書於春秋，而況大丈夫之事虖！
entries.en: If a woman's wit could read fate, save her lineage, and earn a line in the annals, how much more should a grown man grasp the mandate!
entries.literal: If by the insight of a mere woman one can still push principle to its limit, probe the pivot of fortune and disaster, and preserve the ancestral sacrifices without end, leaving one's plan in the Spring and Autumn Annals, how much more the affairs of a great husband!

entries.zh: 是故窮達有命，吉凶由人，嬰母知廢，陵母知興，審此四者，帝王之分決矣。
entries.en: Fortune governs rise and fall, yet human choice steers blessing or curse; Chen's mother knew whom to quit, Wang's mother knew whom to back, and those four judgments settle who may be king.
entries.literal: Therefore failure and success have their allotted fate, good and ill come from men; Ying's mother knew what to abolish, Ling's mother knew what would rise; when these four points are examined, the portion of emperors and kings is decided.

entries.zh: 承靈訓其虛徐兮，竚盤桓而且俟，惟天墬之無窮兮，鱻生民之脢在。
entries.en: I hold the spirit's slow counsel and linger, knowing heaven and earth are endless while new generations crowd the world.
entries.literal: I receive the spirit's lesson, slow and lingering; I stand turning, yet I wait; only Heaven and earth are without end; fresh are the teeming common people who dwell therein.

entries.zh: 紛屯亶與蹇連兮，何艱多而智寡！
entries.en: Obstacles tangle, troubles multiply, yet wisdom stays scarce.
entries.literal: Tangled are obstruction and difficulty, blocked paths and hard straits; why are hardships many and wisdom few!

entries.zh: 上聖寤而後拔兮，豈群黎之所御！
entries.en: Only the greatest sage awakens and escapes; the mob cannot steer that fate.
entries.literal: The highest sage awakens and then is lifted out; how could the mass of commoners control that!

entries.zh: 昔衛叔之御昆兮，昆為寇而喪予。
entries.en: Shu Wu once guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.
entries.literal: Formerly Shu Wu guarded Wei for his elder brother, yet was slain as an enemy when that brother returned.

entries.zh: 管彎弧欲斃讎兮，讎作后而成己。
entries.en: Guan Zhong drew a bow to slay his enemy, only to see that enemy become lord and finish his own rise.
entries.literal: Guan bent his bow intending to kill his foe, yet the foe became ruler and completed himself.

entries.zh: 變化故而相詭兮，孰云豫其終始！
entries.en: Fortunes shift and mock foresight; no one reads the end from the beginning.
entries.literal: Things change their grounds and deceive one another; who says you can know the end from the start!

entries.zh: 雍造怨而先賞兮，丁繇惠而被戮；
entries.en: Some nursed grudge yet won first reward, others earned favor yet died;
entries.literal: Yong nursed resentment yet was rewarded first; Ding received favor yet was executed;

entries.zh: 㮚取弔于逌吉兮，王膺慶於所慼。
entries.en: Li asked for blessing from distant luck, Wang found joy in what had frightened him.
entries.literal: Li sought condolence in far-off good fortune; Wang met celebration in what he had dreaded.

entries.zh: 畔回宂其若茲兮，北叟頗識其倚伏。
entries.en: Twists like these taught the northern elder how gain and loss lean on each other.
entries.literal: Turning and returning are thus; the old man of the north somewhat knew their leaning and resting.

entries.zh: 單治裏而外凋兮，張修襮而內逼，欥中龢為庶幾兮，顏與冉又不得。
entries.en: Shan lost vigor though he ruled a lane, Zhang shone outward yet felt inner pinch; I aimed at the golden mean like the rare few, yet even Yan and Ran missed it.
entries.literal: Shan governed the hamlet yet withered outward; Zhang spread his robe yet was pressed inward; I hoped to hit the mean like a few; yet Yan and Ran again could not attain it.

entries.zh: 溺招路以從己兮，謂孔氏猶未可，安慆慆而不萉兮，卒隕身虖世禍。
entries.en: Jie Ni invited Zilu to follow him, dismissing Confucius as still unworthy; Zilu would not withdraw from the world's turmoil, and in the end it cost him his life.
entries.literal: Ni lured the road to follow himself and said Confucius was still not acceptable; how could he be tranquil and not weary; in the end he fell body into the age's disaster.

entries.zh: 游聖門而靡救兮，顧覆醢其何補？
entries.en: He haunted the Master's school yet found no rescue; when the pickle jar spilled, what good was hindsight?
entries.literal: He roamed the sage's gate yet found no rescue; looking back at the overturned pickle, what could it mend?

entries.zh: 固行行其必凶兮，免盜亂為賴道；
entries.en: Rigid uprightness courts disaster; only shunning chaos is a trustworthy path;
entries.literal: To be stubbornly upright is sure to meet ill; only avoiding robbery and chaos counts as relying on the Way;

entries.zh: 形氣發于根柢兮，柯葉彙而靈茂。
entries.en: Form and breath rise from the root while branches grow thick with spirit.
entries.literal: form and vapor issue from the root; branches and leaves gather in numinous luxuriance.

entries.zh: 恐网蜽之責景兮，慶未得其云已。
entries.en: I fear the mantis scolding its shadow; good fortune has hardly begun to speak.
entries.literal: I fear the mantis reproaches the shadow; the blessing is not yet done with speaking.

entries.zh: 永平中為郎，典校祕書，專篤志於博學，以著述為業。
entries.en: Under Yongping he entered as a court gentleman, supervised collation of the palace library, gave himself wholly to learning, and took writing for his life's work.
entries.literal: In the Yongping years he became a gentleman-attendant, collated the secretariat books, devoted himself single-mindedly to wide learning, and made authorship his occupation.

entries.zh: 或譏以無功，又感東方朔、揚雄自諭以不遭蘇、張、范、蔡之時，曾不折之以正道，明君子之所守，故聊復應焉。
entries.en: Critics mocked his want of deeds; remembering how Dongfang Shuo and Yang Xiong excused their obscurity by the absence of Su or Zhang, yet never rebuked opportunism with the true Way, he felt compelled to answer.
entries.literal: Some ridiculed him for lacking achievement; he was also moved that Dongfang Shuo and Yang Xiong, explaining themselves as having missed the age of Su Qin, Zhang Yi, Fan Ju, and Cai Ze, had not refuted this with the correct Way or clarified what the gentleman guards; therefore he briefly answered in turn.

entries.zh: 其辭曰：
entries.en: The piece opens:
entries.literal: Its words say:

entries.zh: 主人曰：「何為其然也！
entries.en: The host answered, "Why imagine such a thing?
entries.literal: The host said, "Why should it be so?

entries.zh: 昔咎繇謨虞，箕子訪周，言通帝王，謀合聖神；
entries.en: Gao Yao advised Shun, Jizi counseled Zhou—their speech reached kings, their plans matched the spirits;
entries.literal: Formerly Gao Yao counseled Shun, Jizi was questioned in Zhou—their words penetrated emperors and kings, their plans matched sages and spirits;

entries.zh: 殷說夢發於傅巖，周望兆動於渭濱，齊甯激聲於康衢，漢良受書於邳沂，皆俟命而神交，匪詞言之所信，故能建必然之策，展無窮之勳也。
entries.en: Fu Yue was revealed in a dream at Fuyan; Lü Wang's omen stirred on the banks of the Wei; Ning Qi's song rang out at the crossroads; and Zhang Liang received the book at the bridge at Xiapi. All awaited their appointed time and communed in spirit, relying on more than words; thus they could devise certain strategies and achieve immeasurable merit.
entries.literal: The dream of Yin's Fu Yue arose at Fuyan; the omen of Zhou's Lü Wang stirred on the bank of the Wei; Qi's Ning Qi raised his voice at the broad crossroads; and Han's Zhang Liang received the book at the bridge at Xiapi. All awaited their appointed time and met in spirit, not through trust in spoken words; therefore they could establish certain strategies and unfold inexhaustible merit.

entries.zh: 近者陸子優繇，新語以興；
entries.en: Lu Jia, calm and unhurried, raised the New Discourses;
entries.literal: In recent times Master Lu, leisurely and easy, raised the New Discourses to prominence;

entries.zh: 董生下帷，發藻儒林；
entries.en: Dong Zhongshu drew his curtain and lit the grove of scholars;
entries.literal: Dong Zhongshu let down his curtain and sent brilliance through the Confucian grove;

entries.zh: 劉向司籍，辯章舊聞；
entries.en: Liu Xiang ordered the archives and clarified antiquity;
entries.literal: Liu Xiang superintended the registers and sorted the old hearsay;

entries.zh: 揚雄覃思，法言、大玄：皆及時君之門闈，究先聖之壼奧，婆娑虖術藝之場，休息虖篇籍之囿，以全其質而發其文，用納虖聖聽，列炳於後人，斯非其亞與！
entries.en: Yang Xiong brooded out the Model Sayings and Great Arcana; each entered the ruler's gate, sounded the sages' chambers, ranged the field of learning, and left texts that shine for posterity—second only to the greatest.
entries.literal: Yang Xiong pondered deeply and produced the Model Sayings and the Great Mystery: all reached the inner gates of the timely ruler, fathomed the inner rooms of former sages, wandered in the arena of arts, rested in the park of writings, thereby preserving their substance and releasing their pattern, were taken into the sage's hearing, and blaze in rows for later men—are these not next after the highest?

entries.zh: 若乃夷抗行於首陽，惠降志於辱仕，顏耽樂於簞瓢，孔終篇於西狩，聲盈塞於天淵，真吾徒之師表也。
entries.en: Then there were Boyi, who upheld his conduct on Mount Shouyang; Liuxia Hui, who humbled his aspirations to take a dishonorable post; Yan Hui, who delighted in his basket of rice and gourd of water; and Confucius, who brought his classic to an end with the hunt in the west. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are truly exemplars for men such as us.
entries.literal: Or again, Boyi upheld his conduct on Shouyang; Liuxia Hui lowered his aspirations to accept a humiliating post; Yan Hui delighted in a basket of rice and a gourd of water; and Confucius ended his classic with the western hunt. Their fame fills the space between heaven and the abyss; they are true models for men such as us.

entries.zh: 且吾聞之：壹陰壹陽，天墬之方；
entries.en: I have heard that yin and yang are the square of heaven and earth;
entries.literal: Moreover I have heard: one yin, one yang—this is Heaven and earth's square;

entries.zh: 乃文乃質，王道之綱；
entries.en: culture and substance are the twin cords of the kingly Way;
entries.literal: both pattern and substance—this is the kingly Way's cord;

entries.zh: 有同有異，聖喆之常。
entries.en: sameness and difference are the sage's constant scales.
entries.literal: having sameness and having difference—this is the constant of the wise and good.

entries.zh: 故曰：慎修所志，守爾天符，委命共己，味道之腴，神之聽之，名其舍諸！
entries.en: The ode says: polish your purpose, keep Heaven's tally, yield life to what is already yours, taste the Way's fat—when spirits listen, can fame stay away?
entries.literal: Therefore it is said: carefully cultivate what you aim at, guard your Heaven-given tally, entrust life to what is already in yourself, taste the richness of the Way; when the spirits listen, will fame leave you?

entries.zh: 賓又不聞龢氏之璧韞於荊石，隨侯之珠藏於蜯蛤虖？
entries.en: Have you never heard how the He-bi jade slept inside a dull rock or Sui's pearl hid in a shell?
entries.literal: Again, have you not heard that the He clan jade was wrapped in a Jing stone, or that the Marquis of Sui's pearl lay hidden in a mussel?

entries.zh: 歷世莫眡，不知其將含景耀，吐英精，曠千載而流夜光也。
entries.en: Ages passed before anyone knew they would blaze with inner fire and gleam in the dark after a thousand years.
entries.literal: Age after age none saw them, not knowing they would hold radiant light and spit essence, idle a thousand years yet shed light by night.

entries.zh: 應龍潛於潢汙，魚黿媟之，不睹其能奮靈德，合風雲，超忽荒，而躆顥蒼也。
entries.en: The winged dragon wallowed in a puddle while minnows mocked him, blind to the day he would ride the storm into the blue.
entries.literal: The responding dragon lurked in a muddy pool; fish and turtles despised him, not seeing how he could rouse numinous virtue, join wind and cloud, leap beyond the vast waste, and stand in the azure sky.

entries.zh: 故夫泥蟠而天飛者，應龍之神也；
entries.en: Mud-bound yet sky-soaring—that is the responding dragon;
entries.literal: Therefore one who coils in the mud yet flies to Heaven is the spirit of the responding dragon;

entries.zh: 先賤而後貴者，龢、隨之珍也；
entries.en: cheap at first, costly later—that is the He jade and Sui pearl;
entries.literal: one who is base first and honored later is the treasure of He and Sui;

entries.zh: 時闇而久章者，君子之真也。
entries.en: long hidden, long bright—that is the gentleman's truth.
entries.literal: one who is dim for a time yet shines long is the truth of the gentleman.

entries.zh: 若乃牙、曠清耳於管絃，離婁眇目於豪分；
entries.en: When Ya and Kuang tune their ears to music, or Li Lou splits a hair's breadth;
entries.literal: If then Ya and Kuang clear their ears to strings and pipes, and Li Lou strains his eyes to a hair's fraction;

entries.zh: 逢蒙絕技於弧矢，班輸榷巧於斧斤；
entries.en: when Peng Meng masters the bow or Lu Ban the adze;
entries.literal: Peng Meng exhausts his skill on bow and arrow, Lu Ban measures his craft on axe and adze;

entries.zh: 良樂軼能於相馭，烏獲抗力於千鈞；
entries.en: when Wang Liang and Bo Le judge horses or Wu Huo hefts a thousand jun;
entries.literal: Wang Liang and Bo Le surpass others in judging and driving, Wu Huo matches strength against a thousand jun;

entries.zh: 龢、鵲發精於鍼石，研、桑心計於無垠。
entries.en: Yi He and Bian Que mastered the needle and stone probe; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang's financial calculations knew no bounds.
entries.literal: Yi He and Bian Que brought their finest skill to needles and stone probes; Ji Yan and Sang Hongyang applied mental calculation without limit.

entries.zh: 僕亦不任廁技於彼列，故密爾自娛於斯文。」
entries.en: I am not fit to stack my small talent beside theirs, so I take quiet joy in these words alone."
entries.literal: I, your servant, am not fit to crowd my petty skill among them; therefore I quietly take my pleasure in this writing."

entries.zh: 歷古今之得失，驗行事之成敗，稽帝王之世運，考五者之所謂，取舍不厭斯位，符瑞不同斯度，而苟昧於權利，越次妄據，外不量力，內不知命，則必喪保家之主，失天年之壽，遇折足之凶，伏鈇鉞之誅。
entries.en: Review the gains and losses of past and present, test the success and failure of deeds, examine the age's fortunes of emperors and kings, and consider what is meant by the five signs. If one's choices do not fit that position and one's auspicious signs do not match that measure, yet one is blinded by power and profit, oversteps the order, and occupies it recklessly, without measuring one's strength outwardly or knowing the mandate inwardly, then one will surely lose the lord who preserves the house, forfeit the full span of life, meet the ill omen of the broken leg, and submit to execution by axe and halberd.
entries.literal: Reviewing the gains and losses of ancient and modern times, testing the success and failure of deeds done, examining the age's fortune of emperors and kings, investigating what these five mean, if in choosing and rejecting one does not shrink from this position, if auspicious tokens do not match this measure, yet one blindly covets power and profit, leaps out of order and occupies it rashly, outwardly not measuring strength, inwardly not knowing fate, then one is sure to lose the lord who could preserve the family, forfeit the years Heaven grants, meet the misfortune of broken legs, and lie under the executioner's axe and halberd.

entries.zh: 英雄誠知覺寤，畏若禍戒，超然遠覽，淵然深識，收陵、嬰之明分，絕信、布之覬覦，距逐鹿之瞽說，審神器之有授，毋貪不可幾，為二母之所咲，則福祚流于子孫，天祿其永終矣。
entries.en: Had men of ambition truly awakened to these warnings, looked far, and understood deeply; had they heeded the clear judgment shown in the stories of Wang Ling and Chen Ying, abandoned Han Xin and Ying Bu's ambitions, rejected blind talk of chasing the deer, and recognized that the imperial regalia have a destined recipient; had they not grasped at the unattainable and made themselves a laughingstock to those two mothers, then blessings would have flowed to their descendants and Heaven's bounty endured.
entries.literal: If heroes truly awaken in fear as if to omens of disaster, stand aloof with far-ranging sight, plumb the depths with silent understanding, take to heart the clear portions shown by Ling and Ying, cut off the covetous glances of Xin and Bu, reject the blind talk of deer-chasing, examine that the divine regalia have a recipient, do not greedily grasp what cannot be approached, and avoid being laughed at by the two mothers, then blessing and rank will flow to their sons and grandsons and Heaven's stipend will end only with time.

entries.zh: 登孔、顥而上下兮，緯群龍之所經，朝貞觀而夕化兮，猶諠己而遺形，若胤彭而偕老兮，訴來哲以通情。
entries.en: Climb the heights of Confucius and Yan Hui, follow the dragons' tracks, wake to the true pattern by dusk though ego still chatters, shed the shell, and if you walk with Peng Zu into age, leave a thread of feeling for sages yet unborn.
entries.literal: Ascend Confucius and Yan Hui, roam up and down; trace the paths all dragons have traveled; in the morning behold the correct model and by evening transform; though the clamor of self remains, cast off the form; if you follow Peng and grow old together, tell later wise men to convey the feeling.

entries.zh: 卷一百上 敘傳第七十上
entries.en: Hanshu, volume 100a: the afterword and family history, first installment.
entries.literal: Volume 100, Part A: Afterword and Biographical Preface, Number 70, Part A

entries.zh: 十二月庚辰，車駕乃進。
entries.en: On gengchen the column was able to move forward again.
entries.literal: On gengchen of the twelfth month, the imperial carriage then advanced.

entries.zh: 李傕等復來追戰，王師大敗，殺略宮人，少府田芬、大司農張義等皆戰歿。
entries.en: Li Jue struck again, routing the escort, slaughtering and seizing ladies of the palace; Tian Fen, Zhang Yi, and others fell in the melee.
entries.literal: Li Jue and others again came in pursuit and battle; the royal army was greatly defeated; they killed and carried off palace women; Junior Prefect Tian Fen, Grand Minister of Agriculture Zhang Yi, and others all died in battle.

entries.zh: 進幸陜，夜度河。
entries.en: The party pressed on to Shan and forded the river under cover of darkness.
entries.literal: He advanced to visit Shan and crossed the river by night.

entries.zh: 乙亥，幸安邑。
entries.en: On yihai the emperor reached Anyi.
entries.literal: On yihai, he visited Anyi.

entries.zh: 建安元年春正月癸酉，郊祀上帝於安邑，大赦天下，改元建安。
entries.en: On guiyou in the first month of the first Jian’an year the court sacrificed to Heaven at Anyi, proclaimed a general amnesty, and adopted the era name Jian’an.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jian’an, spring, first month guiyou, he sacrificed to High God at the suburban altar in Anyi, issued a great amnesty for all under Heaven, and changed the reign title to Jian’an.

entries.zh: 二月，韓暹攻衛將軍董承。
entries.en: In the second month Han Xian attacked Dong Cheng, general of the guards.
entries.literal: In the second month, Han Xian attacked General of the Guards Dong Cheng.

entries.zh: 夏六月乙未，幸聞喜。
entries.en: In the sixth month, on yiwei, the emperor visited Wenxi.
entries.literal: In summer, on yiwei in the sixth month, he visited Wenxi.

entries.zh: 孝獻皇帝諱協，靈帝中子也。
entries.en: Emperor Xiao Xian's personal name was Xie; he was the middle son of Emperor Ling.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiao Xian's personal name was Xie; he was the middle son of Emperor Ling.

entries.zh: 母王美人，為何皇后所害。
entries.en: His mother, Beauty Wang, was killed by Empress He.
entries.literal: His mother, Beauty Wang, was killed by Empress He.

entries.zh: 中平六年四月，少帝即位，封帝為勃海王，徙封陳留王。
entries.en: In the fourth month of Zhongping 6, when the Young Emperor came to the throne, Xie was enfeoffed as King of Bohai and then transferred as King of Chenliu.
entries.literal: In the fourth month of Zhongping 6, when the Young Emperor ascended the throne, the emperor was enfeoffed as King of Bohai and then transferred in enfeoffment to King of Chenliu.

entries.zh: 九月甲戌，即皇帝位，年九歲。
entries.en: On jiaxu in the ninth month the boy emperor took the throne; he was nine years old.
entries.literal: On jiaxu of the ninth month, he assumed the imperial seat, aged nine.

entries.zh: 遷皇太后於永安宮。
entries.en: The empress dowager was relocated to Yongan Palace.
entries.literal: He moved the empress dowager to Yongan Palace.

entries.zh: 大赦天下。
entries.en: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
entries.literal: He issued a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

entries.zh: 改昭寧為永漢。
entries.en: The era name was changed from Zhaoning to Yonghan.
entries.literal: He changed Zhaoning to Yonghan.

entries.zh: 丙子，董卓殺皇太后何氏。
entries.en: On bingzi Dong Zhuo had Empress Dowager He murdered.
entries.literal: On bingzi, Dong Zhuo killed Empress Dowager née He.

entries.zh: 盧芳字君期，安定三水人也，居左谷中。
entries.en: Lu Fang, styled Junqi, was from Sanshui in Anding and lived in the Zuogu valley.
entries.literal: Lu Fang, styled Junqi, was from Sanshui in Anding and lived in the Zuogu valley.

entries.zh: 《續漢志》曰三水縣有左右谷，故城在今涇州安定縣南。
entries.en: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.
entries.literal: The Treatise of the Continued Han says that Sanshui County had a Left Valley and a Right Valley; its old city lay south of present-day Anding County in Jingzhou.

entries.zh: 王莽時，天下咸思漢德，芳由是詐自稱武帝曾孫劉文伯。
entries.en: While Wang Mang held the realm, men everywhere missed the virtue of Han; Lu Fang therefore passed himself off as Liu Wenbo, a great-grandson of Emperor Wu.
entries.literal: In Wang Mang's time, all under heaven longed for Han virtue; Fang on this account falsely styled himself Emperor Wu's great-grandson Liu Wenbo.

entries.zh: 曾祖母匈奴谷蠡渾邪王之姊為武帝皇后，生三子。
entries.en: His alleged great-grandmother was the sister of the Xiongnu prince Hunye of the Guili rank, who became Emperor Wu’s empress and bore three sons.
entries.literal: His great-grandmother was the Xiongnu Guili Hunye King's elder sister who became Emperor Wu's empress; she bore three sons.

entries.zh: 遭江充之亂，太子誅，皇后坐死，中子次卿亡之長陵，小子回卿逃於左谷。
entries.en: When Jiang Chong’s intrigue struck down the heir, the empress died with him; the middle son, Ciqing, fled to Changling and the youngest, Huiqing, to the Zuogu valley.
entries.literal: They suffered Jiang Chong's turmoil; the heir was executed; the empress died by implication; the middle son Ciqing fled to Changling; the youngest son Huiqing fled to Zuogu.

entries.zh: 霍將軍立次卿，迎回卿。
entries.en: General Huo Guang set up Ciqing and sent for Huiqing.
entries.literal: General Huo established Ciqing, welcomed Huiqing.

entries.zh: 回卿不出，因居左谷，生子孫卿，孫卿生文伯。
entries.en: Huiqing would not emerge and stayed on in Zuogu; his line ran Sunqing and then Wenbo.
entries.literal: Huiqing did not come out, therefore dwelt in Zuogu, bore a son Sunqing; Sunqing bore Wenbo.

entries.zh: 常以是言誑惑安定間。
entries.en: Lu Fang peddled this tale through Anding for years.
entries.literal: He constantly used these words to deceive and confuse within Anding.

entries.zh: 王莽末，乃與三水屬國羌胡起兵。
entries.en: At the close of Wang Mang’s reign he rose with the Qiang and Hu of the Sanshui dependent state.
entries.literal: At Wang Mang's end, then together with the dependent state's Qiang and Hu of Sanshui he raised troops.

entries.zh: 更始至長安，征芳為騎都尉，使鎮撫安定以西。
entries.en: When the Gengshi court entered Chang’an it summoned Lu Fang as cavalry commandant and sent him to pacify the country west of Anding.
entries.literal: When Gengshi reached Chang'an, he summoned Fang as cavalry commandant, ordered him to pacify and comfort west of Anding.

entries.zh: 更始敗，三水豪傑共計議，以芳劉氏子孫，宜承宗廟，乃共立芳為上將軍、西平王，欲平定西方，故以為號。
entries.en: When Gengshi was defeated, the powerful men of Sanshui deliberated together and, because Fang was a descendant of the Liu clan and ought to inherit the ancestral temples, they jointly set up Fang as Supreme General and King of Xiping. They wanted to pacify the west, and therefore used that as his title.
entries.literal: When Gengshi was defeated, the powerful men of Sanshui deliberated together and, because Fang was a descendant of the Liu clan and ought to inherit the ancestral temples, they jointly set up Fang as Supreme General and King of Xiping. They wanted to pacify the west, and therefore used that as his title.

entries.zh: 使使與西羌、匈奴結和親。
entries.en: They sent envoys to form marriage alliances with the Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: They sent envoys to form marriage alliances with the Western Qiang and the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 單于曰：「匈奴本與漢約為兄弟。
entries.en: The chanyu said, “The Xiongnu originally made a covenant with the Han to be brothers.
entries.literal: The chanyu said, “The Xiongnu originally made a covenant with the Han to be brothers.

entries.zh: 高祖時，與冒頓單于約為兄弟。
entries.en: In Gaozu’s time, he made a covenant with Maodun Chanyu to be brothers.
entries.literal: In Gaozu’s time, he made a covenant with Maodun Chanyu to be brothers.

entries.zh: 後匈奴中衰，呼韓邪單于歸漢，漢為發兵擁護，世世稱臣。
entries.en: Later, when the Xiongnu waned, Chanyu Huhanye submitted to Han; Han sent armies to shield him, and for generations his people called themselves vassals.
entries.literal: Later the Xiongnu middle declined; Shanyu Huhanye returned to Han; Han for him raised troops to protect; generation after generation called themselves ministers.

entries.zh: 呼韓邪單于降漢，入朝，宣帝擁護，國內遂定。
entries.en: When Huhanye Chanyu surrendered to Han and came to court, Emperor Xuan protected him, and order was then established within his state.
entries.literal: When Huhanye Chanyu surrendered to Han and came to court, Emperor Xuan protected him, and order was then established within his state.

entries.zh: 今漢亦中絕，劉氏來歸我，亦當立之，令尊事我。』
entries.en: Now Han’s line is broken; the Lius come to me for shelter—I should set one of them up and make him honour my authority.’
entries.literal: Now Han also is cut off in the middle; the Liu clan comes to submit to me; I also ought to establish him, order him to honour and serve me.

entries.zh: 乃使句林王將數千騎迎芳，芳與兄禽、弟程俱入匈奴。
entries.en: He sent the Goulin king with thousands of riders to escort Lu Fang; Lu Fang entered the steppe with his brothers Qin and Cheng.
entries.literal: ’ Thereupon he ordered the Goulin King to lead several thousand cavalry to welcome Fang; Fang together with elder brother Qin, younger brother Cheng, all entered the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 單于遂立芳為漢帝。
entries.en: The chanyu thereupon proclaimed him emperor of Han.
entries.literal: The Shanyu thereupon established Fang as Han emperor.

entries.zh: 以程為中郎將，將胡騎還入安定。
entries.en: He made Cheng a gentleman of the palace and sent him back into Anding at the head of Hu cavalry.
entries.literal: He appointed Cheng as gentleman of the palace, led Hu cavalry back into Anding.

entries.zh: 王昌一名郎，趙國邯鄲人也。
entries.en: Wang Chang, who also went by the name Wang Lang, came from Handan in Zhao.
entries.literal: Wang Chang, another name Lang, was a man of Handan in the state of Zhao.

entries.zh: 素為卜相工，明星曆，常以為河北有天子氣。
entries.en: He made his living reading omens and faces, knew the stars and the calendar, and had long been convinced that the region north of the river bore the portents of an emperor.
entries.literal: He had long worked as a diviner and physiognomist, understood the stars and calendars, and constantly believed that north of the Yellow River there was the aura of a Son of Heaven.

entries.zh: 時趙繆王子林，景帝七代孫也，好奇數，任俠於趙、魏間，多通豪猾，而郎與之親善。
entries.en: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Lin, a son of Prince Miao of Zhao and a seventh-generation descendant of Emperor Jing, delighted in strange numerological arts, acted as a bravo between Zhao and Wei, and had many ties with powerful scoundrels; Wang Lang was close to him.

entries.zh: 好奇數，術數。
entries.en: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.
entries.literal: Delighting in strange shu means in numerological arts.

entries.zh: 初，王莽篡位，長安中或自稱成帝子子輿者，莽殺之。
entries.en: After Wang Mang usurped the throne, a man in Chang’an had claimed to be Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng; Mang had him executed.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Wang Mang seized the throne, someone in Chang’an who called himself Ziyu, a son of Emperor Cheng, was killed by Mang.

entries.zh: 《王莽傳》曰，時男子武仲自稱劉子輿。
entries.en: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.
entries.literal: The Biography of Wang Mang says that at that time a man named Wu Zhong claimed to be Liu Ziyu.

entries.zh: 郎緣是詐稱真子輿，云『母故成帝謳者，嘗下殿卒僵，須臾有黃氣從上下，半日乃解，遂妊身就館。
entries.en: Wang Lang therefore passed himself off as the genuine Liu Ziyu, claiming: "My mother was once a palace singer to Emperor Cheng. She once came down from the hall and suddenly collapsed; after a little while yellow vapor flowed down from above, and only after half a day did she recover. She then conceived and was sent to the birth house.
entries.literal: Lang on this account falsely called himself the true Ziyu, saying: ‘My mother had been a singer for Emperor Cheng; once when descending the hall she suddenly collapsed stiff; in a moment yellow vapour came from above and below; only after half a day did she recover, and then she was pregnant and went to the lying-in quarters.

entries.zh: 趙後欲害之，偽易他人子，以故得全。
entries.en: Empress Zhao tried to destroy me, but another person's child was substituted as a deception, and so I was preserved.
entries.literal: Empress Zhao wished to harm him; she falsely exchanged another person’s child; by this means he was preserved whole.

entries.zh: 趙飛燕也。
entries.en: This was Zhao Feiyan.
entries.literal: This was Zhao Feiyan.

entries.zh: 《東觀記》曰：「宮婢生子，正與同時，即易之」也。
entries.en: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”
entries.literal: The Dongguan Record says, “A palace maid bore a child at exactly the same time, and he was then exchanged for that child.”

entries.zh: 子輿年十二，識命者郎中李曼卿，與俱至蜀；
entries.en: At twelve, Ziyu met the physiognomist and court gentleman Li Manqing and traveled with him into Shu;
entries.literal: When Ziyu was twelve, he met the fate-reader Gentleman-of-the-Palace Li Manqing and together with him went to Shu.

entries.zh: 識命謂知天命也。
entries.en: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.
entries.literal: Shiming, “recognizing destiny,” means knowing Heaven’s command.

entries.zh: 十七，到丹陽；
entries.en: at seventeen, he reached Danyang;
entries.literal: At seventeen, he arrived at Danyang.

entries.zh: 長伯，豐字也。
entries.en: Changbo was Feng’s style name.
entries.literal: Changbo was Feng’s style name.

entries.zh: 豐，平帝時為少府，王莽篡位時為更始將軍。
entries.en: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.
entries.literal: Feng was Lesser Treasurer in Emperor Ping’s time and General Who Renews Beginnings when Wang Mang usurped the throne.

entries.zh: 二十，還長安；
entries.en: at twenty, he returned to Chang'an;
entries.literal: At twenty, he returned to Chang’an.

entries.zh: 展轉中山，來往燕、趙，以須天時』。
entries.en: then he drifted through Zhongshan and between Yan and Zhao, waiting for Heaven's time."
entries.literal: He shifted to Zhongshan, coming and going between Yan and Zhao, in order to await the heavenly season.’

entries.zh: 須，待也。
entries.en: Xu means “to wait.”
entries.literal: Xu means “to wait.”

entries.zh: 林等愈動疑惑，乃與趙國大豪李育、張參等通謀，規共立郎。
entries.en: The story unsettled Liu Lin and his circle; they conspired with Zhao notables Li Yu and Zhang Can to set Wang Lang on the throne.
entries.literal: Lin and the others were increasingly moved to doubt, and then with great magnates of Zhao such as Li Yu and Zhang Can secretly plotted, planning together to establish Lang.

entries.zh: 會人間傳赤眉將度河，林等因此宣言赤眉當立劉子輿以觀眾心，百姓多信之。
entries.en: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.
entries.literal: When word among the people spread that the Red Eyebrows were about to cross the Yellow River, Liu Lin and the others used this to declare that the Red Eyebrows would establish Liu Ziyu, in order to observe the public mood; many commoners believed it.

entries.zh: 初，臨邑侯復好學，能文章。
entries.en: Liu Fu, marquis of Linyi, was a devoted scholar and a polished writer.
entries.literal: In the beginning the marquis of Linyi, Fu, loved learning and was capable at composition.

entries.zh: 永平中，每有講學事，輒令復典掌焉。
entries.en: During Yongping he was routinely put in charge of court lectures and academies.
entries.literal: In the Yongping period, whenever there were affairs of lecturing and learning, he was always ordered to take charge of them.

entries.zh: 與班固、賈逵共述漢史，傅毅等皆宗事之。
entries.en: With Ban Gu and Jia Kui he compiled Han history, while Fu Yi and others looked to him as their patron.
entries.literal: Together with Ban Gu and Jia Kui he narrated Han history, and Fu Yi and others all took him as their teacher in service.

entries.zh: 復子騊駼及從兄平望侯毅，並有才學。
entries.en: His son Taotu and his cousin Yi, marquis of Pingwang, were likewise gifted scholars.
entries.literal: Fu’s son Taotu and his elder male cousin Yi, marquis of Pingwang, both had talent and learning.

entries.zh: 永寧中，鄧太后召毅及騊駼入東觀，與謁者僕射劉珍著中興以下名臣列士傳。
entries.en: Under Yongning the Deng regent brought Yi and Taotu into the Eastern Library to join Liu Zhen in drafting biographies of notable men since the restoration.
entries.literal: In the Yongning period Empress Dowager Deng summoned Yi and Taotu into the Eastern View, where with the herald superintendent Liu Zhen they wrote biographies of famous ministers and stalwarts from the restoration onward.

entries.zh: 騊駼又自造賦、頌、書、論凡四篇。
entries.en: Taotu also wrote four original pieces—fu, hymns, letters, and essays.
entries.literal: Taotu moreover himself composed in all four pieces of rhapsody, eulogy, letter, and discourse.

entries.zh: 平後坐與諸王交通，國除。
entries.en: Ping later lost his title for illicit dealings with other princes.
entries.literal: Later Ping sat guilty of trafficking with the various kings and the kingdom was abolished.

entries.zh: 永平五年，顯宗更封平為竟陵侯。
entries.en: In Yongping 5 Emperor Ming transferred Ping to the marquisate of Jingling.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Yongping the Manifest Ancestor changed the enfeoffment of Ping to be marquis of Jingling.

entries.zh: 平卒，子真嗣。
entries.en: Ping was succeeded by his son Zhen.
entries.literal: When Ping died, his son Zhen succeeded.

entries.zh: 真卒，子禹嗣。
entries.en: Zhen was followed by Yu.
entries.literal: When Zhen died, his son Yu succeeded.

entries.zh: 禹卒，子嘉嗣。
entries.en: Yu was followed by Jia.
entries.literal: When Yu died, his son Jia succeeded.

entries.zh: 齊武王
entries.en: Prince Martial of Qi (Liu Yan)
entries.literal: Prince Martial of Qi

entries.zh: 耿弇字伯昭，扶風茂陵人也。
entries.en: Geng Yan, courtesy name Bozhao, was a native of Maoling in Fufeng commandery.
entries.literal: Geng Yan, styled Bozhao, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng.

entries.zh: 其先武帝時以吏二千石自巨鹿徙焉。
entries.en: His forebears had held a two-thousand-dan post under Emperor Wu and relocated from Julu to Maoling.
entries.literal: His ancestors, in the time of Emperor Wu, as officials at the rank of two thousand shi, moved from Julu to there.

entries.zh: 父況，字俠遊，以明經為郎，與王莽從弟伋共學《老子》於安丘先生，後為朔調連率。
entries.en: His father Geng Kuang, courtesy name Xiayou, entered court as a gentleman-attendant on the strength of his classical learning; with Wang Mang's cousin Wang Ji he studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, and was later appointed chain commandant of the Shuodiao circuit.
entries.literal: His father Kuang, styled Xiayou, through understanding the classics became a gentleman-attendant, and with Wang Mang's cousin Ji together studied the Laozi under Master Anqiu, afterward became chain commandant of Shuodiao.

entries.zh: 弇少好學，習父業。
entries.en: From boyhood Geng Yan loved learning and followed his father's scholarly path.
entries.literal: Yan in youth loved study, practiced his father's occupation.

entries.zh: 常見郡尉試騎士，建旗鼓，肄馳射，由是好將帥之事。
entries.en: He often watched the commandery commandant drill mounted archers—drums and banners raised, bows shot at full gallop—and so grew fond of the business of command.
entries.literal: He often saw the commandery commandant test mounted knights, set up drums and banners, drill mounted archery, thereby came to love generals' and commanders' affairs.

entries.zh: 是時，烏桓、鮮卑屢寇外境，國素有籌策，數言邊事，帝器之。
entries.en: At that time the Wuhuan and Xianbei harried the frontier again and again; Geng Guo was full of stratagems, spoke often on border policy, and the emperor valued him.
entries.literal: At this time, Wuhuan, Xianbei repeatedly raided outer borders, Guo always had plans, several times spoke border affairs, emperor esteemed him.

entries.zh: 及匈奴薁日逐王比自立為呼韓邪單元，款塞稱藩，願扞禦北虜。
entries.en: When the Xiongnu prince Bi, the Ailizhuyu king, set himself up as Chanyu in the manner of Huhanye, crossed the passes as a vassal, and offered to shield the north against other barbarians,
entries.literal: When Xiongnu Ailizhuyu King Bi self-established as Chanyu Huhanye, opened barrier called vassal, wished defend north caitiffs.

entries.zh: 事下公卿。
entries.en: the matter was referred to the high ministers.
entries.literal: Matter sent down to dukes and ministers.

entries.zh: 議者皆以為天下初定，中國空虛，夷狄情偽難知，不可許。
entries.en: The consensus was that the empire was newly pacified, the heartland still drained, and barbarian intentions impossible to read—the court should not agree.
entries.literal: Debaters all thought empire first settled, central plain empty void, barbarians true-false hard know, not permissible grant.

entries.zh: 國獨曰：『臣以為宜如孝宣故事受之，令東扞鮮卑，北拒匈奴，率厲四夷，完復邊郡，使塞下無晏開之警，萬世安寧之策也。』
entries.en: Geng Guo alone said, 'I hold we should follow Emperor Xuan's precedent and accept him, set him to block the Xianbei on the east and hold the Xiongnu on the north, rally the four barbarians, restore the lost border commanderies, and keep the passes free of sudden alarms—that is the plan for peace for ages to come.'
entries.literal: Guo alone said: 'Your subject thinks ought like Filial Emperor Xuan former case receive him, order east block Xianbei, north resist Xiongnu, lead encourage four barbarians, restore complete border commanderies, make below passes no late-opening alarm, ten thousand generations peace quiet plan.'

entries.zh: 帝從其議，遂立比為南單于。
entries.en: The emperor adopted his argument and established Bi as southern chanyu.
entries.literal: Emperor followed his discussion, thereupon established Bi as South Chanyu.

entries.zh: 由是烏桓、鮮卑保塞自守，北虜遠遁，中國少事。
entries.en: Thereafter the Wuhuan and Xianbei guarded the line for themselves, the northern raiders withdrew far away, and the heartland knew less trouble.
entries.literal: Thereby Wuhuan, Xianbei guarded passes self-defend, north caitiffs far fled, central plain few affairs.

entries.zh: 二十七年，代馮勤為大司農。
entries.en: In the twenty-seventh year he succeeded Feng Qin as grand minister of agriculture.
entries.literal: Twenty-seventh year, replaced Feng Qin as grand minister of agriculture.

entries.zh: 又上言宜置度遼將軍、左右校尉，屯五原以防逃亡。
entries.en: He further memorialized that a general-across-the-Liao and left and right colonels should be posted with a garrison at Wuyuan to check desertions.
entries.literal: Again submitted memorial saying ought establish general who crosses the Liao, left and right colonels, garrison Wuyuan to guard against fugitives.

entries.zh: 永平元年卒官。
entries.en: He died in office in the first year of Yongping.
entries.literal: Yongping first year died in office.

entries.zh: 顯宗追思國言，後遂置度遼將軍、左右校尉，如其議焉。
entries.en: Emperor Ming later remembered Geng Guo's counsel and eventually did institute the general-across-the-Liao and the left and right colonels as he had proposed.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming afterward recalled Guo's words, later then established general who crosses the Liao, left and right colonels, as his discussion.

entries.zh: 恭字伯宗，國弟廣之子也。
entries.en: Geng Gong, courtesy name Bozong, was the son of Geng Guo's younger brother Geng Guang.
entries.literal: Gong styled Bozong, was Guo's younger brother Guang's son.

entries.zh: 少孤。
entries.en: He was orphaned while young.
entries.literal: In youth orphaned.

entries.zh: 慷慨多大略，有將帥才。
entries.en: He was high-minded and far-sighted, with a born commander's gifts.
entries.literal: Stirred generous had great plans, had generals' and commanders' talent.

entries.zh: 永平十七年冬，騎都尉劉張出擊車師，請恭為司馬，與奉車都尉竇固及從弟駙馬都尉秉破降之。
entries.en: In the winter of the seventeenth year of Yongping, when Cavalry Commandant Liu Zhang marched against Jushi, he asked for Geng Gong as his major; with Coach Commandant Dou Gu and his cousin Coach Commandant Geng Bing they crushed and received the surrender of Jushi.
entries.literal: Yongping seventeenth year winter, cavalry commandant Liu Zhang exited strike Jushi, requested Gong as major, with coach commandant Dou Gu and cousin coach commandant Bing broke and surrendered them.

entries.zh: 始置西域都護、戊己校尉，乃以恭為戊己校尉，屯後王部金蒲城，謁者關寵為戊己校尉，屯前王柳中城，屯各置數百人。
entries.en: When the protector-general of the Western Regions and the Wu and Ji colonels were first instituted, Geng Gong was named colonel of Wu and Ji and stationed with the rear king's people at Jinfu, while the herald Guan Chong was named colonel of Wu and Ji and stationed at Liuzhong with the front king; each garrison held several hundred men.
entries.literal: First established Western Regions protector, Wu and Ji colonels, then made Gong Wu and Ji colonel, garrisoned rear king's division at Jinfu city, herald Guan Chong as Wu and Ji colonel, garrisoned front king's Liuzhong city, garrisons each placed several hundred men.

entries.zh: 恭至部，移檄烏孫，示漢威德，大昆彌以下皆歡喜，遣使獻名馬，及奉宣帝時所賜公主博具，願遣子入侍。
entries.en: When Geng Gong reached his command he sent a manifesto to Wusun proclaiming Han might and virtue; the great Kunmi and his court rejoiced, sent envoys with famous horses, returned the board games given the princess under Emperor Xuan, and asked to send a son to court.
entries.literal: Gong reached division, transmitted proclamation Wusun, displayed Han might and virtue, great Kunmi down all rejoiced, dispatched envoys presented famous horses, and offered Emperor Xuan-time bestowed princess board games, wished send son enter attend.

entries.zh: 恭乃發使賫金帛，迎其侍子。
entries.en: Geng Gong then sent envoys with gold and silks to escort the hostage prince.
entries.literal: Gong then dispatched envoys carrying gold silks, welcome his attendant son.

entries.zh: 更始立，使使者行郡國，即拜忠都尉官。
entries.en: When the Gengshi Emperor took power, his envoys toured the provinces and on the spot commissioned Li Zhong as commandant.
entries.literal: When Gengshi was established, he sent envoys to tour commanderies and kingdoms, and at once appointed Zhong to the office of commandant.

entries.zh: 忠遂與任光同奉世祖，以為右大將軍，封武固侯。
entries.en: Li Zhong then joined Ren Guang in serving Emperor Guangwu, who named him right grand general and marquis of Wugu.
entries.literal: Zhong thereupon with Ren Guang together served the Shizu, who made him right grand general and enfeoffed him as marquis of Wugu.

entries.zh: 時，世祖自解所佩綬以帶忠，因從攻下屬縣。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu unfastened his own official sash and bound it on Li Zhong as a mark of favor, then led him in the reduction of the outlying counties.
entries.literal: At that time the Shizu himself untied the sash he wore and gave it to Zhong, and for that reason followed in attacking and taking subordinate counties.

entries.zh: 至苦陘，世祖會諸將，問所得財物，唯忠獨無所掠。
entries.en: At Kuxing Emperor Guangwu called the generals together and asked what booty each had seized; Li Zhong alone had taken nothing.
entries.literal: When they reached Kuxing, the Shizu assembled the generals and asked what goods each had taken; only Zhong alone had plundered nothing.

entries.zh: 世祖曰：『我欲特賜，李忠，諸卿得無望乎？』
entries.en: Guangwu said, "I mean to give Li Zhong a special gift—you others won't begrudge him that, I hope?"
entries.literal: The Shizu said: "I intend to give a special reward to Li Zhong—will you gentlemen perhaps resent it?"

entries.zh: 即以所乘大驪馬及繡被衣物賜之。
entries.en: He then gave Li Zhong his own dapple-gray mount, brocade bedding, and fine clothes.
entries.literal: He thereupon bestowed on him the great dapple-gray horse he rode and embroidered coverlets and clothing.

entries.zh: 進圍巨鹿，未下，王郎遣將攻信都，信都大姓馬寵等開城內之，收太守宗廣及忠母、妻，而令親屬招呼忠。
entries.en: While the army was still besieging Julu, Wang Lang sent a force against Xindu. Powerful local families led by Ma Chong betrayed the city, seized Governor Zong Guang and Li Zhong's mother and wife, and tried to lure Li Zhong through his kin.
entries.literal: They advanced to besiege Julu; it had not yet fallen when Wang Lang sent a general to attack Xindu; great clans of Xindu such as Ma Chong opened the city to him within, seized Governor Zong Guang and Zhong's mother and wife, and ordered relatives to summon Zhong.

entries.zh: 時，寵弟從忠為校尉，忠即時召見，責數以背恩反城，因格殺之。
entries.en: Ma Chong's brother was serving under Li Zhong as a colonel; Li Zhong called him in immediately, rebuked him for treason in opening the gates, and cut him down on the spot.
entries.literal: At that time Chong's younger brother followed Zhong as a colonel; Zhong at once summoned him, rebuked him for betraying favor and turning the city, and thereupon struck and killed him.

entries.zh: 諸將皆驚曰：『家屬在人手中，殺其弟，何猛也！』
entries.en: The other generals were stunned: "Your family is hostage to the enemy, and you kill his brother—how ruthless!"
entries.literal: The generals all were startled and said: "Your family members are in others' hands—yet you kill his younger brother; how fierce!"

entries.zh: 忠曰：『若縱賊不誅，則二心也。』
entries.en: Li Zhong replied, "If I spared a traitor, I would be of two minds myself."
entries.literal: Zhong said: "If I let the traitor go unpunished, that would be a second heart."

entries.zh: 世祖聞而美之，謂忠曰：『今吾兵已成矣，將軍可歸救老母、妻、子，宜自募吏民能得家屬者，賜錢千萬，來從我取。』
entries.en: Guangwu heard and approved: "Our host is now solid. You may go back to rescue your mother, wife, and children—recruit anyone who can recover hostages and I will pay ten million cash; collect it from me."
entries.literal: Shizu heard and praised him, saying to Zhong, "Now my troops are formed. You may return to rescue your mother, wife, and children. Recruit officials and commoners capable of recovering your family; I will grant ten million cash—come and collect it from me."

entries.zh: 忠曰：『蒙明公大恩，思得效命，誠不敢內顧宗親。』
entries.en: Li Zhong answered, "I owe you too much to think of anything but repaying it with my life; I cannot spare a thought for my relatives."
entries.literal: Zhong said: "Having received the enlightened lord's great grace, I wish only to repay it with my life; I truly dare not look inward to kin."

entries.zh: 世祖乃使任光將兵救信都，光兵於道散降王郎，無功而還。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu then sent Ren Guang to relieve Xindu, but Ren Guang's men melted away on the march and defected to Wang Lang, so the expedition accomplished nothing.
entries.literal: The Shizu thereupon ordered Ren Guang to lead troops to rescue Xindu; Guang's troops scattered on the road and surrendered to Wang Lang, and returned without achievement.

entries.zh: 會更始遣將攻破信都，忠家屬得全。
entries.en: Soon afterward a Gengshi general retook Xindu, and Li Zhong's family came through unharmed.
entries.literal: It happened that Gengshi sent a general who broke Xindu, and Zhong's family members were preserved whole.

entries.zh: 世祖因使忠還，行太守事，收郡中大姓附邯鄲者，誅殺數百人。
entries.en: Guangwu then sent Li Zhong back as acting governor to round up leading families who had backed Wang Lang of Handan; several hundred were executed.
entries.literal: The Shizu thereupon ordered Zhong to return and act as governor, arresting great clans of the commandery who had sided with Handan, and executed several hundred.

entries.zh: 及任光歸郡，忠乃還復為都尉。
entries.en: After Ren Guang went home to his commandery, Li Zhong resumed his post as commandant.
entries.literal: When Ren Guang returned to his commandery, Zhong then returned again to be commandant.

entries.zh: 建武二年，更封中水侯，食邑三千戶。
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 he was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Zhongshui with income from three thousand households.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed anew as marquis of Zhongshui with a fief of three thousand households.

entries.zh: 其年，征拜五官中郎將，從平寵萌，董憲等。
entries.en: The same year he was called to court as general of the household for the five offices and took part in the campaigns against Pang Meng and Dong Xian.
entries.literal: That year he was summoned and appointed general of the household for the five offices, and followed in pacifying Pang Meng, Dong Xian, and others.

entries.zh: 六年，遷丹陽太守。
entries.en: In Jianwu 6 he became governor of Danyang.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to governor of Danyang.

entries.zh: 是時，海內新定，南方海濱江淮，多擁兵據土。
entries.en: The empire had only just been pacified, yet along the southern coast and the Yangzi-Huai region many still held arms and carved out their own ground.
entries.literal: At that time within the seas had newly been settled, but south of the sea along the rivers and Huai many held troops and occupied territory.

entries.zh: 忠到郡，招懷降附，其不服者悉誅之，旬月皆平。
entries.en: Li Zhong won over those willing to yield and exterminated those who refused; within a month the commandery was quiet.
entries.literal: When Zhong reached the commandery, he summoned and cherished those who submitted; those who would not submit he utterly executed, and within a month all was pacified.

entries.zh: 忠以丹陽越俗不好學，嫁娶禮儀，衰於中國，乃為起學校，習禮容，春秋鄉飲，選用明經，郡中向慕之。
entries.en: Finding the local Yue people little inclined toward scholarship and their wedding etiquette lax compared with the heartland, he founded schools, taught ritual bearing, held the classic village-drinking ceremony, and promoted men versed in the classics until the commandery took notice and began to emulate them.
entries.literal: Zhong because the Yue customs of Danyang did not love learning, and marriage rites had declined compared with the central states, therefore for them established schools, practiced ritual deportment, held spring and autumn village drinking, selected men learned in the classics, and the commandery turned toward and admired this.

entries.zh: 墾田增多，三歲間流民占著者五萬餘口。
entries.en: Under his administration newly opened fields multiplied, and in three years more than fifty thousand displaced people had registered as residents.
entries.literal: Reclaimed fields increased, and within three years wandering people who settled numbered over fifty thousand mouths.

entries.zh: 十四年，三公奏課為天下第一，遷豫章太守。
entries.en: In Jianwu 14 the three highest ministers ranked his performance first in the empire, and he was transferred to Yuzhang.
entries.literal: In the fourteenth year the three dukes reported his assessment as first in the realm, and he was moved to governor of Yuzhang.

entries.zh: 病去官，征詣京師。
entries.en: Illness forced him to resign; he was then summoned to the capital.
entries.literal: Ill he left office and was summoned to the capital.

entries.zh: 十九年，卒。
entries.en: He died in Jianwu 19.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year he died.

entries.zh: 萬脩字君遊，扶風茂陵人也。
entries.en: Wan Xiu, styled Junyou, came from Maoling in Fufeng commandery.
entries.literal: Wan Xiu, courtesy name Junyou, was a native of Maoling in Fufeng.

entries.zh: 更始時，為信都令，與太守任光、都尉李忠共城守，迎世祖，拜為偏將軍，封造義侯。
entries.en: Under Gengshi he was magistrate of Xindu; with Governor Ren Guang and Commandant Li Zhong he held the city, welcomed Emperor Guangwu, was named lieutenant general, and enfeoffed as marquis of Zaoyi.
entries.literal: In the time of Gengshi he was magistrate of Xindu; with Governor Ren Guang and Commandant Li Zhong he together defended the city walls, welcomed the Shizu, was appointed lieutenant general, and enfeoffed as marquis of Zaoyi.

entries.zh: 及破邯鄲，拜右將軍，從平河北。
entries.en: After the fall of Handan he became right general and helped pacify Hebei.
entries.literal: When Handan was broken, he was appointed right general and followed in pacifying Hebei.

entries.zh: 建武二年，更封槐裏侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 his fief was moved to Huaili.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed anew as marquis of Huaili.

entries.zh: 與揚化將軍堅鐔俱擊南陽，未克而病，卒於軍。
entries.en: He campaigned with General Who Spreads Transformation Jian Tan against Nanyang but fell ill before the city fell and died in camp.
entries.literal: Together with General Who Spreads Transformation Jian Tan he struck Nanyang; before it was taken he fell ill and died in the army.

entries.zh: 邳彤字偉君，信都人也。
entries.en: Pi Tong, styled Weijun, was a man of Xindu.
entries.literal: Pi Tong, courtesy name Weijun, was a native of Xindu.

entries.zh: 父吉，為遼西太守。
entries.en: His father Pi Ji had served as governor of Liaoxi.
entries.literal: His father Ji had been governor of Liaoxi.

entries.zh: 彤初為王莽和成卒正。
entries.en: Pi Tong began his career as zuzheng of Hegcheng under Wang Mang.
entries.literal: Tong at first was zuzheng of Hegcheng under Wang Mang.

entries.zh: 世祖徇河北，至下曲陽，彤舉城降，復以為太守，留止數日。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangwu advanced through Hebei and reached Xiaquyang, Pi Tong surrendered the city; Guangwu reappointed him governor and kept him there for a few days.
entries.literal: When the Shizu campaigned through Hebei and reached Xiaquyang, Tong raised the city in surrender; he was again appointed governor and detained several days.

entries.zh: 世祖北至薊，會王郎兵起，使其將徇地，所到縣莫不奉迎，唯和成、信都堅守不下。
entries.en: Guangwu then rode north to Ji just as Wang Lang's rebellion erupted. Wang's officers swept the countryside, and county after county opened its gates—only Hegcheng and Xindu refused to submit.
entries.literal: When the Shizu went north to Ji, it happened that Wang Lang's troops rose; he sent his generals to seize territory, and in every county they reached none failed to welcome them—only Hegcheng and Xindu held fast and would not yield.

entries.zh: 彤聞世祖從薊還，失軍，欲至信都，乃先使五官掾張萬、督郵尹綏，選精騎二千餘匹，緣路迎世祖軍。
entries.en: Hearing that Guangwu was retreating from Ji stripped of his main force and heading for Xindu, Pi Tong sent registrar Zhang Wan and touring investigator Yin Sui ahead with over two thousand picked cavalry to escort him along the route.
entries.literal: Tong heard the Shizu was returning from Ji having lost his army and intending to reach Xindu; he first sent registrar Zhang Wan and touring investigator Yin Sui to select more than two thousand picked horsemen to meet the Shizu's army along the road.

entries.zh: 彤尋與世祖會信都。
entries.en: Pi Tong soon joined Emperor Guangwu at Xindu.
entries.literal: Tong soon thereafter joined the Shizu at Xindu.

entries.zh: 世祖雖得二郡之助，而兵眾未合，議者多言可因信都兵自送，西還長安。
entries.en: Even with two loyal commanderies behind him, Guangwu's army was still scattered; many advisers urged him to use Xindu's men as an escort and withdraw west to Chang'an.
entries.literal: Although the Shizu had obtained the aid of the two commanderies, his host was not yet united, and those who debated mostly said he could ride Xindu's troops to escort himself west back to Chang'an.

entries.zh: 彤廷對曰：
entries.en: Pi Tong rose in council and said:
entries.literal: Tong replied in court:

entries.zh: 世祖善其言而止。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu judged the argument sound and abandoned the plan to withdraw.
entries.literal: The Shizu thought his words good and stopped.

entries.zh: 即日拜彤為後大將軍，和成太守如故，使將兵居前。
entries.en: That same day he named Pi Tong rear grand general while leaving him governor of Hegcheng, and put his command in the lead.
entries.literal: That day he appointed Tong rear grand general, his post as governor of Hegcheng remaining as before, and ordered him to lead troops in the van.

entries.zh: 比至堂陽，堂陽已反屬王郎，彤使張萬、尹綏先曉譬吏民，世祖夜至，即開門出迎。
entries.en: By the time they reached Tangyang, the town had gone over to Wang Lang. Pi Tong sent Zhang Wan and Yin Sui to reason with the people; Guangwu arrived after dark, and the gates flew open in welcome.
entries.literal: By the time they reached Tangyang, Tangyang had already turned back to Wang Lang; Tong sent Zhang Wan and Yin Sui first to explain clearly to officials and people; the Shizu arrived by night, and at once they opened the gates and came out to welcome.

entries.zh: 引兵擊破白奢賊於中山。
entries.en: He then led the column that routed the Baisha bandits in Zhongshan.
entries.literal: He led troops and broke the bandits of Baisha in Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 自此常從戰攻。
entries.en: After that he fought at Guangwu's side in every major action.
entries.literal: From this he constantly followed in battle and attack.

entries.zh: 初，張萬，尹綏與彤俱迎世祖，皆拜偏將軍，亦從征伐。
entries.en: Zhang Wan and Yin Sui had ridden out with Pi Tong to receive Guangwu; each was named lieutenant general and saw action in the wars.
entries.literal: At first Zhang Wan and Yin Sui together with Tong welcomed the Shizu; all were appointed lieutenant generals and also followed in campaigns.

entries.zh: 萬封重平侯，綏封平臺侯。
entries.en: Zhang Wan became marquis of Chongping and Yin Sui marquis of Pingtai.
entries.literal: Wan was enfeoffed as marquis of Chongping, Sui as marquis of Pingtai.

entries.zh: 信都復反為王郎，郎所置信都王捕系彤父弟及妻子，使為手書呼彤曰：『降者封爵，不降族滅。』
entries.en: Xindu rebelled again to Wang Lang. Wang's puppet Prince of Xindu seized Pi Tong's father, brothers, wife, and children and forced him to write: "Surrender and win a title; resist and your clan dies."
entries.literal: Xindu again rebelled to Wang Lang; the Prince of Xindu whom Lang had installed seized Tong's father, younger brothers, wife, and children, and ordered him to write in his own hand summoning Tong, saying: "Those who submit will be enfeoffed with rank; those who do not submit will be exterminated to the lineage."

entries.zh: 彤涕泣報曰：『事君者不得顧家。
entries.en: Pi Tong answered through tears, "A man who serves his prince cannot think first of his kin.
entries.literal: Tong weeping replied: "One who serves a lord cannot attend to family.

entries.zh: 彤親屬所以至今得安於信都者，劉公之恩也。
entries.en: My family has stayed safe in Xindu only because of Lord Liu's protection.
entries.literal: The reason Tong's kin until now have been able to dwell in peace at Xindu is the grace of Lord Liu.

entries.zh: 公方爭國事，彤不得復念私也。』
entries.en: You are fighting for the realm; I cannot weigh private ties."
entries.literal: The lord is now contending for the state affair; Tong cannot again think of private matters."

entries.zh: 會更始所遣將攻拔信都，郎兵敗走，彤家屬得免。
entries.en: Soon an imperial general sent by the Gengshi court recaptured Xindu, Wang Lang's men fled, and Pi Tong's family went free.
entries.literal: It happened that the general Gengshi sent attacked and took Xindu; Lang's troops were defeated and fled, and Tong's family members obtained escape.

entries.zh: 議者之言皆非也。
entries.en: Those counsels are mistaken.
entries.literal: The words of those who debate are all wrong.

entries.zh: 吏民歌吟思漢久矣，故更始舉尊號而天下響應，三輔清宮除道以迎之。
entries.en: Officials and commoners have longed for the house of Han; when the Gengshi Emperor claimed the throne, the empire rallied, and the capital region swept the avenues to receive him.
entries.literal: Officials and people have long sung and sighed, longing for Han; therefore when Gengshi raised the exalted title the realm answered like an echo, and the three adjuncts cleared the palaces and swept the roads to welcome him.

entries.zh: 一夫荷戟大呼，則千里之將無不捐城遁逃，虜伏請降。
entries.en: A single man with a halberd, raising his voice, could send commanders a thousand li away abandoning their walls or kneeling to yield.
entries.literal: If one man shouldered a halberd and shouted aloud, then generals for a thousand li would without exception abandon cities and flee in hiding, or crouch in submission begging to surrender.

entries.zh: 自上古以來，亦未有感物動民其如此者也。
entries.en: Never in recorded memory had popular feeling swung so completely behind a cause.
entries.literal: From high antiquity onward, there has never been one who moved things and stirred the people like this.

entries.zh: 又卜者王郎，假名因勢，驅集烏合之眾，遂震燕、趙之地；
entries.en: Wang Lang the fortune-teller had seized power with a borrowed name and a rabble, yet he still overawed Yan and Zhao.
entries.literal: Moreover the diviner Wang Lang, borrowing a name and riding the moment, drove together a flock of crows and sparrows, and thereupon shook the lands of Yan and Zhao;

entries.zh: 況明公奮二郡之兵，揚響應之威，以攻則何城不克，以戰則何軍不服！
entries.en: How much more may you, my lord, rouse two loyal commanderies and the prestige of a nation that still answers Han—what wall could stand against you, what army refuse you!
entries.literal: How much more, when the enlightened lord rouses the troops of two commanderies and raises the might of answering echoes—with such a force what city would not be taken, with such an army what host would not submit!

entries.zh: 今釋此而歸，豈徒空失河北，必要驚動三輔，墮損威重，非計之得者也。
entries.en: To throw this away and march west would not only forfeit Hebei for nothing; it would shake the heartland and tarnish your authority—no winning strategy.
entries.literal: Now to abandon this and return—would it not only empty-handed lose Hebei, but necessarily also startle the three adjuncts, topple and injure awe-inspiring weight; it is not a plan that gains.

entries.zh: 若明公無復征伐之意，則雖信都之兵猶難會也。
entries.en: If you show the world you will not fight on, even the men of Xindu may not rally again.
entries.literal: If the enlightened lord has no further mind to campaign, then even Xindu's troops would still be hard to assemble.

entries.zh: 何者？
entries.en: Why is that?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 明公既西，則邯鄲城民不肯捐父母、背城主，而千里送公，其離散亡逃可必也。
entries.en: Once you turn west, the people of Handan will not leave parents and lords to follow you a thousand li; your following would melt away for certain.
entries.literal: When the enlightened lord has gone west, then the people of Handan city will not be willing to abandon parents and betray their city lord, and to escort the lord a thousand li; their scattering, fleeing, and running away can be certain.

entries.zh: 及拔邯鄲，封武義侯。
entries.en: When Handan was captured, Pi Tong was enfeoffed as marquis of Wuyi.
entries.literal: When Handan was captured, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuyi.

entries.zh: 建武元年，更封靈壽侯，行大司空事。
entries.en: In Jianwu 1 he was transferred to marquis of Lingshou and acted as Grand Minister of Works.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was further enfeoffed as Marquis of Lingshou and acted as Grand Minister of Works.

entries.zh: 帝入洛陽，拜彤太常，月餘日轉少府，是年免。
entries.en: When the emperor entered Luoyang, Pi Tong was named Minister of Ceremonies; after a little more than a month he was moved to Minister Steward, and that year was dismissed.
entries.literal: When the Emperor entered Luoyang, Tong was appointed Minister of Ceremonies; after more than a month he was transferred to Minister Steward, and that same year was dismissed.

entries.zh: 復為左曹侍中，常從征伐。
entries.en: He was again made Left Cao Palace Attendant and often followed on campaigns.
entries.literal: He was again made Left Cao palace attendant and often followed on campaigns.

entries.zh: 六年，就國。
entries.en: In the sixth year he went to his fief.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he went to his fief.

entries.zh: 論曰：凡言成事者，以功著易顯；
entries.en: The historian remarks: finished deeds shine bright because their merit is visible;
entries.literal: The judgment says: In general those who speak of completed affairs—because achievement is manifest, they are easy to display;

entries.zh: 謀幾初者，以理隱難昭。
entries.en: counsel offered at the turning point stays obscure because its rightness is harder to see.
entries.literal: those who plan at the first hint—because principle is hidden, they are hard to make clear.

entries.zh: 斯固原情比跡，所宜推察者也。
entries.en: Both deserve careful weighing against the evidence of events.
entries.literal: This is indeed what, tracing feeling and comparing traces, one ought to push and examine.

entries.zh: 若乃議者欲因二郡之眾，建入關之策，委成業，臨不測，而世主未悟，謀夫景同，邳彤之廷對，其為幾乎！
entries.en: Consider the advisers who would have marched two loyal commanderies west through the Pass, abandoning a winning position for an unknown—while their lord still hesitated. Pi Tong's speech in council was perilously close to the truth of the moment!
entries.literal: As for those debaters who wished to rely on the masses of two commanderies to build a plan of entering the Pass, to cast away completed enterprise and face the unfathomable, while the age's lord had not yet awakened and planners shared one view—Tong's reply in court, was it not close to the mark!

entries.zh: 語曰『一言可以興邦』，斯近之矣。
entries.en: The proverb says one sentence can restore a kingdom; this comes close.
entries.literal: The saying goes, "One word can raise a state"; this is near to it.

entries.zh: 劉植字伯先，巨鹿昌城人也。
entries.en: Liu Zhi, styled Boxian, came from Changcheng in Julu commandery.
entries.literal: Liu Zhi, courtesy name Boxian, was a native of Changcheng in Julu.

entries.zh: 王郎起，植與弟喜、從兄歆率宗族賓客，聚兵數千人據昌城。
entries.en: When Wang Lang rebelled, Liu Zhi, his brother Liu Xi, and cousin Liu Xin rallied clan and clients, several thousand strong, and held Changcheng.
entries.literal: When Wang Lang rose, Zhi with his younger brother Xi and elder cousin Xin led lineage and retainers, gathered several thousand troops, and occupied Changcheng.

entries.zh: 聞世祖從薊還，乃開門迎世祖，以植為驍騎將軍，喜、歆偏將軍，皆為列侯。
entries.en: Learning that Guangwu was marching back from Ji, they opened the gates to him. Liu Zhi became general of nimble cavalry, Liu Xi and Liu Xin lieutenant generals, each enfeoffed at full marquis rank.
entries.literal: Hearing the Shizu was returning from Ji, they thereupon opened the gates to welcome the Shizu; Zhi was appointed general of nimble cavalry, Xi and Xin lieutenant generals; all became full marquises.

entries.zh: 時真定王劉揚起兵以附王郎，眾十餘萬，世祖遣植說揚，揚乃降。
entries.en: The Prince of Zhending, Liu Yang, had thrown in with Wang Lang at the head of more than a hundred thousand men; Guangwu sent Liu Zhi to parley, and Liu Yang yielded.
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Zhending Liu Yang raised troops to join Wang Lang, his numbers over one hundred thousand; the Shizu sent Zhi to persuade Yang, and Yang thereupon submitted.

entries.zh: 世祖因留真定，納郭后，後即揚之甥也，故以此結之。
entries.en: Guangwu lingered at Zhending and married the future Empress Guo—Liu Yang's niece—thereby cementing the alliance.
entries.literal: The Shizu thereupon stayed at Zhending and took Empress Guo, who was Yang's niece; for that reason he bound him with this.

entries.zh: 乃與揚及諸將置酒郭氏漆裏舍，揚擊築為歡，因得進兵拔邯鄲，從平河北。
entries.en: Guangwu then feasted Liu Yang and the generals at the Guo residence in Qili. Liu Yang played the zhu in celebration; Guangwu was thereby able to advance and capture Handan, and Liu Zhi accompanied him in pacifying Hebei.
entries.literal: Guangwu then held a feast with Yang and the generals at the Guo residence in Qili. Yang played the zhu in celebration; Guangwu was thereby able to advance and capture Handan, and Liu Zhi accompanied him in pacifying Hebei.

entries.zh: 建武二年，更封植為昌城侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 Liu Zhi was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Changcheng.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu Zhi was enfeoffed anew as marquis of Changcheng.

entries.zh: 討密縣賊，戰歿。
entries.en: He fell leading the attack on the rebels at Mi county.
entries.literal: He attacked the bandits of Mi county and died in battle.

entries.zh: 子向嗣。
entries.en: His son Liu Xiang inherited the title.
entries.literal: His son Xiang succeeded.

entries.zh: 帝使喜代將植營，復為驍騎將軍，封觀津侯。
entries.en: The emperor put Liu Xi in command of his brother's troops as general of nimble cavalry and enfeoffed him as marquis of Guanjin.
entries.literal: The Emperor ordered Xi to replace command of Zhi's camp, again as general of nimble cavalry, enfeoffed as marquis of Guanjin.

entries.zh: 喜卒，復以歆為驍騎將軍，封浮陽侯。
entries.en: When Liu Xi died, Liu Xin took the same post and became marquis of Fuyang.
entries.literal: When Xi died, Xin was again made general of nimble cavalry, enfeoffed as marquis of Fuyang.

entries.zh: 喜、歆從征伐，皆傳國於後。
entries.en: Both brothers campaigned through the wars, and their lines kept the marquisates for generations.
entries.literal: Xi and Xin followed in campaigns; both transmitted the state to posterity.

entries.zh: 向徙封東武陽侯，卒，子述嗣，永平十五年，坐與楚王英謀反，國除。
entries.en: Liu Xiang's fief shifted to Dongwuyang; when he died, his son Liu Shu succeeded, and in Yongping 15 Shu lost the title for plotting with Prince Ying of Chu.
entries.literal: Xiang was moved in fief to marquis of Dongwuyang; when he died, his son Shu succeeded; in the fifteenth year of Yongping, because he sat in conspiracy with the Prince of Chu Ying to rebel, the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 會世祖度河至邯鄲，純即謁見，世祖深接之。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangwu crossed the Yellow River to Handan, Geng Chun presented himself and was welcomed with unusual warmth.
entries.literal: It happened the Shizu crossed the He and reached Handan; Chun at once had audience, and the Shizu deeply received him.

entries.zh: 純退，見官屬將兵法度不與它將同，遂求自結納，獻馬及縑帛數百匹。
entries.en: Geng Chun withdrew, noticed that Guangwu's staff ran tighter than other commands, and returned with horses and hundreds of bolts of silk to cement his allegiance.
entries.literal: Chun withdrew, saw that the discipline of officials and generals was not the same as other generals, and thereupon sought to bind himself in friendship, presenting horses and several hundred bolts of silk.

entries.zh: 世祖北至中山，留純邯鄲。
entries.en: When Guangwu marched north into Zhongshan, he left Geng Chun behind at Handan.
entries.literal: The Shizu went north to Zhongshan and left Chun at Handan.

entries.zh: 會王郎反，世祖自薊東南馳，純與從昆弟訢、宿、植共率宗族賓客二千餘人，老病者皆載木自隨，奉迎於育。
entries.en: Wang Lang's revolt broke out while Guangwu was racing southeast from Ji; Geng Chun and his cousins Geng Xin, Geng Su, and Geng Zhi brought more than two thousand kinsmen and clients—even the elderly carried firewood as provisions—to meet him at Yu.
entries.literal: It happened Wang Lang rebelled; the Shizu galloped southeast from Ji; Chun with cousins Xin, Su, and Zhi together led lineage and retainers over two thousand persons, the old and sick all carrying wood with them, and welcomed him at Yu.

entries.zh: 拜純為前將軍，封耿鄉侯，訢、宿、植皆偏將軍，使與純居前，降宋子，從攻下曲陽及中山。
entries.en: Geng Chun became forward general and marquis of Gengxiang; Geng Xin, Geng Su, and Geng Zhi were named lieutenant generals and sent ahead with him to win over Songzi and then strike Xiaquyang and Zhongshan.
entries.literal: Chun was appointed forward general, enfeoffed as marquis of Gengxiang; Xin, Su, and Zhi were all lieutenant generals; he ordered them with Chun to go in front, submit Songzi, and follow in attacking Xiaquyang and Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 是時，郡國多降邯鄲者，純恐宗家懷異心，乃使訢、宿歸燒其廬舍。
entries.en: Many districts had gone over to Wang Lang; fearing divided loyalties in his own clan, Geng Chun sent Geng Xin and Geng Su home to burn the family compounds.
entries.literal: At that time many commanderies and kingdoms had submitted to Handan; Chun feared his clan might harbor a different heart, and thereupon sent Xin and Su back to burn their houses.

entries.zh: 世祖問純故，對曰：『竊見明公單車臨河北，非有府臧之蓄，重賞甘餌，可以聚人者也，徒以恩德懷之，是故士眾樂附。
entries.en: Guangwu asked why. Geng Chun answered, "You came north almost alone, with no treasury of gold to buy men—only your virtue drew them. That is why they follow.
