entries.literal: The Shizu asked Chun the reason; he replied: "Privately I saw the enlightened lord with a single cart came to Hebei, not having stored wealth in treasuries, nor heavy bribes and sweet bait by which to gather people; he relied solely on grace and virtue to cherish them, and for that reason knights and masses joyfully attached.

entries.zh: 今邯鄲自立，北州疑惑，純雖舉族歸命，老弱在行，猶恐宗人賓客半有不同心者，故燔燒屋室，絕其反顧之望。』
entries.en: Handan still claims the throne and the north wavers. I brought every Geng, young and old, to your banner, yet I feared half our retainers might still look homeward—so I burned the roofs behind them."
entries.literal: "Now Handan has set itself up, and the northern provinces hesitate; although Chun has raised the whole clan to submit to fate, old and weak are in the ranks, still I fear that among lineage and retainers half may have hearts not of one mind; therefore I burned houses and cut off their hope of turning back."

entries.zh: 世祖漢息。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu drew a long breath at that.
entries.literal: The Shizu sighed.

entries.zh: 及至鄗，世祖止傳舍，鄗大姓蘇公反城開門內王郎將李惲。
entries.en: At Hao, Guangwu halted at the post station. A local magnate named Su betrayed the town to Wang Lang's officer Li Yun.
entries.literal: When they reached Hao, the Shizu stopped at the relay inn; the great surname Su of Hao turned the city in revolt, opened the gates, and admitted Wang Lang's general Li Yun.

entries.zh: 純先覺知，將兵逆與惲戰，大破斬之。
entries.en: Geng Chun sensed the plot first, sortied against Li Yun, shattered his force, and took his head.
entries.literal: Chun first perceived it, led troops to meet Yun in battle, greatly defeated him, and beheaded him.

entries.zh: 從平邯鄲，又破銅馬。
entries.en: He went on to help reduce Handan and crush the Bronze Horse band.
entries.literal: He followed in pacifying Handan and again broke the Bronze Horse.

entries.zh: 時，赤眉、青犢、上江、大彤、鐵脛、五幡十餘萬眾並在射犬，世祖引兵將擊之。
entries.en: More than a hundred thousand men of the Red Eyebrows, Green Calves, Upper Yang, Great Tong, Iron Shanks, and Five Banners bands were massed at Shequan; Guangwu advanced to attack them.
entries.literal: At that time the Red Eyebrows, Green Calves, Upper Yang, Great Tong, Iron Shin, and Five Banners—over one hundred thousand together—were all at Shequan; the Shizu led troops about to strike them.

entries.zh: 純軍在前，去眾營數裏，賊忽夜攻純，雨射營中，士多死傷。
entries.en: Geng Chun's division camped a few li from the enemy; the rebels rushed his lines by night, arrow volleys riddled the tents, and casualties mounted.
entries.literal: Chun's army was in front, several li from the mass camp; the bandits suddenly by night attacked Chun, raining arrows into the camp, and many soldiers died or were wounded.

entries.zh: 純勒部曲，堅守不動。
entries.en: Geng Chun held his men steady and refused to buckle.
entries.literal: Chun ordered his personal troops, firmly held and did not move.

entries.zh: 選敢死二千人，俱持強弩，各傅三矢，使銜枚間行，繞出賊後，齊聲呼噪，強弩並發，賊眾驚走，追擊，遂破之。
entries.en: He chose two thousand volunteers, each with a heavy crossbow and three bolts, had them advance in silence with bits between their teeth, swing behind the rebel camp, then rise shouting; a single volley broke the enemy, and a pursuit finished them.
entries.literal: He selected two thousand dare-to-die, all bearing strong crossbows, each with three bolts fitted, ordered them to hold rods in the teeth and move by hidden paths, circle behind the bandits, together shout and clamor, strong crossbows all discharged at once; the bandit mass was startled and fled; pursuing the attack, he thereupon broke them.

entries.zh: 馳騎白世祖。
entries.en: He sent horsemen galloping to report to Guangwu.
entries.literal: He dispatched mounted messengers at speed to report to Emperor Guangwu.

entries.zh: 世祖明旦與諸將俱至營，勞純曰：『昨夜困乎？』
entries.en: At dawn Guangwu rode up with his generals to praise Geng Chun: "A rough night?"
entries.literal: The Shizu next morning with the various generals all came to the camp and consoled Chun, saying: "Were you hard pressed last night?"

entries.zh: 純曰：『賴明公威德，幸而獲全。』
entries.en: Geng Chun answered, "Your majesty's prestige saw us through."
entries.literal: Chun said: "Relying on the enlightened lord's awesome virtue, fortunately I obtained preservation whole."

entries.zh: 世祖曰：『大兵不可夜動，故不相救耳。
entries.en: Guangwu said, "A large army cannot march by night—that is why I could not relieve you sooner.
entries.literal: The Shizu said: "Great troops cannot move by night; therefore I did not come to your rescue.

entries.zh: 軍營進退無常，卿宗族不可悉居軍中。』
entries.en: Camps shift too often for your whole clan to stay inside the lines."
entries.literal: Army camps advance and retreat without constancy; your lineage group cannot all dwell in the army."

entries.zh: 乃以純族人耿伋為蒲吾長，悉令將親屬居焉。
entries.en: He named Geng Chun's kinsman Geng Ji magistrate of Puwu and sent the family dependents to live there under his care.
entries.literal: Thereupon he appointed Chun's clansman Geng Ji as magistrate of Puwu and ordered all to lead relatives to dwell there.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，封純高陽侯。
entries.en: At Guangwu's accession Geng Chun became marquis of Gaoyang.
entries.literal: When the Shizu ascended the throne, he enfeoffed Chun as marquis of Gaoyang.

entries.zh: 擊劉永於濟陰，下定陶。
entries.en: He campaigned against Liu Yong in Jiyin and captured Dingtao.
entries.literal: He struck Liu Yong at Jiyin and took Dingtao.

entries.zh: 初，純從攻王郎，墮馬折肩，時疾發，乃還詣懷宮。
entries.en: Earlier, in the war on Wang Lang, he had broken a shoulder in a fall from his horse; now an old malady flared and he withdrew to the Huai palace.
entries.literal: At first, when Chun followed in attacking Wang Lang, he fell from a horse and broke his shoulder; at the time his illness broke out, and he thereupon returned to the Huai palace.

entries.zh: 帝問：『卿兄弟誰可使者？』
entries.en: The emperor asked, "Which of your brothers can I appoint to take your place?"
entries.literal: The Emperor asked: "Among your brothers, whom may be employed?"

entries.zh: 純舉從弟植，於是使植將純營，純猶以前將軍從。
entries.en: Geng Chun named his cousin Geng Zhi, who took command of his troops while Geng Chun kept the title of forward general in the field.
entries.literal: Chun nominated younger cousin Zhi; thereupon he ordered Zhi to lead Chun's camp, Chun still following as forward general.

entries.zh: 時真定王劉揚復造作讖記雲：『赤九之後，癭揚為主。』
entries.en: The Prince of Zhending, Liu Yang, was circulating forged prophecies: "After the house of the Red Ninth, the goitered Yang shall rule."
entries.literal: At that time the Prince of Zhending Liu Yang again forged prognostication texts saying: "After the Red Ninth, goiter Yang shall be lord."

entries.zh: 揚病癭，欲以惑眾，與綿曼賊交通。
entries.en: Liu Yang had a goiter and played on it to sway the crowd, while he colluded with the Mianman bandits.
entries.literal: Yang was ill with a goiter and wished thereby to delude the masses, and communicated with the bandits of Mianman.

entries.zh: 建武二年春，遣騎都尉陳副、遊擊將軍鄧隆征揚，揚閉城門，不內副等。
entries.en: In the spring of Jianwu 2, Guangwu sent Cavalry Commandant Chen Fu and Roaming-Attack General Deng Long to summon Liu Yang; Liu Yang shut the gates and refused to admit them.
entries.literal: In the spring of the second year of Jianwu, Guangwu sent Cavalry Commandant Chen Fu and Roaming-Attack General Deng Long to summon Liu Yang; Liu Yang shut the gates and refused to admit them.

entries.zh: 乃復遣純持節，行赦令於幽、冀，所過並使勞慰王侯。
entries.en: He then gave Geng Chun the staff of office to proclaim amnesty through You and Ji, comforting princes and marquises along the route.
entries.literal: He again sent Chun holding credentials, carrying out amnesty orders in You and Ji, and everywhere he passed also ordered comfort to princes and marquises.

entries.zh: 密敕純曰：『劉揚若見，因而收之。』
entries.en: His secret instruction: seize Liu Yang if he agrees to a meeting."
entries.literal: He secretly ordered Chun: "If Liu Yang should see you, then seize him."

entries.zh: 純從吏士百餘騎與副、隆會元氏，俱至真定，止傳舍。
entries.en: Geng Chun rode to Yuanshi with a hundred-odd horsemen, joined Chen Fu and Deng Long, and entered Zhending to the post station.
entries.literal: Chun with over a hundred mounted clerks and soldiers joined Fu and Long at Yuanshi, together reached Zhending, and stopped at the relay inn.

entries.zh: 揚稱病不謁，以純真定宗室之出，遣使與純書，欲相見。
entries.en: Liu Yang pleaded illness but, knowing Geng Chun's Zhending roots, sent a letter asking for a private meeting.
entries.literal: Yang claimed illness and did not pay visit; because Chun was of Zhending lineage stock, he sent an envoy with a letter to Chun, wishing to meet face to face.

entries.zh: 純報曰：『奉使見王侯牧守，不得先詣，如欲面會，宜出傳舍。』
entries.en: Geng Chun answered that envoys must wait on princes and governors, not the reverse—if Liu Yang wanted to talk, he should come to the station.
entries.literal: Chun replied: "I have been ordered to see princes, marquises, and shepherds and guards; I may not call on them first; if you wish a face meeting, you should come out to the relay inn."

entries.zh: 時，揚弟臨邑侯讓及從兄細各擁兵萬餘人，揚自恃眾強而純意安靜，即從官屬詣之，兄弟並將輕兵在門外。
entries.en: Liu Yang's brother Rang, marquis of Linyi, and cousin Xi each commanded ten thousand men; confident in his numbers, Liu Yang thought Geng Chun harmless and walked in with a light escort while his brothers waited outside with picked troops.
entries.literal: At that time Yang's younger brother the Marquis of Linyi Rang and elder cousin Xi each held troops over ten thousand; Yang relied on his mass strength while Chun's intention was quiet; he at once followed officials and retainers to visit him; the brothers together led light troops outside the gate.

entries.zh: 揚入見純，純接以禮敬，因延請其兄弟，皆入，乃閉閤悉誅之，因勒兵而出。
entries.en: Liu Yang entered; Geng Chun greeted him with elaborate courtesy, invited the brothers inside, then bolted the doors and cut them all down before leading his men into the street.
entries.literal: Yang entered to see Chun; Chun received him with ritual respect, and for that reason extended invitation to his brothers; when all had entered, he thereupon closed the doors and executed them all to the last, then ordered troops and went out.

entries.zh: 真定震怖，無敢動者。
entries.en: Zhending was paralyzed with fear; no one stirred.
entries.literal: Zhending was shaken and terrified; none dared move.

entries.zh: 帝憐揚、讓謀未發，並封其子，復故國。
entries.en: The emperor noted that Liu Yang and Liu Rang had not yet openly rebelled, so he enfeoffed their sons and restored their old titles out of mercy.
entries.literal: The Emperor pitied that Yang and Rang's plot had not yet broken forth, and together enfeoffed their sons, restoring the former states.

entries.zh: 純還京師，因自請曰：『臣本吏家子孫，幸遭大漢復興，聖帝受命，備位列將，爵為通侯。
entries.en: Back at the capital Geng Chun petitioned the throne: "I began as a clerk's son who caught the fortune of Han's restoration. Your majesty received Heaven's charge; I rose among the generals to a full marquis's rank.
entries.literal: Chun returned to the capital and on his own requested: "I was originally a descendant of a clerk's household; fortunately I encountered great Han's restoration, the sage emperor received the mandate; I was fully arrayed among the ranked generals, my nobility is a full marquis.

entries.zh: 天下略定，臣無所用誌，願試治一郡，盡力自效。』
entries.en: The empire is nearly at peace, and I have little left to do as a soldier. Let me try a single commandery and spend whatever strength I have there."
entries.literal: The realm is in the main settled; I have no use in which to record my will; I beg to try governing one commandery and exhaust my strength in self-service."

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：『卿既治武，復欲修文邪？』
entries.en: The emperor smiled. "You have worn armor all your life—now you want to take up the ink brush?"
entries.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "You already administer martial affairs; do you again wish to cultivate civil affairs?"

entries.zh: 乃拜純為東郡太守。
entries.en: He named Geng Chun governor of Dongjun.
entries.literal: Thereupon he appointed Chun governor of Dongjun.

entries.zh: 時，東郡未平，純視事數月，盜賊清寧。
entries.en: Dongjun was still unsettled when he arrived, but within a few months he had cleared the banditry and restored calm.
entries.literal: At that time Dongjun was not yet pacified; Chun assumed office several months, and bandits were cleared and at peace.

entries.zh: 四年，詔純將兵擊更始東平太守範荊，荊降。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Jianwu he sent Geng Chun against Fan Jing, the Gengshi governor of Dongping, who capitulated.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he ordered Chun to lead troops to strike Gengshi's governor of Dongping Fan Jing; Jing surrendered.

entries.zh: 進擊太山濟南及平原賊，皆平之。
entries.en: He then campaigned through Taishan, Jinan, and Pingyuan until every rebel band in the region was broken.
entries.literal: He advanced to strike the bandits of Taishan, Jinan, and Pingyuan, and all pacified them.

entries.zh: 居東郡四歲，時發幹長有罪，純案奏，圍守之，奏未下，長自殺。
entries.en: Four years into his tenure the magistrate of Fagan county broke the law; Geng Chun impeached him and had him confined pending the throne's ruling. Before the rescript came down the man took his own life.
entries.literal: He dwelt in Dongjun four years; at that time the magistrate of Fagan county committed a crime; Chun investigated and memorialized, besieged and guarded him; before the memorial came down, the magistrate committed suicide.

entries.zh: 純坐免，以列侯奉朝請。
entries.en: Geng Chun was stripped of office for the affair but kept his marquis rank and continued to attend court as fengchaoqing.
entries.literal: Chun was sitting dismissed; as full marquis he attended court audience.

entries.zh: 從擊董憲，道過東郡，百姓老小數千隨東駕涕泣，雲『願復得耿君』。
entries.en: On the march against Dong Xian his column crossed Dongjun. Thousands of old and young trailed the imperial train in tears, crying, "Give us Lord Geng again."
entries.literal: He followed in striking Dong Xian; passing through Dongjun, several thousand old and young of the common people followed the imperial carriage weeping, saying, "We wish again to obtain Lord Geng."

entries.zh: 帝謂公卿曰：『純年少被甲胄為軍吏耳，治郡乃能見思若是乎？』
entries.en: The emperor remarked to his ministers, "I knew Geng Chun only as the young officer in mail—who would have thought a turn as governor would win him such love?"
entries.literal: The Emperor said to the dukes: "Chun in youth wore armor and helmet as a military clerk—governing a commandery could make him longed for like this?"

entries.zh: 六年，定封為東光侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 6 his title was fixed as marquis of Dongguang.
entries.literal: In the sixth year his fief was fixed as marquis of Dongguang.

entries.zh: 純辭就國，帝曰：『文帝謂周勃「丞相吾所重，君為我率諸侯就國」，今亦然也。』
entries.en: When Geng Chun asked leave to retire to his fief, the emperor quoted Emperor Wen of Former Han to Zhou Bo: "The chancellor is indispensable to me, but you must still lead the marquises home to their estates." "The same holds now," he said.
entries.literal: Chun took leave to go to his state; the Emperor said: "Wen Di said to Zhou Bo, 'The chancellor is what I esteem; you for me lead the marquises to their states'—now it is likewise."

entries.zh: 純受詔而去。
entries.en: Geng Chun bowed to the decree and left the capital.
entries.literal: Chun received the edict and departed.

entries.zh: 至鄴，賜谷萬斛。
entries.en: At Ye he received an imperial gift of ten thousand hu of grain.
entries.literal: When he reached Ye, he was granted ten thousand hu of grain.

entries.zh: 到國，吊死問病，民愛敬之。
entries.en: Once home he mourned the dead and inquired after the sick; the people loved and honored him for it.
entries.literal: When he arrived in his state, he condoled the dead and asked after illness; the people loved and revered him.

entries.zh: 八年，東郡、濟陰盜賊群起，遣大司空李通、橫野大將軍王常擊之。
entries.en: In Jianwu 8 rebels erupted across Dongjun and Jiyin; the court dispatched Grand Minister of Works Li Tong and Grand General Who Sweeps the Wilderness Wang Chang against them.
entries.literal: In the eighth year bandits of Dongjun and Jiyin rose in groups; he sent Grand Minister of Works Li Tong and Grand General Who Sweeps the Wilderness Wang Chang to strike them.

entries.zh: 帝以純威信著於衛地，遣使拜太中大夫，使與大兵會東郡。
entries.en: Because Geng Chun's name still commanded fear and trust on the Wei plain, the emperor named him grand counselor of the palace and sent him to coordinate with the main host in Dongjun.
entries.literal: The Emperor because Chun's awe and trust were manifest in Wei territory sent an envoy to appoint him grand counselor of the palace and ordered him to join the great army at Dongjun.

entries.zh: 東郡聞純入界，盜賊九千餘人皆詣純降，大兵不戰而還。
entries.en: Word that Geng Chun had crossed the commandery line brought more than nine thousand outlaws to his camp to yield; the expeditionary army marched home without a fight.
entries.literal: When Dongjun heard Chun had entered the border, over nine thousand bandits all came to Chun to surrender; the great army returned without battle.

entries.zh: 璽書復以為東郡太守，吏民悅服。
entries.en: A second edict restored him as governor of Dongjun, to the delight of every clerk and farmer under his rule.
entries.literal: An imperial writ again made him governor of Dongjun; officials and people were pleased and submitted.

entries.zh: 十三年，卒官，謚曰成侯。
entries.en: He died in office in Jianwu 13 and received the posthumous title Marquis Cheng, "Accomplished."
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office; his posthumous title was Marquis Cheng.

entries.zh: 子阜嗣。
entries.en: His son Geng Fu inherited the marquisate.
entries.literal: His son Fu succeeded.

entries.zh: 任光字伯卿，南陽宛人也。
entries.en: Ren Guang, styled Boqing, came from Wan in Nanyang commandery.
entries.literal: Ren Guang, courtesy name Boqing, was a native of Wan in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 少忠厚，為鄉裏所愛。
entries.en: From boyhood he was known for honesty and loyalty, and his neighbors held him in affection.
entries.literal: In youth he was honest and loyal, and was loved by his village and district.

entries.zh: 初為鄉嗇夫、郡縣吏。
entries.en: He began his career as a village overseer and then as a clerk in the commandery and county offices.
entries.literal: At first he served as village sefu and as clerk in the commandery and county.

entries.zh: 漢兵至宛，軍人見光冠服鮮明，令解衣，將殺而奪之。
entries.en: When imperial forces reached Wan, some soldiers spotted Ren Guang's fine hat and robes, ordered him to undress, and were about to kill him for the plunder.
entries.literal: When Han troops reached Wan, soldiers saw that Guang's cap and garments were bright and fine; they ordered him to strip, intending to kill him and seize them.

entries.zh: 會光祿勛劉賜適至，視光容貌長者，乃救全之。
entries.en: Superintendent of the Household Liu Ci happened to arrive, took one look at Ren Guang's dignified bearing, and intervened to spare his life.
entries.literal: It happened that Superintendent of the Household Liu Ci arrived, looked at Guang's bearing as that of an elder man, and thereupon saved him and kept him whole.

entries.zh: 光因率黨與從賜，為安集掾，拜偏將軍，與世祖破王尋、王邑。
entries.en: Ren Guang then brought his followers to Liu Ci's service as an adjutant for pacification, was commissioned lieutenant general, and fought beside Emperor Guangwu to defeat Wang Xun and Wang Yi.
entries.literal: Guang thereupon led his clique and followers to join Ci, served as an Anji adjutant, was appointed lieutenant general, and with the Shizu defeated Wang Xun and Wang Yi.

entries.zh: 時，光武初即位，先訪求茂，茂詣河陽謁見。
entries.en: Guangwu had scarcely taken the throne when he sent for Zhuo Mao; Mao traveled to Heyang for his audience.
entries.literal: At this time, when Guangwu had first ascended the throne, he first sought out Mao; Mao went to Heyang for audience.

entries.zh: 乃下詔曰『前密令卓茂，束身自修，執節淳固，誠能為人所不能為。
entries.en: The emperor then proclaimed: "The former magistrate of Mi, Zhuo Mao, disciplined himself, lived plainly, and held fast to principle—he did what ordinary men cannot.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued saying, "The former magistrate of Mi, Zhuo Mao, restrained himself and cultivated himself, held to integrity purely and firmly—truly able to do what others cannot do.

entries.zh: 夫名冠天下，當受天下重賞，故武王誅紂，封比幹之墓，表商容之閭。
entries.en: A reputation that towers over the empire deserves the empire's richest honors—King Wu slew Zhou yet honored Bi Gan's grave and marked Shang Rong's gate.
entries.literal: One whose fame crowns the realm ought to receive the realm's weighty reward; therefore King Wu punished Zhou and sealed Bi Gan's tomb and marked Shang Rong's lane.

entries.zh: 今以茂為太傅，封褒德侯，食邑二千戶，賜幾杖、車馬，衣一襲，絮五百斤。』
entries.en: We therefore name Mao Grand Tutor and Marquis Who Extols Virtue with a fief of two thousand households, and present him with an honor seat and staff, a carriage team, a full set of robes, and five hundred jin of padded silk."
entries.literal: Now appoint Mao as Grand Tutor, enfeoff him as Marquis Who Extols Virtue with two thousand household fief, grant him a bench and staff, carriage and horses, one suit of clothes, and five hundred jin of silk wadding."

entries.zh: 復以茂長子戎為太中大夫，次子崇為中郎，給事黃門。
entries.en: Mao's eldest son Rong is named Grand Counselor of the Palace and his second son Chong Gentleman of the Household in attendance at the Yellow Gates.
entries.literal: Moreover appoint Mao's eldest son Rong as Grand Counselor of the Palace, second son Chong as Gentleman of the Household, to serve in the Yellow Gates.

entries.zh: 建武四年，薨，賜棺槨冢地，車駕素服親臨送葬。
entries.en: He died in Jianwu 4; the court supplied coffin, burial vault, and tomb ground, and the emperor himself, in mourning white, attended the burial.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he died; a coffin, outer shell, and burial ground were granted; the imperial carriage in plain dress personally attended the funeral.

entries.zh: 初，茂與同縣孔休、陳留蔡勛、安眾劉宣、楚國龔勝、上黨鮑宣六人同志，不仕王莽時，並名重當時。
entries.en: Earlier Zhuo Mao and five like-minded men from his county and beyond—Kong Xiu, Cai Xun, Liu Xuan, Gong Sheng, and Bao Xuan—refused office under Wang Mang and were all famed in their day.
entries.literal: Earlier Mao with Kong Xiu of the same county, Cai Xun of Chenliu, Liu Xuan of Anzhong, Gong Sheng of Chu, and Bao Xuan of Shangdang—six men of one purpose—refused office under Wang Mang and were all famed in their time.

entries.zh: 休字子泉，哀帝初，守新都令。
entries.en: Kong Xiu, styled Ziquan, early in Emperor Ai's reign served as magistrate of Xindu.
entries.literal: Xiu, courtesy name Ziquan, early in Emperor Ai's reign served as magistrate of Xindu.

entries.zh: 後王莽秉權，休去官歸家。
entries.en: When Wang Mang seized power, Kong Xiu resigned and went home.
entries.literal: Later, when Wang Mang seized power, Xiu left office and returned home.

entries.zh: 及莽篡位，遣使賫玄纁、束帛，請為國師，遂歐血託病，杜門自絕。
entries.en: When Mang usurped the throne he sent envoys with ceremonial silks inviting Kong Xiu to serve as National Teacher; Xiu spat blood, feigned illness, shut his gate, and cut himself off.
entries.literal: When Mang usurped the throne he sent envoys bearing dark and crimson silks and bundles of silk to invite him as National Teacher; Xiu then spat blood and feigned illness, shut his gate, and cut himself off.

entries.zh: 光武即位，求休、勛子孫，賜穀以旌顯之。
entries.en: When Guangwu took the throne he sought descendants of Kong Xiu and Cai Xun and granted grain to honor them.
entries.literal: When Guangwu took the throne he sought out the descendants of Xiu and Xun and granted grain to honor them.

entries.zh: 劉宣字子高，安眾侯崇之從弟，知王莽當篡，乃變名姓，抱經書隱避林藪。
entries.en: Liu Xuan, styled Zigao, a cousin of Marquis Chong of Anzhong, foresaw Wang Mang's usurpation, changed his name, and hid in the wilds with his classics.
entries.literal: Liu Xuan, courtesy name Zigao, was a younger cousin of Marquis Chong of Anzhong; knowing Wang Mang would usurp, he changed his name, clutched the classics, and hid in forests and marshes.

entries.zh: 建武初乃出，光武以宣襲封安眾侯。
entries.en: Early in Jianwu he emerged, and Guangwu had him inherit the marquisate of Anzhong.
entries.literal: Early in Jianwu he emerged; Guangwu had Xuan inherit enfeoffment as Marquis of Anzhong.

entries.zh: 擢龔勝子賜為上谷太守。
entries.en: He promoted Gong Sheng's son Ci to grand administrator of Shanggu.
entries.literal: He elevated Gong Sheng's son Ci to grand administrator of Shanggu.

entries.zh: 勝、鮑宣事在《前書》。
entries.en: Accounts of Gong Sheng and Bao Xuan appear in the Former Book.
entries.literal: The affairs of Sheng and Bao Xuan are in the Former Book.

entries.zh: 勛事在玄孫邕傳。
entries.en: Cai Xun's story appears in the biography of his descendant Cai Yong.
entries.literal: Xun's affairs are in the biography of his great-great-grandson Yong.

entries.zh: 論曰：建武之初，雄豪方擾，虓呼者連響，嬰城者相望，斯固倥傯不暇給之日。
entries.en: The appraisal: In the early Jianwu years warlords churned the realm—battle cries echoed from column to column and rival garrisons faced off across the landscape; the empire barely kept pace with its crises.
entries.literal: The historian's judgment says: At the beginning of Jianwu, heroic strongmen were everywhere in turmoil; those who roared answered one another in succession; those who defended walled cities faced one another across the landscape—this was truly a day of pressing urgency when nothing could be spared.

entries.zh: 卓茂斷斷小宰，無它庸能，時已七十餘矣，而首加聘命，優辭重禮，其與周、燕之君表閭立館何異哉？
entries.en: Zhuo Mao was only an honest county officer without dazzling talent—past seventy—yet Guangwu singled him out first with lavish honors; how was that any less than ancient kings honoring virtuous commoners with inscribed gates and endowed halls?
entries.literal: Zhuo Mao was an upright petty magistrate without other mediocre abilities; already he was over seventy, yet first appointment was conferred on him with gracious words and heavy ritual—how does this differ from the rulers of Zhou and Yan marking lanes and establishing lodges?

entries.zh: 於是蘊憤歸道之賓，越關阻，捐宗族，以排金門者眾矣。
entries.en: Scholars nursing grievances yet cleaving to principle crossed frontier barriers and left family estates behind to throng the palace gates.
entries.literal: Thereupon guests harboring resentment who returned to the Way, crossed barriers and passes, cast aside clan and kin to crowd toward the golden gates—were many.

entries.zh: 夫厚性寬中近於仁，犯而不校鄰於恕，率斯道也，怨悔曷其至乎！
entries.en: A generous temper and calm heart skirt benevolence; to endure insult without answering approaches true forgiveness—live like that, and what room remains for bitterness?
entries.literal: Now a generous nature and broad center approach benevolence; being offended yet not retaliating borders on forgiveness—whoever follows this Way, how could resentment and regret reach him!

entries.zh: 卓茂字子康，南陽宛人也。
entries.en: Zhuo Mao, whose courtesy name was Zikang, came from Wan in Nanyang.
entries.literal: Zhuo Mao, courtesy name Zikang, was a man of Wan in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 父祖皆至郡守。
entries.en: His father and grandfather had both reached the rank of grand administrator.
entries.literal: His father and grandfather both rose to the office of grand administrator of a commandery.

entries.zh: 茂，元帝時學於長安，事博士江生，習《詩》、《禮》及歷算。
entries.en: Under Emperor Yuan, Mao studied in Chang'an under Erudite Jiang, mastering the Odes and Rites as well as astronomy and mathematics.
entries.literal: Mao, during the time of Emperor Yuan, studied in Chang'an, served Erudite Jiang, and studied the Odes, the Rites, and calendrical reckoning.

entries.zh: 究極師法，稱為通儒。
entries.en: He mastered his teachers' tradition completely and was honored as a scholar of wide learning.
entries.literal: He exhausted his teachers' methods and was called a thoroughly learned Confucian.

entries.zh: 性寬仁恭愛。
entries.en: He was by nature generous, humane, deferential, and affectionate.
entries.literal: By nature he was tolerant, humane, respectful, and loving.

entries.zh: 鄉黨故舊，雖行能與茂不同，而皆愛慕欣欣焉。
entries.en: Neighbors and old friends whose talents and conduct did not match his still cherished him warmly.
entries.literal: Fellow villagers and old acquaintances, although their conduct and abilities differed from Mao's, all loved and admired him happily.

entries.zh: 丹子有同門生喪家，家在中山，白丹欲往奔慰。
entries.en: Wang Dan's son had a classmate whose family was in mourning in Zhongshan; the boy asked leave to rush there in person.
entries.literal: Dan's son had a fellow student whose family had a bereavement; the home was in Zhongshan, and he informed Dan wishing to go hasten to console.

entries.zh: 結侶將行，丹怒而撻之，令寄縑以祠焉。
entries.en: He was gathering travel companions when Wang Dan beat him in anger and told him to send a bolt of silk for the rites instead.
entries.literal: He tied companions and was about to set out; Dan angrily flogged him and ordered him to send silk by post for sacrifice there.

entries.zh: 或問其故，丹曰：『交道之難，未易言也。
entries.en: Asked why, Wang Dan said, 'The pitfalls of friendship are not easily put into words.'
entries.literal: Someone asked the reason; Dan said, 'The difficulty of friendship is not easy to speak of.'

entries.zh: 世稱管、鮑，次則王、貢。
entries.en: The world praises Guan Zhong and Bao Shuya; next come Wang Ji and Gong Yu.
entries.literal: The age praises Guan and Bao; next come Wang and Gong.

entries.zh: 張、陳兇其終，蕭，朱隙其末，故知全之者鮮矣。』
entries.en: Zhang Er and Chen Yu destroyed each other; Xiao Yu and Zhu Bo fell out at the end—so few friendships stay whole."
entries.literal: Zhang and Chen came to a disastrous end in their friendship; Xiao and Zhu fell out at the last—therefore one knows those who preserve friendship to the end are few."

entries.zh: 時人服其言。
entries.en: His contemporaries conceded the point.
entries.literal: People of the time submitted to his words.

entries.zh: 父卒，襲封。
entries.en: He succeeded to the title when his father died.
entries.literal: When his father died, he inherited the fief.

entries.zh: 出為弘農太守，轉右扶風。
entries.en: He served as grand administrator of Hongnong, then as right administrator of Fufeng.
entries.literal: He went out as grand administrator of Hongnong, then transferred to right Administrator of Fufeng.

entries.zh: 公事去官，征拜城門校尉，轉將作大匠，遷少府，又轉大鴻臚。
entries.en: He left office over an official matter, was recalled as colonel of the city gates, then court architect, privy treasurer, and finally grand herald.
entries.literal: For public affairs he left office, was summoned and appointed Colonel of the City Gates, transferred to Court Architect, transferred to Privy Treasurer, again transferred to Grand Herald.

entries.zh: 時，恩澤諸侯以無勞受封，群臣不悅而莫敢諫，典獨奏曰：『夫無功而賞，勞者不勸，上忝下辱，亂象幹度。
entries.en: When court favorites won marquisates without service, the ministers fumed in silence; Zhao Dian alone wrote, 'Reward without work discourages the deserving, shames the throne, insults the people, and lets disorder mock Heaven's pattern.'
entries.literal: At that time enfeoffed marquises of favor received fiefs without merit; the host of ministers was displeased yet none dared remonstrate; Dian alone submitted memorial, saying, 'When there is reward without merit, those who labor are not encouraged; above is shamed, below insulted, and disorderly signs interfere with the celestial norm.'

entries.zh: 且高祖之誓，非功臣不封。
entries.en: Moreover the founder swore that no man without merit should be enfeoffed.'
entries.literal: Moreover Gaozu's oath was: unless a meritorious minister, do not enfeoff.'

entries.zh: 宜一切削免爵士，以存舊典。』
entries.en: Strip these sinecures away and restore the old standard.'
entries.literal: It is fitting utterly to strip away titles and fiefs, in order to preserve the old norm.'

entries.zh: 帝不從。
entries.en: The emperor would not agree.
entries.literal: The emperor did not follow.

entries.zh: 頃之，轉太仆，遷太常。
entries.en: Soon he moved to grand coachman, then grand master of ceremonies.
entries.literal: Before long, he transferred to Grand Coachman, transferred to Grand Master of Ceremonies.

entries.zh: 朝廷每有災異疑議，輒咨問之。
entries.en: Whenever omens or disputed policy troubled the court, it turned to him for judgment.
entries.literal: Whenever the court had prodigies or doubtful points for deliberation, it always consulted and asked him.

entries.zh: 典據經正對，無所曲折。
entries.en: Zhao Dian answered from the classics without trimming his words.
entries.literal: Dian according to the classics answered straight, without twisting.

entries.zh: 每得賞賜，輒分與諸生之貧者。
entries.en: Every imperial gift he shared with his neediest pupils.
entries.literal: Whenever he obtained rewards and gifts, he always divided them among the students who were poor.

entries.zh: 後以諫爭違旨，免官就國。
entries.en: He later lost office for opposing the throne too bluntly and retired to his fief.
entries.literal: Later for remonstrating and disputing contrary to imperial intent, he was dismissed from office and went to his state.

entries.zh: 宣秉字巨公，馮翊雲陽人也。
entries.en: Xuan Bing, styled Jugong, came from Yunyang in Fengyi.
entries.literal: Xuan Bing, courtesy name Jugong, was a man of Yunyang in Fengyi commandery.

entries.zh: 少修高節，顯名三輔。
entries.en: From his youth he upheld a stern moral standard and made a name for himself across the Three Adjuncts.
entries.literal: In youth he cultivated lofty integrity and became famous in the Three Adjuncts.

entries.zh: 哀、平際，見王氏據權專政，侵削宗室，有逆亂萌，遂隱遁深山，州郡連召，常稱疾不仕。
entries.en: Under Emperors Ai and Ping, when he saw the Wang family monopolize power, chip away at the imperial clan, and the makings of revolt take shape, he withdrew to the deep hills; though province after province called him to serve, he always pleaded illness and stayed out of office.
entries.literal: Between the reigns of Ai and Ping, seeing the Wang clan seize power and monopolize government, encroach on and diminish the imperial house, and the sprouts of rebellion and disorder appear, he thereupon hid himself in deep mountains; the province and commanderies summoned him in succession, but he constantly claimed illness and did not take office.

entries.zh: 王莽為宰衡，辟命不應。
entries.en: When Wang Mang held the title of supreme minister and summoned him to office, he refused the appointment.
entries.literal: When Wang Mang was Grand Regent, he summoned him with a commission, but he did not respond.

entries.zh: 及莽篡位，又遣使者征之，秉固稱疾病。
entries.en: After Wang Mang seized the throne and again sent envoys for him, Xuan Bing insisted he was too ill to come.
entries.literal: When Mang usurped the throne, he again sent envoys to summon him, but Bing firmly claimed illness.

entries.zh: 更始即位，征為侍中。
entries.en: When the Gengshi Emperor took the throne, Xuan Bing was called to court as a palace attendant.
entries.literal: When Gengshi ascended the throne, he was summoned to be Palace Attendant.

entries.zh: 建武元年，拜禦史中丞。
entries.en: In Jianwu 1 he was named imperial clerk grandee.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, he was appointed Imperial Clerk Grandee.

entries.zh: 光武特詔禦史中丞與司隸校尉、尚書令會同並專席而坐，故京師號曰『三獨坐』。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu issued a special order that the imperial clerk grandee, the metropolitan commandant, and the director of the secretariat should hold joint sessions, each with his own seat—hence the capital nickname 'the three solitary seats.'
entries.literal: Guangwu specially issued an edict that the Imperial Clerk Grandee, the Metropolitan Commandant, and the Director of the Secretariat should meet and sit each on a separate mat; therefore in the capital they were called the 'Three Solitary Seats.'

entries.zh: 明年，遷司隸校尉。
entries.en: The following year he was promoted to metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: The next year, he was transferred to Metropolitan Commandant.

entries.zh: 務舉大綱，簡略苛細，百僚敬之。
entries.en: He focused on the broad principles of government and eased petty severity, and the whole bureaucracy stood in awe of him.
entries.literal: He strove to lift up the great principles and was lenient toward harsh minutiae; the hundred officials revered him.

entries.zh: 哀、平間，位不過郎。
entries.en: Under Emperors Ai and Ping he never rose above gentleman cadet.
entries.literal: Between Ai and Ping, his rank did not exceed gentleman.

entries.zh: 傅皇后父孔鄉侯晏深善於譚。
entries.en: Fu Yan, father of Empress Fu and marquis of Kongxiang, was Huan Tan's close friend.
entries.literal: The father of Empress Fu, Marquis of Kongxiang Yan, was deeply on good terms with Tan.

entries.zh: 是時，高安侯董賢寵倖，女弟為昭儀，皇后日已疏，晏嘿嘿不得意。
entries.en: Dong Xian of Gao'an was the emperor's favorite; his sister was a brilliant companion, while Empress Fu drifted daily into neglect—Fu Yan brooded in silence.
entries.literal: At that time Marquis of Gao'an Dong Xian was favored and beloved; his younger sister was Brilliant Companion; the empress daily was already estranged; Yan silently was discontented.

entries.zh: 譚進說曰：“昔武帝欲立衛子夫，陰求陳皇后之過，而陳後終廢，子夫竟立。
entries.en: Huan Tan urged him: "When Emperor Wu wanted Lady Wei as empress, he secretly hunted faults in Empress Chen until she fell and Wei Zifu took her place.
entries.literal: Tan advanced persuasion, saying, "In the past Emperor Wu wished to establish Wei Zifu; he secretly sought faults of Empress Chen, and in the end Empress Chen was deposed and Zifu was at last established.

entries.zh: 今董賢至愛而女弟尤幸，殆將有子夫之變，可不憂哉！”
entries.en: Today Dong Xian and his sister hold the inner palace—you may face the same coup in reverse; can you afford not to worry!"
entries.literal: Now Dong Xian is supremely loved and his younger sister is especially favored—there is peril of a Zifu-style shift; can one not worry!"

entries.zh: 晏驚動，曰：“然，為之奈何？”
entries.en: Fu Yan started and said, "True enough—what should we do?"
entries.literal: Yan was startled and moved, and said, "So—what is to be done about it?"

entries.zh: 譚曰：“刑罰不能加無罪，邪枉不能勝正人。
entries.en: Huan Tan answered, "The law cannot strike the innocent, and intrigue cannot defeat an upright heart.
entries.literal: Tan said, "Punishment cannot be applied to the guiltless; crookedness cannot overcome the upright man.

entries.zh: 夫士以才智要君，女以媚道求主。
entries.en: Men win rulers by talent; women win them by charm.
entries.literal: The gentleman by wit and wisdom importunes the ruler; the woman by the way of allurement seeks the master.

entries.zh: 皇后年少，希更艱難，或驅使醫巫，外求方技，此不可不番。
entries.en: The empress is young and little tested; under strain she may turn to healers, shamans, and occult arts—watch that closely.
entries.literal: The empress is young, rarely having undergone hardship; perhaps she will be driven to employ physicians and shamans and seek arts outside—this cannot but be examined carefully.

entries.zh: 又君侯以後父尊重而多通賓客，必藉以重勢，貽致譏議。
entries.en: You stand high as the empress's father yet traffic with a wide circle of clients—that borrowed weight will draw slander.
entries.literal: Moreover, my lord, as the empress's father you are honored and weighty yet widely receive guests; you are sure to borrow thereby to add to your power and bring on ridicule and criticism.

entries.zh: 不如謝遣門徒，務執廉愨，此修己正家避禍之道也。”
entries.en: Better send your hangers-on away and live modestly—that is how to mend your own house and dodge disaster."
entries.literal: It would be better to dismiss your followers and strive to hold incorrupt sincerity—this is the way to cultivate oneself, rectify the family, and avoid calamity."

entries.zh: 晏曰：“善”。
entries.en: Fu Yan said, "Well spoken."
entries.literal: Yan said, "Good."

entries.zh: 遂罷遣常客，入白皇后，如譚所戒。
entries.en: He dismissed his regular clients, entered the palace, and warned the empress as Huan Tan had advised.
entries.literal: Thereupon he dismissed and sent away his constant guests, entered and reported to the empress, as Tan had warned.

entries.zh: 後賢果風太醫令真欽，使求傅氏罪過，遂逮後弟侍中喜，詔獄無所得，乃解，故傅氏終全於哀帝之時。
entries.en: Dong Xian later prompted the court physician Zhen Qin to dig up dirt on the Fu family and had the empress's brother Fu Xi, a palace attendant, thrown into the imperial jail—but nothing was proved, so the case collapsed and the Fu clan survived Emperor Ai's reign.
entries.literal: Later Xian indeed hinted to Grand Physician-in-chief Zhen Qin, causing him to seek faults of the Fu clan; thereupon they arrested the empress's younger brother, Palace Attendant Xi, but in the edict-ordered prison nothing was obtained, and then it was released; therefore the Fu clan in the end was preserved whole in the time of Emperor Ai.

entries.zh: 及董賢為大司馬，聞譚名，欲與之交。
entries.en: When Dong Xian rose to grand marshal he sought Huan Tan's friendship by reputation.
entries.literal: When Dong Xian became Grand Marshal, he heard Tan's name and wished to befriend him.

entries.zh: 譚先奏書於賢，說以輔國保身之術，賢不能用，遂不與通。
entries.en: Huan Tan wrote first, offering Dong Xian ways to serve the state and save himself; Dong Xian ignored the counsel, so Huan Tan refused all further contact.
entries.literal: Tan first submitted a letter to Xian, explaining to him the arts of assisting the state and preserving the self; Xian could not use it, and thereupon Tan did not communicate with him.

entries.zh: 當王莽居攝篡弑之際，天下之士，莫不竟褒稱德美，作符命以求容媚，譚獨自守，默然無言。
entries.en: While Wang Mang acted as regent and seized the throne, every scholar vied to flatter him with forged prophecies; Huan Tan alone stayed silent and kept his integrity.
entries.literal: At the time when Wang Mang held the regency and usurped and murdered, the gentlemen of the realm none did not compete to praise and declare his virtue and beauty, composing token prophecies to seek accommodation and flattery; Tan alone kept himself and was silent without words.

entries.zh: 莽時為掌樂大夫，更始立，召拜太中大夫。
entries.en: Under Wang Mang he served as grandee for music; the Gengshi Emperor named him grandee of the palace.
entries.literal: In Mang's time he was grandee for music; when Gengshi was established, he was summoned and appointed Grandee of the Palace.

entries.zh: 伏念天上離王莽之害久矣。
entries.en: All under heaven has suffered Wang Mang's scourge long enough.
entries.literal: Bowed in thought: all under heaven has long been parted from Wang Mang's harm.

entries.zh: 始自東郡之師，繼以西海之役，巴、蜀沒于南夷，緣邊破于北狄，遠征萬里，暴兵累年，禍拏未解，兵連不息，刑法彌深，賦斂愈重。
entries.en: From the eastern campaigns to the western wars, Shu swallowed by southern tribes, the frontier broken by the Xiongnu, armies abroad for years, taxes crushing, the law a tightening noose—
entries.literal: Beginning with the army from Dong commandery, continuing to the campaign on the western sea, Ba and Shu sank in the southern barbarians, the border was broken by the northern Di, distant expeditions ten thousand li, exposed troops piled year on year, the grip of calamity not loosened, weapons linked without cease, punishments grew ever deeper, taxes and levies grew heavier.

entries.zh: 眾強之黨，橫擊於外，百僚之臣，貪殘於內，元元無聊，饑寒並臻，父子流亡，夫婦離散，廬落丘墟，田疇蕪穢，疾疫大興，災異蜂起。
entries.en: —strongmen rampaged abroad, officials devoured within, the people starved and froze, families broke, villages turned to ash, plague and omen followed one another.
entries.literal: Factions of the powerful struck outward; the hundred officials' ministers were greedy and cruel within; the common folk had no relief, hunger and cold arrived together, fathers and sons wandered in exile, husbands and wives were scattered, hamlets became mounds and ruins, fields were overgrown and foul, great pestilence arose, prodigies swarmed like bees.

entries.zh: 於是江湖之上，海岱之濱，風騰波湧，更相駘藉，四垂之人，肝腦塗地，死亡之數，不啻太半，殃咎之毒，痛入骨髓，匹夫僮婦，鹹懷怨怒。
entries.en: Along the great rivers and eastern coast mobs surged and trampled one another; beyond the heartland half the people were dead, hatred gnawed to the bone, every peasant and bondmaid nursed rage.
entries.literal: Thereupon on the Yangtze and the lakes, along the coast of sea and Mount Dai, wind rose and waves surged, trampling one another in succession; the people of the four margins smeared liver and brains on the earth; the count of the dead was not less than more than half; the poison of disaster and fault bit into marrow and bone; common men and slave wives all harbored resentment and anger.

entries.zh: 皇帝以聖德靈威，龍興鳳舉，率宛、葉之眾，將散亂之兵，喢血昆陽，長驅武關，破百萬之陳，摧九虎之軍，雷震四海，席捲天下，攘除禍亂，誅滅無道，一期之間，海內大定。
entries.en: Then our emperor rose like dragon and phoenix, led the men of Wan and Ye, shattered a million foemen at Kunyang, stormed Wuguan, broke the Nine Tigers—thunder across the empire, the realm rolled up in one sweep, the wicked cut down, and in a single turning the land knew peace.
entries.literal: The emperor by sagely virtue and numinous might, dragon rising and phoenix lifting, leading the hosts of Wan and Ye, commanding scattered troops, gnawed blood at Kunyang, drove long at Wuguan, broke formations of a million, crushed the army of the Nine Tigers, thunder shook the four seas, rolled up the realm like a mat, swept away disaster and disorder, executed and destroyed the lawless—in the space of one cycle within the seas there was great peace.

entries.zh: 繼高祖之休烈，修文武之絕業，社稷複存，炎精更輝，德冠往初，功無與二。
entries.en: He took up Gaozu's torch, restored the broken work of Wen and Wu, relit Han's red mandate, outshone every predecessor, matched by no successor.
entries.literal: He continued Gaozu's splendid blaze, repaired the cut thread of Wen and Wu's work; the altars of soil and grain again stood, the fiery essence of Han blazed anew; virtue crowned all beginnings, merit matched by none.

entries.zh: 天下自以去亡新，就聖漢，當蒙其福而賴其願。
entries.en: The people thought they had shed Xin and come home to Han, ready for mercy and reward.
entries.literal: All under heaven by themselves thought they had cast off perished Xin and drawn near to sagely Han; they ought to receive its blessing and rely on its wish.

entries.zh: 樹恩布德，易以周洽，其猶順驚風而飛鴻毛也。
entries.en: Kindness shown now would spread as fast as downwind feathers.
entries.literal: To plant favor and spread virtue is easy to reach everywhere; it is still like following a startled wind and flying goose feathers.

entries.zh: 然而諸將虜掠，逆倫絕理，殺人父子，妻人婦女，燔其室屋，略其財產，饑者毛食，寒者裸跣，冤結失望，無所歸命。
entries.en: Yet your generals looted, murdered fathers and sons, seized wives, torched homes, stripped the starving and shamed the cold until the people had nowhere to appeal.
entries.literal: Yet the various generals plundered, reversed norm and cut principle, killed people's fathers and sons, took others' wives and women, burned their houses, seized their goods and property; the hungry gnawed scraps, the cold went naked and barefoot; wrongs knotted and hope failed, there was nowhere to turn for life.

entries.zh: 今大將軍以明淑之德，秉大使之權，統三軍之政，存撫并州之人，惠愛之誠，加乎百姓，高世之聲，聞乎群士，故其延頸企踵而望者，非特一人也。
entries.en: You, great marshal, are clear in virtue, hold imperial mandate, command three armies, cherish Bingzhou—the people strain to hear one kind word from you; you are not speaking to a single listener.
entries.literal: Now the grand marshal by enlightened and pure virtue holds the great envoy's authority, commands the three armies' government, cherishes and soothes the people of Bing province; the sincerity of kindness and love extends to the hundred surnames; the sound of transcending the age is heard among the host of gentlemen—therefore those who crane necks and stand on tiptoe in hope are not merely one man.

entries.zh: 且大將軍之事，豈得珪璧其行，束修其心而已哉？
entries.en: A grand marshal's charge is not merely to polish his manners like a ritual jade.
entries.literal: Moreover can the grand marshal's task be only to polish his conduct like a jade tablet and bind his mind with a bundle of dried meat?

entries.zh: 將定國家之大業，成天地之元功也。
entries.en: He must settle the realm and finish the work Heaven and earth began.
entries.literal: He will settle the state's great enterprise and complete the primordial merit of Heaven and earth.

entries.zh: 昔周宣中興之主，齊桓霸強之君耳，猶有申伯、召虎、夷吾、吉甫攘其蝥賊，安其疆宇。
entries.en: King Xuan and Duke Huan were only restorer and hegemon, yet they needed Shen Bo, Zhao Hu, Guan Zhong, and Yin Jifu to scourge pests and secure the frontier.
entries.literal: In the past King Xuan of Zhou was a ruler who restored the middle; Duke Huan of Qi was a lord who hegemonized by strength—yet still they had Shen Bo, Zhao Hu, Yiguan, and Jifu to drive off their pests and settle their borders.

entries.zh: 況乎萬里之漢，明帝復興，而大將軍為之梁棟，此誠不可以忽也。
entries.en: How much more this renewed Han of boundless extent, with you as its roof beam—this brooks no neglect.
entries.literal: How much more the Han of ten thousand li, the enlightened emperor again rising, while the grand marshal is its beam and pillar—this truly cannot be neglected.

entries.zh: 初，譚著書言當世行事二十九篇，號曰《新論》，上書獻之，世祖善焉。
entries.en: He had written twenty-nine essays on his own times, the New Discussions, which Emperor Guangwu praised.
entries.literal: At first Tan had composed a book on the conduct of the present age in twenty-nine sections, titled New Discourses, and submitted it by memorial; Shizu praised it.

entries.zh: 是時，帝方信讖，多以決定嫌疑。
entries.en: The emperor was trusting apocryphal prophecies to settle every doubt.
entries.literal: At that time the emperor was trusting prophecy texts and mostly used them to decide doubtful points.

entries.zh: 又酬賞少薄，天下不時安定。
entries.en: Rewards for merit were meager, and the land knew no lasting peace.
entries.literal: Moreover rewards for merit were scant and thin; the realm was not timely settled.

entries.zh: 譚複上疏曰：臣前獻瞽言，未蒙詔報，不勝憤懣，冒死得陳。
entries.en: Huan Tan wrote again: "I spoke once without answer; unable to contain my grief, I risk death to repeat it."
entries.literal: Tan again submitted a memorial, saying: Your servant earlier presented blind words and did not receive an edict in reply; unable to overcome indignation, he braves death to state them.

entries.zh: 愚夫策謀，有益於政道者，以合人心而得事理也。
entries.en: Even a commoner's plan helps government when it fits human nature and the facts.
entries.literal: The foolish man's plans and schemes, if they benefit the way of government, are because they match human hearts and obtain the pattern of affairs.

entries.zh: 凡人情忽於見事而貴于異聞，觀先王之所記述，咸以仁義正道為本，非有奇怪虛誕之事。
entries.en: Men dismiss what they see daily and chase marvels; yet the sages wrote only of humanity, duty, and the straight path—never of empty wonders.
entries.literal: As a rule human feeling neglects what is before the eyes and esteems strange hearsay; observing what former kings recorded and wrote, all took benevolence, righteousness, and the correct way as root; they had no strange, empty, and false matters.

entries.zh: 蓋天道性命，聖人所難言也。
entries.en: Heaven's way, fate, and human nature are what even sages discuss rarely.
entries.literal: Now the way of Heaven, nature, and destiny is what sages find hard to speak of.

entries.zh: 自子貢以下，不得而聞，況後世淺儒，能通之乎！
entries.en: Below Zigong's generation disciples could not grasp them—how shall shallow scholars of our day!
entries.literal: From Zigong downward, they could not obtain hearing of it—how much less can shallow Confucians of later ages penetrate it!

entries.zh: 今諸巧慧小才伎數之人，增益圖書，矯稱讖記，以欺惑貪邪，詿誤人主，焉可不抑遠之哉！
entries.en: Today clever charlatans pad apocryphal books, call them prophecy, and beguile greedy minds and mislead the throne—they must be checked and banished!
entries.literal: Now the various clever, petty-talented, artful-number people add to and enlarge charts and books, falsely style them prophecy records, thereby to deceive and delude the greedy and evil, and lead the ruler astray—how can they not be suppressed and kept at distance!

entries.zh: 臣譚伏聞陛下窮折方士黃白之術，甚為明矣；
entries.en: Your servant hears that Your Majesty has exposed the alchemists' gold-and-silver fraud—most enlightened;
entries.literal: Your servant Tan has heard with bowed head that Your Majesty has thoroughly refuted the alchemists' arts of yellow and white—this is very enlightened;

entries.zh: 而乃欲聽納讖記，又何誤也！
entries.en: yet you would heed forged prophecies—how is that less a mistake!
entries.literal: yet you would listen to and accept prophecy records—what error again!

entries.zh: 其事雖有時合，譬猶卜數隻偶之類。
entries.en: When they occasionally prove true, it is mere chance, like a lucky cast of the milfoil.
entries.literal: Though their affairs sometimes match, it is like divination by numbers hitting by chance on a few.

entries.zh: 陛下宜垂明聽，發聖意，屏群小之曲說，述《五經》之正義，略雷同之俗語，詳通人之雅謀。
entries.en: Open your ears, issue clear intent, cast off petty occultism, return to the plain sense of the Five Classics, drop parroted slogans, and weigh the counsel of true scholars.
entries.literal: Your Majesty ought to let fall clear hearing, issue sagely intention, screen the twisted sayings of the petty crowd, pursue the correct meaning of the Five Classics, omit vulgar sayings of mere echo, and examine thoroughly the elegant plans of thorough-going men.

entries.zh: 帝省奏，愈不悅。
entries.en: The emperor read it and liked him even less.
entries.literal: The emperor examined the memorial and was increasingly displeased.

entries.zh: 其後，有詔會議靈台所處，帝謂譚曰：“吾欲以讖決之，何如？”
entries.en: Later, debating where to build the Ling Terrace, the emperor asked Huan Tan, "Shall I let the prophecies decide?"
entries.literal: Afterward there was an edict to convene discussion on where to place the Ling Terrace; the emperor said to Tan, "I wish to use prophecy to decide it—how would that be?"

entries.zh: 譚默然良久，曰：“臣不讀讖。”
entries.en: Huan Tan was silent, then said, "I do not study apocrypha."
entries.literal: Tan was silent a long time and said, "Your servant does not read prophecy texts."

entries.zh: 帝問其故，譚複極言讖之非經。
entries.en: Asked why, he said flatly that such books are not classical.
entries.literal: The emperor asked the reason; Tan again spoke to the utmost that prophecy is not canonical.

entries.zh: 帝大怒曰：“桓譚非聖無法，將下斬之！”
entries.en: The emperor roared, "Huan Tan rejects the sages and spurns the law—off with his head!"
entries.literal: The emperor was greatly angry and said, "Huan Tan denies the sages and has no law—take him down and behead him!"

entries.zh: 譚叩頭流血，良久乃得解。
entries.en: Huan Tan knocked his brow bloody on the stones until the rage cooled.
entries.literal: Tan knocked his head until it bled; after a long time he then obtained release.

entries.zh: 出為六安郡丞，意忽忽不樂，道病卒，時年七十餘。
entries.en: They sent him out as assistant governor of Lu'an; he went in a daze of grief and died on the road, past seventy.
entries.literal: He went out as assistant to the grand administrator of Lu'an commandery; his mind was absent and unhappy; on the road he died of illness, aged over seventy.

entries.zh: 及世祖即位，遣宗正劉延攻天井關，與田邑連戰十餘合，延不得進。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangwu took the throne, he sent Liu Yan, director of the imperial clan, to attack Tianjing Pass; after more than ten clashes with Tian Yi, Yan could not break through.
entries.literal: When Emperor Guangwu took the throne, he sent Director of the Imperial Clan Liu Yan to attack Tianjing Pass; he fought Tian Yi for more than ten engagements, and Yan could not advance.

entries.zh: 邑迎母弟妻子，為延所獲。
entries.en: Tian Yi's mother, younger brother, wife, and children, whom he went out to receive, were captured by Liu Yan.
entries.literal: Yi went out to welcome his mother, younger brother, wife, and children, who were captured by Yan.

entries.zh: 後邑聞更始敗，乃遣使詣洛陽獻璧馬，即拜為上黨太守。
entries.en: When Tian Yi learned Gengshi had fallen, he sent envoys to Luoyang with jade disks and horses and was appointed grand administrator of Shangdang.
entries.literal: Later, when Yi heard Gengshi had been defeated, he sent envoys to Luoyang offering jade disks and horses, and was immediately appointed grand administrator of Shangdang.

entries.zh: 因遣使者招永、衍，永、衍等疑不肯降，而忿邑背前約，衍乃遺邑書曰：蓋聞晉文出奔而子犯宣其忠，趙武逢難而程嬰明其賢，二子之義當矣。
entries.en: He then sent envoys to summon Bao Yong and Feng Yan; they hesitated and refused to submit, and resenting Tian Yi for breaking their earlier pact, Feng Yan wrote to him: "When Duke Wen of Jin fled into exile, Zi Fan showed his loyalty; when Duke Wu of Zhao met disaster, Cheng Ying proved his worth—both acted as righteousness required."
entries.literal: He then sent envoys to summon Yong and Yan; Yong, Yan, and the others, doubting, refused to submit, and resenting Yi for breaking their former pact, Yan sent Yi a letter saying: "I have heard that when Duke Wen of Jin went into exile, Zi Fan proclaimed his loyalty, and when Duke Wu of Zhao met calamity, Cheng Ying made clear his worth—the righteousness of both men was fitting."

entries.zh: 今三王背畔，赤眉危國，天下蟻動，社稷顛隕，是忠臣立功之日，志士馳馬之秋也。
entries.en: The Three Wangs have rebelled, the Red Eyebrows threaten the realm, the empire seethes, and the altars shake—this is the hour for loyal ministers to win merit and for resolute men to ride.
entries.literal: Now the Three Wangs have rebelled, the Red Eyebrows endanger the state, all under heaven stirs like ants, and the altars totter—this is the day for loyal ministers to achieve merit and the season for men of resolve to spur their horses.

entries.zh: 伯玉擢選剖符，專宰大郡。
entries.en: You, Boyu, were elevated, granted a tally, and entrusted with a great commandery.
entries.literal: Boyu, raised and selected, was granted a tally and given sole charge of a great commandery.

entries.zh: 夫上黨之地，有四塞之固，東帶三關，西為國蔽，奈何舉之以資強敵，開天下之匈，假仇讎之刃？
entries.en: Shangdang is locked by four passes, belts three gates on the east, and shields the state on the west—why surrender it to arm a powerful enemy, tear open the realm, and hand blades to a foe?
entries.literal: Shangdang has the strength of four barred passes—east it belts three gates, west it shields the state—how can you hand it over to strengthen a powerful foe, open the empire's breast, and lend blades to an enemy?

entries.zh: 豈不哀哉！
entries.en: Is that not lamentable!
entries.literal: Is it not pitiful!

entries.zh: 間者，上黨黠賊，大眾圍城，義兵兩輩，入據井陘。
entries.en: Lately Shangdang's rebels ringed the city while loyal columns seized Jingxing.
entries.literal: Recently the cunning bandits of Shangdang, a great host, besieged the city; righteous troops in two divisions entered and held Jingxing.

entries.zh: 邑親潰敵圍，拒擊宗正，自試智勇，非不能當。
entries.en: I myself broke their lines and drove back the imperial clansman—rest assured I could fight.
entries.literal: Yi personally broke the enemy siege, resisted and struck the director of the imperial clan—testing wisdom and courage, it was not inability to match.

entries.zh: 誠知故朝為兵所害，新帝司徒已定三輔，隴西、北地從風回應。
entries.en: But I saw the old regime crushed, the new emperor's minister secure the capital region, Longxi and Beidi rallying to him.
entries.literal: Truly knowing the former court was harmed by arms, the new emperor's Minister of Education has already settled the Three Adjuncts, Longxi and Beidi turn in the wind and respond.

entries.zh: 其事昭昭，日月經天，河海帶地，不足以比。
entries.en: That fact shines like sun and moon; no river or sea is clearer.
entries.literal: The affair is bright and bright—sun and moon thread the sky, rivers and seas gird the earth—not enough to compare.

entries.zh: 死生有命，富貴在天。
entries.en: Life and death are fated; wealth rests with Heaven.
entries.literal: Death and life have fate; wealth and honor lie with Heaven.

entries.zh: 天下存亡，誠雲命也。
entries.en: The empire's rise or fall is Heaven's sentence.
entries.literal: The survival or perishing of all under heaven is truly said to be fate.

entries.zh: 邑雖沒身，能如命何？
entries.en: Though I die for it, what quarrel have I with fate?
entries.literal: Though Yi lose his body, what can he do against fate?

entries.zh: 帝怨衍等不時至，永以立功得贖罪，遂任用之，而衍獨見黜。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu resented their late arrival; Bao Yong bought pardon with merit and kept office, but Feng Yan alone was cast aside.
entries.literal: The emperor resented Yan and the others for not arriving in timely fashion; Yong by establishing merit obtained ransom from crime, thereupon was employed and used, while Yan alone was dismissed.

entries.zh: 永謂衍曰：“昔高祖賞季布之罪，誅丁固之功。
entries.en: Bao Yong said, "Gaozu pardoned Ji Bu and executed Ding Gu for ingratitude.
entries.literal: Yong said to Yan, "In the past Gaozu rewarded Ji Bu's crime and executed Ding Gu's merit.

entries.zh: 今遭明主，亦何憂哉！”
entries.en: You now serve an enlightened sovereign—what have you to fear!"
entries.literal: Now you meet an enlightened ruler—what is there to worry about!"

entries.zh: 衍曰：“記有之，人有挑其鄰人之妻者，挑其長者，長者詈之，挑其少者，少者報之，後其夫死而取其長者。
entries.en: Feng Yan answered, "The books tell of a man who flirted with a neighbor's two wives: the elder scolded him, the younger welcomed him, and when their husband died he married the one who had cursed him.
entries.literal: Yan said, "The records have it: there was a man who teased his neighbor's wives; teasing the elder, the elder cursed him; teasing the younger, the younger responded to him; afterward when her husband died he took the elder.

entries.zh: 或謂之曰：‘夫非罵爾者邪？
entries.en: People asked, 'Was that not the woman who reviled you?'
entries.literal: Someone said to him, 'Was that not the one who cursed you?'

entries.zh: ’曰：‘在人欲其報我，在我欲其罵人也。
entries.en: She said, 'When others court me I want devotion; when I court others I want honesty—even if it stings.'
entries.literal: ' He said, 'In others I desire that they respond to me; in myself I desire that they curse people.'

entries.zh: ’夫天命難知，人道易守，守道之臣，何患死亡？”
entries.en: Heaven's will is dark, but a man's course is clear—why should a minister who keeps the Way fear death?"
entries.literal: ' Now Heaven's mandate is hard to know, the human way easy to keep—a minister who keeps the Way, why worry about death?"

entries.zh: 頃之，帝以衍為曲陽令，誅斬劇賊郭勝等，降五千餘人，論功當封，以讒毀，故賞不行。
entries.en: Soon the emperor named him magistrate of Quyang; he executed bandits like Guo Sheng and took five thousand surrenders—merit enough for a fief, but slander blocked any reward.
entries.literal: Before long the emperor appointed Yan magistrate of Quyang; he executed and beheaded the fierce bandit Guo Sheng and others, surrendering more than five thousand; by merit in discussion he ought to have been enfeoffed, but because of slander and defamation, therefore reward was not carried out.

entries.zh: 建武六年日食，衍上書陳八事：其一曰顯文德，二曰褒武烈，三曰修舊功，四曰招俊傑，五曰明好惡，六曰簡法令，七曰差秩祿，八曰撫邊境。
entries.en: After a solar eclipse in Jianwu 6 he memorialized eight points: promote culture, honor arms, restore old services, recruit talent, clarify rewards and punishments, streamline law, grade salaries, and pacify the frontier.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jianwu there was a solar eclipse; Yan submitted a memorial stating eight matters: the first called for displaying civil virtue, the second for praising martial glory, the third for repairing old merit, the fourth for summoning outstanding men, the fifth for clarifying likes and dislikes, the sixth for simplifying laws and orders, the seventh for grading rank salary, the eighth for soothing the border regions.

entries.zh: 書奏，帝將召見。
entries.en: The emperor read it and meant to receive him at court.
entries.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor was about to summon him for audience.

entries.zh: 初，衍為狼孟長，以罪摧陷大姓令狐略。
entries.en: Years before, as magistrate of Langmeng, he had framed the magnate Linghu Lue.
entries.literal: At first, when Yan was chief of Langmeng, by a crime he had crushed and trapped the great surname Linghu Lue.

entries.zh: 是時，略為司空長史，讒之于尚書令王護、尚書周生豐曰：“衍所以求見者，欲毀君也。”
entries.en: Linghu Lue was now clerk to the minister of works; he told Wang Hu and Zhou Sheng Feng that Feng Yan meant to ruin them at audience.
entries.literal: At that time Lue was senior clerk to the Minister of Works; he slandered him to Director of the Secretariat Wang Hu and Director Zhou Sheng Feng, saying, "The reason Yan seeks audience is that he wishes to destroy you gentlemen."

entries.zh: 護等懼之，即共排間，衍遂不得入。
entries.en: They blocked his path to the throne out of fear.
entries.literal: Hu and the others feared him; immediately together they blocked and estranged him, and Yan thereupon could not gain entry.

entries.zh: 後衛尉陰興、新陽侯陰就以外戚貴顯，深敬重衍，衍遂與之交結，是由為諸王所聘請，尋為司隸從事。
entries.en: Later Yin Xing and Yin Jiu, powerful in-laws, befriended him; he entered the princes' service and became a clerk under the metropolitan commandant.
entries.literal: Later Commandant of the Guards Yin Xing and Marquis of Xinyang Yin Jiu, by maternal kinship noble and eminent, deeply respected Yan; Yan thereupon associated and bound himself with them, whereby he was recruited by the various princes; soon he became a clerk to the Metropolitan Commandant.

entries.zh: 帝懲西京外戚賓客，故皆以法繩之，大者抵死徙，其餘至貶黜。
entries.en: Guangwu tightened the law on in-laws and their clients as Western Han had not: the worst died or were exiled, the rest stripped of rank.
entries.literal: The emperor, warning against Western Capital maternal kin and clients, therefore all applied the law to them; the great went to death or exile, the rest to demotion and dismissal.

entries.zh: 衍由此得罪，嘗自詣獄，有詔赦不問。
entries.en: Feng Yan fell under the edict; he turned himself in to jail but received a general pardon.
entries.literal: Yan by this incurred guilt; he once went in person to prison; there was an edict pardoning and not prosecuting.

entries.zh: 西歸故郡，閉門自保，不敢復與親故通。
entries.en: He went home to his native commandery, shut his gate, and broke with kin and old companions.
entries.literal: He returned west to his old commandery, closed the gate and preserved himself, and no longer communicated with kin and old friends.

entries.zh: 馮衍字敬通，京兆杜陵人也。
entries.en: Feng Yan, styled Jingtong, came from Duling in the Jingzhao capital district.
entries.literal: Feng Yan, courtesy name Jingtong, was a man of Duling in the metropolitan region of Jingzhao.

entries.zh: 祖野王，元帝時為大鴻臚。
entries.en: His grandfather Feng Yewang had been grand herald under Emperor Yuan.
entries.literal: His grandfather Yewang, in the time of Yuandi, was Grand Herald.

entries.zh: 衍幼有奇才，年九歲，能誦《詩》，至二十而博通群書。
entries.en: A prodigy, he knew the Odes by heart at nine and had read everything worth reading by twenty.
entries.literal: Yan in youth had unusual talent; at nine sui he could recite the Odes; reaching twenty he was broadly conversant with all books.

entries.zh: 王莽時，諸公多薦舉之者，衍辭不肯仕。
entries.en: Wang Mang's high ministers recommended him repeatedly; he refused office.
entries.literal: In the time of Wang Mang, the various dukes mostly recommended him; Yan declined and was unwilling to serve.

entries.zh: 時，天下兵起，莽遣更始將軍廉丹討伐山東。
entries.en: When rebellion flared, Wang Mang sent General Gengshi Lian Dan east of the Taihang range.
entries.literal: At that time military uprising arose in the realm; Mang sent General Gengshi Lian Dan to campaign east of the mountains.

entries.zh: 丹辟衍為掾，與俱至定陶。
entries.en: Lian Dan made Feng Yan his clerk and took him to Dingtao.
entries.literal: Dan summoned Yan as clerk and with him reached Dingtao.

entries.zh: 莽追詔丹曰：“倉廩盡矣，府庫空矣，可以怒矣，可以戰矣。
entries.en: Wang Mang's follow-up edict read, "Granaries are bare and treasuries empty—anger is due, battle is due.
entries.literal: Mang pursued with an edict to Dan, saying, "The granaries are exhausted, the treasuries are empty; one may be angry, one may fight.

entries.zh: 將軍受國重任，不捐身於中野，無以報恩塞責。”
entries.en: You bear the state's heavy charge: unless you die in the field you cannot repay it or answer for it."
entries.literal: The general has received the state's heavy burden; if you do not cast away your body in the wilds of the field, there is no means to repay favor and stop responsibility."

entries.zh: 丹惶恐，夜召衍，以書示之。
entries.en: Lian Dan was terrified; that night he called Feng Yan and showed him the letter.
entries.literal: Dan was fearful and alarmed; at night he summoned Yan and showed him the letter.

entries.zh: 衍因說丹曰：“衍聞順而成者，道之所大也；
entries.en: Feng Yan answered, "I have heard that success won with the tide is what the Way most honors;
entries.literal: Yan thereupon persuaded Dan, saying, "Your servant Yan has heard that what follows the current and completes is what the Way greatly esteems;

entries.zh: 逆而功者，權之所貴也。
entries.en: success won against the tide is what circumstance most prizes.
entries.literal: what opposes the current yet achieves merit is what expediency esteems.

entries.zh: 是故期於有成，不問所由；
entries.en: So aim at the outcome, not the path;
entries.literal: Therefore one aims at having achievement, not asking by what path;

entries.zh: 論於大體，不守小節。
entries.en: weigh the great pattern, not petty scruples.
entries.literal: debating the great frame, not guarding petty points.

entries.zh: 昔逢醜父伏軾而使其君取飲，稱于諸侯；
entries.en: Feng Choufu once hid his lord under the chariot rail and was praised in the odes;
entries.literal: In the past Feng Choufu leaned on the carriage bar and made his ruler go for a drink, and was praised among the feudal lords;

entries.zh: 鄭祭仲立突而出忽，終得復位，美於《春秋》。
entries.en: Zhai Zhong of Zheng set Prince Tu on the throne and drove Prince Hu into exile, then restored right order—Spring and Autumn judges him kindly.
entries.literal: Zhai Zhong of Zheng raised Prince Tu and expelled Prince Hu, and in the end the rightful heir was restored—an act the Spring and Autumn praises.

entries.zh: 蓋以死易生，以存易亡，君子之道也。
entries.en: To trade certain death for a chance at life is the gentleman's path.
entries.literal: For thus to exchange death for life, exchange perishing for survival, is the way of the gentleman.

entries.zh: 詭于眾意，甯國存身，賢智之慮也。
entries.en: Bend to popular opinion yet save the realm and your skin—that is what a wise man weighs.
entries.literal: To deceive the multitude's intent yet settle the state and preserve the self is the consideration of the worthy and wise.

entries.zh: 故《易》曰‘窮則變，變則通，通則久，是以自天祐之，吉，無不利’。
entries.en: The Classic of Changes says: 'Blockage forces change, change opens the way, an open way endures'—Heaven itself blesses that course.
entries.literal: Therefore the Changes says, 'When exhausted, then change; when changed, then penetrate; when penetrated, then long enduring—therefore from Heaven there is blessing, auspicious, without nothing not favorable.'

entries.zh: 若夫知其不可而必行之，破軍殘眾，無補於主，身死之日，負義于時，智者不為，勇者不行。
entries.en: To charge into a hopeless fight, waste your army, die disgraced, and help your lord not at all—no wise or brave man chooses that.
entries.literal: As for knowing it cannot be done yet necessarily doing it, breaking the army and maiming the host, without benefit to the lord, on the day of one's death bearing unrighteousness toward the age—the wise do not do it, the brave do not carry it out.

entries.zh: 且衍聞之，得時無怠。
entries.en: And I say: when Heaven offers an opening, seize it without delay.
entries.literal: Moreover your servant Yan has heard: obtaining the moment, do not slack.

entries.zh: 張良以五世相韓，椎秦始皇博浪之中，勇冠乎賁、育，名高乎太山。
entries.en: Zhang Liang, whose forebears had served the state of Han for five generations as ministers, struck at the First Emperor in the surf at Bolang—courage beyond warriors Ben and Yu, fame higher than Taishan.
entries.literal: Zhang Liang, with five generations serving as minister to Han, struck at the First Emperor of Qin amid the waves at Bolang; his courage crowned Ben and Yu; his name was higher than Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 將軍之先，為漢信臣。
entries.en: Your own ancestors were loyal servants of the Han house.
entries.literal: The general's ancestors were trusted ministers of Han.

entries.zh: 新室之興，英俊不附。
entries.en: When Wang Mang founded Xin, no true talent rallied to him.
entries.literal: At the rise of the New house, outstanding men did not attach.

entries.zh: 今海內潰亂，人懷漢德，甚于詩人思召公也，愛其甘棠，而況子孫乎？
entries.en: The realm is in ruins, yet the people cling to Han as the poets clung to the memory of the Duke of Shao under the sweet pear—how much more his heirs?
entries.literal: Now within the seas there is collapse and disorder; people cherish Han virtue more than the poets longed for Duke Shao—they loved his sweet pear tree—how much more their descendants?

entries.zh: 人所歌舞，天必從之。
entries.en: What the people celebrate, Heaven seconds.
entries.literal: What men sing and dance, Heaven is sure to follow.

entries.zh: 方今為將軍計，莫若屯據大郡，鎮撫吏士，砥厲其節，百里之內，牛酒日賜，納雄桀之士，詢忠智之謀，要將來之心，待從橫之變，興社稷之利，除萬人之害，則福祿流於無窮，功烈著於不滅。
entries.en: My counsel: occupy a rich commandery, hearten your troops, feast the brave within a hundred li, gather wise counsel, win wavering lords, watch how the chessboard shifts, then strike for the altars' good and the people's relief—your name will shine forever.
entries.literal: For the present, to plan for the general, nothing is better than to encamp and hold a great commandery, pacify and soothe clerks and soldiers, grind sharp their integrity, within a hundred li daily bestow oxen and wine, take in bold and outstanding gentlemen, inquire into loyal and wise plans, seize the hearts of those who will come, await the changes of vertical and horizontal alliances, raise the altars of soil and grain to profit, remove the harm of the myriad people—then blessing and salary will flow without end, merit and blaze be inscribed imperishable.

entries.zh: 何與軍覆于中原，身膏於草野，功敗名喪，恥及先祖哉？
entries.en: Why choose instead total defeat on the plain, your corpse crow-bait, honor lost and ancestors shamed?
entries.literal: What of having the army overturned in the central plain, your body rendered fat on the wild grass, merit defeated and name lost, shame reaching the former ancestors?

entries.zh: 聖人轉禍而為福，智士因敗而為功，願明公深計而無與俗同。”
entries.en: Sages turn disaster to gain; wise men ride defeat to victory—think hard, general, and do not drift with the crowd."
entries.literal: Sages turn calamity into blessing; wise men by defeat achieve merit—I hope my lord will think deeply and not be the same as the vulgar."

entries.zh: 丹不能從。
entries.en: Lian Dan would not listen.
entries.literal: Dan could not follow.

entries.zh: 且衍聞之，兵久則力屈，人悉則變生。
entries.en: Prolonged war exhausts an army; a spent people breeds revolt.
entries.literal: Moreover your servant Yan has heard: troops long deployed then strength is exhausted; people exhausted then change is born.

entries.zh: 今邯鄲之賊未滅，真定之際複擾，而大將軍所部不過百里，守城不休，戰軍不息，兵革雲翔，百姓震駭，奈何自怠，不為深憂？
entries.en: Handan still burns, Zhending stirs again, yet your district is barely a hundred li across, garrisons endless, battles unceasing, arms piled sky-high, the people terrified—how can you rest easy?
entries.literal: Now the bandits of Handan are not yet destroyed; the region of Zhending is again disturbed; yet the territory the grand marshal holds does not exceed a hundred li, garrisoning cities without rest, fighting armies without cease, weapons and armor cloud-soaring, the hundred surnames quake in alarm—how can you yourself slacken and not harbor deep worry?

entries.zh: 夫并州之地，東帶名關，北逼強胡，年穀獨孰，人庶多資，斯四戰之地，攻守之場也。
entries.en: Bingzhou is belted by great passes in the east, pressed by the Hu in the north, its harvests richest, its people resilient—a crossroads every army covets.
entries.literal: Now the land of Bing province, east girdled by famous passes, north pressed by mighty Hu; the year's grain alone ripens; the people and multitude have much to rely on—it is a place of battle on four sides, a field for attack and defense.

entries.zh: 如其不虞，何以待之？
entries.en: If surprise strikes, what will you meet it with?
entries.literal: If there should be mischance, with what will you await it?

entries.zh: 故曰“德不素積，人不為用。
entries.en: The proverb says, "Without stored virtue, men will not serve you.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said, 'Virtue not piled up in ordinary times, men will not be usable.'

entries.zh: 備不豫具，難以應卒”。
entries.en: Without stockpiled readiness you cannot meet a sudden storm."
entries.literal: If preparations are not laid in advance, it is hard to answer sudden crisis.'

entries.zh: 今生人之命，縣于將軍，將軍所杖，必須良才，宜改易非任，更選賢能。
entries.en: The people's lives hang on you; your staff must be worthy—replace the unfit and name better men.
entries.literal: Now the life of the living hangs from the general; what the general leans on must be good talent—it is fitting to change those wrongly placed and anew select the worthy and able.

entries.zh: 夫十室之邑，必有忠信。
entries.en: Even a hamlet of ten holds loyal hearts.
entries.literal: In a settlement of ten houses there is sure to be one loyal and trustworthy.

entries.zh: 審得其人，以承大將軍之明，雖則山澤之人，無不感德，思樂為用矣。
entries.en: Win the right men under your banner and even hill folk will die for your kindness.
entries.literal: If truly you obtain such men to receive the grand marshal's enlightenment, though they be men of mountains and marshes, none will fail to feel virtue and wish joyfully to be employed.

entries.zh: 然後簡精銳之卒，發屯守之士，三軍既整，甲兵已具，相其土地之饒，觀其水泉之利，制屯田之術，習戰射之教，則威風遠暢，人安其業矣。
entries.en: Then drill picked troops, open military farms on rich soil and good water, teach archery and shield—your awe will carry far and the people will farm in peace.
entries.literal: Then pick crack troops, call out garrison guards, once the three armies are ordered and armor and weapons provided, inspect where the land is rich, observe where springs and water profit, institute the method of frontier farming, drill them in battle and archery—then awesome might will reach far, and men will rest secure in their occupations.

entries.zh: 若鎮太原，撫上党，收百姓之歡心，樹名賢之良佐，天下無變，則足以顯聲譽，一朝有事，則可以建大功。
entries.en: Hold Taiyuan, win Shangdang, bind the people with good rule and wise aides—peace will burnish your name, crisis will let you win undying merit.
entries.literal: If you secure Taiyuan and soothe Shangdang, harvest the hundred surnames' glad hearts and plant worthy assistants of good name, when all under heaven has no change, then it suffices to display reputation; if in one morning there is affair, then you can establish great merit.

entries.zh: 惟大將軍開日月之明，發深淵之慮，監《六經》之論，觀孫、吳之策，省群議之是非，詳眾士之白黑，以超《周南》之跡，垂《甘棠》之風，令夫功烈施於千載，富貴傳於無窮。
entries.en: Only open your mind like sun and moon, sound the Six Classics and Sun Wu's art, sift counsel true from false, men loyal from hollow, outshine the southern Zhou, leave a Duke of Shao's sweet-pear fame, and your glory will span the ages.
entries.literal: Only may the grand marshal open sun-and-moon brightness, issue deep-pool reflection, examine the discussions of the Six Classics, observe the stratagems of Sun and Wu, review whether the host of counsels is right or wrong, scrutinize black and white among the many gentlemen, so as to surpass the traces south of Zhou, let fall the wind of the sweet pear tree, cause husband merit and blaze to extend over a thousand ages, wealth and honor to transmit without end.

entries.zh: 伊、望之策，何以加茲！
entries.en: What could Yi Yin or Lü Wang add beyond that?
entries.literal: How can the plans of Yi Yin and Lü Wang add to this!

entries.zh: 永既素重衍，為且受使得自置偏裨，乃以衍為立漢將軍，領狼孟長，屯太原，與上党太守田邑等繕甲養士，扞衛並土。
entries.en: Bao Yong, who already respected Feng Yan, let him name subordinates and made him General Who Establishes Han and magistrate of Langmeng, camped at Taiyuan with Tian Yi of Shangdang to arm the border.
entries.literal: Yong had long esteemed Yan; because he was about to receive mission and was allowed himself to appoint subordinate generals, he thereupon made Yan General Who Establishes Han, concurrently chief of Langmeng, encamped at Taiyuan, and together with grand administrator of Shangdang Tian Yi and others repaired armor and nurtured soldiers, defending Bing soil.

entries.zh: 衍聞之，委質為臣，無有二心；
entries.en: I have heard that a subject who pledges loyalty has but one heart;
entries.literal: Your servant Yan has heard: casting one's substance to be a minister, there is no second heart;

entries.zh: 挈瓶之智，守不假器。
entries.en: the wit that fills a small jar does not pawn another's trust.
entries.literal: the wisdom that fills a pitcher guards and does not borrow vessels.

entries.zh: 是以晏嬰臨盟，擬以曲戟，不易其辭；
entries.en: Yan Ying at a league faced a halberd at his throat yet never bent his word;
entries.literal: Therefore Yan Ying at the covenant, threatened with a bent halberd, did not alter his words;

entries.zh: 謝息守郕，脅以晉、魯，不喪其邑。
entries.en: Xie Xi held Cheng against Jin and Lu and never lost his city.
entries.literal: Xie Xi guarding Cheng was coerced by Jin and Lu, yet did not lose his town.

entries.zh: 由是言之，內無鉤頸之禍，外無桃萊之利，而被畔人之聲，蒙降城之恥，竊為左右羞之。
entries.en: Thus one may die without the halberd at one's neck yet gain no bribe of orchards—only the name of traitor and the shame of yielding a wall; I blush for your counselors.
