entries.literal: From this speaking, having within no misfortune of hooking the neck, without the profit of peach and lai, yet bearing the reputation of a rebel, wearing the shame of surrendering a city—your servant privately is ashamed for those at your left and right.

entries.zh: 且邾庶其竊邑畔君，以要大利，曰賤而必書；
entries.en: Zhu Shuqi seized a town to extort his prince—the Annals still records such baseness;
entries.literal: Moreover Zhu Shuqi stole a town and rebelled against the lord to seek great profit—though base, the Spring and Autumn must record it;

entries.zh: 莒牟夷以土地求食，而名不滅。
entries.en: Mou Yi of Ju traded land for safety yet kept his name.
entries.literal: Mou Yi of Ju sought food with land yet his name was not extinguished.

entries.zh: 是以大丈夫動則思禮，行則思義，未有背此而身名能全者也。
entries.en: A gentleman weighs every step by rite and right; abandon those and neither life nor fame survives.
entries.literal: Therefore the great man in moving thinks of ritual, in acting thinks of righteousness; there has never been one who turned his back on these yet could preserve body and name whole.

entries.zh: 為伯玉深計，莫若與鮑尚書同情戮力，顯忠貞之節，立超世之功。
entries.en: For Tian Yi's good, join Bao Yong in one loyal effort and win a fame beyond your time.
entries.literal: To plan deeply for Boyu, nothing is better than to share mind and join strength with Director Bao Yong, display the integrity of loyalty and steadfastness, and establish merit that transcends the age.

entries.zh: 如以尊親系累之故，能捐位投命，歸之尚書，大義既全，敵人紓怨，上不損剖符之責，下足救老幼之命，申眉高談，無愧天下。
entries.en: If kinship moves you to lay down command and return to Bao Yong, you keep the great right, slacken your foe's hate, honor your commission above, save your family below, and hold your head high before the world.
entries.literal: If because of the burden of honored kin you can cast away office and hazard life, returning to the Director of the Secretariat, the great righteousness already whole, the enemy loosens resentment, above not damaging the responsibility of the split tally, below sufficing to save old and young lives, brows stretched in high discourse, without shame before all under heaven.

entries.zh: 若乃貪上党之權，惜全邦之實，衍恐伯玉必懷周趙之憂，上黨複有前年之禍。
entries.en: Cling to Shangdang's power and the whole commandery's wealth, and I fear you court the fate of Zhou and Zhao and repeat last year's calamity.
entries.literal: If on the other hand you are greedy for power in Shangdang and cling to the substance of a whole state, your servant Yan fears Boyu will harbor the worry of Zhou and Zhao, and Shangdang again have the disaster of the former year.

entries.zh: 昔晏平仲納延陵之誨，終免欒高之難；
entries.en: Yan Ying heeded Yanling's warning and escaped the Luan-Gao purge;
entries.literal: In the past Yan Pingzhong accepted Yanling's instruction and in the end escaped the disaster of Luan and Gao;

entries.zh: 孫林父違穆子之戒，故陷終身之惡。
entries.en: Sun Linfu spurned Muzi's counsel and earned lifelong infamy.
entries.literal: Sun Linfu disobeyed Muzi's warning, therefore fell into lifelong evil.

entries.zh: 以為伯玉聞此至言，必若刺心，自非嬰城而堅守，則策馬而不顧也。
entries.en: When Tian Yi hears this straight talk it should pierce his heart—either bolt the gates or gallop away without a backward glance.
entries.literal: Your servant thought that when Boyu heard this utmost speech, it would be like piercing the heart; unless he defended the city to the last, he would whip his horse and not look back.

entries.zh: 聖人轉禍而為福，智士因敗以成勝，願自強于時，無與俗同。
entries.en: Sages turn ruin to gain; wise men ride defeat to victory—brace to the hour, sir, and do not drift with the mob.
entries.literal: Sages turn calamity into blessing; wise men by defeat achieve victory—I hope you will strengthen yourself to the times and not be the same as the vulgar.

entries.zh: 桓譚字君山，沛國相人也。
entries.en: Huan Tan, styled Junshan, came from Xiang in the princedom of Pei.
entries.literal: Huan Tan, courtesy name Junshan, was a man of Xiang in the Principality of Pei.

entries.zh: 父成帝時為太樂令。
entries.en: His father had been director of grand music under Emperor Cheng.
entries.literal: His father in the time of Chengdi was Director of Grand Music.

entries.zh: 譚以父任為郎，因好音律，善鼓琴。
entries.en: Through his father's rank he entered court as a gentleman cadet; he loved music theory and played the zither well.
entries.literal: Tan by his father's privilege became a gentleman, and because he was fond of pitch and mode was skilled at strumming the zither.

entries.zh: 博學多通，遍習《五經》，皆詁訓大義，不為章句。
entries.en: He read widely and mastered the Five Classics for their great themes, not for pedantic glosses on single lines.
entries.literal: Broadly learned and broadly conversant, he thoroughly studied the Five Classics, all glossing and explaining great meanings, not doing chapter-and-verse commentary.

entries.zh: 能文章，尤好古學，數從劉歆、楊雄辯析疑異。
entries.en: He wrote well and doted on antiquarian scholarship, often debating knotty questions with Liu Xin and Yang Xiong.
entries.literal: He could compose literary pieces, especially loved ancient learning, and repeatedly followed Liu Xin and Yang Xiong in debating and analyzing doubtful points.

entries.zh: 性嗜倡樂，簡易不修威儀，而憙非毀俗儒，由是多見排抵。
entries.en: He loved popular entertainments, dressed down without official gravitas, and delighted in mocking pedantic scholars—so he made many enemies.
entries.literal: By nature he was addicted to entertainers' music, was simple and easy and did not cultivate awe-inspiring deportment, yet delighted in condemning vulgar Confucians, whereby he was often rejected and attacked.

entries.zh: 臣伏念高祖之略而陳平之謀，毀之則疏，譽之則親。
entries.en: I reflect on how Gaozu's strategic insight and Chen Ping's counsel worked: speak ill of them and you are pushed aside; speak well of them and you are drawn close.
entries.literal: Your minister humbly reflects that Gaozu's strategic grasp and Chen Ping's schemes—if one slanders them, one becomes estranged; if one praises them, one becomes intimate.

entries.zh: 以文帝以明而魏尚之忠，繩之以法則為罪，施之以德則為功。
entries.en: Consider Emperor Wen's clarity of judgment and Wei Shang's loyalty: judged strictly by the statutes they could be called crimes; weighed with humane virtue they count as service.
entries.literal: By Emperor Wen's perspicacity and Wei Shang's loyalty—measured by law they become crime; applied with virtue they become merit.

entries.zh: 逮至晚世，董仲舒言道德，見妒於公孫弘，李廣奮節於匈奴，見排於衛青，此忠臣之常所為流涕也。
entries.en: In more recent times Dong Zhongshu taught moral principle and was resented by Gongsun Hong; Li Guang held firm against the Xiongnu and was sidelined by Wei Qing—such things are why loyal ministers so often shed tears.
entries.literal: Coming down to a later age, Dong Zhongshu spoke of morality and was envied by Gongsun Hong; Li Guang exerted his integrity against the Xiongnu and was squeezed out by Wei Qing—this is what constantly makes loyal ministers weep.

entries.zh: 臣衍自惟微賤之臣，上無無知之薦，下無馮唐之說，乏董生之才，寡李廣之勢，而欲免讒口，濟怨嫌，豈不難哉！
entries.en: I am only a man of small station: I have no patron like Wei Wuji above me, no advocate like Feng Tang below, neither Dong Zhongshu's gifts nor Li Guang's stature—and still I hoped to escape backbiting and patch over ill will. How could that be easy?
entries.literal: Your minister Yan considers himself a mean and lowly official: above he has no Wei Wuji's recommendation; below he has no Feng Tang's advocacy; he lacks Mr. Dong's talent and Li Guang's standing—yet he wishes to escape slanderous mouths and remedy resentment and suspicion—is this not difficult!

entries.zh: 臣衍之先祖，以忠貞之故，成私門之禍。
entries.en: My ancestors were ruined in a family tragedy precisely because they stood loyal and true.
entries.literal: Your minister Yan's forebears, because of loyalty and steadfastness, brought disaster upon the private household.

entries.zh: 而臣衍復遭擾攘之時，值兵革之際，不敢回行求時之利，事君無傾邪之謀，將帥無虜掠之心。
entries.en: I then lived through chaos and war; I did not twist my conduct to chase opportunistic gain; in serving the throne I harbored no deceit; leading troops I felt no urge to pillage.
entries.literal: And your minister Yan again encountered a time of turmoil and met the season of arms; he did not dare to turn his course to seek profit from the moment; in serving his lord he had no crooked schemes; as a commander he had no mind to plunder captives.

entries.zh: 衛尉陰興，敬慎周密，內自修敕，外遠嫌疑，故敢與交通。
entries.en: Yin Xing, the Commandant of the Guards, was careful and discreet; he cultivated himself within and avoided every shadow of scandal abroad—so I deemed it safe to deal with him.
entries.literal: Commandant of the Guards Yin Xing was reverent, cautious, and thorough; inwardly he disciplined himself, outwardly he kept clear of suspicion—therefore I dared to associate with him.

entries.zh: 興知臣之貧，數欲本業之。
entries.en: He knew I was poor and more than once tried to set me up with land and a livelihood of my own.
entries.literal: Xing knew your minister's poverty and repeatedly wished to establish him in a basic livelihood.

entries.zh: 臣自惟無三益之才，不敢處三損之地，固讓而不受之，昔在更始，太原執貨財之柄，居蒼卒之間，據位食祿二十餘年，而財產歲狹，居處日貧，家無布帛之積，出無輿馬之飾。
entries.en: Knowing I was no fit companion for the three kinds of friend—and no fit associate for the three kinds that harm a gentleman—I steadfastly refused his offers. Under Gengshi I held fiscal office in Taiyuan; even in those frantic years I kept my post and my stipend for over two decades, yet my means shrank every year and my home grew poorer: no cloth piled in the house, no fine carriage when I went abroad.
entries.literal: Your minister considered that he lacked the talent of the three benefits and did not dare to occupy the place of the three harms—firmly he declined and did not accept. Formerly under Gengshi, in Taiyuan he held the handle of goods and wealth; amid sudden crises he occupied office and drew salary for more than twenty years, yet his property grew narrower year by year and his dwelling daily poorer; his household had no store of cloth or silk, and abroad he had no adornment of carriage and horses.

entries.zh: 於今遭清明之時，飭躬力行之秋，而怨仇叢興，譏議橫世。
entries.en: Now, in an age meant for clarity and honest effort, I find myself hemmed in by grudges and smeared by gossip from every side.
entries.literal: Now encountering a clear and enlightened time, a season for correcting the person and exerting conduct, yet resentment and enmity arise in clusters, ridicule and criticism fill the age.

entries.zh: 蓋富貴易為善，貧賤難為工也。
entries.en: The rich and honored find virtue easy; the poor and obscure can scarcely win a fair hearing—no matter how carefully they live.
entries.literal: For wealth and honor make it easy to do good; poverty and low status make it hard to achieve refinement.

entries.zh: 疏遠壟畝之臣，無望高闕之下，惶恐自陳，以救罪尤。
entries.en: I am only a man from the fields, with no access to the high court; in fear and trembling I lay this before you, begging relief from my offenses.
entries.literal: A minister distant and far from the furrowed fields has no hope beneath the high palace gates—trembling in fear he states his own case to redeem his faults.

entries.zh: 瞰太行之嵯峨兮，觀壺口之崢嶸；
entries.en: I look across Taihang's ridges and the fierce gorge at Hukou;
entries.literal: I gaze down on Taihang's towering height—ah, I observe Hukou's jagged majesty;

entries.zh: 悼丘墓之蕪穢兮，恨昭穆之不榮。
entries.en: I grieve for weed-choked graves and the broken order of our ancestral rites.
entries.literal: I mourn the tombs' overgrown foulness—ah, I resent that senior and junior lack glory.

entries.zh: 歲忽忽而日邁兮，壽冉冉其不與；
entries.en: The years race; my allotted span will not wait;
entries.literal: The years hurry and daily advance—ah, life slowly does not grant itself;

entries.zh: 恥功業之無成兮，赴原野而窮處。
entries.en: I blush that I have achieved nothing; I flee to the wilds and hide.
entries.literal: I shame at merit and enterprise without completion—ah, I go to the open wilds and dwell in uttermost retreat.

entries.zh: 昔伊尹之幹湯兮，七十說而乃信；
entries.en: Yi Yin pled his case to Tang seventy times before he was believed;
entries.literal: Formerly Yi Yin's seeking Tang—ah, seventy times he spoke and then was trusted;

entries.zh: 臯陶釣於雷澤兮，賴虞舜而後親。
entries.en: Gao Yao angled in Lei Marsh until Shun raised him up.
entries.literal: Gao Yao fished in Lei Marsh—ah, relying on Shun of Yu afterward he became intimate.

entries.zh: 無二士之遭遇兮，抱忠貞而莫達；
entries.en: Without their timely meeting with power, I hold loyalty to no purpose;
entries.literal: Lacking the two men's encounters—ah, embracing loyalty and steadfastness yet not penetrating;

entries.zh: 率妻子而耕耘兮，委厥美而不伐。
entries.en: I lead my family at the plough and bury my gifts unsung.
entries.literal: Leading wife and children I plow and weed—ah, I entrust my excellence and do not boast.

entries.zh: 韓盧抑而不縱兮，騏驥絆而不試；
entries.en: The keen hound is held leashed; the swift horse stands tethered, never raced;
entries.literal: Han Lu is checked and not unleashed—ah, the thoroughbred is hobbled and not tried;

entries.zh: 獨慷慨而遠覽兮，非庸庸之所識。
entries.en: I alone rage and scan the distance—things the petty never grasp.
entries.literal: Alone generous of spirit and gazing far—ah, not what the commonplace recognize.

entries.zh: 卑衛賜之阜貨兮，高顏回之所慕；
entries.en: I scorn Zigong's clever wealth and lift what Yan Hui loved;
entries.literal: I deem low Zigong's piled goods—ah, I exalt what Yan Hui admired;

entries.zh: 重祖考之洪烈兮，故收功於此路。
entries.en: My forebears' great deed weighs on me; on this path I seek to finish their work.
entries.literal: I weigh heavy my ancestors' vast merit—ah, therefore I gather achievement on this road.

entries.zh: 循四時之代謝兮，分五土之刑德；
entries.en: I follow the turning seasons and read each soil's blessing or bane;
entries.literal: Following the four seasons' succession—ah, I distinguish the five soils' virtue and severity;

entries.zh: 林相麓之所產兮，嘗水泉之所殖。
entries.en: I note what woods and foothills yield and sample what spring-water raises.
entries.literal: Forests matching foothills' produce—ah, I taste what springs and streams nourish.

entries.zh: 修神農之本業兮，采軒轅之奇策；
entries.en: I return to Shennong's husbandry and borrow the Yellow Emperor's craft;
entries.literal: I cultivate Shennong's basic occupation—ah, I adopt Xuanyuan's strange stratagems;

entries.zh: 追周棄之遺教兮，軼范蠡之絕跡。
entries.en: I follow the grain god's ancient lesson and leave Fan Li's track behind.
entries.literal: I pursue Zhouqi's remaining teaching—ah, I pass beyond Fan Li's vanished tracks.

entries.zh: 陟隴山以逾望兮，眇然覽於八荒；
entries.en: I climb Longshan and strain my sight across the eight reaches;
entries.literal: I ascend Long Mountain to gaze beyond—ah, dimly I survey the eight wilds;

entries.zh: 風波飄其並興兮，情惆悵而增傷。
entries.en: Wind and wave surge together; my heart aches more.
entries.literal: Wind and waves whirl and rise together—ah, feeling is melancholy and adds wound.

entries.zh: 覽河華之泱漭兮，望秦晉之故國。
entries.en: The Yellow River and Mount Hua spread vast; I look toward the lost realms of Qin and Jin.
entries.literal: I view the Yellow River and Mount Hua vast and boundless—ah, I gaze on Qin and Jin's old states.

entries.zh: 憤馮亭之不遂兮，慍去疾之遭惑。
entries.en: I rage that Feng Ting's plan miscarried and smart at Quji's fatal mistake.
entries.literal: I resent Feng Ting's not succeeding—ah, I am angry at Quji's encountering delusion.

entries.zh: 流山嶽而周覽兮，徇碣石與洞庭；
entries.en: I drift past sacred peaks, circle Jieshi, sweep toward Dongting;
entries.literal: Flowing mountains and peaks I scan all around—ah, I follow Jieshi and Dongting;

entries.zh: 浮江河而入海兮，溯淮濟而上征。
entries.en: I ride the great rivers to the sea, then trace the Huai and Ji upstream.
entries.literal: Floating the Yangtze and Yellow River I enter the sea—ah, I trace Huai and Ji upward in expedition.

entries.zh: 瞻燕齊之舊居兮，歷宋楚之名都；
entries.en: I pass Yan and Qi's old seats and Song and Chu's storied towns;
entries.literal: I look upon Yan and Qi's old dwellings—ah, I pass through Song and Chu's famous capitals;

entries.zh: 哀群後之不祀兮，痛列國之為墟。
entries.en: I mourn kings without heirs and kingdoms ground to dust.
entries.literal: I mourn the many lords' lack of sacrifice—ah, I grieve the feudal states become ruins.

entries.zh: 馳中夏而升降兮，路紆軫而多艱；
entries.en: I race the heartland's rises and falls on roads that twist and fight me;
entries.literal: Galloping the central Xia I rise and descend—ah, the road winds and turns with much hardship;

entries.zh: 講聖哲之通論兮，心愊憶而紛紜。
entries.en: I rehearse the sages' great themes until my heart knots with tangled thought.
entries.literal: I expound the sage-wise men's penetrating discourse—ah, the heart is depressed and memories confused.

entries.zh: 惟天路之同軌兮，或帝王之異政；
entries.en: Heaven's law runs one track, yet kings rule each in his own way;
entries.literal: Only Heaven's road shares one track—ah, or emperors and kings have differing government;

entries.zh: 堯、舜煥其蕩蕩兮，禹承平而革命。
entries.en: Yao and Shun shone with effortless breadth; Yu took a settled age and forged a new mandate.
entries.literal: Yao and Shun blaze with their vast vastness—ah, Yu received peace and changed the mandate.

entries.zh: 並日夜而幽思兮，終悇憛而洞疑；
entries.en: Day and night I brood until anxiety hollows me out;
entries.literal: Together day and night I darkly ponder—ah, in the end anxious and pierced with doubt;

entries.zh: 高陽□其超遠兮，世孰可與論茲？
entries.en: Gaoyang's line rose remote as heaven—who alive can weigh such things with me?
entries.literal: Gaoyang [text missing] his transcendently distant—ah, in the age who can discuss this with me?

entries.zh: 訊夏啟於甘澤兮，傷帝典之始傾；
entries.en: I question Qi of Xia by Gan Pool and mourn where the golden age first cracked;
entries.literal: I question Xia Qi at Gan marsh—ah, I wound at the imperial norm's beginning to tilt;

entries.zh: 頌成、康之載德兮，詠《南風》之歌聲。
entries.en: I hymn Cheng and Kang's virtue and the tune of the 'South Wind.'
entries.literal: I praise Cheng and Kang's bearing virtue—ah, I chant the 'South Wind' song's sound.

entries.zh: 思唐、虞之晏晏兮，揖稷、契與為朋；
entries.en: I dwell on the calm of Yao and Shun's age and would take Hou Ji and Xie as my companions;
entries.literal: I think of Yao and Shun's peace and ease—ah, I bow to Ji and Xie and make them friends;

entries.zh: 苗裔紛其條暢兮，至湯、武而勃興。
entries.en: Their line branched and flourished until Tang and Wu burst forth in power.
entries.literal: Offspring and shoots profusely their branches spread—ah, down to Tang and Wu they surged to rise.

entries.zh: 昔三後之純粹兮，每季世而窮禍；
entries.en: The three ancient kings were utterly good—yet each dynasty ended in ruin;
entries.literal: Formerly the three rulers' purity—ah, each late age met utmost calamity;

entries.zh: 吊夏桀於南巢兮，哭殷紂於牧野。
entries.en: I mourn Jie of Xia besieged at Southern Nest and Zhou of Yin defeated at Muye.
entries.literal: I console Xia Jie at Southern Nest—ah, I weep for Yin Zhou at Muye.

entries.zh: 詔伊尹於亳郊兮，享呂望於酆州；
entries.en: I call Yi Yin from the outskirts of Bo and feast Lü Wang by Fengzhou;
entries.literal: I summon Yi Yin at Bo's outskirts—ah, I feast Lü Wang at Fengzhou;

entries.zh: 功與日月齊光兮，名與三王爭流。
entries.en: Their deeds shone with sun and moon; their fame runs alongside the three sage kings.
entries.literal: Merit with sun and moon shares light—ah, name with the three kings vies in flowing.

entries.zh: 楊朱號乎衢路兮，墨子泣乎白絲；
entries.en: Yang Zhu cried out at the crossroads; Mozi wept for silk turned from white;
entries.literal: Yang Zhu wails on the crossroads—ah, Mozi weeps over white silk;

entries.zh: 知漸染之易性兮，怨造作之弗思。
entries.en: They knew how habit alters the heart, and grieved that people plot without reflection.
entries.literal: Knowing gradual dyeing changes nature—ah, I resent contrivance that does not think.

entries.zh: 美《關雎》之識微兮，湣王道之將崩；
entries.en: I honor how the 'Guan ju' read the small signs; I pity the royal way as it crumbled;
entries.literal: I praise the 'Guan ju's' perceiving the subtle—ah, I pity the kingly way about to collapse;

entries.zh: 拔周唐之盛德兮，捃桓、文之譎功。
entries.en: I lift up the great virtue of the Zhou founders and collect the cunning triumphs of Huan and Wen.
entries.literal: I pluck Zhou and Tang's abundant virtue—ah, I gather Huan and Wen's crafty achievements.

entries.zh: 忿戰國之遘禍兮，憎權臣之擅強；
entries.en: I rage at the disasters of the Warring States and hate ministers who seized strength for themselves;
entries.literal: I resent the Warring States' meeting calamity—ah, I hate powerful ministers' usurping strength;

entries.zh: 黜楚子於南郢兮，執趙武於湨梁。
entries.en: I cast down the lord of Chu at his southern capital and hold Zhao Wu to account at Ju-liang.
entries.literal: I dismiss the Chu lord at southern Ying—ah, I seize Zhao Wu at Ju-liang.

entries.zh: 善忠信之救時兮，惡詐謀之妄作；
entries.en: I praise loyalty that saves the times and despise hollow stratagems;
entries.literal: I approve loyalty and good faith that rescue the age—ah, I hate deceitful plots' reckless making;

entries.zh: 聘申叔於陳蔡兮，禽荀息於虞虢。
entries.en: I would summon Shen Shu from Chen and Cai and seize Xun Xi where Yu and Guo fell;
entries.literal: I engage Shen Shu in Chen and Cai—ah, I capture Xun Xi at Yu and Guo.

entries.zh: 誅犁鋤之介聖兮，討臧倉之訴知；
entries.en: I would punish Li Chu for obstructing the sage and chastise Zang Cang for slandering the wise;
entries.literal: I punish Li's stubborn saintliness—ah, I chastise Zang Cang's accusing wisdom;

entries.zh: 巽子反於彭城兮，爵管仲於夷儀。
entries.en: I judge Zifan at Pengcheng and raise Guan Zhong at Yiyi with a noble title;
entries.literal: I humiliate Zifan at Pengcheng—ah, I ennoble Guan Zhong at Yiyi.

entries.zh: 疾兵革之浸滋兮，苦攻伐之萌生；
entries.en: I loathe the steady spread of war and the endless rise of campaigns;
entries.literal: I hate arms and leather's gradual spread—ah, I suffer attack and invasion's sprouting birth;

entries.zh: 沈孫武於五湖兮，斬白起於長平。
entries.en: I would drown Sun Wu in the five lakes and strike down Bai Qi at Changping.
entries.literal: I sink Sun Wu in the five lakes—ah, I behead Bai Qi at Changping.

entries.zh: 惡叢巧之亂世兮，毒從橫之敗俗；
entries.en: I abhor the tricks that disorder the world and the alliance arts that poisoned custom;
entries.literal: I hate clustered craftiness that disorders the age—ah, I poison vertical-horizontal alliance's ruining custom;

entries.zh: 流蘇秦於洹水兮，幽張儀於鬼谷。
entries.en: I would cast Su Qin into the Huan and shut Zhang Yi away in Ghost Valley.
entries.literal: I banish Su Qin to the Huan waters—ah, I imprison Zhang Yi in Ghost Valley.

entries.zh: 澄德化之陵遲兮，烈刑罰之峭峻；
entries.en: I mourn how moral influence faded and how cruel punishments flamed;
entries.literal: I clarify virtue-transforming's decline—ah, I blaze punishments' sheer harshness;

entries.zh: 燔商鞅之法術兮，燒韓非之說論。
entries.en: I would burn Shang Yang's statutes and consume Han Fei's treatises in flame.
entries.literal: I burn Shang Yang's methods—ah, I scorch Han Fei's discourse.

entries.zh: 誚始皇之跋扈兮，投李斯於四裔；
entries.en: I deride the First Emperor's tyranny and banish Li Si to the farthest frontier;
entries.literal: I mock First Emperor's domineering—ah, I cast Li Si to the four wilds;

entries.zh: 滅先王之法則兮，禍浸淫而弘大。
entries.en: They wiped out the laws of the ancient kings until disaster spread without end.
entries.literal: They extinguished former kings' norms—ah, disaster seeped and spread vast.

entries.zh: 援前聖以制中兮，矯二主之驕奢；
entries.en: I take the ancient sages as my measure and rebuke the pride and excess of two rulers;
entries.literal: Drawing former sages to establish the mean—ah, I correct the two lords' arrogance and luxury;

entries.zh: 馌女齊於絳臺兮，饗椒舉於章華。
entries.en: I feed Nü Qi at the Jiang terrace and feast Jiao Ju at Zhanghua Pavilion;
entries.literal: I bring provisions to Nü Qi at Jiang Terrace—ah, I feast Jiao Ju at Zhanghua.

entries.zh: 摛道德之光耀兮，匡衰世之眇風；
entries.en: I would unfold the light of the Way and set right the puny temper of a failing age;
entries.literal: I spread morality's brightness—ah, I rectify a declining age's feeble wind;

entries.zh: 褒宋襄於泓谷兮，表季劄於延陵。
entries.en: I honor Duke Xiang of Song at Hong and raise up Jizha of Yanling as a model;
entries.literal: I praise Duke Xiang of Song at Hong valley—ah, I display Jizha at Yanling.

entries.zh: 摭仁智之英華兮，激亂國之末流；
entries.en: I gather the flower of humanity and insight and try to stir the dying tide of ruined states;
entries.literal: I gather benevolence and wisdom's flower—ah, I stir chaotic states' dying current;

entries.zh: 觀鄭僑於溱洧兮，訪晏嬰於營丘。
entries.en: I watch Zichan by the Zhen and Wei and seek Yan Ying at Yingqiu.
entries.literal: I observe Zichan at Zhen and Wei—ah, I visit Yan Ying at Yingqiu.

entries.zh: 日曀曀其將暮兮，獨於邑而煩惑；
entries.en: The sun sinks in haze; alone in my hamlet I fret and lose my way;
entries.literal: The sun dimly is about to set—ah, alone I am vexed and troubled in the town;

entries.zh: 夫何九州之博大兮，迷不知路之南北；
entries.en: How wide the nine regions—yet I cannot tell south from north;
entries.literal: How vast the nine provinces' breadth—ah, lost I know not road's south or north;

entries.zh: 駟素□而馳聘兮，乘翠雲而相佯；
entries.en: My team of white horses flies; I ride the green clouds and roam at ease;
entries.literal: Four plain [text missing] horses gallop—ah, I ride emerald clouds and wander;

entries.zh: 就伯夷而折中兮，得務光而愈明。
entries.en: I seek Boyi for balance and find Wuguang until my purpose shines clearer.
entries.literal: I approach Boyi to find the mean—ah, I obtain Wuguang and grow clearer.

entries.zh: 款子高於中野兮，遇伯成而定慮；
entries.en: I call on Zigao in the open fields and meet Bocheng until my mind steadies;
entries.literal: I knock for Zigao in the central wild—ah, I meet Bocheng and settle intent;

entries.zh: 欽真人之德美兮，淹躊躇而弗去。
entries.en: I marvel at the worthies' virtue and linger, unable to tear myself away.
entries.literal: I admire the perfected man's virtue and beauty—ah, I linger hesitant and do not leave.

entries.zh: 意斟愖而不淡兮，俟回風而容與；
entries.en: My heart is anxious and never light; I wait on the turning wind and drift;
entries.literal: Intent cautious and not bland—ah, I await the whirlwind and wander easy;

entries.zh: 求善卷之所存兮，遇許由於負黍。
entries.en: I search for Shan Juan's dwelling and meet Xu You at Fushu.
entries.literal: I seek Shan Juan's whereabouts—ah, I meet Xu You at Fushu.

entries.zh: 軔吾車於箕陽兮，秣吾馬於潁滸；
entries.en: I halt my carriage at Jiyang and water my horses by the Ying;
entries.literal: I set my carriage brake at Jiyang—ah, I feed my horses at Ying's shore;

entries.zh: 聞至言而曉領兮，還吾反乎故宇。
entries.en: Perfect teaching clears my mind; I turn back toward my home.
entries.literal: Hearing utmost words I understand—ah, I return and turn back to my old house.

entries.zh: 顯宗即位，又多短衍以文過其實，遂廢於家。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, many maligned Feng Yan for rhetoric that outran the facts, and he was cast aside to live at home.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, again many belittled Yan for ornament exceeding substance—thereupon he was dismissed and stayed home.

entries.zh: 論曰：夫貴者負勢而驕人，才士負能而遺行，其大略然也。
entries.en: The historian remarks: the privileged rely on rank and slight others; clever men trust their gifts and neglect conduct—that is the usual pattern.
entries.literal: The judgment says: Now the noble rely on position and are arrogant to others; talented men rely on ability and abandon conduct—their general outline is thus.

entries.zh: 二子不其然乎！
entries.en: Were not these two men exactly such cases!
entries.literal: Did not the two sons conform to this!

entries.zh: 馮衍之引挑妻之譬，得矣。
entries.en: Feng Yan was right to compare choosing a wife to choosing allies.
entries.literal: Feng Yan's citing the analogy of picking a wife—he got it.

entries.zh: 夫納妻皆知取詈己者，而取士則不能。
entries.en: Everyone knows to marry someone who will speak plainly—even harshly—about her own faults, yet no one applies that rule when recruiting officials.
entries.literal: Now in taking a wife all know to take one who scolds herself—but in taking gentlemen they cannot.

entries.zh: 何也？
entries.en: Why is that?
entries.literal: Why?

entries.zh: 豈非反妒情易，而恕義情難。
entries.en: Perhaps resentment comes easily to human nature, while generosity grounded in duty does not.
entries.literal: Is it not that returning jealousy feeling is easy, while forgiving righteousness feeling is hard?

entries.zh: 光武雖得之於鮑永，猶失之於馮衍。
entries.en: Thus Guangwu gained Bao Yong but lost Feng Yan.
entries.literal: Guangwu although obtained him in Bao Yong, still lost him in Feng Yan.

entries.zh: 夫然，義直所以見屈於既往，守節故亦彌阻於來情。
entries.en: So it is: an unbending sense of right explains the slights of the past, and clinging to principle will only draw harder resistance from the world to come.
entries.literal: Thus it is that righteous straightness is the reason for being humiliated in what is past, and preserving integrity therefore is also ever more blocked in what is to come in feeling.

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: Alas!
entries.literal: Alas!

entries.zh: 建武末，上疏自陳曰：
entries.en: Toward the end of Jianwu, he submitted a memorial in his own defense:
entries.literal: At the end of the Jianwu era, he submitted a memorial stating his own case, saying:

entries.zh: 昔周公先遣伯禽守封於魯，以義割恩，寵不加後，故配天郊祀，三十餘世。
entries.en: Formerly, the Duke of Zhou sent Boqin to guard his fief in Lu, cutting affection off by duty and not piling later favor on his kin. Therefore his house was paired with Heaven in suburban sacrifice for more than thirty generations.
entries.literal: Formerly, the Duke of Zhou first sent Boqin to guard his fief in Lu, cutting off affection by duty and not adding favor afterward; therefore his line was paired with Heaven in suburban sacrifice for more than thirty generations.

entries.zh: 霍光秉政，輔翼少主，修善進士，名為忠直，而尊崇其宗黨，摧抑外戚，結貴據權，至堅至固，終沒之後，受禍滅門。
entries.en: Huo Guang governed for the boy emperor, promoted good men, and passed for loyal—yet he exalted his own clan, crushed the imperial in-laws, bound himself to power so tightly that when he died his whole line was destroyed.
entries.literal: Huo Guang held government, aided the young lord, cultivated goodness and advanced gentlemen—named loyal and upright—yet he honored and exalted his clan party, crushed and suppressed outer kin, tied to the noble and grasped power—most firm and solid; after he finally died, they suffered disaster and extermination of the whole gate.

entries.zh: 方今師傅皆以伊、周之位，據賢保之任，以此思化，則功何不至？
entries.en: Your tutors and guardians stand in the place of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou and bear the charge to protect wise counsel—if they truly taught reform, what goal could be beyond reach?
entries.literal: Now the tutors and guardians all hold Yi Yin and Duke of Zhou's positions, occupy the duty of protecting worthies—by this thinking of transformation, how could achievement not arrive?

entries.zh: 不思其危，則禍何不到？
entries.en: If they ignore the danger, how can ruin stay away?
entries.literal: If they do not think of its peril, how could disaster not arrive?

entries.zh: 損益之際，孔父攸嘆，持滿之戒，老氏所慎。
entries.en: At the turning between gain and loss Kongzi sighed; holding a full cup—what Laozi warned against.
entries.literal: At the juncture of diminishing and increasing, Kong Fu sighed; the warning of holding fullness—what Laozi cautioned.

entries.zh: 蓋功冠天下者不安，威震人主者不全。
entries.en: Whoever towers above the realm cannot rest easy; whoever terrifies his ruler cannot stay whole.
entries.literal: For merit crowning all under Heaven is not secure; awe shaking the human lord is not preserved.

entries.zh: 今承衰亂之後，繼重敝之世，公家屈竭，賦斂重數，苛吏奪其時，貪夫侵其財，百姓困乏，疾疫夭命。
entries.en: We stand on the ruins of turmoil: the treasury is dry, taxes multiply, harsh clerks steal farmers' seasons and predators seize their goods; common families starve and pestilence carries off the young.
entries.literal: Now inheriting after decline and chaos, succeeding a generation heavy with exhaustion—the ducal houses are drained and exhausted; levies and taxes are heavy and repeated; harsh clerks seize their seasons; greedy men encroach their wealth; the hundred surnames are destitute; plague and sickness cut short lives.

entries.zh: 盜賊群輩，且以萬數，軍行眾止，竊號自立，攻犯京師，燔燒縣邑，至乃訛言積弩入宮，宿衛驚懼。
entries.en: Brigands gather by the tens of thousands; armies march and halts multiply; rebels proclaim themselves and strike toward the capital; towns burn until rumor says crossbows have entered the palace and the night guard trembles.
entries.literal: Bandits swarm in groups—almost numbering ten thousand—armies march and masses halt; they steal titles and establish themselves; they attack and violate the capital region; they burn counties and cities—to the extent of false rumor that massed crossbows entered the palace; night guards were frightened and fearful.

entries.zh: 自漢興以來，誠未有也。
entries.en: Since the founding of Han nothing like this has been seen.
entries.literal: Since Han arose, truly there has never been such.

entries.zh: 國家微弱，奸謀不禁，六極之效，危於累卵。
entries.en: The dynasty is feeble and intrigue unchecked—the six extremes threaten us like eggs stacked high.
entries.literal: The state is weak and slight; treacherous plots are not forbidden—the effect of the six extremes is more perilous than a pile of eggs.

entries.zh: 王者承天順地，典爵主刑，不敢以天官私其宗，不敢以天罰輕其親。
entries.en: The true king receives his mandate from Heaven and walks the earth's pattern; he sets ranks and wields punishment—yet he does not treat heavenly office as a family monopoly nor lighten Heaven's sentence for kin.
entries.literal: The king receives Heaven and follows earth; he regulates ranks and administers punishments—he does not dare to privatize Heaven's offices for his clan; he does not dare lightly to apply Heaven's punishments to his kin.

entries.zh: 陛下宜遂聖明之德，昭然覺悟，遠述帝王之跡，近遵孝文之業，差五品之屬，納至親之序，亟遣使者征中山太後，置之別官，令時朝見。
entries.en: Your Majesty should recover enlightened rule: look far to the ancient kings and near to Emperor Wen—order the five grades of kin, restore precedence among close relatives, send envoys at once to bring the Queen Dowager of Zhongshan to a separate residence, and let her appear at court on schedule.
entries.literal: Your Majesty ought to complete sagely enlightened virtue, clearly awaken, far trace emperors and kings' tracks, near follow Emperor Xiaowen's enterprise; arrange the five grades' kin, admit utmost kin's order; urgently dispatch envoys to summon the Dowager of Zhongshan, place her in a separate palace, command timely court audiences.

entries.zh: 又召馮、衛二族，裁與冗職，使得執戟，親奉宿衛，以防未然之符，以抑患禍之端，上安社稷，下全保傅，內和親戚，外絕邪謀。
entries.en: Recall the Feng and Wei houses to nominal posts and halberd duty in the night guard—forestall what has not yet happened and choke off calamity at the source: secure the state above, protect your tutors below, bind kin within, and foil intrigue without.
entries.literal: Further summon the Feng and Wei two clans, assign them only supernumerary posts, let them hold halberds, personally attend night guard—to guard against omens not yet manifest, to suppress the beginnings of disaster and misfortune—above pacifying altars of soil and grain, below completing tutors and guardians; within harmonizing kin, without cutting off wicked plots.

entries.zh: 王莽時，寇賊群發，惲乃仰占玄象，嘆謂友人曰：『方今鎮、歲、熒惑並在漢分翼、軫之域，去而復來，漢必再受命，福歸有德。
entries.en: Under Wang Mang, Yun read the stars and told friends: "Jupiter, Saturn, and Mars stand together in the Wings and Chariot—the Han asterism; they left and returned—Han will receive the mandate again and fortune will favor the worthy.
entries.literal: At Wang Mang's time—bandits swarmed forth—Yun then upward observed dark patterns—sighed telling friends, saying: 'Now Jupiter, Saturn, Mars together in Han's division Wings and Chariot's region—departed yet again come—Han surely again receives mandate—blessing returns to the virtuous.

entries.zh: 如有順天發策者，必成大功。』
entries.en: Whoever answers Heaven's call will win a great achievement."
entries.literal: If there is one who obeys Heaven and raises strategy—must complete great merit.'

entries.zh: 時左隊大夫逯並素好士，惲說之曰：『當今上天垂象，智者以昌，愚者以亡。
entries.en: Lu Bing of the Left Corps loved talent; Yun urged him: "Heaven is signing—wise men rise and fools fall.
entries.literal: At the time Left Corps Grandee Lu Bing always loved gentlemen—Yun persuaded him, saying: 'Now upper Heaven hangs signs—wise ones thereby flourish—foolish ones thereby perish.

entries.zh: 昔伊尹自鬻輔商，立功全人。
entries.en: Yi Yin once sold himself to aid Shang and saved the people.
entries.literal: Formerly Yi Yin sold himself aiding Shang—completed merit preserved people.

entries.zh: 惲竊不遜，敢希伊尹之蹤，應天人之變。
entries.en: I dare aspire to Yi Yin's path and answer Heaven and humanity.
entries.literal: Yun rudely presumes not humble—dares hope Yi Yin's tracks—respond Heaven and man's changes.

entries.zh: 明府儻不疑逆，俾成天德。』
entries.en: If you do not doubt omens of revolt, you will fulfill Heaven's power."
entries.literal: Illustrious prefect if not doubting rebellion—will complete Heaven's virtue.'

entries.zh: 並奇之，使署為吏。
entries.en: Bing marveled and offered him a clerkship.
entries.literal: Bing marveled at him—ordered appoint as clerk.

entries.zh: 惲不謁，曰：『昔文王拔呂尚於渭濱，高宗禮傅說於巖築，桓公取管仲於射鉤，故能立弘烈，就元勛。
entries.en: Yun declined: "Wen met Taigong by the Wei; Wuding hailed Fu Yue from the cliffs; Huan Gong took Guan Zhong from captivity—never were chief ministers hired as mere clerks.
entries.literal: Yun did not pay a court visit, and said: 'Formerly King Wen drew Lü Shang from the Wei bank; Gaozong ritually honored Fu Yue from cliff-building; Duke Huan took Guan Zhong after the hook-shot; therefore they could establish vast merit and complete supreme achievement.

entries.zh: 未聞師相仲父，而可為吏位也。
entries.en: No one ever treated a chief counselor like a petty clerk.
entries.literal: Not heard teacher-minister uncle-like—yet can be clerk post.

entries.zh: 非窺天者不可與圖遠。
entries.en: Only one who reads Heaven may plan for the long term.
entries.literal: Not one who peers into Heaven—may not with plan far.

entries.zh: 君不授驥以重任，驥亦俯首裹足而去耳。』
entries.en: If you will not give the stallion a great burden, it will lower its head and walk away."
entries.literal: If lord does not give thoroughbred heavy burden—thoroughbred also lowers head wraps hooves and leaves.'

entries.zh: 遂不受署。
entries.en: He refused the post.
entries.literal: Thereupon did not accept appointment.

entries.zh: 鄭敬素與惲厚，見其言許歙，乃相招去，曰：『子廷爭繇延，君猶不納。
entries.en: Zheng Jing, Yun's friend, said: "You challenged Yan in open court and the governor still would not listen.
entries.literal: Zheng Jing always with Yun thick—saw his words reproved She—thereupon mutually invited to leave, saying: 'You court disputed Yao Yan—lord still not accepted.

entries.zh: 延今雖去，其勢必還。
entries.en: Yan may leave but he will surely come back.
entries.literal: Yan now although gone—his trend certainly will return.

entries.zh: 直心無諱，誠三代之道。
entries.en: Plain speech without concealment was the way of the Three Ages.
entries.literal: Straight mind without taboo—truly three dynasties' Way.

entries.zh: 然道不同者不相為謀，吾不能忍見子有不容君之危，盍去之乎！』
entries.en: Men who differ in principle cannot scheme together—I cannot watch you risk banishment—let us go!"
entries.literal: Yet those whose Way differs do not plot together—I cannot bear seeing you have danger of not being tolerated by lord—why not leave!'

entries.zh: 惲曰：『孟軻以強其君之所不能為忠，量其君之所不能為賊。
entries.en: Yun quoted Mencius: "To urge on your lord past his strength is loyalty; to demand what he cannot give is harm.
entries.literal: Yun said: 'Meng Ke took forcing his lord what he cannot as loyalty—measuring his lord what he cannot as injury.

entries.zh: 惲業已強之矣。
entries.en: I have already pressed him hard.
entries.literal: Yun's enterprise already forced him.

entries.zh: 障君於朝，既有其直，而不死職，罪也。
entries.en: Having challenged him in open court, to flee office now would itself be a crime.
entries.literal: Blocking lord at court—already having his straight—yet not dying in duty—crime.

entries.zh: 延退而惲又去，不可。』
entries.en: If Yan goes and I follow, it cannot be done."
entries.literal: Yan withdraws and Yun again leaves—cannot.'

entries.zh: 敬乃獨隱於弋陽山中，居數月，歙果復召延，惲於是乃去，從敬止，漁釣自娛，留數十日。
entries.en: Jing hid alone in the Yiyang hills; months later She recalled Yan, and Yun joined Jing to fish and idle away weeks.
entries.literal: Jing then alone hid in Yiyang mountains—dwelt several months—She indeed again summoned Yan—Yun thereupon left—followed Jing's stopping—fishing angling self-amused—remained several tens days.

entries.zh: 惲誌在從政，既乃喟然而嘆，謂敬曰：『天生俊士，以為人也。
entries.en: Yun still hungered for office and sighed to Jing: "Heaven breeds heroes for the world's use.
entries.literal: Yun's intent was in following government—thereupon sighed greatly—told Jing, saying: 'Heaven produces handsome gentlemen—to act for others.

entries.zh: 鳥獸不可與同群，子從我為伊、呂乎？
entries.en: Will you roam with beasts or follow me as Yi Yin and Lü Wang?
entries.literal: Birds and beasts cannot with same flock—you follow me to be Yi and Lü?

entries.zh: 將為巢、許，而父老堯、舜乎？』
entries.en: Or hide like Chaofu and Xu You while I serve Yao and Shun?"
entries.literal: Will be Chao and Xu—yet father elders Yao and Shun?'

entries.zh: 敬曰：『吾足矣。
entries.en: Jing said: "I have had enough.
entries.literal: Jing said: 'Your servant is enough.

entries.zh: 初從生步重華於南野，謂來歸為松子，今幸得全軀樹類，還奉墳墓，盡學問道，雖不從政，施之有政，是亦為政也。
entries.en: Long ago I walked with Shun in the southern wastes and dreamed of becoming the immortal Chisongzi; now I am content to keep this body, tend my parents' graves, and study—though I hold no office, teaching is also ruling.
entries.literal: First followed raw student pacing Chonghua at southern wild—called coming home pine seed—now fortunately obtained preserving body tree kind—returning serving tombs—exhausting learning asking Way—although not following government—applying it has government—this also is government.

entries.zh: 吾年耄矣，安得從子？
entries.en: I am too old to march with you.
entries.literal: Your servant's years aged—how obtain following you?

entries.zh: 子勉正性命，勿勞神以害生。』
entries.en: Tend your nature and spare your soul."
entries.literal: You strive to correct nature and life—do not weary spirit to harm life.'

entries.zh: 惲於是告別而去。
entries.en: Yun said farewell and departed.
entries.literal: Yun thereupon took leave and left.

entries.zh: 敬字次都，清誌高世，光武連征不到。
entries.en: Zheng Jing, courtesy name Cidu, kept aloof; Guangwu summoned him many times in vain.
entries.literal: Jing's style was Cidu—pure intent high age—Guangwu repeatedly summoned did not arrive.

entries.zh: 申屠剛
entries.en: Shentu Gang
entries.literal: Shentu Gang.

entries.zh: 蘇竟字伯況，扶風平陵人也。
entries.en: Su Jing, whose courtesy name was Bokuang, came from Pingling in Fufeng commandery.
entries.literal: Su Jing, courtesy name Bokuang, was a native of Pingling in Fufeng.

entries.zh: 平帝世，竟以明《易》為博士講《書》祭酒。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ping, Su Jing’s mastery of the Book of Changes earned him appointment as Erudite Libationer charged with expounding the Book of Documents.
entries.literal: In the era of Emperor Ping, Jing, because he was proficient in the Changes, became Erudite Libationer for lectures on the Documents.

entries.zh: 善圖緯，能通百家之言。
entries.en: He excelled at prognostic charts and apocryphal "weft" texts and commanded the literature of the hundred schools.
entries.literal: He was skilled in charts and weft texts and could embrace the teachings of the hundred schools.

entries.zh: 王莽時，與劉歆等共典校書，拜代郡中尉。
entries.en: Under Wang Mang he joined Liu Xin and others in overseeing editorial work on the palace books and received appointment as commandant of Dai commandery.
entries.literal: In Wang Mang’s time, together with Liu Xin and others he jointly supervised collation of the classics and was appointed Commandant of Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 時匈奴擾亂，北邊多罹其禍，竟終完輯一郡。
entries.en: While the Xiongnu ravaged the north and most border regions suffered, Su Jing nevertheless kept Dai commandery intact and at peace.
entries.literal: At that time the Xiongnu caused turmoil, and the northern frontier mostly suffered their harm; Jing in the end preserved and pacified the entire commandery intact.

entries.zh: 光武即位，就拜代郡太守，使固塞以拒匈奴。
entries.en: When Emperor Guangwu took the throne, Su Jing was confirmed as administrator of Dai commandery and tasked with fortifying the frontier against the Xiongnu.
entries.literal: When Guangwu ascended the throne, he was appointed on the spot as Administrator of Dai commandery and ordered to strengthen the passes to resist the Xiongnu.

entries.zh: 建武五年冬，盧芳略得北邊諸郡，帝使偏將軍隨弟屯代郡。
entries.en: In winter of Jianwu 5, Lu Fang overran the northern commanderies, and the emperor dispatched Adjutant-General Sui Di to station troops in Dai.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu, winter, Lu Fang seized control of the northern-border commanderies; the emperor sent Adjutant-General Sui Di to encamp in Dai commandery.

entries.zh: 竟病篤，以兵屬弟，詣京師謝罪。
entries.en: Su Jing fell seriously ill, transferred military authority to his brother, and traveled to the capital to submit himself for punishment.
entries.literal: Jing was gravely ill; he handed the troops to his younger brother and went to the capital to apologize for his faults.

entries.zh: 拜侍中，數月，以病免。
entries.en: He was made a palace attendant but within a few months resigned on grounds of ill health.
entries.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant; after several months he was dismissed because of illness.

entries.zh: 君執事無恙。
entries.en: I trust those who serve you are all well.
entries.literal: May those who attend you be without illness.

entries.zh: 走昔以摩研編削之才，與國師公從事出入，校定秘書，竊自依依，末由自遠。
entries.en: In former days I went in and out at the National Instructor’s side with nothing more than editing skill, helping collate the palace library; I cherished that connection in private yet could never break free of it.
entries.literal: I who formerly with the talent for polishing and editing went in and out in employment with the National Instructor, collating the secret books—secretly I clung to that tie myself, yet had no way to distance myself.

entries.zh: 蓋聞君子湣同類而傷不遇。
entries.en: They say a gentleman feels for his fellows and sorrows when worthy men go unrecognized.
entries.literal: I have heard that the gentleman pities those of his kind and grieves when they meet no proper recognition.

entries.zh: 人無愚智，莫不先避害然後求利，先定誌然後求名。
entries.en: Whether clever or dull, everyone first avoids danger, then pursues gain; first fixes intent, then pursues reputation.
entries.literal: Among people there is none, foolish or wise, who does not first flee harm and then seek profit, first settle his purpose and then seek a name.

entries.zh: 昔智果見智伯窮兵必亡，故變名遠逝，陳平知項王為天所棄，故歸心高祖，皆智之至也。
entries.en: Zhiguo saw Zhibo’s warmongering would destroy him and fled under an altered name; Chen Ping knew Xiang Yu was heaven-forsaken and gave his loyalty to Gaozu—both reached the height of discernment.
entries.literal: Formerly Zhiguo saw that Zhibo’s endless warfare would bring ruin, and so changed his name and fled far away; Chen Ping knew that the Hegemon-King of Chu was abandoned by Heaven, and so turned his heart to Gaozu—these were the utmost in wisdom.

entries.zh: 聞郡前權時屈節，北面延牙，乃後覺悟，棲遲養德。
entries.en: I hear your prefect once bent the knee to Yan Cen, then saw the light and withdrew to nurture his moral standing.
entries.literal: I hear that your commandery head once temporized and bowed north to Yan Ya, then afterward came to awareness and dwelt in retirement cultivating virtue.

entries.zh: 先世數子，又何以加。
entries.en: How could the worthy examples of earlier generations be improved upon?
entries.literal: The several sons of former generations—how could anything surpass them?

entries.zh: 君處陰中，土多賢士，若以須臾之間，研考異同，揆之圖書，測之人事，則得失利害，可陳於目，何自負畔亂之困，不移守惡之名乎？
entries.en: You live among talented men in obscurity; given a little time to weigh competing opinions against the charts and annals and the facts on the ground, you could see clearly what profits and what harms—why stay trapped in revolt and bear the stain of willful wrongdoing?
entries.literal: You dwell in obscurity, and the land has many worthy scholars; if in a brief span you examine and compare divergent views, measure them against the charts and documents and test them against human affairs, then gain and loss, benefit and harm can be arrayed before your eyes—why burden yourself with the straits of rebellion and cling to the reputation of clinging to evil?

entries.zh: 與君子之道，何其反也？
entries.en: How does that square with the conduct of a gentleman?
entries.literal: Compared with the way of the gentleman, how contrary is this?

entries.zh: 乃者，五月甲申，天有白虹，自子加午，廣可十丈，長可萬丈，正臨倚彌。
entries.en: Lately, on a fifth-month jiashen day, a white arc spanned from zi to wu—some ten feet wide and immense in length—hovering directly above Yimi.
entries.literal: Recently, on jiashen in the fifth month, Heaven had a white rainbow from zi striking wu, about ten Chinese feet wide and ten thousand feet long, directly overlying Yimi.

entries.zh: 倚彌即黎丘，秦豐之都也。
entries.en: Yimi is Liqiu, the seat of Qin Feng.
entries.literal: Yimi is Liqiu, the capital of Qin Feng.

entries.zh: 是時月入於畢。
entries.en: That same time the moon entered the Bi lodge.
entries.literal: At that time the moon entered Bi.

entries.zh: 畢為天網，主網羅無道之君，故武王將伐紂，上祭於畢，求助天也。
entries.en: Bi is the celestial net that snares wicked rulers. King Wu therefore sacrificed at Bi before marching against Shang, invoking Heaven’s aid.
entries.literal: Bi is Heaven’s net; it presides over netting lawless lords. Therefore when King Wu was about to attack Zhou, he sacrificed aloft at Bi, seeking aid from Heaven.

entries.zh: 夫仲夏甲申為八魁。
entries.en: A jiashen day in midsummer falls among the Eight Chiefs (bagui, spirits of closure).
entries.literal: Now midsummer jiashen is one of the Eight Chiefs (bagui).

entries.zh: 八魁，上帝開塞之將也，主退惡攘逆。
entries.en: Those Eight Chiefs are Heaven’s marshals of closure and release; they govern expulsion of wickedness and suppression of rebellion.
entries.literal: The Eight Chiefs are Heaven’s generals who open and block; they preside over driving off evil and rebelling against insurrection.

entries.zh: 流星狀似蚩尤旗，或曰營頭，或曰天槍，出奎而西北行，至延牙營上，散為數百而滅，奎為毒螫，主庫兵。
entries.en: A meteor like Chiyou’s banner—called "camp head" or "sky lance"—rose from Kui, streaked northwest to Yan Cen’s camp, broke into hundreds of sparks, and died; Kui stands for poison sting and armory stores.
entries.literal: A shooting star shaped like the Banner of Chiyou—some call it "camp head," some "sky lance"—issued from Kui and ran northwest to halt above Yan Ya’s camp, scattered into hundreds and vanished; Kui is venomous sting and presides over stored weapons.

entries.zh: 此二變，郡中及延牙士眾所共見也。
entries.en: Everyone in the district and Yan Cen’s troops saw both phenomena.
entries.literal: These two changes were jointly witnessed by the commandery and Yan Ya’s soldiers.

entries.zh: 是故延牙遂之武當，托言發兵，實避其殃。
entries.en: So Yan Cen withdrew toward Wudang under the pretext of mobilizing—actually fleeing Heaven’s warning.
entries.literal: Therefore Yan Ya then went to Wudang, claiming he was raising troops but in truth avoiding that calamity.

entries.zh: 今年《比卦》部歲，《坤》主立冬，《坎》主冬至，水性滅火，南方之兵受歲禍也。
entries.en: This year’s ruling hexagram is Bi; Kun holds Beginning of Winter, Kan the solstice; water quenches fire—southern armies will bear the year’s curse.
entries.literal: This year the Bi hexagram rules the year; Kun governs the Beginning of Winter; Kan governs the Winter Solstice; water’s nature extinguishes fire—the southern army will suffer the year’s bane.

entries.zh: 德在中宮，刑在木，木勝土，刑制德，今年兵事畢已，中國安寧之效也。
entries.en: Virtue sits in the central palace, retribution in wood; wood prevails over earth and checks virtue—campaigns will close and the heartland will rest.
entries.literal: Virtue lies in the central palace; punishment lies in wood; wood overcomes earth; punishment restrains virtue—this year military affairs will end, an omen of peace within the Middle Kingdom.

entries.zh: 五七之家三十五姓，彭、秦、延氏不得豫焉。
entries.en: The thirty-five great lineages of the five-and-seven houses omit Peng, Qin, and Yan.
entries.literal: The thirty-five surnames of the houses of five and seven do not include Peng, Qin, or Yan.

entries.zh: 如何怪惑，依而恃之？
entries.en: Why linger in wonder and pin hope on them?
entries.literal: How can you marvel and waver, relying on and trusting them?

entries.zh: 《葛累》之詩，『求福不回』，其若是乎！
entries.en: As the "Ge Lei" ode says, "Seek blessing without deviating"—surely that is the course.
entries.literal: The poem "Ge Lei" says, "Seeking blessing without turning aside"—can it be like this?

entries.zh: 夫周公之善康叔，以不從管、蔡之亂也；
entries.en: The Duke of Zhou favored Kangshu because Kangshu did not join Guan and Cai’s revolt.
entries.literal: The Duke of Zhou’s kindness to Kangshu lay in not following the rebellion of Guan and Cai.

entries.zh: 景帝之悅濟北，以不從吳濞之畔也。
entries.en: Emperor Jing favored the king of Jibei for refusing to follow Liu Pi’s rebellion.
entries.literal: Emperor Jing’s pleasure with the prince of Jibei lay in not following Wu Pi’s rebellion.

entries.zh: 自更始以來，孤恩背逆，歸義向善，臧否粲然，可不察歟！
entries.en: From Emperor Gengshi onward, traitors and loyalists stand in sharp contrast—how can you not see which side is which?
entries.literal: Since Gengshi, those who betrayed grace and turned rebel stand against those who returned to righteousness—good and bad are dazzlingly clear; can one fail to inspect this?

entries.zh: 良醫不能救無命，強梁不能與天爭，故天之所壞，人不得支。
entries.en: No doctor cures Heaven-doomed patients; brute force cannot rival fate—what Heaven tears down, mortals cannot shore up.
entries.literal: A fine physician cannot save those Heaven has doomed; the violent cannot contend with Heaven—therefore what Heaven ruins, man cannot prop up.

entries.zh: 宜密與太守劉君共謀降議。
entries.en: You should quietly confer with Administrator Liu on terms of surrender.
entries.literal: You ought secretly to plot surrender together with Administrator Liu.

entries.zh: 仲尼棲棲，墨子遑遑，憂人之甚也。
entries.en: Confucius hurried from court to court; Mozi rushed about—they cared for humanity that intensely.
entries.literal: Confucius was anxious and hurried; Mozi was frantic—such was their extreme care for others.

entries.zh: 屠羊救楚，非要爵祿；
entries.en: The butcher who rescued Chu sought no fiefs or salary.
entries.literal: The butcher who saved Chu did not crave titles and stipends.

entries.zh: 茅焦幹秦，豈求報利？
entries.en: When Mao Jiao confronted the Qin court, was he angling for profit?
entries.literal: Mao Jiao remonstrated with Qin—did he hunt repayment?

entries.zh: 盡忠博愛之誠，憤懣不能已耳。
entries.en: They acted from devotion and universal compassion—wrath at wrong simply could not be contained.
entries.literal: It was the earnestness of utter loyalty and universal love; indignation could not be stopped.

entries.zh: 樊宏字靡卿，南陽湖陽人也，世祖之舅。
entries.en: Fan Hong, courtesy name Miqing, came from Huyang in Nanyang and was Emperor Guangwu's maternal uncle.
entries.literal: Fan Hong, courtesy name Miqing, was a man of Huyang in Nanyang; he was Shizu's maternal uncle.

entries.zh: 其先周仲山甫，封於樊，因而氏焉，為鄉里著姓。
entries.en: The line descended from Zhong Shanfu of Zhou, enfeoffed at Fan, whence the surname—a leading local family.
entries.literal: His ancestor was Zhou Zhongshanfu, enfeoffed at Fan, and from this took the surname; they became a prominent clan of the village.

entries.zh: 父重，字君雲，世善農稼，好貨殖。
entries.en: His father Chong, courtesy name Junyun, came from a line of skilled farmers and had a gift for commerce.
entries.literal: His father Chong, courtesy name Junyun, for generations was good at farming and liked trade and accumulation.

entries.zh: 重性溫厚，有法度，三世共財，子孫朝夕禮敬，常若公家。
entries.en: Chong was gentle and principled. Three generations held property in common; descendants greeted one another morning and evening with the formality of a court household.
entries.literal: Chong's nature was mild and generous; he had standards and measures; three generations shared property; sons and grandsons morning and evening observed ritual respect, always as if in a public household.

entries.zh: 其營理產業，物無所棄，課役童隸，各得其宜，故能上下戮力，財利歲倍，至乃開廣田土三百餘頃。
entries.en: He ran his lands without waste, matched every servant to the right task, and doubled his income year by year until he held more than three hundred qing.
entries.literal: In managing his estates he wasted nothing; he assigned tasks to boys and slaves, each getting what was fitting; therefore above and below could join strength, profits doubled yearly, until he had opened and extended over three hundred qing of fields.

entries.zh: 其所起廬舍，皆有重堂高閣，陂渠灌註。
entries.en: His manor houses had double halls and tall pavilions, with dikes and canals for irrigation.
entries.literal: The lodges and houses he built all had double halls and high towers, ponds and channels for irrigation.

entries.zh: 又池魚牧畜，有求必給。
entries.en: Fishponds and herds supplied every request.
entries.literal: Moreover pond fish and pastured livestock—whatever was sought was always supplied.

entries.zh: 嘗欲作器物，先種梓漆，時人嗤之，然積以歲月，皆得其用，向之笑者咸求假焉。
entries.en: Planning to furnish his estate, he planted catalpa and lacquer years ahead; neighbors mocked him until the timber and lacquer matured—then they all came begging to borrow.
entries.literal: When he wished to make tools and vessels, he first planted catalpa and lacquer; people of the time scoffed, yet accumulated over years, all obtained their use; those who had laughed all sought to borrow.

entries.zh: 資至巨萬，而賑贍宗族，恩加鄉閭。
entries.en: His fortune ran to millions, yet he fed his kin and spread generosity through the countryside.
entries.literal: His wealth reached tens of millions, yet he relieved and supplied the clan lineage, and grace extended to the village lanes.

entries.zh: 外孫何氏兄弟爭財，重恥之，以田二頃解其忿訟。
entries.en: When his He grandsons quarreled over an inheritance, Chong ended the suit with two qing of land out of shame at the dispute.
entries.literal: His grandsons by his daughter, the He brothers, disputed property; Chong shamed at it, with two qing of fields resolved their angry lawsuit.

entries.zh: 縣中稱美，推為三老。
entries.en: The county honored him and named him one of the three village elders.
entries.literal: The county praised his excellence and pushed him to be one of the three elders.

entries.zh: 年八十餘終。
entries.en: He died in his eighties.
entries.literal: He ended at over eighty years of age.

entries.zh: 其素所假貸人間數百萬，遺令焚削文契。
entries.en: He had lent millions across the neighborhood; his dying order was to burn the IOUs.
entries.literal: What he had habitually lent to others among the people was several million cash; he left instructions to burn and cut the written contracts.

entries.zh: 責家聞者皆慚，爭往償之，諸子從敕，竟不肯受。
entries.en: Debtors, shamed, rushed to repay; his sons obeyed his will and refused every coin.
entries.literal: Debtors who heard were all ashamed and vied to go repay; his sons followed the command and to the end refused to accept.

entries.zh: 臣聞賈誼有言，『人君不可以不學』。
entries.en: Jia Yi said, 'A ruler must never stop learning.'
entries.literal: Your servant has heard Jia Yi had words: 'The lord of men cannot but study.'

entries.zh: 故雖大舜聖德，孳孳為善；
entries.en: Even Shun, for all his sagely virtue, strove endlessly for goodness;
entries.literal: Therefore though great Shun had sagely virtue, he was zealous in doing good;

entries.zh: 成王賢主，崇明師傅。
entries.en: King Cheng was a wise king who honored his teachers.
entries.literal: King Cheng was a worthy lord; he exalted and clarified tutors and masters.

entries.zh: 及光武皇帝受命中興，群雄崩擾，旌旗亂野，東西誅戰，不遑啟處，然猶投戈講藝，息馬論道。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu raised the Han amid chaos and war, yet still laid down arms to teach the classics and dismounted to discuss the Way.
entries.literal: When Emperor Guangwu received the mandate and revived the house, the host of heroes collapsed in turmoil, banners and flags maddened the wilderness, east and west punished and battled, no leisure to kneel or sit—yet still he cast aside the spear and lectured on arts, rested horses and discussed the Way.

entries.zh: 至孝明皇帝，兼天地之姿，用日月之明，庶政萬機，無不簡心，而垂情古典，遊意經藝，每饗射禮畢，正坐自講，諸儒並聽，四方欣欣。
entries.en: Emperor Ming combined natural brilliance with care for every duty, yet loved the classics: after each archery rite he lectured the erudites himself, and the realm rejoiced.
entries.literal: Coming to Emperor Xiaoming, combining Heaven and Earth's bearing, employing sun and moon's brightness—myriad affairs of the myriad tasks, none not simplified in heart—yet he let feeling hang on classical antiquity, roamed intent in the classics and arts; each time the banquet archery rite finished, he sat upright and lectured himself; the various scholars all listened; the four quarters were joyful.

entries.zh: 雖闕里之化，矍相之事，誠不足言。
entries.en: Confucius's school at Que and the archery grounds at Juexiang hardly compare.
entries.literal: Though the transformation of Que village, the affairs of Juexiang—truly not worth speaking of.

entries.zh: 又多徵名儒，以充禮官，如沛國趙孝、瑯邪承宮等，或安車結駟，告歸鄉里；
entries.en: Famous scholars such as Zhao Xiao of Pei and Cheng Gong of Langye filled ritual posts—some rode home in honor carriages;
entries.literal: Moreover many were summoned, famous scholars, to fill ritual offices, such as Zhao Xiao of Pei state, Cheng Gong of Langye, and others—some with secure carriages and four-horse teams, announcing return to village lanes;

entries.zh: 或豐衣博帶，從見宗廟。
entries.en: others in full dress attended the imperial shrines.
entries.literal: some in rich robes and broad belts, following to see the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 其餘以經術見優者，布在廊廟。
entries.en: Every scholar who excelled in the classics held a place at court.
entries.literal: The rest who by classic arts were shown favor were spread through hall and temple.

entries.zh: 故朝多皤皤之良，華首之老。
entries.en: The court thronged with white-haired worthies.
entries.literal: Therefore the court had many hoary-headed worthies, flower-headed elders.

entries.zh: 每宴會，則論難衎衎，共求政化。
entries.en: At every feast they debated the classics in good humor, all seeking sound government.
entries.literal: Whenever there was banquet assembly, then they debated difficulties with harmonious ease, jointly seeking government and transformation.

entries.zh: 詳覽群言，響如振玉。
entries.en: He weighed every opinion; their resonance was like the chime of jade.
entries.literal: He examined in detail the host of words; the echo was like shaking jade.

entries.zh: 朝者進而思政，罷者退而備問。
entries.en: Men at court thought on policy; men who left office studied to ask better questions.
entries.literal: Those who courted advanced and pondered governance; those who left office withdrew and prepared questions.

entries.zh: 小大隨化，雍雍可嘉。
entries.en: High and low moved with the civilizing tide—harmony worth praising.
entries.literal: Small and great followed transformation; harmonious, worthy of praise.

entries.zh: 期門羽林介胄之士，悉通《孝經》。
entries.en: Even the armored guards of the palace gates and feathered forest knew the Classic of Filial Piety.
entries.literal: Gentlemen of the palace gate and feathered forest in armor and helmet—all comprehended the Classic of Filial Piety.

entries.zh: 博士議郎，一人開門，徒眾百數。
entries.en: Each erudite or consultant who opened a school drew hundreds of disciples.
entries.literal: Erudites and gentleman consultants—one man opening a gate, followers numbering in the hundreds.

entries.zh: 化自聖躬，流及蠻荒，匈奴遣伊秩訾王大車且渠來入就學。
entries.en: Culture radiated from the throne to the barbarian marches—the Xiongnu even sent the Worthy King of the Left and senior chief Juqu to study at court.
entries.literal: Transformation came from the sage's person, flowed to the wild Man; the Xiongnu sent the Yizhi Zi king, great cart Juqu, to come in and attend study.

entries.zh: 八方肅清，上下無事。
entries.en: The realm was at peace from every quarter; court and country were untroubled.
entries.literal: The eight directions were cleared and pure; above and below had no troubles.

entries.zh: 是以議者每稱盛時，咸言永平。
entries.en: Critics who praise a golden age always name the Yongping years.
entries.literal: Therefore discussers whenever they praised a flourishing age all spoke of Yongping.

entries.zh: 建武元年，光武遣使迎陰貴人於新野，並徵識。
entries.en: In Jianwu 1 Guangwu sent for Lady Yin from Xinye and summoned Yin Shi as well.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, Guangwu sent envoys to welcome the Yin honorable lady at Xinye, and concurrently summoned Shi.

entries.zh: 識隨貴人至，以為騎都尉，更封陰鄉侯。
entries.en: He accompanied his sister to court as commandant of cavalry and received a new fief as marquis of Yin township.
entries.literal: Shi followed the honorable lady in arriving; he was made commandant of cavalry, transferred enfeoffment to marquis of Yin township.

entries.zh: 二年，以征伐軍功增封，識叩頭讓曰：『天下初定，將帥有功者眾，臣托屬掖廷，仍加爵邑，不可以示天下。』
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 his fief was enlarged for military merit; Yin Shi kowtowed and refused: 'The empire is new and many generals deserve reward; I am kin to the harem—more land for me would send the wrong message.'
entries.literal: In the second year, for campaign and punitive merit his enfeoffment was increased; Shi knocked his head and yielded, saying, 'The realm is newly settled; commanders and generals with merit are many; your servant relies on connection to the rear palace, yet is again added noble rank and territory—it cannot be shown to the realm.'

entries.zh: 帝甚美之，以為關都尉，鎮函谷。
entries.en: The emperor admired his modesty and named him colonel of the passes to guard Hangu.
entries.literal: The emperor greatly praised him, made him colonel of the passes, garrisoned Hangu.

entries.zh: 遷侍中，以母憂辭歸。
entries.en: He rose to palace attendant, then resigned to mourn his mother.
entries.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant; for mother's mourning he resigned and returned.

entries.zh: 十五年，定封原鹿侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 15 his fief was fixed at Yuanlu.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, his enfeoffment was fixed as marquis of Yuanlu.

entries.zh: 及顯宗立為皇太子，以識守執金吾，輔導東宮。
entries.en: When the future Emperor Ming became heir apparent, Yin Shi served as bearer of the mace and tutored the eastern palace.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming was established as heir apparent, Shi was made to guard the bearer of the mace and instruct and guide the eastern palace.

entries.zh: 帝每巡郡國，識常留鎮守京師，委以禁兵。
entries.en: Whenever the emperor toured the provinces, Yin Shi stayed to guard the capital and command the guards.
entries.literal: Whenever the emperor toured commanderies and kingdoms, Shi always remained to garrison and guard the capital, entrusting him with forbidden troops.

entries.zh: 入雖極言正議，及與賓客語，未嘗及國事。
entries.en: He spoke frankly in audience but never discussed state business with visitors.
entries.literal: In entering though he spoke to the utmost correct views, when speaking with guests he never touched state affairs.

entries.zh: 帝敬重之，常指識以敕戒貴戚，激厲左右焉。
entries.en: The emperor esteemed him and held him up as a model to imperial in-laws and the court.
entries.literal: The emperor respected and valued him, often pointed to Shi to instruct and warn noble affines, and to stimulate and encourage those around him.

entries.zh: 識所用掾史皆簡賢者，如虞廷、傅寬、薛愔等，多至公卿校尉。
entries.en: He chose worthy subordinates such as Yu Ting, Fu Kuan, and Xue Yin; many rose to ministerial rank.
entries.literal: The clerks Shi employed were all selected worthies, such as Yu Ting, Fu Kuan, Xue Yin, and others; many reached three dukes and colonels.

entries.zh: 世祖即位，拜光祿大夫，位特進，次三公。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu named him minister of the household with specially advanced rank, standing just below the three dukes.
entries.literal: When Shizu ascended the throne, he appointed Hong minister of the household, rank specially advanced, next after the three dukes.

entries.zh: 建武五年，封長羅侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 5 he received the marquisate of Changluo.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu, he was enfeoffed as marquis of Changluo.

entries.zh: 十三年，封弟丹為射陽侯，兄子尋玄鄉侯，族兄忠更父侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 13 his brother Dan became marquis of Sheyang, his nephew Xun marquis of Xuan township, and his cousin Zhong marquis of Gengfu.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year, his younger brother Dan was enfeoffed as marquis of Sheyang, his elder brother's son Xun as marquis of Xuan township, his clan elder brother Zhong as marquis of Gengfu.

entries.zh: 十五年，定封宏壽張侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 15 his fief was fixed at Shouzhang.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year, Hong's enfeoffment was fixed as marquis of Shouzhang.

entries.zh: 十八年，帝南祠章陵，過湖陽，祠重墓，追爵謚為壽張敬侯，立廟於湖陽，車駕每南巡，常幸其墓，賞賜大會。
entries.en: In Jianwu 18 the emperor sacrificed at Zhangling, stopped at Huyang to honor Fan Chong's grave, posthumously titled him Reverent Marquis of Shouzhang, built a temple, and on every southern tour visited the tomb with rich gifts.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year, the emperor sacrificed south at Zhangling, passed Huyang, sacrificed at Chong's tomb, posthumously enfeoffed and posthumously titled him reverent marquis of Shouzhang, established a temple at Huyang; whenever the imperial carriage toured south, he always favored his tomb with great grants and a great assembly.

entries.zh: 鯈字長魚，謹約有父風。
entries.en: Fan Tiao, courtesy name Changyu, was as careful and restrained as his father.
entries.literal: Tiao, courtesy name Changyu, was cautious and restrained and had his father's manner.

entries.zh: 事後母至孝，及母卒，哀思過禮，毀病不自支，世祖常遣中黃門朝暮送饘粥。
entries.en: He mourned his stepmother past the bounds of ritual until he fell ill; Emperor Guangwu sent eunuchs morning and evening with gruel.
entries.literal: He served his stepmother with utmost filiality; when she died, grief and longing exceeded the rites; he wasted away ill and could not support himself; Shizu often sent palace attendants morning and evening to deliver gruel.

entries.zh: 服闋，就侍中丁恭受《公羊嚴氏春秋》。
entries.en: After mourning he studied the Yan school Gongyang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals under Attendant-in-Chief Ding Gong.
entries.literal: When mourning was complete, he went to attendant Ding Gong to receive the Gongyang Yan lineage Spring and Autumn Annals.

entries.zh: 建武中，禁網尚闊，諸王既長，各招引賓客，以鯈外戚，爭遣致之，而鯈清靜自保，無所交結。
entries.en: In Jianwu the laws were loose; grown princes vied for clients and courted Fan Tiao as imperial in-law, but he kept to himself and joined no faction.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu period, the prohibition net was still loose; the various princes having grown, each summoned and drew retainers; because Tiao was outer kin, they vied to send and bring him, yet Tiao was clear and quiet, preserving himself, associating and connecting with none.

entries.zh: 及沛王輔事發，貴戚子弟多見收捕，鯈以不豫得免。
entries.en: When Prince Liu Fu of Pei fell, many imperial in-laws were arrested; Fan Tiao escaped because he had never joined their circle.
entries.literal: When the Prince of Pei Fu affair broke, noble affines' sons and younger kin were mostly seized and arrested; Tiao because he had not participated obtained exemption.

entries.zh: 帝崩，鯈為復土校尉。
entries.en: When the emperor died, Fan Tiao served as colonel in charge of the imperial burial.
entries.literal: When the emperor died, Tiao became colonel of the earth-returning [burial].

entries.zh: 興字君陵，光烈皇后母弟也，為人有膂力。
entries.en: Yin Xing, courtesy name Junling, was Empress Yin's younger brother and a man of great physical strength.
entries.literal: Xing, courtesy name Junling, was Empress Guanglie's mother's younger brother; as a person he had physical strength.

entries.zh: 建武二年，為黃門侍郎，守期門僕射，典將武騎，從征伐，平定郡國。
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 he became a palace attendant and acting superintendent of the palace gate, led the imperial cavalry on campaign, and helped pacify the realm.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, he was palace attendant of the yellow gate, acting superintendent of the palace gate, in charge of leading martial cavalry; he followed in campaigns and punishments, pacifying commanderies and kingdoms.

entries.zh: 興每從出入，常操持小蓋，障翳風雨，躬履塗泥，率先期門。
entries.en: On every outing he carried an umbrella over the emperor, waded mud, and led the palace guards.
entries.literal: Whenever Xing followed in and out, he always held a small umbrella, screened wind and rain, personally trod mud, and led the palace gate first.

entries.zh: 光武所幸之處，輒先入清宮，甚見親信。
entries.en: He always entered first to secure whatever lodging Guangwu chose and won deep trust.
entries.literal: Wherever Guangwu favored going, he always entered first to clear the palace; he was greatly trusted.

entries.zh: 雖好施接賓，然門無俠客。
entries.en: Though generous to guests, he kept no adventurers at his door.
entries.literal: Though he liked giving and receiving guests, yet his gate had no knight-errant clients.

entries.zh: 與同郡張宗、上谷鮮于裒不相好，知其有用，猶稱所長而達之；
entries.en: He disliked Zhang Zong and Xianyu Pou but still recommended their strengths when it served the state;
entries.literal: With Zhang Zong of the same commandery and Xianyu Pou of Shanggu he was not on good terms; knowing they had usefulness, he still praised their strengths and advanced them;

entries.zh: 友人張汜、杜禽與興厚善，以為華而少實，但私之以財，終不為言：是以世稱其忠平。
entries.en: Friends Zhang Fan and Du Qin were close, but he thought them flashy and shallow—he gave them money privately but never recommended them. The world called him loyal and fair.
entries.literal: Friends Zhang Fan and Du Qin were thickly good with Xing; he thought them splendid but lacking substance, only privately gave them wealth, in the end did not speak for them—therefore the age called him loyal and fair.

entries.zh: 第宅茍完，裁蔽風雨。
entries.en: His house was barely finished—only enough to keep out the weather.
entries.literal: His mansion was barely complete, only enough to screen wind and rain.

entries.zh: 九年，遷侍中，賜爵關內侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 9 he became palace attendant and received the rank of full marquis within the passes.
entries.literal: In the ninth year, he was promoted to palace attendant and granted the noble rank of full marquis within the passes.

entries.zh: 帝後召興，欲封之，置印綬於前，興固讓曰：『臣未有先登陷陣之功，而一家數人並蒙爵士，令天下觖望，誠為盈溢。
entries.en: The emperor offered a fief; Yin Xing refused: 'I have never stormed the enemy first, yet our family already holds many titles—the empire would resent further reward.'
entries.literal: Later the emperor summoned Xing, wished to enfeoff him, placed seals and ribbons before him; Xing firmly yielded, saying, 'Your servant has no merit of first ascending and breaching the ranks, yet several persons of one family together receive noble rank and territory—making the realm look askance—it is truly overflowing.'

entries.zh: 臣蒙陛下、貴人恩澤至厚，富貴已極，不可復加，至誠不願。』
entries.en: Your majesty and my sister have honored me enough; I cannot accept more.'
entries.literal: Your servant has received Your Majesty's and the honorable lady's grace and favor to the utmost; wealth and honor are already extreme, cannot be further increased—sincerely I do not wish it.'

entries.zh: 帝嘉興之讓，不奪其志。
entries.en: The emperor respected his refusal and did not force the title on him.
entries.literal: The emperor praised Xing's yielding and did not seize his intent.

entries.zh: 貴人問其故，興曰：『貴人不讀書心邪？
entries.en: His sister asked why. He said, 'Have you not read the Book of Changes?'
entries.literal: The honorable lady asked his reason; Xing said, 'Has the honorable lady not read the Changes?'

entries.zh: 「亢龍有悔。」
entries.en: The line on the dragon at the top of the hexagram: pride brings regret.'
entries.literal: 'The proud dragon will have cause to repent.'

entries.zh: 夫外戚家苦不知廉退，嫁女欲配侯王，取婦眄睨公主，愚心實不安也。
entries.en: In-law families never know when to stop—marrying daughters to princes, sons to princesses. That path terrifies me.'
entries.literal: Now affinal families bitterly fail to know modest retreat; marrying daughters they wish to match marquises and kings; taking wives they leer at princesses—this foolish heart is truly uneasy.'

entries.zh: 富貴有極，人當知足，誇奢益為觀聽所譏。』
entries.en: Fortune has its limit; greed for display only draws ridicule.'
entries.literal: Wealth and honor have a limit; people ought to know satisfaction; boasting extravagance is further mocked by sight and hearing.'

entries.zh: 貴人感其言，深自降挹，卒不為宗親求位。
entries.en: The empress took his words to heart, checked her family's ambition, and never sought posts for kin.
entries.literal: The honorable lady was moved by his words, deeply lowered and restrained herself, in the end did not seek office for clan kin.

entries.zh: 十九年，拜衛尉，亦輔導皇太子。
entries.en: In Jianwu 19 he became superintendent of the guards and tutored the heir apparent.
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year, he was appointed superintendent of the guards, also instructing and guiding the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 明年夏，帝風眩疾甚，後以興領侍中，受顧命於雲臺廣室。
entries.en: The next summer Guangwu's vertigo grew severe; Yin Xing was named chief palace attendant and received the deathbed charge in the Cloud Terrace hall.
entries.literal: The next summer, the emperor's wind-dizziness illness was severe; afterward Xing was put in charge of palace attendant, received testamentary charge in the Cloud Terrace broad chamber.

entries.zh: 會疾廖，召見興，欲以代吳漢為大司馬。
entries.en: When the emperor recovered, he wished to replace Wu Han with Yin Xing as grand marshal.
entries.literal: It happened that the illness abated; he summoned and saw Xing, wished to use him to replace Wu Han as grand marshal.

entries.zh: 興叩頭流涕，固讓曰：『臣不敢惜身，誠虧損聖德，不可茍冒。』
entries.en: Yin Xing kowtowed in tears: 'I do not cling to life, but accepting would harm your reputation—I cannot.'
entries.literal: Xing knocked his head and wept, firmly yielding, saying, 'Your servant does not dare spare his person; truly it would injure sagely virtue—cannot carelessly presume.'

entries.zh: 至誠發中，感動左右，帝遂聽之。
entries.en: His sincerity moved everyone present, and the emperor yielded.
entries.literal: Sincerity issued from within, moved those left and right; the emperor thereupon listened to him.

entries.zh: 宏少有誌行。
entries.en: Fan Hong showed purpose and integrity from an early age.
entries.literal: Hong in youth had aims and conduct.

entries.zh: 王莽末，義兵起，劉伯升與族兄賜俱將兵攻湖陽，城守不下。
entries.en: Late in Wang Mang's reign, Liu Yan (Bosheng) and his cousin Liu Ci besieged Huyang without taking it.
entries.literal: At the end of Wang Mang, righteous troops rose; Liu Bosheng together with his clan elder brother Ci both led troops to attack Huyang; the city held and would not fall.

entries.zh: 賜女弟為宏妻，湖陽由是收系宏妻子，令出譬伯升，宏因留不反。
entries.en: Liu Ci's sister was Fan Hong's wife, so Huyang jailed Hong's family and ordered him to persuade Liu Yan to lift the siege. Hong stayed with the rebels instead.
entries.literal: Ci's younger sister was Hong's wife; Huyang thereupon seized and bound Hong's wife and children, ordered him to go out and persuade Bosheng; Hong thereupon stayed and did not return.

entries.zh: 湖陽軍帥欲殺其妻子，長吏以下共相謂曰：『樊重子父，禮義恩德行於鄉里，雖有罪，且當在後。』
entries.en: The garrison commander wanted them executed, but local officials said, 'The Fan family has earned the district's respect—punishment can wait.'
entries.literal: The Huyang army commander wished to kill his wife and children; the senior clerk downward all said to one another, 'Fan Chong's son and father—ritual, righteousness, kindness, and virtue move through the village lanes; though there is guilt, it should wait for later.'

entries.zh: 會漢兵日盛，湖陽惶急，未敢殺之，遂得免脫。
entries.en: As Han forces grew, Huyang panicked and never carried out the execution; the family went free.
entries.literal: It happened that Han troops grew stronger daily; Huyang was alarmed and urgent and did not dare kill them; thereupon they obtained release.

entries.zh: 更始立，欲以宏為將，宏叩頭辭曰：『書生不習兵事。』
entries.en: The Gengshi regime wanted Fan Hong as a general; he kowtowed and refused: 'I am a scholar, not a soldier.'
entries.literal: When Gengshi was established, he wished to make Hong a general; Hong knocked his head and declined, saying, 'A scholar does not practice military affairs.'

entries.zh: 竟得免歸。
entries.en: He was allowed to go home.
entries.literal: In the end he obtained dismissal and return.

entries.zh: 與宗家親屬作營塹自守，老弱歸之者千餘家。
entries.en: He and his clan threw up earthworks for defense; more than a thousand households of refugees joined him.
