entries.literal: Together with lineage kin he made ramparts and moats to defend himself; old and weak who came to him were over a thousand households.

entries.zh: 時赤眉賊掠唐子鄉，多所殘殺，欲前攻宏營，宏遣人持牛酒米穀，勞遺赤眉。
entries.en: When Red Eyebrows ravaged Tangzi and turned toward Fan Hong's camp, he sent gifts of food and drink.
entries.literal: At that time the Red Eyebrow bandits plundered Tangzi township, killing many; they wished to advance and attack Hong's camp; Hong sent men bearing cattle, wine, rice, and grain to comfort and gift the Red Eyebrows.

entries.zh: 赤眉長老先聞宏仁厚，皆稱曰：『樊君素善，且今見待如此，何心攻之。』
entries.en: Their elders had heard of Fan Hong's kindness. 'He has always been good to people, and now he treats us like this—how could we attack him?'
entries.literal: The Red Eyebrow elders had earlier heard Hong was benevolent and generous; they all declared, 'Lord Fan has always been good, and now we are treated thus—what heart would attack him?'

entries.zh: 引兵而去，遂免寇難。
entries.en: They marched away, and Fan Hong's people were spared.
entries.literal: They led troops and departed; thereupon he escaped bandit calamity.

entries.zh: 及劉伯升起義兵，識時遊學長安，聞之，委業而歸，率子弟、宗族、賓客千餘人往詣伯升。
entries.en: When Liu Yan raised troops, Yin Shi was studying in Chang'an; he rushed home with more than a thousand kinsmen and retainers to join Liu Yan.
entries.literal: When Liu Bosheng raised righteous troops, Shi at that time was studying abroad in Chang'an; hearing it, he abandoned his enterprise and returned, leading sons and younger brothers, clan lineage, and guests over a thousand persons to go to Bosheng.

entries.zh: 伯升乃以識為校尉。
entries.en: Liu Yan named him a colonel.
entries.literal: Bosheng thereupon made Shi a colonel.

entries.zh: 更始元年，遷偏將軍，從攻宛，別降新野、淯陽、杜衍、冠軍、湖陽。
entries.en: In Gengshi 1 he became lieutenant general, joined the attack on Wan, and separately brought Xinye, Yuyang, Duyan, Guanjun, and Huyang to surrender.
entries.literal: In the first year of Gengshi, he was promoted to lieutenant general, followed in attacking Wan, separately submitted Xinye, Yuyang, Duyan, Guanjun, Huyang.

entries.zh: 二年，更始封識陰德侯，行大將軍事。
entries.en: In the second year the Gengshi court enfeoffed him as marquis of Yinde with the powers of grand general.
entries.literal: In the second year, Gengshi enfeoffed Shi as marquis of Yinde, acting grand general affairs.

entries.zh: 永平元年，拜長水校尉，與公卿雜定郊祠禮儀，以讖記正《五經》異說。
entries.en: In Yongping 1 he was appointed Colonel of the Chang River and, with the high ministers, jointly settled suburban sacrifice ritual, using prognostic texts to correct variant readings in the Five Classics.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongping he was appointed Colonel of the Chang River and, with the high ministers, jointly settled suburban sacrifice ritual, using prognostic texts to correct variant readings in the Five Classics.

entries.zh: 北海周澤、瑯邪承宮並海內大儒，鯈皆以為師友而致之於朝。
entries.en: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both leading scholars of the realm; Fan Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.
entries.literal: Zhou Ze of Beihai and Cheng Gong of Langya were both great Confucian scholars within the realm; Tiao took both as teacher-friends and brought them to court.

entries.zh: 上言郡國舉孝廉，率取年少能報恩者，耆宿大賢多見廢棄，宜敕郡國簡用良俊。
entries.en: He memorialized that commanderies and kingdoms recommending Filial and Incorrupt candidates favored the young who could repay favors, while elderly worthies were often passed over, and urged that they select truly outstanding men.
entries.literal: He memorialized that when commanderies and kingdoms recommended Filial and Incorrupt candidates, they consistently took the young who could repay favors, while elderly great worthies were mostly cast aside—commanderies and kingdoms should be ordered to select good outstanding men.

entries.zh: 又議刑辟宜須秋月，以順時氣。
entries.en: He also argued that capital punishments should await the autumn month, in accord with seasonal qi.
entries.literal: He also argued that capital punishments should await the autumn month, to accord with seasonal qi.

entries.zh: 顯宗並從之。
entries.en: Emperor Ming accepted both proposals.
entries.literal: Emperor Ming followed both proposals.

entries.zh: 二年，以壽張國益東平王，徙封鯈燕侯。
entries.en: In the second year the state of Shouzhang was added to the Prince of Dongping, and Fan Tiao was transferred to marquis of Yan.
entries.literal: In the second year, the state of Shouzhang was added to the Prince of Dongping, and Tiao was transferred to marquis of Yan.

entries.zh: 其後廣陵王荊有罪，帝以至親悼傷之，詔鯈與羽林監南陽任隗雜理其獄。
entries.en: Later Prince Liu Jing of Guangling committed crimes; grieving as close kin, the emperor ordered Fan Tiao and the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Ren Wei of Nanyang to jointly try the case.
entries.literal: Later Prince Jing of Guangling committed crimes; the emperor, grieving as close kin, ordered Tiao and the Supervisor of the Feathered Forest Ren Wei of Nanyang to jointly try the case.

entries.zh: 事竟，奏請誅荊。
entries.en: When the case was concluded, they memorialized requesting Jing's execution.
entries.literal: When the affair was concluded, they memorialized requesting Jing's execution.

entries.zh: 引見宣明殿，帝怒曰：『諸卿以我弟故，欲誅之，即我子，卿等敢爾邪！』
entries.en: Summoned to the Hall of Illuminating Clarity, the emperor said angrily: 'You wish to execute him because he is my brother—if he were my son, would you dare do the same!'
entries.literal: Summoned to the Hall of Illuminating Clarity, the emperor said angrily: 'You gentlemen wish to execute him because he is my brother—if he were my son, would you dare thus!'

entries.zh: 鯈仰而對曰：『天下高帝天下，非陛下之天下也。
entries.en: Fan Tiao looked up and replied: 'The realm is Emperor Gao's realm, not Your Majesty's realm alone.
entries.literal: Tiao looked up and replied: 'The realm is Gao Di's realm, not Your Majesty's realm alone.

entries.zh: 《春秋》之義。
entries.en: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals:
entries.literal: The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals:

entries.zh: 「君親無將，將而誅焉」。
entries.en: "For lord and parent there must be no rebellious intent—one who rebels shall be executed."
entries.literal: "For lord and parent there must be no rebellious intent—one who rebels shall be executed."

entries.zh: 是以周公誅弟，季友鴆兄，經傳大之。
entries.en: Therefore the Duke of Zhou executed his younger brother and Ji You poisoned his elder brother—the classics and commentaries greatly praise this.
entries.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou executed his younger brother, and Ji You poisoned his elder brother—the classics and commentaries greatly praise this.

entries.zh: 臣等以荊屬託母弟，陛下留聖心，加惻隱，故敢請耳。
entries.en: We thought that because Jing is the empress-dowager's younger brother, Your Majesty would retain sage consideration and show compassion—therefore we dared only to petition.
entries.literal: We, your servants, because Jing is the empress-dowager's younger brother, thought Your Majesty would retain sage consideration and add compassion—therefore we dared only to petition.

entries.zh: 如令陛下子，臣等專誅而已。』
entries.en: Had he been Your Majesty's son, we would have executed him outright.'
entries.literal: Had he been Your Majesty's son, we would have executed him outright.'

entries.zh: 帝嘆息良久。
entries.en: The emperor sighed deeply for a long while.
entries.literal: The emperor sighed deeply for a long while.

entries.zh: 鯈益以此知名。
entries.en: Fan Tiao became even more renowned for this.
entries.literal: Tiao became even more famed for this.

entries.zh: 其後弟鮪為子賞求楚王英女敬鄉公主，鯈聞而止之，曰：『建武時，吾家並受榮寵，一宗五侯。
entries.en: Later his younger brother Wei sought for his son Shang the Princess Jingxiang, daughter of Prince Ying of Chu; Fan Tiao heard of it and stopped him, saying: 'In the Jianwu era our family all received glory and favor—one clan, five marquises.
entries.literal: Later his younger brother Wei sought for his son Shang the Princess Jingxiang, daughter of Prince Ying of Chu; Tiao heard of it and stopped him, saying: 'In the Jianwu era our family all received glory and favor—one clan, five marquises.

entries.zh: 時特進一言，女可以配王，男可以尚主，但以貴寵過盛，即為禍患，故不為也。
entries.en: At that time an eminence grandee needed but one word and daughters could marry princes and sons could marry princesses—but because excessive honor becomes calamity, I did not do so.
entries.literal: At that time an eminence grandee needed but one word and daughters could marry princes and sons could marry princesses—but because excessive honor becomes calamity, I did not do so.

entries.zh: 且爾一子，奈何棄之於楚乎？』
entries.en: Moreover you have but one son—how can you cast him off to Chu?'
entries.literal: Moreover you have but one son—how can you cast him off to Chu?'

entries.zh: 鮪不從。
entries.en: Wei did not listen.
entries.literal: Wei did not listen.

entries.zh: 顯宗即位，拜為執金吾，位特進。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Yin Shi became bearer of the mace with specially advanced rank.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he was appointed bearer of the mace, rank specially advanced.

entries.zh: 永平二年，卒，贈以本官印綬，謚曰貞侯。
entries.en: He died in Yongping 2 with posthumous honors at his former rank and the title Steadfast Marquis.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongping, he died; he was granted his original office's seals and ribbons; posthumous title was steadfast marquis.

entries.zh: 二十三年，卒，時年三十九。
entries.en: In the twenty-third year of Jianwu he died, aged thirty-nine.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year he died, aged thirty-nine.

entries.zh: 興素與從兄嵩不相能，然敬其威重。
entries.en: Yin Xing had long been at odds with his cousin Yin Song, yet he respected Song's authority.
entries.literal: Xing had long been incompatible with his cousin-brother Song, yet respected his commanding dignity.

entries.zh: 興疾病，帝親臨，問以政事以群臣能不。
entries.en: When Yin Xing fell ill, the emperor visited him in person and asked about state affairs and the competence of his ministers.
entries.literal: Xing was ill; the emperor personally visited and asked about government affairs and whether the ministers were capable.

entries.zh: 興頓首曰：『臣愚不足以知之。
entries.en: Yin Xing kowtowed and said: 'I am too foolish to judge this.
entries.literal: Xing knocked his head and said: 'Your servant is foolish and not sufficient to know this.

entries.zh: 然伏見議郎席廣、謁者陰嵩，並經行明深，逾於公卿。』
entries.en: Yet I have observed Consultant Gentleman Xi Guang and Usher Yin Song—both of exemplary conduct who surpass the senior ministers.'
entries.literal: Yet I respectfully see Consultant Gentleman Xi Guang and Usher Yin Song—both in conduct bright and deep, surpassing the public ministers.'

entries.zh: 興沒後，帝思其言，遂擢廣為光祿勛；
entries.en: After Yin Xing's death the emperor heeded his advice and promoted Xi Guang to Director of the Imperial Household;
entries.literal: After Xing died, the emperor reflected on his words and thereupon promoted Guang to Director of the Imperial Household;

entries.zh: 嵩為中郎將，監羽林十餘年，以謹敕見幸。
entries.en: Yin Song became General of the Gentlemen and oversaw the Feathered Forest guard for over ten years, winning favor through diligence and restraint.
entries.literal: Song as General of the Gentlemen, supervised the Feathered Forest for more than ten years, and through diligence and restraint gained favor.

entries.zh: 顯宗即位，拜長樂衛尉，遷執金吾。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Song was appointed Commandant of Changle and later transferred to Bearer of the Mace.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, [Song] was appointed Commandant of Changle and transferred to Bearer of the Mace.

entries.zh: 永平元年詔曰：『故侍中衛尉關內侯興，典領禁兵，從平天下，當以軍功顯受封爵，又諸舅比例，應蒙恩澤，興皆固讓，安乎裏巷。
entries.en: In Yongping 1 an edict proclaimed: 'The late Secretariat Director and Commandant of the Guard, Marquis Within the Passes Yin Xing, commanded the palace guards and helped pacify the realm—by military merit he deserved an open fief, and as imperial in-laws his kin were due proportional honors, yet he steadfastly refused and lived quietly in his lane.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongping an edict said: 'The late Secretariat Director and Commandant of the Guard, Marquis Within the Passes Xing, commanded the palace guards and followed in pacifying the realm—by military merit he should have received open enfeoffment; moreover, as kinsmen of the empress he should have shared proportional grace, yet Xing firmly yielded all and dwelt at ease in lane and alley.

entries.zh: 輔導朕躬，有周昌之直，在家仁孝，有曾、閔之行，不幸早卒，朕甚傷之。
entries.en: He guided me with Zhou Chang's integrity, and at home showed the filial devotion of Zeng and Min. His untimely death grieves Us deeply.
entries.literal: He guided Our person with Zhou Chang's forthrightness; in the home he was kind and filial, with Zeng and Min's conduct—unfortunately he died young, and We deeply mourn him.

entries.zh: 賢者子孫，宜加優異。
entries.en: The descendants of the worthy deserve special favor.
entries.literal: The descendants of the worthy should receive special favor.

entries.zh: 其以汝南之鲖陽封興子慶為鯛陽侯，慶弟博為㶏強侯。』
entries.en: Let his son Qing be enfeoffed as marquis of Diaoyang in Runan, and Qing's younger brother Bo as marquis of Ruqiang.'
entries.literal: Let Xing's son Qing be enfeoffed as marquis of Diaoyang in Runan, and Qing's younger brother Bo as marquis of Ruqiang.'

entries.zh: 博弟員、丹竝為郎，慶推田宅財物悉與員、丹。
entries.en: Bo's younger brothers Yuan and Dan both became palace gentlemen; Qing gave all his land, houses, and property to Yuan and Dan.
entries.literal: Bo's younger brothers Yuan and Dan were both made gentlemen of the palace; Qing gave over all his fields, houses, and goods to Yuan and Dan.

entries.zh: 帝以慶義讓，擢為黃門侍郎。
entries.en: Impressed by Qing's selfless generosity, the emperor promoted him to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
entries.literal: The emperor, because of Qing's righteous yielding, promoted him to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate.

entries.zh: 慶卒，子琴嗣。
entries.en: When Qing died, his son Qin succeeded him.
entries.literal: Qing died; his son Qin succeeded.

entries.zh: 建初五年，興夫人卒，肅宗使五官中郎將持節即墓賜策，追謚興曰翼侯。
entries.en: In Jianchu 5, when Yin Xing's wife died, Emperor Zhang sent the General of the Five Offices with imperial credentials to the tomb to grant an edict posthumously enfeoffing Yin Xing as marquis of Yi.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Jianchu, Xing's lady died; Emperor Zhang sent the General of the Five Offices bearing credentials to the tomb to bestow an edict, posthumously enfeoffing Xing as marquis of Yi.

entries.zh: 琴卒，子萬全嗣。
entries.en: When Qin died, his son Wanquan succeeded.
entries.literal: Qin died; his son Wanquan succeeded.

entries.zh: 萬全卒，子桂嗣。
entries.en: When Wanquan died, his son Gui succeeded.
entries.literal: Wanquan died; his son Gui succeeded.

entries.zh: 興弟就，嗣父封宣恩侯，後改封為新陽侯。
entries.en: Yin Jiu inherited their father's fief as marquis of Xuan'en, later transferred to Xinyang.
entries.literal: Xing's younger brother Jiu succeeded to the father's enfeoffment as marquis of Xuan'en, later transferred enfeoffment to become marquis of Xinyang.

entries.zh: 就善談論，朝臣莫及，然性剛傲，不得眾譽。
entries.en: Yin Jiu was the finest debater at court but was arrogant and unpopular.
entries.literal: Jiu was good at discourse and discussion; court ministers could not match him, yet his nature was rigid and proud; he did not obtain crowd praise.

entries.zh: 顯宗即位，以就為少府，位特進。
entries.en: Emperor Ming named him privy treasurer with specially advanced rank.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, he made Jiu privy treasurer, rank specially advanced.

entries.zh: 就子豐尚酈邑公主。
entries.en: Yin Jiu's son Yin Feng married Princess Liyi.
entries.literal: Jiu's son Feng married the Liyi princess.

entries.zh: 公主嬌妒，豐亦狷急。
entries.en: The princess was jealous and spoiled; Yin Feng was hot-tempered as well.
entries.literal: The princess was pampered and jealous; Feng was also impatient and harsh.

entries.zh: 永平二年，遂殺主，被誅，父母當坐，皆自殺，國除。
entries.en: In Yongping 2 Yin Feng murdered the princess and was put to death. His parents faced collective guilt and took their own lives; the fief was abolished.
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongping, thereupon he killed the mistress, was executed, parents ought to sit for the crime—all killed themselves; the state was abolished.

entries.zh: 帝以舅氏故，不極其刑。
entries.en: Out of regard for the maternal kin, the emperor did not extend punishment to the full extent of the law.
entries.literal: The emperor because of the maternal uncle clan did not carry his punishment to the limit.

entries.zh: 今學者蓋少，遠方尤甚。
entries.en: Today scholars are scarce, and the frontier regions worst of all.
entries.literal: Now scholars are perhaps few; the distant regions are especially severe.

entries.zh: 博士倚席不講，儒者竟論浮麗，忘謇謇之忠，習諓々之辭。
entries.en: Erudites no longer teach; scholars chase flashy rhetoric, abandon blunt loyalty, and trade in slick phrases.
entries.literal: Erudites lean on the mat and do not lecture; Confucians compete in discussing floating splendor, forget outspoken loyalty, practice slanderous phrases.

entries.zh: 文吏則去法律而學詆欺，銳錐刀之鋒，斷刑辟之重，德陋俗薄，以致苛刻。
entries.en: Clerical officials ignore the code and learn petty tricks; they sharpen quibbles over the death penalty—mean virtue, thin custom, and cruel judgments follow.
entries.literal: Document clerks then leave law and statutes and study slander and deceit, sharpen awl-and-knife points, judge the weight of punishments and executions—virtue base, customs thin, thereby bringing harsh severity.

entries.zh: 昔孝文竇後性好黃老，而清靜之化流景、武之間。
entries.en: Empress Dou under Emperor Wen loved Huang-Lao, yet her quiet influence lasted into the reigns of Emperors Jing and Wu.
entries.literal: Formerly Empress Dou of Emperor Wen's nature liked Huang-Lao, yet the transformation of clarity and quiet flowed between Jing and Wu.

entries.zh: 臣愚以為宜下明詔，博求幽隱，發揚巖穴，寵進儒雅，有如孝、宮者，徵詣公車，以侯聖上講習之期。
entries.en: Issue an edict summoning hidden scholars and men of learning like Zhao Xiao and Cheng Gong to the capital to await your lectures.
entries.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks it fitting to issue a clear edict, broadly seek the hidden and concealed, raise up cliff and cave, favor and advance Confucian elegance—such as Xiao and Gong—summon them to the public carriage, to await the sage superior's period of lecturing and practice.

entries.zh: 公卿各舉明經及舊儒子孫，進其爵位，使纘其業。
entries.en: Let every minister nominate classicists and heirs of old scholarly lines, raise their rank, and set them to carry on the tradition.
entries.literal: Dukes and ministers each recommend those clear in the classics and old Confucians' descendants, advance their noble ranks, make them continue their enterprises.

entries.zh: 復召郡國書佐，使讀律令。
entries.en: Recall clerks from the commanderies to study the legal code.
entries.literal: Again summon commandery and kingdom document assistants, make them read statutes and orders.

entries.zh: 如此，則廷頸者日有所見，傾耳者月有所聞。
entries.en: Then those who strain to see and hear will daily and monthly find something worth learning.
entries.literal: Thus, then those craning necks daily have something to see, those tilting ears monthly have something to hear.

entries.zh: 伏願陛下推述先帝進業之道。
entries.en: I beg you to follow the path by which former emperors advanced learning.
entries.literal: Prostrate, I wish Your Majesty would extend and narrate the former emperors' way of advancing enterprise.

entries.zh: 伏見被災之郡，百姓雕殘，恐非賑給所能勝贍，雖有其名，終無其實。
entries.en: The stricken districts are devastated; nominal relief cannot feed them in fact.
entries.literal: Prostrate, I see the stricken commanderies; the hundred surnames are carved and maimed—I fear relief grants cannot suffice to support; though they have the name, in the end they lack the reality.

entries.zh: 可依徵和元年故事，遣使持節慰安。
entries.en: Follow Emperor Wu's Zhenghe precedent: send credentialed envoys to comfort the people.
entries.literal: One can follow the precedent of the first year of Zhenghe, send envoys bearing credentials to comfort and soothe.

entries.zh: 尤困乏者，徙置荊、揚孰郡，既省轉運之費，且令百姓各安其所。
entries.en: Resettle the worst cases in the fertile Jing and Yang commanderies to cut transport costs and let people find stable homes.
entries.literal: Those especially destitute, move and place them in Jing and Yang ripe commanderies—both saving transport costs and ordering the hundred surnames each to settle their place.

entries.zh: 今雖有西屯之役，宜先東州之急。
entries.en: Even with the western campaign, the east's famine must come first.
entries.literal: Now though there is the western garrison campaign, one ought first for the eastern provinces' urgency.

entries.zh: 如遣使者與二千石隨事消息，悉留富人守其舊士，轉尤貧者過所衣食，誠父母之計也。
entries.en: Send envoys with governors to manage resettlement: keep the wealthy on their land, move only the destitute, and supply them on the road—that would be true parental care for the people.
entries.literal: If envoys are sent with two-thousand-shi officials to handle matters as they arise, entirely keep rich men guarding their old lands, transfer the especially poor past what they eat and wear—it is truly a parent's plan.

entries.zh: 願以臣言下公卿平議。
entries.en: Submit these proposals to the ministers for debate.
entries.literal: I wish to take your servant's words and send them down to dukes and ministers for balanced discussion.

entries.zh: 陰識字次伯，南陽新野人也，光烈皇后之前母兄也。
entries.en: Yin Shi, courtesy name Cibo, came from Xinye in Nanyang and was the elder brother of Empress Yin Lihua by the same mother.
entries.literal: Yin Shi, courtesy name Cibo, was a man of Xinye in Nanyang; he was the Empress Guanglie's elder uterine brother by her birth mother.

entries.zh: 其先出自管仲，管仲七世孫修，自齊適楚，為陰大夫，因而氏焉。
entries.en: The line descended from Guan Zhong; seven generations later Xiu left Qi for Chu, became lord Yin, and took Yin as the clan name.
entries.literal: His ancestor came from Guan Zhong; Guan Zhong's seventh-generation descendant Xiu, from Qi went to Chu, became Yin grandee, and from this took the surname.

entries.zh: 秦、漢之際，始家新野。
entries.en: At the fall of Qin they settled in Xinye.
entries.literal: At the juncture of Qin and Han, they first settled household at Xinye.

entries.zh: 陰氏侯者凡四人。
entries.en: Four branches of the Yin clan held marquisates.
entries.literal: Those of the Yin clan who were marquises were in all four persons.

entries.zh: 初，陰氏世奉管仲之祀，謂為『相君』。
entries.en: For generations the Yin family had sacrificed to Guan Zhong as 'Lord Chancellor.'
entries.literal: Earlier, the Yin clan for generations offered sacrifice to Guan Zhong, calling him 'lord minister.'

entries.zh: 宣帝時，陰子方者，至孝有仁恩，臘日晨炊而竈神形見，子方再拜受慶。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan, Yin Zifang was famously filial. On the la festival he lit the kitchen fire at dawn, the stove god appeared, and Zifang bowed twice to receive its blessing.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Xuan, there was Yin Zifang—of utmost filial piety and benevolent grace; on the la sacrifice day he cooked at dawn and the stove god's form appeared; Zifang twice bowed and received blessing.

entries.zh: 家有黃羊，因以祀之。
entries.en: He sacrificed a yellow sheep from his flock to the god.
entries.literal: The household had a yellow sheep; thereupon with it they sacrificed to him.

entries.zh: 自是已後，暴至巨富，田有七百餘頃，輿馬僕隸，比於邦君。
entries.en: After that the family rose overnight to enormous wealth—more than seven hundred qing of land, carriages, horses, and retainers like a prince's household.
entries.literal: From this after, suddenly he reached vast wealth; fields had over seven hundred qing; carriages, horses, servants, and slaves compared to a state lord.

entries.zh: 子方常言『我子孫必將強大』，至識三世而遂繁昌，故後常以臘日祀竈，而薦黃羊焉。
entries.en: Zifang used to say, 'My descendants will grow powerful'—and by Yin Shi's generation, three lines later, the clan had indeed flourished. Hence the custom of sacrificing a yellow sheep to the stove on the la day.
entries.literal: Zifang often said, 'My sons and grandsons will surely grow mighty'; reaching Shi, three generations, and thereupon flourished and prospered; therefore later they always on the la day sacrificed to the stove, and presented the yellow sheep.

entries.zh: 昔楚、宋列國，俱為諸侯，莊王以宋執其使，遂有投袂之師。
entries.en: When Chu and Song were coequal states, King Zhuang of Chu marched the moment Song seized his envoy—sleeve flung, army on the move.
entries.literal: Formerly Chu and Song, arrayed states, were both feudal lords; King Zhuang of Chu because Song seized his envoy, thereupon had the army of casting aside the sleeve.

entries.zh: 魏公子顧朋友之要，觸冒強秦之鋒。
entries.en: Lord Xinling honored a friend's plea and threw himself against Qin's blades.
entries.literal: The lord of Wei remembered a friend's obligation and braved the keen edge of mighty Qin.

entries.zh: 夫楚、魏非有分職匡正之大義也，莊王但為爭強而發忿，公子以一言而立信耳。
entries.en: Neither Chu nor Wei had the solemn mandate of setting the realm right; King Zhuang acted from wounded pride, Xinling from a single pledge kept.
entries.literal: Now Chu and Wei did not have the great duty of divided offices and rectifying wrongs; King Zhuang merely for striving for dominance issued resentment; the lord by one word established trust.

entries.zh: 今彭寵反畔，張豐逆節，以為陛下必棄捐它事，以時滅之，既歷時月，寂寞無音。
entries.en: Peng Chong and Zhang Feng stand in open rebellion; we assumed Your Majesty would drop everything else and crush them promptly—yet months have dragged by in silence.
entries.literal: Now Peng Chong rebels and turns traitor, Zhang Feng violates the norm; I thought Your Majesty would surely set aside other affairs and in due time destroy them; already months have passed, silent without sound.

entries.zh: 從圍城而不救，放逆虜而不討，臣誠惑之。
entries.en: Our cities are besieged with no relief; rebels roam unpunished—I am at a loss to explain it.
entries.literal: Following upon besieged cities yet not rescuing, releasing rebellious captives yet not punishing—your servant truly is perplexed.

entries.zh: 昔高祖聖武，天下既定，猶身自征伐，未嘗寧居。
entries.en: Even Gaozu, sage-warrior that he was, took the field himself once the empire was his—he never knew ease.
entries.literal: Formerly Gaozu was sacredly martial; though the realm was already settled, he still personally campaigned and never dwelt in tranquility.

entries.zh: 陛下雖興大業，海內未集，而獨逸豫，不顧北垂，百姓遑遑，無所系心。
entries.en: Your Majesty has restored the great enterprise while the realm is still unsettled, yet you linger at ease and ignore the northern frontier; the people drift anxious, with nothing to steady them.
entries.literal: Your Majesty though has raised great enterprise, within the seas not yet gathered, yet alone is leisurely and at ease, not attending to the northern border; the hundred surnames are restless, with nothing to tie their hearts.

entries.zh: 三河、冀州，曷足以傳後哉！
entries.en: Will the Central Plain and Ji province alone be legacy enough for posterity?
entries.literal: The Three Rivers and Ji Province—how can they suffice to transmit to posterity!

entries.zh: 今秋稼已熟，復為漁陽所掠。
entries.en: The autumn harvest stands ready—and Yuyang strips it again.
entries.literal: Now autumn crops are already ripe, again they are plundered by Yuyang.

entries.zh: 張豐狂悖，奸黨日增，連年拒守，吏士疲勞，甲胄生蟣虱，弓弩不得施，上下焦心，相望救護，仰希陛下生活之恩。
entries.en: Zhang Feng grows bolder and his faction swells; year after year we endure siege until officers and men stagger under lice-ridden armor and idle crossbows. Every rank waits on tenterhooks for relief and Your Majesty's lifesaving grace.
entries.literal: Zhang Feng is wild and perverse; villainous factions daily increase; year after year they hold out on the defensive; clerks and soldiers are weary and exhausted; armor breeds lice and fleas; bows and crossbows cannot be deployed; high and low burn with anxiety, look to each other for rescue and protection, looking up in hope for Your Majesty's grace of granting life.

entries.zh: 定弟石，襲母公主封獲嘉侯，亦為侍中，稍遷衛尉。
entries.en: His younger brother Feng Shi inherited the Princess of Huojia's marquisate of Huojia, served as palace attendant, and advanced to minister of the guards.
entries.literal: Ding's younger brother Shi, inherited mother's princess fief as marquis of Huojia; also was attendant at the palace gates; gradually transferred to minister of the guards.

entries.zh: 能取悅當世，為安帝所寵。
entries.en: He knew how to please the court and became a favorite of Emperor An.
entries.literal: Able to please his generation; was favored by Emperor An.

entries.zh: 帝嘗幸其府，留飲十許日，賜駁犀具劍、佩刀、紫艾綬、玉玦各一，拜子世為黃門侍郎，世弟二人皆郎中。
entries.en: The emperor once lodged at his mansion for some ten days of feasting and gave him a rhinoceros-horn hilt sword, belt knife, purple grandee's ribbon, and jade ring. He appointed Feng Shi's son Shi as gentleman of the Yellow Gates and named both of Shi's younger brothers court gentlemen.
entries.literal: The emperor once favored his residence, stayed drinking about ten days, granted a dappled-rhino-hilt sword, belt knife, purple mugwort ribbon, and jade ring, one of each; appointed his son Shi as gentleman of the Yellow Gates; two younger brothers of Shi were all consultants (langzhong).

entries.zh: 自永初兵荒，王侯租秩多不充，於是特詔以它縣租稅足石，今如舊限，歲入谷三萬斛，錢四萬。
entries.en: After the Yongchu wars many marquises could not collect their stipends; an edict topped up Feng Shi's income from other counties' taxes—restoring the old quota of thirty thousand hu of grain and forty thousand cash a year.
entries.literal: From Yongchu military famine, marquises' rent and stipends mostly did not suffice; then a special edict used other counties' rent and tax to complete Shi's quota; now like old limit, yearly income grain thirty thousand hu, cash forty thousand.

entries.zh: 遷光祿勛，遂代楊震為太尉。
entries.en: He rose to superintendent of the palace guards and succeeded Yang Zhen as grand commandant.
entries.literal: He was transferred to superintendent of the palace guards, then replaced Yang Zhen as grand commandant.

entries.zh: 及北鄉侯立，遷太傅，與太尉東萊劉喜參錄尚書事。
entries.en: When the Marquis of Beixiang acceded, Feng Shi became grand tutor and, with Grand Commandant Liu Xi of Donglai, shared supervision of the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When the marquis of Beixiang was established, he was transferred to grand tutor, with grand commandant Liu Xi of Donglai jointly recording Masters of Writing affairs.

entries.zh: 順帝既立，石與喜皆以阿黨閻顯、江京等策免，復為衛尉。
entries.en: When Emperor Shun took the throne, Feng Shi and Liu Xi were cashiered for colluding with Yan Xian and Jiang Jing; Feng Shi later returned as minister of the guards.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun was already established, Shi and Xi both because of currying faction with Yan Xian, Jiang Jing and others were removed by edict; again became minister of the guards.

entries.zh: 卒，子代嗣。
entries.en: He died and his son Feng Dai inherited.
entries.literal: He died; his son Dai succeeded.

entries.zh: 代卒，弟承嗣，為步兵校尉。
entries.en: When Feng Dai died, his brother Feng Cheng inherited and served as colonel of infantry.
entries.literal: When Dai died, younger brother Cheng succeeded; became colonel of foot soldiers.

entries.zh: 後去官還鄉裏，太守富宗聞延名，召署功曹。
entries.en: After he resigned and went home, Governor Fu Zong, having heard his reputation, named him merit assessor.
entries.literal: Later he left office and returned to village; Governor Fu Zong heard Yan's name, summoned and appointed him merit assessor.

entries.zh: 宗性奢靡，車服器物，多不中節。
entries.en: Fu Zong lived lavishly: his carriages, dress, and furnishings were far beyond what was proper.
entries.literal: Zong's nature was extravagant; carriages, dress, tools, and objects mostly did not hit the measure.

entries.zh: 延諫曰：『昔晏嬰輔齊，鹿裘不完，季文子相魯，妾不衣帛，以約失之者鮮矣。』
entries.en: Yu Yan urged him: 'Yan Ying served Qi in a patched deer cloak; Ji Wenzi ruled Lu while his concubines wore no silk—few who live plainly ever lose their footing.'
entries.literal: Yan remonstrated saying: 'Formerly Yan Ying aided Qi—his deer-fur cloak was never whole; Ji Wenzi ministered Lu while his concubines wore no silk. Few who err through restraint come to grief.'

entries.zh: 宗不悅，延即辭退。
entries.en: Fu Zong took offense and Yu Yan resigned at once.
entries.literal: Zong was not pleased; Yan immediately resigned and withdrew.

entries.zh: 居有頃，宗果以侈從被誅，臨當伏刑，攬涕而嘆曰：『恨不用功曹虞延之諫！』
entries.en: Soon afterward Fu Zong was executed for extravagance. On the block he wept and cried, 'If only I had listened to Yu Yan!'
entries.literal: After dwelling a short while, Zong indeed because of extravagant following was executed; when about to suffer punishment, grasping tears sighed saying: 'I regret not using merit assessor Yu Yan's remonstrance!'

entries.zh: 光武聞而奇之。
entries.en: Guangwu heard the story and marked Yu Yan as remarkable.
entries.literal: Guangwu heard and deemed him extraordinary.

entries.zh: 二十年東巡，路過小黃，高帝母昭靈後園陵在焉，時延為部督郵，詔呼引見，問園陵之事。
entries.en: On his eastern tour in year 20 the emperor passed Xiaohuang, where Gaozu's mother the Empress Dowager Zhaoling lay buried. Yu Yan was serving as inspector; the emperor summoned him to ask about the tomb precinct.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year eastern tour, passing Xiaohuang—Gaodi's mother Empress Zhaoling's garden tomb was there; at the time Yan was departmental postal inspector; edict called him led to audience, asked garden tomb matters.

entries.zh: 延進止從容，占拜可觀，其陵樹株蘗，皆諳其數，俎豆犧牲，頗曉其禮。
entries.en: Yu Yan moved and answered with poise; he knew every tree and shoot on the burial mound and the ritual of vessels and offerings.
entries.literal: Yan's advancing and stopping was leisurely; divining and bowing were observable; its mound trees stumps and sprouts, all knew their numbers; stands and vessels sacrificial victims, rather understood their ritual.

entries.zh: 帝善之，敕延從駕到魯。
entries.en: Pleased, the emperor had Yu Yan ride with him to Lu.
entries.literal: The emperor praised him; ordered Yan to follow carriage to Lu.

entries.zh: 還經封丘城門，門下小，不容羽蓋，帝怒，使撻侍禦史，延因下見引咎，以為罪在督郵。
entries.en: On the return through Fengqiu the gate was too low for the imperial umbrella-carriage. The emperor flogged his carriage attendant; Yu Yan stepped forward and took the blame on himself as local postal inspector.
entries.literal: Returning passed Fengqiu city gate; the gate below was small, did not accommodate feather canopy; emperor angry, caused flogging attendant imperial clerk; Yan thereupon descended audience and drew blame on himself, held that guilt lay with the postal inspector.

entries.zh: 言辭激揚，有感帝意，乃制誥曰：『以陳留督郵虞延故，貰禦史罪。』
entries.en: His honest plea moved the throne, which proclaimed: 'For Chenliu postal inspector Yu Yan's sake, spare the attendant.'
entries.literal: Words and phrases were stirring; had moving emperor's intent; then issued edict saying: 'Because of Chenliu postal inspector Yu Yan, pardon imperial clerk's crime.'

entries.zh: 延從送車駕西盡郡界，賜錢及劍帶佩刀還郡，於是聲名遂振。
entries.en: Yu Yan escorted the train to the commandery border, received cash, sword belt, and dagger, and returned—his name rang out thereafter.
entries.literal: Yan followed sending carriage west to the end of commandery border; granted cash and sword belt waist knife returning to commandery; from this reputation then shook.

entries.zh: 三年，征代趙憙為太尉；
entries.en: In year 3 he was summoned to succeed Zhao Xi as grand commandant;
entries.literal: In the third year, summoned to replace Zhao Xi as grand commandant;

entries.zh: 八年，代範遷為司徒，歷位二府，十餘年無異政績。
entries.en: In year 8 he succeeded Fan Qian as minister of education; for a decade at the summit of government he left no striking mark.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, replaced Fan Qian as minister of education; passing through two offices, more than ten years without exceptional administrative traces.

entries.zh: 會楚王英謀反，陰氏欲中傷之，使人私之楚謀告延，延以英藩戚至親，不然其言，又欲辟幽州從事公孫弘，以弘交通楚王而止，並不奏聞。
entries.en: When Liu Ying, king of Chu, plotted revolt, the Yins tried to entrap Yu Yan by secretly passing him word of the plot. Yan would not believe it—Ying was too close in blood to the throne—and he dropped a summons for Youzhou staffer Gongsun Hong when he learned Hong was in contact with the prince. He reported nothing to the court.
entries.literal: It happened the king of Chu, Ying, plotted rebellion; the Yin clan wished to injure him, sent someone secretly to use Chu's plot to inform Yan; Yan because Ying was close kin of the imperial house, did not credit the report; also wished to summon Youzhou staffer Gongsun Hong, but because Hong was in contact with the king of Chu desisted; together he did not memorialize.

entries.zh: 及英事發覺，詔書切讓，延遂自殺。
entries.en: When Ying's plot surfaced, a blistering edict blamed Yu Yan, who took his own life.
entries.literal: When Ying's affair was discovered and revealed, edict script sternly blamed; Yan thereupon killed himself.

entries.zh: 家至清貧，子孫不免寒餧。
entries.en: His household was bitterly poor; even his descendants went cold and hungry.
entries.literal: House extremely clear and poor; children and grandchildren did not avoid cold and hunger.

entries.zh: 鄭弘字巨君，會稽山陰人也。
entries.en: Zheng Hong, styled Jujun, came from Shanyin in Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: Zheng Hong, courtesy name Junju, was a man of Shanyin in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 從祖吉，宣帝時為西域都護。
entries.en: His grandfather's cousin Zheng Ji had been protector of the Western Regions under Emperor Xuan.
entries.literal: His senior cousin Ji in Emperor Xuan's time was protector of the Western Regions.

entries.zh: 弘少為鄉嗇夫，太守第五倫行春，見而深奇之，召署督郵，舉孝廉。
entries.en: As a young village bailiff he impressed Governor Diwu Lun on a spring inspection tour; Lun named him postal inspector and nominated him filial and incorrupt.
entries.literal: Hong in youth was village bailiff; Governor Diwu Lun on spring circuit saw him and deeply deemed him extraordinary, summoned and appointed postal inspector, raised filial and incorrupt.

entries.zh: 弘師同郡河東太守焦貺。
entries.en: Zheng Hong studied under his fellow townsman Jiao Kuang, governor of Hedong.
entries.literal: Hong took as teacher Jiao Kuang, governor of Hedong of the same commandery.

entries.zh: 楚王英謀反發覺，以疏引貺，貺被收捕，疾病於道亡沒，妻子閉系詔獄，掠考連年。
entries.en: When Liu Ying of Chu's plot surfaced, a memorial named Jiao Kuang; Kuang was arrested but died on the road while fleeing illness, leaving wife and children shackled in the imperial jail for years of torture.
entries.literal: King of Chu Ying's rebellion plot was discovered; by memorial Kuang was implicated; Kuang was seized and captured; ill on the road he died while fleeing; wife and children shut bound in edict prison; flog-examined successive years.

entries.zh: 諸生故人懼相連及，皆改變名姓，以逃其禍，弘獨髡頭負鈇锧，詣闕上章，為貺訟罪。
entries.en: Students and friends hid under aliases to escape guilt; Zheng Hong alone shaved his head, carried an executioner's block to the palace, and filed a memorial defending Jiao Kuang.
entries.literal: Students and old friends feared mutual linkage and involvement; all changed names and surnames to escape its calamity; Hong alone shaved head, bore axe and chopping-block, went to palace gate and submitted a memorial, for Kuang pleaded his innocence.

entries.zh: 顯宗覺悟，即赦其家屬，弘躬送貺喪及妻子還鄉裏，由是顯名。
entries.en: Emperor Ming took his meaning, freed the family, and Hong personally escorted Kuang's body and kin home—a deed that made his name known.
entries.literal: Emperor Xianzong awakened and understood; immediately pardoned his family members; Hong personally escorted Kuang's corpse and wife and children returning to village; from this name became manifest.

entries.zh: 論曰：孔子稱『可與立，未可與權』。
entries.en: The historian remarks: Confucius said, 'You can stand firm with some men—not weigh shifting circumstances with every one.'
entries.literal: The appraisal says: Confucius called 'May stand with him, not yet may weigh circumstances with him.'

entries.zh: 權也者，反常者也。
entries.en: Expediency means departing from the usual rule.
entries.literal: Weighing circumstances is departing from the norm.

entries.zh: 將從反常之事，必資非常之會，使夫舉無違妄，誌行名全。
entries.en: Acting outside the norm calls for extraordinary timing—only then can the deed avoid folly and leave ambition, deed, and reputation intact.
entries.literal: About to follow abnormal affairs, must rely on extraordinary conjunctions, causing those undertakings without violation or recklessness, aspiration and conduct name preserved whole.

entries.zh: 周章身非負圖之托，德乏萬夫之望，主無絕天之釁，
entries.en: Zhou Zhang bore no Duke-of-Zhou mandate; he lacked popular esteem; the emperor gave Heaven no cause for revolt,
entries.literal: Zhou Zhang bore no regent's charge like the Duke of Zhou; virtue fell short of the multitude's hopes; the ruler showed no crime against Heaven's mandate,

entries.zh: 地有既安之埶，而創慮於難圖，希功於理絕，不已悖乎！
entries.en: the realm already rested secure—yet he plotted the impossible and hoped for success where cause was dead—was that not folly?
entries.literal: earth had already settled posture, yet he devised schemes on hard-to-plan matters, hoped achievement where principle was cut off—is it not already perverse!

entries.zh: 如令君器易以下議，即鬥筲必能叨天業，狂夫豎臣亦自奮矣。
entries.en: If high office bends to petty counsel, every small talent will grasp at the Mandate and cranks will rush forward.
entries.literal: If high office yields easily to counsel from below, then petty measure could seize heaven's enterprise; madmen and petty ministers too would exert themselves.

entries.zh: 孟軻有言曰：『有伊尹之心則可，無伊尹之心則篡矣。』
entries.en: Mencius said, 'With Yi Yin's intent it is permissible; without it, it is usurpation.'
entries.literal: Meng Ke had words saying: 'Having Yi Yin's heart then acceptable; lacking Yi Yin's heart then usurpation.'

entries.zh: 於戲，方來之人戒之哉！
entries.en: Alas—let those who come after take warning!
entries.literal: Alas, those who come after—guard against it!

entries.zh: 朱浮字叔元，沛國蕭人也。
entries.en: Zhu Fu, styled Shuyuan, came from Xiao in the state of Pei.
entries.literal: Zhu Fu, courtesy name Shuyuan, was a man of Xiao in the Pei kingdom.

entries.zh: 初從光武為大司馬主簿，遷偏將軍，從破邯鄲。
entries.en: He first served Emperor Guangwu as secretary to the Grand Marshal, rose to general of the flank, and took part in the reduction of Handan.
entries.literal: At first he followed Guangwu as clerk of the Grand Marshal, was promoted to general of the flank, and followed him in capturing Handan.

entries.zh: 光武遣吳漢誅更始幽州牧苗曾，乃拜浮為大將軍幽州牧，守薊城，遂討定北邊。
entries.en: Guangwu dispatched Wu Han to put to death Miao Zeng, whom the Gengshi Emperor had placed over Youzhou; Zhu Fu was then named Grand General and governor of Youzhou, held Ji, and brought the northern border under control.
entries.literal: Guangwu sent Wu Han to execute Gengshi's governor of Youzhou Miao Zeng, then appointed Fu as Grand General and governor of Youzhou, garrisoned Ji city, and thus pacified the northern frontier.

entries.zh: 建武二年，封舞陽侯，食三縣。
entries.en: In Jianwu 2 he was invested as Marquis of Wuyang with an income drawn from three counties.
entries.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he was enfeoffed as marquis of Wuyang with revenue from three counties.

entries.zh: 統性剛毅而好法律。
entries.en: Liang Tong was stern by temperament and devoted to the law.
entries.literal: Tong's nature was firm and resolute and he loved statutes.

entries.zh: 初仕州郡。
entries.en: He began his career in provincial and commandery office.
entries.literal: At first he served in province and commandery.

entries.zh: 更始二年，召補中郎將，使安集涼州，拜酒泉太守。
entries.en: In Gengshi 2 he was named general of the gentlemen of the palace, dispatched to settle Liangzhou, and made governor of Jiuquan.
entries.literal: In the second year of Gengshi he was summoned and supplemented as general of the gentlemen of the palace, sent to pacify and gather Liangzhou, appointed governor of Jiuquan.

entries.zh: 會更始敗，赤眉入長安，統與竇融及諸郡守起兵保境，謀共立帥。
entries.en: When Gengshi fell and the Red Eyebrows took Chang'an, Liang Tong joined Dou Rong and the frontier governors in mobilizing to defend their territory and choose a leader.
entries.literal: When Gengshi failed, the Red Eyebrows entered Chang'an; Tong with Dou Rong and various commandery governors raised troops to guard the borders, plotted together to establish a leader.

entries.zh: 初以位次，咸共推統，統固辭曰：『昔陳嬰不受王者，以有老母也。
entries.en: At first they pressed Liang Tong by seniority, but he refused: 'Chen Ying once declined a throne because his mother was old.'
entries.literal: At first by order of rank all jointly pushed Tong; Tong firmly declined saying: 'Formerly Chen Ying did not accept kingship because he had an aged mother.

entries.zh: 今統內有尊親，又德薄能寡，誠不足以當之。』
entries.en: I still have elders at home and mean talent—I am not fit for such a burden.'
entries.literal: Now Tong within has honored kin; moreover virtue thin ability few—truly not sufficient to undertake it.'

entries.zh: 遂共推融為河西大將軍，更以統為武威大守。
entries.en: They chose Dou Rong as Grand General of Hexi and named Liang Tong governor of Wuwei.
entries.literal: Then jointly they pushed Rong as Grand General west of the river; changed and made Tong governor of Wuwei.

entries.zh: 為政嚴猛，威行鄰郡。
entries.en: He ruled with severity; neighboring commanderies felt his authority.
entries.literal: In governing he was stern and fierce; awe extended neighboring commanderies.

entries.zh: 臣竊見元、哀二帝輕殊死之刑以一百二十三事，手殺人者減死一等，自是以後，著為常準，故人輕犯法，吏易殺人。
entries.en: I note that under Yuandi and Aidi capital crimes were relaxed in 123 provisions—manslaughter dropped one degree below death—and that precedent invited petty crime and quick executions by officials.
entries.literal: Your servant has privately seen Emperors Yuan and Ai lighten capital punishment in one hundred twenty-three matters; those who killed with their own hand had death reduced one grade; from this afterward recorded as constant norm; therefore people lightly violated law; clerks easily killed men.

entries.zh: 臣聞立君之道，仁義為主，仁者愛人，義者政理，愛人以除殘為務，政理以去亂為心。
entries.en: The ruler's way rests on humanity and justice: humanity cherishes the people and crusades against cruelty; justice orders the realm and aims at ending chaos.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that establishing a lord's way takes humanity and rightness as lord; the humane love men; the righteous regulate governance; loving men takes removing cruelty as task; regulating governance takes removing chaos as heart.

entries.zh: 刑罰在衷，無取於勸，是以五帝有流、殛、放、殺之誅，三王有大辟、刻肌之法。
entries.en: Penalties must strike the balance—no empty preaching—and so the Five Thearchs knew exile and execution, while the Three Kings relied on capital punishment and branding.
entries.literal: Punishments lie in the middle—nothing taken from exhortation—therefore the Five Thearchs had exile, spear-execution, banishment, and killing punishments; the Three Kings had great execution and cutting flesh laws.

entries.zh: 故孔子稱『仁者必有勇』，又曰『理財正辭，禁民為非曰義』。
entries.en: Confucius said the humane are brave, and that ordering livelihoods, correcting speech, and barring wrongdoing is righteousness.
entries.literal: Therefore Confucius praised 'The humane must have courage,' and also said 'ordering wealth and correcting words, forbidding the people wrongdoing is called righteousness.'

entries.zh: 高帝受命誅暴，平蕩天下，約令定律，誠得其宜。
entries.en: Gaozu swept away tyranny and framed statutes that fit the age.
entries.literal: Gaodi received mandate executed cruelty, leveled and swept the realm, covenant ordered fixing statutes—truly obtained its fitness.

entries.zh: 文帝寬惠柔克，遭世康平，惟除省肉刑、相坐之法，它皆率由，無革舊章。
entries.en: Emperor Wen ruled gently in tranquil times, trimming only the mutilating punishments and clan liability—otherwise he followed Han precedent untouched.
entries.literal: Wendi was generous and mild subduing; encountered age peace and calm; only eliminated reduced flesh punishment and linked-guilt laws; other all followed along; none altered old regulations.

entries.zh: 武帝值中國隆盛，財力有餘，征伐遠方，軍役數興，豪桀犯禁，奸吏弄法，故重首匿之科，著知從之律，以破朋黨，以懲隱匿。
entries.en: Emperor Wu flourished with surplus revenue and constant campaigns; bold men broke the law and corrupt clerks twisted it—so he tightened harboring statutes and accessory guilt to smash factions and punish concealment.
entries.literal: Wudi encountered Central States lofty flourishing; wealth power had surplus; campaigned attacked distant regions; military service repeatedly arose; heroes violated prohibitions; villainous clerks played with law; therefore heavy chief concealing categories, established knowing-follow statutes, to break faction parties, to punish concealment.

entries.zh: 宣帝聰明正直，總禦海內，臣下奉憲，無所失墜，因循先典，天下稱理。
entries.en: Emperor Xuan was astute and upright: officials obeyed the code, precedent held, and the realm was deemed well governed.
entries.literal: Xuandi clever and upright, overall commanded within seas; ministers below upheld statutes, none missed fall; followed along former canons; realm called ordered.

entries.zh: 至哀、平繼體，而即位日淺，聽斷尚寡，丞相王嘉輕為穿鑿，虧除先帝舊約成律，數年之間，百有餘事，或不便於理，或不厭民心。
entries.en: Under Aidi and Pingdi—short reigns and thin court experience—Chancellor Wang Jia rashly chipped away at statutes Gaodi had settled; in a few years over a hundred changes either offended reason or the people.
entries.literal: Reaching Ai and Ping succeeding the body, yet enthronement days shallow, hearing judgments still few; Chancellor Wang Jia lightly made boring-through; harmed removed former emperors' old compacts completed statutes; within several years, more than hundred matters; some not convenient to pattern; some not satisfying people's hearts.

entries.zh: 謹表其尤害於體者傅奏於左。
entries.en: I append the worst of these—those that damage good rule—to the left.
entries.literal: Respectfully listing those especially harmful to the body attach memorial at left.

entries.zh: 伏惟陛下包元履德，權時撥亂，功逾文、武，德侔高皇，誠不宜因循季末衰微之軌。
entries.en: Your Majesty embraces primal virtue and has acted as the times required to restore order; your achievements surpass those of Kings Wen and Wu, and your virtue matches that of the Exalted Emperor. You truly should not follow the declining precedents of the dynasty's final years.
entries.literal: Prostrate I consider Your Majesty embraces origin treads virtue, weighs times removes chaos; merit surpasses Wen and Wu; virtue matches Gaodi—truly ought not follow late-age declining faint tracks.

entries.zh: 回神明察，考量得失，宣詔有司，詳擇其善，定不易之典，施無窮之法，天下幸甚。
entries.en: May Your Majesty weigh right and wrong, instruct the offices to choose the best, fix enduring statutes, and lay down lasting law—the empire would rejoice.
entries.literal: Turn divine brightness examine; examine measure gain loss; proclaim edict responsible offices; detailed choose their good; fix unchanging canons; apply inexhaustible laws—realm greatly fortunate.

entries.zh: 統復上言曰：『有司以臣今所言，不可施行。
entries.en: Liang Tong wrote again: 'The ministries say my proposals cannot be carried out.'
entries.literal: Tong again submitted speech saying: 'Responsible offices hold that what your servant now speaks cannot be implemented.

entries.zh: 尋臣之所奏，非曰嚴刑。
entries.en: Consider my point: I am not merely crying for cruelty.
entries.literal: Trace what your servant has memorialized—it is not called severe punishments.

entries.zh: 竊謂高帝以後，至乎孝宣，其所施行，多合經傳，宜比方今事，驗之往古，聿遵前典，事無難改，不勝至願。
entries.en: From Gaozu through Xuandi the code matched the classics; compare present cases to antiquity, restore sound precedent—such reform is no great hurdle and would fulfill my deepest hope.
entries.literal: Privately I hold from Gaodi onward, reaching to Xiaoxuan, what they implemented mostly matched classics and commentaries; it is fitting to compare square today's affairs, verify them in ancient past, then follow former canons—affairs are not hard to change—unsurpassed utmost wish.

entries.zh: 願得召見，若對尚書近臣，口陳其要。』
entries.en: Let me face the throne—or at least the Masters of Writing—and state the essentials in person.'
entries.literal: I wish to obtain summons and audience; if facing Masters of Writing close ministers, orally state its essentials.'

entries.zh: 帝令尚書問狀，統對曰：
entries.en: The emperor had the Masters of Writing question him, and Liang Tong answered:
entries.literal: The emperor ordered the Masters of Writing to ask the situation; Tong replied saying:

entries.zh: 自高祖之興，至於孝宣，君明臣忠，謨謀深博，猶因循舊章，不輕改革，海內稱理，斷獄益少。
entries.en: From Gaozu to Xuandi, wise rulers and loyal ministers kept established law and seldom altered it—the realm was deemed orderly and lawsuits dwindled.
entries.literal: From Gaozu's rise to Xiaoxuan, lord bright ministers loyal, plans deep and broad; still followed old regulations, did not lightly reform; within seas called ordered; judged cases increasingly few.

entries.zh: 至初元、建平，所減刑罰百有餘條，而盜賊浸多，歲以萬數。
entries.en: Under Chuyuan and Jianping over a hundred mitigations piled up—yet bandits multiplied by tens of thousands each year.
entries.literal: Reaching Chuyuan and Jianping, reduced punishments more than hundred articles; yet robbers and bandits gradually many, yearly by tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 間者三輔從橫，群輩並起，至燔燒茂陵，火見未央。
entries.en: Lately the capital region erupted—bands ran riot until Maoling burned and flames lit Weiyang Palace.
entries.literal: Recently the Three Adjuncts ran rampant; crowds arose together; reaching burning Maoling; fire appeared Weiyang.

entries.zh: 其後隴西、北地、西河之賊，越州度郡，萬里交結，攻取庫兵，劫略吏人，詔書討捕，連年不獲。
entries.en: Then Longxi, Beidi, and Xihe rebels ranged across provinces, seized arsenals, looted officials and commoners, and defied years of imperial hunts.
entries.literal: Afterward Longxi, Beidi, Xihe bandits crossed provinces passed commanderies, ten thousand li linked; attacked took armory weapons; robbed plundered clerks and people; edict script punish capture; successive years not caught.

entries.zh: 是時以天下無難，百姓安平，而狂狡之勢，猶至於此，皆刑罰不衷，愚人易犯之所致也。
entries.en: Though the age seemed calm, villainy still exploded—that stems from penalties missing the mean and inviting petty crime.
entries.literal: At this time though the realm had no hardship, hundred surnames peaceful and calm; yet wild and crafty momentum still reached thus—all punishments not centered, foolish people easily offending caused.

entries.zh: 永元九年，竇太后崩，松子扈遣從兄禪奏記三府，以為漢家舊典，崇貴母氏，而梁貴人親育聖躬，不蒙尊號，求得申議。
entries.en: In Yongyuan 9 Dowager Dou died; Liang Hu sent his cousin Liang Shan to memorialize the Three Offices that Han tradition honors birth mothers, yet the Liang honored ladies who bore the emperor had received no posthumous dignity—he asked redress.
entries.literal: In ninth year of Yongyuan, Empress Dowager Dou collapsed; Song's son Hu sent cousin Shan memorial-record Three Offices, holding Han family's old canons exalted honored mother's clan, yet Liang honored lady personally nurtured sagely body, did not receive honored title; sought obtain extending deliberation.

entries.zh: 太尉張酺引禪訊問事理，會後召見，因白禪奏記之狀。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Zhang Pu questioned Liang Shan on the merits; shortly afterward Shan was summoned to audience, and Zhang then explained Shan's memorial.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Zhang Pu questioned Liang Shan on the merits of the case; shortly afterward Shan was summoned to audience; Zhang then explained Shan's memorial.

entries.zh: 帝感慟良久，曰：『於君意若何？』
entries.en: The emperor was moved and asked Zhang Pu, 'What do you think?'
entries.literal: Emperor moved sorrow long while, said: 'In your lord's intent how?'

entries.zh: 酺對曰：『《春秋》之義，母以子貴。
entries.en: Zhang Pu answered, "The Spring and Autumn teaches that the mother rises with the son."'
entries.literal: Pu replied saying: 'Spring and Autumn's meaning—mother by son honored.

entries.zh: 漢興以來，母氏莫不降顯，臣愚以為宜上尊號，追慰聖靈，存錄諸舅，以明親親。』
entries.en: Since Han began every birth mother's clan has been honored—grant posthumous titles, comfort their spirits, and ennoble the uncles to show loving kinship.'
entries.literal: Since Han's rise, every mother's clan has been elevated to honor—your servant foolishly holds it fitting to ascend honored titles, pursue comforting the sagely spirits, preserve and record the maternal uncles, to clarify loving kin.'

entries.zh: 帝悲泣曰：『非君孰為朕思之！』
entries.en: The emperor wept, 'Who but you would speak for me!'
entries.literal: Emperor wept saying: 'If not you lord who for Us thinks it!'

entries.zh: 會貴人姊南陽樊調妻嫕上書自訟曰：妾同產女弟貴人，前充後宮，蒙先帝厚恩，得見寵幸。
entries.en: The honored ladies' elder sister—Fan Diao's wife, née Yi—petitioned in her own defense: "My own sister, an honored lady, once served in the inner palace and won the late emperor's favor."
entries.literal: The honored ladies' elder sister—wife of Fan Diao of Nanyang, née Yi—submitted a memorial pleading her own case: "Your servant's full sister by the same mother was an honored lady who once served in the inner palace, receiving the late emperor's great favor and winning his affection."

entries.zh: 皇天授命，誕生聖明。
entries.en: Heaven granted the mandate and brought forth a sage sovereign.
entries.literal: Heaven granted the mandate and brought forth a sage sovereign.

entries.zh: 而爲竇憲兄弟所見譖訴，使妾父竦冤死牢獄，骸骨不掩。
entries.en: Yet the Dou Xian brothers slandered us, and my father Liang Song died wrongfully in prison with his bones unburied.
entries.literal: Yet the Dou Xian brothers slandered us, causing your servant's father Song to die wrongfully in prison with his bones unburied.

entries.zh: 老母孤弟，遠徙萬里。
entries.en: My aged mother and younger brother were exiled far away.
entries.literal: My aged mother and lone younger brother were exiled ten thousand li.

entries.zh: 獨妾遺脫，逸伏草野，常恐沒命，無由自達。
entries.en: I alone escaped and hid in the wilds, ever fearing death with no way to reach Your Majesty.
entries.literal: Only your servant escaped, hiding in the wilds, ever fearing death with no means to reach you.

entries.zh: 今遭值陛下神聖之運，親統萬機，群物得所。
entries.en: Now under Your Majesty's sacred rule, all things find their place.
entries.literal: Now I meet Your Majesty's sacred rule, personally governing all affairs so that all things find their place.

entries.zh: 憲兄弟奸惡，既伏辜誅，海內曠然，各獲其宜。
entries.en: The Xian brothers have been punished, and the realm is at peace.
entries.literal: The Xian brothers' wickedness has met punishment; within the seas all is open and each obtains what is fitting.

entries.zh: 妾得蘇息，拭目更視，乃敢昧死自陳所天。
entries.en: I can breathe again and dare risk death to plead my case.
entries.literal: Your servant can breathe again, wipe her eyes and look anew, and so dares risk death to state her case to her lord.

entries.zh: 妾聞太宗即位，薄氏蒙榮，宣帝繼統，史族復興。
entries.en: When Emperor Wen took the throne the Bo clan was honored; when Emperor Xuan succeeded the Shi clan revived.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when Emperor Taizong took the throne the Bo clan was honored, and when Emperor Xuan succeeded the Shi clan revived.

entries.zh: 妾門雖有薄、史之親，獨無外戚餘恩，誠自悼傷。
entries.en: Though our house has Bo and Shi kin, we alone lack the grace shown to maternal kin—I grieve for this.
entries.literal: Though our house has kinship with the Bo and Shi lines, it alone lacks the lingering grace given to maternal kin—truly I grieve.

entries.zh: 妾父既冤，不可復生，母氏年殊七十，乃弟棠等，遠在絕域，不知死生。
entries.en: My wronged father cannot live again; my mother is nearly seventy; my brothers Tang and the rest are far in the borderlands, and I do not know whether they live.
entries.literal: Your servant's father, once wronged, cannot live again; my mother is nearly seventy; my younger brothers Tang and the rest are far in the borderlands, their life or death unknown.

entries.zh: 願乞收竦朽骨。
entries.en: I beg leave to recover Liang Song's remains.
entries.literal: I beg permission to recover Song's wasted bones.

entries.zh: 使母、弟得歸本郡，則施過天地，存歿幸賴。
entries.en: Let my mother and brothers return home—then Your Majesty's grace would surpass heaven and earth, and the living and dead alike would be blessed.
entries.literal: Let mother and brothers return to their native commandery—then your grace would surpass heaven and earth, and living and dead would be blessed.

entries.zh: 於是追尊恭懷皇后。
entries.en: Empress Gonghuai was posthumously honored.
entries.literal: Thereupon posthumously honored Empress Gonghuai.

entries.zh: 其冬，制詔三公、大鴻臚曰：『夫孝莫大於尊尊親親，其義一也。
entries.en: That winter an edict to the Three Dukes and grand herald read: 'Filial duty chiefly means honoring elders and cherishing kin—the principle is one.'
entries.literal: That winter, regulated edict Three Offices, grand herald saying: 'Now filial piety none greater than honoring the honored and cherishing kin—its meaning one.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：「父兮生我，母兮鞠我，撫我畜我，長我育我，顧我復我，出入腹我。
entries.en: The Songs say: "Father begot me, mother nursed me, reared and fed me, watched me come and go, sheltered my going out and in.
entries.literal: Book of Songs says: "Father oh bore me, mother oh nurtured me, cherish me rear me, grow me raise me, turn to me return me, go out enter shelter me.

entries.zh: 欲報之德，昊天罔極。」
entries.en: How can I repay such kindness? Heaven is boundless."
entries.literal: Desiring repay its virtue—vast heaven without limit.

entries.zh: 朕不敢興事，覽於前世，太宗、中宗，實有舊典，追命外祖，以篤親親。
entries.en: I dare not lightly undertake new rites; reviewing former ages, Taizong and Zhongzong truly had old canons of posthumously charging the maternal grandfather to deepen kinship.
entries.literal: I dare not lightly undertake new rites; reviewing past reigns, sovereigns set precedent in honoring a mother's parents to strengthen family bonds.

entries.zh: 其追封謚皇太后父竦為褒親湣侯，比靈文、順成、恩成侯。
entries.en: Liang Song the younger was posthumously invested as Marquis Aiqin Min, in line with earlier honors to empresses' fathers.
entries.literal: Let posthumous rank and title be granted to the father of the Empress Dowager, Liang Song the younger, as Marquis Aiqin Min—rank comparable to the marquises Lingwen, Shuncheng, and Encheng.

entries.zh: 魂而有靈，嘉斯寵榮，好爵顯服，以慰母心。』
entries.en: May his spirit welcome this honor and splendid robes to ease her sorrow."
entries.literal: If his ghost yet knows, may he rejoice in this glory—fine rank and splendid robes—to comfort his mother's heart."

entries.zh: 遣中謁者與嫕及扈，備禮西迎竦喪，詣京師改殯，賜東園畫館、玉匣、衣衾，建塋於恭懷皇后陵傍。
entries.en: Ushers accompanied Yi and Hu west to fetch Liang Song's remains for reburial at court with imperial mortuary gifts beside Empress Gonghuai's mausoleum.
entries.literal: He dispatched palace ushers with Yi and Hu to greet Liang Song's coffin from the west with full rites, bring it to the capital for reburial, and granted an eastern-garden painted inner coffin, jade cases, and quilts; a mound was raised beside Empress Gonghuai's tomb.

entries.zh: 帝親臨送葬，百官畢會。
entries.en: The emperor escorted the funeral; officials thronged the rites.
entries.literal: The emperor personally attended the burial; the full bureaucracy assembled.

entries.zh: 及帝崩，沖帝始在繈褓，太后臨朝，詔冀與太傅趙峻、太尉李固參錄尚書事。
entries.en: Regency placed Ji with Zhao Jun and Li Gu over the Masters of Writing.
entries.literal: When emperor died Emperor Chong was infant; empress dowager ruled—ordered Ji with tutors Zhao Jun and Li Gu supervise Masters of Writing.

entries.zh: 冀雖辭不肯當，而侈暴滋甚。
entries.en: Ji feigned refusal while growing worse.
entries.literal: Though Ji declined office his arrogance grew.

entries.zh: 冀心疑超等，乃使中黃門張惲入省宿，以防其變。
entries.en: Ji posted Zhang Yun inside the palace as a precaution.
entries.literal: Ji suspected Chao and the others; therefore sent palace attendant Zhang Yun into the palace quarters overnight to guard against a coup.

entries.zh: 具瑗敕吏收惲，以輒從外入，欲圖不軌。
entries.en: Ju Yuan arrested Zhang Yun on a forged charge of intrusion.
entries.literal: Ju Yuan ordered clerks seize Yun—charging that he had entered from outside without authority intending treason.

entries.zh: 帝因是御前殿，召諸尚書入，發其事，使尚書令尹勛持節勒丞郎以下皆操兵守省閣，斂諸符節送省中。
entries.en: Emperor Huan seized the palace offices, armed the clerks, and collected imperial tallies.
entries.literal: The emperor therefore ascended the front hall, summoned the Masters of Writing, exposed the affair, ordered Yin Xun with staff to compel assistants downward—all bearing arms guarding palace gates—and gathered tally credentials to the palace.

entries.zh: 使黃門令具瑗將左右廄騶、虎賁、羽林、都候斂戟士，合千餘人，與司隸校尉張彪共圍冀第。
entries.en: Over a thousand guards encircled Liang Ji's mansion under Zhang Biao.
entries.literal: He ordered Huangmen director Ju Yuan to lead stable grooms, tiger runners, feather forest guards, and capital halberdiers—over a thousand men—with metropolitan commander Zhang Biao to surround Ji's residence.

entries.zh: 使光祿勛袁盱持節收冀大將軍印綬，徙封比景都鄉侯。
entries.en: Yuan Xu stripped Liang Ji of command and demoted him to a village marquis at Bijing.
entries.literal: He ordered superintendent Yuan Xu with staff to take Ji's grand general seal and ribbon and transfer his fief to village marquis of Bijing.

entries.zh: 冀及妻壽即日皆自殺。
entries.en: Liang Ji and Sun Shou killed themselves the same day.
entries.literal: Ji and wife Shou that same day both committed suicide.

entries.zh: 悉收子河南尹胤、叔父屯騎校尉讓，及親從衛尉淑、越騎校尉忠、長水校尉戟等，諸梁及孫氏中外宗親送詔獄，無長少皆棄市。
entries.en: The purge swept Liang and Sun kin—none spared the scaffold.
entries.literal: All seized—son Yin governor of Henan, uncle colonel Rang, kin Su, Zhong, Ji the halberdier—every Liang and Sun inside and outside kin sent to edict prison—all executed in market square young and old alike.

entries.zh: 不疑、蒙先卒。
entries.en: Liang Buyi and Liang Meng were already dead.
entries.literal: Buyi and Meng had died earlier.

entries.zh: 其它所連及公卿、列校、尉刺史、二千石死者數十人，故吏賓客免黜者三百餘人，朝廷為空，惟尹勛、袁盱及廷尉邯鄲義在焉。
entries.en: Scores of officials fell; only Yin Xun, Yuan Xu, and Handan Yi remained at their posts.
entries.literal: Others implicated—dozens of ministers, colonels, prefects, two-thousand-shi officials dead; three hundred former clients dismissed—the court stood empty save Yin Xun, Yuan Xu, and commandant Handan Yi.

entries.zh: 是時事卒從中發，使者交馳，公卿失其度，官府市里鼎沸，數日乃定，百姓莫不稱慶。
entries.en: Luoyang churned for days until calm returned—the people celebrated.
entries.literal: The coup erupted suddenly—messengers galloped—officials lost composure—capital markets boiled—days passed before calm—commoners everywhere rejoiced.

entries.zh: 梁統字仲寧，安定烏氏人，晉大夫梁益耳，即其先也。
entries.en: Liang Tong, styled Zhongning, came from Wushi in Anding; his line descended from the Jin minister Liang Yier.
entries.literal: Liang Tong, courtesy name Zhongning, was a man of Wushi in Anding; the Jin noble Liang Yier was his ancestor.

entries.zh: 統高祖父子都，自河東遷居北地，子都子橋，以資千萬徙茂陵，至哀、平之末，歸安定。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Liang Zidu had relocated from Hedong to Beidi; Zidu's son Liang Qiao took a fortune of ten million to settle at Maoling, then the family returned to Anding late in the Ai and Ping era.
entries.literal: Tong's great-grandfather Zidu moved from Hedong to reside in Beidi; Zidu's son Qiao, with assets of ten million cash, moved to Maoling; reaching the end of the Ai and Ping reigns, they returned to Anding.

entries.zh: 張純字伯仁，京兆杜陵人也。
entries.en: Zhang Chun, style Boren, came from Duling in the Jingzhao commandery area.
entries.literal: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Boren, was a native of Duling in the capital region.

entries.zh: 高祖父安世，宣帝時為大司馬衛將軍，封富平侯。
entries.en: Four generations back, his ancestor Zhang Anshi had served under Emperor Xuan as grand marshal and general of the guard and had been made marquis of Fuping.
entries.literal: His great-great-grandfather Anshi, in the time of Emperor Xuan, was grand marshal and general of the guard, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Fuping.

entries.zh: 父放，為成帝侍中。
entries.en: His father Zhang Fang had been attendant-in-chief under Emperor Cheng.
entries.literal: His father Fang was attendant-in-chief under Emperor Cheng.

entries.zh: 純少襲爵士，哀、平間為侍中，王莽時至列卿。
entries.en: Zhang Chun succeeded to the title while still young; during the Ai and Ping reigns he became attendant-in-chief, and under Wang Mang he advanced to senior ministerial rank.
entries.literal: Chun in his youth inherited the noble rank; between the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping he was attendant-in-chief, and under Wang Mang he rose to the rank of one of the nine ministers.

entries.zh: 遭值篡偽，多亡爵士，純以敦謹守約，保全前封。
entries.en: Many houses lost their fiefs when the usurpation came, but Zhang Chun kept his earlier grant by staying scrupulous and reliable.
entries.literal: When usurpation occurred, many lost their noble titles, but Chun, through earnest care and faithful observance of his obligations, preserved his earlier enfeoffment.

entries.zh: 純在朝歷世，明習故事。
entries.en: Zhang Chun had served through several reigns and knew administrative precedent inside out.
entries.literal: Chun had been in court for successive reigns and was thoroughly familiar with precedent.

entries.zh: 建武初，舊章多闕，每有疑議，輒以訪純，自郊廟婚冠喪紀禮儀義，多所正定。
entries.en: Early in Jianwu the statutes were full of gaps; on every doubtful point the court turned to Zhang Chun, and he fixed much of the ritual for suburban sacrifices, temples, weddings, cappings, and mourning.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, old regulations were largely missing; whenever there was a doubtful point, they would consult Chun; from suburban and temple rites through capping, marriage, and mourning observances, much was settled and corrected on his advice.

entries.zh: 帝甚重之，以純兼虎賁中郎將，數被引見，一日或至數四。
entries.en: The emperor thought highly of him, gave him the concurrent post of leader of the household gentlemen of the tiger guard, and called him in so often that he might be seen four times in one day.
entries.literal: The emperor greatly valued him, and appointed Chun concurrently as leader of the household gentlemen of the tiger guard; he was summoned repeatedly, sometimes four times in a single day.

entries.zh: 純以宗廟未定，昭穆失序，十九年，乃與太仆朱浮共奏言：『陛下興於匹庶，蕩滌天下，誅鋤暴亂，興繼祖宗。
entries.en: In the nineteenth year of Jianwu, because the imperial shrines were unsettled and the zhao-mu sequence wrong, he and grand coachman Zhu Fu jointly argued: "You rose from outside the court, purged the empire, crushed rebellion, and restored the ancestral house.
entries.literal: Chun, because the ancestral temples were not yet fixed and the zhao-mu order was confused, in the nineteenth year together with the grand coachman Zhu Fu jointly submitted a memorial saying: 'Your Majesty rose from commoner status, swept away the realm, punished violence and disorder, and restored the line of the ancestors.

entries.zh: 竊以經義所紀，人事眾心，雖實同創革，而名為中興，宜奉先帝，恭承祭祀者也。
entries.en: The canon and common expectation alike treat this as a restoration in name though like a new foundation; the former emperors must be honored and their cult maintained.
entries.literal: According to what the classics record and what human affairs and popular sentiment require, although in substance it is the same as founding anew, in name it is a restoration; one ought to honor the former emperors and respectfully undertake the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 元帝以來，宗廟奉祠高皇帝為受命祖，孝文皇帝為太宗，孝武皇帝為世宗，皆如舊制。
entries.en: Since Emperor Yuan, the ancestral temples had offered sacrifices to Emperor Gao as the ancestor who received the mandate, to Emperor Wen as Taizong, and to Emperor Wu as Shizong, all according to the old system.
entries.literal: From Emperor Yuan onward, in the ancestral temple the high emperor was honored as the ancestor who received the mandate, Emperor Xiaowen as the great ancestor, and Emperor Wu as the exalted ancestor, all according to the old system.

entries.zh: 又立親廟四世，推南頓君以上盡於舂陵節侯。
entries.en: Four generations of "close" shrines had also been set, running from Lord Nandun back to Marquis Jieling of Chunling.
entries.literal: In addition four generations of personal temples were established, tracing from Lord Nandun upward to Marquis Jieling of Chunling.

entries.zh: 禮，為人後者則為之子，既事大宗，則降其私親。
entries.en: Ritual says an adopted heir is a son of the line he enters; serving the great trunk means demoting one's own blood relatives.
entries.literal: By ritual, one who becomes heir to another line becomes that line's son; once the great descent is served, one's private kin is demoted in rank.

entries.zh: 今禘祫高廟，陳序昭穆，而舂陵四世，君臣並列，以卑廁尊，不合禮意，設不遭王莽，而國嗣無寄，推求宗室，以陛下繼統者，安得復顧私親，違禮制乎？
entries.en: At the great di and xia rites in the high temple the generations are ordered, yet the four Chunling generations appear as lord and subject together—base beside exalted—which breaks ritual. Had Wang Mang never seized power and the throne lacked an heir, and a clansman had been chosen for you to succeed, would private kin still override the code?
entries.literal: Now at the di and xia sacrifices in the high temple the zhao-mu order is arrayed, yet the four Chunling generations stand lord and minister side by side, placing the low beside the high, which does not accord with ritual meaning; supposing Wang Mang had not appeared and the imperial succession had nowhere to turn, and one sought among the imperial house for one to continue the line whom Your Majesty succeeded—how could one again heed private kin and violate the ritual system?

entries.zh: 昔高帝以自受命，不由太上，宣帝以孫後祖，不敢私親，故為父立廟，獨群臣侍祠。
entries.en: Gaozu took the mandate in his own person, not from a "supreme emperor"; Emperor Xuan, exalting an ancestor as a grandson, still shrank from privileging kin and built a father-temple served only by ministers.
entries.literal: Formerly the high emperor, because he received the mandate himself, did not derive it from the supreme emperor; Emperor Xuan, as a grandson who honored an ancestor, did not dare favor private kin, and therefore established a temple for his father with only the ministers attending the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 臣愚謂宜除今親廟，以則二帝舊典，願下有司博采其議。』
entries.en: I would abolish the current "close" shrines to match those two precedents and ask that the ministries debate this broadly."
entries.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the present personal temples ought to be abolished to follow the precedent of the two emperors; I beg that the matter be referred to the officials for wide discussion.'

entries.zh: 詔下公卿，大司徒戴涉、大司空竇融議：『宜以宣、元、成、哀、平五帝四世代今親廟，宣、元皇帝尊為祖、父，可親奉祠，成帝以下，有司行事，別為南頓君立皇考廟。
entries.en: The edict went to the high ministers. Dai She and Dou Rong proposed: "Use the five rulers from Xuan through Ping, with four generations, in place of today's private shrines; Xuan and Yuan as grandfather and father may receive worship from you in person; from Cheng on let officials officiate; add a separate "imperial father" temple for Lord Nandun.
entries.literal: An edict was issued to the dukes and ministers; grand minister over the masses Dai She and grand minister of works Dou Rong deliberated: 'The five emperors Xuan, Yuan, Cheng, Ai, and Ping, in four generations, should replace the present personal temples; Emperors Xuan and Yuan should be honored as grandfather and father and may receive sacrifice in person; from Emperor Cheng downward the officials should perform the rites; separately establish a temple to the imperial father for Lord Nandun.

entries.zh: 其祭上至舂陵節侯，群臣奉祠，以明尊尊之敬，親親之恩。』
entries.en: Worship should reach up to Marquis Jieling of Chunling with ministers conducting it, to mark both reverence for rank and affection for kin."
entries.literal: Let sacrifice extend upward to Marquis Jieling of Chunling, with the ministers performing the cult, to clarify the respect due to exalted rank and the kindness due to close kin.'

entries.zh: 帝從之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted their recommendation.
entries.literal: The emperor followed this.

entries.zh: 是時宗廟未備，自元帝以上，祭於洛陽高廟，成帝以下，祠於長安高廟，其南頓四世，隨所在而祭焉。
entries.en: The national shrines were still incomplete: from Yuan upward rites were at Luoyang's high temple, from Cheng downward at Chang'an's high temple, while the four Nandun generations were honored wherever their tablets happened to be.
entries.literal: At that time the ancestral shrines were not complete; from Emperor Yuan upward sacrifice was at the high temple in Luoyang; from Emperor Cheng downward it was at the high temple in Chang'an; the four Nandun generations were sacrificed to wherever they were located.

entries.zh: 二十六年，詔純曰：『禘、祫之祭，不行已久矣。
entries.en: In Jianwu 26 an edict told him: "The di and xia sacrifices have long been neglected.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year an edict to Chun said: 'The di and xia sacrifices have not been carried out for a long time.

entries.zh: 「三年不為禮，禮必壞；
entries.en: "If ritual is neglected for three years, it will decay;
entries.literal: "If for three years one does not practice ritual, ritual is sure to decay;

entries.zh: 三年不為樂，樂必崩」。
entries.en: if music is neglected for three years, it will fall apart."
entries.literal: if for three years one does not practice music, music is sure to collapse."

entries.zh: 宜據經典，詳為其制。』
entries.en: Ground the schedule in the classics and spell it out in detail."
entries.literal: You should rely on the classics and set out the system in detail.'

entries.zh: 純奏曰：『《禮》，三年一祫，五年一禘。
entries.en: Zhang Chun replied: "The Rites prescribe a xia every three years and a di every five.
entries.literal: Chun submitted a memorial saying: 'According to the Rites, once every three years there is a xia, once every five years a di.

entries.zh: 《春秋傳》曰：「大祫者何？
entries.en: The Zuo asks what the great xia is:
entries.literal: The Zuo commentary asks: "What is the great xia?

entries.zh: 合祭也。」
entries.en: a combined offering to all ancestors."
entries.literal: It is a joint sacrifice.'

entries.zh: 毀廟及未毀廟之主皆登，合食乎太祖，五年而再殷。
entries.en: Tablets from demolished and standing shrines alike ascend to feast with the first ancestor; the grand assembly recurs every five years.
entries.literal: The destroyed-temple and not-yet-destroyed-temple lords all ascend and share food with the grand ancestor; once every five years there is a second great assembly.

entries.zh: 漢舊制三年一祫，毀廟主合良高廟，存廟主未嘗合祭。
entries.en: Under Han practice a triennial xia joined the deposed-line tablets at Gaozu's temple, whereas lines still in their own shrines had not been merged in one rite.
entries.literal: Han's old system was a xia every three years: destroyed-temple lords were brought together at Gaozu's temple, while lords of standing temples had never been jointly sacrificed.

entries.zh: 元始五年，諸王公列侯廟會，始為禘祭。
entries.en: In Yuanshi 5, when the nobles and shrines assembled, the di rite was first performed.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanshi reign, when the kings, dukes, marquises, and temples assembled, the di sacrifice was first instituted.

entries.zh: 又前十八年親幸長安，亦行此禮。
entries.en: Eighteen years earlier you had gone to Chang'an in person and observed the same ceremony.
entries.literal: Moreover eighteen years before Your Majesty personally visited Chang'an and also performed this rite.

entries.zh: 禮說三年一閏，天氣小備；
entries.en: Canonists compare the three-year cycle to one intercalation—heaven's breath partly restored;
entries.literal: Ritual theory says that in three years there is one intercalary month, when minor completeness of heaven's qi is achieved;

entries.zh: 五年再閏，天氣大備。
entries.en: the five-year span to two intercalations—full restoration of the seasonal order.
entries.literal: in five years there are two intercalary months, when great completeness of heaven's qi is achieved.

entries.zh: 故三年一祫，五年一禘。
entries.en: Hence the triennial xia and the quinquennial di.
entries.literal: Therefore once every three years there is a xia, once every five years a di.

entries.zh: 禘之為言諦，諦定昭穆尊卑之義也。
entries.en: Di means "to sort": it fixes who is zhao, who is mu, who ranks above whom.
entries.literal: The word di means "examine"; it settles the meaning of zhao-mu and exalted versus humble.

entries.zh: 禘祭以夏四月，夏者陽氣在上，陰氣在下，故正尊卑之義也。
entries.en: The di falls in summer's fourth month, yang aloft and yin below, the right season to order high and low.
entries.literal: The di is held in the fourth month of summer, when yang qi is above and yin qi below, and therefore rectifies the meaning of exalted and humble.

entries.zh: 祫祭以冬十月，冬者五谷成孰，物備禮成，故合聚飲食也。
entries.en: The xia comes in winter's tenth month, when grain is in, goods gathered, and the rites complete—time for the great common meal.
entries.literal: The xia is held in the tenth month of winter, when the five grains are ripe, things are ready and the rites complete, and therefore gathers all for a communal feast.

entries.zh: 斯典之廢，於茲八年，謂可如禮施行，以時定議。』
entries.en: That norm has lapsed eight years; it should be restored on schedule and the calendar fixed."
