entries.literal: This canon has been in abeyance for eight years now; I say it may be practiced according to ritual and a decision fixed in due season.'

entries.zh: 定從之，自是禘、祫遂定。
entries.en: The court agreed, and from then on di and xia were on the books.
entries.literal: The decision followed this, and thereafter di and xia were fixed.

entries.zh: 時，南單於及烏桓來降，邊境無事，百姓新去兵革，歲仍有年，家給人足。
entries.en: The southern Shanyu and Wuhuan had surrendered, the frontier was calm, the realm had just put down weapons, harvests ran in succession, and families were well fed.
entries.literal: At that time the southern Shanyu and the Wuhuan had submitted; the border was quiet; the people had newly been delivered from arms; successive years brought harvests; every household had enough.

entries.zh: 純以聖王之建辟雍，所以崇尊禮義，既富而教者也。
entries.en: Zhang Chun argued that the sage-kings built the ritual enclosure (biyong) to magnify li and yi and to instruct a people already prosperous.
entries.literal: Chun held that when the sage kings established the ringed ritual hall (biyong), it was to exalt ritual and righteousness and to teach those already enriched.

entries.zh: 乃案七經讖、明堂圖、河間《古辟雍記》、孝武太山明堂制度，及平帝時議，欲具奏之。
entries.en: He collated the seven-classics weft-texts, a Bright Hall diagram, the Hejian "Ancient Bright Hall" record, Emperor Wu's Tai-shan Bright Hall plan, and Ping-era debates, preparing a full memorial.
entries.literal: He therefore collated the prognostications on the seven classics, the Bright Hall chart, the ancient Bright Hall record from Hejian, Emperor Wu's Bright Hall regulations on Mount Tai, and the discussions from Emperor Ping's time, intending to submit them all in a memorial.

entries.zh: 未及上，會博士桓榮上言宜立辟雍、明堂，章下三公、太常，而純議同榮，帝乃許之。
entries.en: Before he could present it, Erudite Huan Rong urged building Bright Hall and the ritual hall; the memorial went to the three dukes and the grand master of ceremonies, Zhang Chun concurred with Huan Rong, and the emperor approved.
entries.literal: Before he could submit it, the erudite Huan Rong submitted a statement that the ritual enclosure (biyong) and the Bright Hall ought to be established; the document was sent down to the three dukes and the grand master of ceremonies, and since Chun's opinion agreed with Rong's, the emperor approved.

entries.zh: 三十年，純奏上宜封禪，曰：『自古受命而帝，治世之隆，必有封禪，以告成功焉。
entries.en: In the thirtieth year Chun submitted that feng and shan ought to be performed, saying: "Since antiquity, one who received the mandate and became emperor, at the height of a well-ordered age, invariably performed feng and shan to announce success.
entries.literal: In the thirtieth year Chun submitted that feng and shan ought to be performed, saying: 'From antiquity, one who received the mandate and became emperor, at the height of a well-ordered age, invariably performed feng and shan to announce success.

entries.zh: 《樂動聲儀》曰：「以《雅》治人，《風》成於《頌》。」
entries.en: The Yue dong sheng yi says: The Ya orders the people; the Feng and Song crown the ode."
entries.literal: The Yue dong sheng yi says: "With the Ya one governs men; with the Feng the Sheng is completed in the Song.'"

entries.zh: 有周之盛，成、康之間，郊配封禪，皆可見也。
entries.en: Zhou's glory under Cheng and Kang shows suburban pairing and feng-shan alike.
entries.literal: At the height of Zhou, between Kings Cheng and Kang, suburban pairing and feng and shan are all visible.

entries.zh: 書曰：「歲二月，東巡狩，至於岱宗，祡」，則封禪之義也。
entries.en: The Documents say: "In the second month of the year, he toured east to the hunting inspection, arriving at Daizong and performing the chai offering"—this is the meaning of feng and shan.
entries.literal: The Documents say: "In the second month of the year, he toured east to the hunting inspection, arriving at Daizong and performing the chai offering"—this is the meaning of feng and shan.

entries.zh: 臣伏見陛下受中興之命，平海內之亂，修復祖宗，撫存萬姓，天下曠然，咸蒙更生，恩德雲行，惠澤雨施，黎元安寧，夷狄慕義。
entries.en: I have watched you take up the restoration mandate, end civil war, repair the ancestral enterprise, and nurture the people: the land lies open, all feel reborn, grace spreads like clouds, bounty falls like rain, commoners rest easy, and foreigners incline to duty.
entries.literal: Your servant has observed that Your Majesty received the mandate of restoration, pacified rebellion within the seas, repaired the work of the ancestors, and cherished the myriad households; the realm is open and clear, all have received new life; favor moves like clouds, kindness falls like rain; the black-haired people are at peace and the barbarians admire righteousness.

entries.zh: 《詩》云：『受天之祜，四方來賀。」
entries.en: The Odes say: Heaven's blessing draws tribute from every quarter.
entries.literal: The Odes say: 'Receiving heaven's blessing, the four quarters come with congratulations.'

entries.zh: 今攝提之歲，倉龍甲寅，德在東宮。
entries.en: This is the Sheti year, jia-yin of the azure dragon, with virtue in the eastern quarter.
entries.literal: Now in the year-star of Sheti, the azure dragon jia-yin year, virtue lies in the eastern palace.

entries.zh: 宜及嘉時，遵唐帝之典，繼孝武之業，以二月東巡狩，封於岱宗，明中興，勒功勛，復祖統，報天神，禪梁父，祀地祇，傳祚子孫，萬世之基也。』
entries.en: You should use this propitious season, follow Yao's model and Emperor Wu's example, tour east in the second month, feng Mount Tai to proclaim the restoration, record achievements, realign the cult with the founders, thank heaven above, shan at Liangfu, honor earth below, and lay a foundation for endless generations."
entries.literal: It is fitting to seize this auspicious season, follow the canon of Emperor Tang, continue the enterprise of Emperor Wu, in the second month tour east for the hunting inspection, perform feng at Daizong to manifest the restoration, inscribe merit, restore the ancestral alignment, repay heaven above, perform shan at Liangfu, sacrifice to earth below, and transmit the foundation to posterity for ten thousand generations.'

entries.zh: 中元元年，帝乃東巡岱宗，以純視禦史大夫從，並上元封舊儀及刻石文。
entries.en: In the first year of Zhongyuan, the emperor then made an eastern tour to Daizong, Mount Tai. Zhang Chun accompanied him as acting Imperial Counselor and submitted the old Yuanfeng rites and the stele inscription text.
entries.literal: In the first year of the Zhongyuan era the emperor then toured east to Daizong, with Chun acting as imperial counsellor in attendance, and together presented the old Yuanfeng protocol and the inscribed stone texts.

entries.zh: 三月，薨，謚曰節候。
entries.en: He died in the third month and was posthumously titled marquis Jie.
entries.literal: In the third month he died; his posthumous title was marquis Jie.

entries.zh: 奮在位清白，無他異績。
entries.en: Zhang Fen's tenure was clean but otherwise unremarkable.
entries.literal: Fen while in office was incorrupt and had no other remarkable achievements.

entries.zh: 九年，以病罷。
entries.en: In the ninth year he stepped down on grounds of illness.
entries.literal: In the ninth year he resigned because of illness.

entries.zh: 在家上疏曰：『聖人所美，政道至要，本在禮樂。
entries.en: From retirement he wrote: "The sages prized above all the essentials of good rule—ritual and music.
entries.literal: At home he submitted a memorial saying: 'What the sages praise and what is most essential in governing the way fundamentally lies in ritual and music.

entries.zh: 《五經》同歸，而禮樂之用尤急。
entries.en: The Five Classics converge on one aim, yet ritual and music matter most urgently.
entries.literal: The Five Classics return to one purpose, yet the use of ritual and music is especially pressing.

entries.zh: 孔子曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮；
entries.en: Confucius said: "To secure superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual;
entries.literal: Confucius said: "To secure superiors and govern the people, nothing is better than ritual;

entries.zh: 移風易俗，莫善於樂。」
entries.en: nothing changes manners like music."
entries.literal: to change customs and transform the people, nothing is better than music.'

entries.zh: 又曰：「揖讓而化天下者，禮樂之謂也。」
entries.en: He also said: "He who with yielding courtesy transforms the world speaks of ritual and music.'
entries.literal: He also said: "He who with yielding courtesy transforms the world speaks of ritual and music.'

entries.zh: 先王之道，禮樂可謂盛矣。
entries.en: The way of the ancient kings shows how splendid ritual and music can be.
entries.literal: The way of the former kings—ritual and music may be called splendid.

entries.zh: 孔子謂子夏曰：「禮以修外，樂以制內，丘已矣夫！」
entries.en: Confucius said to Zi Xia: "Ritual adorns the outer, music regulates the inner—I am finished!'
entries.literal: Confucius said to Zi Xia: "Ritual adorns the outer, music regulates the inner—I am finished!'

entries.zh: 又曰：「禮樂不興，則刑罰不中；
entries.en: He also said: "If ritual and music do not flourish, punishments will not hit the mark;
entries.literal: He also said: "If ritual and music do not flourish, punishments will not hit the mark;

entries.zh: 刑罰不中，則民無所厝其手足。」
entries.en: when penalties go awry, the people do not know where to set hand or foot."
entries.literal: if punishments do not hit the mark, the people have nowhere to put hand or foot.'

entries.zh: 臣以為漢當制作禮樂，是以先帝聖德，數下詔書，湣傷崩缺，而眾儒不達，議多駁異。
entries.en: I believe Han should promulgate ritual and music; past sage emperors sent edict after edict lamenting the gaps, but the scholars quarreled and contradicted one another.
entries.literal: Your servant thinks that Han ought to produce ritual and music; for this reason former emperors with sagely virtue repeatedly issued edicts, grieving at gaps and losses, yet the many scholars did not understand and their opinions were mostly contradictory.

entries.zh: 臣累世臺輔，而大典未定，私竊惟憂，不忘寢食。
entries.en: My house has served at the summit for generations, yet the great codes remain unsettled—I cannot sleep or eat for thinking of it.
entries.literal: Your servant's family for generations has stood at the highest councils, yet the great canons are not fixed; privately he worries and cannot forget it waking or sleeping.

entries.zh: 臣犬馬齒盡，誠冀先死見禮樂之定。』
entries.en: I am old as a spent horse and only hope to see ritual and music settled before I die."
entries.literal: Your servant's dog-and-horse teeth are at an end; he sincerely hopes before death to see ritual and music fixed.'

entries.zh: 十三年，更召拜太常。
entries.en: In the thirteenth year he was recalled and made grand master of ceremonies.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year he was again summoned and appointed grand master of ceremonies.

entries.zh: 復上疏曰：『漢當改作禮樂，圖書著明。
entries.en: He wrote again: "Han must revise and institute ritual and music—the charts and texts say so plainly.
entries.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: 'Han ought to reform and produce ritual and music; the charts and documents make this clear.

entries.zh: 王者化定制禮，功成作樂。
entries.en: When a king's civilizing work is set he prescribes ritual; when his achievement is full he composes music.
entries.literal: When a king's transformation is fixed he orders ritual, when his merit is complete he makes music.

entries.zh: 謹條禮樂異議三事，願下有司，以時考定。
entries.en: I list three disputed points on ritual and music and ask the ministries to settle them soon.
entries.literal: Respectfully I list three points of dispute on ritual and music; I beg that they be sent to the officials for timely determination.

entries.zh: 昔者孝武皇帝、光武皇帝封禪告成，而禮樂不定，事不相副。
entries.en: Emperors Wu and Guangwu had already reported success on Tai, yet ritual and music stayed unsettled—deed and word did not match.
entries.literal: Formerly Emperor Xiaowu and Emperor Guangwu performed feng and shan to announce completion, yet ritual and music were not fixed—the deeds did not match the words.

entries.zh: 先帝已詔曹褒，今陛下但奉而成之，猶周公斟酌文武之道，非自為制，誠無所疑。
entries.en: The late emperor commissioned Cao Bao; you need only enact his work, as the Duke of Zhou adjusted Wen and Wu without inventing law—there is no real doubt here.
entries.literal: The late emperor already ordered Cao Bao; now Your Majesty need only carry it out, like the Duke of Zhou's weighing of the ways of Wen and Wu—not making law on one's own—and truly there is nothing to doubt.

entries.zh: 久執謙謙，令大漢之業不以時成，非所以章顯祖宗功德，建太平之基，為後世法。』
entries.en: Endless modesty that delays Han's great work ill serves the ancestors' glory, the peace of the realm, or an example to posterity."
entries.literal: To hold long to excessive modesty and not let the great enterprise of Han be completed in its season is not the way to display the merit of the ancestors, establish the foundation of great peace, or be a model for later ages.'

entries.zh: 帝雖善之，猶未施行。
entries.en: The emperor praised the plea but did not act on it.
entries.literal: The emperor though he approved it still did not put it into practice.

entries.zh: 其冬，復以病罷。
entries.en: That winter he again retired ill.
entries.literal: That winter he again resigned because of illness.

entries.zh: 明年，卒於家。
entries.en: The next year he died at home.
entries.literal: The next year he died at home.

entries.zh: 褒少篤誌，有大度，結發傳充業，博雅疏通，尤好禮事。
entries.en: Cao Bao was serious-minded from boyhood, generous in spirit, took up the family calling at adulthood, was learned and clear-thinking, and cared above all for ritual.
entries.literal: Bao from youth was steadfast in purpose, had breadth of mind, inherited the family enterprise upon capping, was erudite, broad, and perspicacious, and especially loved matters of ritual.

entries.zh: 常感朝廷制度未備，慕叔孫通為漢禮儀，晝夜研精，沈吟專思，寢則懷抱筆劄，行則誦習文書，當其念至，忘所之適。
entries.en: He felt the dynasty's ceremonial code was still half-built and modeled himself on Shusun Tong; he pored over texts day and night, slept with brush and tablets in his belt, muttered classics on the road, and when an idea struck he would lose track of his path.
entries.literal: He constantly felt that court institutions were incomplete and admired Shusun Tong for having made Han ritual; day and night he studied intently, pondering in concentration; in bed he kept brush and slips in his arms, on the road he recited documents, and when a thought came he forgot where he was going.

entries.zh: 章和元年正月，乃召褒詣嘉德門，令小黃門持班固所上叔孫通《漢儀》十二篇，敕褒曰：『此制散略，多不合經，今宜依禮條正，使可族行。
entries.en: In Zhanghe 1, first month, he called Cao Bao to the Gate of Virtuous Blessing, had a junior eunuch hand him the twelve-fascicle Han ceremonies of Shusun Tong that Ban Gu had submitted, and ordered: "This draft is loose and often uncanonical—revise it by the classics so it can be enforced everywhere.
entries.literal: In the first month of the first year of the Zhanghe era he therefore summoned Bao to the Gate of Virtuous Blessing, had a minor yellow gate hold the twelve chapters of Shusun Tong's Han yi that Ban Gu had presented, and instructed Bao: 'This system is scattered and sketchy, much of it does not match the classics; now you should correct it according to ritual so it may be put into practice for all.

entries.zh: 於南宮、東觀盡心集作。』
entries.en: Compile it with full care at the Southern Palace and the Eastern View."
entries.literal: At the Southern Palace and the Eastern View devote your mind to compiling it.'

entries.zh: 褒既受命，及次序禮事，依準舊典，雜以《五經》讖記之文，撰次天子至於庶人冠婚吉兇終始制度，以為百五十篇，寫以二尺四寸簡。
entries.en: Once commissioned he sequenced the rites from old precedents and Five-Classic weft-books, covering the Son of Heaven down to commoners—capping, weddings, lucky and unlucky rites from birth to death—in one hundred fifty chapters on two-foot-four slips.
entries.literal: Bao, having received the mandate, thereupon ordered the ritual matters, relying on old canons and blending in the texts of the prognostications on the Five Classics, and arranged the institutions from capping and marriage through auspicious and inauspicious matters for the Son of Heaven down to the common people, making one hundred fifty chapters, written on slips two feet four inches long.

entries.zh: 其年十二月奏上。
entries.en: That December he presented the work.
entries.literal: In the twelfth month of that year he presented it.

entries.zh: 帝以眾論難一，故但納之，不復令有司平奏。
entries.en: Opinions were too divided for the throne to impose one view, so the emperor filed the work away without ordering a full ministerial review.
entries.literal: Because the multitude of opinions could not be unified, the emperor therefore only accepted it and did not again order the officials to debate and memorialize.

entries.zh: 會帝崩，和帝即位，褒乃為作章句，帝遂以《新禮》二篇冠。
entries.en: When the emperor died and Emperor He succeeded, Cao Bao wrote glosses; the emperor then used two chapters of the New Rites for the capping ceremony.
entries.literal: When the emperor died and Emperor He ascended, Bao then composed commentaries on it; the emperor thereupon used two chapters of the Xin li for the capping.

entries.zh: 擢褒監羽林左騎。
entries.en: He was raised to superintendent of the left wing of the feathered forest guard.
entries.literal: Bao was promoted to supervise the left wing of the feathered forest.

entries.zh: 永元四年，遷射聲校尉。
entries.en: In Yongyuan 4 he became colonel of the shout-sheng corps.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of the Yongyuan era he was promoted to colonel of the shout-sheng corps.

entries.zh: 後太尉張酺、尚書張敏等奏褒擅制《漢禮》，破亂聖術，宜加刑誅。
entries.en: Later Zhang Fu, Zhang Min, and others charged him with arrogating the Han ritual code and corrupting the sages' teaching—they demanded his death.
entries.literal: Later the grand commandant Zhang Fu, minister Zhang Min, and others memorialized that Bao had presumptuously compiled Han li, had disrupted the sages' art, and ought to suffer execution.

entries.zh: 帝雖寢其奏，而《漢禮》遂不行。
entries.en: The emperor tabled the indictment, but Cao Bao's Han li never went into force.
entries.literal: Although the emperor shelved their memorial, Han li was never implemented.

entries.zh: 初舉孝廉，再遷圉令，以禮理人，以德化俗。
entries.en: Recommended as filial and honest, he rose twice to magistrate of Yu, ruling through ritual and reshaping manners with virtue.
entries.literal: At first he was recommended as filial and incorrupt, was twice promoted to magistrate of Yu, governed the people by ritual, and transformed custom by virtue.

entries.zh: 時它郡盜徒五人來入圉界，吏捕得入，陳留太守馬嚴聞而疾惡，風縣殺之。
entries.en: Five thieves from a neighboring district crossed into Yu; his officers arrested them; Ma Yan, prefect of Chenliu, heard the news, hated the criminals, and signaled the county to execute them.
entries.literal: At that time five bandits from another commandery entered Yu's borders; the clerks seized and brought them in; the grand administrator of Chenliu Ma Yan heard of it and detested them, and hinted to the county to kill them.

entries.zh: 褒敕吏曰：『夫絕人命者，天亦絕之。
entries.en: Cao Bao told his staff: "Those who take life will have life taken from them.
entries.literal: Bao instructed the clerks: 'He who cuts short human life, heaven also cuts short his.

entries.zh: 臯陶不為盜制死刑，管仲遇盜而升諸公。
entries.en: Gao Yao did not fix death as the penalty for theft; Guan Zhong once promoted thieves to the lord's notice.
entries.literal: Gao Yao did not prescribe death for robbers, and when Guan Zhong met robbers he advanced them to the duke.

entries.zh: 今承旨而殺之，是逆天心，順府意也，其罰重矣。
entries.en: To kill them now on a superior's nod would defy heaven and merely please the prefect—that would be the graver fault.
entries.literal: Now to kill them on orders from above is to oppose heaven's mind and comply with the prefect's wish—the penalty would be heavy.

entries.zh: 如得全此人命而身坐之，吾所願也。』
entries.en: If I may save their lives and take the blame myself, I will gladly do it."
entries.literal: If I can preserve these persons' lives while myself bearing the punishment, that is what I wish.'

entries.zh: 遂不為殺。
entries.en: He refused to execute them.
entries.literal: Therefore he did not kill them.

entries.zh: 嚴奏褒耎弱，免官歸郡，為功曹。
entries.en: Ma Yan denounced him as soft; Cao Bao was stripped of office and went home to serve as merit clerk.
entries.literal: Yan memorialized that Bao was weak and irresolute; he was dismissed and returned to his commandery, where he became chief clerk.

entries.zh: 論曰：『漢初天下創定，朝制無文，叔孫通頗采經禮，參酌秦法，雖適物觀時，有救崩敝，然先王之容典蓋多闕矣，是以賈誼、仲舒、王吉、劉向之徒，懷憤嘆息所不能已也。
entries.en: The historian comments: "Early Han had no written court ritual; Shusun Tong drew on classical rites and Qin statutes—it met the moment and staunched decay, yet the old kings' forms were largely gone, which is why men like Jia Yi, Dong Zhongshu, Wang Ji, and Liu Xiang fumed and could not rest.
entries.literal: The judgment says: 'At the beginning of Han the realm was newly settled, court institutions had no literary form; Shusun Tong took somewhat from the canonical rites and consulted Qin law—though suited to things and observant of the times, and though it rescued collapse and decay, yet the outward forms of the former kings were for the most part missing; hence Jia Yi, Dong Zhongshu, Wang Ji, Liu Xiang, and their sort, harboring indignation and sighing, could not rest.

entries.zh: 資文、宣之遠圖明懿，而終莫或用，故知自燕而觀，有不盡矣。
entries.en: Wen and Xuan had long vision and clear virtue, yet none of these schemes was adopted—so viewing from a swallow's nest, one never sees the whole.
entries.literal: They had the distant plans and clear virtue of Emperors Wen and Xuan, yet in the end none of it was used—thus one knows that gazing from the swallow's nest, the view is not exhaustive.

entries.zh: 孝章永言前王，明發興作，專命禮臣，撰定國憲，洋洋乎盛德之事焉。
entries.en: Zhangdi never ceased invoking the ancient kings, rose at dawn intent on creation, charged ritual officers, and drafted the national code—a magnificent act of virtue.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhang forever spoke of the former kings, dawned on the need to create, specially ordered the ritual ministers, and drafted the state's fundamental statutes—how vast a work of abundant virtue.

entries.zh: 而業絕天算，議黜異端，斯道竟復墜矣。
entries.en: Heaven cut short his years, faction dismissed rival opinions, and the whole effort collapsed.
entries.literal: Yet the enterprise was cut off by heaven's reckoning, debate dismissed divergent views, and this way in the end fell again.

entries.zh: 夫三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂，所以《咸》、《莖》異調，中都殊絕。
entries.en: The Three Kings did not inherit each other's rites nor the Five Emperors each other's music—hence the Xian and Jing odes differ and the two capitals stand worlds apart.
entries.literal: The Three Kings did not copy one another's ritual, the Five Emperors did not follow one another's music—therefore Xian and Jing had different modes and the central capitals were utterly unlike.

entries.zh: 況物運遷回，情數萬化，制則不能隨其流變，品度未足定其滋章，斯固世主所當損益者也。
entries.en: Far more today, as things revolve and feeling shifts endlessly—written rules cannot chase every change, nor can measures fix their swelling tangle; that is what each age's ruler must adjust.
entries.literal: How much more when the movement of things turns and returns and the patterns of feeling shift in myriad ways—fixed regulations cannot follow every current change, and standards are not enough to settle their ever-growing complexity; this is surely what the rulers of the age ought to trim or enlarge.

entries.zh: 且樂非夔、襄，而新音代起，律謝臯、蘇，而制令亟易，修補舊文，獨何猜焉？
entries.en: Music was never only Kui and Master Xiang, yet new airs keep coming; pitch was never only Gao and Su, yet scales and edicts change fast—why shrink from revising old texts?
entries.literal: Moreover music is not only Kui and Xiang, yet new tones arise in succession; pitch yields to Gao and Su, yet systems and commands change urgently—why be suspicious of mending the old texts alone?

entries.zh: 禮云禮云，曷其然哉！』
entries.en: They say "ritual, ritual"—can it really be only that?"
entries.literal: They speak of ritual, they speak of ritual—how can it be so!'

entries.zh: 及鄧禹徵還，光武以宗為京輔都尉，將突騎與征西大將軍馮異共擊關中諸營保，破之，遷河南都尉。
entries.en: After Deng Yu was withdrawn, Emperor Guangwu named Zong commandant of the capital districts; with Feng Yi, the western expedition commander, he rode against the fortified camps of Guanzhong, broke them, and was promoted to commandant of Henan.
entries.literal: When Deng Yu was recalled, Guangwu appointed Zong Metropolitan Commandant of the capital region; he led mounted raiders with Grand General Who Conquers the West Feng Yi to jointly strike the fort camps of Guanzhong, defeated them, and was promoted to Commandant of Henan.

entries.zh: 建武六年，都尉官省，拜太中大夫。
entries.en: In Jianwu 6 the commandant post was eliminated, and he received appointment as grand palace grandee.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Jianwu, the commandant office was abolished; he was appointed Grand Palace Grandee.

entries.zh: 八年，潁川桑中盜賊群起，宗將兵擊定之。
entries.en: In year 8 bandit gangs sprang up around Sangzhong in Yingchuan; Zong took troops and suppressed them.
entries.literal: In the eighth year, bandits rose in a crowd at Sangzhong in Yingchuan; Zong led troops to strike and pacify them.

entries.zh: 後青、冀盜賊屯聚山澤，宗以謁者督諸郡兵討平之。
entries.en: Later, when outlaws from Qingzhou and Ji province holed up in the hills and marshes, Zong, holding the office of messenger, coordinated county levies and stamped them out.
entries.literal: Later bandits of Qing and Ji gathered in mountains and marshes; Zong, as messenger, supervised the troops of the commanderies and attacked and pacified them.

entries.zh: 十六年，琅邪、北海盜賊復起，宗督二郡兵討之，乃設方略，明購賞，皆悉破散，於是沛、楚、東海、臨淮群賊懼其威武，相捕斬者數千人，青、徐震慄。
entries.en: In year 16 unrest flared again in Langya and Beihai; Zong commanded both commanderies' forces, laid out a clear strategy and generous bounties, and scattered every band. Across Pei, Chu, Donghai, and Linhuai the gangs quailed at his reputation—rival factions turned on one another and claimed thousands of heads—and Qingzhou and Xuzhou shook with fear.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, bandits of Langya and Beihai rose again; Zong supervised the troops of the two commanderies to attack them, then laid plans and made clear rewards for capture—all were utterly broken and scattered. Thereupon the mass bandits of Pei, Chu, Donghai, and Linhuai feared his might; those who captured and killed one another numbered several thousand; Qing and Xu trembled.

entries.zh: 後遷琅邪相，其政好嚴猛，敢殺伐。
entries.en: He was later promoted to chancellor of Langya, where he governed with a heavy hand and did not shrink from capital punishment.
entries.literal: Later he was transferred to be chancellor of Langya; his administration favored severity and harshness, daring execution and killing.

entries.zh: 永平二年，卒於官。
entries.en: He died in office in the second year of the Yongping era (59 CE).
entries.literal: In the second year of Yongping, he died in office.

entries.zh: 法雄字文彊，扶風郿人也，齊襄王法章之後。
entries.en: Fa Xiong, styled Wenqiang, was a native of Mei in Fufeng and traced his line to Fa Zhang, King Xiang of Qi.
entries.literal: Fa Xiong, courtesy name Wenqiang, was a man of Mei in Fufeng, a descendant of Fa Zhang, King Xiang of Qi.

entries.zh: 秦滅齊，子孫不敢稱田姓，故以法為氏。
entries.en: When Qin conquered Qi, the family dared not keep the royal surname Tian and adopted Fa instead.
entries.literal: When Qin destroyed Qi, the descendants dared not use the surname Tian, therefore they took Fa as the clan name.

entries.zh: 宣帝時，徙三輔，世為二千石。
entries.en: Under Emperor Xuan they relocated to the capital region, and for generations they held top salary-grade posts.
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Xuan, they moved to the Three Adjuncts; for generations they held two-thousand–picul rank.

entries.zh: 雄初仕郡功曹，辟太傅張禹府，舉雄高第，除平氏長。
entries.en: Xiong began as a commandery merit officer, entered the staff of Grand Tutor Zhang Yu, graduated with high marks, and was named magistrate of Pingshi.
entries.literal: Xiong at first served as merit officer of the commandery, was summoned to the Grand Tutor Zhang Yu's office, was recommended in the high grade, and was appointed magistrate of Pingshi.

entries.zh: 善政事，好發擿姦伏，盜賊稀發，吏人畏愛之。
entries.en: He ran an efficient government, dug out concealed crime, and kept banditry rare; officials and commoners alike respected and trusted him.
entries.literal: He was skilled in administration, fond of exposing hidden villainy; bandits rarely arose; clerks and people feared and loved him.

entries.zh: 南陽太守鮑得上其理狀，遷宛陵令。
entries.en: Governor Bao De of Nanyang reported his exemplary record, and Xiong was promoted to magistrate of Wanling.
entries.literal: The governor of Nanyang, Bao De, submitted upward his record of good governance; he was transferred to be magistrate of Wanling.

entries.zh: 楊琁字機平，會稽烏傷人也。
entries.en: Yang Xuan, styled Jiping, came from Wushang in Kuaiji commandery.
entries.literal: Yang Xuan, courtesy name Jiping, was a man of Wushang in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 高祖父茂，本河東人，從光武征伐，為威寇將軍，封烏傷新陽鄉侯。
entries.en: His great-grandfather Yang Mao was a Hedong man who campaigned with Emperor Guangwu as General Who Subdues Raiders and received the marquisate of Xinyang township in Wushang.
entries.literal: His great-grandfather Mao was originally a man of Hedong; he followed Guangwu in campaigns, became General Who Might Smite the Bandits, was enfeoffed as marquis of Xinyang township of Wushang.

entries.zh: 建武中就國，傳封三世，有罪國除，因而家焉。
entries.en: In the Jianwu era he took up his fief; the title passed three generations until a crime forfeited it, and the family remained there.
entries.literal: In Jianwu he went to his state; the enfeoffment passed three generations; having crime the state was abolished; therefore they made home there.

entries.zh: 父扶，交阯刺史，有理能名。
entries.en: His father Yang Fu served as inspector of Jiaozhi and was known as a capable administrator.
entries.literal: His father Fu was governor of Jiaozhi, had a name for governing ability.

entries.zh: 兄喬，為尚書，容儀偉麗，數上言政事，桓帝愛其才貌，詔妻以公主，喬固辭不聽，遂閉口不食，七日而死。
entries.en: His elder brother Yang Qiao was a Master of Writing; he was handsome and often advised the throne. Emperor Huan admired his looks and talent and offered him an imperial princess. Qiao refused again and again; when the emperor would not relent, he stopped eating and died on the seventh day.
entries.literal: His elder brother Qiao was a Master of Writing; countenance and bearing were great and beautiful; repeatedly submitted speech on government affairs; Emperor Huan loved his talent and appearance; an edict would marry him to a princess; Qiao firmly declined and was not listened to; thereupon he closed his mouth and did not eat, and died in seven days.

entries.zh: 張宗字諸君，南陽魯陽人也。
entries.en: Zhang Zong, styled Zhujun, came from Luyang in Nanyang commandery.
entries.literal: Zhang Zong, courtesy name Zhujun, was a man of Luyang in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 王莽時，為縣陽泉鄉佐。
entries.en: Under Wang Mang he held the post of township aide at Yangquan in his home county.
entries.literal: In the time of Wang Mang, he served as township assistant in Yangquan township of the county.

entries.zh: 會莽敗，義兵起，宗乃率陽泉民三四百人起兵略地，西至長安，更始以宗為偏將軍。
entries.en: After Wang Mang fell and loyal forces rose, Zong rallied three or four hundred men from Yangquan, took the field to seize ground, and marched west to Chang'an, where the Gengshi Emperor named him lieutenant general.
entries.literal: When Mang fell and righteous armies rose, Zong then led three or four hundred men of Yangquan to raise troops and seize territory, west to Chang'an; Gengshi appointed Zong Lieutenant General.

entries.zh: 宗見更始政亂，因將家屬客安邑。
entries.en: Seeing the Gengshi regime unravel, he moved his household and settled as a guest in Anyi.
entries.literal: Zong saw Gengshi's government in chaos and therefore took his family and lodged as a guest at Anyi.

entries.zh: 並遺宛馬一匹，血從前髆上小孔中出。
entries.en: With it goes a Ferghana horse whose blood beads from a pore on the shoulder.
entries.literal: Together leave Wan horse one piece—blood from front shoulder blade upper small hole emerges.

entries.zh: 常聞武帝歌天馬，沾赤汗，今親見其然也。
entries.en: I grew up on the songs of Emperor Wu's sweating steeds—now I have seen one.
entries.literal: Constantly heard Martial Emperor sing heaven horse—stained red sweat—now personally see it thus.

entries.zh: 頃反虜尚屯，將帥在外，憂念遑遑，未有閒寧。
entries.en: [68] Rebels still hold the field and our generals are abroad—I have no peace of mind.
entries.literal: [68] Recently rebel captives still camp—generals outside—worry thought restless—have not yet idle peace.

entries.zh: 願王寶精神，加供養。
entries.en: [69] Guard your health and take care of yourself.
entries.literal: [69] Wish king treasure spirit—add nourishing.

entries.zh: 苦言至戒，望之如渴。」
entries.en: I thirst for your blunt counsel."
entries.literal: Bitter words utmost warning—long for them like thirst."

entries.zh: 東海恭王彊
entries.en: King Gong of the East Sea, Liu Qiang
entries.literal: King Gong of East Sea, Qiang.

entries.zh: 終又言：「宣帝博征群儒，論定五經於石渠閣。
entries.en: Zhong also said: "Emperor Xuan widely summoned Confucian scholars and fixed the meaning of the Five Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion.
entries.literal: Zhong also said: "Emperor Xuan widely summoned Confucian scholars and fixed the meaning of the Five Classics in the Stone Canal Pavilion.

entries.zh: 方今天下少事，學者得成其業，而章句之徒，破壞大體。
entries.en: Today, with few disturbances in the empire, learners could perfect their craft, but petty exegetes are tearing apart the larger tradition.
entries.literal: Now the realm has few troubles and students can complete their studies, yet the chapter-and-verse crowd ruin the great pattern.

entries.zh: 宜如石渠故事，永為後世則。」
entries.en: He proposed repeating the Stone Canal conference so as to leave a permanent standard for posterity."
entries.literal: It would be fitting to follow the Stone Canal precedent and make a lasting model for later ages."

entries.zh: 於是詔諸儒於白虎觀論考同異焉。
entries.en: An edict followed, summoning Confucians to the White Tiger Hall to thrash out textual agreement and disagreement.
entries.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered the scholars to debate agreements and differences at the White Tiger Hall.

entries.zh: 會終坐事系獄，博士趙博、校書郎班固、賈逵等，以終深曉春秋，學多異聞，表請之，終又上書自訟，即日貰出，乃得與於白虎觀焉。
entries.en: When Yang Zhong was jailed for a separate matter, Zhao Bo, Ban Gu, Jia Kui, and others petitioned that his mastery of the Annals and wide learning deserved mercy; his own memorial won him a pardon that very day, and he joined the White Tiger deliberations.
entries.literal: It happened that Zhong was imprisoned for an offense; Erudite Zhao Bo, collator Ban Gu, Jia Kui, and others, because Zhong thoroughly understood the Chunqiu and had learned many unusual traditions, memorialized for him; Zhong also submitted a memorial in his own defense, and the same day he was pardoned and released, and so was able to take part in the White Tiger conference.

entries.zh: [一]後受詔刪太史公書為十餘萬言。
entries.en: He was later commissioned to condense Sima Qian's history to more than one hundred thousand characters.
entries.literal: Later he received orders to abridge the Grand Scribe's book to over a hundred thousand characters.

entries.zh: 注[三]公羊傳曰：「晉侯殺其太子申生。
entries.en: Commentary [3]: "The Gongyang asks why the text says the marquis of Jin killed Crown Prince Shensheng.
entries.literal: Note [3] The Gongyang says: "The Marquis of Jin killed his heir Shengsheng.

entries.zh: 曷為直稱晉侯？
entries.en: Why name the ruler of Jin alone?
entries.literal: Why is the Marquis of Jin named straight?

entries.zh: 曰以殺其太子母弟，直稱君者甚之也。」
entries.en: The answer: naming only the lord when he kills his heir or full brother heaps the guilt on him."
entries.literal: It says: because in killing his heir and younger brother by full blood, to name the ruler alone is to blame him heavily."

entries.zh: 初，酺之為大匠，上言：「孝文皇帝始置一經博士，[一]武帝大合天下之書，[二] 而孝宣論六經於石渠，學者滋盛，弟子萬數。
entries.en: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: Earlier, when Pu was superintendent of construction, he submitted a statement: 'Emperor Wen first established erudites for a single classic; [1] Emperor Wu broadly gathered the books of All under Heaven; [2] while Emperor Xuan debated the six classics at the Stone Canal—scholars flourished and disciples numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: [三]光武初興，愍其荒廢，起太學博士捨、內外講堂，諸生橫巷，為海內所集。
entries.en: [3] Emperor Guangwu, grieving the ruin of learning, had rebuilt the Grand Academy with dormitories, inner and outer lecture halls, and student quarters that drew scholars from everywhere.
entries.literal: [3] When Guangwu first rose, pitying their ruin and waste, he raised the Grand Academy, erudite lodgings, inner and outer lecture halls, and lanes of students—it became the gathering place of the realm.

entries.zh: 明帝時辟雍始成，欲毀太學，太尉趙憙以為太學、辟雍皆宜兼存，故並傳至今。
entries.en: When Emperor Ming finished the circular moat school, some wanted the Grand Academy torn down; Grand Commandant Zhao Xi argued that both institutions should survive, and both stand today.
entries.literal: In Emperor Ming's time, when the Biyong was first completed, they wished to destroy the Grand Academy. Grand Commandant Zhao Xi held that the Grand Academy and the Biyong should both be kept, and therefore both have been transmitted to the present.

entries.zh: 而頃者頹廢，至為園采芻牧之處。
entries.en: Lately the grounds had fallen into disuse as vegetable patches, hayfields, and sheep walks.
entries.literal: But recently it has decayed and wasted until it became a place for garden plots, gathering fodder, and herding.

entries.zh: 宜更修繕，誘進後學。」
entries.en: Zhai Pu urged a fresh restoration to attract the next generation of learners."
entries.literal: It is fitting to repair and build anew and entice later students.'

entries.zh: 帝從之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted the advice.
entries.literal: The emperor followed it.'"

entries.zh: 酺免後，遂起太學，更開拓房室，學者為酺立碑銘於學雲。
entries.en: After his disgrace the Grand Academy was rebuilt and expanded; students are said to have raised a stele in his honor on the campus.
entries.literal: After Pu was dismissed, thereupon they raised the Grand Academy, again opened and expanded rooms, and scholars set up a stele inscription for Pu at the academy, it is said.

entries.zh: 注[一]武帝建元五年始置五經博士，文帝之時未遑庠序之事，酺之此言，不知何據。
entries.en: Commentary [1]: Emperor Wu first established Erudites for the Five Classics in the fifth year of Jianyuan. In Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for affairs of schools and academies, so it is unclear what authority Zhai Pu had for this statement.
entries.literal: Note [1] In Emperor Wu's Jianyuan 5 the five-classics erudites were first established; in Emperor Wen's time there was not yet leisure for school matters—what Pu's statement relies on is unknown.

entries.zh: 注[二]武帝詔曰：「其令禮官勸學，舉遺興禮。」
entries.en: Commentary [2]: "Emperor Wu had ordered the ritual bureau to revive neglected learning and rites."
entries.literal: Note [2] Emperor Wu's edict said: 'Let the ritual officials encourage learning and raise the lost and promote ritual.'

entries.zh: 舉遺謂搜求遺逸，是合天下之書也。
entries.en: Raising the lost meant recovering lost texts, that is, the empire-wide book hunt.
entries.literal: Raise the lost' means to search out the scattered and hidden—this is gathering the books of All under Heaven.'

entries.zh: 注[三]宣帝甘露三年，詔諸儒講五經於殿中，兼平公羊、谷梁同異，上親臨決焉。
entries.en: Commentary [3]: In Ganlu 3 Emperor Xuan held a palace conference on the five classics and adjudicated Gongyang versus Guliang in person.
entries.literal: Note [3] In Emperor Xuan's Ganlu 3 an edict ordered the scholars to lecture on the five classics in the palace, also settling agreements and differences between Gongyang and Guliang, and the emperor personally attended to decide.

entries.zh: 時更崇谷梁傳，故此言「六經」也。
entries.en: At that time they further honored the Guliang commentary, hence this speaks of 'six classics.'
entries.literal: At that time they further honored the Guliang commentary, hence this speaks of 'six classics.'

entries.zh: 石渠，閣名。
entries.en: Stone Canal was the name of the palace gallery where the debate met.
entries.literal: Stone Canal is the name of a pavilion.

entries.zh: 昭帝時博士弟子員百人，宣帝末增倍之，元帝時詔無置弟子員，以廣學者，故言以萬數也。
entries.en: Student rolls had grown from one hundred under Zhao to doubled under Xuan, then Yuan removed caps so enrollments could soar toward ten thousand.
entries.literal: In Emperor Zhao's time erudite disciples numbered one hundred; at the end of Emperor Xuan it was doubled; in Emperor Yuan's time an edict ordered not to fix a quota of disciples so as to broaden learners—hence it says they numbered in the tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 帝以延儒生，常特宴見。
entries.en: Emperor Huan often feasted Yuan Yan alone as a scholar-favorite.
entries.literal: Because Yan was a Confucian scholar, the emperor often gave him special feasts and audiences.

entries.zh: 時太史令上言客星經帝坐，帝密以問延。
entries.en: When a stray star crossed the throne asterism, the emperor quietly asked Yuan Yan what it meant.
entries.literal: At that time the grand astrologer submitted that a guest star had crossed the emperor's seat; the emperor secretly asked Yan about it.

entries.zh: 延因上封事曰：「臣聞天子尊無為上，故天以為子，位臨臣庶，威重四海。
entries.en: Yan thereupon submitted a sealed memorial, saying: 'I have heard the Son of Heaven is honored as none above—therefore Heaven makes him son; his position overlooks ministers and commoners; his awesome might fills the four seas.
entries.literal: Yan thereupon submitted a sealed memorial, saying: 'I have heard the Son of Heaven is honored as none above—therefore Heaven makes him son; his position overlooks ministers and commoners; his awesome might fills the four seas.

entries.zh: 動靜以禮，則星辰順序；
entries.en: Right conduct keeps the constellations in harmony;
entries.literal: When movement and stillness follow ritual, then the stars march in order;

entries.zh: 意有邪僻，則晷度錯違。
entries.en: wicked intent throws the calendar and omens out of true.
entries.literal: if the mind harbors depravity, then the gnomon's degrees miss and violate.

entries.zh: 陛下以河南尹鄧萬有龍潛之舊，封為通侯，恩重公卿，惠豐宗室。
entries.en: Emperor Huan ennobled Deng Wan, an old companion from before the throne, beyond normal ministerial favor.
entries.literal: Your Majesty, because metropolitan governor of Henan Deng Wan had old ties from before your accession, enfeoffed him as full marquis—favor heavier than the dukes and ministers, bounty rich for the imperial house.

entries.zh: 加頃引見，與之對博，上下媟黷，有虧尊嚴。
entries.en: He added that gambling with Wan in public shamed the throne.
entries.literal: Further you lately summoned him to meet and played liubo with him; high and low were lewd and defiled, injuring august dignity.

entries.zh: 臣聞之，帝左右者，所以咨政德也。
entries.en: Court companions should refine policy, not dice games.
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that those at the emperor's left and right are the means to consult on virtue in government.

entries.zh: 故周公戒成王曰『其朋其朋』，言慎所與也。
entries.en: He quoted the Documents' warning about friends of the ruler.
entries.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou warned King Cheng, saying 'Be careful of your companions, be careful of your companions'—meaning be careful whom you befriend.

entries.zh: [一]昔宋閔公與強臣共博，列婦人於側，積此無禮，以致大災。
entries.en: [1] Duke Min of Song's fatal dice game illustrated the danger.
entries.literal: [1] Formerly Duke Min of Song played liubo with a powerful minister, ranged women at the side—accumulating such lack of ritual led to great disaster.

entries.zh: [二]武帝與幸臣李延年﹑韓嫣同臥起，尊爵重賜，情慾無猒，遂生驕淫之心，行不義之事，卒延年被戮，嫣伏其辜。
entries.en: [2] Emperor Wu's intimacy with singers ended in executions.
entries.literal: [2] Emperor Wu slept and rose with favored ministers Li Yannian and Han Yan, honored them with noble rank and heavy gifts, lust and appetite insatiable—thereupon arose arrogant and dissolute hearts, unrighteous deeds were done, and in the end Yannian was executed and Yan submitted to his crime.

entries.zh: [三]夫愛之則不覺其過，惡之則不知其善，所以事多放濫，物情生怨。
entries.en: [3] Passion blinds rulers to fault and merit alike.
entries.literal: [3] When you love them you do not notice their faults; when you hate them you do not know their good—therefore affairs mostly run wild and feeling breeds resentment.

entries.zh: 注[三]李延年，中山人也。
entries.en: Commentary [3]: Li Yannian's origin.
entries.literal: Note [3] Li Yannian was a man of Zhongshan.

entries.zh: 身及父母兄弟皆故倡人也。
entries.en: His whole family were performers.
entries.literal: He and his parents and brothers had all been entertainers.

entries.zh: 武帝時，延年女弟得幸，號曰李夫人。
entries.en: His sister became Lady Li.
entries.literal: In Emperor Wu's time his younger sister won favor—she was titled Lady Li.

entries.zh: 延年善歌舞，為協律都尉，佩二千石印綬，與上臥起。
entries.en: He rose to music director with ministerial rank and shared the emperor's bed.
entries.literal: Yannian was skilled at songs and dances, became director of harmony, wore a two-thousand-bushel seal ribbon, and slept and rose with the emperor.

entries.zh: 弟季與中人亂，出入驕恣，上遂誅延年兄弟。
entries.en: His brother's scandal cost the whole family their lives.
entries.literal: His younger brother Ji debauched with a palace man, came and went arrogantly; the emperor thereupon executed Yannian and his brothers.

entries.zh: 韓嫣，韓王信之曾孫也。
entries.en: Han Yan descended from Han Xin.
entries.literal: Han Yan was the great-grandson of King Xin of Han.

entries.zh: 武帝為王時，與嫣相愛，後位至上大夫，賞賜擬鄧通，與上臥起，出入永巷，以奸聞被誅。
entries.en: Yan had been Wu's boyhood favorite until scandal brought execution.
entries.literal: When Emperor Wu was a king he loved Yan; later his rank reached senior grandee; rewards rivaled Deng Tong's; he slept and rose with the emperor, went in and out of the long lanes, and was executed when his debauchery was heard.

entries.zh: 楊終字子山，蜀郡成都人也。
entries.en: Yang Zhong, styled Zishan, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
entries.literal: Yang Zhong, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

entries.zh: 年十三，為郡小吏，太守奇其才，遣詣京師受業，習春秋。
entries.en: When he was thirteen he served as a junior clerk in the commandery. The grand administrator, struck by his ability, sent him to the capital for schooling, and there he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
entries.literal: At age thirteen he became a petty clerk in the commandery; the grand administrator marveled at his talent and sent him to the capital to study, where he learned the Chunqiu.

entries.zh: [一]顯宗時，征詣蘭台，拜校書郎。
entries.en: Under Emperor Ming he was called to the Orchid Terrace and given the post of collating secretary [1].
entries.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming [note 1], he was summoned to the Orchid Terrace and appointed collator.

entries.zh: 出為益州刺史。
entries.en: He became governor of Yi province.
entries.literal: He went out as governor of Yi province.

entries.zh: 暠素慷慨，好立功立事。
entries.en: Zhong Hao was bold and ambitious.
entries.literal: Hao by nature was generous and ardent, fond of establishing merit and accomplishing deeds.

entries.zh: 在職三年，宣恩遠夷，開曉殊俗，岷山雜落皆懷服漢德。
entries.en: In three years he won the tribes of Minshan to Han rule.
entries.literal: In office three years he spread grace to distant Yi, opened and enlightened alien customs, and the mixed settlements on Mount Min all cherished and submitted to Han virtue.

entries.zh: 其白狼﹑盤木﹑唐菆﹑滘﹑僰諸國，[一]自前刺史朱輔卒後遂絕；
entries.en: Note [1]: Tribes such as Bailang had cut tribute since Zhu Fu died;
entries.literal: The states of Bailang, Panmu, Tangzou, Jiao, Bo, and others, [one] since the former governor Zhu Fu died had broken off;

entries.zh: 暠至，乃復舉種向化。
entries.en: when Zhong Hao came, they renewed submission.
entries.literal: when Hao arrived, they again raised their tribes toward transformation.

entries.zh: 時永昌太守冶鑄黃金為文蛇，以獻梁冀，暠糾發逮捕，馳傳上言，而二府畏懦，不敢案之，冀由是銜怒於暠。
entries.en: He arrested Yongchang's governor for bribing Liang Ji with a golden snake; the high ministers quailed, and Liang Ji hated him for it.
entries.literal: At that time the governor of Yongchang cast gold into a patterned serpent to present to Liang Ji; Hao impeached, exposed, and arrested him, sent post-haste upward to speak, but the two offices were timid and dared not try the case, whereupon Ji bore hatred in his heart toward Hao.

entries.zh: 會巴郡人服直聚黨數百人，自稱「天王」，[二]暠與太守應承討捕，不克，吏人多被傷害。
entries.en: Note [2]: A cult leader Fu Zhi in Ba rose as 'Heaven's King'; Zhong Hao and Ying Cheng failed to suppress him and took casualties.
entries.literal: It happened that a man of Ba commandery, Fu Zhi, gathered a faction of several hundred who called themselves 'Heaven's King,' [two] Hao together with governor Ying Cheng attacked and seized them but could not overcome them; many clerks and people were harmed.

entries.zh: 冀因此陷之，傳逮暠﹑承。
entries.en: Liang Ji used the failure to impeach Zhong Hao and Ying Cheng.
entries.literal: Ji by this trapped them, transmitting orders to seize Hao and Cheng.

entries.zh: 太尉李固上疏救曰：「臣伏聞討捕所傷，本非暠﹑承之意，實由縣吏懼法畏罪，迫逐深苦，致此不詳。
entries.en: Grand Commandant Li Gu submitted a memorial of rescue saying: 'Your servant has heard that the harm in the attack and seizure was originally not the intent of Hao and Cheng; truly it was because county clerks feared the law and dreaded crime, pressed pursuit in bitter depth, and brought about this ill-omened outcome.
entries.literal: Grand Commandant Li Gu submitted a memorial of rescue saying: 'Your servant has heard that the harm in the attack and seizure was originally not the intent of Hao and Cheng; truly it was because county clerks feared the law and dreaded crime, pressed pursuit in bitter depth, and brought about this ill-omened outcome.

entries.zh: 比盜賊腢起，處處未絕。
entries.en: Rebels were rising everywhere.
entries.literal: Moreover bandits and robbers lately rise everywhere and are not yet cut off.

entries.zh: 暠﹑承以首舉大奸，而相隨受罪，臣恐沮傷州縣糾發之意，更共飾匿，莫復盡心。」
entries.en: Punishing men who first exposed major crime would make officials cover up wrongdoing."
entries.literal: Hao and Cheng for first exposing great wickedness yet follow in receiving punishment; your servant fears this will discourage the intent of commanderies and counties to impeach and expose, and they will together gloss over and hide, never again exhausting their hearts.'

entries.zh: [三] 梁太后省奏，乃赦暠﹑承罪，免官而已。
entries.en: Note [3]: Empress Dowager Liang read Li Gu's plea and pardoned them, stripping only their posts.
entries.literal: [Three] Empress Dowager Liang examined the memorial and thereupon pardoned Hao and Cheng's crimes, dismissing from office only.

entries.zh: 注[二]「直」或作「宜」。
entries.en: Commentary [2]: "Manuscript variant Yi for Zhi in the rebel's name."
entries.literal: Commentary [two]: 'Zhi' is sometimes written 'Yi.'

entries.zh: 張□字叔明，犍為武陽人也。
entries.en: Zhang Hao (the patronymic graph is missing in some manuscripts), styled Shuming, came from Wuyang in Qianwei.
entries.literal: Zhang [lacuna in text], styled Shuming, was a native of Wuyang in Qianwei commandery.

entries.zh: 六世祖良，高帝時為太子少傅，封留侯。
entries.en: Six generations back, Zhang Liang had been junior tutor to the crown prince under Gaozu and held the title Marquis of Liu.
entries.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Liang, in the time of the High Emperor, served as junior tutor to the heir apparent and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Liu.

entries.zh: □少遊學京師，*
entries.en: In his youth Zhang Hao studied in Luoyang; the sentence breaks in the received text.
entries.literal: Zhang [lacuna in text] in his youth traveled to study in the capital,

entries.en: At first,
entries.literal: (At first)

entries.zh: *永元中，歸仕州郡，辟大將軍鄧騭府，五遷尚書僕射，職事八年，出為彭城相。
entries.en: During Yongyuan he took posts in the provinces, entered Grand General Deng Zhi's headquarters, rose through five steps to vice director of the masters of writing, served eight years, and was then sent out as chancellor of Pengcheng.
entries.literal: In the Yongyuan era he returned to serve in the commanderies, was summoned to Grand General Deng Zhi's office, was promoted five times to vice director of the masters of writing, held office eight years, then went out as chancellor of Pengcheng.

entries.en: Note [1]: (footnote marker)
entries.literal: [One]

entries.zh: 注[一二]方猶並也。
entries.en: Fang marks paired hulls.
entries.literal: Note [12] Fang means side by side.

entries.zh: 余皇，吳之船名也。
entries.en: Yuhuang was the great Wu dreadnought.
entries.literal: Yuhuang is Wu’s ship name.

entries.zh: 見左傳。
entries.en: See Zuo’s battle of Huangchi.
entries.literal: See the Zuo Zhuan.

entries.zh: 舼，小舟也，音渠恭反。
entries.en: Qiong skiffs use fanqie qu-gong.
entries.literal: Qiong is a small boat; pronunciation qu-gong fan.

entries.zh: 淮南子曰：「越舼、蜀艇，不能無水而浮。」
entries.en: The Huainanzi says: "Yue qiong and Shu boats cannot float without water."
entries.literal: The Huainanzi says: "Yue qiong and Shu boats cannot float without water."

entries.zh: 帆音凡。
entries.en: Fan as in ‘sail.’
entries.literal: Fan is pronounced fan.

entries.zh: 幬，帳也，音直由反。
entries.en: Chou is awning—fanqie zhi-you.
entries.literal: Chou is canopy; pronunciation zhi-you fan.

entries.zh: 颸，疾風也，音楚疑也。
entries.en: Si names slick breezes.
entries.literal: Si is swift wind; pronunciation chu-yi.

entries.zh: 武帝秋風詞曰：「蕭鼓鳴兮發棹歌。」
entries.en: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."
entries.literal: Emperor Wu's Autumn Wind Song says: "Flutes and drums sound; the oar song begins."

entries.zh: 劉向列女傳曰：「津更之女，中流奏河激之歌。」
entries.en: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."
entries.literal: Liu Xiang's Biographies of Exemplary Women says: "The ferryman's daughter performed the song "River Surge" in midstream."

entries.zh: 韓詩外傳曰：「瓠巴鼓琴，淫魚出聽。」
entries.en: The Han shi waizhuan says: "When Hu Ba strummed his qin, leaping fish came out to listen."
entries.literal: The Han shi waizhuan says: "When Hu Ba strummed his qin, leaping fish came out to listen."

entries.zh: 淮南子曰：「上有叢蓍，下有伏龜。」
entries.en: The Huainanzi says: "Where clusters of yarrow grow above, turtles lie below."
entries.literal: The Huainanzi says: "Where clusters of yarrow grow above, turtles lie below."

entries.zh: 論語曰：「臧文仲居蔡。」
entries.en: The Analects says: "Zang Wenzhong housed the Cai tortoise."
entries.literal: The Analects says: "Zang Wenzhong housed the Cai tortoise."

entries.zh: 注云：「龜出蔡地，故以為名也。」
entries.en: Commentary says: "The tortoise came from Cai lands—hence the name."
entries.literal: Commentary says: "The tortoise came from Cai lands—hence the name."

entries.zh: 湘靈，舜妃，溺於湘水，為湘夫人也。
entries.en: Lady Xiang guards the Xiang shallows.
entries.literal: Xiang Ling is Shun’s consort—she drowned in the Xiang and became Lady Xiang.

entries.zh: 見楚詞。
entries.en: See the Songs of Chu.
entries.literal: See the Chu ci.

entries.zh: 漢女，漢水之神*[女]*。
entries.en: Han Maiden personifies the Han.
entries.literal: Han Maiden is the goddess of the Han River.

entries.zh: 詩云：「漢有游女。」
entries.en: The Canon sings ‘Han girls at play.’
entries.literal: The poem says: "On the Han roam touring girls."

entries.zh: 馬融字季長，扶風茂陵人也，[一]將作大匠嚴之子。
entries.en: Ma Rong, styled Jizhang, came from Maoling in Fufeng. He was the son of Yan, who served as Grand Architect of Works.
entries.literal: Ma Rong, courtesy name Jizhang, was a man of Maoling in Fufeng; [1] he was the son of Yan, the Grand Architect.

entries.zh: [二]為人美辭貌，有俊才。
entries.en: He was gifted in both speech and looks, and carried uncommon intellectual brilliance.
entries.literal: [2] In person he was handsome in speech and bearing, and possessed outstanding talent.

entries.zh: 故其詩云：「四國無政，不用其良。」
entries.en: Hence the Poetry laments: "Throughout the four quarters there is no sound rule; the good are not employed."
entries.literal: Therefore its Odes says: "In the four states there is no good government; they do not use their good men."

entries.zh: 又曰：「哀今之人，胡為虺蜴？」
entries.en: It adds: "Pity the people of this age—why are they treated like poisonous snakes and lizards?"
entries.literal: It also says: "Alas for the people of today—why are they like vipers and lizards?"

entries.zh: 言人畏吏如虺蜴也。
entries.en: The point is that the people dread magistrates as they would venomous reptiles.
entries.literal: It means people fear officials like vipers and lizards.

entries.zh: [四]宗周既滅，六國並秦，坑儒泯典，僄革五等，更立郡縣，[五] 縣設令長，郡置守尉，什伍相司，封豕其民。
entries.en: [4] After Western Zhou fell and the six states were swallowed by Qin, the First Emperor buried scholars alive and burned the classics, abolished the feudal grades, and replaced them with commanderies and counties; [5] each county had a magistrate, each commandery a governor and commandant, and the mutual-surveillance groups of households penned the people in like hogs for the slaughter.
entries.literal: [4] When the Zhou of the west was destroyed, the six states were annexed by Qin; it buried the scholars and extinguished the canons; it drastically cut away the five ranks and instead established commanderies and counties; [5] counties had magistrates and elders, commanderies had governors and commandants; the ten-and-five households watched one another; it treated its people like a great boar.

entries.zh: [六]大漢受命，雖未復古，然克慎庶官，蠲苛救敝，悅以濟難，撫而循之。
entries.en: [6] When Han received Heaven's charge it did not fully revive the old order, yet it was scrupulous about offices, lifted oppressive laws, and nursed the realm through hardship with kindness and restraint.
entries.literal: [6] When the great Han received the mandate, although it did not fully restore antiquity, yet it was able to be careful with the multitude of offices, abolish harshness and rescue what was flawed, please the people to cross difficulties, and soothe and follow them.

entries.zh: 至於文、景，天下康乂。
entries.en: By the reigns of Emperors Wen and Jing the empire was secure and orderly.
entries.literal: As for Wen and Jing, the realm was peaceful and well-governed.

entries.zh: 誠由玄靖寬柔，克慎官人故也。
entries.en: This was due to their deep calm, their gentle rule, and their care in choosing officials.
entries.literal: Truly it was because of profound quietness, lenient softness, and being able to be careful in appointing men.

entries.zh: 降及宣帝，興於仄陋，綜核名實，知時所病，刺史守相，輒親引見，考察言行，信賞必罰。
entries.en: Down to Emperor Xuan, who had risen from obscurity, who matched names to deeds and grasped what ailed the age—when he dealt with regional inspectors, governors, and chancellors he would call them in himself, weigh word against deed, and never waver on reward or punishment.
entries.literal: Descending to Emperor Xuan, who rose from a humble corner, he comprehensively examined names and realities, knew the ills of the times, and for governors and shepherds and ministers he would personally summon and interview them, investigate their words and deeds, and in rewards and punishments was trustworthy and certain.

entries.zh: 帝乃歎曰：「民所以安而無怨者，政平吏良也。
entries.en: The emperor once sighed and said, "The people live untroubled and without complaint because policy is fair and the magistrates are good.
entries.literal: The Emperor then sighed, saying: "The reason the people are peaceful and without resentment is that government is even and officials are good.

entries.zh: 注[七]宣帝時鳳皇五至，因以紀年。
entries.en: Note [7]: under Emperor Xuan the phoenix appeared five times, and reign titles commemorated it.
entries.literal: Note [7] In Emperor Xuan's time phoenixes came five times, and thereby years were recorded.

entries.zh: 夫子聽衛國之政，修其班制，不亦文乎？
entries.en: He put Wei's government in order—is that not refinement?
entries.literal: The master heard Wei's government, cultivated its ranks and regulations—is this not cultured?

entries.zh: 謂夫子『貞惠文子』。」
entries.en: Call him the Loyal, Kind, Refined Master.
entries.literal: We call the master 'Loyal, Kindly, Cultured Master.'

entries.zh: 事見禮記。
entries.en: The story is in the Book of Rites.
entries.literal: The affair is seen in the Record of Rites.

entries.zh: 尹翁歸為右扶風，*[卒]*，宣帝下詔□揚，賜金百斤。
entries.en: Yin Wengui, governor of You Fufeng, died in office; Emperor Xuan issued an edict of praise and sent a hundred jin of gold.
entries.literal: Yin Wengui was Governor of You Fufeng; [when he died], Emperor Xuan issued an edict [lacuna] praising him and bestowed one hundred jin of gold.

entries.zh: 班固曰：「翁歸承風，帝揚厥聲。」
entries.en: Ban Gu wrote, "Wengui caught the imperial breeze, and the throne magnified his name."
entries.literal: Ban Gu says: "Wengui received the wind; the Emperor raised his fame."

entries.zh: 故曰蒙述也。
entries.en: Hence the phrase that the throne "spread his fame" in a written tribute.
entries.literal: Therefore it is said he received narrative.

entries.zh: 注[二]萬歲亭在今洛州故嵩陽縣西北。
entries.en: Note [2]: Wansui Post stood northwest of old Songyang.
entries.literal: Note [2] Wansui Pavilion is northwest of the old Songyang county in modern Luo prefecture.

entries.zh: 武帝元封元年，幸緱氏，登太室，聞山上呼萬歲聲者三，因以名焉。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Wu of Han, the emperor visited Goushi, climbed Taishi, and heard cries of "long life" three times from the mountain; he therefore named the place Wansui.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng under Emperor Wu of Han, the emperor visited Goushi, climbed Taishi, and heard cries of "long life" three times from the mountain; he therefore named the place Wansui.

entries.zh: 論曰：古者諸侯歲貢士，進賢受上賞，非賢貶爵土。
entries.en: The historian remarks: feudal lords once presented talent yearly; recommending worthies won reward, sending dross cost rank.
entries.literal: The essay says: In antiquity the feudal lords yearly presented scholars; advancing the worthy received upper reward, presenting the unworthy demoted rank and territory.

entries.zh: 升之司馬，辯論其才，論定然後官之，任官然後祿之。
entries.en: Candidates went to the minister of war for debate, then office, then salary.
entries.literal: They raised them to the Minister of War, debated their talents, fixed the evaluation and then gave them office, gave them office and then salary.

entries.zh: [一]故王者得其人，進仕勸其行，經邦弘務，所由久矣。
entries.en: [1] Thus wise kings matched men to posts and built lasting rule.
entries.literal: [1] Therefore when the king obtained the right men, promotion encouraged their conduct; ordering the state and magnifying tasks—this is the source of long endurance.

entries.zh: 漢初詔舉賢良、方正，州郡察孝廉、秀才，斯亦貢士之方也。
entries.en: Han edicts called for worthies; provinces nominated filial and cultivated talents—the same principle.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Han edicts summoned worthy, good, and upright men; provinces and commanderies inspected filial and incorrupt and cultivated talents—this too was the method of presenting scholars.

entries.zh: 中興以後，復增敦樸、有道、賢能、直言、獨行、高節、質直、清白、敦厚之屬。
entries.en: After Guangwu came further categories—honest, reclusive, outspoken, and the like.
entries.literal: After the restoration, again were added honest and plain, possessed of the Way, worthy and able, straight-speaking, solitary in conduct, lofty in integrity, plain and straight, pure and white, honest and thick—and such categories.

entries.zh: 榮路既廣，觖望難裁，自是竊名偽服，浸以流競。
entries.en: Broad paths to honor bred false reputations and fierce rivalry.
entries.literal: With honor roads so wide, disappointed hopes were hard to restrain; from this stealing names and false garb gradually flowed into reckless competition.

entries.zh: 權門貴仕，請謁繁興。
entries.en: Great houses and high posts traded favors openly.
entries.literal: Powerful gates and noble offices—seeking favor and visiting flourished.

entries.zh: 自左雄任事，限年試才，雖頗有不密，固亦因識時宜。
entries.en: Zuo Xiong's age limits and exams, though imperfect, fit the age.
entries.literal: From the time Zuo Xiong held office, limiting years and testing talent—although there were places not tight, it solidly was because he recognized the times' needs.

entries.zh: 而黃瓊、胡廣、張衡、崔瑗之徒，泥滯舊方，互相詭駁，循名者屈其短，筭實者挺其□。
entries.en: Huang Qiong, Hu Guang, Zhang Heng, and Cui Yuan clung to old rules and crossed purposes—formalists hid faults, realists exposed them.
entries.literal: Yet Huang Qiong, Hu Guang, Zhang Heng, Cui Yuan, and such men, stuck in old patterns, mutually made strange refutations; those who followed names bent their shortcomings, those who calculated substance straightened their [lacuna].

entries.zh: 故雄在尚書，天下不敢妄選，十餘年閒，稱為得人，斯亦□實之征乎？
entries.en: Under Zuo Xiong the capital dared not traffic in office for a decade—proof that substance could be tested.
entries.literal: Therefore while Xiong was at the Masters of Writing, the realm under Heaven did not dare recklessly select; within more than ten years he was called to have obtained the right men—is this not a sign of [lacuna] substance?

entries.zh: 順帝始以童弱反政，而號令自出，知能任使，故士得用情，天下喁喁仰其風采。
entries.en: Emperor Shun, though young, held real power, chose men well, and the empire looked up to him.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun first took the government back from childhood, yet commands issued from himself, knowing how to employ men, therefore scholars could use their sincerity; all under Heaven craned their necks admiring his bearing.

entries.zh: 遂乃備玄纁玉帛，以聘南陽樊英，天子降寢殿，設□席，尚書奉引，延問失得。
entries.en: He sent black and yellow silks to hire Fan Ying, received him below the imperial couch, and asked what was wrong with the state.
entries.literal: Thereupon he prepared dark and light silks and jade and silk to hire Fan Ying of Nanyang; the Son of Heaven descended to the sleeping hall, spread [lacuna] mats, the Master of Writing led the way, and extended inquiry on gains and losses.

entries.zh: 急登賢之舉，虛降己之禮，於是處士鄙生，忘其拘儒，[二]拂巾衽褐，以企旌車之招矣。
entries.en: Such urgency to find talent and humility toward scholars made hermits dust off caps and wait for the imperial carriage.
entries.literal: Urgent in elevating the worthy, humble in lowering himself—in this way recluses and rustic scholars forgot their cramped Confucianism, [2] brushed caps and wore coarse cloth, hoping for the summoning carriage's invitation.

entries.zh: 至乃英能承風，俊乂鹹事，若李固、周舉之淵謨弘深，左雄、黃瓊之政事貞固，桓焉、楊厚以儒學進，崔瑗、馬融以文章顯，吳佑、蘇章、種暠、欒巴牧民之良干，龐參、虞詡將帥之宏規，王龔、張皓虛心以推士，張綱、杜喬直道以糾違，郎顗陰陽詳密，張衡機術特妙：東京之士，於茲盛焉。
entries.en: Fan Ying answered the call; Li Gu, Zhou Ju, Zuo Xiong, Huang Qiong, Huan Yan, Yang Hou, Cui Yuan, Ma Rong, Wu You, Su Zhang, Chong Hao, Luan Ba, Pang Shen, Yu Xu, Wang Gong, Zhang Hao, Zhang Gang, Du Qiao, Lang Yi, and Zhang Heng—statesmen, generals, and scientists—made the eastern capital bloom.
entries.literal: Thus even Ying could catch the wind, and the talented all served—such as the deep and broad counsel of Li Gu and Zhou Ju, the upright administration of Zuo Xiong and Huang Qiong, Huan Yan and Yang Hou advancing by Confucian learning, Cui Yuan and Ma Rong displaying literary brilliance, Wu You, Su Zhang, Chong Hao, and Luan Ba as fine tools for shepherding the people, Pang Shen and Yu Xu as grand models for generals, Wang Gong and Zhang Hao with open mind recommending scholars, Zhang Gang and Du Qiao with straight path correcting violations, Lang Yi detailed in yin-yang, Zhang Heng uniquely subtle in devices and arts: the scholars of eastern capital flourished here.

entries.zh: 向使廟堂納其高謀，強*
entries.en: Had high policy taken their counsel, and on every contested
entries.literal: If the court had accepted their high plans, and on the hard-fought

entries.en: (battle)
entries.literal: (battle)

entries.zh: **[埸]*宣其智力，帷幄容其謇辭，舉厝稟其成式，則武、宣之軌，豈其遠而？
entries.en: frontier, generals had matched wit to force, while the inner court heard blunt truth and the throne followed their models—the glory of Emperors Wu and Xuan would lie within reach.
entries.literal: [frontier] field commanders had deployed their wit and strength, if the inner tent had welcomed blunt counsel and every decision had followed their proven models—would the age of Wu and Xuan be far away?

entries.zh: [三]詩云：「靡不有初，鮮克有終。」
entries.en: [3] The Odes say, 'Few can finish what they begin.'
entries.literal: [3] The Poetry says: "There is none without a beginning; few can keep the end."

entries.zh: 可為恨哉！
entries.en: A lasting regret!
entries.literal: It can be counted a regret!

entries.zh: 及孝桓之時，碩德繼興，[四]陳蕃、楊秉處稱賢宰，皇甫、張、段出號名將，王暢、李膺彌縫袞闕，[五]朱穆、劉陶獻替匡時，郭有道□鑒人倫，陳仲弓弘道下邑。
entries.en: Under Emperor Huan came Chen Fan, Yang Bing, Huangfu Song, Zhang Huan, Duan Jiong, Wang Chang, Li Ying, Zhu Mu, Liu Tao, Guo Tai, and Chen Shi—statesmen who shored up the throne.
entries.literal: By the time of Emperor Huan, great virtue arose in succession, [4] Chen Fan and Yang Bing at court were called worthy chancellors, Huangfu, Zhang, and Duan abroad were famed generals, Wang Chang and Li Ying patched the emperor's robe, [5] Zhu Mu and Liu Tao offered counsel to correct the age, Guo Tai [lacuna] mirrored human relations, Chen Zhong expanded the Way in a lowly county.

entries.zh: 其餘宏儒遠智，高心絜行，激揚風流者，不可勝言。
entries.en: Other great scholars and pure men are too many to list.
entries.literal: The rest—great Confucians and far-seeing men, high in mind and pure in conduct, who stirred the currents—cannot all be told.

entries.zh: 而斯道莫振，文武陵隊，在朝者以正議嬰戮，謝事者以黨錮致□。
entries.en: Yet the way withered: courtiers died for speaking truth; retirees were caught in faction bans.
entries.literal: Yet this way did not flourish; civil and military fell in ranks; those at court met slaughter for upright counsel; those who retired met proscription from faction.

entries.zh: 往車雖折，而來軫方遒。
entries.en: The front axle snapped, but the rear wheels still thundered.
entries.literal: The forward carriage though broken, yet the coming axle-boxes are still strong.

entries.zh: [六] 所以傾而未顛，決而未潰，豈非仁人君子心力之為乎？
entries.en: [6] The dynasty leaned yet stood, cracked yet held—thanks to humane men who braced it.
entries.literal: [6] That therefore it leaned yet did not topple, burst yet did not collapse—is it not the work of the hearts and strength of humane gentlemen?

entries.zh: 嗚呼！
entries.en: What a pity it is to say so.
entries.literal: Ah—!

entries.zh: 注[一]尚書大傳曰「古者諸侯之於天子，三年一貢士。
entries.en: Note one: "the Shangshu dazhuan says regional lords presented one candidate every three years.
entries.literal: Note [1] The Great Tradition on the Documents says: "In antiquity the feudal lords toward the Son of Heaven, once in three years presented one scholar.

entries.zh: 一適謂之好德，再適謂之賢賢，三適謂之有功。
entries.en: The first acceptable tribute was 'loves virtue,' the second 'honors worthies,' the third 'has merit.'
entries.literal: One meeting was called 'loving virtue,' a second meeting 'honoring the worthy,' a third meeting 'having merit.'

entries.zh: 有功者，天子賜以車服弓矢，號曰命。
entries.en: Meritorious lords received chariot dress, bow and arrows, and a formal mandate.
entries.literal: Those with merit—the Son of Heaven bestowed chariot robes, bows and arrows, and called it a mandate.

entries.zh: 諸侯有不貢士謂之不率正，一不適謂之過，再不適謂之傲，三不適謂之誣。
entries.en: Lords who sent no talent were 'not rectifying'; one miss was a fault, two arrogance, three deceit.
entries.literal: Feudal lords who did not present scholars were called 'not leading correctly'; one failure was called 'fault,' a second 'arrogance,' a third 'deceit.'

entries.zh: 誣者，天子絀之，一絀以爵，再絀以地，三絀而爵地畢」也。
entries.en: After three failures the throne stripped rank, then land, then both.'
entries.literal: The deceitful—the Son of Heaven degraded them: first degradation by rank, second by land, third and rank and land were exhausted."

entries.zh: 左雄字伯豪，南*
entries.en: Zuo Xiong, whose courtesy name was Bohao, came from Nanyang commandery
entries.literal: Zuo Xiong, courtesy name Bohao, was a native of Nanyang

entries.en: (the commandery name)
entries.literal: (commandery)

entries.zh: **[陽]*涅陽人也。
entries.en: specifically of Nieyang.
entries.literal: [Yang]—of Nieyang.

entries.zh: 安帝時，舉孝廉，稍遷冀州刺史。
entries.en: During the reign of Emperor An, he was nominated as filial and incorrupt and rose step by step to the governorship of Ji Province.
entries.literal: Under Emperor An, he was recommended as filial and incorrupt, and was gradually promoted to Governor of Ji Province.

entries.zh: 州部多豪族，好請托，雄常閉門不與交通。
entries.en: The region was full of powerful families who habitually pulled strings; Zuo Xiong routinely kept his gate closed and refused such traffic.
entries.literal: The province abounded in powerful clans who loved to seek favors through connections; Xiong often shut his doors and had no dealings with them.

entries.zh: 奏案貪猾二千石，無所回忌。
entries.en: He impeached and prosecuted venal and evasive prefects and commandery governors, showing neither hesitation nor favor.
entries.literal: He memorialized to investigate corrupt and slippery two-thousand-dan officials, without any turning back or scruple.

entries.zh: 左原者，陳留人也。
entries.en: Zuo Yuan came from Chenliu.
entries.literal: Zuo Yuan was a man of Chenliu.

entries.zh: 爲郡學生，犯法見斥。
entries.en: A student in the commandery academy, he broke the rules and was expelled.
entries.literal: He was a student of the commandery school; he violated the law and was dismissed.

entries.zh: 林宗甞遇諸路，爲設酒肴以慰之。
entries.en: Guo Tai met him on the road once and laid out food and wine to comfort him.
entries.literal: Linzong once met him on the road and for him set out wine and dishes to console him.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「昔顏涿聚梁甫之巨盜，段干木晉國之大駔，卒爲齊之忠臣，魏之名賢。
entries.en: He told him: "Yan Zhuoju was a notorious brigand on Mount Liangfu; Duan Ganmu was Jin's leading broker—yet one became a loyal minister of Qi, the other a paragon in Wei.
entries.literal: He said to him: "In former times Yan Zhuoju was a great bandit of Liangfu, Duan Ganmu a great broker of Jin; in the end they became a loyal minister of Qi and a celebrated worthy of Wei.

entries.zh: 〈《呂氏春秋》曰：「顏涿聚，梁父大盜也，學於孔子。」
entries.en: 〈(The Lüshi Chunqiu calls Yan Zhuoju a Liangfu outlaw who became Confucius's pupil."
entries.literal: 〈(The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Yan Zhuoju was a great bandit of Liangfu who studied with Confucius."

entries.zh: 《左傳》曰：「晉伐齊，戰于黎丘，齊師敗績，親禽顏庚。」
entries.en: The Zuo Zhuan records Jin's campaign against Qi at Liqiu—a rout, with Yan Geng taken alive."
entries.literal: The Zuo Zhuan says: "Jin attacked Qi and fought at Liqiu; the Qi army was routed, and [the Jin commander] personally captured Yan Geng."

entries.zh: 杜預注曰：「黎丘，隰也。
entries.en: Du Yu identifies Liqiu with Xi.
entries.literal: Du Yu's commentary says: "Liqiu is Xi.

entries.zh: 顏庚，齊大夫顏涿聚也。」
entries.en: Yan Geng is Qi minister Yan Zhuoju."
entries.literal: Yan Geng was the Qi grandee Yan Zhuoju."

entries.zh: 又曰：「晉荀瑤伐鄭，鄭駟弘請救於齊。
entries.en: Elsewhere: when Xun Yao of Jin attacked Zheng, Si Hong of Zheng begged Qi for help.
entries.literal: It also says: "Jin's Xun Yao attacked Zheng; Zheng's Si Hong requested aid from Qi.

entries.zh: 齊師將興，陳成子屬孤子，三日朝，設乘車兩馬，繫五邑焉。
entries.en: As Qi mobilized, Chen Chengzi mustered the war orphans: three days of court, chariots and pairs of horses, five towns pledged to the cause.
entries.literal: When the Qi army was about to march, Chen Chengzi assigned orphans; for three days they held court, setting out two-horse chariots and attaching five settlements.

entries.zh: 召顏涿聚之子晉，曰：『隰之役，而父死焉，以國之多難，未汝恤也。
entries.en: He called in Yan Jin, son of Yan Zhuoju: 『Your father fell at Xi; the realm was in such turmoil we never properly honored his sacrifice.
entries.literal: He summoned Yan Zhuoju's son Jin, saying: 『In the Xi campaign your father died there; because the state had many difficulties, we did not show you condolence.

entries.zh: 今君命汝以是邑也，服車而朝，無廢前勞。』」
entries.en: Now your lord invests you with this town—ride to court and do not dishonor your father's service.』
entries.literal: Now the lord commands you with regard to this settlement—attend court in your chariot; do not neglect your predecessor's labor.』

entries.zh: 《呂氏春秋》曰：「段干木，晉國之駔。」
entries.en: "The Lüshi Chunqiu adds: Duan Ganmu was Jin's market broker."
entries.literal: "The Lüshi Chunqiu says: "Duan Ganmu was a broker of Jin."

entries.zh: 《說文》曰：「駔，會也。
entries.en: The Shuowen defines zang as "agent" or "go-between.
entries.literal: The Shuowen says: "zang means broker.

entries.zh: 謂合兩家之賣買，如今之度巿也。」
entries.en: It denotes the middleman who brings buyer and seller together, as in a licensed market today."
entries.literal: It means joining the selling and buying of two parties, like today's market brokers."

entries.zh: 《新序》曰「魏文侯過段干木之閭而軾之，遂致祿百萬，而時往問之。
entries.en: The Xin Xu tells how Marquis Wen of Wei bowed from his chariot at Duan Ganmu's lane, granted him a vast stipend, and called on him often.
entries.literal: The Xin Xu says "Marquis Wen of Wei, passing Duan Ganmu's lane, leaned on his chariot rail; thereupon he sent him a salary of a million and from time to time went to inquire of him.

entries.zh: 國人皆喜，相與誦之曰：『吾君好正，段干木之敬；
entries.en: The capital sang: 『Our lord loves uprightness—see how he honors Duan Ganmu;
entries.literal: The people of the state all rejoiced and together recited: 『Our lord loves rectitude—Duan Ganmu's reverence;

entries.zh: 吾君好忠，段干木之隆。』
entries.en: our lord loves loyalty—see how he exalts Duan Ganmu.』
entries.literal: our lord loves loyalty—Duan Ganmu's eminence.』

entries.zh: 秦欲攻魏，司馬唐諫曰：『段干木賢者也，而魏禮之，天下莫不聞，無乃不可加兵乎？』
entries.en: When Qin planned to strike Wei, Sima Tang objected: "Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with ceremony—the whole world has heard of it; is it not perhaps impermissible to apply arms?"
entries.literal: Qin wished to attack Wei; Sima Tang remonstrated, saying: 『Duan Ganmu is a worthy man, and Wei treats him with ceremony—the whole world has heard of it—is it perhaps not fitting to refrain from applying arms?』

entries.zh: 秦君以爲然」也。
entries.en: The Qin ruler agreed."
entries.literal: The ruler of Qin deemed it so"—that is the sense.

entries.zh: 駔音子朗反。〉
entries.en: (Gloss: zang, reading zi-lang.)〉
entries.literal: zang is pronounced with the zi-lang fanqie.)〉

entries.zh: 蘧瑗、顏回尚不能無過，況其餘乎？
entries.en: Even Qu Boyu and Yan Hui slipped sometimes—what mortal does not?
entries.literal: Qu Boyu and Yan Hui still could not be without fault—how much more the rest?

entries.zh: 〈《論語》曰：「蘧伯玉使人於孔子，問之曰：『夫子何爲？』
entries.en: 〈(The Analects: Qu Boyu sent a man to Confucius, who asked him, 『What has the Master been doing?』
entries.literal: 〈(The Analects says: "Qu Boyu sent someone to Confucius, who asked him: 『What is the Master doing?』

entries.zh: 對曰：『夫子欲寡其過而未能也。』」
entries.en: The answer: 『He is trying to have fewer faults—and still cannot manage it."』
entries.literal: He replied: 『The Master wishes to lessen his faults but has not yet been able.』

entries.zh: 又曰：「顏回好學，不貳過。」〉
entries.en: "And Yan Hui "never made the same mistake twice.")〉
entries.literal: "It also says: "Yan Hui loved learning and did not repeat a fault.")〉

entries.zh: 慎勿恚恨，責躬而已。」
entries.en: Do not nurse bitterness—look to your own conduct."
entries.literal: Be careful not to harbor resentment; blame only yourself."

entries.zh: 原納其言而去。
entries.en: Zuo Yuan took the advice and left.
entries.literal: Yuan accepted his words and departed.

entries.zh: 或有譏林宗不絕惡人者。
entries.en: Some faulted Guo Tai for not shunning wrongdoers outright.
entries.literal: Some criticized Linzong for not cutting off evil men.

entries.zh: 對曰：「人而不仁，疾之以甚，亂也。」
entries.en: He answered: "If a person is not humane, to hate him to excess is to bring disorder."
entries.literal: He replied: "For a person who lacks humaneness, to hate him excessively is to bring disorder."

entries.zh: 〈《論語》孔子之言也。
entries.en: 〈(A line from Confucius in the Analects.)
entries.literal: 〈(These are the words of Confucius in the Analects.

entries.zh: 鄭玄注云：「不仁之人，當以風化之。
entries.en: Zheng Xuan glosses the passage: "the unworthy ought to be reformed by example and teaching, not crushed.
entries.literal: Zheng Xuan's commentary states: "As for a person who lacks humaneness, he should be transformed by moral influence.

entries.zh: 若疾之以甚，是益使爲亂也。」〉
entries.en: To pursue him with bitter hatred only drives him further into rebellion.")〉
entries.literal: If you hate him excessively, this only makes him turn all the more to disorder.")〉

entries.zh: 原後忽更懷忿，結客欲報諸生。
entries.en: Zuo Yuan later nursed a fresh grudge and recruited bravos to settle scores with the school.
entries.literal: Later Yuan suddenly harbored resentment again; he gathered retainers intending to take revenge on the students.

entries.zh: 其日林宗在學，原愧負前言，因遂罷去。
