entries.en: When all-powerful Qin first carved its realm, dominance sprang from Qi and Yong; wealth and population swelled until conquest unified the land—yet cruelty like Jie's invited revolt.
entries.literal: In the days of mighty Qin, when first they opened the frontiers, hegemony rose from Qi and Yong; the state grew rich and its people multiplied, until at last they annexed all—Jie-like cruelty bred rebellion.

entries.zh: 天命有圣，托之大汉。
entries.en: Heaven ordained a sage-king and entrusted the mandate to great Han.
entries.literal: Heaven mandated a sage and entrusted the mandate to the great Han.

entries.zh: 大汉开基，高祖有勋。
entries.en: Han laid its foundations through the merit of the Supreme Founder.
entries.literal: The great Han opened its foundation; the Supreme Founder earned merit.

entries.zh: 斩白蛇，屯黑云，聚五星于东井，提干将而呵暴秦。
entries.en: He cut the white serpent, drew black clouds about him, watched five planets gather over the Eastern Well, seized the storied sword Ganjiang, and roared down the cruelty of Qin.
entries.literal: He slew the white serpent, massed black clouds, gathered the five planets above the Eastern Well, grasped the Ganjiang sword and shouted down brutal Qin.

entries.zh: 蹈沧海，跨昆仑，奋彗光，扫项军，遂济人难，荡涤于泗、沂。
entries.en: He strode to the eastern sea, vaulted Kunlun, flashed like a comet across Xiang Yu's armies, lifted the people from disaster, and rinsed the Si and Yi clean of slaughter.
entries.literal: He trod the eastern seas, crossed Kunlun, brandished comet-like light, swept away Xiang Yu's host, rescued the people from calamity, and cleansed the Si and Yi rivers.

entries.zh: 刘敬建策，初都长安。
entries.en: Liu Jing shaped the strategy, and the capital was first settled at Chang'an.
entries.literal: Liu Jing framed the plan; first they fixed the capital at Chang'an.

entries.zh: 太宗承流，守之以文。
entries.en: Emperor Wen inherited that tide of fortune and sustained it with humane government.
entries.literal: The August Ancestor inherited that flow and guarded it through civil virtue.

entries.zh: 躬履节俭，侧身行仁，食不二味，衣无异采。
entries.en: He lived plainly, bent his person to kindness, took only one dish per meal, and wore undyed cloth without pattern.
entries.literal: Personally he practiced thrift, humbled himself to enact benevolence, ate no second flavor at a meal, and wore no varied colors.

entries.zh: 赈人以农桑，率下以约已，曼丽之容不悦于目，郑、卫之声不过于耳，佞邪之臣不列于朝，巧伪之物不鬻于市，故能理升平而刑几措。
entries.en: He fed the people through tillage and silk, taught restraint by example; painted faces did not delight his eyes, the tunes of Zheng and Wei did not reach his ears, flatterers held no seat at court and shoddy wares no stall in the market—so peace ascended and punishments nearly vanished.
entries.literal: He relieved the people through farming and sericulture, led those below by restraining himself; lavish beauty did not please his eyes, the sounds of Zheng and Wei did not reach his ears, fawning ministers gained no place at court, crafty goods were not sold in the market—therefore he could achieve rising peace and nearly abolish punishments.

entries.zh: 富衍于孝、景，功传于后嗣。
entries.en: Prosperity spilled into the reigns of Xiaowen and Xiaojing; their achievement flowed to succeeding generations.
entries.literal: Wealth overflowed under Emperors Xiao and Jing; merit passed to later heirs.

entries.zh: 于赫我祖，显于殷国。
entries.en: Great our forebear, famed throughout Yin.
entries.literal: Ah, glorious our ancestor, shining in the Yin realm.

entries.zh: 二迹阿衡，克光其则。
entries.en: Twin pillars like Yi Yin—shining through his standard.
entries.literal: Twofold like Yi Yin—able to brighten his norm.

entries.zh: 武丁兴商，伊宗皇士。
entries.en: King Wuding lifted Shang anew; Yi lineage ministers became the royal limbs.
entries.literal: Wuding revived Shang; ministers of the Yi clan stood as royal pillars.

entries.zh: 爰作股肱，万邦是纪。
entries.en: They served as arms and legs; every state fell under their rule.
entries.literal: Thus they became thighs and arms; myriad regions took their measure from them.

entries.zh: 毅以显宗求贤不笃，士多隐处，故作《七激》以为讽。
entries.en: Fu Yi felt Emperor Ming courted talent too timidly and scholars stayed hidden, so he wrote 《Seven Exhortations》 to needle the throne.
entries.literal: Yi believed Emperor Ming did not seek worthies earnestly enough and many scholars hid away; therefore he composed 《Seven Exhortations》 as remonstrance.

entries.zh: 建初中，肃宗博召文学之士，以毅为兰台令史，拜郎中，与班固、贾逵共典校书。
entries.en: Midway through Jianchu, Emperor Zhang called literati widely—named Fu Yi to the Orchid Terrace, made him a gentleman, and paired him with Ban Gu and Jia Kui to collate the canon.
entries.literal: In mid-Jianchu Emperor Zhang broadly summoned literary men: he appointed Yi Orchid Terrace clerk, promoted him to gentleman, and had him collate texts with Ban Gu and Jia Kui.

entries.zh: 毅追美李明皇帝功德最盛，而庙颂未立，乃依《清庙》作《显宗颂》十篇奏之，由是文雅显于朝廷。
entries.en: Fu Yi argued that Emperor Ming's deeds topped every predecessor yet lacked a temple hymn, so he echoed 《Qing Temple Ode》 in ten 《Hymns for Emperor Ming》; afterward his style dominated court letters.
entries.literal: Yi praised Emperor Ming's virtue and merit as supreme, yet no temple hymn stood; accordingly he modeled 《Qing Temple Ode》 and presented ten chapters of 《Hymns for Emperor Ming》, after which his prose graced the court.

entries.zh: 刘毅，北海敬王子也。
entries.en: Liu Yi belonged to Prince Jing of Beihai’s house.
entries.literal: Liu Yi was a son of Prince Jing of Beihai.

entries.zh: 初封平望侯，永元中，坐事夺爵。
entries.en: He began as Marquis of Pingwang but Yongyuan stripped him for a crime.
entries.literal: First enfeoffed Marquis of Pingwang; in Yongyuan stripped of the fief for an offense.

entries.zh: 毅少有文辩称。
entries.en: Even young he was known for rhetorical skill.
entries.literal: Yi from youth was famed for literary eloquence.

entries.zh: 元初元年，上《汉德论》并《宪论》十二篇。
entries.en: Yuanchu 1 saw him submit twelve chapters titled 《Discourse on Han Virtue》 and 《Discourse on the Charter》.
entries.literal: First Yuanchu year he presented 《Discourse on Han Virtue》 and 《Discourse on the Charter》—twelve chapters.

entries.zh: 时，刘珍、邓耽、尹兑、马融共上书称其美，安帝嘉之，赐钱三万，拜议郎。
entries.en: Liu Zhen, Deng Dan, Yin Dui, and Ma Rong praised him in a joint memorial; Emperor An gave thirty thousand cash and made him a counselor.
entries.literal: At the time Liu Zhen, Deng Dan, Yin Dui, and Ma Rong jointly memorialized praising him; Emperor An commended him, granted thirty thousand cash, and appointed Counselor.

entries.zh: 李尤字伯仁，广汉雒人也。
entries.en: Li You, called Boren, came from Luo in Guanghan.
entries.literal: Li You, courtesy name Boren, was a native of Luo in Guanghan.

entries.zh: 少以文章显。
entries.en: He won notice young on the strength of his prose.
entries.literal: In youth he rose to fame through writing.

entries.zh: 和帝时，侍中贾逵荐尤有相如、杨雄之风，召诣东观，受诏作赋，拜兰台令史。
entries.en: Emperor He’s attendant Jia Kui likened him to Sima Xiangru and Yang Xiong; summoned to the Eastern Lodge for commissioned fu, he became Orchid Terrace clerk.
entries.literal: Under Emperor He, Palace Attendant Jia Kui recommended You as having the manner of Xiangru and Yang Xiong; summoned to the Eastern Lodge, ordered to compose fu, appointed Orchid Terrace clerk.

entries.zh: 稍迁，安帝时为谏议大夫，受诏与谒者仆射刘珍等俱撰《汉记》。
entries.en: Promoted stepwise, he served Emperor An as remonstrance counselor and joined Herald chief Liu Zhen to compile 《Han Records》.
entries.literal: Gradually promoted; under Emperor An he was remonstrance counselor; ordered with Herald Superintendent Liu Zhen and others to compile 《Han Records》.

entries.zh: 后帝废太子为济阴王，尤上书谏争。
entries.en: When the heir was demoted to prince of Jiyin, Li You protested in writing.
entries.literal: Later the emperor demoted the heir apparent to Prince of Jiyin; You submitted a memorial remonstrating.

entries.zh: 顺帝立，迁乐安相。
entries.en: Emperor Shun raised him to Le’an chancellor.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun ascended, promoted to Chancellor of Le’an.

entries.zh: 年八十三卒。
entries.en: He died at eighty-three.
entries.literal: Died at eighty-three.

entries.zh: 所著诗、赋、铭、诔、颂、《七叹》、《哀典》，凡二十八篇。
entries.en: He left twenty-eight works: verse, fu, inscriptions, laments, songs, 《Seven Laments》, and 《Canon of Lament》.
entries.literal: His writings: poems, fu, inscriptions, dirges, hymns, 《Seven Laments》, 《Canon of Lament》—twenty-eight pieces.

entries.zh: 所著赋、颂、铭、诔、箴、吊、论、《九咨》、《七言》，凡十五篇。
entries.en: He left fifteen works: fu, songs, stele texts, laments, warnings, elegies, essays, 《Nine Consultations》, and 《Seven-Character Lines》.
entries.literal: His writings include fu, hymns, inscriptions, dirges, admonitions, condolences, treatises, 《Nine Consultations》, and 《Seven-Character Lines》—fifteen pieces.

entries.zh: 刘珍字秋孙，一名宝，南阳蔡阳人也。
entries.en: Liu Zhen, style Qiusun and also named Bao, came from Caiyang in Nanyang.
entries.literal: Liu Zhen, style Qiusun and also named Bao, was a man of Caiyang in Nanyang.

entries.zh: 少好学。
entries.en: He loved learning from youth.
entries.literal: In youth he loved learning.

entries.zh: 永初中，为谒者仆射。
entries.en: During Yongchu he became supervisor of court gentlemen for consultation.
entries.literal: During the Yongchu period, he became supervisor of court gentlemen for consultation.

entries.zh: 邓太后诏，使与校书刘騊駼、马融及《五经》博士，校定东观五经、诸子传记、百家艺术，整齐脱误，是正文字。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Deng ordered him, with the collators Liu Taotu and Ma Rong and the erudites of the Five Classics, to work in the Eastern Lodge collating the Five Classics, masters, biographies, and technical writings of the hundred schools, putting omissions and errors in order and correcting the text.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Deng ordered him, together with the collators Liu Taotu and Ma Rong and the erudites of the Five Classics, to collate and settle in the Eastern Lodge the Five Classics, masters, biographies, and the arts and techniques of the hundred schools, arranging omissions and errors and correcting the written text.

entries.zh: 永宁元年，太后又诏珍与騊駼作建武已来名臣传，迁侍中、越骑校尉。
entries.en: In Yongning 1, the empress dowager again ordered Zhen and Taotu to compile Biographies of Famous Ministers Since Jianwu. He was promoted to palace attendant and colonel of the Yue cavalry.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongning, the empress dowager again ordered Zhen and Taotu to compose Biographies of Famous Ministers Since Jianwu; he was promoted to palace attendant and colonel of the Yue cavalry.

entries.zh: 延光四年，拜宗正。
entries.en: In Yanguang 4 he was appointed minister of the imperial clan.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yanguang, he was appointed minister of the imperial clan.

entries.zh: 明年，转卫尉，卒官。
entries.en: The next year he was transferred to chamberlain for the palace garrison and died in office.
entries.literal: The next year he was transferred to chamberlain for the palace garrison, and he died in office.

entries.zh: 著诔、颂、连珠凡七篇。
entries.en: He wrote seven pieces in all: laments, hymns, and linked pearls.
entries.literal: He wrote seven pieces in all: laments, hymns, and linked pearls.

entries.zh: 又撰《释名》三十篇，以辩万物之称号云。
entries.en: He also composed the thirty-chapter Explaining Names, distinguishing the names and designations of things.
entries.literal: He also composed thirty chapters of Explaining Names, to distinguish the names and designations of all things.

entries.zh: 葛龚字元甫，梁国宁陵人也。
entries.en: Ge Gong, style Yuanfu, came from Ningling in the kingdom of Liang.
entries.literal: Ge Gong, style Yuanfu, was a man of Ningling in the kingdom of Liang.

entries.zh: 赦赦外戚，华宠煌煌。
entries.en: Splendid are the imperial in-laws—glory dazzling the court.
entries.literal: Illustrious, illustrious the imperial in-laws—splendor blazing bright.

entries.zh: 昔在帝舜，德隆英、皇。
entries.en: Emperor Shun’s virtue shone through his Ying and Huang consorts.
entries.literal: Anciently under Emperor Shun virtue rose through Ying and Huang.

entries.zh: 周兴三母，有莘崇汤。
entries.en: The Zhou house leaned on three royal mothers; Youxin ladies lifted Tang.
entries.literal: Zhou rose through three mothers; Youxin honored Tang.

entries.zh: 宣王晏起，姜后脱簪。
entries.en: King Xuan of Zhou lingered in bed until Queen Jiang pulled her pins.
entries.literal: King Xuan of Zhou slept late; Jiang the queen removed her hairpins.

entries.zh: 齐桓好乐，卫姬不音。
entries.en: Duke Huan of Qi craved song—Lady Wei of Wei withheld her zither.
entries.literal: Duke Huan of Qi loved music; Lady Wei of Wei gave no tunes.

entries.zh: 皆辅主以礼，扶君以仁，达才进善，以义济身。
entries.en: Each aided her lord with ritual, steadied him with kindness, lifted worthy men, and walked by righteousness.
entries.literal: All aided their lords by ritual, supported them by benevolence, advanced talent and goodness, and aided themselves by righteousness.

entries.zh: 琦以言不从，失意，复作《白鹄赋》以为风。
entries.en: Ignored by Liang Ji, Cui Qi wrote 《White Swan Fu》 to needle him obliquely.
entries.literal: Because his advice went unheeded Qi grew despondent and composed 《White Swan Fu》 as indirect criticism.

entries.zh: 梁冀见之，呼琦问曰：“百官外内，各有司存，天下云云，岂独吾人之尤，君何激刺之过乎！
entries.en: Liang Ji called him in: everyone has an office; gossip runs everywhere—why blame only us? Why cut so deep with satire!
entries.literal: Liang Ji read it and summoned Qi, demanding: 'Court and capital each has its duties; murmurs fill the realm—is my house alone to blame? Why stab so viciously at me!'

entries.zh: 琦对曰：“昔管仲相齐，乐闻机谏之言；
entries.en: Cui Qi answered: Guan Zhong serving Qi thirsted for delicate warnings.
entries.literal: Qi replied: 'Anciently Guan Zhong served Qi and loved to hear subtle remonstrance.'

entries.zh: 萧何佐汉，乃设书过之吏。
entries.en: Xiao He serving Han assigned clerks to write down missteps.
entries.literal: 'Xiao He aided Han and even posted clerks to record faults.'

entries.zh: 今将军累世台辅，任齐伊、公，而德政未闻，黎元涂炭。
entries.en: You have been the dynasty's backbone for generations—weight like Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou—yet no humane rule appears and the people burn in misery.
entries.literal: 'Today you, general, have filled generation after generation as pillar minister—your burden rivals Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou—yet worthy rule is unheard and the common folk lie charred in ruin.'

entries.zh: 不能结纳贞良，以救祸败，反复欲钳塞士口，杜蔽主听，将使玄黄改色，马鹿易形乎？
entries.en: You neither recruit good men to stop collapse nor open your ears—you would gag every tongue until truth inverts like swapping horse for deer?
entries.literal: 'Unable to gather upright men to stem disaster, you would gag scholars and deafen the sovereign—do you mean to swap black for yellow and turn horses into deer?'

entries.zh: 冀无以对，因遣琦归。
entries.en: Liang Ji had nothing to say and dismissed him.
entries.literal: Ji could not answer and sent Qi away.

entries.zh: 漢自武帝頗好方術，天下懷協道藝之士，莫不負策抵掌，順風而屆焉。
entries.en: Under the Han, once Emperor Wu took a strong interest in esoteric techniques, every adept who hoarded a trick or two shouldered his satchel and hurried to court, eager to catch the imperial breeze.
entries.literal: From the Han, since Emperor Wu was quite fond of occult arts, every scholar in the realm who hugged secret skills to his breast came with satchel under arm and palms clapped in eagerness, riding the wind to present himself.

entries.zh: 後王莽矯用符命，及光武尤信讖言，士之赴趣時宜者，皆騁馳穿鑿，爭談之也。
entries.en: Wang Mang then twisted the chenwei oracles to his ends, and Emperor Guangwu believed the apocrypha with unusual fervor, so opportunists raced to wrench texts into shape and outdid one another in expounding them.
entries.literal: Later Wang Mang falsely employed token prophecies, and Guangwu in turn trusted apocryphal pronouncements exceedingly; gentlemen who rushed to suit the temper of the age all galloped off, drilling holes and forcing meanings, vying to discourse on them.

entries.zh: 故王梁、孫咸，名應圖籙，越登槐鼎之任；
entries.en: So Wang Liang and Sun Xian, whose names matched prophetic slips, vaulted into the highest ministerial seats overnight;
entries.literal: Therefore Wang Liang and Sun Xian, their names answering to charts and registers, leapt straight into the rank of the Three Dukes;

entries.zh: 鄭興、賈逵，以附同稱顯；
entries.en: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui climbed to prominence by swimming with the tide;
entries.literal: Zheng Xing and Jia Kui, by going along with the trend, won renown;

entries.zh: 恆譚、尹敏，以乖忤淪敗。
entries.en: Huan Tan and Yin Min were ruined because they stood athwart it.
entries.literal: Huan Tan and Yin Min, by opposing it, sank into ruin.

entries.zh: 自是習為內學，尚奇文，貴異數，不乏於時矣。
entries.en: After that the fashion was to call them 'inner classics,' to dote on bizarre writings and rare numerologies, and the age never lacked for either.
entries.literal: From this it became habitual to treat these as 'inner learning,' to prize strange texts and esteem uncanny reckonings, and they were never wanting in that age.

entries.zh: 是以通儒碩生，忿其奸妄不經，奏議慷慨，以為宜見藏擯。
entries.en: Learned men, furious at the fraud and want of canonical grounding, petitioned in blunt anger that the lot be locked away and cast aside.
entries.literal: Therefore thorough Confucians and eminent scholars, resenting their deceitful falsehood and lack of classical warrant, submitted memorials in high indignation, holding that such things ought to be shelved and rejected.

entries.zh: 子長亦云：「觀陰陽之書，使人拘而多忌。」
entries.en: Zi Chang also said, 'Reading the books of yin and yang makes one cramped and full of taboos.'
entries.literal: Zi Chang also said, 'Reading the books of yin and yang makes one cramped and full of taboos.'

entries.zh: 蓋為此也。
entries.en: He had this very abuse in mind.
entries.literal: —it was broadly for this reason.

entries.zh: 光武即位，求天下有道之人，乃徵憲拜博士。
entries.en: When Guangwu took the throne he searched the realm for men of the Way and summoned Xian as Erudite.
entries.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he sought men of the Way throughout the realm and thereupon summoned Xian, appointing him Erudite.

entries.zh: 再遷，建武七年，代張堪為光祿勳。
entries.en: Promoted again, in Jianwu 7 he succeeded Zhang Kan as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.
entries.literal: After further promotions, in the seventh year of Jianwu he replaced Zhang Kan as Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

entries.zh: 從駕南郊。
entries.en: He attended the emperor at the southern suburban rite.
entries.literal: He accompanied the imperial carriage to the southern suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 憲在位，忽迴向東北，含酒三潠。
entries.en: At his post Xian suddenly faced northeast and spat wine three times.
entries.literal: Xian was in his place when he suddenly turned toward the northeast and spat wine three times.

entries.zh: 執法奏為不敬。
entries.en: Ritual officers reported him for disrespect.
entries.literal: The law officers memorialized that this was disrespectful.

entries.zh: 詔問其故。
entries.en: The emperor ordered an inquiry into the cause.
entries.literal: An edict asked the reason.

entries.zh: 憲對曰：「齊國失火，故以此厭之。」
entries.en: Xian answered, "There is a fire in Qi; I am doing this to avert the disaster."
entries.literal: Xian replied, "There is a fire in Qi, so I am using this to avert it."

entries.zh: 後齊果上火災，與郊同日。
entries.en: Later Qi indeed reported a fire—on the very day of the suburban rite.
entries.literal: Later Qi indeed reported a fire disaster on the same day as the suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 八年，車駕西征隗囂。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Jianwu the emperor marched west against Wei Xiao.
entries.literal: In the eighth year the imperial carriage marched west against Wei Xiao.

entries.zh: 憲諫曰：「天下初定，車駕未可以動。」
entries.en: Xian remonstrated, saying, 'The realm has only just been settled; the imperial carriage ought not to move.'
entries.literal: Xian remonstrated, saying, 'The realm has only just been settled; the imperial carriage ought not to move.'

entries.zh: 憲乃當車拔佩刀以斷車靷。
entries.en: He planted himself before the team, drew his belt knife, and cut the traces.
entries.literal: Xian then stood blocking the chariot, drew his girdle knife, and severed the traces.

entries.zh: 帝不從，遂上隴。
entries.en: The emperor ignored him and climbed Long Mountain.
entries.literal: The emperor did not follow him and ascended Long.

entries.zh: 其後潁川兵起，乃回駕而還。
entries.en: When Yingchuan rose in revolt he had to wheel about and ride back.
entries.literal: Later, when troops rose in Yingchuan, he turned the carriage and returned.

entries.zh: 帝歎曰：「恨不用子橫之言。」
entries.en: The emperor sighed, saying, 'I regret I did not use Ziheng's words.'
entries.literal: The emperor sighed, saying, 'I regret I did not use Ziheng's words.'

entries.zh: 時，匈奴數犯塞，帝患之，乃召百僚廷議。
entries.en: As the Xiongnu kept raiding the passes, he called a full court to debate a response.
entries.literal: At that time the Xiongnu repeatedly raided the frontier, and the emperor worried over it and summoned the hundred officials to deliberate in court.

entries.zh: 憲以為天下疲敝，不宜動眾。
entries.en: Guo Xian argued the country was too spent for another campaign.
entries.literal: Xian held that the realm was exhausted and that it was not fitting to move the hosts.

entries.zh: 諫爭不合，乃伏地稱眩瞀，不復言。
entries.en: When he lost the argument he dropped flat, feigned vertigo, and fell silent.
entries.literal: His remonstrance did not prevail, so he lay prostrate claiming dizziness and blurred vision and spoke no more.

entries.zh: 帝令兩郎扶下殿，憲亦不拜。
entries.en: Two attendants were told to haul him off the dais, yet he refused even a curt bow.
entries.literal: The emperor ordered two gentlemen to help him down from the hall, yet Xian did not bow.

entries.zh: 帝曰：「常聞『關東觥觥郭子橫』，竟不虛也。」
entries.en: The emperor remarked, 'They say east of the pass Guo Ziheng fears nothing—true enough.'
entries.literal: The emperor said, 'I have often heard “East of the Pass Guo Ziheng stands fearless”—it was indeed no empty praise.'

entries.zh: 憲遂以病辭退，卒於家。
entries.en: Guo Xian then retired citing illness and died at home.
entries.literal: Xian thereupon resigned on grounds of illness and died at home.

entries.zh: 高獲字敬公，汝南新息人也。
entries.en: Gao Huo, styled Jinggong, came from Xinxi in Runan.
entries.literal: Gao Huo, courtesy name Jinggong, was a native of Xinxi in Runan.

entries.zh: 為人尼首方面。
entries.en: He was built like a man with a sloping forehead and a square jaw.
entries.literal: In person he had a receding crown and a square face.

entries.zh: 少游學京師，與光武有舊。
entries.en: As a young scholar in the capital he had known Emperor Guangwu long before.
entries.literal: In his youth he traveled to study in the capital and had old ties with Guangwu.

entries.zh: 師事司徒歐陽歙。
entries.en: He studied under Ouyang Xi, the minister over the masses.
entries.literal: He took Minister over the Masses Ouyang Xi as his teacher.

entries.zh: 歙下獄當斷，獲冠鐵冠，帶鈇鑕，詣闕請歙。
entries.en: When Ouyang Xi was jailed and sentenced to die, Gao Huo put on an iron cap, buckled on the felon's axe and fetters, and pleaded at the palace gate.
entries.literal: When Xi was cast into prison and faced execution, Huo donned an iron cap, girded on axe and fetter, and went to the palace gate to beg for Xi.

entries.zh: 帝雖不赦，而引見之。
entries.en: The emperor refused the pardon but still granted him an audience.
entries.literal: Although the emperor did not grant a pardon, he nonetheless summoned and received him.

entries.zh: 謂曰：「敬公，朕欲用子為吏，宜改常性。」
entries.en: He told him, 'Jinggong, I mean to give you office; you must mend your stubborn ways.'
entries.literal: He said to him, 'Jinggong, I wish to employ you as an official—you ought to change your usual disposition.'

entries.zh: 獲對曰：「臣受性於父母，不可改之於陛下。」
entries.en: Gao Huo answered, 'What my parents gave me in temperament no edict can reshape.'
entries.literal: Huo replied, 'Your servant received his nature from his parents; it cannot be altered before Your Majesty.'

entries.zh: 出便辭去。
entries.en: He bowed out and left without looking back.
entries.literal: He went out and at once took his leave.

entries.zh: 臣聞堯登稷、契，政隆太平；
entries.en: Your servant has heard that when Yao raised Ji and Xie, peace spread across the realm;
entries.literal: Your servant has heard that when Yao elevated Ji and Xie, government flourished into great peace;

entries.zh: 舜用皋陶，政致雍熙、殷、周雖有高宗、昌、發之君，猶賴傅說、呂望之策，故能克崇其業，允協大中。
entries.en: Shun used Gao Yao and harmony followed. Yin and Zhou boasted kings like Gaozong, Wen, and Wu, yet even they leaned on Fu Yue and Lü Wang—only thus could they magnify their work and hit the great mean.
entries.literal: Shun employed Gao Yao and government reached perfect harmony; although Yin and Zhou had sovereigns such as Gaozong, Chang, and Fa, they still relied on the plans of Fu Yue and Lü Wang, and therefore were able to exalt their enterprises and truly accord with the great mean.

entries.zh: 竊見鉅鹿太守會稽謝夷吾，出自東州，厥土塗泥，而英姿挺特，奇偉秀出。
entries.en: Your servant has watched Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he springs from the eastern mudflats, his mien is heroic, his talent towering.
entries.literal: Your servant has privately observed Julu Governor Xie Yiwu of Kuaiji: though he comes from the eastern regions where the soil is mud and mire, his heroic bearing stands apart, strange and grand, outstanding among his peers.

entries.zh: 才兼四科，行包九德，仁足濟時，知周萬物。
entries.en: He unites the four classes of talent, walks the nine virtues, has benevolence enough to save the times, and knowledge wide as creation.
entries.literal: His talents combine the four categories of worthies; his conduct embraces the nine virtues; his benevolence suffices to succor the age; his knowledge encircles the myriad things.

entries.zh: 加以少膺儒雅，韜含六籍，推考星度，綜校圖錄，探賾聖秘，觀變曆徵，佔天知地，與神合契，據其道德，以經王務。
entries.en: Trained in the classics, he stores the Six Books, tracks the constellations, collates apocrypha, probes the sages' arcana, reads omens in the calendar, knows heaven and earth, moves in tune with the gods, and steers statecraft by virtue.
entries.literal: Add to this that in youth he received Confucian refinement, harbored the Six Classics within, pushed the reckoning of the stars, collated charts and registers, plumbed the sage's secrets, observed change and examined portents, divined heaven and knew earth, matched spirits in covenant, and grounded royal business in his moral power.

entries.zh: 昔為陪隸，與臣從事，奮忠毅之操，躬史魚之節，董臣嚴綱，勗臣懦弱，得以免戾，實賴厥勳。
entries.en: When he served under me, he displayed loyal resolve and the integrity of Shi Yu. He tightened my lax discipline, strengthened my weak resolve, and kept me from fault; I truly owe that to his merit.
entries.literal: Formerly, when he was a menial attendant serving with your servant, he displayed loyal and resolute conduct and personally embodied the integrity of Shi Yu, tightened your servant's slack discipline, and stiffened your servant's timidity, so that your servant escaped blame—truly we rely on his merit.

entries.zh: 及其應選作宰，惠敷百里，降福彌異，流化若神，爰牧荊州，威行邦國。
entries.en: As magistrate his grace soaked a hundred li, blessings fell strangely, his teaching seemed divine; as Jing inspector his majesty ran the whole province.
entries.literal: When afterward he answered selection and became a magistrate, his kindness spread over a hundred li, blessings descended in singular ways, and his transforming influence was like a spirit's; when he shepherded Jing province, his awesomeness ran through the regional states.

entries.zh: 奉法作政，有周、召之風；
entries.en: His government has the Duke of Zhou's discipline and the Duke of Shao's clarity;
entries.literal: Upholding law and conducting government, he has the air of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao;

entries.zh: 居儉履約，紹公儀之操。
entries.en: living spare and keeping faith, he matches Gongyi Xiu.
entries.literal: dwelling in frugality and keeping faith with restraint, he continues the conduct of Gongyi Xiu.

entries.zh: 尋功簡能，為外臺之表；
entries.en: In weighing merit and talent he is the outer court's paragon;
entries.literal: Seeking merit and sorting ability, he is a model for the outer terraces;

entries.zh: 聽聲察實，為九伯之冠。
entries.en: in testing rumor against fact he leads the nine regional inspectors.
entries.literal: listening to reputations and inspecting realities, he is chief among the nine shepherds.

entries.zh: 遷守鉅鹿，政合時雍。
entries.en: As Julu governor his rule matched the season of harmony.
entries.literal: Transferred to guard Julu, his government harmonized with the timely peace.

entries.zh: 德量績謀，有伊、呂、管、晏之任；
entries.en: In moral breadth and policy depth he rivals Yi Yin, Lü Wang, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying;
entries.literal: In virtuous capacity, accumulated plans, he bears the charge of Yi Yin, Lü Wang, Guan Zhong, and Yan Ying;

entries.zh: 闡弘道奧，同史蘇、京房之倫。
entries.en: in opening the Way's depths he ranks with Shi Su and Jing Fang.
entries.literal: expounding the profound of the Way, he is of the same class as Shi Su and Jing Fang.

entries.zh: 雖密勿在公，而身出心隱，不殉名以求譽，不馳鶩以要寵，念存遜遁，演志箕山。
entries.en: Though he slaves for the state, his mind stays hidden; he trades neither fame nor favor for ambition, and his heart already wanders toward Mount Ji's reclusion.
entries.literal: Although he toils incessantly for the public good, his body is in office while his heart withdraws; he does not sell his name to seek praise, nor gallop after favor; his thoughts incline to yielding retirement, his ambition unfolds toward Mount Ji.

entries.zh: 方之古賢，實有倫序；
entries.en: Set beside the ancients he holds his rank;
entries.literal: Compared with the worthies of antiquity, he truly has his proper ordering;

entries.zh: 采之於今，超焉絕俗。
entries.en: measured against our own age he stands clean above the crowd.
entries.literal: gathered from among men of today, he towers alone beyond vulgar custom.

entries.zh: 誠社稷之元龜，大漢之棟甍。
entries.en: He is the tortoise-oracle of the state, the roof-tree of Han.
entries.literal: He is truly the great tortoise-shell of the altars of soil and grain, the ridge-beam of the great Han.

entries.zh: 宜當拔擢，使登鼎司。
entries.en: He should be lifted into the three highest seats.
entries.literal: It is fitting that he be promoted and caused to ascend to the ministerial trio.

entries.zh: 上令三辰順軌於歷象，下使五品咸訓於嘉時，必致休徵克昌之慶，非徒循法奉職而已。
entries.en: Above he would set sun, moon, and stars to their tracks; below he would school the five ranks in a golden age—more than a dutiful clerk, he would summon the omens of a golden peace.
entries.literal: Above he would make the three luminaries run true to the calendar's reckonings; below he would bring the five grades all instructed in a propitious season—surely he would bring about the felicity of auspicious omens and flourishing prosperity, not merely follow the law and hold to office.

entries.zh: 臣以頑駑，器非其疇，屍祿負乘，夕惕若厲。
entries.en: Your servant is a dull nag, unfit for the yoke, fat on unearned pay and riding above his station, and quakes each night like a man on a cliff.
entries.literal: Your servant, dull and worn-out, is not the vessel for such a charge; he occupies salary beyond his worth and rides above his capacity, and trembles nightly as if on the brink.

entries.zh: 願乞骸骨，更授夷吾，上以光七曜之明，下以厭率土之望，庶令微臣塞咎免悔。
entries.en: Let me yield my bones and yield the post to Yiwu—above to light the seven governors, below to quiet the empire—so this fool may dodge blame and regret.
entries.literal: I beg to surrender my bones and in turn appoint Yiwu—above to brighten the seven luminaries, below to satisfy the hopes of all within the seas—so that perhaps your humble servant may block fault and escape regret.

entries.zh: 仲尼稱《易》有君子之道四焉，曰「卜筮者尚其占」。
entries.en: Confucius said that the Changes has four aspects of the way of the superior man, and among them he said, 'Those who divine by tortoise shell and milfoil esteem its prognostications.'
entries.literal: Confucius said that the Changes has four aspects of the way of the superior man, and among them he said, 'Those who divine by tortoise shell and milfoil esteem its prognostications.'

entries.zh: 佔也者，先王所以定禍福，決嫌疑，幽贊於神明，遂知來物者也。
entries.en: Divination was how the ancient kings fixed fortune against misfortune, cut through uncertainty, drew hidden aid from the gods, and so discerned what lay ahead.
entries.literal: As for divination, it is what the former kings used to settle blessing and calamity, resolve what is doubtful, secretly assist the spirits and bright powers, and thereby know what is to come.

entries.zh: 若夫陰陽推步之學，往往見於墳記矣。
entries.en: The yin-yang arts and astronomical computation already turn up again and again in those old grave records.
entries.literal: As for the learning of yin and yang and calendrical reckoning, it is often seen already in old tomb inscriptions.

entries.zh: 然神經怪牒、玉策金繩，關扃於明靈之府、封縢於瑤壇之上者，靡得而窺也。
entries.en: The spirit texts and marvel registers, the jade slips bound with golden cord, locked away in the courts of the numinous and sealed on high altars, remain beyond anyone's sight.
entries.literal: Yet spirit scriptures and strange documents, jade tablets and golden cords, barred and bolted in the halls of the luminous spirits, sealed with vermilion lacquer upon the jade altar—none may spy them.

entries.zh: 至乃《河》、《洛》之文，龜龍之圖，箕子之術，師曠之書，緯候之部，鈐決之符，皆所以探抽冥賾、參驗人區，時有可聞者焉。
entries.en: Then there are the River and Luo documents, the tortoise-and-dragon diagrams, Jizi's methods, Shi Kuang's writings, apocryphal weft-books, and talismanic slips—all tools to sound the hidden depths and test them against the human world, and occasionally something credible surfaces.
entries.literal: As for the writings of the Yellow River and the Luo, the charts of the tortoise and dragon, the arts of Jizi, the books of Shi Kuang, the categories of weft prognostications, and the tally-slips of secret decisions—all are means to plumb the dark profundities and cross-check the human realm, and from time to time something of them may be heard.

entries.zh: 其流又有風角、遁甲、七政、元氣、六日七分、逢佔、日者、挺專、須臾、孤虛之術，乃望雲省氣，推處祥妖，時亦有以效於事也。
entries.en: The tradition also spawned wind-angle, Dunjia, the seven governors, original breath, six-day-seven-part reckoning, encounter divination, day-selectors, the ting-zhuan and shunyu methods, orphan-and-void calculation—ways of reading the sky and qi to trace good or ill omens—and sometimes they really seemed to work.
entries.literal: In its wake there are further such arts as wind-angle, hidden stems, the seven luminaries, primordial qi, six days and seven parts, chance divination, day-masters, the bamboo slip method, momentary reckoning, and orphan-and-void calculations—by which men scan the clouds and read vapors, inferring auspicious portents and uncanny signs—and at times they have proved effective in affairs.

entries.zh: 而斯道隱遠，玄奧難原，故聖人不語怪神，罕言性命。
entries.en: But the way runs dark and far off, too abstruse to pin down, which is why the sage kept silent about ghosts and marvels and seldom spoke of fate or human nature.
entries.literal: Yet this path is hidden and remote, profound and hard to trace to its source; therefore the sage did not speak of prodigies and spirits, and rarely discussed nature and destiny.

entries.zh: 或開末而抑其端，或曲辭以章其義，所謂「民可使由之，不可使知之」。
entries.en: Some opened the branch ends while restraining the root, others used tortuous wording to display the meaning—what is called 'The people may be made to follow it, but may not be made to understand it.'
entries.literal: Some opened the branch ends while restraining the root, others used tortuous wording to display the meaning—what is called 'The people may be made to follow it, but may not be made to understand it.'

entries.zh: 靈帝時，大將軍何進薦扶，徵拜侍中，甚見器重。
entries.en: Emperor Ling's regent He Jin recommended him; summoned as palace attendant, he won deep favor.
entries.literal: Under Emperor Ling, Grand General He Jin recommended Fu; he was summoned and appointed palace attendant and was greatly valued.

entries.zh: 扶私謂太常劉焉曰：「京師將亂，益州分野有天子氣。」
entries.en: Privately he told Minister Liu Yan, "The capital will soon convulse; the Yizhou sky sector carries the qi of an emperor."
entries.literal: Fu privately said to Minister Liu Yan, "The capital is about to fall into chaos; in the field division of Yi province there is the aura of a Son of Heaven."

entries.zh: 焉信之，遂求出为益州牧，扶亦为蜀郡属国都尉，相与入蜀。
entries.en: Yan believed him, begged a posting as Yi provincial shepherd, and entered Shu with Fu, who became commandant of Shu's dependent state.
entries.literal: Yan believed it, and therefore sought appointment as shepherd of Yi province; Fu also became commandant of the dependent state attached to Shu commandery, and together they entered Shu.

entries.zh: 去後一歲，帝崩，天下大亂，乃去官還家。
entries.en: A year after they departed the emperor died and the empire collapsed, so Fu resigned and went home.
entries.literal: One year after they left, the emperor died and the realm fell into great chaos, and therefore he left office and returned home.

entries.zh: 年八十二卒。
entries.en: He died at eighty-two.
entries.literal: He died at age eighty-two.

entries.zh: 唐檀字子产，豫章南昌人也。
entries.en: Tang Tan, styled Zichan, came from Nanchang in Yuzhang.
entries.literal: Tang Tan, courtesy name Zichan, was a man of Nanchang in Yuzhang commandery.

entries.zh: 少游太学，习《京氏易》、《韩诗》、《颜氏春秋》，尤好灾异星占。
entries.en: As a young man he attended the Imperial Academy, mastering the Jing Yi, the Han Poetry, and Yan's Spring and Autumn Annals, with a particular passion for omens, prodigies, and astrology.
entries.literal: In his youth he studied at the Imperial Academy, learning the Jing family's Changes, the Han Poetry, and the Yan clan's Spring and Autumn Annals, and he was especially fond of portents, anomalies, and stellar divination.

entries.zh: 后还乡里，教授常百余人。
entries.en: He later went home and taught, often keeping well over a hundred students.
entries.literal: Later he returned to his home region and regularly had more than a hundred pupils whom he instructed.

entries.zh: 《易》稱「遯之時義大矣哉」。
entries.en: The Book of Changes says, "In the hour of Withdrawal, the meaning of timing is vast indeed."
entries.literal: The Changes states, "The timely significance of the hexagram Dun (Withdrawal) is great indeed."

entries.zh: 又曰：“不事王侯，高尚其事。”
entries.en: It adds, "They will not wait on lords and princes; they exalt their own calling instead."
entries.literal: It also says, "They do not serve kings and marquises; they make lofty their own undertakings."

entries.zh: 是以尧称则天，不屈颍阳之高；
entries.en: So Yao could mirror Heaven and still leave the recluses of Yingyang untroubled in their height;
entries.literal: Therefore Yao was said to pattern himself on Heaven, yet he did not bend the height of those at Yingyang;

entries.zh: 武尽美矣，终全孤竹之洁。
entries.en: King Wu won perfect renown, yet he still spared the stainless recluses of Mount Guzhu.
entries.literal: King Wu was utterly admirable, yet in the end he preserved the purity of those of Guzhu.

entries.zh: 自兹以降，风流弥繁，长往之轨未殊，而感致之数匪一。
entries.en: Afterward the tradition only spread: the path of withdrawal stayed one, but the motives that led men to it multiplied.
entries.literal: From this time downward, the current of such conduct grew ever richer; the track of those who went far away was not different, yet the ways they were moved and brought to it were not one.

entries.zh: 或隐居以求其志，或回避以全其道，或静已以镇其躁，或去危以图其安，或垢俗以动其概，或疵物以激其清。
entries.en: Some hid to pursue a purpose; some fled to keep the Way intact; some stilled themselves against inner hurry; some quit peril for safety; some smeared themselves in the mire to steel their honor; some scorned the world to sharpen their cleanness.
entries.literal: Some concealed themselves in order to seek their aims; some withdrew in order to preserve their Way; some quieted themselves to still their restlessness; some left danger to plan their safety; some befouled themselves amid vulgarity to rouse their integrity; some faulted things to quicken their purity.

entries.zh: 然观其甘心畎亩之中，憔悴江海之上，岂必亲鱼鸟、乐林草哉！
entries.en: Yet see them content in plowed fields, worn thin along the rivers—surely it was not only love of birds, fish, and wild growth!
entries.literal: Yet observe how they were willing to remain in the furrows of the fields, haggard upon the rivers and seas—was it surely that they had to fondle fish and birds and delight in woods and grass!

entries.zh: 亦云性分所至而已。
entries.en: They were simply following the grain of their own natures, nothing more.
entries.literal: One may also say it reached what their nature and allotment decreed, that is all.

entries.zh: 故蒙耻之宾，屡黜不去其国；
entries.en: Thus men who swallowed humiliation might be cast out again and again yet never quit their homeland;
entries.literal: Therefore guests who bore shame were repeatedly dismissed yet did not leave their states;

entries.zh: 蹈海之节，千乘莫移其情。
entries.en: while others who chose the sea's integrity could not be moved by the offer of a thousand chariots.
entries.literal: those who trod the integrity of leaping into the sea—no state of a thousand chariots could shift their resolve.

entries.zh: 适使矫易去就，则不能相为矣。
entries.en: Had you forced them to swap places, none could have stood in another's stead.
entries.literal: Had they been forced to twist their choices of staying or going, they could not have acted for one another.

entries.zh: 彼虽硁硁有类沽名者，然而蝉蜕嚣埃之中，自致寰区之外，异夫饰智巧以逐浮利者乎！
entries.en: A few may look stiff-necked, almost like fame-hunters, yet they shed the world's racket and walk outside its borders—far from the clever types angling for hollow gain.
entries.literal: Though they may seem rigidly narrow, resembling reputation-mongers, yet they slough off the clamor of dust and place themselves beyond the realm—how different from those who polish cleverness to chase floating profit!

entries.zh: 荀卿有言曰，“志意修则骄富贵，道义重则轻王公”也。
entries.en: Xunzi said, "Refine your intent and you scorn riches and rank; weight your conduct with the Way and you think little of kings and princes."
entries.literal: Xun Qing had a saying: "When one's aims and thoughts are cultivated, one is proud toward wealth and honor; when the Way and righteousness weigh heavily, one is light toward kings and dukes."

entries.zh: 汉室中微，王莽篡位，士之蕴藉义愤甚矣。
entries.en: Mid-Han faltered, Wang Mang seized the throne, and every scholar's breast burned with loyal rage.
entries.literal: The house of Han waned in its middle period; Wang Mang usurped the throne, and gentlemen of learning nursed righteous indignation to an extreme degree.

entries.zh: 是时裂冠毁冕，相携持而去之者，盖不可胜数。
entries.en: Then came the wave who rent their caps and crowns and marched away together—no reckoning could count them.
entries.literal: At that time those who tore caps and shattered coronets and, hand in hand, departed could not be counted.

entries.zh: 杨雄曰：“鸿飞冥冥，弋者何篡焉。”
entries.en: Yang Xiong wrote, "The wild goose vanishes into the gloom—what can the fowler's string catch?"
entries.literal: Yang Xiong said, "The swan flies into the dark depths; what can the archer's string snare?"

entries.zh: 言其违患之远也。
entries.en: —meaning how far they flew from harm.
entries.literal: This speaks of how far they kept from calamity.

entries.zh: 光武侧席幽人，求之若不及，旌帛蒲车之所征贲，相望于岩中矣。
entries.en: Guangwu turned his mat for hidden men and hunted them as if always a step behind—silk summons and rush-wheeled coaches thickly threaded the cliffs.
entries.literal: Emperor Guangwu set aside a seat for recluses and sought them as if he could not catch up; the silken banners and rush-wheeled coaches that summoned and honored them were visible one after another in the mountain valleys.

entries.zh: 若薛方、逢萌，聘而不肯至；
entries.en: Xue Fang and Feng Meng were called but would not appear;
entries.literal: Such men as Xue Fang and Feng Meng were summoned yet were unwilling to come;

entries.zh: 严光、周党、王霸，至而不能屈。
entries.en: Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, and Wang Ba came yet could not be bowed.
entries.literal: Yan Guang, Zhou Dang, and Wang Ba came yet could not be bent.

entries.zh: 群方咸遂，志士怀仁，斯固所谓“举逸民天下归心”者乎！
entries.en: Each found his path, and high-minded men kept faith with humaneness—was this not the "raise the recluses and all hearts incline" of the Analects?
entries.literal: The many regions all had their fulfillment; men of high purpose cherished humaneness—was this not indeed what is called "Raise up withdrawn men and the realm will turn its heart to you"?

entries.zh: 肃宗亦礼郑均而征高凤，以成其节。
entries.en: Emperor Zhang likewise honored Zheng Jun and summoned Gao Feng to crown their resolve.
entries.literal: Emperor Su also honored Zheng Jun with ritual and summoned Gao Feng, thereby completing their integrity.

entries.zh: 自后帝德稍衰，邪孽当朝，处子耿介，羞与卿相等列，至乃抗愤而不顾，多失其中行焉。
entries.en: Later the throne's virtue thinned, vicious favorites ruled the hall, and hermits—too proud to sit among ministers—sometimes flamed into defiance and lost the golden mean.
entries.literal: Afterward imperial virtue gradually declined; evil favorites held the court, gentlemen-recluses stood stiffly aloof, ashamed to rank with ministers and grandees, until some flared in defiance and recklessly missed the middle course.

entries.zh: 盖录其绝尘不反，同夫作者，列之此篇。
entries.en: Here I record those who shook off the dust and never looked back—true authors of their own lives—and set them in this scroll.
entries.literal: Therefore I record those who cut off the dust and never returned, peers of the makers of texts, and array them in this chapter.

entries.zh: 博士范升奏毁党曰：“臣闻尧不须许由、巢父，而建号天下；
entries.en: Erudite Fan Sheng attacked him: "Yao needed neither Xu You nor Chao Father to rule the world;
entries.literal: Erudite Fan Sheng memorialized to attack Dang, saying, "Your servant has heard that Yao did not need Xu You and Chao Fu yet established his title over the realm;

entries.zh: 周不待伯夷、叔齐，而王道以成。
entries.en: Zhou needed neither Bo Yi nor Shu Qi to perfect the royal Way.
entries.literal: Zhou did not wait for Bo Yi and Shu Qi, yet the kingly Way was thereby accomplished.

entries.zh: 伏见太原周党、东海王良、山阳王成等，蒙受厚恩，使者三聘，乃肯就车。
entries.en: Yet Taiyuan's Zhou Dang, Donghai's Wang Liang, and Shanyang's Wang Cheng soaked up imperial grace and only mounted the coach after three embassies.
entries.literal: Your servant has seen Taiyuan's Zhou Dang, Donghai's Wang Liang, Shanyang's Wang Cheng, and others who received deep favor—only after envoys thrice summoned them were they willing to mount the carriage.

entries.zh: 及陛见帝廷，党不以礼屈，伏而不谒，偃蹇骄悍，同时俱逝。
entries.en: At court they sprawled without bowing—proud, rude, and gone together.
entries.literal: When they ascended the hall to be granted audience at the imperial court, Dang did not yield in ritual, lay prostrate and did not perform the obeisance, were arrogant and fierce, and at the same time all departed.

entries.zh: 党等文不能演义，武不能死君，钓采华名，庶几三公之位。
entries.en: They wield neither brush nor blade for the throne—only angle for empty fame and dream of the three excellencies.
entries.literal: Dang and the others in letters could not unfold doctrine; in arms they could not die for their lord; they angle for a flowery name, hoping perchance for the rank of the three dukes.

entries.zh: 臣愿与坐云台之下，考试图国之道。
entries.en: Let me sit them beneath the Cloud Terrace and test their statecraft.
entries.literal: Your servant wishes to sit with them beneath the Cloud Terrace and examine them on the arts of ordering the state.

entries.zh: 不如臣言，伏虚妄之罪。
entries.en: If I lie, I accept the charge of slander.
entries.literal: If they are not as your servant says, let them suffer the crime of empty falsehood.

entries.zh: 而敢私窃虚名，夸上求高，皆大不敬。”
entries.en: Privately trading on hollow renown to dazzle the throne is grave disrespect."
entries.literal: Yet daring privately to steal empty reputation, boasting to the ruler to seek height—all is great irreverence."

entries.zh: 书奏，天子以示公卿。
entries.en: The emperor circulated Fan's memorial among the high ministers.
entries.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Son of Heaven showed it to the dukes and ministers.

entries.zh: 诏曰：“自古明王圣主，必有不宾之士。
entries.en: The edict read, "Every wise king has guests who refuse to bend.
entries.literal: An edict stated, "From antiquity enlightened kings and sage lords have surely had guests who would not submit.

entries.zh: 伯夷、叔齐不食周粟，太原周党不受朕禄，亦各有志焉。
entries.en: Bo Yi and Shu Qi spurned Zhou grain; Taiyuan's Zhou Dang spurns our stipend—each follows his star.
entries.literal: Bo Yi and Shu Qi would not eat Zhou grain; Taiyuan's Zhou Dang will not accept Our salary—each has his resolve.

entries.zh: 其赐帛四十匹。”
entries.en: Gift him forty bolts of silk."
entries.literal: We grant him forty bolts of silk."

entries.zh: 党遂隐居黾池，著书上下篇而终。
entries.en: Zhou Dang hid at Mianchi, wrote a two-part book, and died.
entries.literal: Dang thereupon concealed himself at Mianchi, wrote a book in upper and lower fascicles, and ended.

entries.zh: 邑人贤而祠之。
entries.en: His townsfolk judged him worthy and built him a shrine.
entries.literal: The people of his town thought him worthy and sacrificed to him.

entries.zh: 野王二老者，不知何许人也。
entries.en: No one knows where the two elders of Yewang came from.
entries.literal: The two old men of Yewang—no one knows what place they were from.

entries.zh: 初，光武贰于更始，会关中扰乱，遣前将军邓禹西征，送之于道。
entries.en: When Guangwu still hedged toward Gengshi and Guanzhong boiled, he sent Forward General Deng Yu west and escorted him along the road.
entries.literal: In the beginning, when Guangwu was of two minds toward Emperor Gengshi, there happened turmoil in the Guanzhong region; he dispatched Forward General Deng Yu on a western expedition and saw him off along the road.

entries.zh: 既反，因于野王猎，路见二老者即禽。
entries.en: On the return hunt at Yewang he met two greybeards about to shoot game.
entries.literal: Having turned back, he therefore hunted at Yewang on the way and, on the road, saw two old men about to take game.

entries.zh: 光武问曰：“禽何向？”
entries.en: Guangwu asked, "Which way lies the quarry?"
entries.literal: Guangwu asked, saying, "In what direction is the game?"

entries.zh: 并举手西指，言“此中多虎，臣每即禽，虎亦即臣，大王勿往也。”
entries.en: Both pointed west: "Tigers swarm there—we hunt them, they hunt us—do not ride that way, great king."
entries.literal: Together they raised their hands and pointed west, saying, "In here there are many tigers; we each time take game, and the tigers also each time take us—great king, do not go there."

entries.zh: 光武曰：“苟有其备，虎亦何患。”
entries.en: Guangwu said, "With proper precautions, what fear of tigers?"
entries.literal: Guangwu said, "If one has preparations for it, what worry have tigers?"

entries.zh: 父曰：“何大王之谬邪！
entries.en: The elder answered, "How wrong you are, great king!
entries.literal: The elder said, "How mistaken is the great king!

entries.zh: 昔汤即桀于鸣条，而大城于亳；
entries.en: Tang seized Jie at Mingtiao, then raised mighty ramparts at Bo;
entries.literal: In antiquity Tang took Jie at Mingtiao, yet built a great wall at Bo;

entries.zh: 武王亦即纣于牧野，而大城于郏鄏。
entries.en: King Wu struck Zhou at Muye, then ringed Jiaru with great walls.
entries.literal: King Wu likewise took Zhou at Muye, yet built a great wall at Jiaru.

entries.zh: 彼二王者，其备非不深也。
entries.en: Neither king lacked deep defenses.
entries.literal: Those two kings—their preparations were not shallow.

entries.zh: 是以即人者，人亦即之，虽有其备，庸可忽乎！”
entries.en: He who hunts men is hunted in turn—how can you trust walls alone?"
entries.literal: Therefore those who seize others are also seized by others; though they have preparations, how can they be treated lightly!"

entries.zh: 光武悟其旨，顾左右曰：“此隐者也。”
entries.en: Guangwu understood and murmured to his attendants, "These are hidden sages."
entries.literal: Guangwu grasped their intent, looked to those at his left and right, and said, "These are recluses."

entries.zh: 将用之，辞而去，莫知所在。
entries.en: He moved to retain them, but they slipped away—none traced their path.
entries.literal: He was about to employ them, but they declined and departed; no one knew where they went.

entries.zh: 及光武即位，乃之琅邪劳山，养志修道，人皆化其德。
entries.en: When Guangwu rose, Feng withdrew to Mount Lao in Langye, nursed his purpose, and won every neighbor by his virtue.
entries.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he then went to Mount Lao in Langye, nurtured his aims and cultivated the Way, and people were all transformed by his virtue.

entries.zh: 向长字子平，河内朝歌人也。
entries.en: Xiang Chang, styled Ziping, came from Zhaoge in Henei.
entries.literal: Xiang Chang, courtesy name Ziping, was a man of Zhaoge in Henei.

entries.zh: 隐居不仕，性尚中和，好通《老》、《易》。
entries.en: He lived in reclusion, prized equipoise, and loved plumbing the Laozi and the Changes.
entries.literal: He concealed himself and did not take office; by nature he esteemed centrality and harmony and loved to penetrate the Laozi and the Changes.

entries.zh: 贫无资食，好事者更馈焉，受之取足而反其余。
entries.en: Destitute, he lived on neighbors' gifts—taking only what he needed and sending the rest back.
entries.literal: Poor, without means for food, well-wishers alternately sent gifts; he accepted only enough to suffice and returned the remainder.

entries.zh: 王莽大司空王邑辟之，连年乃至，欲荐之于莽，固辞乃止。
entries.en: Wang Mang's grand minister Wang Yi summoned him; he dragged his feet for years, and when Yi tried to push him at court he refused point-blank.
entries.literal: Grand Minister of Works under Wang Mang, Wang Yi, summoned him; only after successive years did he arrive; Yi wished to recommend him to Mang, but he firmly declined and only then stopped.

entries.zh: 潜隐于家。
entries.en: He sank from sight in his own house.
entries.literal: He hid away at home.

entries.zh: 读《易》至《损》、《益》卦，喟然叹曰：“吾已知富不如贫，贵不如贱，但未知死何如生耳。”
entries.en: At the Sun and Yi hexagrams he sighed, "I know wealth cannot beat poverty nor rank a humble station—but how death stacks against life I cannot tell."
entries.literal: Reading the Changes to the hexagrams Sun and Yi, he sighed with feeling and said, "I already know that wealth is not as good as poverty, honor not as good as low status, but I still do not know how death compares to life."

entries.zh: 建武中，男女娶嫁既毕，敕断家事勿相关，当如我死也。
entries.en: In the Jianwu years, once his children were wed, he commanded the household to treat him as dead and ask nothing of him.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu era, when the marrying of his sons and daughters was finished, he ordered that domestic affairs should no longer concern one another, as if he had died.

entries.zh: 于是遂肆意，与同好北海禽庆俱游五岳名山，竟不知所终。
entries.en: Then he wandered at will with his friend Qin Qing of Beihai across the five sacred peaks until both vanished from record.
entries.literal: Thereupon he followed his whim and, together with his like-minded friend Qin Qing of Beihai, roamed the five marchmounts and famous mountains, and in the end no one knew his final end.

entries.zh: 建武中，征为议郎，以病去职，遂将妻子居黾池。
entries.en: Jianwu brought a summons as remonstrance official; pleading illness he quit and moved his household to Mianchi.
entries.literal: In the Jianwu era he was summoned as remonstrance official; because of illness he left office, and therefore led his wife and children to dwell at Mianchi.

entries.zh: 复被征，不得已，乃着短布单衣，穀皮绡头，待见尚书。
entries.en: Called again, he donned rough cloth, a bark-fiber kerchief, and presented himself to the masters of writing.
entries.literal: He was summoned again; having no choice, he then put on short cloth unlined garments, a husk-silk head-wrap, and waited to see the secretary.

entries.zh: 及光武引见，党伏而不谒，自陈愿守所志，帝乃许焉。
entries.en: Before Guangwu he lay flat and refused the court bow, begging to keep his reclusive vow; the emperor allowed it.
entries.literal: When Guangwu granted him audience, Dang lay prostrate and did not perform the obeisance, stating himself that he wished to keep to his resolve, and the emperor thereupon granted it.

entries.zh: 严光字子陵，一名遵，会稽余姚人也。
entries.en: Yan Guang, styled Ziling—also called Yan Zun—hailed from Yuyao in Kuaiji.
entries.literal: Yan Guang, courtesy name Ziling, also named Zun, was a man of Yuyao in Kuaiji.

entries.zh: 少有高名，与光武同游学。
entries.en: In youth he was already famous and studied abroad with the future Guangwu.
entries.literal: In his youth he had a lofty reputation and roamed-study together with Guangwu.

entries.zh: 及光武即位，乃变名姓，隐身不见。
entries.en: When his friend became emperor, Yan changed his name and vanished from sight.
entries.literal: When Guangwu took the throne, he then changed his name and surname and concealed himself so as not to appear.

entries.zh: 帝思其贤，乃令以物色访之。
entries.en: The emperor missed his virtue and sent agents to hunt him by description.
entries.literal: The emperor thought on his worthiness and therefore ordered him sought by likeness of appearance.

entries.zh: 后齐国上言：“有一男子，披羊裘钓泽中。”
entries.en: Qi commandery later reported a man in sheepskin angling in the reeds.
entries.literal: Later Qi commandery reported upward, "There is one man, draped in sheepskin, fishing in a marsh."

entries.zh: 帝疑其光，乃备安车玄纁，遣使聘之。
entries.en: Guangwu guessed it was Yan Guang and sent a cushioned coach and black silk to fetch him.
entries.literal: The emperor suspected it was Guang and therefore prepared a comfortable carriage and dark silk and dispatched an envoy to summon him.

entries.zh: 三反而后至。
entries.en: The envoy went back and forth three times before he came.
entries.literal: After three returns he then arrived.

entries.zh: 舍于北军。
entries.en: They quartered him in the Northern Army camp.
entries.literal: He lodged at the Northern Army.

entries.zh: 给床褥，太官朝夕进膳。
entries.en: The court gave him a bed and daily meals from the imperial kitchen.
entries.literal: They supplied bedding; morning and evening the grand provisioner advanced meals.

entries.zh: 司徒侯霸与光素旧，遣使奉书。
entries.en: Minister Hou Ba, an old friend, sent a letter by courier.
entries.literal: Minister of Education Hou Ba was of old friendship with Guang and sent a messenger bearing a letter.

entries.zh: 使人因谓光曰：“公闻先生至，区区欲即诣造。
entries.en: The courier said, "His Lordship burns to call on you at once.
entries.literal: The messenger therefore said to Guang, "The lord has heard that the master has arrived; in utmost earnestness he wishes immediately to come pay a visit.

entries.zh: 迫于典司，是以不获。
entries.en: Duty chains him—he cannot slip away.
entries.literal: Pressed by the duties of his office, he therefore cannot obtain it.

entries.zh: 愿因日暮，自屈语言。”
entries.en: He begs the favor of a twilight talk."
entries.literal: He hopes, relying on dusk's falling, humbly to bend himself to converse in words."

entries.zh: 光不答，乃投札与之，口授曰：“君房足下：位至鼎足，甚善。
entries.en: Yan said nothing, tossed Hou a scrap, and dictated: "Junfang, you stand as one leg of the ruling tripod—well done.
entries.literal: Guang did not answer but cast a slip to him and orally dictated, saying, "Sir Junfang, at your feet: your position has reached the tripod's third leg—very good.

entries.zh: 怀仁辅义天下悦，阿谀顺旨要领绝。”
entries.en: Nourish benevolence and aid the right, and the world smiles; flatter power and your throat meets the blade."
entries.literal: Cherish humaneness and assist righteousness and the realm rejoices; flatter and follow orders and your neck will be severed."

entries.zh: 霸得书，封奏之。
entries.en: Hou sealed the note and forwarded it to the throne.
entries.literal: When Ba received the letter, he sealed and memorialized it.

entries.zh: 帝笑曰：“狂奴故态也。”
entries.en: The emperor laughed, "There is the wild friend I remember."
entries.literal: The emperor laughed and said, "The mad servant's old manner."

entries.zh: 车驾即日幸其馆。
entries.en: That day the imperial carriage rolled to his door.
entries.literal: That very day the imperial carriage visited his lodging.

entries.zh: 光卧不起，帝即其卧所，抚光腹曰：“咄咄子陵，不可相助为理邪？”
entries.en: Yan feigned sleep; Guangwu sat on his couch, patted his belly, and said, "Ziling, Ziling—will you not help me rule?"
entries.literal: Guang lay down and did not rise; the emperor came to where he lay, stroked Guang's belly, and said, "Tut-tut, Ziling—can you not assist Us in ordering the realm?"

entries.zh: 光又眠不应，良久，乃张目熟视，曰：“昔唐尧著德，巢父洗耳。
entries.en: Yan kept his eyes shut, then opened them slowly: "When Yao shone with virtue, Chao Father still washed the taint from his ears.
entries.literal: Guang again slept and did not answer; after a long while he then opened his eyes, stared fixedly, and said, "In antiquity Tang Yao displayed virtue, yet Chao Father washed his ears.

entries.zh: 士故有志，何至相迫乎！”
entries.en: A scholar keeps his own star—why hound him!"
entries.literal: Gentlemen therefore have their resolve—how could you press one another!"

entries.zh: 帝曰：“子陵，我竟不能下汝邪？”
entries.en: Guangwu sighed, "So even I cannot bend you?"
entries.literal: The emperor said, "Ziling, am I ultimately unable to make you submit?"

entries.zh: 于是升舆叹息而去。
entries.en: He climbed into his carriage, sighed, and rode away.
entries.literal: Thereupon he mounted the carriage, sighed, and departed.

entries.zh: 仲彦足下：勤处隐约，虽乘云行泥，栖宿不同，每有西风，何尝不叹！
entries.en: Zhongyan, you live hidden while others ride high—whenever the west wind blows I sigh for you.
entries.literal: Sir Zhongyan, at your feet: you diligently dwell in obscurity; though one rides clouds and the other walks mud, roosting and lodging differ—whenever the west wind blows, how could I not sigh!

entries.zh: 盖闻黄、老之言，乘虚入冥，藏身远遁，亦有理国养人，施于为政。
entries.en: Huang-Lao speak of mounting void and hiding far away—yet their teaching can also order states and nurture the people.
entries.literal: I have heard the words of Huang and Lao: mounting emptiness and entering darkness, concealing the body and fleeing far—there is also ordering the state and nurturing the people, applied in governing.

entries.zh: 至如登山绝迹，神不著其证，人不睹其验。
entries.en: But mountaintop exile shows no spirit-sign; no man sees its proof.
entries.literal: As for climbing mountains and cutting off tracks, the spirits do not display their verification, and people do not witness their proof.

entries.zh: 吾欲先生从其可者，于意何如？
entries.en: I urge you to take the workable path—what say you?
entries.literal: I wish the master to follow what is feasible in this—what is your thought?

entries.zh: 昔伊尹不怀道以待尧、舜之君。
entries.en: Yi Yin did not clutch the Way waiting for a Yao or Shun.
entries.literal: In antiquity Yi Yin did not hug his doctrine while waiting for a Yao or Shun lord.

entries.zh: 方今明明，四海开辟，巢、许无为箕山，夷、齐悔入首阳。
entries.en: Today the sage shines and the seas are open—Chao and Xu need not idle on Ji Ridge; Bo and Yi would rue Shouyang.
entries.literal: Now the realm is bright and clear, the four seas opened wide; Chao and Xu need not idle on Mount Ji, Bo and Qi would regret entering Mount Shouyang.

entries.zh: 足下审能骑龙弄凤，翔嬉云间者，亦非狐兔燕雀所敢谋也。
entries.en: If you can ride dragons among the clouds, no fox or sparrow may counsel you.
entries.literal: If you, sir, can truly ride dragons and sport with phoenixes, soaring and playing amid the clouds, that is also not something foxes, hares, swallows, and sparrows would dare to plot.

entries.zh: 秦并六國，其淮、泗夷皆散為民户。
entries.en: Qin's unification broke up the Huai and Si valley Yi; they were absorbed into ordinary registered households.
entries.literal: When Qin annexed the six states, the Huai and Si Yi all dispersed and became common households.

entries.zh: 陳涉起兵，天下崩潰，燕人衛滿避地朝鮮，因王其國。
entries.en: When Chen She's rebellion shattered the empire, Wei Man of Yan took refuge in Korea and founded a kingdom there.
entries.literal: Chen She raised troops; the realm collapsed; the Yan man Wei Man fled to Korea and thereupon became king of that land.

entries.zh: 百有餘歲，武帝滅之，於是東夷始通上京。
entries.en: A century later Emperor Wu extinguished Wei Man's state, and only then did the eastern peoples open formal ties with the imperial court.
entries.literal: After more than a hundred years, Emperor Wu destroyed it; thereupon the eastern Yi first had communication with the capital.

entries.zh: 王莽篡位，貊人寇邊。
entries.en: Wang Mang's usurpation brought Mo tribes down on the border.
entries.literal: Wang Mang usurped the throne; the Mo people raided the frontier.

entries.zh: 建武之初，復來朝貢。
entries.en: Early in Emperor Guangwu's Jianwu reign they resumed tribute missions.
entries.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era, they again came to court with tribute.

entries.zh: 時遼東太守祭肜威讋北方，声行海表，於是濊、貊、倭、韓，萬里朝獻，故章、和已後，使聘流通。
entries.en: Ji Rong of Liaodong cowed the northern tribes until his name carried across the sea; Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han all sent envoys from immense distances, and from the reigns of Emperors Zhang and He onward diplomatic traffic never stopped.
entries.literal: At that time the Liaodong governor Ji Rong awed the north with his might; his reputation reached beyond the seas; thereupon the Hui, Mo, Wa, and Han, from ten thousand li away, came to court with offerings; therefore after Emperors Zhang and He, embassies flowed without cease.

entries.zh: 逮永初多難，始入寇鈔；
entries.en: The troubles of the Yongchu years opened a season of border raids;
entries.literal: When the Yongchu era brought many troubles, they began to enter and raid;

entries.zh: 桓、靈失政，漸滋曼焉。
entries.en: under the feckless Emperors Huan and Ling the problem festered and spread.
entries.literal: under Huan and Ling, government failed, and it gradually grew and spread.

entries.zh: 《王制》云：“東方曰夷。”
entries.en: The "Royal Regulations" records: "To the east they are called the Yi."
entries.literal: The "Royal Regulations" states: "The east is called Yi."

entries.zh: 夷者，柢也，言仁而好生，萬物柢地而出。
entries.en: The gloss reads "Yi" as "root": they are humane and cherish life, and all living things sprout from the soil as from a rootstock.
entries.literal: Yi" means "root"; it speaks of benevolence and cherishing life; the myriad things take root in the ground and come forth.

entries.zh: 故天性柔順，易以道御，至有君子、不死之國焉。
entries.en: Their temperament is therefore mild and tractable, readily guided by moral rule—so much so that tradition speaks of a "land of gentlemen" and even an "undying" realm.
entries.literal: Therefore their nature is gentle and yielding, and they are easy to govern by the Way; there are even lands called the "state of gentlemen" and the "state where none die."

entries.zh: 夷有九種，曰畎夷、於夷、方夷、黄夷、白夷、赤夷、玄夷、風夷、陽夷。
entries.en: The Yi are reckoned in nine branches: the Quan, Yu, Fang, Yellow, White, Red, Black, Wind, and Yang Yi.
entries.literal: There are nine kinds of Yi, named Quan Yi, Yu Yi, Fang Yi, Huang Yi, Bai Yi, Chi Yi, Xuan Yi, Feng Yi, and Yang Yi.

entries.zh: 故孔子欲居九夷也。
entries.en: That is why Confucius said he would gladly go and live among the nine Yi.
entries.literal: Therefore Confucius wished to dwell among the nine Yi.

entries.zh: 三０三八頁五行*
entries.en: Broken line before emperor clause.
entries.literal: Page 3038, line 5: …—lemma opens.

entries.en: Wrong graph for Martial Emperor.
entries.literal: (Huang)

entries.zh: **[武]*帝始用太初丁丑之元*
entries.en: Restores Wu di for Huang.
entries.literal: [Martial] Emperor first employed the Taichu dingchou origin …—lemma opens.

entries.en: Continuative particle.
entries.literal: (you [thereupon])

entries.zh: *六家紛錯據盧文弨腢書拾補校改。
entries.en: Lu fixes the six-calendar confusion.
entries.literal: “six houses disputed”—emended after Lu Wenchao’s Omitted Characters.

entries.zh: 按：宋志作「昔始用太初丁丑之後」。
entries.en: Note: the Song treatise reads “formerly began using Taichu dingchou thereafter.”
entries.literal: Note: the Song treatise reads “formerly began using Taichu dingchou thereafter.”

entries.zh: 御覽一六引作「昔太初始用丁丑之後」。
entries.en: Imperial Readings 16 cites “formerly Taichu first used dingchou thereafter.”
entries.literal: Imperial Readings 16 cites “formerly Taichu first used dingchou thereafter.”

entries.zh: 後漢書志第二 律歷中 賈逵論歷永元論歷延光論歷漢安論歷熹平論歷論月食
entries.en: Treatise Two of the Book of Later Han: Music and Calendars, Part Two — Treatises on Jia Kui's calendar memorials and the debates under Yongyuan, Yanguang, Han'an, and Xiping, together with the discussion of lunar eclipses
entries.literal: Book of Later Han, Treatise Two: Pitch-Pipes and Calendar, Part Two — On Jia Kui Discussing the Calendar, On the Yongyuan Discussion of the Calendar, On the Yanguang Discussion of the Calendar, On the Han'an Discussion of the Calendar, On the Xiping Discussion of the Calendar, On Lunar Eclipses

entries.zh: 光武即位告天 郊 封禅
entries.en: Guangwu’s accession: reporting to Heaven, the suburban rites, and the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai.
entries.literal: Guangwu’s accession: announcement to Heaven; suburban sacrifice; feng and shan.

entries.zh: 建武元年，光武即位于鄗，爲壇營於鄗之陽。
entries.en: In Jianwu 1 (25 CE), Guangwu was enthroned at Hao, where he raised an altar on the sunny slope south of the town.
entries.literal: In the first year of Jianwu, Guangwu took the throne at Hao and built an altar enclosure on the south side of Hao.

entries.zh: 祭告天地，采用元始中郊祭故事。
entries.en: He reported his accession to Heaven and Earth, following the suburban-sacrifice precedents of the Yuanshi period (1–5 CE).
entries.literal: He sacrificed and announced to Heaven and Earth, adopting the precedent of the suburban sacrifices in the Yuanshi era.

entries.zh: 六宗羣神皆從，未以祖配。
entries.en: The Six Honored Powers and the full pantheon were included, but no imperial ancestor was yet paired at the high altar.
entries.literal: The Six Ancestors and the host of spirits all attended; he had not yet matched the Ancestor.

entries.zh: 天地共犢，餘牲尚約。
entries.en: Heaven and Earth received a single calf between them; other offerings were still kept comparatively modest.
entries.literal: Heaven and Earth shared one calf; the remaining victims still tended toward simplicity.

entries.zh: 其文曰：「皇天上帝，后土神祇，睠顧降命，屬秀黎元，爲民父母，秀不敢當。
entries.en: The prayer read: “August Heaven and High God, Sovereign Earth and the spirits—you have looked down and issued your mandate, setting Xiu over the common people as their parent; Xiu dares not presume to accept such a burden.
entries.literal: The text said: “August Heaven, Supreme Lord; Sovereign Earth, numinous powers—you have turned your gaze and sent down the charge, entrusting Xiu to the black-haired people as father and mother to the folk; Xiu does not dare accept this.

entries.zh: 羣下百僚，不謀同辭。
entries.en: Every minister below, without having plotted together beforehand, spoke as one.
entries.literal: The host of officials below, without prior counsel, spoke with one voice.

entries.zh: 咸曰王莽篡弑竊位，秀發憤興義兵，破王邑百萬眾於昆陽，誅王郎、銅馬、赤眉、青犢賊，平定天下，海内蒙恩，上當天心，下爲元元所歸。
entries.en: They declared that Wang Mang had seized the throne by murder and usurpation; that Xiu, roused to action, had raised a loyal army, shattered Wang Yi’s host of a million at Kunyang, put down Wang Lang and the Bronze Horse, Red Eyebrows, and Green Calf rebels, restored peace to the realm, and won the gratitude of every shore—that Heaven above approved him and the people below rallied to him.
entries.literal: They all said: Wang Mang usurped and murdered and stole the throne; Xiu, stirred by indignation, raised righteous troops, broke Wang Yi’s million men at Kunyang, executed Wang Lang and the Bronze Horse, Red Eyebrows, and Green Calf bandits, pacified all under Heaven, and within the seas the people received grace; above he matches Heaven’s mind, below he is what the common folk turn to.

entries.zh: 讖記曰：『劉秀發兵捕不道，卯金修德爲天子。』
entries.en: The apocrypha ran: “Liu Xiu takes up arms against the wicked; the Liu house, refining its virtue, is destined for the throne.”
entries.literal: A prophecy text said: “Liu Xiu raises troops to seize the lawless; the metal of Mao cultivates virtue and becomes Son of Heaven.”

entries.zh: 秀猶固辭，至於再，至於三。
entries.en: Yet Xiu still refused—once, twice, and yet again.
entries.literal: Xiu still firmly declined, to a second time, to a third time.

entries.zh: 羣下曰：『皇天大命，不可稽留。』
entries.en: His officers replied: “Heaven’s great mandate brooks no delay.”
entries.literal: The host below said: “The great charge of August Heaven cannot be delayed.”

entries.zh: 敢不敬承！」
entries.en: How could we fail to accept it with reverence!”
entries.literal: How dare we not respectfully receive it!”

entries.zh: 二月，上至奉高，遣侍御史与蘭臺令史，將工先上山刻石。
entries.en: In the second month the emperor reached Fenggao and sent an attendant censor and a palace clerk to lead workmen up the mountain ahead of him to cut the stele.
entries.literal: In the second month, the Sovereign arrived at Fenggao; he dispatched an attendant censor and a Lan-tai clerk of records, leading workmen first up the mountain to carve the stone.

entries.zh: 文曰：維建武三十有二年二月，皇帝東巡狩，至於岱宗，柴，望秩于山川，班于羣神，遂觐東后。
entries.en: The inscription read: In the second month of Jianwu 32 (56 CE), the emperor made an eastern tour of inspection, reached the Eastern Marchmount, performed the firewood rite, ranked offerings to mountains and rivers, distributed them among the host of spirits, and then received the Eastern Lord.
entries.literal: The text said: In the second month of the thirty-second year of Jianwu, the Emperor made an eastern tour of inspection, arrived at Dai's Marchmount, performed the firewood rite, ranked offerings to mountains and rivers, distributed them among the host of spirits, and then received the Eastern Lord.

entries.zh: 從臣太尉熹、行司徒事特进高密侯禹等。
entries.en: Attending ministers included Grand Commandant Xi, Acting Minister over the Masses and Special Advancement Marquis of Gaomi Yu, and others.
entries.literal: Attending ministers included Grand Commandant Xi, Acting Minister over the Masses and Special Advancement Marquis of Gaomi Yu, and others.

entries.zh: 漢宾二王之后在位。
entries.en: The descendants of the two kings who were guests of Han took their places.
entries.literal: The descendants of the two kings who were guests of Han took their places.

entries.zh: 孔子之后褒成侯，序在東后，蕃王十二，咸來助祭。
entries.en: Confucius's descendant, the Marquis of Baocheng, was ranked after the Eastern Lord; twelve feudal kings all came to assist in the sacrifice.
entries.literal: The descendant of Confucius, Marquis of Baocheng, was ranked after the Eastern Lord; twelve feudal kings all came to assist in the sacrifice.

entries.zh: 《河圖赤伏符》曰：「劉秀發兵捕不道，四夷云集龙斗野，四七之际火爲主。」
entries.en: The River Chart's Red Talisman of Hidden Submission said: "Liu Xiu takes up arms against the wicked; the four barbarians gather like clouds at Longdou Field; at the juncture of four and seven, Fire is master."
entries.literal: The Hetu Chifu fu said: "Liu Xiu raises troops to seize the lawless; the four barbarians gather like clouds at Longdou Field; at the juncture of four and seven, Fire is master."

entries.zh: 《河圖會昌符》曰：「赤帝九世，巡省得中，治平則封，誠合帝道孔矩，則天文靈出，地祇瑞興。
entries.en: The River Chart's Talisman of Flourishing Accord said: "The ninth generation of the Red Thearch, touring and inspecting, attains the center; when governance is settled, then the feng is performed; if truly it matches the Thearch's Way and Confucius's measure, then celestial signs appear and earthly numina bring auspicious omens.
entries.literal: The Hetu Huichang fu said: "The Red Thearch's ninth generation, touring and inspecting, attains the center; when governance is settled, then feng is performed; if truly it matches the Thearch's Way and Confucius's measure, then celestial signs appear and earthly numina bring auspicious omens.

entries.zh: 帝劉之九，會命岱宗，誠善用之，奸伪不萌。
entries.en: The ninth of the Liu emperors will receive the mandate on the Eastern Marchmount; wielded in good faith, it leaves no room for deceit.
entries.literal: The ninth of the Liu Thearchs will convene the mandate on Dai's Marchmount; if truly one uses it well, treachery and falsehood will not sprout.

entries.zh: 赤漢德興，九世會昌，巡岱皆當。
entries.en: The Red Han's virtue rises; the ninth generation meets flourishing accord; touring Dai is always fitting.
entries.literal: The Red Han's virtue rises; the ninth generation meets flourishing accord; touring Dai is always fitting.

entries.zh: 天地扶九，崇經之常。
entries.en: Heaven and Earth support the Nine; honoring the classics is the constant way.
entries.literal: Heaven and Earth support the Nine; honoring the classics is the constant way.

entries.zh: 漢大興之，道在九世之王。
entries.en: When Han greatly rises, the Way lies with the king of the ninth generation.
entries.literal: When Han greatly rises, the Way lies with the king of the ninth generation.

entries.zh: 封于泰山，刻石著纪，禅于梁父，退省考五。」
entries.en: Perform the feng on Mount Tai, carve stone to set forth the record, perform the shan at Liangfu, withdraw and examine the Five."
entries.literal: Perform feng on Mount Tai, carve stone to set forth the record, perform shan at Liangfu, withdraw and examine the Five."

entries.zh: 《河圖合古篇》曰：「帝劉之秀，九名之世，帝行德，封刻政。」
entries.en: The River Chart's "Conforming to Antiquity" said: "The Thearch Liu's Xiu, the generation of the ninth name; the Thearch practices virtue, feng and carving establish governance."
entries.literal: The Hetu Hegu pian said: "The Thearch Liu's Xiu, the generation of the ninth name; the Thearch practices virtue, feng and carving establish governance."

entries.zh: 《河圖提劉予》曰：「九世之帝，方明聖，持衡拒，九州平，天下予。」
entries.en: The River Chart's "Presenting Liu with the Grant" said: "The Thearch of the ninth generation, squarely bright and sage, holds the balance and resists; the Nine Provinces are pacified, and all under Heaven is granted."
entries.literal: The Hetu Tiliu yu said: "The Thearch of the ninth generation, squarely bright and sage, holds the balance and resists; the Nine Provinces are pacified, and all under Heaven is granted."

entries.zh: 《雒書甄曜度》曰：「赤三德，昌九世，會修符，合帝际，勉刻封。」
entries.en: The Luo River Writing's "Discipline of Radiant Brilliance" said: "Red, three virtues; flourishing, nine generations; meeting, repairing the talisman; matching the Thearch's juncture; strive to carve and feng."
entries.literal: The Luoshu Zhenyaodu said: "Red, three virtues; flourishing, nine generations; meeting, repairing the talisman; matching the Thearch's juncture; strive to carve and feng."

entries.zh: 《孝經钩命决》曰：「予谁行，赤劉用帝，三建孝，九會修，专兹竭行封岱青。」
entries.en: The Classic of Filial Piety's "Hooked Mandate Verdict" said: "To whom is the grant—who will act? The Red Liu uses the Thearch; thrice establishing filial piety, nine meetings repairing; exclusively here exhaust effort to perform feng at Dai and Qing."
entries.literal: The Xiaojing Gouming jue said: "To whom is the grant—who will act? The Red Liu uses the Thearch; thrice establishing filial piety, nine meetings repairing; exclusively here exhaust effort to perform feng at Dai and Qing."

entries.zh: 《河》、《雒》命后，經讖所传。
entries.en: After the mandates of the River and Luo, the classics and prophecies transmitted them.
entries.literal: After the mandates of the River and Luo, the classics and prophecies transmitted them.

entries.zh: 昔在帝尧，聪明密微，让与舜庶，后裔握机。
entries.en: Formerly under Emperor Yao, intelligence was subtle and profound; he yielded to Shun the common people, and his descendants grasped the pivot.
entries.literal: Formerly under Emperor Yao, intelligence was subtle and profound; he yielded to Shun the common people, and his descendants grasped the pivot.

entries.zh: 王莽以舅后之家、三司鼎足冢宰之权势，依托周公、霍光辅幼歸政之義，遂以篡叛，僭号自立。
entries.en: Wang Mang, wielding the power of the empress's clan, the Three Excellencies, and the chancellor, invoked the precedent of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang assisting a young ruler and returning power—then usurped the throne and rebelled.
entries.literal: Wang Mang, by the power of the empress's clan, the Three Excellencies standing like a tripod, and the Chancellor's authority, relying on the principle of the Duke of Zhou and Huo Guang assisting the young and returning power, then by usurpation and rebellion usurped the title and established himself.

entries.zh: 宗廟堕坏，社稷丧亡，不得血食，十有八年。
entries.en: The ancestral temples collapsed; the altars of soil and grain perished; they received no blood offerings for eighteen years.
entries.literal: The ancestral temples collapsed and were ruined; the altars of soil and grain perished; they received no blood offerings for eighteen years.

entries.zh: 杨、徐、青三州首乱，兵革横行，延及荆州，豪杰并兼，百里屯聚，往往僭号。
entries.en: The three provinces of Yang, Xu, and Qing first rebelled; warfare spread as far as Jing Province; local strongmen annexed one another; within a hundred li they gathered in camps, often usurping titles.
