entries.literal: The three provinces of Yang, Xu, and Qing first rebelled; weapons and armor ran rampant, extending to Jing Province; heroes and champions annexed one another; within a hundred li they gathered in camps, often usurping titles.

entries.zh: 北夷作寇，千里無烟，無鸡鸣狗吠之声。
entries.en: Northern barbarians raided the frontier; for a thousand li there was no smoke; not even the sound of crowing cocks or barking dogs could be heard.
entries.literal: Northern barbarians made raids; for a thousand li there was no smoke; there was no sound of crowing cocks or barking dogs.

entries.zh: 皇天睠顧皇帝，以匹庶受命中興，年二十八载興兵，以次誅讨，十有餘年，罪人斯得。
entries.en: August Heaven turned its gaze and favored the emperor; as a common man he received the mandate and restored the dynasty; at age twenty-eight he raised troops and in sequence suppressed the rebels; for more than ten years, the guilty were brought to justice.
entries.literal: August Heaven turned its gaze and favored the Emperor; as a common man he received the mandate and restored the dynasty; at age twenty-eight he raised troops, and in sequence punished and suppressed; for more than ten years, the guilty were brought to justice.

entries.zh: 黎庶得居尔田，安尔宅。
entries.en: The common people were able to dwell in their fields and settle in their homes.
entries.literal: The black-haired people were able to dwell in their fields and settle in their homes.

entries.zh: 舟舆所通，人迹所至，靡不贡职。
entries.en: Where boats and chariots reach, where human tracks extend—none failed to offer tribute and service.
entries.literal: Where boats and chariots reach, where human tracks extend—none failed to offer tribute and service.

entries.zh: 建明堂，立辟雍，起靈臺，設庠序。
entries.en: He built the Bright Hall, established the Imperial Academy, raised the Spirit Terrace, and set up schools.
entries.literal: He built the Bright Hall, established the Imperial Academy, raised the Spirit Terrace, and set up schools.

entries.zh: 同律、度、量、衡。
entries.en: He standardized pitch pipes, measures, capacity, and weights.
entries.literal: He standardized pitch pipes, measures, capacity, and weights.

entries.zh: 修五禮，五玉，三帛，二牲，一死，贽。
entries.en: He restored the Five Rites, five jades, three silks, two victims, one death-offering, and presentation gifts.
entries.literal: He restored the Five Rites, five jades, three silks, two victims, one death-offering, and presentation gifts.

entries.zh: 吏各修职，复于舊典。
entries.en: Officials each restored their duties and returned to the old canons.
entries.literal: Officials each restored their duties and returned to the old canons.

entries.zh: 在位三十有二年，年六十二。
entries.en: On the throne thirty-two years; age sixty-two.
entries.literal: On the throne thirty-two years; age sixty-two.

entries.zh: 乾乾日曰矢，不敢荒宁，涉危历险，亲巡黎元，恭肃神祇，惠恤耆老，理庶遵古，聪允明恕。
entries.en: Diligent day by day, he dared not be idle or at ease; crossing dangers and braving hardships, he personally toured the people; reverent and solemn toward the numinous powers, he kindly cared for the aged; governing the people he followed antiquity—perceptive, fair, bright, and forgiving.
entries.literal: Diligent day by day, he dared not be idle or at ease; crossing dangers and braving hardships, he personally toured the black-haired people; reverent and solemn toward the numinous powers, he kindly cared for the aged; governing the people he followed antiquity—perceptive, fair, bright, and forgiving.

entries.zh: 皇帝唯慎《河圖》、《雒書》正文，是月辛卯，柴，登封泰山。
entries.en: The emperor alone carefully verified the orthodox text of the River Chart and Luo River Writing; in this month on xinmao, he performed the firewood rite and ascended to perform the feng on Mount Tai.
entries.literal: The Emperor alone carefully verified the orthodox text of the Hetu and Luoshu; in this month on xinmao, he performed the firewood rite and ascended to feng Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 甲午，禅于梁阴。
entries.en: On jiawu, he performed the shan at Liang's northern slope.
entries.literal: On jiawu, he performed shan at Liang's shady side.

entries.zh: 以承靈瑞，以爲兆民，永兹一宇，垂于後昆。
entries.en: To receive numinous auspice, to serve as lord of the myriad people, forever in this one realm, handed down to later generations.
entries.literal: To receive numinous auspice, to serve as lord of the myriad people, forever in this one realm, handed down to later generations.

entries.zh: 百僚從臣，郡守師尹，咸蒙祉福，永永無极。
entries.en: The host of officials and attending ministers, commandery governors and district chiefs—all received blessed fortune, forever without limit.
entries.literal: The host of officials and attending ministers, commandery governors and district chiefs—all received blessed fortune, forever without limit.

entries.zh: 秦相李斯燔《诗》、《書》，乐崩禮坏。
entries.en: Qin's Chancellor Li Si burned the Odes and Documents; music collapsed and rites were ruined.
entries.literal: Qin's Chancellor Li Si burned the Odes and Documents; music collapsed and rites were ruined.

entries.zh: 建武元年已前，文書散亡，舊典不具，不能明經文，以章句细微相況八十一卷，明者爲验，又其十卷，皆不昭晰。
entries.en: Before Jianwu 1 (25 CE), documents were scattered and lost; old canons were incomplete; the classic texts could not be made clear; fine clauses were compared across eighty-one scrolls, with the clear ones taken as verification; another ten scrolls were all obscure.
entries.literal: Before the first year of Jianwu, documents were scattered and lost; old canons were incomplete; the classic texts could not be made clear; fine clauses were compared across eighty-one scrolls, with the clear ones taken as verification; another ten scrolls were all obscure.

entries.zh: 子贡欲去告朔之饩羊，子曰：「賜也，尔爱其羊，我受其禮。」
entries.en: Zigong wished to abolish the sacrificial sheep for the first-of-month announcement; the Master said: "Ci, you love the sheep; I receive the rite."
entries.literal: Zigong wished to abolish the sacrificial sheep for the first-of-month announcement; the Master said: "Ci, you love the sheep; I receive the rite."

entries.zh: 后有聖人，正失誤，刻石記。
entries.en: Later there will be a sage who corrects errors and records them by carving stone.
entries.literal: Later there will be a sage who corrects errors and records them by carving stone.

entries.zh: 二十二日辛卯晨，燎祭天于泰山下南方，羣神皆從，用樂如南郊。
entries.en: On the morning of the twenty-second day, a xinmao day, they burned offerings and sacrificed to Heaven south of Mount Tai; the host of spirits all followed; music was used as at the southern suburb.
entries.literal: On the morning of the twenty-second day, xinmao, they burned offerings and sacrificed to Heaven south of Mount Tai; the host of spirits all followed; music was used as at the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 諸王、王者後二公、孔子後褒成君，皆助祭位事也。
entries.en: The kings, the two dukes who were descendants of kings, and Confucius's descendant, Lord of Baocheng—all assisted in the sacrificial stations and duties.
entries.literal: The kings, the two dukes who were descendants of kings, and the descendant of Confucius, Lord of Baocheng—all assisted in the sacrificial stations and duties.

entries.zh: 事毕，將升封。
entries.en: When the rites were finished, they were about to ascend for the feng.
entries.literal: When the affair was finished, they were about to ascend for the feng.

entries.zh: 或曰：「泰山虽已從食于柴祭，今亲升告功，宜有禮祭。」
entries.en: Someone said: "Although Mount Tai has already received offerings in the firewood sacrifice, now in personally ascending to announce merit, there ought to be a ritual sacrifice."
entries.literal: Someone said: "Although Mount Tai has already received offerings in the firewood sacrifice, now in personally ascending to announce merit, there ought to be a ritual sacrifice."

entries.zh: 于是使謁者以一特牲于常祠泰山處，告祠泰山，如亲耕、貙劉、先祠、先農、先虞故事。
entries.en: Therefore they sent an usher with one specially prepared victim to the place of the regular sacrifice to Mount Tai, to announce and sacrifice to Mount Tai, following the precedents of the emperor's personal plowing, the autumn hunt, the prior shrine, the prior agriculture, and the prior Yu.
entries.literal: Therefore they sent a usher with one specially [raised] victim to the place of the regular sacrifice to Mount Tai, to announce and sacrifice to Mount Tai, following the precedents of the emperor's personal plowing, the autumn hunt, the prior shrine, the prior agriculture, and the prior Yu.

entries.zh: 至食時，御輦升山，日中后到山上更衣，早晡時即位于壇，北面。
entries.en: At mealtime the imperial carriage ascended the mountain; after midday he reached the summit to change clothes; in early afternoon he took his position on the mound, facing north.
entries.literal: At mealtime the imperial carriage ascended the mountain; after midday he reached the mountain top to change clothes; in early afternoon he took his position on the mound, facing north.

entries.zh: 羣臣以次陳後，西上，毕位升壇。
entries.en: The ministers in sequence arrayed behind, ascending from the west; when all were in place they ascended the mound.
entries.literal: The host of ministers in sequence arrayed behind, ascending from the west; when all were in place they ascended the mound.

entries.zh: 尚書令奉玉牒檢，皇帝以寸二分璽亲封之，訖，太常命人发壇上石，尚書令藏玉牒已，复石覆讫，尚書令以五寸印封石檢。
entries.en: The Director of the Masters of Writing bore the jade slip and cover-plate; the emperor personally sealed it with the one-cun-two-fen seal; when finished, the Grand Master of Ceremonies ordered men to open the stone on the mound; after the Director of the Masters of Writing stored the jade slip, the stone was covered again; the Director of the Masters of Writing sealed the stone cover-plate with the five-cun seal.
entries.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing bore the jade slip and cover-plate; the Emperor personally sealed it with the one-cun-two-fen seal; when finished, the Grand Master of Ceremonies ordered men to open the stone on the mound; after the Director of the Masters of Writing stored the jade slip, the stone was covered again; the Director of the Masters of Writing sealed the stone cover-plate with the five-cun seal.

entries.zh: 事毕，皇帝再拜，羣臣稱萬岁。
entries.en: When the rites were finished, the emperor bowed twice; the ministers proclaimed "Ten thousand years!"
entries.literal: When the affair was finished, the Emperor bowed twice; the host of ministers proclaimed "Ten thousand years!"

entries.zh: 命人立所刻石碑，乃复道下。
entries.en: He ordered men to set up the carved stone stele; then he descended by the covered way.
entries.literal: He ordered men to set up the carved stone stele; then he descended by the covered way.

entries.zh: 至七年五月，詔三公曰：「漢當郊尧。
entries.en: In the fifth month of the seventh year, he issued an edict to the Three Excellencies, saying, “Han ought to sacrifice to Yao at the suburbs.
entries.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year, he issued an edict to the Three Excellencies, saying, “Han ought to sacrifice to Yao at the suburbs.

entries.zh: 其与卿大夫、博士议。」
entries.en: He bade them take counsel with senior ministers and academicians.”
entries.literal: Let them deliberate together with ministers, great officers, and erudits.”

entries.zh: 時侍御史杜林上疏，以爲「漢起不因缘尧，与殷、周異宜，而舊制以高帝配。
entries.en: At that time Attendant Censor Du Lin presented a memorial, holding that “Han’s rise did not follow a line from Yao; its proper observances differ from those of Yin and Zhou, whereas the old arrangement matches Emperor Gao.
entries.literal: At that time Attendant Censor Du Lin presented a memorial, holding that “Han’s rise did not follow a line from Yao; its proper observances differ from those of Yin and Zhou, whereas the old arrangement matches Emperor Gao.

entries.zh: 方軍師在外，且可如元年郊祀故事」。
entries.en: With the armies still in the field, he argued, the court should for now adhere to the suburban rites observed in the first year of the reign.”
entries.literal: Since the army and its commanders are still abroad, for the moment one may follow the suburban-sacrifice precedent of the first year.”

entries.zh: 上從之。
entries.en: The emperor accepted his advice.
entries.literal: The Sovereign followed this.

entries.zh: 語在《林传》。
entries.en: Du Lin’s memorial is preserved in his biography.
entries.literal: The account is in the “Biography of Lin.”

entries.zh: 祭祀之道，自生民以來則有之矣。
entries.en: The practice of sacrifice has existed ever since human society began.
entries.literal: As for the way of sacrifice, from the time the people first arose there have been such things.

entries.zh: 豺獺知祭祀，而況人乎！
entries.en: Even jackals and otters observe sacrificial customs; surely people can do no less.
entries.literal: Jackals and otters know sacrifice; how much more so human beings!

entries.zh: 故人知之至於念想，猶豺獺之自然也，顧古質略而後文飾耳。
entries.en: Human beings carry sacrifice in mind and memory as instinctively as those beasts do in nature; the difference is simply that early ages kept the rites spare and later ages elaborated them.
entries.literal: Therefore for people to know it reaching to thoughts and recollections is like the naturalness of jackals and otters; only that antiquity was plain and simple and later times added ornament.

entries.zh: 自古以來王公所爲羣祀，至於王莽，《漢書·郊祀志》既著矣，故今但列自中興以來所修用者，以爲《祭祀志》。
entries.en: The great state sacrifices of kings and nobles down through Wang Mang are already recorded in the Book of Han’s “Suburban Sacrifices”; this treatise therefore confines itself to what has been established and practiced since the dynasty’s revival.
entries.literal: From antiquity the mass sacrifices performed by kings and dukes down to Wang Mang are already set forth in the “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice” in the Hanshu; therefore here only those instituted and used since the restoration are listed, to form the “Treatise on Sacrifice.”

entries.zh: 二年正月，初制郊兆於于雒陽城南七里，依鄗。
entries.en: In the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), he first marked out the suburban altar seven li south of Luoyang, following the layout used at Hao.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year, he first laid out the suburban-sacrifice precinct seven li south of Luoyang city, modeled on Hao.

entries.zh: 采元始中故事。
entries.en: The design drew on the Yuanshi-era precedents.
entries.literal: He adopted the precedents of the Yuanshi era.

entries.zh: 爲圓壇八陛，中又爲重壇，天地位其上，皆南嚮乡，西上。
entries.en: They built a round altar with eight flights of steps and a nested inner terrace; Heaven and Earth were set atop it, every station facing south, with approach from the west.
entries.literal: They made a round mound with eight stairways; inside it they made a double mound; Heaven and Earth had their positions on it; all faced south; ascending was from the west.

entries.zh: 其外壇上爲五帝位。
entries.en: The outer ring held the stations of the Five Thearchs.
entries.literal: On its outer mound were made the positions of the Five Thearchs.

entries.zh: 青帝位在甲寅之地，赤帝位在丙巳之地，黄帝位在丁未之地，白帝位在庚申之地，黑帝位在壬亥之地。
entries.en: The Green Thearch stood at the jiayin compass point, the Red at bingsi, the Yellow at dingwei, the White at gengshen, and the Black at renhai.
entries.literal: The Green Thearch’s position was in the jiayin place; the Red Thearch’s in the bingsi; the Yellow Thearch’s in the dingwei; the White Thearch’s in the gengshen; the Black Thearch’s in the renhai.

entries.zh: 其外壝，重營皆紫，以像紫宫；
entries.en: Beyond the inner wall the layered enclosures were draped in purple, evoking the Purple Palace constellation;
entries.literal: Outside its enclosing wall, the layered enclosures were all purple, to resemble the Purple Palace;

entries.zh: 有四通道以爲門。
entries.en: Four avenues served as gates.
entries.literal: There were four thoroughfares serving as gates.

entries.zh: 日月在中營内南道，日在東，月在西，北斗在北道之西，皆别位，不在羣神列中。
entries.en: Within the inner camp’s southern aisle stood the Sun and Moon—the Sun to the east, the Moon to the west—with the Northern Dipper west of the northern aisle; each had its own station apart from the general ranks of deities.
entries.literal: Sun and Moon were inside the inner enclosure on the south path; the Sun in the east, the Moon in the west; the Northern Dipper was west of the north path; all had separate positions and were not in the array of the host of spirits.

entries.zh: 八陛，陛五十八醊，合四百六十四醊。
entries.en: The eight flights of steps held fifty-eight ritual mounds apiece, four hundred sixty-four in all.
entries.literal: Eight stairways; each stairway fifty-eight zhui; in all four hundred sixty-four zhui.

entries.zh: 五帝陛郭，帝七十二醊，合三百六十五醊。
entries.en: Around the Five Thearchs’ steps ran seventy-two mounds for each ruler—three hundred sixty-five altogether, one for each day of the year.
entries.literal: For the Five Thearchs’ stairway enclosures, each Thearch had seventy-two zhui; in all three hundred sixty-five zhui.

entries.zh: 中營四門，門五十四神，合二百一十六神。
entries.en: The inner precinct’s four gates held fifty-four deities each—two hundred sixteen in total.
entries.literal: The inner enclosure had four gates; each gate fifty-four spirits; in all two hundred sixteen spirits.

entries.zh: 外營四門，門百八神，合四百三十二神。
entries.en: The outer ring’s four gates held a hundred eight spirits apiece, four hundred thirty-two altogether.
entries.literal: The outer enclosure had four gates; each gate one hundred eight spirits; in all four hundred thirty-two spirits.

entries.zh: 皆背營内乡。
entries.en: Each deity faced outward, backs turned toward the center of the camp.
entries.literal: All turned their backs toward the inside of the enclosure and faced outward.

entries.zh: 中營四門，門封神四，外營四門，門封神四，合三十二神。
entries.en: Four gate-gods were posted at each of the inner camp’s four doors and four at each outer door—thirty-two gate spirits in all.
entries.literal: The inner enclosure’s four gates, each gate enfeoffing four spirits; the outer enclosure’s four gates, each gate enfeoffing four spirits; in all thirty-two spirits.

entries.zh: 凡千五百一十四神。
entries.en: The pantheon numbered one thousand five hundred fourteen deities.
entries.literal: In all one thousand five hundred fourteen spirits.

entries.zh: 營即壝也。
entries.en: Here “enclosure” (ying) means the earthen wall (wei) around the altar.
entries.literal: The ying is the wei.

entries.zh: 封，封土筑也。
entries.en: A feng is a mound of heaped earth.
entries.literal: Feng: piling earth and building.

entries.zh: 背中營神，五星也，及中官宿五官神及五岳之屬也。
entries.en: Those facing outward from the inner ring represented the Five Planets, the stellar gods of the central palace and the five bureaus, and the marchmounts and their affiliates.
entries.literal: The spirits with their backs to the inner enclosure are the Five Planets, and the spirits of the Central Palace lodges and the Five Offices, and those belonging to the Five Marchmounts.

entries.zh: 背外營神，二十八宿外官星，雷公、先農、風伯、雨師、四海、四瀆、名山、大川之屬也。
entries.en: The outer ring’s outward-facing gods included the Twenty-Eight Mansions and outer asterisms, Thunder Duke, the god of agriculture, Wind and Rain, the four seas and four channel rivers, and celebrated peaks and streams.
entries.literal: The spirits with their backs to the outer enclosure are the Twenty-Eight Lodges’ outer star officials, Thunder Duke, First Farmer, Wind Earl, Rain Master, the Four Seas, the Four Great Rivers, famous mountains, great rivers, and the like.

entries.zh: 陇、蜀平后，乃增广郊祀，高帝配食，位在中壇上，西面北上。
entries.en: Once Long and Shu had been subdued, the court expanded the suburban cult and set Emperor Gao as correlative recipient on the central terrace, facing west with senior rank to the north.
entries.literal: After Long and Shu were pacified, then they enlarged the suburban sacrifices; Gaodi shared in the offerings, his position on the central mound, facing west, with precedence to the north.

entries.zh: 天、地、高帝、黄帝各用犢一头，青帝、赤帝共用犢一头，白帝、黑帝共用犢一头，凡用犢六头。
entries.en: Heaven, Earth, Emperor Gao, and the Yellow Thearch each received a calf; the Green and Red Thearchs shared one, as did the White and Black Thearchs—six calves in all.
entries.literal: Heaven, Earth, Gaodi, and the Yellow Thearch each used one calf; the Green Thearch and Red Thearch shared one calf; the White Thearch and Black Thearch shared one calf; in all six calves were used.

entries.zh: 日、月、北斗共用牛一头，四營羣神共用牛四头，凡用牛五头。
entries.en: The Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper shared a single ox; the deities of the four precincts shared four more—five oxen altogether.
entries.literal: Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper shared one ox; the four camps’ host of spirits shared four oxen; in all five oxen were used.

entries.zh: 凡乐奏《青陽》、《朱明》、《西皓》、《玄冥》，及《云翘》、《育命》舞。
entries.en: The musicians played the seasonal hymns Qingyang, Zhuming, Xihao, and Xuanming, accompanied by the Yunqiao and Yuming dances.
entries.literal: For music they performed “Green Yang,” “Red Brightness,” “Western Radiance,” and “Dark Obscurity,” and the dances “Cloud Crest” and “Nurturing the Mandate.”

entries.zh: 中營四門，門用席十八枚，外營四門，門用席三十六枚，凡用席二百一十六枚，皆莞簟，率一席三神。
entries.en: Each inner gate held eighteen rush mats and each outer gate thirty-six—two hundred sixteen mats of coiled rush and bamboo, generally three deities to a mat.
entries.literal: The inner enclosure’s four gates, each gate used eighteen mats; the outer enclosure’s four gates, each gate used thirty-six mats; in all two hundred sixteen mats were used, all rush and bamboo mats; on average one mat for three spirits.

entries.zh: 日、月、北斗無陛郭醊。
entries.en: No stepped mounds (zhui) ringed the stations of the Sun, Moon, or Northern Dipper.
entries.literal: Sun, Moon, and Northern Dipper had no stairway-enclosure zhui.

entries.zh: 既送神，燎俎實于壇南巳地。
entries.en: Once the spirits had been dismissed, the meat from the sacrificial stands was burned at the south side of the altar in the si quarter.
entries.literal: After sending off the spirits, they burned the stand’s meat offerings on the mound’s south in the si position.

entries.zh: 建武三十年二月，羣臣上言，即位三十年，宜封禅泰山。
entries.en: In the second month of Jianwu 30 (54 CE), ministers urged that after thirty years on the throne the emperor should perform the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai.
entries.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year of Jianwu, the host of ministers memorialized that, having reigned thirty years, it was fitting to perform the feng and shan sacrifices on Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 詔書曰：「即位三十年，百姓怨气满腹，吾谁欺，欺天乎？
entries.en: An edict declared: "After thirty years on the throne, the people are seething with grievance—whom could I fool? Could I fool Heaven?
entries.literal: An edict said: "Thirty years on the throne—the common people are filled with resentment; whom would I deceive—could I deceive Heaven?

entries.zh: 曾谓泰山不如林放，何事污七十二代之編錄！
entries.en: Confucius once held Mount Tai less worthy than Lin Fang—why should I stain the annals of seventy-two dynasties!
entries.literal: It was once said that Mount Tai is not equal to Lin Fang—why should I defile the records of seventy-two generations!

entries.zh: 桓公欲封，管仲非之」若郡縣遠遣吏上壽，盛稱虚美，必髡，兼令屯田。」
entries.en: Duke Huan wished to perform the feng rite, and Guan Zhong opposed it. If any commandery or county sends officials from afar to offer birthday congratulations with lavish empty flattery, the offenders will be shaved and assigned to frontier garrison farming."
entries.literal: Duke Huan wished to perform feng; Guan Zhong objected. If commanderies and counties send officials from afar to offer birthday felicitations with extravagant empty praise, [the offenders] will be shaved bald and also ordered to garrison farming."

entries.zh: 從此羣臣不敢复言。
entries.en: After that, no minister dared raise the subject again.
entries.literal: From this point the host of ministers dared not speak of it again.

entries.zh: 三月，上幸鲁，过泰山，告太守以上过，故承詔祭山及梁父。
entries.en: In the third month the emperor visited Lu, passed Mount Tai, informed the governor of his route, and in accordance with the edict sacrificed at the mountain and at Liangfu.
entries.literal: In the third month the Sovereign visited Lu, passed Mount Tai, told the governor of his itinerary, and therefore, following the edict, sacrificed at the mountain and at Liangfu.

entries.zh: 時，虎贲中郎將梁松等议：「《記》曰'齊將有事泰山，先有事配林'，蓋諸侯之禮也。
entries.en: At that time Liang Song, commander of the Tiger Guard, and others argued: "The Record says, 'When Qi is about to perform rites at Mount Tai, it first performs rites at Peilin'—that is essentially the feudal-lord protocol.
entries.literal: At that time Commander of the Tiger Guard Liang Song and others deliberated: "The Record says, 'When Qi is about to have business at Mount Tai, it first has business at Peilin'—this is roughly the rite of feudal lords.

entries.zh: 河岳視公侯，王者祭焉。
entries.en: Rivers and marchmounts rank with dukes and marquises; only a king may sacrifice to them directly.
entries.literal: Rivers and marchmounts are treated like dukes and marquises; only kings sacrifice to them.

entries.zh: 宜無即事之漸，不祭配林。」
entries.en: There should therefore be no preliminary rite before the principal ceremony; do not sacrifice at Peilin."
entries.literal: Accordingly there should be no preliminary approach to the rite, and no sacrifice at Peilin."

entries.zh: 二十五日甲午，禅，祭地于梁阴，以高后配，山川羣神從，如元始中北郊故事。
entries.en: On the twenty-fifth day, a jiawu day, he performed the shan, offering to Earth on the northern slope of Mount Liang with Empress Lü as consort and the terrestrial spirits in attendance, following the northern-suburban model of the Yuanshi era.
entries.literal: On the twenty-fifth day, jiawu, they performed the shan; they sacrificed to Earth on Liang’s shady side, with Empress Gao as correlative; mountains and rivers and the host of spirits followed, according to the Yuanshi-era northern suburban precedent.

entries.zh: 四月己卯，大赦天下，以建武三十二年爲建武中元元年，复博、奉高、赢勿出元年租、刍稿。
entries.en: On the jimao day of the fourth month he proclaimed a general amnesty, renamed the year from Jianwu 32 to the first year of the Zhongyuan era, and remitted rent and fodder levies for Bo, Fenggao, and Ying for that year.
entries.literal: On jimao of the fourth month, he greatly pardoned all under Heaven; he took Jianwu thirty-second year as Jianwu middle era first year; he restored Bo, Fenggao, and Ying so as not to issue the first year’s rent and straw.

entries.zh: 以吉日刻玉牒書函藏金匮，璽印封之。
entries.en: On an auspicious day the jade text was boxed, placed in a metal casket, and sealed with the imperial seals.
entries.literal: On an auspicious day they carved the jade slip document’s case and stored it in a metal coffer; with seal impressions they sealed it.

entries.zh: 乙酉，使太尉行事，以特告至高廟。
entries.en: On yiyou he had the Grand Commandant officiate and announce the deed at Gaodi’s temple with a specially prepared bull.
entries.literal: On yiyou, he ordered the Grand Commandant to conduct the affair, with a bull specially [raised] to announce to Gaodi’s temple.

entries.zh: 太尉奉匮以告高廟，藏于廟室西壁石室高主室之下。
entries.en: The Grand Commandant presented the coffer at the shrine to Emperor Gao and deposited it in the stone vault under the western wall of the inner sanctum.
entries.literal: The Grand Commandant bore the coffer to announce to Gaodi’s temple; it was stored beneath Gaodi’s chamber in the temple room’s west wall stone chamber.

entries.zh: 三十二年正月，上齋，夜讀《河圖會昌符》曰：「赤劉之九，會命岱宗。
entries.en: In the first month of Jianwu 32 (56 CE), while observing the fast, he read by lamplight the River Chart’s Talisman of Flourishing Accord: “The ninth generation of the Red Liu will receive its charge on the Eastern Marchmount.
entries.literal: In the first month of the thirty-second year, the Sovereign fasted; at night he read the Hetu Huichang fu, which said, “The ninth of the Red Liu will convene the mandate on Dai’s Marchmount.

entries.zh: 不慎克用，何益于承！
entries.en: Unless it is applied with scrupulous care, what good can it do the heir who receives the mandate?
entries.literal: If one does not carefully be able to use it, what benefit is there to receiving!

entries.zh: 誠善用之，奸伪不萌。」
entries.en: Wielded in good faith, it leaves no room for deceit.”
entries.literal: If truly one uses it well, treachery and falsehood will not sprout.”

entries.zh: 感此文，乃詔松等复案索《河》、《雒》讖文言九世封禅事者。
entries.en: Stirred by these lines, he instructed Liang Song and his colleagues to comb the Yellow River and Luo River apocrypha for passages on the ninth-generation feng and shan.
entries.literal: Moved by this text, he then ordered Song and others again to search through River and Luo prophecy texts that spoke of the ninth generation’s feng and shan affairs.

entries.zh: 松等列奏，乃許焉。
entries.en: Liang Song and the others laid their findings before the throne, and the emperor gave his assent.
entries.literal: Song and others arrayed a memorial; then he granted it.

entries.zh: 上許梁松等奏，乃求元封時封禅故事，议封禅所施用。
entries.en: The emperor approved the memorial from Liang Song and his colleagues, ordered a search for Western Han precedents from the Yuanfeng performance, and convened discussion of the equipment and ritual program.
entries.literal: The Sovereign granted Liang Song and others’ memorial; then he sought the Yuanfeng-era feng and shan precedents and deliberated what feng and shan should employ and apply.

entries.zh: 有司奏當用方石再累置壇中，皆方方尺，厚一尺，用玉牒書藏方石。
entries.en: Officials reported that the altar should hold stacked square stones a foot thick on each face, with the jade proclamation sealed inside.
entries.literal: The responsible officials memorialized that one ought to use square stones piled in layers placed in the mound; all were square one chi to a side, one chi thick; with a jade slip document written and stored in the square stone.

entries.zh: 牒厚五寸，长尺三寸，广五寸，有玉檢。
entries.en: The jade slip was five cun thick, thirteen cun long, five cun wide, and fitted with a jade sealing plate.
entries.literal: The slip was five cun thick, one chi three cun long, five cun wide, and had a jade cover-plate.

entries.zh: 又用石檢十枚，列于石傍，東西各三，南北各二，皆长三尺，广一尺，厚七寸。
entries.en: Ten stone sealing blocks were to flank the central stone—three on the east and west, two on the north and south—each three feet long, a foot wide, and seven inches thick.
entries.literal: Also they used ten stone cover-plates, arrayed beside the stone; east and west three each, south and north two each; all were three chi long, one chi wide, seven cun thick.

entries.zh: 檢中刻三處，深四寸，方五寸，有蓋。
entries.en: Each stone seal was carved with three recesses, four inches deep and five inches square, and capped with a lid.
entries.literal: In the cover-plate were carved three places, four cun deep, five cun square; there was a lid.

entries.zh: 檢用金縷五周，以水銀和金以爲泥。
entries.en: They bound the seals with five turns of gold wire and sealed the joints with an amalgam of mercury and gold.
entries.literal: The cover-plate used gold thread five circuits; with mercury mixed with gold they made mud.

entries.zh: 玉璽一方寸二分，一枚方五寸。
entries.en: One jade seal measured an inch and two tenths square; another slab measured five inches square.
entries.literal: The jade seal was one cun two fen square; one piece was five cun square.

entries.zh: 方石四角又有距石，皆再累。
entries.en: Corner posts were set at each angle of the central block, each built up in courses.
entries.literal: At the square stone’s four corners there were again footing stones; all were again layered.

entries.zh: 枚长一丈，厚一尺，广二尺，皆在圓壇上。
entries.en: Each measured ten feet in length, a foot thick, and two feet wide, standing on the round terrace.
entries.literal: Each was one zhang long, one chi thick, two chi wide; all were on the round mound.

entries.zh: 其下用距石十八枚，皆高三尺，厚一尺，广二尺，如小碑，环壇立之，去壇三步。
entries.en: Eighteen supporting stones, each three feet high and shaped like miniature steles, ringed the altar three paces out.
entries.literal: Below it used eighteen footing stones; all were three chi high, one chi thick, two chi wide, like small steles; they ringed the mound and stood them, three paces from the mound.

entries.zh: 距石下皆有石跗，入地四尺。
entries.en: Each footing stone sat on a socket sunk four feet into the earth.
entries.literal: Beneath the footing stones all had stone bases, entering the ground four chi.

entries.zh: 又用石碑，高九尺，广三尺五寸，厚尺二寸，立壇丙地，去壇三丈以上，以刻書。
entries.en: A stone stele nine feet high, three feet five inches wide, and a little over a foot thick was raised in the bing sector more than thirty feet from the mound to bear the inscription.
entries.literal: Also they used a stone stele, nine chi high, three chi five cun wide, one chi two cun thick, set up on the mound’s bing ground, more than three zhang from the mound, to carve writing.

entries.zh: 上以用石功难，又欲及二月封，故詔松欲因故封石空檢，更加封而已。
entries.en: Because quarrying new stone would be slow and he hoped to perform the feng in the second month, he initially told Liang Song to reuse the old Western Han block, hollow out a new cavity in its seal, and simply reseal it.
entries.literal: The Sovereign, because using stone work was difficult, and also desiring to catch the second month’s feng, therefore ordered Song to desire to follow the old feng stone’s empty cover-plate and merely add sealing.

entries.zh: 松上疏争之，以爲「登封之禮，告功皇天，垂后無窮，以爲萬民也。
entries.en: Liang Song protested in a memorial: “The feng rite proclaims your achievement to Heaven and must stand for ages to come on behalf of the people.
entries.literal: Song presented a memorial disputing it, holding that “The rite of ascending to feng announces merit to August Heaven, hangs down to later ages without end, and is for the sake of the myriad people.

entries.zh: 承天之敬，尤宜章明。
entries.en: The reverence owed to Heaven ought above all to be displayed openly.
entries.literal: Receiving Heaven’s reverence, especially ought to be made clear and bright.

entries.zh: 奉圖書之瑞，尤宜顯著。
entries.en: The auspicious charts that justify the rite should be honored with equal clarity.
entries.literal: Presenting the charts’ and documents’ auspicious signs, especially ought to be made manifest and prominent.

entries.zh: 今因舊封，窜寄玉牒故石下，恐非重命之義。
entries.en: To tuck the new jade text under the old Western Han stone would look furtive and ill suit a renewed mandate.
entries.literal: Now relying on the old feng, furtively lodging the jade slip document under the old stone, I fear this is not the meaning of a renewed charge.

entries.zh: 受命中興，宜當特異，以明天意」。
entries.en: This restoration deserves its own monument, plainly declaring Heaven’s will.”
entries.literal: Receiving the charge and restoring the dynasty, ought appropriately to be specially distinctive, to make clear Heaven’s intent.”

entries.zh: 遂使泰山郡及鲁趣石工，宜取完青石，無必五色。
entries.en: He therefore instructed Taishan and Lu to press masons into service and quarry sound bluestone without insisting on polychrome marble.
entries.literal: Therefore he ordered Taishan commandery and Lu to hurry stoneworkers; they should take intact greenish stone; there was no necessity for five colors.

entries.zh: 時以印工不能刻玉牒，欲用丹漆書之；
entries.en: Seal-cutters at first could not incise the jade slip, so the court considered writing the text in vermilion lacquer instead;
entries.literal: At the time because seal craftsmen could not carve the jade slip document, they desired to use cinnabar lacquer to write it;

entries.zh: 會求得能刻玉者，遂書。
entries.en: but when a craftsman skilled in jade carving was found, the text was engraved after all.
entries.literal: In the end they sought and obtained one able to carve jade; then they wrote it.

entries.zh: 書秘刻方石中，命容玉牒。
entries.en: The inscription was cut secretly into the square stone, hollowed to receive the jade document.
entries.literal: The writing was secretly carved inside the square stone, ordered to contain the jade slip document.

entries.zh: 初，孝武帝欲求神仙，以扶方者言黄帝由封禅而後仙，于是欲封禅。
entries.en: Earlier, Emperor Wu had sought immortality; his fangshi advisers claimed the Yellow Thearch had ascended only after performing the feng and shan rites on Mount Tai, which fired the emperor’s own ambition to do the same.
entries.literal: At first, Emperor Xiaowu desired to seek transcendents; because those who supported the methods said the Yellow Thearch through feng and shan afterward became a transcendent, therefore he desired feng and shan.

entries.zh: 封禅不常，時人莫知。
entries.en: The feng and shan observances were rare, and contemporaries knew little about them.
entries.literal: Feng and shan were not constant; people of the time did not know.

entries.zh: 元封元年，上以方士言作封禅器，以示羣儒，多言不合古，于是罷諸儒不用。
entries.en: In the first year of Yuanfeng (110 BC), following his occult advisers' advice, he had ritual vessels for the feng and shan sacrifices made and shown to the Confucian scholars; most pronounced them uncanonical, so he set the literati aside.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yuanfeng (110 BC), following his occult advisers' advice, he had ritual vessels for the feng and shan sacrifices made and shown to the Confucian scholars; most pronounced them uncanonical, so he set the literati aside.

entries.zh: 三月，上東上泰山，乃上石立之泰山颠。
entries.en: In the third month he climbed Mount Tai from the east and set a stone marker on its peak.
entries.literal: In the third month, the Sovereign went east and ascended Mount Tai; then he ascended a stone and set it up on Mount Tai’s summit.

entries.zh: 遂東巡海上，求仙人，無所見而還。
entries.en: He then cruised the eastern sea in search of immortals, found none, and turned back.
entries.literal: Then he toured east on the sea, seeking transcendents; seeing nothing he returned.

entries.zh: 四月，封泰山。
entries.en: In the fourth month he performed the feng sacrifice on Mount Tai.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, he feng’d Mount Tai.

entries.zh: 恐所施用非是，乃秘其事。
entries.en: Doubting whether the procedure had been correct, he kept the details secret.
entries.literal: Fearing that what was employed and applied was not correct, he then concealed the affair.

entries.zh: 語在《漢書·郊祀志》。
entries.en: The full story appears in the Book of Han’s “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifices.”
entries.literal: The account is in the “Treatise on Suburban Sacrifice” in the Hanshu.

entries.zh: 志第七 祭祀上
entries.en: Treatise 7: Sacrifices, Part One.
entries.literal: Treatise Seven: Sacrifices, Part One.

entries.zh: 是年初营北郊，明堂、辟雍、灵台未用事。
entries.en: In that year work began on the northern suburban altar, while the Bright Hall, Biyong, and Spirit Terrace were still not in active use.
entries.literal: That year they first laid out the northern suburb; the Bright Hall, Biyong, and Spirit Terrace had not yet been put to use.

entries.zh: 迁吕太后于园。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Lü’s spirit seat was removed to an outlying cemetery shrine.
entries.literal: They moved Empress Dowager Lü to a garden [tomb].

entries.zh: 上簿太后尊号曰高皇后，当配地，郊高庙。
entries.en: The emperor registered her posthumous style as Empress Gao, pairing her with Earth at the northern rite and honoring her at Gaodi’s suburban temple.
entries.literal: The Sovereign recorded the Empress Dowager’s honorific title as Empress Gao; she was to match Earth and sacrifice at Gaodi’s temple.

entries.zh: 语在《光武纪》。
entries.en: The details appear in the annals of Emperor Guangwu.
entries.literal: The account is in the “Annals of Guangwu.”

entries.zh: 明帝即位，永平二年正月辛未，初祀五帝于明堂，光武帝配。
entries.en: After Emperor Ming’s accession, on the xinwei day of the first month of Yongping 2 (59 CE), the court first offered to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall, with Emperor Guangwu as joint recipient.
entries.literal: When Mingdi took the throne, on xinwei of the first month of Yongping 2, they first sacrificed to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall, with Guangwudi as correlative.

entries.zh: 五帝坐位堂上，各处其方。
entries.en: The Five Thearchs sat on the upper hall, each in his own cosmic quarter.
entries.literal: The Five Thearchs’ seats were on the hall above, each occupying its direction.

entries.zh: 黄帝在未，皆如南郊之位。
entries.en: The Yellow Thearch occupied the wei position, the same arrangement as at the southern suburban altar.
entries.literal: The Yellow Thearch was at wei; all were like the southern suburb’s positions.

entries.zh: 光武帝位在青帝之南少退，西面。
entries.en: Emperor Guangwu’s seat stood just south of the Green Thearch, set slightly behind it, facing west.
entries.literal: Guangwudi’s position was south of the Green Thearch, slightly set back, facing west.

entries.zh: 牲各一犊，奏乐如南郊。
entries.en: Each deity received a calf, and the musicians followed the southern suburban score.
entries.literal: Each victim was one calf; performing music was like the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 卒事，遂升灵台，以望云物。
entries.en: When the rites ended, they climbed the Spirit Terrace to scan the sky for omens.
entries.literal: When the affair was finished, then they ascended the Spirit Terrace to observe clouds and prodigies.

entries.zh: 二月，上东巡狩，将至泰山，道使使者奉一太牢祠帝尧于济阴成阳灵台。
entries.en: In the second month the emperor set out on an eastern tour; before reaching Mount Tai he dispatched envoys with a full tailao offering to honor Emperor Yao at the Spirit Terrace in Chengyang, Jiyin.
entries.literal: In the second month, the Sovereign toured east on the hunt; when about to reach Mount Tai, on the way he sent envoys bearing one grand sacrifice to sacrifice to Emperor Yao at the Spirit Terrace of Chengyang in Jiyin.

entries.zh: 上至泰山，修光武山南坛兆。
entries.en: Upon reaching Mount Tai he restored the southern-altar site that Guangwu had established.
entries.literal: The Sovereign arrived at Mount Tai and repaired Guangwu’s southern-mountain altar precinct.

entries.zh: 辛未，柴祭天地群神如故事。
entries.en: On xinwei he offered the chai burnt sacrifice to Heaven, Earth, and the full pantheon, following established form.
entries.literal: On xinwei, they performed the firewood sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the host of spirits according to precedent.

entries.zh: 壬申，宗祀五帝于孝武所作汶上明堂，光武帝配，如雒阳明堂礼。
entries.en: On renshen he offered the lineal sacrifice to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall above the Wen River built by Emperor Wu, pairing Guangwu as at the Luoyang Bright Hall.
entries.literal: On renshen, they performed the lineal sacrifice to the Five Thearchs in the Bright Hall on the Wen that Xiaowu had built, with Guangwudi as correlative, like the Luoyang Bright Hall ritual.

entries.zh: 癸酉，更告祀高祖、太宗、世宗、中宗、世祖、显宗于明堂，各一太牢。
entries.en: On guiyou he reported separately to Gaozu, Taizong, Shizong, Zhongzong, Shizu, and Xianzong in the Bright Hall, each with a full tailao.
entries.literal: On guiyou, they further announced sacrifice to Gaozu, Taizong, Shizong, Zhongzong, Shizu, and Xianzong in the Bright Hall, each one grand sacrifice.

entries.zh: 卒事，遂觐东后，飨赐王侯群臣。
entries.en: When the ceremonies ended, he received the eastern lords in audience, then feasted and rewarded the kings, marquises, and ministers.
entries.literal: When the rites were complete, he received the eastern lords in audience and held a banquet and bestowed gifts on the kings, marquises, and assembled ministers.

entries.zh: 因行郡国，幸鲁，祠东海恭王，及孔子七十二弟子。
entries.en: He then toured the provinces, visited Lu, sacrificed to Prince Gong of Eastern Sea, and to Confucius’s seventy-two disciples.
entries.literal: Thereupon he traveled commanderies and kingdoms, favored Lu, sacrificed to the Respectful Prince of the Eastern Sea, and to Confucius’s seventy-two disciples.

entries.zh: 四月，还京都。
entries.en: In the fourth month he returned to the capital.
entries.literal: In the fourth month, he returned to the capital.

entries.zh: 庚申，告至，祠高庙、世祖，各一特牛。
entries.en: On gengshen he reported his return and offered a specially raised bull each at the shrines to Emperor Gao and Shizu.
entries.literal: On gengshen, he announced arrival and sacrificed to Gaodi’s temple and Shizu, each one specially raised ox.

entries.zh: 又为灵台十二门作诗，各以其月祀而奏之。
entries.en: He also composed hymns for the twelve gates of the Spirit Terrace, one for each month’s sacrifice.
entries.literal: Also for the Spirit Terrace’s twelve gates he made poems; each according to its month sacrificed and performed them.

entries.zh: 和帝无所增改。
entries.en: Emperor He altered none of this.
entries.literal: Hedi added or changed nothing.

entries.zh: 北效在雒阳城北四里，为方坛四陛。
entries.en: The northern suburban site lay four li north of Luoyang, laid out as a square altar with four flights of steps.
entries.literal: The northern suburb was four li north of Luoyang city; they made a square mound with four stairways.

entries.zh: 三十三年正月辛未，郊。
entries.en: On the xinwei day of the first month of Jianwu 33 (57 CE), the court held the suburban rite.
entries.literal: On xinwei of the first month of the thirty-third year, they performed the suburban sacrifice.

entries.zh: 别祀地祇、位南面西上，高皇后配，西面北上，皆在坛上，地理群神从食，皆在坛下，如元始中故事。
entries.en: Earth received a distinct cult on the terrace, stations facing south with senior rank to the west, while Empress Gao stood as consort facing west to the north; terrestrial deities who shared the offerings stood below the mound, following Western Han practice under Yuanshi.
entries.literal: They separately sacrificed to Earth’s numen; positions faced south with precedence to the west; Empress Gao was correlative, facing west with precedence to the north; all were on the mound; terrestrial spirits sharing the offerings were all below the mound, according to the Yuanshi-era precedent.

entries.zh: 中岳在未，四岳各在其方孟辰之地，中营内。
entries.en: Mount Song stood at the wei compass point, and each of the four outer marchmounts occupied the “first-chen” slot for its quarter—all within the inner camp.
entries.literal: The Central Marchmount was at wei; the four marchmounts each were at their direction’s first chen position, inside the inner enclosure.

entries.zh: 海在东；
entries.en: The sea god was placed on the east;
entries.literal: The sea was in the east;

entries.zh: 西渎河西，济北，淮来，江南；
entries.en: the western rivers ran west of the Yellow River, north of the Ji, with the Huai approaching from the east and the Yangzi to the south;
entries.literal: the western channel-rivers: west of the Yellow River, north of the Ji, Huai coming, south of the Yangzi;

entries.zh: 他山川各如其方，皆在外营内。
entries.en: Other hills and streams were assigned to their proper quarters, all within the outer precinct.
entries.literal: Other mountains and rivers each according to their direction, all were inside the outer enclosure.

entries.zh: 四陛□及中外营门封神如南郊。
entries.en: The four stairways, the inner and outer gates, and the gate deities matched the southern suburban layout.
entries.literal: The four stairways [lacuna] and inner and outer enclosure gate enfeoffed spirits were like the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 地祇、高后用犊各一头，五岳共牛一头，海、四渎共牛一头，群神共二头。
entries.en: Earth and Empress Gao each received a calf; the five marchmounts shared one ox, the sea and four great rivers another, and the lesser gods two oxen between them.
entries.literal: Earth’s numen and Empress Gao each used one calf; the five marchmounts shared one ox; sea and four channel-rivers shared one ox; the host of spirits shared two head.

entries.zh: 奏乐亦如南郊。
entries.en: The musical program duplicated that of the southern suburban sacrifice.
entries.literal: Performing music was also like the southern suburb.

entries.zh: 既送神，瘗俎实于坛北。
entries.en: When the spirits had been dismissed, the meat from the sacrificial stands was interred north of the altar.
entries.literal: After sending off the spirits, they buried the stand’s meat offerings north of the mound.

entries.zh: 迎时气，五郊之兆。
entries.en: Welcoming the seasonal qi: the five suburban altar sites.
entries.literal: Welcoming the seasonal ethers: the five suburbs’ precincts.

entries.zh: 自永平中，以《礼谶》及《月令》有五郊迎气服色，因采元始中故事，兆五郊于雒阳四方。
entries.en: During the Yongping era the court, citing the ritual apocrypha and the Monthly Ordinances on the five suburban welcomes and their prescribed colors, followed Yuanshi precedents and marked out five suburban sites around Luoyang.
entries.literal: From within Yongping, because the Rites Apocrypha and the Monthly Ordinances had five suburbs’ welcoming-the-ether garment colors, therefore adopting Yuanshi-era precedents, they laid out five suburbs on Luoyang’s four sides.

entries.zh: 中兆在未，坛皆三尺，阶无等。
entries.en: The central altar stood at wei, each mound rose three feet, and the steps had no staggered tiers.
entries.literal: The central precinct was at wei; the mounds were all three chi; the steps had no ranks.

entries.zh: 志第八 祭祀中
entries.en: Treatise 8: Sacrifices, Part Two.
entries.literal: Treatise Eight: Sacrifices, Part Two.

entries.zh: 光武帝建武二年正月，立高庙于雒阳。
entries.en: In the first month of Jianwu 2 (26 CE), Guangwu founded the High Ancestor’s temple in Luoyang.
entries.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu established the shrine to Emperor Gao (Liu Bang) at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 四时祫祀，高帝为太祖，文帝为太宗，武帝为世宗，如旧。
entries.en: At the four seasonal xia sacrifices, Emperor Gao was honored as Taizu, Emperor Wen as Taizong, and Emperor Wu as Shizong, as in the old system.
entries.literal: At the seasonal xi sacrifices and the collective offering, Emperor Gao was honored as Grand Progenitor, Emperor Wen as Grand Exemplar, and Emperor Wu as World Exemplar, as before.

entries.zh: 余帝四时春以正月，夏以四月，秋以七月，冬以十月及腊，一岁五祀。
entries.en: The remaining sovereigns were honored five times a year: spring in the first month, summer in the fourth, autumn in the seventh, winter in the tenth, plus the la offering at year’s end.
entries.literal: For the other emperors, the four seasons were observed in spring in the first month, in summer in the fourth month, in autumn in the seventh month, and in winter in the tenth month and at the year-end la sacrifice—five sacrifices in one year.

entries.zh: 三年正月，立亲庙雒阳，祀父南顿君以上至舂陵节侯。
entries.en: In Jianwu 3 he set up shrines to his own line in Luoyang, reaching from his father, the Lord of Nandun, up to the Jieling marquis of Chunling.
entries.literal: In the first month of the third year he established private ancestral shrines at Luoyang, sacrificing from his father Lord of Nandun upward to Marquis Jieling of Chunling.

entries.zh: 时寇贼未夷，方务征伐，祀仪未设。
entries.en: Rebels were still active and the state was absorbed in war, so the liturgy of sacrifice had not yet been fixed.
entries.literal: At that time bandits had not yet been pacified, and the court was busy with campaigns, so the full ritual program had not been instituted.

entries.zh: 至十九年，盗贼讨除，戎事差息，于是五官中郎将张纯与太仆朱浮奏议：「礼，为人子事大宗，降其私亲。
entries.en: By year nineteen the rebels were gone and arms could rest. Zhang Chun and Zhu Fu submitted: "According to the Rites, a son who serves the main imperial line must demote one's private kin.
entries.literal: By the nineteenth year the robbers had been eliminated and military affairs had somewhat eased; then Central Court Gentleman-General Zhang Chun and Grand Coachman Zhu Fu submitted a memorial: “According to the Rites, a son who serves the great lineage lowers his private kin.

entries.zh: 礼之设施，不授之与自得之异意。
entries.en: Whether rites are imposed from above or arise from inner conviction, the principle is not the same.
entries.literal: The setting up of ritual is not a matter of granting it from without versus obtaining it from within—different intentions.

entries.zh: 当除今亲庙四。
entries.en: Four shrines to his immediate forebears should therefore be removed.
entries.literal: The four private shrines now standing should be abolished.

entries.zh: 孝宣皇以孙后祖，为父立庙于奉明，曰皇考庙，独群臣侍祠。
entries.en: Xuan had raised a “royal father” temple at Fengming for his natural father, served only by officials, because he had inherited from his grandfather.
entries.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan, being a grandson who succeeded his grandfather, had built for his father a temple at Fengming called the Temple of the Imperial Father, where only ministers attended the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 愿下有司议先帝四庙当代亲庙者及皇考庙事。」
entries.en: They asked the court to decide which four earlier Han shrines should substitute for Guangwu's private halls, and how to treat the "imperial father" shrine."
entries.literal: We ask that the authorities deliberate which four shrines of former emperors should replace the present private shrines, and what to do with the Temple of the Imperial Father.”

entries.zh: 下公卿、博士、议郎。
entries.en: The emperor sent the question to the three dukes, the academicians, and the deliberation gentlemen.
entries.literal: The matter was referred to the excellencies, erudits, and deliberation gentlemen.

entries.zh: 大司徒涉等议：「宜奉所代，立平帝、哀帝、成帝、元帝庙，代今亲庙。
entries.en: Dai She and others argued: "You should honor those you have succeeded by establishing temples to Ping, Ai, Cheng, and Yuan in place of the present private shrines.
entries.literal: Grand Minister of Education Dai She and others argued: “You should honor those you have succeeded by establishing temples to Emperor Ping, Emperor Ai, Emperor Cheng, and Emperor Yuan, in place of the present private shrines.

entries.zh: 兄弟以下，使有司祠。
entries.en: Younger brothers and more distant kin could be tended by routine official cults.
entries.literal: For brothers and those below, let the relevant offices sacrifice.

entries.zh: 宜为南顿君立皇考庙，祭上至舂陵节侯，群臣奉祠。」
entries.en: For his own father they proposed a "royal father" temple from Nandun up to Jieling, with the bureaucracy as celebrants."
entries.literal: You should establish a Temple of the Imperial Father for the Lord of Nandun, sacrificing up to the Marquis of Jieling, with ministers attending.”

entries.zh: 时议有异，不著。
entries.en: Debate split the court, and the minority positions went unwritten in the record.
entries.literal: At that time opinions differed, and the dissenting views were not recorded.

entries.zh: 上可涉等议，诏曰：「以宗庙处所未定，且祫祭高庙。
entries.en: The emperor approved and issued an edict: "Because the sites for the ancestral temples are not yet settled, for now perform the joint sacrifice at the High Temple.
entries.literal: The emperor approved She’s proposal and issued an edict: “Because the sites for the ancestral temples are not yet settled, for now perform the joint sacrifice at the High Temple.

entries.zh: 其成、哀、平且祠祭长安故高庙。
entries.en: Cheng, Ai, and Ping would meanwhile receive cult at the former Chang’an High Temple.
entries.literal: For the time being let Cheng, Ai, and Ping be worshipped at the old High Temple in Chang’an.

entries.zh: 其南阳舂陵岁时各且因故园庙祭祀。
entries.en: Nanyang and Chunling could keep seasonal offerings at their existing garden-temples for the moment.
entries.literal: Let Nanyang and Chunling each, at the proper seasons, sacrifice for the time being at the old garden shrines.

entries.zh: 园庙去太守治所远者，在所令长行太守事侍祠。
entries.en: If a garden-temple sat beyond easy reach of the prefect, the local magistrate was to stand in for him at the rites.
entries.literal: Where a garden shrine lay far from the prefect’s seat, the magistrate on site should act as prefect and attend the cult.

entries.zh: 惟孝宣帝有功德，其上尊号曰中宗。」
entries.en: Xuan alone, for genuine achievement, deserved the title Central Exemplar."
entries.literal: Only Emperor Xiaoxuan, who had true merit and virtue, should receive the posthumous honorific Central Exemplar.”

entries.zh: 于是雒阳高庙四时加祭孝宣、孝元，凡五帝。
entries.en: Luoyang’s High Temple then honored five sovereigns in the seasonal round, adding Xuan and Yuan.
entries.literal: Thereupon at Luoyang's High Temple the four seasonal rites added sacrifices to Xuan and Yuan, making five emperors in all.

entries.zh: 其西庙成、哀、平三帝主，四时祭于故高庙。
entries.en: The western hall kept the tablets of Cheng, Ai, and Ping, served at the old High Temple each season.
entries.literal: The western temple housed the spirit tablets of Cheng, Ai, and Ping, with seasonal sacrifice at the old High Temple.

entries.zh: 东庙，京兆尹侍祠，冠衣车服如太常祠陵庙之礼。
entries.en: The eastern hall fell to the metropolitan governor, who matched the Chamberlain’s tomb ritual in dress and equipage.
entries.literal: The eastern temple was tended by the Governor of the Capital, with caps, robes, chariots, and equipage like those used when the Chamberlain for Ceremonial tended imperial tombs.

entries.zh: 南顿君以上至节侯，皆就园庙。
entries.en: The line from Nandun through Jieling was worshipped only at the garden-temples.
entries.literal: From the Lord of Nandun up to Marquis Jieling, all cult was returned to the garden shrines.

entries.zh: 南顿君称皇考庙，钜鹿都尉称皇祖考庙，郁林太守称皇曾祖考庙，节侯称皇高祖考庙，在所郡县侍祠。
entries.en: Lord Nandun's temple was called the Imperial Deceased Father's Temple; the Julu Commandant's temple was called the Imperial Deceased Grandfather's Temple; the Yulin Administrator's temple was called the Imperial Deceased Great-Grandfather's Temple; and Marquis Jie’s temple was called the Imperial Deceased Great-Great-Grandfather's Temple. The commanderies and counties where they were located attended to the sacrifices.
entries.literal: The Lord of Nandun was titled Temple of the Imperial Father, the Commandant of Julu Temple of the Imperial Grandfather, the Governor of Yulin Temple of the Imperial Great-Grandfather, and Marquis Jieling Temple of the Imperial High-Great-Grandfather; the counties where they lay supplied the attendants.

entries.zh: 二十六年，有诏问张纯，禘祫之礼不施行几年。
entries.en: In year twenty-six the court questioned Zhang Chun on how long the grand di and xia offerings had been suspended.
entries.literal: In the twenty-sixth year an edict asked Zhang Chun how many years it had been since the di and xia joint rites had last been carried out.

entries.zh: 纯奏：「礼，三年一祫，五年一禘。
entries.en: Chun submitted: “The Rites prescribe a collective xi every three years and a di every five years.
entries.literal: Chun submitted: “The Rites prescribe a collective xi every three years and a di every five years.

entries.zh: 毁庙之主，陈于太祖；
entries.en: Tablets from abolished temples were brought before the first ancestor.
entries.literal: Spirits from destroyed shrines are arrayed before the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 未毁庙之主，皆升，合食太祖；
entries.en: Tablets of still-standing temples likewise ascended to feast with the founding ancestor.
entries.literal: Spirits from shrines not yet destroyed all ascend and share a meal with the Grand Progenitor.

entries.zh: 五年再殷察。
entries.en: The ritual canon calls for two great Yin offerings within each five-year span; received editions vary this line.
entries.literal: Within five years the grand Yin sacrifices are performed twice.

entries.zh: 旧制，三年三祫，毁庙主合食高庙，存庙主未尝合。
entries.en: Former practice held three xi in three years: only spirits from razed shrines ate with Gao; standing temples had not yet been merged.
entries.literal: Under the old Han system there were three xi in three years: tablets from destroyed temples joined Gao’s meal, while tablets from surviving temples had never joined in one meal.

entries.zh: 元始五年，始行禘礼。
entries.en: The di was first enacted in Yuanshi 5 (5 CE).
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Yuanshi era the di rite was first performed.

entries.zh: 父为昭，南向；
entries.en: Fathers stood on the zhao, the southern file.
entries.literal: Fathers occupy the zhao (south-facing) side.

entries.zh: 子为穆，北向。
entries.en: Sons stood on the mu, facing north.
entries.literal: Sons occupy the mu (north-facing) side.

entries.zh: 父子不并坐，而孙从王父。
entries.en: Father and son were not paired in the same row; grandsons aligned under the grandfather’s column.
entries.literal: Father and son do not sit side by side; grandsons follow their grandfather’s file.

entries.zh: 禘之为言谛，禘諟昭穆，尊卑之义。
entries.en: Di means “discernment”: it sets zhao and mu and thereby rank.
entries.literal: The word di means ‘to make clear’; the di sorts zhao and mu and fixes the meaning of high and low.

entries.zh: 以夏四月阳气在上，阴气在下，故正尊卑之义。
entries.en: Held in the fourth month, when yang rides high and yin lies below, it expresses who is senior and who junior.
entries.literal: Because in the fourth month of summer the yang ether is above and the yin below, it rectifies the meaning of precedence.

entries.zh: 祫以冬十月，五谷成熟，故骨肉合饮食。
entries.en: The winter xia in the tenth month, when grain is gathered, gathers the lineage for a communal meal with the dead.
entries.literal: The xia takes place in the tenth month of winter, when the five grains are ripe, so bone and flesh share a common meal.

entries.zh: 祖宗庙未定，且合祭。
entries.en: Until the founding temples were settled, only the combined offering was used.
entries.literal: Because the shrines of the founding ancestors are not yet fixed, for now perform only the joint sacrifice.

entries.zh: 今宜以时定。」
entries.en: The time had come to settle the schedule in law."
entries.literal: Now it should be fixed in due course.”

entries.zh: 语在《纯传》。
entries.en: Details appear in Zhang Chun’s biography.
entries.literal: The account is given in Zhang Chun’s biography.”

entries.zh: 上难复立庙，遂以合祭高庙为常。
entries.en: Guangwu kept rebuilding separate halls impracticable, so the collective offering at the High Temple became the norm.
entries.literal: The emperor found it hard to rebuild separate temples, so he made the joint sacrifice at the High Temple the standing rule.

entries.zh: 后以三年冬祫，五年夏禘之时，但就陈祭毁庙主而已，谓之殷。
entries.en: Thereafter, at the third year’s winter xi and the fifth year’s summer di, only tablets from dismantled shrines were brought out—the so-called Yin rite.
entries.literal: Later, at the winter xi of the third year and the summer di of the fifth year, they merely set out and sacrificed the tablets from destroyed shrines—this was called the Yin offering.”

entries.zh: 太祖东面，惠、文、武、元帝为昭，景、宣帝为穆。
entries.en: The founding ancestor faced east; Hui, Wen, Wu, and Yuan were zhao; Jing and Xuan were mu.
entries.literal: The Grand Progenitor faced east; Emperors Hui, Wen, Wu, and Yuan formed the zhao file; Emperors Jing and Xuan the mu file.

entries.zh: 惠、景、昭三帝非殷祭时不祭。
entries.en: Hui, Jing, and Zhao were omitted from ordinary seasonal cult and appeared only at the grand Yin.
entries.literal: The three emperors Hui, Jing, and Zhao received no sacrifice except at these grand Yin rites.

entries.zh: 光武皇帝崩，明帝即位，以光武帝拨乱中兴，更为起庙，尊号曰世祖庙。
entries.en: Mingdi, crediting Guangwu with restoring the house, raised a new temple titled Shrine of the World Exemplar.
entries.literal: When Emperor Guangwu died and Emperor Ming succeeded, because Guangwu had quelled chaos and restored the dynasty, a new temple was built for him with the honorific title Shrine of the World Exemplar.”

entries.zh: 以元帝于光武为穆，故虽非宗，不毁也。
entries.en: Yuan, though not a “numbered” exemplar, stayed on the mu side opposite Guangwu and so escaped abolition.
entries.literal: Because Emperor Yuan stood in the mu column relative to Guangwu, although he was not counted a “exemplar” shrine, his temple was not destroyed.”

entries.zh: 后遂为常。
entries.en: The arrangement then stayed permanent.
entries.literal: This later became fixed practice.

entries.zh: 明帝临终遗诏，遵俭无起寝庙，藏主于世祖庙更衣。
entries.en: Mingdi’s final edict ordered frugal rites and forbade a separate resting temple; his tablet was housed in the robing chamber of the Shizu shrine.
entries.literal: On his deathbed Emperor Ming issued a testamentary edict to follow frugality and not raise a resting temple; his spirit tablet was deposited in the robing chamber of the Shrine of the World Exemplar.

entries.zh: 孝章即位，不敢违，以更衣有小别，上尊号曰显宗庙，间祠于更衣，四时合祭于世祖庙。
entries.en: Zhangdi obeyed; because the robing hall stood apart, he gave it the temple name Xianzong, held minor rites there, and merged the four seasonal offerings at the Shizu temple.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhang succeeded he dared not disobey; because the robing chamber was a separate place, he honored it with the temple title Shrine of the Manifest Exemplar, performed intervening sacrifices at the robing chamber, and joined the four seasonal sacrifices at the Shrine of the World Exemplar.

entries.zh: 语在《章纪》。
entries.en: Details appear in the Annals of Zhang.
entries.literal: The account is given in the Annals of Zhang.

entries.zh: 章帝临崩，遗诏无起寝庙，庙如先帝故事。
entries.en: Zhangdi’s deathbed edict likewise forbade a resting temple and followed Mingdi’s precedent.
entries.literal: When Emperor Zhang was near death his testamentary edict ordered that no resting temple be raised; the temple arrangement followed the former emperor’s precedent.

entries.zh: 和帝即位不敢违，上尊号曰肃宗。
entries.en: Hedi obeyed and gave him the temple epithet Suzong.
entries.literal: When Emperor He succeeded he dared not disobey and honored him with the temple title Suzong.

entries.zh: 后帝承尊，皆藏主于世祖庙，积多无别，是后显宗但为陵寝之号。
entries.en: Later sovereigns all stored tablets in the Shizu shrine until the titles piled up indistinguishably; Xianzong then became merely the mausoleum name.
entries.literal: Later emperors who received honored titles all deposited their tablets in the Shrine of the World Exemplar; as they accumulated there was no distinction, and thereafter Xianzong served only as the name of the mausoleum lodge.

entries.zh: 永元中，和帝追尊其母梁贵人曰恭怀皇后，陵曰西陵。
entries.en: In Yongyuan, Hedi posthumously raised his mother, Lady Liang, to Empress Gonghuai; her tomb was Xiling.
entries.literal: In the Yongyuan era Emperor He posthumously honored his mother, the Lady of Liang, as Empress Gonghuai, and her tomb was called Xiling.

entries.zh: 以窦后配食章帝，恭怀后别就陵寝祭之。
entries.en: Empress Dou shared Zhangdi’s cult, but Empress Gonghuai was worshipped separately at her tomb lodge.
entries.literal: Empress Dou was paired to share Zhangdi’s offering, while Empress Gonghuai was separately worshipped at her mausoleum lodge.

entries.zh: 和帝崩，上尊号曰穆宗。
entries.en: At Hedi’s death he received the temple name Muzong.
entries.literal: When Emperor He died he was honored with the temple title Muzong.

entries.zh: 殇帝生三百余日而崩，邓太后摄政，以尚婴孩，故不列于庙，就陵寝祭之而已。
entries.en: Shangdi died in infancy; Dowager Deng kept him out of the temple line and offered cult only at his tomb lodge.
entries.literal: Emperor Shang lived a little more than three hundred days and died; Empress Dowager Deng acted as regent; because he was still an infant he was not entered in the ancestral temple and was worshipped only at the mausoleum lodge.

entries.zh: 安帝以清河孝王子即位，建光元年，追尊其祖母宋贵人曰敬隐后，陵曰敬北陵。
entries.en: Andi, a Qinghe prince’s son, took the throne; in Jianguang 1 he raised his grandmother, Lady Song, to Empress Jingyin; her tomb was Jingbeiling.
entries.literal: Emperor An, a son of the Filial King of Qinghe, succeeded; in the first year of Jianguang he posthumously honored his grandmother, the Lady of Song, as Empress Jingyin, and her tomb was called Jingbeiling.

entries.zh: 亦就陵寝祭，太常领如西陵。
entries.en: She too was served at her tomb lodge under the Chamberlain for Ceremonial, as at Xiling.
entries.literal: She too was worshipped at the mausoleum lodge, with the Chamberlain for Ceremonial supervising as at Xiling.

entries.zh: 追尊父清河孝王曰孝德皇，母曰孝德后，清河嗣王奉祭而已。
entries.en: His father was posthumously titled Xiaode Huang and his mother Xiaode Hou; the Qinghe heir king alone maintained their cult.
entries.literal: He posthumously honored his father, the Filial King of Qinghe, as the Filial Virtue Emperor and his mother as Empress of Filial Virtue; the heir king of Qinghe alone performed the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 安帝以谗害大臣，废太子，及崩，无上宗之奏。
entries.en: Andi’s slander of ministers and deposition of the heir left no proposal for a zong title when he died.
entries.literal: Because Emperor An slandered and harmed great ministers and deposed the heir, when he died there was no memorial proposing a zong temple title.

entries.zh: 后以自建武以来无毁者，故遂常祭，因以其陵号称恭宗。
entries.en: Because no Jianwu temple had been dismantled, he received regular cult anyway, and his tomb name became Gongzong.
entries.literal: Later, because since Jianwu no [Shizu-line] temple had been abolished, regular sacrifice continued, and his mausoleum name was used as Gongzong.

entries.zh: 顺帝即位，追尊其母曰恭愍后，陵曰恭北陵，就陵寝祭，如敬北陵。
entries.en: Shundi raised his mother to Empress Gongmin; her Gongbeiling tomb was served at the lodge, like Jingbeiling.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun succeeded he posthumously honored his mother as Empress Gongmin; her tomb was called Gongbeiling; she was worshipped at the mausoleum lodge, as at Jingbeiling.

entries.zh: 顺帝崩，上尊号曰敬宗。
entries.en: At Shundi’s death he received the temple name Jingzong.
entries.literal: When Emperor Shun died he was honored with the temple title Jingzong.

entries.zh: 冲质帝皆小崩，梁太后摄政，以殇帝故事，就陵寝祭。
entries.en: Chongdi and Zhidi died young; Dowager Liang, following Shangdi’s precedent, worshipped them only at their tomb lodges.
entries.literal: Emperors Chong and Zhi both died young; Empress Dowager Liang acted as regent and, following Shangdi’s precedent, worshipped them at the mausoleum lodges.

entries.zh: 凡祠庙讫，三公分祭之。
entries.en: After each temple round the three excellencies took turns offering sacrifice.
entries.literal: Whenever temple sacrifices were completed, the three excellencies divided and performed them.

entries.zh: 桓帝以河间孝王孙蠡吾侯即位，亦追尊祖考，王国奉祀。
entries.en: Huandi, the Liwu marquis and Hejian prince’s grandson, likewise raised his ancestors; the fief maintained their cult.
entries.literal: Emperor Huan, the Liyou marquis of Liwu, a grandson of the Filial King of Hejian, succeeded; he too posthumously honored his forebears, and the kingdom performed the sacrifices.

entries.zh: 语在《章和八王传》。
entries.en: Details appear in the Biographies of the Eight Princes of Zhang and He.
entries.literal: The account is given in the Biographies of the Eight Princes of Zhang and He.

entries.zh: 桓帝崩，上尊号曰威宗，无嗣。
entries.en: At Huandi’s death he received the temple name Weizong; he had no son.
entries.literal: When Emperor Huan died he was honored with the temple title Weizong; he left no heir.

entries.zh: 灵帝以河间孝王曾孙解犊侯即位，亦追尊祖考。
entries.en: Lingdi, the Jiedu marquis and Hejian prince’s great-grandson, likewise raised his ancestors.
entries.literal: Emperor Ling, the marquis of Jiedu, a great-grandson of the Filial King of Hejian, succeeded and likewise posthumously honored his forebears.

entries.zh: 语在《章和八王传》。
entries.en: Details appear in the Biographies of the Eight Princes of Zhang and He.
entries.literal: The account is given in the Biographies of the Eight Princes of Zhang and He.

entries.zh: 灵帝时，京都四时所祭高庙五主，世祖庙七主，少帝三陵，追尊后三陵，凡牲用十八太牢，皆有副倅。
entries.en: Under Lingdi the capital’s seasonal round required eighteen tai-lao victims—with duplicates—for five High Temple tablets, seven Shizu tablets, three child-emperor tombs, and three honored empresses’ tombs.
entries.literal: In Lingdi’s time the capital’s four seasonal sacrifices used five tablets at the High Temple, seven at the Shrine of the World Exemplar, three tombs of young emperors, and three tombs of posthumously honored empresses; victims totaled eighteen full tai-lao, each with a duplicate set.

entries.zh: 故高庙三主亲毁之后，亦但殷祭之岁奉祠。
entries.en: After the three western High Temple tablets were abolished, they too were served only in Yin years.
entries.literal: Therefore after the three High Temple tablets personally abolished [at the western temple] were gone, they too were worshipped only in the years of the grand Yin sacrifice.

entries.zh: 灵帝崩，献帝即位。
entries.en: Lingdi died and Xiandi succeeded.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ling died Emperor Xian succeeded.

entries.zh: 初平中，相国董卓、左中郎将蔡邕等以和帝以下，功德无殊，而有过差，不应为宗，及余非宗者追尊三后，皆奏毁之。
entries.en: In Chuping, Dong Zhuo, Cai Yong, and others argued that from Hedi onward the emperors lacked distinct merit yet had been over-honored as zong, and that three improperly raised empresses should be stripped; all were ordered dismantled.
entries.literal: In the Chuping era the Chancellor Dong Zhuo, the Left Palace Gentleman Cai Yong, and others argued that from Emperor He downward merit and virtue were not distinctive yet there were excesses, so they ought not to be called zong, and that the three posthumously honored empresses who were not proper zong should also be memorialized for removal; all were submitted for abolition.

entries.zh: 四时所祭，高庙一祖二宗，及近帝四，凡七帝。
entries.en: Thereafter the seasonal round honored seven sovereigns: one progenitor, two zong, and four recent emperors.
entries.literal: The four seasonal sacrifices then honored at the High Temple one progenitor and two zong, plus four recent emperors—seven emperors in all.

entries.zh: 论曰：「臧文仲祀爰居，而孔子以为不知。
entries.en: The essayist remarks: "Zang Wenzhong sacrificed to the seabird Yuanju, and Confucius thought him ignorant.
entries.literal: The essayist remarks: “Zang Wenzhong sacrificed to the seabird Yuanju, and Confucius thought him ignorant.

entries.zh: 《汉书·郊祀志》著自秦以来迄于王莽，典祀或有未修，而爰居之类众焉。
entries.en: The Western Han treatise shows how irregular cults piled up from Qin through Wang Mang.
entries.literal: The ‘Han Treatise on Suburban and Other Sacrifices’ records from Qin down to Wang Mang: some canonical cults were neglected, while oddities like Yuanju multiplied.

entries.zh: 世祖中兴，蠲除非常，修复旧祀，方之前事邈殊矣。
entries.en: Guangwu’s restoration scrapped the exotic and revived the old rites—a world away from the past.
entries.literal: Our Founding Emperor restored the middle and cut away the abnormal, repairing old sacrifices—how far that is from the earlier tangle!

entries.zh: 尝闻儒言，三皇无文，结绳以治，自五帝始有书契。
entries.en: Confucians say the Three Sovereigns had no script and used knotted cords; records begin with the Five Thearchs.
entries.literal: I once heard scholars say that the Three August Ones left no writing and governed by knotted cords; writing and contracts begin with the Five Thearchs.

entries.zh: 至于三王，俗化雕文，诈伪渐兴，始有印玺，以检奸萌，然犹未有金玉银铜之器也。
entries.en: Under the three dynasties ornament and fraud grew; seals curbed malice, but precious metal ware did not yet exist.
entries.literal: By the Three Kings custom had carved patterns, deceit gradually arose, and seals first appeared to check treachery—yet there were still no vessels of gold, jade, silver, or copper.

entries.zh: 自上皇以来封泰山者，至周七十二代。
entries.en: Seventy-two generations from remote antiquity through Zhou are said to have performed the Tai feng.
entries.literal: From high antiquity those who feng Mount Tai down to Zhou number seventy-two generations.

entries.zh: 封者，谓封土为坛，柴祭告天，代兴成功也。
entries.en: Feng meant raising a mound and burning the report that a new mandate had fulfilled its task.
entries.literal: Feng means piling earth into an altar, burning firewood to announce to Heaven that a new age has succeeded and its work is complete.

entries.zh: 《礼记》所谓「因名山升中于天」者也。
entries.en: It matches the Rites: “By a famed peak ascend and report to Heaven.”
entries.literal: This is what the Book of Rites calls ‘by a famous mountain ascending and reporting in the middle of Heaven.’

entries.zh: 易姓则改封者，著一代之始，明不相袭也。
entries.en: A change of dynasty required a new feng to signal a fresh mandate, not a mere copy of the old.
entries.literal: When the surname of the ruling house changes, the feng is altered, to mark the beginning of a new age and show that one does not simply inherit the former rite.

entries.zh: 继世之王巡狩，则修封以祭而已。
entries.en: Later sovereigns on inspection tours only refurbished the altar and offered sacrifice.
entries.literal: Later kings on tour merely repaired the feng and sacrificed—that was all.

entries.zh: 自秦始皇、孝武帝封泰山，本由好仙、信方士之言，造为石检印封之事也。
entries.en: Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi climbed Tai out of quest for immortals and occultists’ tales, hence stone caskets and sealed credentials.
entries.literal: From the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han, the feng on Mount Tai arose from love of immortality and trust in fangshi talk, producing the business of stone casings and sealed imprints.

entries.zh: 所闻如此。
entries.en: Such is the tradition I have heard.
entries.literal: What I have heard is like this.

entries.zh: 虽诚天道难可度知，然其大较犹有本要。
entries.en: Heaven’s way may be unfathomable, yet its broad pattern has an intelligible basis.
entries.literal: Although the Way of Heaven is hard to measure, its general outline still has a root principle.

entries.zh: 天道质诚，约而不费者也。
entries.en: Heaven’s way is simple and true—spare and without extravagance.
entries.literal: The Way of Heaven is plain and sincere—economical and free of waste.

entries.zh: 故牲有犊，器用陶匏，殆将无事于检封之间，而乐难攻之石也。
entries.en: So the rites used young calves and plain earthenware and gourds—far from the stone-casket sealing fad—yet rulers still took perverse pleasure in smashing those rocks.
entries.literal: Therefore the victims were calves, and the vessels were pottery and gourd—probably nothing to do with the business of stone casings and sealing, yet they delighted in attacking those stones.

entries.zh: 且唯封为改代，故曰岱宗。
entries.en: Only the Tai feng announces a new mandate, which is why Mount Dai is called the Ancestral Peak.
entries.literal: Moreover it is only the feng that marks a change of mandate; hence Mount Dai is called the Exalted Peak of the Lineage.

entries.zh: 夏康、周宣，由废复兴，不闻改封。
entries.en: Xia’s Kang and Zhou’s Xuan revived ruined dynasties without redoing the Tai rite.
entries.literal: Xia Kang and King Xuan of Zhou restored their houses after ruin; one never hears that they altered the feng.

entries.zh: 世祖欲因孝武故封，实继祖宗之道也。
entries.en: Guangwu meant to repeat Wudi’s climb in spirit, inheriting the founders’ path.
entries.literal: The Founding Emperor wished to follow Emperor Wu’s old feng in substance, truly continuing the way of the founding ancestors.

entries.zh: 而梁松固争，以为必改。
entries.en: But Liang Song insisted the ceremony had to be reinvented.
entries.literal: Yet Liang Song stubbornly argued that the rite must be changed.

entries.zh: 乃当夫既封之后，未有福，而松卒被诛死。
entries.en: After the deed was done heaven sent no favor, and Song himself died under the headsman’s blade.
entries.literal: Then, after the feng had already been performed, no blessing appeared, and Song soon met execution.

entries.zh: 虽罪由身，盖亦诬神之咎也。
entries.en: His crimes were his own, yet they also look like punishment for profaning the gods.
entries.literal: Although his guilt was personal, it was also the retribution of having insulted the spirits.

entries.zh: 且帝王所以能大显于后者，实在其德加于民，不闻其在封矣。
entries.en: What makes a ruler remembered is virtue among the living, not a mound on Tai.
entries.literal: Moreover what enables an emperor to shine brightly to posterity lies truly in his virtue spreading among the people, not in whether he performs the feng.

entries.zh: 言天地者莫大于《易》，《易》无六宗在中之象。
entries.en: The Classic of Changes, supreme discourse on Heaven and Earth, nowhere pictures the Six Ancestors sandwiched between them.
entries.literal: Of all who speak of Heaven and Earth none is greater than the Book of Changes, and the Changes shows no image of the Six Ancestors standing between them.

entries.zh: 若信为天地四方所宗，是至大也。
entries.en: To treat them as the supreme foci of heaven, earth, and the four directions would elevate them beyond measure.
entries.literal: If they are truly to be venerated as what Heaven, Earth, and the four quarters take as their ancestors, that would make them supremely great.

entries.zh: 而比太社，又为失所，难以为诚矣！」
entries.en: Yet to rank them beside the Grand Altar of Soil is again misplaced—it is hard to call such a scheme sincere!"
entries.literal: Yet to rank them beside the Grand Altar of Soil is again misplaced; it is hard to call such a scheme sincere!"

entries.zh: 汉兴八年，有言周兴而邑立后稷之祀，于是高帝令天下立灵星祠。
entries.en: Han’s eighth year saw a memorial likening Zhou’s capital cult of Hou Ji to Han’s need; Gaozu then ordered Lingxing shrines throughout the realm.
entries.literal: In the eighth year after the founding of Han someone said that when Zhou rose it founded sacrifice to Hou Ji in the capital; therefore Emperor Gao ordered Lingxing shrines established empire-wide.

entries.zh: 言祠后稷而谓之灵星者，以后稷又配食星也。
entries.en: The name Lingxing (“spirit star”) attached to Hou Ji because he shared offerings with a star.
entries.literal: The reason the sacrifice to Hou Ji was called Lingxing is that Hou Ji also received paired worship with a constellation.

entries.zh: 旧说，星谓天田星也。
entries.en: Tradition equates that star with the celestial field.
entries.literal: Old glosses identify the star as the “heavenly field” star.

entries.zh: 一曰，龙左角为天田官，主谷。
entries.en: Another opinion makes the dragon’s left horn the celestial granary.
entries.literal: Another view: the dragon’s left horn is the office of the heavenly field and governs grain.

entries.zh: 祀用壬辰位祠之。
entries.en: Sacrifice was oriented to the ren-chen alignment.
entries.literal: The cult uses the stem ren and branch chen position.

entries.zh: 壬为水，辰为龙，就其类也。
