entries.en: Water (ren) and the dragon (chen) were paired by sympathetic category.
entries.literal: Ren belongs to water and chen to the dragon; one chooses its kindred element.

entries.zh: 牲用太牢，县邑令长侍祠。
entries.en: Victims were tai-lao; county magistrates presided.
entries.literal: The victim was a full tai-lao; county magistrates attended.

entries.zh: 舞者用童男十六人。
entries.en: Sixteen boy dancers performed.
entries.literal: The dancers were sixteen boys.

entries.zh: 舞者象教田，初为芟除，次耕种、芸耨、驱爵及获刈、舂簸之形，象其功也。
entries.en: Their dance enacted the farming year—slash, plough, hoe, shoo birds, reap, pound, and winnow.
entries.literal: The dance mimicked teaching fieldwork: first clearing brush, then ploughing, weeding, chasing sparrows, reaping, threshing, and winnowing—acting out the whole labor.

entries.zh: 志第九 祭祀下
entries.en: Treatise 9: Sacrifices, Part Two.
entries.literal: Treatise Nine: Sacrifices, Part Two.

entries.zh: 熹平元年十月，荧惑入南斗中。
entries.en: In the tenth month of Xiping 1 Mars entered the Southern Dipper.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xiping, in the tenth month, Mars entered the Southern Dipper.

entries.zh: 占曰：「荧惑所守为兵乱。」
entries.en: The gloss reads: "Where Mars stations itself expect mutiny and arms."
entries.literal: Omens say: “Where Mars guards there will be troops and rebellion.”

entries.zh: 斗为吴，其十一月，会稽贼许昭聚众自称大将军，昭父生为越王，攻破郡县。
entries.en: The Dipper marks Wu; that November Xu Zhao of Kuaiji raised an army as self-styled great general while his father Sheng proclaimed a Yue kingship and overran the countryside.
entries.literal: The Dipper is Wu; that eleventh month Kuaiji bandit Xu Zhao gathered a host and called himself great general; Zhao’s father Sheng declared himself king of Yue and stormed commanderies and counties.

entries.zh: 志第十二 天文下
entries.en: Treatise 12: Astronomy, lower fascicle.
entries.literal: Treatise twelve: Astronomy, part two.

entries.zh: 袁山松〔書〕曰：「禪位於魏。」
entries.en: Yuan Shansong's Book records: "The throne was yielded to Wei."
entries.literal: Yuan Shansong's Book says: "The abdication was transferred to Wei."

entries.zh: 靈帝光和元年，南宫侍中寺雌雞欲化雄，一身毛皆似雄，但頭冠尚未變。
entries.en: In Guanghe 1, at the Southern Palace's Palace Attendants' Office a hen began turning into a rooster—every feather looked male, yet the comb had not changed.
entries.literal: In Emperor Ling's first year of Guanghe, at the Palace Attendants' Office in the Southern Palace a hen wished to transform into a cock; its whole body's feathers all resembled a cock's, but the head crest had not yet changed.

entries.zh: 诏以問議郎蔡邕。
entries.en: The court asked Cai Yong, a gentleman consultant.
entries.literal: An edict asked the gentleman consultant Cai Yong.

entries.zh: 邕对曰：「貌之不恭，則有雞禍。
entries.en: Yong answered: "Irreverent bearing brings calamities among fowl.
entries.literal: Yong replied: "When demeanor lacks dignity, there are chicken disasters.

entries.zh: 宣帝黄龍元年，未央宫雌雞化爲雄，不鸣无距。
entries.en: In Huanglong 1 of Emperor Xuan, a Weiyang Palace hen became a rooster that neither crowed nor grew spurs.
entries.literal: In Emperor Xuan's first year of Huanglong, at Weiyang Palace a hen transformed into a cock, neither crowing nor having spurs.

entries.zh: 是岁元帝初即位，立王皇后。
entries.en: That year the newly enthroned Emperor Yuan made Lady Wang empress.
entries.literal: That year Emperor Yuan first took the throne and installed Empress Wang.

entries.zh: 至初元元年，丞相史家雌雞化爲雄，冠距鸣將。
entries.en: By Chuyuan 1 a hen at a chancellor's clerk's home had become a crowing rooster with comb and spurs.
entries.literal: By the first year of Chuyuan, at the chief minister's clerk's house a hen transformed into a cock, with crest, spurs, and about to crow.

entries.zh: 是岁后父禁爲陽平侯，女立爲皇后。
entries.en: Soon after, the empress's father Wang Jin was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangping and his daughter was crowned.
entries.literal: After that year the empress's father Wang Jin became marquis of Yangping; the daughter was installed as empress.

entries.zh: 至哀帝晏駕，后攝政，王莽以后兄子爲大司馬，由是爲亂。
entries.en: When Emperor Ai died, the empress held the regency; Wang Mang, the empress's elder brother's son, became grand marshal—and chaos followed.
entries.literal: When Emperor Ai died, the empress held regency; Wang Mang made the empress's elder brother's son grand marshal—thereby came disorder.

entries.zh: 臣窃推之：頭，元首，人君之象。
entries.en: I read the omen thus: the head is the sovereign's image.
entries.literal: Your servant privately infers: the head is the chief member, the image of the ruler.

entries.zh: 今雞一身已變，未至於頭，而上知之，是將有其事而不遂成之象也。
entries.en: The bird's body had changed but not its head, yet Heaven had already warned the throne—an omen of crisis not yet complete.
entries.literal: Now the chicken's whole body has changed but not yet reached the head, yet the sovereign knows it—this is the image of something about to happen but not yet fully accomplished.

entries.zh: 若應之不精，政无所改，頭冠或成，爲患兹大。」
entries.en: If the court ignored the warning and reformed nothing, the comb might finish forming—and the disaster would be worse."
entries.literal: If the response is not precise and government changes nothing, the head crest may complete itself and the harm will be all the greater."

entries.zh: 是后張角作亂称黄巾，遂破壞。
entries.en: Soon Zhang Jiao raised the Yellow Turban revolt and the realm was torn apart.
entries.literal: After this Zhang Jiao rebelled, calling himself the Yellow Turbans, and destruction followed.

entries.zh: 四方疲於赋役，多叛者。
entries.en: Taxes and labor broke the provinces; rebellion spread.
entries.literal: The four quarters were exhausted by levies and corvée; many rebelled.

entries.zh: 上不改政，遂至天下大亂。
entries.en: The emperor changed nothing—and the empire slid into total chaos.
entries.literal: The sovereign did not reform government, and all under Heaven reached great disorder.

entries.zh: 世祖古今注曰：「建武三年七月，雒陽大旱，帝至南郊求雨，即日雨。」
entries.en: The Founder's Ancient and Modern Notes record: "In the seventh month of Jianwu 3 Luoyang baked; the emperor prayed at the southern altar and rain came the same day."
entries.literal: The Ancient and Modern Notes of the Founder say: "In the seventh month of the third year of Jianwu Luoyang had great drought; the emperor went to the southern suburb to pray for rain, and rain fell that day."

entries.zh: 世祖建武五年夏，旱。
entries.en: A drought struck in the summer of Emperor Guangwu's fifth Jianwu year.
entries.literal: In Shizu's fifth year of Jianwu, summer, there was drought.

entries.zh: 《京房傳》曰：「欲德不用，兹謂張，厥災荒，其旱陰雲不雨，變而赤，因四陰。
entries.en: Jing Fang lists omens of drought: "when virtue is spurned, Heaven stretches the land into waste; clouds gather but yield no rain, then flush an ominous red as yin forces encroach.
entries.literal: Jing Fang's Treatise says: "When desired virtue is not used, this is called stretching; its disaster is wasteland; its drought—yin clouds do not rain, they change and become red, following the four yin.

entries.zh: 眾出過時，兹謂廣，其旱不生。
entries.en: Armies kept in the field too long "spread" exhaustion; the fields then refuse every shoot.
entries.literal: When hosts go out beyond the season, this is called broadening; its drought—nothing grows.

entries.zh: 上下皆蔽，兹謂隔，其旱天赤三月，時有雹殺飛禽。
entries.en: When ruler and minister deceive each other, Heaven "blocks" the rain—the heavens burn red for months and hailstones cut down birds in flight.
entries.literal: When above and below are both obscured, this is called blocking; its drought—the sky is red three months; at times hail kills flying birds.

entries.zh: 上缘求妃，兹謂僭，其旱三月大温亡云。
entries.en: A ruler who chases women beyond measure commits usurpation against Heaven; the land then swelters for three cloudless months.
entries.literal: When the sovereign on account seeks concubines, this is called usurpation; its drought—three months of great warmth without clouds.

entries.zh: 君高臺府，兹謂犯，陰侵陽，其旱萬物根死，有火災。
entries.en: Towering palaces offend the balance of yin and yang; drought kills every root, and fires follow.
entries.literal: When the lord raises high terraces and mansions, this is called violation; yin encroaches on yang; its drought—the roots of the myriad things die; there are fire disasters.

entries.zh: 庶位逾節，兹謂僭，其旱泽物枯，爲火所傷。」
entries.en: When petty officials overstep their rank, usurpation dries the wetlands and scorches what should be moist."
entries.literal: When common offices exceed their measure, this is called usurpation; its drought—marsh things wither and are harmed by fire."

entries.zh: 是時，天下僭逆者未尽誅，軍多過時。
entries.en: Rebels still lived while imperial columns overstayed in the field—both sins on Jing Fang's list.
entries.literal: At this time those who had usurped and rebelled under Heaven had not all been executed; armies were for the most part beyond their season.

entries.zh: 更始時，南陽有童謠曰：「諧不諧，在赤眉。
entries.en: During the Gengshi interregnum a rhyme ran through Nanyang: "Whether the tune holds—ask the Red Eyebrows.
entries.literal: In Gengshi's time, Nanyang had a children's song saying: "Harmonious or not harmonious, lies with the Red Eyebrows.

entries.zh: 得不得，在河北。」
entries.en: Whether the prize is won—look to the north of the Yellow River."
entries.literal: Obtaining or not obtaining, lies with Hebei."

entries.zh: 是時，更始在長安，世祖爲大司馬平定河北。
entries.en: Gengshi held Chang'an while Liu Xiu, as grand marshal, was pacifying the north.
entries.literal: At this time Gengshi was in Chang'an; Shizu was grand marshal pacifying Hebei.

entries.zh: 更始大臣並僭專權，故謠妖作也。
entries.en: Gengshi's ministers had all seized power beyond their right—hence these portentous rhymes.
entries.literal: Gengshi's great ministers together usurped sole power; therefore song prodigies arose.

entries.zh: 后更始遂爲赤眉所殺，是更始之不諧在赤眉也。
entries.en: The Red Eyebrows soon killed Gengshi—the "lack of harmony" line had pointed straight at them.
entries.literal: Later Gengshi was then killed by the Red Eyebrows; this was Gengshi's lack of harmony lying with the Red Eyebrows.

entries.zh: 世祖自河北興。
entries.en: Liu Xiu rose to power from the Hebei plain.
entries.literal: Shizu rose from Hebei.

entries.zh: 世祖建武六年，蜀童謠曰：「黄牛白腹，五铢當復。」
entries.en: In Jianwu 6 a Shu children's rhyme ran: "The yellow bull shows a white belly—the Han five-zhu coin will return."
entries.literal: In Shizu's sixth year of Jianwu, Shu had a children's song saying: "Yellow ox, white belly; the five-zhu coin ought to return."

entries.zh: 是時，公孙述僭號於蜀，時人窃言王莽称黄，述欲继之，故称白；
entries.en: Gongsun Shu had declared himself emperor in Shu; gossips said Wang Mang's regime had been the "yellow" phase and Shu styled itself "white" as his successor;
entries.literal: At this time Gongsun Shu usurped title in Shu; people of the time secretly said Wang Mang was called yellow, Shu wished to succeed him, therefore called white;

entries.zh: 五铢，漢家货，明當復也。
entries.en: the five-zhu was Han coinage—plainly it would be restored.
entries.literal: the five-zhu is Han house currency; clearly it ought to return.

entries.zh: 述遂誅滅。
entries.en: Gongsun Shu was destroyed.
entries.literal: He was then executed and destroyed.

entries.zh: 志第十三 五行一
entries.en: Treatise Thirteen: The Five Elements, Part One.
entries.literal: Treatise, the thirteenth: Five Elements, part one.

entries.zh: 安帝永初二年四月甲寅，汉阳阿阳城中失火，烧殺三千五百七十人。
entries.en: On an jiayin day in the fourth month of Yongchu 2 a conflagration in Ayang, Hanyang, killed 3,570 people.
entries.literal: In Emperor An’s second year of Yongchu, fourth month, day jiayin, fire broke out in Ayang city in Hanyang, burning to death three thousand five hundred seventy people.

entries.zh: 先是和帝崩，有皇子二人，皇子胜长，邓皇后贪殇帝少，欲自养长立之。
entries.en: After He’s death two princes survived; Liu Sheng was the elder, but Empress Deng preferred the infant Shang so she could prolong her regency.
entries.literal: Before this, when Emperor He died there were two imperial sons; Prince Sheng was the elder; Empress Deng coveted Emperor Shang’s youth and wished to rear him herself and establish him when grown.

entries.zh: 延平元年，殇帝崩。
entries.en: The child emperor died in Yanping 1.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yanping, Emperor Shang died.

entries.zh: 胜有厥疾不笃，群臣咸欲立之，太后以前既不立胜，遂更立清河王子，是为安帝。
entries.en: Liu Sheng was fit enough to rule, and the court wanted him, but the dowager—having once passed him over—enthroned the Qinghe prince’s son as Emperor An instead.
entries.literal: Sheng had chronic ailments but was not gravely ill; the host of ministers all wished to enthrone him; because the empress dowager had earlier refused to establish Sheng, she thereupon instead set up the Prince of Qinghe’s son—this is Emperor An.

entries.zh: 司空周章等心不厌服，谋欲诛邓氏，废太后、安帝，而更立胜。
entries.en: Zhou Zhang and other ministers secretly planned a coup: wipe out the Deng family, depose regent and emperor, and restore Liu Sheng.
entries.literal: Minister of Works Zhou Zhang and others inwardly did not submit; they plotted to execute the Deng clan, depose the empress dowager and Emperor An, and again enthrone Sheng.

entries.zh: 元年十一月，事觉，章等被诛。
entries.en: The plot surfaced that eleventh month and the conspirators died.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year the affair was discovered; Zhang and the others were executed.

entries.zh: 其后凉州叛羌为害大甚，凉州诸郡寄治冯翊、扶风界。
entries.en: Then the Liangzhou Qiang revolted so fiercely that the northwestern commanderies had to be administered from Fengyi and Fufeng in the interior.
entries.literal: Afterward the rebel Qiang of Liangzhou did harm on a great scale; the commanderies of Liangzhou were relocated for administration within the borders of Fengyi and Fufeng.

entries.zh: 及太后崩，邓氏被诛。
entries.en: After the dowager’s death the Dengs were extirpated.
entries.literal: When the empress dowager died, the Deng clan was executed.

entries.zh: 安帝延光三年二月戊子，有五色大鸟集济南台，十月，又集新丰，时以为凤皇。
entries.en: On wuzi in the second month of Yanguang 3 a huge polychrome bird perched on Jinan’s terrace and again at Xinfeng—courtiers hailed it as a phoenix.
entries.literal: In Emperor An’s third year of Yanguang, second month, day wuzi, a great five-colored bird alighted on the terrace in Jinan; in the tenth month it again alighted at Xinfeng; the time took it for a phoenix.

entries.zh: 或以为凤皇阳明之应，故非明主，则隐不见。
entries.en: Some argued a true phoenix appears only under a sage-king; otherwise it stays hidden.
entries.literal: Some held that the phoenix is the response of yang brightness; therefore if it is not a bright lord, it hides and does not appear.

entries.zh: 凡五色大鸟似凤者，多羽虫之孽。
entries.en: Such rainbow birds are usually classed as winged omens, not true phoenixes.
entries.literal: In general great five-colored birds resembling phoenixes are for the most part winged-insect prodigies.

entries.zh: 是时，安帝信中常侍樊丰、江京、阿母王圣及外属耿宝等谗言，免太尉杨震，废太子为济阴王，不悊之异也。
entries.en: Emperor An was listening to Fan Feng, Jiang Jing, Wang Sheng, and Geng Bao: he cashiered Yang Zhen and cast down the crown prince—exactly the blindness those birds foretold.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor An trusted palace attendants Fan Feng, Jiang Jing, nurse Wang Sheng, and outer kin Geng Bao and others’ slanderous words, dismissed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and deposed the heir apparent as Prince of Jiyin—a prodigy of lack of discernment.

entries.zh: 章帝末，号凤皇百四十九见。
entries.en: Late in Emperor Zhang’s reign the court logged 149 “phoenix” sightings.
entries.literal: At the end of Zhangdi’s reign, phoenixes were titled one hundred forty-nine sightings.

entries.zh: 时，直臣何敞以为羽孽，似凤，翱翔殿屋，不察也。
entries.en: He Chang called them counterfeit phoenixes wheeling over the halls—omens no one cared to read.
entries.literal: At the time straight minister He Chang held them to be winged prodigies, resembling phoenixes, soaring over palace roofs—lack of inspection.

entries.zh: 记者以为其后章帝崩，以为验。
entries.en: The compiler notes that Emperor Zhang soon died—proof, he thought, of ill omen.
entries.literal: The recorder thought that afterward Zhangdi died and took it as verification.

entries.zh: 案宣帝、明帝时，五色鸟群翔殿屋，贾逵以为胡降征也。
entries.en: Under Xuandi and Mingdi similar flocks had appeared; Jia Kui read them as portents of barbarian submission.
entries.literal: Examining: in the times of Emperors Xuan and Ming, flocks of five-colored birds soared over palace halls; Jia Kui held it to be the sign of surrender of the Hu.

entries.zh: 帝多善政，虽有过，不及至衰缺，末年胡降二十万口，是其验也。
entries.en: Those were strong reigns; when 200,000 tribesmen submitted late in the era, Jia Kui’s reading seemed vindicated.
entries.literal: Those emperors had many good policies; although they had faults, they did not reach decline and want; in the last years the Hu surrendered two hundred thousand persons—this was its verification.

entries.zh: 帝之时，羌胡外叛，谗慝内兴，羽孽之时也。
entries.en: Under An the frontiers rose in revolt and calumny filled the palace—the age of false phoenixes.
entries.literal: In this emperor’s time, Qiang and Hu rebelled outside while slander flourished within—the season of winged prodigies.

entries.zh: 《乐叶图征》说五凤皆五色，为瑞者一，为孽者四。
entries.en: The weft-text on the five phoenixes counts one bird as lucky and four as baleful.
entries.literal: The Music Leaf Chart Prognostication says the five phoenixes are all five-colored: one is auspicious, four are prodigies.

entries.zh: 志第十四 五行二
entries.en: Treatise Fourteen: The Five Elements, Part Two.
entries.literal: Treatise, the fourteenth: Five Elements, part two.

entries.zh: 安帝永初元年冬十月辛酉，河南新城山水虣出，突坏民田，坏处泉水出，深三丈。
entries.en: Yongchu 1 (107 CE), late autumn: a flash flood out of the Xincheng hills in Henan tore through farmland, and new springs welled ten yards deep in the scour.
entries.literal: In the winter, tenth month, on the day xinyou of the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An, mountains and rivers in Xincheng, Henan, burst forth violently, smashed private fields, and where they broke open springs gushed up three zhang deep.

entries.zh: 是时司空周章等以邓太后不立皇太子胜而立清河王子，故谋欲废置。
entries.en: Zhou Zhang and his fellow ministers resented the dowager's choice of the Qinghe infant over Prince Sheng and conspired to reverse the succession.
entries.literal: At that time Minister of Works Zhou Zhang and others, because Empress Dowager Deng had not enthroned Heir Apparent Sheng but the son of the Prince of Qinghe, therefore plotted to depose and replace.

entries.zh: 十一月，事觉，章等被诛。
entries.en: Eleventh month: the plot leaked; Zhou Zhang and his allies went to the block.
entries.literal: In the eleventh month the affair was discovered; Zhang and the others were executed.

entries.zh: 是年郡国四十一水出，漂没民人。
entries.en: That same year forty-one jurisdictions saw rivers overrun their banks and sweep away whole communities.
entries.literal: That year forty-one commanderies and kingdoms had water break out, drifting away and drowning the people.

entries.zh: 《谶》曰：「水者，纯阴之精也。
entries.en: The "Chen" prophecy says: "Water is the essence of pure yin.
entries.literal: The "Chen" prophecy says: "Water is the essence of pure yin.

entries.zh: 阴气盛洋溢者，小人专制擅权，妒疾贤者，依公结私，侵乘君子，小人席胜，失怀得志，故涌水为灾。」
entries.en: When yin swells past measure, mean men seize the levers of state, envy the good, trade on public trust for private gain, and trample their betters—so the rivers boil up in answer."
entries.literal: When yin qi flourishes and overflows, petty men monopolize power, are jealous of the worthy, rely on public office to pursue private ends, encroach upon gentlemen; petty men sit atop victory, lose restraint and get their will—therefore surging water becomes calamity."

entries.zh: 延光三年，大水，流杀民人，伤苗稼。
entries.en: Yanguang 3 (124 CE): catastrophic freshets drowned people and laid waste to the young grain.
entries.literal: In the third year of Yanguang there was a great flood; flowing water killed the people and injured the seedling crops.

entries.zh: 是时安帝信江京、樊丰及阿母王圣等谗言，免太尉杨震，废皇太子。
entries.en: The emperor listened to his eunuchs and his wet nurse, cashiered Yang Zhen, and cast down the crown prince—classic signs of a tottering house.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor An believed the slander of Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and his nurse Wang Sheng and the like, dismissed Grand Commandant Yang Zhen, and deposed the heir apparent.

entries.zh: 延光四年，郡国十九冬雷。
entries.en: Yanguang 4 (125 CE): nineteen commanderies reported winter thunder—a widespread sign.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Yanguang nineteen commanderies and kingdoms had winter thunder.

entries.zh: 是时，太后摄政，上无所与。
entries.en: The dowager regent ran every decision; the sovereign had no voice in affairs.
entries.literal: At that time the empress dowager held the government; the emperor participated in nothing.

entries.zh: 太后既崩，阿母王圣及皇后兄阎显兄弟更秉威权，上遂不亲万机，从容宽仁任臣下。
entries.en: When she died, the emperor's wet nurse Wang Sheng and Empress Yan's brothers seized the reins; the ruler withdrew from the daily grind of government, indulged a reputation for mildness, and left policy to his officials.
entries.literal: After the empress dowager died, the nurse Wang Sheng and the empress's elder brothers Yan Xian and company in turn grasped awesome power; the emperor thereupon did not personally attend to the myriad threads of state, but was easygoing, lenient, and entrusted things to his ministers.

entries.zh: 志第十五 五行三
entries.en: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.
entries.literal: Treatise Fifteen: The Five Elements, Part Three.

entries.zh: 世祖建武二十二年九月，郡国四十二地震，南阳尤甚，地裂压杀人。
entries.en: Jianwu 22 (46 CE), ninth month: forty-two jurisdictions shook; Nanyang worst, with fissures that swallowed lives.
entries.literal: In the ninth month of the twenty-second year of Jianwu, Emperor Guangwu, forty-two commanderies and kingdoms suffered earthquakes; Nanyang was especially severe—the earth split open and crushed people to death.

entries.zh: 其后武谿蛮夷反，为寇害，至南郡，发荆州诸郡兵，遣武威将军刘尚击之，为夷所围，复发兵赴之，尚遂为所没。
entries.en: Then the Wuxi tribes rose, raided south to Nanjun, and trapped Liu Shang's relief army—he and his men were wiped out.
entries.literal: Afterward the Wuxi Man and Yi rebelled, becoming bandit scourges as far as Nanjun; troops from the several commanderies of Jingzhou were mobilized, and General of Martial Might Liu Shang was sent to strike them; he was surrounded by the tribes, troops were sent again to relieve him, and Shang was then lost with his force.

entries.zh: 建光元年九月己丑，郡国三十五地震，或地坼裂，坏城郭室屋，压杀人。
entries.en: Jianguang 1 (121 CE), ninth month, jichou: thirty-five commanderies; ground split, towns ruined, lives lost.
entries.literal: On the day jichou in the ninth month of the first year of Jianguang thirty-five commanderies and kingdoms suffered earthquakes; in places the earth split open, city walls and houses were ruined, and people were crushed to death.

entries.zh: 是时，安帝不能明察，信宫人及阿母圣等谗言，破坏邓太后家，于是专听信圣及宦者，中常侍江京、樊丰等皆得用权。
entries.en: An turned on the Dengs on whispered lies from Wang Sheng and the harem, then handed the realm to Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and their fellow eunuchs.
entries.literal: At that time Emperor An could not investigate clearly; he believed slander from palace women and his nurse Wang Sheng and the like, ruined Empress Dowager Deng's family, and thereafter listened exclusively to Sheng and the eunuchs—Regular Attendants Jiang Jing, Fan Feng, and others all came to wield power.

entries.zh: 安帝永初元年，大风拔树。
entries.en: Yongchu 1: gales ripped trees from the earth.
entries.literal: In the first year of Yongchu, Emperor An, a great wind uprooted trees.

entries.zh: 是时，邓太后摄政，以清河王子年少，号精耳，故立之，是为安帝。
entries.en: The Deng dowager enthroned the young Qinghe prince, praising his precocity; he became Emperor An.
entries.literal: At that time Empress Dowager Deng held the government; because the prince of Qinghe was young—in reputation still a clever child—therefore he was set up; this was Emperor An.

entries.zh: 不立皇太子胜，以为安帝贤，必当德邓氏也；
entries.en: She bypassed Prince Sheng, betting that An would reward the Dengs for the throne.
entries.literal: She did not enthrone Imperial Son Sheng, holding that Emperor An was worthy and would surely repay the Deng clan with gratitude.

entries.zh: 后安帝亲谗，废免邓氏，令郡县迫切，死者八九人，家至破坏。
entries.en: An later swallowed lies about the Dengs, purged them savagely, and left eight or nine dead—whole houses destroyed.
entries.literal: Afterward Emperor An personally believed slander, deposed and dismissed the Deng clan, and ordered the commanderies and counties to press them urgently—eight or nine died, families down to ruin.

entries.zh: 此为瞉霿也。
entries.en: That was the arrogant obscuration the omen text names as the blame.
entries.literal: This was arrogant obscuration.

entries.zh: 是后西羌亦大乱凉州十有余年。
entries.en: Then the Qiang war convulsed Liangzhou for another decade.
entries.literal: Afterward the Western Qiang also threw Liangzhou into great chaos for more than ten years.

entries.zh: 二年六月，京都及郡国四十大风拔树。
entries.en: Yongchu 2, sixth month: forty jurisdictions lost trees to wind.
entries.literal: In the sixth month of the second year the capital and forty commanderies and kingdoms had great winds that uprooted trees.

entries.zh: 三年五月癸酉，京都大风，拔南郊道梓树九十六枚。
entries.en: Yongchu 3, fifth month, guiyou: a wind sheared ninety-six catalpas from the processional avenue to the southern altar.
entries.literal: On the day guiyou in the fifth month of the third year the capital had a great wind that uprooted ninety-six catalpa trees along the southern suburban road.

entries.zh: 七年八月丙寅，京都大风拔树。
entries.en: Yongchu 7, eighth month, bingyin: Luoyang gales again.
entries.literal: On the day bingyin in the eighth month of the seventh year the capital had a great wind that uprooted trees.

entries.zh: 明帝永平十八年，牛疫死。
entries.en: Yongping 18 (75 CE): murrain wiped out the herds.
entries.literal: In the eighteenth year of Yongping, Emperor Ming, cattle died in plague.

entries.zh: 是岁，遣窦固等征西域，置都护、戊己校尉。
entries.en: The same year Dou Gu marched west and the court posted a protector-general and Wuji colonels.
entries.literal: That year Dou Gu and others were dispatched to campaign in the Western Regions; a protector-general and the Wuji garrison colonels were established.

entries.zh: 固等适还而西域叛，杀都护陈睦、戊己校尉关宠。
entries.en: No sooner had the army withdrawn than the west rebelled—Chen Mu and Guan Chong fell.
entries.literal: When Gu and the others had just returned the Western Regions rebelled, killing Protector-General Chen Mu and Wuji Colonel Guan Chong.

entries.zh: 于是大怒，欲复发兴讨，会秋明帝崩，是思心不容也。
entries.en: Ming meant to strike again but died that autumn—Heaven cutting short a ruler who would not listen.
entries.literal: Thereupon the court was greatly angered and wished to launch another great punitive expedition; it happened that in autumn Emperor Ming died—this is "reflective thought finding no room."

entries.zh: 志第十六 五行四
entries.en: Treatise Sixteen: The Five Elements, Part Four.
entries.literal: Treatise Sixteen: The Five Elements, Part Four.

entries.zh: 桓帝延熹七年六月壬子，河内野王山上有龙死，长可数十丈。
entries.en: In the seventh year of Yanxi (164), on a day renzi in the sixth month, a dead dragon tens of zhang long was found on a mountain at Yewang in Henei.
entries.literal: On the renzi day of the sixth month in the seventh year of Yanxi of Emperor Huan, on a mountain in Yewang in Henei a dragon died, perhaps several dozen zhang in length.

entries.zh: 襄楷以为夫龙者为帝王瑞，《易》论大人。
entries.en: Xiang Kai argued that the dragon is the classical emblem of the true king; the Book of Changes, after all, speaks of the "great man" in such terms.
entries.literal: Xiang Kai held that the dragon is an auspicious sign for emperors and kings, and the Changes treats the great man.
